## 《让我看看金钱》

<!--en-->
*Show Me the Money*

*《让我看看金钱》* 是一本权威的商业新闻学教材，为从事商业新闻工作的记者提供了实用的建议与案例。作者克里斯·罗斯凭借其作为商业新闻记者及教育工作者的经验，讲解了如何报道企业、行业与经济动态，以及如何寻找新闻素材。他还清晰地展示了记者如何将财务信息转化为能向读者解释相关主题的事实。

<!--en-->
*Show Me the Money* is the definitive business journalism textbook that offers hands-on advice and examples on doing the job of a business journalist. Author Chris Roush draws on his experience as a business journalist and educator to explain how to cover businesses, industries, and the economy, as well as where to find sources of information for stories. He demonstrates clearly how reporters take financial information and turn it into relevant facts that explain a topic to readers.

这本权威的商业新闻学著作：

<!--en-->
This definitive business journalism text:

* 提供了商业文章的实战案例；
* 以通俗易懂的方式阐述复杂主题；
* 给出了在SEC文件中寻找新闻素材的示例；
* 对企业财务报表、资产负债表及现金流量表进行了全面解读；
* 提供了寻找消息来源的技巧，如企业投资者及难以获取的企业文件；以及
* 列出了供商业新闻记者使用的各类网站。第二版的主要更新包括：
* 全书穿插了专业商业新闻记者的实用建议；
* 新增了关于个人财经报道及特定商业领域报道的章节；
* 扩展了房地产报道的内容；以及
* 对SEC、金融及经济领域的重大变化进行了更新。书中配有大量文档与新闻案例，是从事商业新闻工作的学生与从业者的必备指南。克里斯·罗斯是沃尔特·E·赫斯曼商业新闻杰出学者，也是北卡罗来纳大学教堂山分校“卡罗莱纳商业新闻计划”的创始主任，该计划为专业记者及学生提供培训。他已撰写了两本关于商业新闻的书籍：*《让我看看金钱：面向大众传媒的商业与经济报道写作》* 和 *《利润与亏损：商业新闻及其在社会中的作用》*。2010年，罗斯获得了由斯克里普斯霍华德基金会与新闻与大众传播教育协会（AEJMC）联合颁发的查尔斯·E·斯克里普斯年度新闻教师奖。

<!--en-->
* Provides real-world examples of business articles;
* Presents complex topics in a form easy to read and understand;
* Offers examples of where to find news stories in SEC filings;
* Gives comprehensive explanations and reviews of corporate financial, balance sheet, and cash flow statements;
* Provides tips on finding sources, such as corporate investors and hard-to-find corporate documents; and
* Gives a comprehensive listing of websites for business journalists to use.
Key updates for the second edition include:
* Tips from professional business journalists provided throughout the text;
* New chapters on Personal Finance reporting and covering specific business beats;
* Expanded coverage of real estate reporting; and
* Updates throughout to reflect significant changes in SEC, finance, and economics industries.
With numerous examples of documents and stories in the text, *Show Me the Money* is an essential guide for students and practitioners doing business journalism.
Chris Roush is Walter E. Hussman Sr. Distinguished Scholar in business journalism and founding director of the Carolina Business News Initiative, which provides training for professional journalists and students at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill. He has authored two books on business journalism: *Show Me the Money: Writing Business and Economics Stories for Mass Communication* and *Profits and Losses: Business Journalism and its Role in Society*. Roush received the Charles E. Scripps Award for the Journalism Teacher of the Year in 2010, awarded by the Scripps Howard Foundation in collaboration with the Association for Education in Journalism and Mass Communication (AEJMC).

# 前言

<!--en-->
*Foreword*

ALEC KLEIN 西北大学梅迪尔新闻学院教授 我当时正弯着腰坐在《华尔街日报》的办公桌前，一滴汗渗进了我那件熨烫得一丝不苟的牛津衬衫领口，我知道我的职业生涯就此结束了。

<!--en-->
ALEC KLEIN
Professor, Medill School of Journalism
Northwestern University
So there I was, hunched over my desk at *The Wall Street Journal*, feeling a bead of sweat seep into the collar of my well-pressed, button-down Oxford, and I knew this was the end of my career.

那是20世纪90年代末，我正在与全国各地的数十名华尔街分析师和记者进行电话会议，听IBM介绍其最新的财务业绩。这对我来说是个难题——我对IBM一无所知，对电脑也完全不懂，从未拥有过一台电脑。更糟糕的是，我对金融知识也知之甚少。不知怎的，不久前我竟被这家国内顶尖财经报纸聘为记者；显然他们喜欢我的报道和写作风格，尽管我根本分不清资产负债表和床单的区别。而现在，我却要为第二天的报纸撰写这篇重要新闻稿。

<!--en-->
It was in the late 1990s, and I was on a conference call with scores of Wall Street analysts and reporters throughout the country, listening to IBM talk about its latest financial results. This presented a problem. I didn't know anything about IBM. I didn't know the first thing about computers; I had never owned one. Worse: I knew little about finances. Somehow, I had been hired not long before as a reporter at the nation's leading financial paper; evidently they liked my reporting and writing even though I couldn't tell a balance sheet from a bed sheet. And now I was assigned to write this story—a lead news piece—for the next day's paper.

我环顾四周：电话会议中的IBM官员们正在念叨着一些听起来像财务密码的东西。我困惑至极，甚至都没费心记下任何内容。我瞥了一眼时钟——情况不妙。宝贵的时间正在飞速流逝，而我的文章还没写完。突然间，我脑海中浮现出第二天《华尔街日报》的版面：本该刊登我文章的位置将出现一个巨大的空白。

<!--en-->
I took inventory: IBM officials on the call were intoning about what sounded like financial hieroglyphics. I was so befuddled that I hadn't bothered to jot anything down. I glanced at the clock. Not good. Precious minutes were ticking to the deadline, and, suddenly, I imagined tomorrow's *Wall Street Journal*: a big gaping hole where my article was supposed to be.

电话会议一结束，我就给一位华尔街分析师打电话，让他解释刚才IBM电话会议里发生了什么。那位分析师开始列举一些与“P&L”相关的内容。“‘P&L’是什么？”我问道。长时间的沉默之后，分析师难以置信地问：“你不知道‘P&L’是什么意思？”

<!--en-->
As soon as the conference call ended, I dialed a Wall Street analyst and asked him to explain what had just happened on the IBM call. The analyst rattled off something to do with “P&L.”
“What's 'P&L?'” I asked.
Long pause.
“You don't know what 'P&L' is?” the analyst asked in utter disbelief.

我承认自己不懂，他便解释说“‘P&L’”即“‘利润与损失’”——这是世界上最基础的财务术语之一——说完后，他大概还考虑取消订阅《华尔街日报》。

<!--en-->
I professed ignorance, and he explained that “ 'P&L'” stood for “ 'profit and loss'”—one of the most basic financial terms known on the planet—and then, no doubt, considered canceling his subscription to *The Wall Street Journal*.

就我而言，我只希望自己能具备扎实的财务报告基础。我只希望自己能拥有像北卡罗来纳大学教堂山分校商业新闻领域的沃尔特·E·胡斯曼杰出学者克里斯·劳什那样的专业技能。我只希望自己读过他那本著名的著作《给我看钱：为大众传媒撰写商业与经济新闻》。

<!--en-->
For my part, I only wish I had had the benefit of a good foundation in financial reporting. I only wish I had had the expertise of someone like Chris Roush, the Walter E. Hussman Sr. Distinguished Scholar in business journalism at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill. I only wish I had read an esteemed book like his *Show Me the Money: Writing Business and Economics Stories for Mass Communication*.

如果那时就有这本书，就能让我免受许多羞辱。更重要的是，它还能为我提供所有财经记者和商业新闻专业学生所需的必要工具：在开始撰写相关内容之前，先深入理解重要的商业和经济概念。vii viii • 前言 这本教科书涵盖了诸多核心内容，如企业财务报告的基础、并购、私营企业、非营利组织、破产法庭、房地产以及监管机构等。这些内容并非仅仅是理论范畴。如今，财务报告在国内外新闻领域占据着极其重要的地位。这不仅仅是因为无数人的退休储蓄与股市的起伏息息相关，也因为工资和大学学费越来越与全球经济的波动紧密相连。更关键的是，商业新闻涉及到我们社会的根基——建立在自由市场理念之上的民主制度。

<!--en-->
This book, had it been around back then, would have spared me a good deal of humiliation. Even more, the book would have given me the critical tools that all financial journalists and students of business journalism need: a deep understanding of important business and economic concepts, before sitting down to write about them.
vii viii • Foreword
This textbook covers the essential landscape, such as the basics of a company’s financial reporting, mergers and acquisitions, private firms, nonprofits, bankruptcy court, real estate and regulatory agencies. These and other covered topics are not just a matter of theory. Never before has financial reporting so dominated the news here and abroad. It’s not just that untold people have their retirement savings tied to the vicissitudes of the stock market or that paychecks and college tuition are increasingly entwined in the ups and downs of the global economy. It’s that business reporting touches on the very foundation of our society: a democracy built on the idea of a free market.

然而，仅仅理解基本概念已经不够了。至少现在不再如此。我在2000年离开《华尔街日报》，成为《华盛顿邮报》的调查性商业记者后，才逐渐意识到这一点。在那里，我花了整整一年时间调查AOL收购时代华纳的事件，获取了数百份机密文件，这要求我不仅要掌握华尔街那些复杂的数学知识，还要了解会计和法律问题。最终，我撰写了一系列报道，揭露了AOL如何通过秘密虚增收入，完成了美国历史上规模最大的并购，从而打造出全球最大的媒体公司。

<!--en-->
It isn’t enough, though, to understand basic concepts. Not anymore. I began to appreciate that when I left *The Wall Street Journal* to become an investigative business reporter at *The Washington Post* in 2000. There, I conducted a yearlong investigation of AOL’s takeover of Time Warner, obtaining hundreds of confidential documents that demanded I grasp issues involving not just the arcane math of Wall Street, but accounting and legal matters. The end result: I wrote a series of stories showing how AOL secretly inflated its revenue to pull off the largest merger in U.S. history to create the biggest media company in the world.

如今，作为西北大学梅迪尔新闻学院的教授，我在商业新闻课程中教导学生掌握基础知识——包括利润与损失等概念——然后再深入研究财务问题。我希望他们能比我准备得更充分，这样就不会在截止日期前手心冒汗。值得欣慰的是，有了这本内容全面的教科书，现在的和未来的商业记者都能有现成的指南，帮助他们在这个复杂而有趣的商业世界中前行。

<!--en-->
Now, as a professor at Northwestern University’s Medill School of Journalism, I teach students in my business reporting class to learn the fundamentals—profit and loss among them—and then to dig further into financials. I want them to be better prepared than I was so they won’t find themselves sweating on deadline. It’s good to know that, with this comprehensive textbook, there is a ready guide to help business journalists of the present and future navigate the fascinating and complex world of business.

## 序言

<!--en-->
*Preface*

我作为商业记者的第一个星期仿佛就在昨天。1989年5月，我在*萨拉索塔先驱论坛报*的马纳蒂县分社工作，第一周由即将调往报社总部的前任指导我。一周后她离开了，我顿时慌了神。

<!--en-->
My first week as a business reporter seems like yesterday. At the Manatee County bureau of the *Sarasota Herald-Tribune* in May 1989, I spent the first week being trained by my predecessor, who was transferring to the newspaper’s main office. After a week, she left, and I panicked.

我以前从未做过商业记者。此前我在*圣彼得堡时报*的帕斯科县分社负责报道警察和法庭新闻——顺便说一句，这是我极其讨厌的工作。我不想再看到尸体，于是打电话给萨拉索塔的一个朋友，他告诉了我有这个职位空缺的消息。过了第一周后，我不再恐慌，虽然犯了一些错误，但也逐渐学会了如何开展工作。

<!--en-->
I had never been a business reporter before. My previous job was covering cops and courts in the Pasco County bureau of the *St. Petersburg Times*—a job, I might add, I hated. I wanted to do anything other than look at dead bodies. So I called a friend in Sarasota who told me about the business opening. After the first week, I got over the panic, made some mistakes, and learned what to do on the job.

这正是我需要的休息机会，也是正确的职业选择。成为商业记者让我进入了报纸、杂志乃至后来的互联网上发展最快的新闻内容领域。那些懂商业知识的记者会被其他媒体招揽，我的事业也因此像许多人的事业一样迅速发展起来。

<!--en-->
It was the break I needed, and the right career move. Becoming a business reporter put me in the fastest-growing part of editorial content in newspapers, magazines, and, later, the Internet. Reporters who knew something about business were recruited by other publications, and my career took off, like the careers of many others.

在萨拉索塔工作一年后，*坦帕论坛报*的商业编辑给我打了电话。我不知道他是谁，也不清楚他看过我的哪些报道。但他想雇用我，并提供了更高的薪水以及在更大规模报纸工作的机会。这种趋势持续存在：*商业周刊*需要一位熟悉保险行业报道的康涅狄格州分社成员；彭博新闻社希望其亚特兰大办事处能有报道过饮料行业的记者；弗吉尼亚州的一家出版公司还聘请了招聘人员来寻找能创办保险杂志的人选。

<!--en-->
After a year in Sarasota, the business editor at the *Tampa Tribune* called me. I had no idea who he was, or what stories of mine he had seen. But he wanted to hire me, and offered me more money and the opportunity to work at a larger newspaper. The trend continued. *BusinessWeek* needed someone in its Connecticut bureau who knew how to write about insurance. Bloomberg News wanted someone in its Atlanta office that had covered the beverage industry. A publishing company in Virginia hired a recruiter to find someone who could start an insurance magazine.

过去20年来，无论以何种形式呈现，商业新闻一直是大众传媒领域中发展最快的板块。然而，在我的整个职业生涯中，我一直回想起那份最初的工作以及自己缺乏经验的情况。和该领域的许多人一样，我也是边工作边学习收入与利润、净利润与营业利润之间的区别。我也像其他记者一样通过他人告知了解到上市公司公开文件的内容及其意义。

<!--en-->
Business news, whatever the form, has been the growth industry of mass communication for the last 20 years. Yet, during the entire progression of my career, I kept thinking back to that first job and my lack of experience. I learned on the job, just like many others in the field, about the differences between revenue and profits, and net income and operating income. I discovered public company filings the way other reporters did—someone with more experience told me about them and what they contained.

随着我的职业转向教学，我更加思考大多数商业记者是如何进入这一行业的。为什么他们一开始就要对美国企业几乎一无所知呢？

<!--en-->
And as my career has transitioned into teaching, I have thought even more about how most business reporters get into the business. Why should they start off with little or no knowledge of corporate America?

答案是：他们本就不应该如此。公众有权从由知识渊博的记者撰写和编辑的各种大众传媒作品中获取关于商业世界的资讯，这些记者能够用任何人都能理解的方式向读者解释新闻的重要性。

<!--en-->
The answer is they shouldn’t. The public deserves to have information about the business world from all forms of mass communication written and edited by journalists who are knowledgeable and who can explain the significance of stories to consumers in a way anybody can understand.

然而，高等教育和大众传媒在培养适合从事商业新闻报道的记者方面表现得极为糟糕。2002年，塞尔泽公司与美国新闻协会及雷诺兹基金会共同进行的一项调查显示，没有一所新闻学院的负责人认为自己的课程在培养商业新闻领域的学生方面表现优异，只有28%的人认为他们的课程效果不错。而新闻机构的高管们则表示，招聘商业记者是最难找到合适人选的岗位；仅有38%的人认为商业新闻是他们新闻编辑室的重点工作，这反映出这一重要领域并未得到足够重视。ix x • 前言 全国的大学需要与大众传媒机构合作，提供更多关于商业新闻报道的培训和教育。在某些地区，这样的合作已经展开。密苏里大学、西北大学、哥伦比亚大学、波士顿大学等知名院校都设有商业新闻课程，此外伊利诺伊大学、纽约的巴鲁克学院以及华盛顿与李大学等也开设了相关课程。

<!--en-->
Yet higher education and mass communication have failed miserably in effectively training journalists for careers in business reporting. In a 2002 survey by Selzer & Co. for the American Press Institute and the Reynolds Foundation, not one journalism school administrator rated his or her program as doing an excellent job of training students for careers in business journalism. Only 28 percent said their program does a good job. And news executives say hiring business reporters is thehardest beat for which to find qualified workers; just 38 percent of them say that business is a high priority in their newsrooms, showing the lack of emphasis placed on this important field.
ix x • Preface
Universities and colleges across the country need to team with mass communication outlets to provide more training and teaching in business journalism. In some areas, this is happening. Business journalism programs exist at major schools such as the University of Missouri, Northwestern, Columbia, and Boston Universities, as well as others, including the University of Illinois, Baruch College in New York, and Washington & Lee University.

此外，报纸、杂志、电视台和网站也在不断派记者和编辑参加各种培训会议以获取经验和建议。美国商业编辑与作家协会，以及美国新闻协会和雷诺兹基金会，也在共同努力提升商业新闻领域的教育水平与知识储备。

<!--en-->
In addition, newspapers, magazines, TV stations, and Web sites are sending their reporters and editors to more and more conferences for training and tips. The Society of American Business Editors and Writers, along with the American Press Institute and the Reynolds Foundation, are also making concerted efforts to improve business journalism education and knowledge.

本书旨在为初入行的商业记者以及从业多年的记者提供指导。它涵盖了所有撰写商业相关报道的人都会遇到的重要主题和问题。书中首先简要介绍了商业新闻对所有人而言的重要性，随后教授读者每位商业记者都应该掌握的知识——从如何阅读公司的损益表和资产负债表，到在证券交易委员会（SEC）的公开文件中应注意什么。

<!--en-->
This book strives to be a guide for both the beginning business reporter and one who has worked the beat for years. It provides guidance on important topics and issues that everyone who writes a business-related story encounters. It starts off with a basic history lesson on the importance of business journalism to everyone, and then seeks to teach readers what every business reporter should know—from reading an income statement and balance sheet for a company to what to look for in Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) filings.

尽管已有其他书籍为商业记者提供帮助，但至今还没有一本专门指导他们如何撰写关于公司和经济的报道的指南。

<!--en-->
Although there have been other books to help business reporters along the way, there has never been a guide to show them specifically how to write stories about companies and the economy.

这些是我希望在1989年就拥有的技能。如今，商业记者再也不用在没有这些知识的情况下开始工作了。

<!--en-->
These are skills I wish I had back in 1989. Now, business journalists will not have to start their jobs without this knowledge.

虽然这本书主要是从报纸业务编辑的角度撰写的，但我也收录了来自电视、互联网和杂志领域的优秀商业新闻案例。书中讨论的所有报道技巧和方法都适用于任何媒体。

<!--en-->
Though this book is written primarily from the viewpoint of the newspaper business editor, I have also included examples of excellent business journalism from television, the Internet, and magazines. All of the reporting techniques and methods discussed herein are relevant to any media.

## 1

商业新闻比你想象得更有趣 一位肯塔基州报纸的前编辑喜欢讲述她的某位商业记者去采访当地一家管理式医疗公司Humana Incorporated首席执行官的故事。

<!--en-->
Business Journalism is More Fun than
You Think
A former editor of a Kentucky newspaper likes to tell the story of when one of her business reporters went to interview the CEO of Humana Incorporated, a locally based managed care company.

首席执行官开始谈论SEC。几分钟后，这位刚接触该领域的记者打断了他，问道：“打扰一下，东南联盟跟您的业务有什么关系？”

<!--en-->
The CEO began talking about the SEC. After several minutes, the reporter, who was new to the beat, interrupted the CEO and asked, “Excuse me, but what does the Southeastern Conference have to do with your business?”

首席执行官说的并不是那个从肯塔基州到佛罗里达州、参与从橄榄球到游泳等各种体育赛事的大学联盟，而是负责监管全国数千家公司的联邦机构——证券交易委员会。

<!--en-->
The CEO was not talking about the conference of universities from Kentucky to Florida that compete in sports ranging from football to swimming. He was talking about the Securities and Exchange Commission, the federal agency that regulates thousands of companies across the country.

商业报道与其他领域的报道并无不同。记者必须清楚自己要写什么、需要查找哪些文件以及使用哪些信息来源。尽管过去15年来商业新闻的质量有所提升，但仍有观点认为该领域的记者对其报道主题的了解并不充分。此外，一些商业记者和编辑不知道该去何处寻找所需信息，以便完成报道或让现有报道更加出色。还有些人不了解决定企业利润起伏的基本经济原理，更不用说理解股市与贸易关系对企业未来发展的影响了。

<!--en-->
Business reporting is just like reporting any other beat. You have to know what you are writing about, which documents to look for, and which sources to use. Even though the quality of business journalism has improved in the past 15 years, there are still concerns that reporters in the field are not fully knowledgeable about their topics. Also, some business reporters and editors do not know the appropriate place to look for the information they need to get the story or to make the story they already have even better. Still others do not understand the basic principles of economics that help a company's profits rise and fall, and even more do not understand the importance of the stock market and trade relations to a business's future prospects.

2008年和2009年，对商业新闻的批评声日益增多，因为有人指责该领域未能及时向消费者预警该十年后半段发生的经济危机。

<!--en-->
Criticism of business journalism increased in 2008 and 2009 as some blamed the field for failing to alert consumers to the economic crisis that occurred in the later part of the decade.

各种信息来源和文件有助于向消费者解释复杂的商业和经济话题。但记者同样需要将这些商业知识运用到实际工作中。正因如此，提升商业记者和编辑的知识水平将有助于他们在未来做得更好。

<!--en-->
Sources and documents can help explain complicated business and economic topics to consumers. But it is also important for reporters to take this knowledge of business and do something with it. That is why furthering the knowledge of business reporters and editors will help them do a better job in the future.

这会对未来的商业报道产生影响吗？人们只能希望其质量能够得到提高。2001年2月5日，《财富》杂志将恩龙公司……2 • 商业新闻比你想象中更有趣

<!--en-->

10. 《福布斯》杂志将该公司评为“美国最具创新力的公司”。在该杂志评选的“最受尊敬的公司”榜单中，该公司也位列第18名。诚然，安然公司确实具有创新性，或许还赢得了竞争对手及其他企业高管的赞赏。然而，《财富》杂志的持怀疑态度的记者贝瑟尼·麦克莱恩却相信一些消息来源告诉她的话：这家总部位于休斯顿的公司存在问题，它不值得赞赏，也不算有创新力，唯一可取之处或许只是擅长想出各种办法规避法律。她深入研究了该公司的财务文件，发现很难准确判断其盈利来源。“对于记者以及其他自认为精通业务的人而言，这是一个非常重要的教训：有时候最显而易见的问题恰恰就是关键问题，”麦克莱恩在采访中表示，“以安然为例：它是如何赚钱的？这个问题如此明显，以至于问出来都让人觉得自己很愚蠢。”（史密斯，2002年）尽管她的编辑们收到了公司管理层的抗议，且她在寻求信息时也被安然拒之门外，麦克莱恩仍继续深入调查，相关报道最终于2001年3月发表。到那年年底，该公司的财务状况已彻底恶化，安然不得不申请破产保护。那些读了麦克莱恩的文章并因她的报道而感到恐慌的人，很可能在股价约为80美元/股时卖出了手中的股票，从而节省了数百万美元。而那些坚持持有股票的人则损失惨重，因为这家公司早已不复存在。商业新闻报道，尤其是像安然这样复杂的案例，绝非易事。至少在本案中，复杂的会计手段以及未列入资产负债表的分公司，让除了那些最为怀疑且经验最丰富的商业记者之外，几乎无人察觉到安然的问题。不过，还是有一些线索的。那些注意到安然股价在前一年出现剧烈上涨的商业记者本应发现，这一上涨趋势与市场其他部分的走势完全相反。2000年的前九个月，安然的股价翻了一番多，但其营收和利润并未跟上如此强劲的增长速度。根据基本的经济规律，从长远来看，大多数公司的股价上升速度应与其营收和利润的增长速度保持一致。这些正是可能表明存在问题的线索。如果一位思维敏锐的商业记者能进行这样的简单分析，很可能会发现危险信号并进一步深入调查该公司。然而，当时报道安然的记者中很少有人能建立起这样的关联。虽然揭露安然的困境远比单纯比较股价要复杂得多，但安然的成功表现与市场其他部分走势之间的反差本应成为揭示更深层问题的第一个信号。可以说，有些记者并不理解一家公司的财务表现与其股价之间的关系，这本应促使他们质疑安然的运作方式。“在它最辉煌的时期，商业新闻界简直就是那只不会叫的狗——那只不起作用的看门犬，”担任《福布斯》杂志编辑38年的吉姆·迈克尔斯如此说道。（巴恩哈特，2002年）许多安然高管正在抛售公司股票，这一情况已被众多通讯社记者报道。对于了解其中含义的记者来说，这些对安然未来前景极为熟悉的高管们若认为股价短期内不会上涨，这一事实本身就应该引起他们的警觉。至少对于那些愿意花时间学习的记者而言，识别这些行为及其他相关迹象并将其串联起来，形成一篇能让读者了解企业相关情况的报道，并非难事。 商业新闻比你想象中更有趣 • 3 股市已从历史最高点下跌超过25%，数十家公司在剧烈崩盘中倒闭。许多人将2000年和2001年的华尔街泡沫，以及2008年和2009年衍生品和次级抵押贷款对经济造成的深远影响归咎于商业记者。为何媒体没能更好地揭露恩龙、世界通信和阿德尔菲亚等公司的丑闻呢？答案是他们本可以做到，尽管这些公司倒闭的恶行并非记者的过错。但商业记者可以从过去的错误中吸取教训。让商业记者写出更好作品的最佳方式之一，就是为他们提供培训，帮助他们理解所报道事件的重要性。虽然如今商业版块的报道和写作水平已远超三十年前，但仍有一些内容缺乏必要的背景解释，难以帮助本地读者更好地理解商业对他们生活的意义。因此，那些希望获取优质商业新闻的精明读者开始放弃本地报纸，转而选择能提供深度报道的网站。对于那些努力维持发行量和收视率的报纸、杂志和电视台而言，道理很明确：要想留住商业新闻的受众，就需要更广泛、更深入的报道。在如今这个人人都想了解经济状况的时代，这一目标尤为重要。主要问题似乎在于那些未能充分理解商业问题和复杂经济话题的报道与编辑团队。很少有商业记者和编辑拥有相关商业学位，也很少有人接受过关于如何报道企业和经济的培训。由于过去二十年对商业新闻报道的需求急剧增长，记者和编辑们仓促涉足这一领域。*旧金山纪事报*的媒体专栏作家丹·福斯特在2002年初指出：“许多记者在仅具备基本资产负债表阅读能力的情况下就转行了”（Fost, 2002, p. G1）。其结果便是报道流于表面，有时甚至完全偏离主题。个人财经编辑克里斯·普默在CBSMarketWatch.com上表示：“商业新闻在股市崩溃前还夸大股价，直到灾难已经发生才发出警示，还对企业腐败的严重程度一无所知。”根据2002年春夏刊《报纸研究期刊》上的一篇文章，解决之道在于加强培训和教育。在对西海岸报纸的商业编辑和记者进行的研究中，几乎所有人都认为“商业记者和编辑需要接受商业和经济方面的课程或培训，以获得工作所需的工具”。该研究还指出，受访者“也强调，不仅商业记者，所有记者都需要具备基本的商业经济学知识”（Ludwig, 2002, p. 139）。提升记者和编辑对商业和经济学的理解，能够提高他们关于企业决策和经济因素如何影响全球读者日常生活的报道质量，帮助读者做出更明智的财务和生活决策。

2. *The New York Times* business section
3. *BusinessWeek* magazine
4. *Fortune* magazine

Corporation the “Most Innovative Company in America.” The company also placed 18th overall in the magazine’s list of “Most Admired Companies” in the country.
To be sure, Enron was innovative and perhaps even admired by competitors and other corporate executives. However, a skeptical *Fortune* reporter, Bethany McLean, believed what some sources were telling her: Something was amiss at the Houston-based company, and it was not to be admired or considered innovative, except in finding creative ways to skirt the law. She dug into the company’s financial filings and discovered that it was hard to determine exactly where the company was making money.
“It’s a really important lesson for reporters to keep in mind, as well as other supposedly sophisticated people, that sometimes the most obvious question really is the question,” said McLean in an interview. “In Enron’s case: How do you make money? It’s such an obvious question that you almost feel stupid asking it” (Smith, 2002).
Despite her editors receiving protests from company management and being turned away by Enron when she asked for information, McLean continued researching her story, which ran in March 2001. By the end of the year, the company’s financial performance had unraveled, and Enron filed for bankruptcy court protection. People who read McLean’s article and became scared by what she reported likely sold their stock in the company at around $80 per share, saving themselves millions. Those that held onto their shares lost everything, as the company no longer exists.
Business reporting, particularly on stories as complicated as that of Enron, is not easy. At least in this case, arcane accounting techniques and subsidiaries excluded from its balance sheet hid Enron’s problems from all but the most skeptical and expert business journalist. There were clues, however. Business reporters who watched the dramatic rise in Enron’s stock price the previous year should have noticed that that increase was in direct opposition to how the rest of the market was performing. In the first nine months of 2000, Enron’s stock more than doubled, but its revenues and profits did not match that strong growth rate. It is a basic economic principle that in the long run, most companies see their stock price rise at the same rate as their revenue and profits. These were clues that maybe something was not right.
A critically minded business reporter making this simple analysis would likely have seen the red flags and investigated the company more closely. Yet, few covering Enron at the time made such a connection. Though uncovering Enron’s troubles became far more complicated than just comparing stock prices, the discontinuity between Enron’s success and the performance of the rest of the market should have been the first indicator of deeper problems. Arguably, some reporters did not understand how a company’s financial performance is related to its stock price, which should have led them to question Enron’s tactics.
“Business journalism in what has been its glory days has been the dog that didn’t bark—the watchdog that didn’t bark,” said Jim Michaels, editor of *Forbes* magazine for 38 years (Barnhart, 2002). Many Enron executives were selling their company stock, a story tracked by numerous wire service reporters. This should tell a reporter who understands the significance that these executives, who had an intimate knowledge of Enron’s future prospects, did not think the stock price wasgoing to get higher anytime soon. It is not that hard for reporters, at least those willing to take the time to learn, to recognize what these and other actions mean and to connect the dots into a story that tells the reader what he or she needs to know about a business.
Business Journalism is More Fun than You Think • 3
The stock market has dropped more than 25 percent from its all-time high, and dozens of companies have failed in spectacular crashes. Many blame business journalists for the Wall Street bubble of 2000 and 2001 and for failing to understand the significant effect of derivatives and sub-prime mortgages on the economy in 2008 and 2009. Why couldn't the media have done a better job in uncovering Enron, WorldCom, and Adelphia, to name a few? The answer is they could have, although journalists are not to blame for the misdeeds that caused these and other companies to fail. But business reporters can learn lessons from what went wrong in the past. One of the best ways for business journalists to produce better work is to give them training that will enable them to understand the significance of the events they are writing about.
Although reporting and writing in business sections is much better than it was three decades ago, some of it still lacks the contextualization that would help local readers better understand what business means to them. As a result, savvy readers who want good business news are eschewing their local newspapers for Internet sites that provide the in-depth coverage they want. For newspapers, magazines, and television stations struggling to keep circulation and viewership up, the message is clear: To retain consumers of business news, more breadth and depth of coverage is needed. This goal is especially important during times like today, when everyone wants to know what is happening with the economy.
The chief problem appears to be reporting and editing staffs that do not fully understand business issues and complicated economic topics. Few business reporters and editors have business-related degrees, and few have been trained in how to cover corporations and the economy. Because of the rapid demand for business news coverage in the past two decades, reporters and editors were thrown into the topic. “Many reporters made the switch with only a rudimentary understanding of how to read a balance sheet,” noted *San Francisco Chronicle* media columnist Dan Fost in early 2002 (Fost, 2002, p. G1).
The result has been shallow reporting that sometimes misses the point entirely. Business journalism “pumped up stocks before the market collapsed, failed to sound a bear alarm until the mauling was well underway, and [was] ignorant to the scope of corporate corruption,” said personal finance editor Chris Pummer (2002) on CBSMarketWatch.com.
The solution, according to an article in the Spring/Summer 2002 *Newspaper Research Journal*, is better training and education. In a study of West Coast newspaper business editors and reporters, nearly all agreed that “business reporters and editors need classes or training in business and economics to provide them with the tools necessary for their work.” The study added that those surveyed “were also emphatic that a basic understanding of business economics isn’t necessary just for business journalists, but for all journalists” (Ludwig, 2002, p. 139). Improving reporters’ and editors’ understanding of business and economics can strengthen the quality of their writing about how corporate decisions and economic factors impact everyday life for readers around the world, allowing readers to make more informed decisions about their money and their lives.
