4 • Business Journalism is More Fun than You Think
Imagine you walk into your local McDonald's today and buy a hamburger. That simple purchase ultimately affects the company's profits, in turn, affecting the performance of dozens of competitors, including Burger King and Wendy's. All of these companies have spent money on advertising and developing products in an attempt to woo you into their restaurants. But imagine money is tight, and you decide instead to go purchase hamburger meat and buns at your local grocery store. Your economic decision still impacts these companies. You are also affecting the financial results of the grocery store and of the company that processed the meat. Your decision to drive to the grocery store or the restaurant affects still other companies. What gas station did you buy fuel at to allow you to make that trip? What influenced your decision to purchase the car you are driving?
We are just talking about one decision about eating lunch. Imagine all of the other decisions that you and other consumers make each day, and think how those decisions affect the local and national economies and the performance of the companies whose goods, products, and services you are or are not purchasing. Now, how are you going to explain the effect of all of those decisions to readers of your local newspaper, viewers of the evening news, or listeners of your radio station?

### 商业新闻的历史

<!--en-->
*The History of Business Journalism*

商业新闻对美国以及数以百万计通过购买各类商品、产品和服务与企业日常互动的民众产生了深远影响。

<!--en-->
Business journalism has had a profound effect on the United States and the millions of people who interact with companies on an everyday basis by purchasing their goods, products, and services.

美国的早期定居者依靠报纸获取农作物和牲畜的价格信息，以及哪些船只进港及其装载的货物情况。到了19世纪，专门报道商业新闻的报纸应运而生。《商业杂志》创刊于1827年，《华尔街日报》则诞生于1889年。不过这一时期商业新闻领域一些最重要的报道其实发表在主流报纸上。

<!--en-->
Early settlers in America depended on newspapers to provide them with details of crop and livestock prices and information about which ships had entered the port and the goods they contained. By the nineteenth century, newspapers devoted solely to business news were established. *The Journal of Commerce* began in 1827. *The Wall Street Journal* came along in 1889. But some of the most important stories in business journalism during this time ran in mainstream papers.

19世纪50年代末，《纽约论坛报》的霍勒斯·格里利积极推动修建连接东西部的铁路。他的报道是当时首次大力推动整合这个不断发展的国家各区域经济的举措。格里利还撰写了关于需要低价宅基地的文章，这也是美国经济发展的另一个重要方面。十年后，《纽约太阳报》揭露了参与修建第一条横贯大陆铁路的建筑公司实际上是由那些铁路公司自己成立的，它们实质上是与自己签订合同，并通过以低价向国会议员出售公司股票来收买他们的沉默。这篇报道引发了美国国会针对企业的首次重大调查，也为后来对安然、世界通信等公司的调查埋下了伏笔。

<!--en-->
In the late 1850s, Horace Greeley of the *New York Tribune* pushed for a railroad that would connect the East and the West. His stories were the first major push to combine the regional economies of a growing country. Greeley also wrote about the need for low-cost homestead lands, another important development in the U.S. economy. A decade later, the *New York Sun* exposed how the construction company that helped build the first intercontinental railroad had been formed by the railroad companies themselves, who were essentially making contracts with themselves and bribing members of Congress to keep quiet by selling them shares in the company at a discounted price. The story led to the first major Congressional investigation into a corporation, foreshadowing later hearings on the downfall of Enron, WorldCom, and others.

报纸也影响了政府对企业监管的方式。就在格里利推动铁路建设的同一时期，纽约的另一份报纸《弗兰克·莱斯利的插图报》揭露了劣质牛奶正在危害儿童生命的问题。这篇文章促使监管机构出台了禁止销售劣质牛奶的法律。这起牛奶丑闻并非新闻界首次针对企业或公司的调查。在整个19世纪90年代末和20世纪初，许多报纸都派记者去调查企业是如何影响人们生活的。1899年，《芝加哥每日论坛报》开始刊登相关报道，指出每年用于庆祝独立日的鞭炮及其他爆炸物都在造成人员伤亡。这些报道促使政府对烟花的生产和销售制定了更多限制措施。

<!--en-->
Newspapers also influenced how government regulated business. Around the same time Greeley was pushing for a railroad, another newspaper in New York, *Frank Leslie's Illustrated Newspaper*, exposed how bad milk was killing children. The article pushed regulators into passing laws banning swill milk. The milk exposé was not the first in journalism that took aim at a business or corporation. Throughout the late 1890s and the early part of the twentieth century, many newspapers directed reporters to investigate how companies were affecting thelives of people. In 1899, the *Chicago Daily Tribune* began publishing stories about how firecrackers and other explosives sold to celebrate the Fourth of July were killing people every year. Its stories led to restrictions on how fireworks were manufactured and sold.

商业新闻比你想象中更有趣 • 5 最著名的推动企业改革的商业新闻案例包括厄普顿·辛克莱所著的小说《丛林》，该书揭露了肉类加工业的不卫生状况；以及艾达·塔贝尔在《麦克卢尔》杂志上发表的文章，这些文章揭示了标准石油公司如何迫使竞争对手倒闭。在读完辛克莱的小说后，西奥多·罗斯福下令展开调查，最终促使1906年通过了《纯净食品与药品法》和《肉类检验法》。1911年，美国最高法院下令拆分标准石油公司。世纪之交后，《麦克卢尔》杂志上的其他文章又抨击了铁路行业，这促使出台了限制铁路运输货物收费的法律。1906年发表在《世界杂志》上的一篇关于童工问题的文章，帮助杜绝了全国范围内工厂对未成年工人的剥削行为。

<!--en-->
Business Journalism is More Fun than You Think • 5
The most famous examples of business journalism that led to business operation reforms are Upton Sinclair's novel *The Jungle*, which documented the unsanitary conditions of the meat-packing industry, and Ida Tarbell's *McClure's* magazine articles about how Standard Oil had forced its competitors out of business. After reading Sinclair's novel, Theodore Roosevelt ordered an investigation that culminated in the passing of the Pure Food and Drugs Act and the Meat Inspection Act in 1906. And in 1911, the U.S. Supreme Court ordered Standard Oil to be split up. After the turn of the century other articles in *McClure's* attacked the railroad industry, which led to laws limiting shipping charges on goods and products transported by rail. In *Cosmopolitan*, a 1906 article about child labor helped discontinue the abuse of young workers in factories across the country.

记者们也将目光转向了投资领域。1920年，《波士顿邮报》揭露了当地金融专家查尔斯·庞齐的金融欺诈行为——他向投资者承诺高额回报。在这些报道的基础上，庞齐被捕并被定罪，还曾入狱服刑。当然，他的名字至今仍存在于商业界，“庞氏骗局”这一术语如今被用来指代任何那种用其他投资者的资金支付给现有投资者的非法金字塔骗局，比如最近有关前纽约投资者伯纳德·麦道夫的报道。

<!--en-->
Journalists also turned their attention to investments. In 1920, the *Boston Post* uncovered the financial wrongdoings of Charles Ponzi, a local financial expert who promised huge returns to investors. Ponzi was arrested and convicted based on the articles and spent time in prison. His name, of course, lives on in the business world, as the term Ponzi scheme is now used to refer to any illegal pyramid scheme in which investors are paid with money from other investors, such as in the recent reporting of former New York investor Bernard Madoff.

近年来，各类出版物通过向消费者普及知识，引导他们购买更安全的产品，从而推动了生活条件的改善。例如，《读者文摘》虽然如今并不以报道重大新闻或引领社会运动而闻名，但它却是最早揭露吸烟潜在危害并将其与癌症联系起来的大众媒体。1952年12月发表的那篇文章被认为引发了反吸烟辩论，并迫使香烟行业承认其产品具有危害性。

<!--en-->
More recently, publications have led the way to improved living conditions by educating consumers, thereby leading them to purchase safer products. For example, *Reader's Digest*, not known today for breaking stories or leading causes, was the first broad publication to expose the potential dangers of smoking and link it to cancer. The December 1952 article is credited with starting the antismoking debate and forcing the cigarette industry to admit its products were harmful.

1959年4月，著名的消费者权益倡导者拉尔夫·纳德在《国家》杂志上发表了一篇文章，由此开始了他对汽车安全问题的调查，这项调查最终促成了新的联邦法规的出台，要求在大多数车辆上配备安全带、进行召回、开展碰撞测试并安装安全气囊。当有消息称通用汽车公司雇佣私家侦探跟踪纳德时，他的主张获得了更多支持。

<!--en-->
With an article in *The Nation* in April 1959, well-known consumer advocate Ralph Nader began his investigation into automobile safety that eventually led to new federal regulations requiring seat belts, recalls, crash tests, and air bags in most vehicles. His argument gained clout after it was disclosed that General Motors Corporation hired private investigators to track Nader.

20世纪60年代，《得梅因纪事报》刊登的系列文章促使国会堵上了监管漏洞，这些漏洞曾让患病的动物被加工成肉类并在杂货店出售。1977年，《母亲琼斯》杂志上的一篇文章让读者意识到了驾驶平托汽车的危险——由于其油箱设计缺陷，这种汽车在从后方受到撞击时极易发生爆炸。这篇文章导致了福特汽车公司的这款汽车被召回并停产。二十多年后，休斯顿KHOU电视台的一名记者发现福特SUV与火石轮胎之间存在频繁的碰撞事故模式。相关的报道促使数百万条轮胎被召回。

<!--en-->
In the 1960s, the *Des Moines Register* printed articles that led to Congress closing loopholes in inspections that allowed for diseased animals to be turned into meat sold in grocery stores. A 1977 article in *Mother Jones* exposed readers to the dangers of driving a Pinto, which, because of its poorly designed fuel tank, easily exploded when hit from behind. The article led to a recall of the Ford Motor Company's car and the end of its production. More than two decades later, a television reporter at KHOU in Houston found an unsettling pattern of crashes involving Ford SUVs and Firestone tires. The resulting coverage led to the recall of millions of tires.

这些文章都是由那些理解商业在社会中重要性的记者经过调研后撰写的，他们毫无保留地揭露了各种问题。其中一些记者并未接受过专门的企业运营培训，但他们通过学习掌握了企业运作及盈利方式的关键信息，从而将坚持不懈的报道转化为改变经济与人们生活的故事。这正是当今商业记者需要努力达到的标准。在过去的100年里，还有许多其他记者和编辑推动了商业新闻的发展，将报道与撰写企业及经济相关内容的艺术形式发展成了过去20年来最重要的新闻类型之一。

<!--en-->
These articles were all researched and written by reporters who understood the importance of business in society and exposed the problems, warts and all. Some of these reporters were not specifically trained in understanding how businesses operate but learned the vital information about how companies work and how they make money, thus turning dogged reporting into stories that changed our economy and our lives. That is the standard that today's business reporters needto strive to match. Many other reporters and editors have changed business journalism during the last 100 years, evolving the art of reporting and writing about companies and the economy into arguably the most important journalism of the last 20 years.

6 • 商业新闻比你想象中更有趣 《商业周刊》创刊于1929年，就在导致大萧条的股市崩盘发生前的几周。《财富》杂志则由《时代》杂志的创始人亨利·卢斯在一年后创办。在这两家杂志以及《福布斯》的共同作用下，接下来的七十年里，它们以杂志形式定义了商业新闻，刊登了大量关于各个行业、华尔街以及劳工问题的长篇报道——这些都是让读者全面了解商业对国家影响的重点话题。

<!--en-->
6 • Business Journalism is More Fun than You Think
*BusinessWeek* magazine was founded in 1929, just weeks before the stock market crash that led to the Great Depression. *Fortune* magazine, created by *Time* founder Henry Luce, followed a year later. Both publications, along with *Forbes*, spent the next seven decades defining business journalism in a magazine format, printing long articles about industries, Wall Street, and labor—all important topics that gave readers a broad understanding of the effects of business on the country.

新的、有趣的报道风格也应运而生。1935年，西尔维娅·F·波特开始在《纽约邮报》上撰写财经新闻专栏。她的写作为个人理财报道奠定了标准，用通俗的语言向读者解释如何管理他们辛苦赚来的钱，这一成就使她于1960年登上了《时代》杂志的封面。在事业巅峰时期，波特的专栏在全球450多家报纸上刊载，她的风格也培养出了其他知名的个人理财作家，如简·布赖恩特·奎因和凯西·克里斯托夫，她们至今仍在为数百万人提供实用的基础个人理财建议。若没有这些记者，许多人可能永远无法理解401(k)计划是如何运作的，也无法区分成长型股票与价值型股票。

<!--en-->
New and interesting reporting styles also developed. In 1935, Sylvia F. Porter began writing a column in the *New York Post* on financial news. Her writing defined personal finance reporting, explaining to readers in simple terms how they should take care of their hard-earned money, and it landed her on the cover of *Time* in 1960. At the height of her career, Porter's column ran in more than 450 newspapers around the world, and her style spawned other well-known personal finance writers, such as Jane Bryant Quinn and Kathy Kristof, who today continue the tradition of bringing sound, basic personal finance advice to millions. Without these reporters, many people would have never understood how a 401(k) plan works or the difference between growth and value stocks.

1941年，32岁的巴尼·基尔戈尔接管了《华尔街日报》，将这份原本主要服务于纽约市少量订阅者的报纸逐步打造成了每天都在发布全球顶尖商业新闻的国际性报纸。被誉为现代商业新闻之父的基尔戈尔将一份财经报纸转变成了阐释劳动力、资本与企业之间关系的刊物。“他还认为，那些需要处理这些问题的人会青睐这样一份能深入、客观地报道他们所处世界各种状况的报纸，”该报的所有者道琼斯公司的首席执行官彼得·坎恩说道（Kann, 2000, p. 1）。基尔戈尔接手时，该报有41,000名订阅者；到1967年他去世时，其发行量已超过110万份。自1977年起，它每个工作日的销量都高于美国其他任何报纸。基尔戈尔明白，最好的商业报道应当面向最广泛的受众——银行家需要了解的经济信息，与希望从银行借款的消费者所需的信息并无不同；经验丰富的华尔街投资者需要了解股市下跌的原因，其表达方式应简单到乔治亚州托马斯维尔的祖母也能理解。富兰克林·德拉诺·罗斯福极为信赖基尔戈尔的描述能力，以至于他告诉那些试图理解新社会保障体系经济原理的记者：“去问问基尔戈尔吧。”

<!--en-->
In 1941, Barney Kilgore took control of the *Wall Street Journal* at the age of 32 and turned a newspaper that basically catered to a small subscriber base in New York City into an international newspaper that day in and day out publishes the best business journalism in the world. Kilgore, considered the father of modern business journalism, took a financial newspaper and turned it into a publication that explained the relationship between labor, capital, and enterprise. “He also believed that those who had to deal with these problems would value a newspaper that informed them in depth and without sensation about the world they live in in all its variety,” said Peter Kann, CEO of Dow Jones & Company, the newspaper's owner (Kann, 2000, p. 1). When Kilgore began running the paper, it had 41,000 subscribers. By the time he died in 1967, it had a circulation of more than 1.1 million. And since 1977, it has sold more copies each business day than any other paper in the United States. Kilgore understood that the best business reporting was written for the broadest audience possible. A banker needed to understand the same information about the economy as did a consumer wanting to borrow money from the bank. A seasoned Wall Street investor needed to know why the stock market was falling in the same simple terms that a grandmother in Thomasville, Georgia, could comprehend. Franklin Delano Roosevelt so trusted Kilgore's descriptive ability that he told other reporters attempting to understand the economics of the new Social Security system to “go ask Kilgore.”

1970年，路易斯·鲁基瑟开始在公共电视台主持节目《华尔街周刊》。这是第一档专门面向数百万观众、内容仅围绕股市和经济展开的节目。该节目成为了了解华尔街如何影响普通民众生活的标准电视节目，也为后来诸如彭博电视、CNBC和福克斯商业网络等只报道商业和经济领域的电视节目及频道奠定了基础。如今，全世界的观众都觉得在办公室里打开CNBC并全天播放毫无不妥。二十年前，要是有人想一直观看专门播放商业新闻的电视频道，那只会让他赶紧去度假；而现在，这已几乎成为社会大部分群体的常态。

<!--en-->
In 1970, Louis Rukeyser began hosting *Wall Street Week* on public television. It became the first show broadcast to millions of viewers that discussed nothing but the stock market and the economy. The program became the standard television show for understanding how Wall Street affected Main Street and was the precursor of other television shows and even networks such as Bloomberg Television, CNBC, and Fox Business Network that now report exclusively about business and the economy. Viewers around the world now think nothing of turning on CNBCin their offices and leaving it on all day. Two decades ago, the mere thought of someone who wanted to constantly watch a television network devoted solely to business news would have earned that person a well-earned vacation. Now, it is considered almost standard for large segments of society.

商业新闻比你想象得更有趣 • 7 即使在今天，商业新闻的形式仍在不断演变。国际通讯社彭博新闻虽成立仅十多年，但其对华尔街和企业的密集报道迫使其他媒体更加重视日常新闻报道。道琼斯和路透社也是重要竞争者，它们与彭博争夺最新的商业新闻。在很多方面，商业新闻已经变得即时化，几乎能瞬间传递给我们。例如，《华尔街日报》对并购事件的报道，往往能在官方宣布之前就抢先报道许多重大交易，这极大地改变了其他媒体撰写商业交易报道的风格和结构。

<!--en-->
Business Journalism is More Fun than You Think • 7
Even today, the shape of business journalism continues to evolve. Bloomberg News, an international wire service, is slightly more than a decade old, but its aggressive coverage of Wall Street and corporations has forced others to pay more attention to daily coverage. Dow Jones and Reuters are also major players, competing against Bloomberg for breaking business news stories. In many ways, business news has become immediate, supplied to us almost instantaneously. For example, the *Journal's* coverage of mergers and acquisitions, breaking many big deals before they were officially announced, has significantly changed the style and structure of how others write about business deals.

越来越多带有浓厚商业色彩的报道正在赢得普利策奖。1999年，《俄勒冈人报》的一位记者通过追踪从美国运往亚洲的冷冻薯条，阐述了亚洲经济衰退对太平洋西北地区的影响，因此获得了普利策奖。在主流新闻奖项评选中获奖的新闻作品数量不断增加，这证明了商业新闻在各地报纸中的重要性。

<!--en-->
Increasingly, reporting with strong business overtones is winning Pulitzer Prizes. In 1999, a reporter for *The Oregonian* in Portland won a Pulitzer Prize for explaining the effect of the Asian economic downturn on the Pacific Northwest by tracing shipments of frozen French fries from the United States to Asia. The increasing number of stories winning awards in mainstream journalism prize competitions validates the importance of business journalism in newspapers around the country.

商业新闻业正在安慰那些受苦的人，同时伤害那些安逸的人。有意从事这一领域的初学者需要了解商业新闻业的来龙去脉、发展历程以及未来走向。商业新闻业带来了诸多成就与进步，我们应当为此心存感激。随着商业成为人们日常生活中的重要焦点，商业记者在媒体界和社会中的作用也愈发重要。

<!--en-->
Business journalism is comforting the afflicted and afflicting the comfortable. Budding students interested in the field need to understand the ins and outs of business journalism, where it has come from, and where it is headed. There have been numerous successes and advances as a result of business journalism, and for that we should all be thankful. As business has become a major focus of everyday life, the role of the business journalist has become increasingly more important to both media and society.

## 成功与失败

<!--en-->
*Hits and Misses*

尽管以商业和经济为主题的报道为社会带来了诸多进步与影响，但商业新闻业也必须为过去和现在世界上的一些问题承担相应责任。

<!--en-->
Yet for all of the advancements and impact brought upon society by reporting and writing that has focused on business and the economy, business journalism must also rightly take the blame for some of the problems in the world, past and present.

就在揭发者揭露肉类加工厂的不卫生状况及垄断行为的同时，企业们开始寻求专家帮助以应对媒体。这些公关领域的先驱为商业新闻业带来了新的变化。在报纸报道中遭到抨击的CEO们需要找到回应方式。20世纪初，通用电气和通用汽车等大型企业聘请公关专家来回答媒体提问，并试图让记者相信这些营利性企业并不像许多人认为的那样邪恶。第二次世界大战后，随着经济的发展，公关岗位数量大幅增加。公关专业人士的任务就是向媒体宣传企业所做的积极事迹。

<!--en-->
At the same time that the muckrakers were exposing unsanitary conditions in meatpacking plants and monopolistic business practices, companies were turning to experts to help them deal with the media. These forebears of public relations professionals brought a new twist to business journalism. CEOs attacked in newspaper stories wanted a way to respond. In the early twentieth century, major corporations such as General Electric and General Motors hired public relations experts to answer questions from the media and to try to persuade reporters that these for-profit businesses were not as evil as many believed. After World War II, public relations jobs proliferated as the economy grew. The task of public relations professionals was to tell the media the good things that their companies were doing.

从某种程度上说，公关行业的兴起导致了商业新闻业的整体衰退。在20世纪50年代和60年代，报纸的商务版块成了安置那些无法胜任报道市政或州政府事务的记者的地方。资深记者则被派去负责资源相关报道。每位商业记者都应掌握以下内容，此外还有一本书：

<!--en-->
In a way, the rise in public relations led to an overall down period for business journalism. In the 1950s and 1960s, the business desk became a place where newspapers put reporters who could not hack it covering city hall or state government. Older reporters were put out to pasture with an assignment to cover
Resources every business journalist should have, beside this book:

1. 《理解财务报表：记者指南》。这本书由芝加哥金融专家杰伊·塔帕里亚撰写，语言通俗易懂。
2. 订阅《华尔街日报》。这是最优秀的商业报道，每日更新。要想做到最好，就必须阅读最好的内容。
3. 能够使用彭博终端。这台设备可以提供丰富的数据来增强报道质量，还能帮助获取全球各地消息来源的联系方式。
4. 《24天：两位《华尔街日报》记者如何揭露摧毁美国企业信任的谎言》一书，详细讲述了记者们是如何报道上世纪最大企业倒闭事件背后的真相的。
5. 美国商业编辑与作家协会的会员资格。该协会举办各种研讨会和会议，让商业记者能够向行业内的同行学习。8 • 商业新闻比你想象的要有趣得多。除少数例外情况外，商业报道往往被越南战争和种族骚乱等事件的报道所掩盖。20世纪80年代和90年代的情况稍好一些：随着记者和编辑经验的积累，商业新闻的质量有所提升，但重要的新闻事件仍被忽视，而且商业报道也遭受了一些打击。20世纪80年代初，福斯特·威南斯在《华尔街日报》上撰写了广受欢迎的“街头传闻”专栏，这些报道会透露专业投资者对某些股票的看涨或看跌态度。威南斯在文章发表前就泄露信息，最终被捕并入狱服刑。十年后，著名的商业专栏作家丹·多夫曼因在其他媒体报道指出其与投资者关系密切后，未能向编辑披露消息而被《金钱》杂志解雇。在此期间，很少有记者会提醒读者即将到来的问题。1987年10月初，没有任何醒目的头条呼吁投资者在股市下跌前撤资。又过十年后，各类商业版面和杂志用如今看来荒谬的措辞赞扬安然公司的管理。在《达拉斯晨报》的一则标题中，安然被称为“全球电子商务领域的领头羊”（North, 2002）；《休斯顿商业杂志》的一名记者写道：“安然展现出了公认的创新能力，这种能力不断为其创造新的收入来源、潜在利润以及更多资本”（North, 2002）。这种吹捧并非仅限于为本地企业摇旗呐喊的本地媒体，就连那些自诩为报道新兴行业和企业专家的杂志和刊物也未能及时向读者通报存在的问题。《时代欧洲》的商业编辑、曾任职于《工业标准》的詹姆斯·莱德贝特表示：“这些新兴的杂志和网站往往只是盲目欢呼的啦啦队，一味追捧高管和创新企业，却从不质疑他们的账目。例如，在2000年之前在这些刊物的数据库中搜索‘安然’这个词，你会发现几乎全是对其市场创新的赞美之词”（Ledbetter, 2003, p. A17）。就连备受推崇的大众媒体也未能履行其监督职责。《纽约时报》将安然的总裁称为“创意机器”（Salpukas, 1999, p. C1）。经济杂志《挑战》的编辑杰弗里·马迪克说：“媒体不仅错过了安然丑闻，甚至还主动助长了这一丑闻的产生。它不仅没有看清安然那些极其复杂的合作结构中的种种问题，反而将其优点夸大到几乎超越所有企业。《财富》杂志连续五六年将安然评为最具创新力的公司，想必从未核实过其账目”（Madick, 2003, p. 3）。即便当大众媒体调查严重的商业问题时，比如1996年3月《纽约时报》推出的系列报道，试图探讨在经济强劲增长的情况下为何全国仍有民众失业，依然存在诸多漏洞。该系列报道做出了错误的断言，比如称经济无法培养出能长期从事同一工作的劳动者，称失业者更难找到新工作，以及称新创造的就业岗位多为低薪服务类工作，而非高薪制造业岗位。 商业新闻比你想象中更有趣 • 9 “20世纪90年代商业报道的问题并非记者不够聪明，无法揭露腐败行为，”查尔斯·莱顿在2003年3月的《美国新闻评论》中写道。“阅读过去半十年的相关报道，人们会惊讶于某些记者确实揭露了多少问题。但即便在他们所在的新闻机构内部，他们的见解也淹没在大量天真的报道声中——这些报道让我们误以为整个体系是健全的，分析师、审计师和CEO基本上都是值得信赖的，市场繁荣还将持续下去”（莱顿，2003年，第22页）。近年来，商业记者不得不回答一些棘手的问题：为何他们未能在2008年由房地产市场价格虚高等问题引发的经济危机爆发时及时警告消费者。然而，对过去十年报道内容的回顾显示，这次商业记者和编辑的表现有所改善。他们撰写了大量关于房地产泡沫的文章，并警告华尔街公司面临衍生品带来的风险。哈佛商学院前教授格雷戈里·米勒发现，企业中发现的会计违规行为中，近三分之一最初是由商业记者发现的。尽管如此，仍有一些重大事件被忽视，包括前述的麦道夫丑闻——在罪行被揭露的三年前，就有线人将相关文件交给了《华尔街日报》的一名记者，但该报道直到起诉后才得以刊登。既然商业报道中开始出现现实因素，那么商业记者的工作质量依然得不到认可也就不足为奇了，尤其是那些经常阅读商业版面的企业高管们。即便在新闻编辑部及记者群体中，商业报道仍被视为知识和专业能力相对薄弱的领域。在路易斯·哈里斯1992年进行的一项调查中，46%的高管对商业新闻的整体质量评价为负面；另有17%的高管认为自1967年以来商业新闻的质量实际上有所下降。在同一项调查中，超过四分之三的高管以及几乎相同比例的新闻学学者都认为，媒体过度侧重于“人物特写”，即撰写关于CEO的故事。只有34%的记者同意这一观点，因此这类报道往往将后来因公司经营不善而倒台的CEO塑造成英雄形象。但最能说明问题的数据是：92%的高管以及72%的记者和新闻学学者都担心记者对其报道对象的业务了解不足。两年后，自由论坛第一修正案中心发布了一项名为《标题与实质：商业界与新闻媒体之间的互不信任》的研究。该研究发现，超过三分之二的记者认为自己在商业报道的技术细节上没有犯错，但超过四分之三的高管却持相反观点（哈格蒂和拉斯穆森，1994年，第12页）。此外，同一项调查还显示，近一半的记者认为自己的商业报道培训不够充分，而10名高管中有7人坚信记者缺乏所需的商业背景知识（哈格蒂和拉斯穆森，1994年，第10页）。十年后，关于商业新闻价值的许多原有态度和看法依然存在。2000年，塞尔泽公司为雷诺兹基金会和美国新闻协会开展的一项调查得出结论：美国的企业领袖对大多数日报的商业报道质量并不满意，认为商业记者根本不了解企业的运作方式。 该报告指出：“他们不会提出深入探究本质的问题，因此他们的报道无法提供企业领导者所需的详细信息”（Selzer, 2000, 第2页）。10 • 商业新闻比你想象中更有趣。调查还发现，当新闻编辑部的高管对五种报道主题进行评分时，负责商业领域的记者得分最低，而且新闻编辑部在资源分配上也较少重视商业新闻——尽管许多优秀的、甚至是出色的商业新闻作品已经帮助读者理解复杂问题，并预警未来可能出现的危机。例如，2008年普利策奖授予了《华盛顿邮报》的商业专栏作家史蒂文·珀尔斯坦，2009年则授予了《拉斯维加斯太阳报》的商务记者亚历山德拉·伯宗，以表彰她对拉斯维加斯大道上建筑工人恶劣工作条件的报道。既然商业新闻的质量和内容总体上已有所提升，且比50年前更加客观，为何它仍受到如此低的评价呢？部分原因在于人们的认知偏差。许多人认为商业新闻枯燥乏味、篇幅冗长，充斥着大量数字和复杂话题，普通读者根本不会感兴趣。商业新闻往往是为企业和高管准备的，而面向普通工人的内容却很少。但实际上，商业写作完全可以——也应当——吸引大众的兴趣，它应当成为当今报纸、杂志和电视媒体中最优秀的新闻形式之一。这个国家的几乎每个人每天都在思考自己的收入多少、工作是否稳定，或者是否应该寻找新工作。他们想知道现在是否是重新办理房贷的好时机，或者自己所在公司的CEO是否正在考虑出售企业。他们想了解哪些公司存在财务问题，从而避免投资其股票。此外，他们还想知道哪些企业可能是不错的就业选择。简而言之，他们希望看到更好的商业新闻报道。

<!--en-->
1. *Understanding financial statements: A journalist's guide.* The book by Chicago financial guru Jay Taparia is written in an easy-to-understand style.
2. A subscription to *The Wall Street Journal*. Simply the best business reporting, day in and day out. To be the best, read the best.
3. Access to a Bloomberg terminal. This machine can provide the data to make a story stronger, and contact information for sources across the globe.
4. The book *24 Days: How Two Wall Street Journal Reporters Uncovered the Lies that Destroyed Faith in Corporate America*, which details how reporters reported the story behind one of the biggest company failures in the past century.
5. Membership in the Society of American Business Editors and Writers. SABEW offers workshops and conferences where business journalists learn from others in the field.
8 • Business Journalism is More Fun than You Think
business. With a few notable exceptions, business reporting took a back seat to writing about the Vietnam War and the race riots.
The 1980s and 1990s were better. The quality of business journalism improved as reporters and editors gained experience, but major stories were still missed. And business reporting took some hits. Foster Winans wrote the popular “Heard on the Street” column for *The Wall Street Journal* in the early 1980s. The stories disclosed whether professional investors were bullish or bearish on certain stocks. Winans started leaking information before his stories were published and was eventually caught and served time in prison. A decade later, well-known business columnist Dan Dorfman was fired from *Money* magazine for failing to disclose his sources to his editor after reports in other publications noted his close relationship with investors.
Along the way, few reporters were warning readers about impending problems. There were no glaring headlines in early October 1987 urging investors to take their money out of the stock market before it fell. A decade later, business sections and magazines lauded the management of Enron in prose that now seems ludicrous. In the *Dallas Morning News*, Enron was dubbed in a headline as a “global e-commerce leader” (North, 2002). A reporter for the *Houston Business Journal* wrote, “Enron has shown a widely recognized knack for innovation that consistently generates additional sources of revenue, potential profits and more capital” (North, 2002).
The boosterism was not confined to local publications touting hometown companies. Even the magazines and publications that were the so-called experts in writing about these new industries and businesses missed out on notifying readers of the problems. “Too often the new magazines and Web sites acted as incurious cheerleaders, championing executives and innovative companies without questioning their books,” said James Ledbetter, business editor of *Time Europe* and a former employee of *The Industry Standard*, one of the publications that chronicled the meteoric rise of many Internet companies without realizing that many of them were doomed to failure. “Do a search, for example, of the word ‘Enron’ in the databases of those publications prior to 2000 and you’ll find little but praise for its market innovations” (Ledbetter, 2003, p. A17).
Even revered mass communication outlets failed in their watchdog role. *The New York Times* called Enron’s president an “idea machine” (Salpukas, 1999, p. C1). “Not only did the press miss the Enron scandal, it actively helped create the Enron scandal,” said Jeffrey Madick, editor of *Challenge*, an economics magazine. “It not only missed the complications of Enron’s fancy partnerships, which are indeed complicated, but it extolled Enron’s virtues beyond almost any company. *Fortune* named Enron the most innovative company five or six years in a row, presumably without once checking the books” (Madick, 2003, p. 3).
And even when mass communication outlets investigated serious business issues, such as the series run by *The New York Times* in March 1996 that examined why people around the country were losing their jobs despite strong economic growth, gaps remained. The series made faulty assertions, such as that the economy was not producing workers who stayed in the same jobs for long periods of time, that it was harder for a laid-off worker to find a new job, and that many of the jobs being created were low-paying service jobs, not higher paying manufacturing jobs.
Business Journalism is More Fun than You Think • 9
"The problem with business coverage in the 1990s was not that journalists weren't smart enough to root out the corruption," wrote Charles Layton in *American Journalism Review* in March 2003. "Reading the coverage of the past half-decade, one is struck by how much certain reporters *did* uncover. But even within their own news organizations, their insights were lost in a cacophony of naive reportage that reassured us the system was sound, analysts and auditors and CEOs were basically trustworthy, and the market boom might go on forever" (Layton, 2003, p. 22).
In recent years, business journalists have had to answer tough questions about why they failed to warn consumers about the economic crisis that began in 2008 and was caused by problems, such as inflated prices, in the real estate market. However, a review of coverage from the past decade shows that business reporters and editors performed better this time around. They wrote numerous stories about the housing bubble and warned about the dangers of derivatives on Wall Street firms. A former Harvard Business School professor, Gregory Miller, found that nearly one-third of the accounting improprieties uncovered at companies are first discovered by business journalists.
Still, a number of major stories were missed, including the aforementioned Madoff scandal, in which one tipster sent documents to a *Wall Street Journal* reporter three years before the crime was uncovered. The story went unreported until charges were filed.
With a dose of reality now entering business reporting, is it any wonder that confidence in the quality of work by business journalists remains low, particularly among those who regularly read the business section, namely, corporate executives? Even in newsrooms and among journalists, business reporting is still considered a backwater in knowledge and expertise. In a 1992 poll by Louis Harris, 46 percent of executives rated the overall quality of business journalism as negative. Furthermore, 17 percent of executives felt that the quality of business journalism had actually declined since 1967. In the same survey, more than three-fourths of executives—and nearly the same amount of journalism academics—agreed that too much emphasis was being placed on "personality" reporting, or writing stories about the CEO. Only 34 percent of journalists agreed, resulting in stories that made heroes of CEOs that later fell from grace as their companies faltered. But the most telling numbers are these: 92 percent of executives and 72 percent of journalists and journalism academics were concerned about a reporter's knowledge of the businesses they were covering.
Two years later, the Freedom Forum First Amendment Center published a study called *The Headline vs. The Bottom Line: Mutual Distrust Between Business and the News Media*. The study found that more than two-thirds of journalists believed that they did not make mistakes on the technical details of business stories. However, more than three-fourths of executives felt the opposite way (Haggerty and Rasmussen, 1994, p. 12). In addition, the same survey found that nearly half of all journalists believed they were not adequately trained for reporting about business, whereas 7 out of 10 executives were convinced that reporters did not have the business background they needed (Haggerty and Rasmussen, 1994, p. 10).
Ten years later, many of the same attitudes and beliefs exist about the value of business journalism. A survey conducted in the year 2000 by Selzer & Companyfor the Reynolds Foundation and the American Press Institute concluded that the nation's business leaders were unimpressed with the quality of business reporting in most daily newspapers and described business journalists as lacking a basic understanding of how businesses operate. "They don't ask questions that probe below the surface and so their reports do not convey the detailed information business leaders need," said the report (Selzer, 2000, p. 2).
10 • Business Journalism is More Fun than You Think
The survey also found that when newsroom executives rated five beats, business desk reporters earned the lowest ratings, and business was a low priority for resources in the newsroom, even though a number of solid—even brilliant—stories in business journalism have helped readers understand complex issues and warned them of future problems. For example, Pulitzer Prizes were awarded in 2008 to the *Washington Post's* business columnist, Steven Pearlstein, and, in 2009, to *Las Vegas Sun* business reporter Alexandra Berzon for her coverage of unsafe working conditions for construction workers on The Strip.
Why, then, is business journalism held in such low esteem, given that the quality of stories and the content in business coverage has improved overall and is more objective than it was 50 years ago?
Part of the problem is perception. Business stories are considered by many to be staid and unwieldy, with too many numbers and complicated topics to be of any interest to the average reader. Business is too often covered for managers and executives in business and not enough for the worker.
But business writing can—and should—be interesting to the masses, and it should be some of the best journalism today in newspapers, magazines, and on television. Virtually every person in the country spends time each day thinking about how much money they make, whether they have job security, or whether they should be looking for a new job. They want to know if now is the time to refinance a home mortgage, or whether the CEO of the company where they work is considering selling the business. They want to know which companies are in financial trouble so they do not invest in their stocks. And they want to know which businesses might be good places to work.
Simply put, they want better business coverage.

## 理解与分析

<!--en-->
*Understand and Analyze*

对于全世界的商业记者而言，最重要的事情就是弄清楚自己正在报道的内容是什么。某大型都市报纸的前商业版编辑一想到15年前他作为职业作家写的第一篇稿子就感到汗颜——当时他将营收与净收入混为一谈。若非一位细心的编辑发现了这个错误，整篇报道乃至整个商业版的事实都会受到质疑。

<!--en-->
The most important thing for business journalists around the world to do is to understand what they are writing about. A former business editor at a large metropolitan newspaper recoils at remembering his first story as a professional writer 15 years earlier, when he confused revenue with net income. That mistake, if it had not been caught by a careful editor, would have called into question the facts throughout that story and the entire business section.

然而，正如我们所见，大众媒体从未十分重视对商业记者和编辑进行商业领域专业知识的培训与教育。不幸的是，不仅负责商业新闻的记者需要了解这些商业主题与概念，所有报纸、杂志、网络新闻网站以及电视新闻台的记者最终都会遇到涉及金钱或商业内容的报道。若没有足够的知识来妥善处理这类报道，他们就是在辜负受众。

<!--en-->
But, as we've seen, mass communication outlets have never placed much emphasis on training and teaching their business reporters and editors the ins and outs of the business world. It is not just reporters on the business desk, unfortunately, who need this understanding of business topics and concepts. Reporters throughout every section of every newspaper, magazine, Internet news site, and television news station will eventually come across a story that involves money or business in some fashion. Without the knowledge to cover the story adequately, they will be doing a disservice to their audiences.

商业新闻比你想象中更有趣 • 11 不仅是记者如此，公关专业人士在为企业撰写新闻稿时也常常不理解其中涉及的许多概念与理念。他们同样没有接受过如何阅读资产负债表或分析高管薪酬结构的培训。

<!--en-->
Business Journalism is More Fun than You Think • 11
And it's not just the journalists. Public relations professionals also often do not understand many of the concepts and ideas that they are writing about in press releases for companies. They, too, have not gone to school to learn how to read a balance sheet or analyze an executive's compensation package.

要想成为优秀的商业记者，他们还有许多东西需要学习。他们需要掌握如何报道和撰写有关经济、政府监管以及影响企业的税收等方面的内容。他们需要了解企业是如何运作的，以及为何有些企业盈利而有些则亏损。他们还需要知道公司内部高管及其他管理人员的角色，还要明白有些企业的存在目的并非盈利，而是服务社区。

<!--en-->
There is so much for business journalists to learn to be effective reporters. They need to know how to report and write about the economy, government regulation, and taxes affecting businesses. They need to understand how businesses operate and why some businesses make money, whereas others lose money. They need to know the role of executives and other managers inside a company and that some businesses do not exist to make money but to serve the community.

若缺乏这些知识以及其他更多相关知识，商业记者就会在报道中犯下错误。一些商业新闻专家会选择向读者揭露业内其他人所犯的错误。以下是《圣保罗先锋报》记者爱德华·洛特曼撰写的专栏，展示了记者如何对商业和经济问题做出可能被他人反驳的断言：

<!--en-->
Without all of this knowledge and more, mistakes that hurt all business journalists get into the story. Some business journalism experts resort to letting their readers know when others in the field are making mistakes. The following column by *St. Paul Pioneer Press* writer Edward Lotterman shows how a reporter can make assertions about business and the economy that may be refuted by others:

部分财经媒体仍在国际经济问题上犯错。请看本周二该报刊登的美联社的一篇报道。

<!--en-->
Some members of the financial press continue to flub international economic issues. Consider an Associated Press article published in this newspaper Tuesday.

这篇报道的标题为“美元对欧元、日元依然疲软”，文中写道：“周一，美元对欧元和日元的汇率仍处于去年底以来的最低水平。美国股市也因会议委员会发布的综合领先指标指数而遭受冲击。”

<!--en-->
Under the headline of "Dollar still lags against euro, yen," it states: "The dollar continued to languish Monday at its lowest levels against the euro and yen since around the end of last year. The dollar and U.S. equities sustained a blow from the Conference Board's composite Index of Leading Indicators."

随后文章提到：“外汇市场的关注焦点主要集中在美元对日元汇率的脆弱性上。”

<!--en-->
Later, it notes, "Much of the foreign exchange market's focus was on the dollar's fragility against the Japanese currency."

就在三天前，同一家通讯社还报道称：“由于出口增长……快于进口增长，3月美国的贸易逆差略有改善。”

<!--en-->
This same wire service reported three days earlier that "the U.S. trade deficit improved slightly in March as growth in exports . . . outpaced the growth in imports."

美联社的编辑和记者显然没有意识到，将贸易逆差描述为坏消息，三天后又用“疲软”之类的负面词汇形容略微走弱的美元，这种做法本身具有讽刺意味。

<!--en-->
Associated Press editors and writers apparently don't see any irony in reporting a trade deficit as bad news, then three days later describing an infinitesimally weaker dollar in negative terms, such as lags and languish.

这就好比天气预报员兴高采烈地宣布又是一个没有雨水、适合活动的美好日子，而在广告之后却称“严重的干旱”仍在持续。

<!--en-->
This could be compared to a weather forecaster who cheerily reports we had another beautiful day with no rain to interrupt anyone's activities. Then, after a commercial, he notes that "the devastating drought" continues.

我们的进口之所以超过出口，恰恰是因为美元较强，就像干旱往往发生在连续多日晴朗无雨的情况下一样。为贸易逆差缩小欢呼、为美元疲软哀叹，其实和为晴朗的天气欢呼、为缺少雨水抱怨一样愚蠢。

<!--en-->
Our imports exceed our exports precisely because the dollar is strong, just as a drought occurs when there are many sunny, rainless days. It is as idiotic to cheer a narrowing trade gap and decry a weaker dollar, as it is to cheer a bright, clear day and moan about the lack of rain.

从多种衡量标准来看，美元都被高估了。这虽然有利于消费者，但却损害了生产者，尤其是那些出口商品或与进口产品竞争的企业。

<!--en-->
The U.S. dollar is overvalued by any number of measures. This helps consumers, but hurts producers, especially those firms that export goods or compete with imports.

“强劲”的美元显然意味着美国产品在海外价格更高。周二那篇报道的讽刺之处在于，它的结尾是这样的表述：

<!--en-->
A "strong" dollar clearly equals "expensive" American products abroad.
The irony of Tuesday's article is that it ended with the following observation:

“日本养老基金正面临压力，被迫购买外国资产，以制造资本外流，从而防止日元升值。”

<!--en-->
"Japanese pension funds have been getting pressure to buy foreign assets to generate capital outflow that is necessary to keep the yen from appreciating."

如果“强劲”的货币对经济有益，那么日本政府为何要采取措施让日元保持疲软呢？日本的经济发展模式与美国有本质不同吗？答案是否定的。

<!--en-->
If a "strong" currency were good for the economy, why would theJapanese government initiate actions to keep the yen weak? Does the Japanese economy function in a fundamentally different way from that of the United States? No, it doesn’t.

12 • 商业新闻比你想象中更有趣 日本企业和政府都明白，昂贵的日元会损害日本的产出与生产，就像昂贵的美元会损害美国的生产商和就业状况一样。

<!--en-->
12 • Business Journalism is More Fun than You Think
Japanese business and government know that an expensive yen is bad for Japanese output and production, just as an expensive dollar is bad for U.S. producers and employment.

历史告诉我们，当各国的国际收支表中的经常账户出现长期赤字——这些账户包括进出口数据——其货币价值必然会下降。

<!--en-->
History tells us that when nations incur long-running deficits in their current account sections of balance-of-payments tabulations—which include imports and exports—currencies inevitably decline in value.

当美元贬值后，美国消费者会减少购买价格上涨的进口商品，而美国生产商则会增加出口价格较低的产品的销售。

<!--en-->
When the dollar gets cheaper, American consumers will buy fewer newly expensive imports, and U.S. producers will sell more newly inexpensive exports.

这一过程可能逐渐发生，给消费者和企业足够时间调整策略；也可能在几个月或几个季度内突然发生。同样，历史表明，渐进式的调整通常比剧烈的调整造成的破坏更小。

<!--en-->
This can occur gradually, giving consumers and businesses time to adjust strategies, or it can occur abruptly in a few months or quarters. Again, history tells us that gradual adjustments usually are less disruptive than harsh ones.

理性的美国公民应当欢迎美元在较长时间内逐步走弱。除了错误的排外情绪外，美国人没有理由坚持维持强势美元。

<!--en-->
Thoughtful U.S. citizens should welcome gradual weakening of the dollar over a sustained period. There’s no reason other than misguided xenophobia for Americans to cling to a strong dollar.

但媒体仍将持续将美元价值的任何下跌视为坏消息，任何上升则视为好消息。

<!--en-->
But the media continue to report any decline in the value of the dollar as bad news and any increase as good news.

媒体在民主社会中起着至关重要的作用。能够启发公众的文章有助于制定更好的经济政策并提升生活水平。¹读过那篇批评文章后，你是不是对撰写第一篇关于经济的报道感到紧张？别担心，其实并没有看上去那么难。

<!--en-->
The media play a vital role in a democracy. Articles that enlighten the public foster better economic policies and a better level of living.¹
After reading that critique, you’re nervous about writing that first story about the economy, aren’t you? Not to worry. It is not as hard as it seems.

洛特曼对强势货币与贸易关系的简明解释，有助于任何读者理解他所论述的内容。（当然也有与洛特曼观点相反的观点：即如果美元贬值过度，持有美国金融股票的外国人可能会抛售这些股票，从而导致利率迅速上升。）然而，包括财经记者在内的许多记者试图通过使用多音节词汇来解释那些他们自己也未必完全理解的复杂话题，以此给读者留下深刻印象。

<!--en-->
The simplicity of Lotterman’s explanations of a strong currency and trade help any reader understand what he is writing about. (A contrary argument to Lotterman’s can also be made: That is, if the dollar weakens too much, foreigners who own U.S. financial stocks may sell them, causing a rapid rise in interest rates.) Yet too many journalists, including business journalists, seek to impress their readers by using multi-syllabic words to explain arcane topics, the meaning of which many of them quietly admit they are not 100 percent sure of.

此外，许多记者只是机械地复述他们被告知或读到的有关商业话题的信息，既不质疑其正确性，也不真正理解所写内容。这会给记者以及读者或听众带来问题。正如众多调查所示，企业高管和其他读者很容易通过文章就能看出记者是否真正理解所写内容。本不该如此。的确，新闻编辑部面临着截止日期的压力，使得记者无法花一两天时间深入研究某个话题后再进行报道。但正是在这种情况下，具备相关知识的编辑应当抽出时间耐心指导记者，传授自己的经验。[^219]：¹摘自E.洛特曼2002年5月26日发表于《圣保罗先锋报》的文章《媒体需了解美元价值与贸易逆差的关系》，第1C页。版权归《圣保罗先锋报》所有，经许可转载。

<!--en-->
In addition, many reporters simply regurgitate what they have been told or have read regarding a business topic without questioning the validity of the meaning or fully understanding what they are writing about. And that can lead to problems for both the reporter and the reader or listener. As we have seen in numerous surveys, business executives and other readers can easily tell by reading a story when a reporter does not fully understand what he or she is writing. That should not be the case. True, newsrooms are places where deadline pressure prohibits reporters from spending a day or two researching a topic until they feel comfortable writing about it. But that is when an editor with the relevant knowledge should take the time and care to guide the reporter along, imparting his or her wisdom.
[^219]: ¹ From “Media Need to Know Value of Dollar vs. Trade Defeat,” by E. Lotterman, May 26, 2002, *St. Paul Pioneer Press*, p. 1C. Copyright 2002 by *St. Paul Pioneer Press*. Reprinted with permission.

财经新闻比你想象中更有趣 • 13 因此，了解商业话题的知识不仅对记者至关重要，对他们的编辑也同样重要。负责报道县或市政府工作的记者，凭借高中和大学的政治学课程已具备政府运作的基本认知；而许多体育记者在年轻时也花了无数时间观看和参与如今他们要撰文描述的那些运动项目。

<!--en-->
Business Journalism is More Fun than You Think • 13
So, knowledge and understanding of business topics is vital not just for reporters, but for their editors as well. Reporters who cover county or city government have a basic understanding of how governments operate from their high school and college political science classes. And many sports reporters have spent countless hours as youths watching and playing the games that they now write stories about.

然而，很少有财经记者和编辑通过上课或主修商业学科来获取工作所需的知识。《纽约时报》的财经专栏作家弗洛伊德·诺里斯在2003年美国商业编辑与作家协会年会上表示：“没人会派一个不知道什么是游击手的人去报道红袜队。”但他同时也指出，“很多人却派那些根本不确定每股收益含义的记者去报道商业新闻”（纳尔逊，2003年，第6页）。

<!--en-->
Yet few business reporters and editors ever took a class or majored in business to obtain the knowledge that they needed to do their job. “Nobody would send someone to cover the Red Sox who doesn’t know what a shortstop is,” said *New York Times* business columnist Floyd Norris at the 2003 Society of American Business Editors and Writers annual conference. Yet “many people send reporters to cover business who are not real [sic] sure what earnings per share means” (Nelson, 2003, p. 6).

### 所有的财经新闻都关乎金钱。

<!--en-->
*All Business Journalism is About Money*

但对于负责报道政府事务、体育赛事，以及教育、警情或法庭情况的记者而言，了解企业的运作方式同样非常重要。每一个新闻故事都可以追溯到一个核心的共同点：金钱。

<!--en-->
But for the government reporter and the sports reporter, as well as reporters covering education, the police beat, or the courts, it can be important to know and understand how businesses operate. Every single story can be traced back to one single important common denominator: money.

金钱在社会的各个层面都至关重要。在整个社会中，大部分资金来源于商业活动和消费者支出。政府则依靠税收来维持运作。这些税收从何而来？来自政府管辖范围内的消费者和企业。体育团队需要资金来支付运动员的工资以及建造体育场和竞技场。这些资金又从哪里来？来自购买比赛门票的民众和企业。商业与经济与一切事物息息相关。如今，私人企业也在运营学校。大学则越来越依赖其捐赠金，以及这些资金在华尔街的投资收益，以此来支付教职工的薪水并控制学费水平。谋杀、盗窃和抢劫等犯罪行为往往源于某人获取更多金钱或昂贵物品的需求。

<!--en-->
Money is important in every part of society. Throughout society, most of that money is generated from business and consumer spending. Governments receive tax money to operate. Where does the tax money come from? From consumers and businesses in the government’s jurisdiction. Sports teams need money to pay athletes and to build stadiums and arenas. Where does that money come from? From the people and corporations who pay to watch the games. Business and the economy are related to everything. Private companies are now running schools. Universities now rely more on their endowments and how that money is invested on Wall Street to pay for faculty salaries and to keep tuition costs low. Murders, thefts, and robberies often revolve around one person’s need to obtain more money or costly material items.

以下是《北卡罗来纳州罗利市新闻观察家报》头版上的一篇优秀报道案例，它展示了利率下降——尽管有些记者写过相关文章，但可能并未完全理解这一商业话题——所带来的深远影响，这种影响很可能遍及全国：

<!--en-->
Here’s an excellent example of a story on the front page of *The News & Observer* in Raleigh, N.C., that shows how a decline in interest rates—one of those business topics that a few reporters may not fully understand even though they have written stories mentioning it—has had far-reaching effects, likely across the country:

> 该州各城市，包括三角洲地区的城市，在过去一年中的投资收益均出现大幅下降，这一财务困境让那些正在编制预算并试图控制财产税的官员们面临更大压力。对许多地方政府而言，这些损失额甚至与迈克·伊斯利州长去年为解决州预算问题而扣留的金额相当或更高。“这是个沉重的打击，”罗利市财政主管佩里·詹姆斯说道，“资金减少后，自然能用于支出的金额也会相应减少。”不过，这些地方政府不能将投资表现不佳的责任归咎于州长，而应怪罪美联储。为刺激经济，美联储在2001年共11次下调短期利率，去年11月又再次下调。每次利率下调都会降低地方政府的潜在收益，因为根据州法律，它们必须将大部分资金投入与联邦基金利率挂钩的保守型投资产品，如定期存单和国库券。因此，在经历了数年的良好回报后，这些投资在截至2002年6月30日的财年中大幅下跌。几乎所有与股市挂钩的投资组合也都出现了下滑，其中包括州养老基金，该基金去年亏损了33亿美元，相当于其资产价值的5.8%。虽然没人能预测市场的未来，但随着美联储将基金利率维持在数十年来最低水平，预计今年地方政府的投资回报仍将疲软。不过也有积极的一面：地方政府在用于建设建筑及其他基础设施项目的贷款上能够获得更低的利率，尽管在经济和预算状况不明朗的情况下，这类项目已大幅放缓。对于地方预算编制人员和财务官员来说，较低的收益使得本已紧张的预算更加难以应对。州政府记录显示，罗利市在2001–02财年的投资收益约为1200万美元，这一数字比上一财年的2210万美元以及再上一财年的2060万美元下降了46%。达勒姆市在2002年的投资收益为700万美元，比前一年减少了670万美元，降幅达49%。“在某些年份，这曾是我们的重要收入来源，”达勒姆市预算主管朱莉·布伦曼说，“通过投资而非向市民征税来获取收入真是不错。没有这笔收入，我们就不得不削减服务开支或寻找其他增收途径。”对于罗利市和达勒姆市而言，这些投资损失甚至超过了伊斯利州长扣留给地方政府的补偿金和其他款项，这一举措引发了当地官员的强烈抗议，并有诉讼威胁。在整体投资规模较小的查珀尔希尔市，2002年的投资收益减少了70万美元，仅为2001年120万美元的57%。在所有大型三角洲地区地方政府中，加里市的状况相对较好，2002财年的投资收益比前一年仅减少了约310万美元，降幅为23.8%。在三角洲地区的城市中，温斯顿-塞勒姆的处境最为糟糕，它是北卡罗来纳州为数不多获州议会许可可将资金投入波动性更大的股票的市场之一。温斯顿-塞勒姆在2002年和2001年的投资不仅收益较低，甚至出现了实际亏损，两年度累计亏损达5140万美元。然而在之前的三年里，得益于蓬勃发展的股市，该市的投资表现优于州内其他所有城市，累计投资收益高达1.37亿美元。去年夏天，达勒姆市在州议会的代表们获得了授权，允许达勒姆市和达勒姆县像温斯顿-塞勒姆那样使用纳税人的钱进行投资：将最多一半至少五年内不会用到的现金投入股票市场。 商业新闻比你想象中更有趣 • 15 目前，布尔城的官员们表示，由于温斯顿-塞勒姆发生的事情，他们尚未采取行动。与其他城市一样，达勒姆也为其可用资金设定了三个优先事项：前两项是安全以及“流动性”，即不将资金锁定在长期投资中。第三项则是收益。负责监督投资的州地方政府财务委员会副主任万斯·霍洛曼称，损失相当严重。“这是一项收入在减少的领域，”他说，“再加上销售税也在下降且没有增长。”不过目前，大多数地方政府表示会承受这些损失，等待更好的时机。根据北卡罗来纳州市政联盟的说法，目前还没有任何集中的游说努力来允许各市镇将更多资金投入股票市场。正如温斯顿-塞勒姆所展现的那样，更大的灵活性意味着更高的风险。“大多数人目前都专注于改善经济状况，”该联盟的女发言人玛戈特·克里斯滕森说，“这样，他们现有的投资就能表现得更好。”² 这篇报道向生活在这些城镇的民众简单解释了低利率和股市下跌的影响。归根结底：这些城市政府的银行账户里可用于为当地居民提供服务的资金减少了。用这种方式解释的话，就连自称不懂商业的人也能理解。还有一篇报道，记者们费尽周折、常常枯燥地阅读了提交给美国证券交易委员会的公开文件，以此解释一家飞机制造商、一家拥有出事飞机的航空公司，以及一家本应负责该飞机维护的公司之间的关系。这篇报道刊登在《新闻与观察家报》“城市与州”版面的头版——而非商业版面——而且是由一名都市记者撰写的，并非精通商业文件的人。尽管记者们对这些文件的含义了解有限，但报道仍清晰地阐明了这种商业关系中的利益冲突。上周三那架19座涡轮螺旋桨通勤机在火球中坠毁，而制造这架飞机的公司，与该飞机执飞的航空公司以及本周早些时候负责其维护的公司都有财务关联。据一些行业专家称，由于该航空公司的母公司近年来损失惨重并正在积极削减成本，这些公司之间的财务联系引发了人们对于安全性是否可能受到影响的质疑。“如果你本应要求供应商确保质量，而这家供应商又是你的股东之一，那你还能多么坚决地要求一切按最高标准执行呢？”负责调查事故原因的联邦机构——国家运输安全委员会的前主席吉姆·伯内特说道，“这其中可能存在安全问题。”[^258]：² 摘自安德鲁·柯里西斯2003年2月10日发表于《新闻与观察家报》第1A版的文章《美联储的低利率冲击城市预算：投资与收入双双暴跌》，版权所有2003年《新闻与观察家报》，经许可转载。16 • 商业新闻比你想象中更有趣 但也有人认为，这种关系在航空业很常见，并不会引发冲突。而该飞机的制造商雷神飞机公司的发言人则表示，该公司并未参与维修公司雷神航空航天公司或所属航空公司Air Midwest的日常运营。“我们与这两家公司的日常运营没有任何关联，”位于堪萨斯州威奇托的雷神飞机公司发言人蒂姆·特拉维斯说道。 由于这架飞机在雷神航空航天公司完成尾翼升降舵控制组件的维修仅几天后就发生坠毁，相关的财务关联正在接受仔细审查。这些维修工作以及过重的行李被视作可能导致坠机的原因。负责此次维修的公司有26%的股份归飞机制造商所有，此前它曾是该制造商的全资子公司。2001年6月，雷神飞机公司以2.7亿美元的价格将这家维修子公司的大部分股权卖给了纽约的私人投资机构Veritas Capital。几个月后，随着制造商获得了总部位于菲尼克斯的Air Midwest母公司Mesa Air Group的部分股权，两家公司的财务联系进一步加深。根据Mesa Air Group向美国证券交易委员会提交的文件，去年2月制造商同意每年向Mesa支付最多550万美元，以便后者能够偿还从雷神飞机公司购买的飞机的款项。作为回报，Mesa向制造商提供了以每股10美元的价格购买233,068股Mesa股票的认股权证。截至目前，雷神飞机公司已购买了价值近130万美元的Mesa股票，同时还持有可购买另外103,133股的认股权证。上周三，该制造商还获得了另一家航空公司的部分股权。总部位于怀俄明州夏延的Great Lakes Aviation运营着数十架比奇1900系列飞机，由于未能按时支付多架飞机的费用，该公司将36%的股权转让给了制造商以减轻债务负担。Air Midwest并未回复多次致电。不过，与制造商一样总部位于威奇托的这家航空公司也在逐步淘汰其1990款比奇客机队中的部分飞机。许多乘客更倾向于乘坐喷气式飞机，因此在上一财年中，Air Midwest已退回12架比奇1900系列飞机，目前该航空公司仍拥有43架此类飞机。Air Midwest的母公司也在努力降低维护成本。根据美国证券交易委员会的文件，在截至9月30日的上一财年中，Mesa Air Group与那家维修公司达成了成本削减协议，从而节省了340万美元，同时减少了涡轮螺旋桨飞机的飞行次数。与其他大多数航空公司一样，Mesa也因经济疲软以及2001年9月恐怖袭击后乘客数量的锐减而遭受重创。该公司在2000年的利润接近5900万美元，但在2001年亏损4800万美元，而在最新的财年则亏损930万美元。12月，该公司要求其3300名员工自愿接受为期一年的5%减薪，以此换取奖金。前NTSB成员、现为阿肯色州律师的伯内特表示，这种相互持股的关系存在风险。“目前我们还不知道是否存在问题，但潜在风险是存在的，”伯内特说道，“这使得Air Midwest很难说‘我们对服务不满意，我们要去别的地方’。从安全角度考虑，保持一种独立的关系会更好。”其他行业专家则持不同观点。“不存在利益冲突，因为让飞机持续飞行并保持安全符合制造商的利益，毕竟这是他们的产品，”总部位于科罗拉多州埃弗格林的航空咨询公司Boyd Group的总裁迈克尔·博伊德说，“归根结底，这关系到他们的声誉以及责任。如果飞机发生事故，所有人都会把目光投向他们。还有谁比制造飞机的人更合适来处理这个问题呢？”博伊德指出，总部位于弗吉尼亚州阿灵顿的长期航空顾问莫特·贝耶也认同这一观点。他们以通用电气为例，该公司多年来一直为航空公司提供由其生产的喷气引擎的融资服务，同时还对这些引擎进行翻新。贝耶将其比作为汽车买家提供融资服务的汽车经销商。“这并非一种独特的安排，”贝耶在谈到Mesa与雷神的合作时说道，“我认为这是一个值得探索的机会领域。” 它使航空公司能够高效地获取飞机、运营飞机并对其进行维护。同时，它也为乘客带来了航空服务，否则他们可能无法享受这些服务。”博伊德表示：“我更希望由雷神公司来承担这项工作，因为他们熟悉该产品。如果工作没有做好，受损失的将是Air Midwest、维修公司以及制造商。”³ 阅读《新闻与观察家报》的这篇报道，读者可以清楚地了解这三家公司之间的关联，以及为何一些航空专家反对这种关系。对于那些在航班事故中失去亲人的家庭而言，这篇报道指出了可能出问题的地方。诚然，这本身并非一篇纯粹的商业报道，但要让读者充分理解其重要性，并自行推断导致飞机坠毁的可能原因，就需要具备商业知识。

<!--en-->
> Cities across the state, including in the Triangle, saw huge declines in investment earnings this past year, a financial setback that complicates matters for officials who are putting budgets together and trying to hold the line on property taxes. To many local governments, the losses amounted to as much or more than what Gov. Mike Easley withheld last year in settling state budget woes.
> “It’s a big hit,” Raleigh Finance Director Perry James said. “You can’t do as much with the money, naturally, if you’ve got less of it.” But the municipalities can’t fault the governor for the poor investment showing. Blame the Fed. Trying to boost the economy, the Federal Reserve cut short-term interest rates 11 times in 2001, and then once more last November.
14 • Business Journalism is More Fun than You Think
With each cut, the Fed lopped off potential returns for local governments, which by state law must put most of their cash in conservative investments tied to the federal fund rate—things such as certificates of deposit and treasury bills.
As a result, after several years of rosy returns, those investments tanked in the fiscal year that ended June 30, 2002.
Just about any portfolio tied to the stock markets did, too, including the state pension fund, which lost $3.3 billion a year ago, or 5.8 percent of its assets.
While no one can predict the future of markets, the returns for local governments are expected to remain weak this year as the Fed keeps the fund rate at its lowest level in decades.
There is a bright side: Local governments are getting lower interest rates on money they borrow to erect buildings and other infrastructure projects, though much of that activity has slowed with the uncertain economy and budget picture.
For local budget writers and finance officers, the low earnings make already tight budgets even more difficult.
Raleigh pocketed about $12 million on its investments in the 2001–02 fiscal year, state records show. That’s a steep, 46 percent decline from the $22.1 million it made the previous fiscal year and $20.6 million the year before that.
Durham pulled in $7 million on its investments in 2002. But that’s $6.7 million, or 49 percent, less than the year before.
"This had been, in some years, a really big source of income for us," said Julie Brenman, Durham's budget director. "It was nice to generate money through investments and not by going to the citizens. Without it, you have to make service cuts or go find other ways to get revenue."
For both Raleigh and Durham, those investment losses exceeded what Easley withheld in reimbursements and other payments to local governments, an action that prompted an outcry from local officials and threats of lawsuits.
In Chapel Hill, where less money is invested overall, the town saw a $700,000 decrease in 2002. That’s 57 percent below the $1.2 million it made on investments in 2001.
Gary did the best of all the large local Triangle governments, bringing in about $3.1 million less in fiscal 2002 than the year before, a 23.8 percent decline.
None of the Triangle cities fared as badly as Winston-Salem, one of the few governments in North Carolina with permission from the General Assembly to invest money in more volatile stocks.
Winston-Salem posted an actual loss—not just a lower gain—on its investments in fiscal 2002 and 2001, losing a combined $51.4 million. In the previous three years, however, Winston-Salem rode the booming stock market, outperforming all other cities in the state and bringing in $137 million in combined investment profits.
Last summer, Durham's representatives in the General Assembly won authority to let Durham City and Durham County invest taxpayer moneythe same way Winston-Salem does: by putting up to half its cash not needed for at least five years into stocks.
Business Journalism is More Fun than You Think • 15
So far, Bull City officials said, they haven't followed through because of what has happened in Winston-Salem.
Durham, like other cities, has three priorities for its available cash: The top two are safety and “liquidity” which means not locking it up in long-term investments. Next is the yield, or earnings.
Vance Holloman, deputy director of the state's Local Government Finance Commission, which monitors investments, said the losses have been significant.
“It's another revenue there's less of,” he said. “And it adds to the fact that sales taxes are down and haven't grown.”
For now, though, most local governments say they will ride out the losses and wait for better times. There's no concerted lobbying effort to allow municipalities to put more money in stocks, according to the N.C. League of Municipalities.
More flexibility brings greater risk—as Winston-Salem has seen.
“Mostly, people are focused on getting this economy improved,” said Margot Christensen, a league spokeswoman. “That way, the investments they are in already will do better and perform better.”²
This story explains simply the effects of lower interest rates and a falling stock market to anyone who lives in these towns. The bottom line: There is less money in the bank accounts of these city governments to spend on the services that they provide to the people living in their areas. And explained that way, it is a concept even the self-admitted business illiterate can understand.
Here is a story in which the reporters have gone through the tedious and often boring task of reading public documents filed with the SEC to explain the relationship between an aircraft manufacturer, an airline that owned a plane that crashed, and a company that was supposed to service and maintain the airplane. The story ran on the front page of the “City and State” section of *The News & Observer*—not in the business section. And it was co-written by a metro reporter, not someone with extensive knowledge of business documents. Despite the reporters' limited understanding of what these documents mean, the story clearly explains the conflict of interest in the business relationship.
The company that built the 19-seat turboprop commuter plane that crashed in a fireball last Wednesday has a financial stake in both the airline that flew the plane and the firm that did maintenance on it earlier in the week.
With the airline's parent losing millions in recent years and actively trying to cut costs, the companies' financial ties have raised questions whether safety may have been compromised, according to some industry experts.
“If the vendor whose feet you're supposed to hold to the fire for quality control was also one of your owners, how robust can you be about[demanding] everything being done to the highest standard?” said Jim Burnett, a former chairman of the National Transportation Safety Board, the federal agency that investigates crash causes. “There could be a safety issue there.”
[^258]: ² From “Fed's low rates zap city budgets: Investment+Income goes into free fall,” by Andrew Curliss, February 10, 2003, *The News & Observer*, p. 1A. Copyright 2003 by *The News & Observer*. Reprinted with permission.
16 • Business Journalism is More Fun than You Think
But others say such relationships are common in the airline industry and pose no conflict. And a spokesman for the manufacturer, Raytheon Aircraft, said it had no active role in the operations of either the repair company, Raytheon Aerospace, or the owner airline, Air Midwest. “We don’t have any involvement in the day-to-day operations of either company,” said Tim Travis, a spokesman for the manufacturer, Raytheon Aircraft Co. of Wichita, Kan.
The financial links are being scrutinized because the plane crashed only a few days after repairs were made to the tail elevator control assembly by Raytheon Aerospace, a company based in Madison, Miss. Those repairs, along with a heavy load of baggage, have emerged as possible causes of the crash.
The company that did the repair is 26 percent owned by the plane’s manufacturer and, formerly, was a wholly owned subsidiary. Raytheon Aircraft sold off a majority stake in the repair subsidiary to privately held Veritas Capital of New York for $270 million in June 2001.
The financial ties between the companies spread a few months later when the manufacturer got partial ownership of Air Midwest’s parent company, Phoenix-based Mesa Air Group.
According to documents filed by Mesa Air Group with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, the manufacturer last February agreed to pay Mesa up to $5.5 million annually so Mesa could keep up with payments on planes it had acquired from Raytheon Aircraft. In turn, Mesa gave the manufacturer warrants to buy 233,068 shares of Mesa stock at $10 a share.
To date, Raytheon Aircraft has bought nearly $1.3 million in Mesa stock and still holds warrants to buy another 103,133 shares. Last Wednesday, the manufacturer took a partial interest in another airline, too.
Cheyenne, Wyo.-based Great Lakes Aviation, which flies dozens of the Beech 1900s, was late on the payments for many of the aircraft and gave the manufacturer a 36 percent stake in the airline to reduce debt.
Air Midwest did not return repeated calls. But the airline, which, like the manufacturer, is based in Wichita, has been shedding planes from its fleet of 1990 Beech commuters. Many passengers prefer jets, and during the past fiscal year, Air Midwest returned 12 of the Beech 1900s. The airline currently has a fleet of 43 of the planes.
Air Midwest’s parent company also has been trying to reduce its maintenance bills. During its last fiscal year, which ended Sept. 30, Mesa Air Group reached a cost reduction agreement with the repair company that resulted in $3.4 million in savings along with reduced turboprop flights, according to SEC documents.
Like most other airlines, Mesa has been hit hard by the sluggish economy and sharp dropoff in passengers following the September 2001 terrorist attacks. After earning almost $59 million in 2000, the company lost $48 million in 2001 and lost $9.3 million during the latest fiscal year. InDecember the company asked its 3,300 employees to voluntarily take a 5 percent, one-year pay cut in return for bonuses.
Business Journalism is More Fun than You Think • 17
Burnett, the former NTSB member, said the web of shared ownership poses risks.
"Right now we don't know if there was a problem, but the potential is there," said Burnett, now a lawyer in Arkansas. "It makes it very difficult for Air Midwest to say, 'We're not satisfied with the service; we're going somewhere else.' It would be better from a safety standpoint to have an arms-length relationship," Burnett said.
Other industry experts disagreed.
"There's no conflict because it's in the manufacturer's best interest to keep the planes flying and safe because it's their product," said Michael Boyd, president of the Boyd Group, an Evergreen, Colo.-based aviation consulting firm. "Ultimately it's their reputation on the line and their liability, too." If a plane goes down, everybody looks at them.
"Who is better to be involved than those who built it?" Boyd said.
Boyd and longtime aviation consultant Mort Beyer of Arlington, Va., pointed to General Electric, which for years has financed airlines' purchases of jet engines, which the company builds. GE also overhauls the same engines, they said.
Beyer compared it to auto dealerships that offer financing deals for car buyers.
"It is not a unique arrangement," Beyer said of the Mesa-Raytheon deals. "I think it's an area of opportunity. It enables airlines to get airplanes and to fly them and maintain them efficiently. It also helps passengers, because they have air service, which they might otherwise not have."
Boyd said, "I'd rather have Raytheon do the work than someone else because they know the product. If it isn't being done right, Air Midwest is the one that gets burned; the repair company gets burned; and the manufacturer gets burned."³
A reader looking at the *News & Observer* story gets a great explanation of how these three companies are tied together and why some aviation experts object to such a relationship. For the families who lost relatives on the flight, the story points to what might have gone wrong. Again, this is not a business story, per se. But it takes an understanding of business to fully explain the topic in such a way that the reader can grasp its importance and reach his or her own conclusions about what might have happened to cause the plane to crash.

#### 为受众带来更优质的内容

<!--en-->
*Doing Better For Audiences*

由此可见，商业新闻业已取得了巨大进步，让世界变得更美好，但仍未能达到最佳状态。不过，商业新闻领域正在出现一些细微变化——越来越多的编辑和记者意识到，他们需要更多、更好的培训才能胜任工作。[^283]：³摘自D. Price与L. Perez所著《危机引发供应商问题》，发表于2003年1月12日的《The News & Observer》杂志第1B版。版权所有2003年《The News & Observer》，经许可转载。

<!--en-->
Thus we see that business journalism has made great strides and has made the world a better place to live but still falls short of being as good as it can be. Butsmall changes are occurring in business journalism. More editors and reporters have realized that they need more and better training to do their jobs.
[^283]: ³ From "Crash Raises Vendor Issue," by D. Price and L. Perez, January 12, 2003, *The News & Observer*, p. 1B. Copyright 2003 by *The News & Observer*. Reprinted with permission.

18 • 商业新闻比你想象中更有趣 对商业新闻质量感兴趣的人们正在采取措施加以改进。2008年，雷诺兹基金会向亚利桑那州立大学提供了500万美元的资助，用于扩展唐纳德·W·雷诺兹国家新闻中心开设的培训项目。该基金会还拨款在密苏里大学和内华达大学里诺分校增设专门教授商业报道的教师岗位。如今，全国各地的大学新闻学院开设的商业与经济报道课程数量比以往任何时候都多，为学生提供基础培训与相关知识。但最重要的是，报纸、杂志、网站和电视台似乎都更加注重在商业报道中保持批判性思维。

<!--en-->
18 • Business Journalism is More Fun than You Think
Those interested in the quality of business journalism are taking steps to improve it. In 2008, the Reynolds Foundation gave a $5 million grant to Arizona State University to expand training programs offered by the Donald W. Reynolds National Center for Journalism. It also gave money to add journalism professors focused on teaching business reporting at the University of Missouri and the University of Nevada-Reno. On college campuses across the country, more journalism schools are teaching business and economics reporting classes than ever before, giving students some basic training and understanding. Most importantly, however, there appears to be a newfound diligence on the part of newspapers, magazines, websites, and television stations to be more critical in their business coverage.

为《华盛顿邮报》撰写杂志评论的彼得·卡尔森在读过两篇重要文章后，对这种转变给予了高度评价：一篇发表在《财富》杂志上，揭露了白领犯罪；另一篇则刊登在《Business 2.0》上，抨击了美国企业界。“商业杂志已经变成了斗牛犬，不断刊登文章，将那些曾经被神化的企业家描绘成腐败、欺诈、贪婪的强盗大亨，”卡尔森写道。“说实话，我更喜欢这些新文章，”他补充道，“它们不仅更有趣，可能也更为准确。”（卡尔森，2002年，第C4页）

<!--en-->
Peter Carlson, who critiques magazines for *The Washington Post*, lauded this change of heart recently after reading two important articles: one in *Fortune* that exposed white-collar crime and another in *Business 2.0* that skewered American business. “Business magazines have turned into pit bulls, printing stories excoriating these once-deified entrepreneurs as crooked, mendacious, rapacious robber barons,” wrote Carlson. “To tell you the truth, I much prefer these new stories,” he added. “They’re a lot more fun—and probably a lot more accurate, too” (Carlson, 2002, p. C4).

由受过专业培训、更了解报道对象的记者撰写的更严谨、更深入的商业报道，将大幅提升当今大众媒体所报道的内容质量与话题深度。

<!--en-->
Harder, tougher, more thorough business reporting done by reporters who have been properly trained and who better understand what they are writing about will dramatically raise the quality of stories and topics discussed in mass communication today.

许多人认为20世纪90年代是商业新闻的黄金时代，那时的报道范围大幅扩大，相关文章数量也显著增加。但也有人认为，商业新闻尚未达到顶峰。如今，随着越来越多的消费者面临失业以及更难找到投资机会，对高质量报道和编辑的需求比以往任何时候都更高。过去商业新闻确实为他们提供了帮助，但程度尚不及其潜力所能达到的水平。“是时候让商业新闻从业者更具雄心了，”《波士顿环球报》编辑马丁·巴伦说道，“他们应该设定更高的目标，持续产出美国最优秀的新闻作品。”（巴伦，2001年）

<!--en-->
Many consider the 1990s a golden age for business journalism, a time in which coverage expanded dramatically and more stories were written. Others would argue that business journalism has yet to reach its peak. Quality reporting and editing is needed now more than ever, as more and more consumers cope with job losses and harder-to-find investment ideas. Business journalism has helped them in the past, but not as much as it could have. “It is time for business journalists to be more ambitious,” said Martin Baron, editor of *The Boston Globe*, “to set their sights higher, to routinely produce the finest journalism in America” (Baron, 2001).

读者需要且希望看到更优质的商业新闻。

<!--en-->
The readers need and want better business journalism.

## 建议练习

<!--en-->
*Suggested Exercises*

1. 写一篇500字的文章，阐述商业如何影响你的生活——从你购买的产品和服务到你父母的工作单位。如果其中一两家企业不复存在，你的生活将会有何不同？20 • 商业新闻比你想象中更有趣
2. 连续一周浏览报纸的商务版块。将相关版面带来并与班级同学讨论哪些报道对你而言有参考价值，哪些你不理解。是什么帮助你理解这些报道？有哪些内容难以理解？
3. 与班级其他同学一起探讨CEO与商业记者之间的关系。CEO是否应该尝试帮助那些在某个话题上遇到困难的记者？
4. 在小组讨论中，谈谈成为商业记者或编辑的资格要求。他们应具备哪些技能？需要了解关于商业和经济运作的哪些知识？这些知识应从何处获取？
5. 根据你阅读的关于近期经济衰退的报道，写一篇一页纸的文章，总结你对经济的认识。重点介绍你之前不理解的经济概念以及个人理财策略。

<!--en-->
1. Write a 500-word essay explaining how business has affected your life, from the products and services you purchase to where your parents work. How would your life be different without one or two of those businesses being in operation?
20 • Business Journalism is More Fun than You Think
2. Review a newspaper's business section for a week. Bring in the sections and discuss with the class what stories you thought were informative and what stories you did not understand. What helped you understand the stories? What was hard to decipher?
3. With the rest of the class, discuss the relationship between a CEO and a business reporter. Should a CEO attempt to help educate a reporter that he or she sees is struggling with a topic?
4. In a group discussion, talk about the qualifications for being a business reporter or editor. What skills should they have? What should they know about how business and the economy operate? Where should they obtain that knowledge?
5. Write a one-page paper about what you have learned about the economy based on coverage you have read of the recent recession. Focus on economic concepts that you previously did not understand as well as personal finance strategies.

## 2

公共与私营企业，还有伦理问题！

<!--en-->
Public and Private and Ethics, Oh My!

### 定义公共公司与私营公司

<!--en-->
*Defining Public and Private Companies*

阅读几乎所有大型都市报纸的商务版块，你会发现大多数报道都是关于在纽约证券交易所上市的大型企业。

<!--en-->
Read the business section of almost any major metropolitan newspaper, and you will find that most of the stories are written about large companies with stock traded on an exchange in New York.

在北卡罗来纳州罗利市的《新闻与观察家报》的商务版块首页上，某天可能会出现一篇关于总部位于夏洛特的公共银行——美国银行的报道。该版块内还会有关于国防承包商诺斯罗普·格鲁曼公司和电话公司斯普林特公司的报道，它们也都是公共公司。所有这些报道都会提及这些公司在营收或利润方面的规模。

<!--en-->
One day, a typical front page of the business section of *The News & Observer* in Raleigh, N.C., could feature an article on Bank of America, the Charlotte-based public bank. Inside the section would be articles about defense contractor Northrop Grumman and phone company Sprint, also public companies. All of these stories mention how big these companies are in terms of revenue or profits.

但如果阅读小城镇报纸的商务版块，报道的内容很可能是关于那些无需公开运营信息的小型私营企业。例如，《亨茨维尔时报》（阿拉巴马州）某天商务版块首页上就有一篇关于一家由单人经营的服装修改与缝纫店的报道。作为私营企业，这家店无需公开其营收和利润，记者很可能也从未询问过这些信息。

<!--en-->
But read the business section of a paper in a smaller town or city, and the stories will likely be about small private companies that are not required to disclose information about their operations. For example, the front page of the business section of the *Huntsville Times* (Alabama) one day contained a story about Alterations & More, a one-woman alteration and sewing business. As a private company, this business was not required to disclose its revenue and profits. The reporter likely never even asked for them.

这种差异显而易见。公共公司向公众出售股票，其股票在交易所交易。正因如此，公共公司必须向证券交易委员会（SEC）提交信息，这使得商业记者能够轻松获取撰写报道所需的事实。

<!--en-->
The dichotomy is evident. A public company sells stock to the public, and its stock is traded on an exchange. Because of this, the public company is required to file information with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), making it easy for business reporters to obtain facts for their stories.

而私营公司大多无需提交此类信息。（你将在本书后面了解到如何获取某些私营公司的财务信息。）因此，除非企业主动披露业绩，否则记者很难获得足够的财务数据来撰写关于私营企业的报道。尽管如此，学会解读和分析公共公司的财务信息仍然是非常有价值的。公共公司与私营公司的运作方式其实类似，两者都是以盈利为目的，且通常都由CEO负责管理。

<!--en-->
Private companies, for the most part, are not required to file such information. (You will learn later in the book where to find financial information about some private companies.) As such, reporters have access to few financial numbers to flesh out a story on a private company unless the company willingly discloses its performance. Still, it is valuable to learn how to read and dissect the financial information available on public companies. Public and private companies operate similarly. They are both in business to make money, and a CEO typically runs both.

这两种结构各有优缺点。公共公司

<!--en-->
There are advantages and disadvantages to both structures. Public companies

### 专业人士的经验之谈

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

前《诺福克弗吉尼亚领航员报》商务版块编辑比尔·乔伊克关于商业写作技巧的建议：

<!--en-->
Former Norfolk Virginian-Pilot business editor *Bill Choyke* on the craft of business writing:

**全局思考，本地写作与编辑：**要更多考虑背景等因素。一份优秀的报纸首先应刊登本地新闻，偶尔对全国性新闻进行本地化处理，而在处理本地新闻时则力求做到精益求精。

<!--en-->
**Think globally, write and edit locally:** Think context and more. A good newspaper is first with local news, occasionally localizes the national news and reaches for excellence when it nationalizes (or regionalizes) the local news.

### 专业人士的经验之谈

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

前《诺福克弗吉尼亚领航员报》商务版块编辑比尔·乔伊克关于商业写作技巧的建议：

<!--en-->
Former Norfolk Virginian-Pilot business editor Bill Choyke on the craft of business writing:

多读书：这一最佳实践在新闻行业同样适用。阅读《华尔街日报》、《纽约时报》以及其他都市类报纸，不仅要关注内容，还要留意叙事方式和结构。当然要多读，但也要努力每周阅读、消化甚至研究几篇报道。公共公司更容易筹集资金用于扩张，但它们也必须每三个月公开一次财务业绩，这在业绩不佳的季度可能会成为劣势。相比之下，私营公司往往更难筹集资金扩张，如果需要迅速抓住商机进行扩张，这就成了问题。不过如果它们出现业绩不佳的情况，很少有人会知道，这在那些重视形象的企业中可能反而是一种优势。

<!--en-->
Read, read, read: Best practice works in journalism too. Read the *Wall Street Journal*, *New York Times* and other metros and read not only for content but storytelling and structure. Read more, of course, but make an effort to read, digest and even study several stories per week.
are more easily able to raise cash to expand. However, they are also required to disclose their financial performance every three months. That can be a disadvantage, particularly after a bad quarter. In contrast, private companies often have a harder time raising the money to expand, which is a problem if they need to expand quickly to take advantage of a business opportunity. But if they have a bad quarter, few people know. That can be an advantage, particularly in businesses in which perception is important.

总部位于加州的航空货运公司DHL Airways的前执行副总裁兼首席财务官比尔·斯马特表示，私有制使该公司能够保持低调。如果它必须以上市公司的身份向美国证券交易委员会提交信息，像联邦快递这样的竞争对手就能分析这些数据并获得竞争优势。不过归根结底，上市公司与私有公司在衡量成功标准上并无二致——即通过增加销售额或收入以及提升利润来体现。遗憾的是，这些概念常常被许多缺乏经验的商业记者混淆。

<!--en-->
Bill Smartt, a former executive vice president and chief financial officer (CFO) at DHL Airways, a California-based airfreight carrier, said that private ownership allowed the company to maintain a low profile. If it had to file information with the SEC as a public company, competitors like Federal Express could analyze those facts and gain a competitive advantage. In the end, though, public and private companies are similar in how they measure success—that is, by increased sales or revenues and improved profits. Unfortunately, these are concepts that many inexperienced business reporters confuse.

本章将探讨每位商业记者和编辑都应了解的一些基本概念，首先是从商业记者的工作方式讲起。商业报道与编辑工作与报纸、电视台、广播电台甚至网站上的其他报道领域并无不同，它要求记者知道哪些人是最佳消息来源，以及去哪里寻找能够解答问题并提供细节以写出优质报道的文件。

<!--en-->
This chapter explores some basic concepts that every business reporter and editor should know, beginning with how the business journalist does his or her job. Business reporting and editing is just like any other beat at a newspaper, a television or radio station, or even an Internet site. It requires knowledge of who the best sources are and where to find documents that will answer questions and provide the details to make great stories.

商业报道还需要了解企业的运营方式，这就好比校园记者需要知道学校董事会的运作机制及开会时间一样。企业通常以守口如瓶、不愿提供信息而著称，了解企业何时有义务披露信息能让记者占据优势。当企业高管看到记者具备相关知识时，会更愿意与之交谈。

<!--en-->
Business reporting also requires knowing something about how business operates, much like the school reporter needs to know how the school board works and when it meets. Businesses have a reputation of being tight-lipped and unwilling to provide information. Knowing when they are required to provide information can give reporters an edge. Sources such as company executives will be more willing to talk when they see the reporter as a knowledgeable person.

有时，上市公司与私有公司的界限会变得模糊，而这并非仅限于商业记者。一家上市公司的CEO也可能拥有可能受该上市公司业绩影响的私有企业。当监管机构因前HealthSouth公司CEO理查德·斯克鲁希涉嫌虚报这家康复医疗公司的盈利而对他展开调查时，他们还试图冻结其私有企业的资产。

<!--en-->
Sometimes, the worlds of public and private companies overlap, and not just for the business reporter. The CEO of a public company may also own private businesses that could be affected by the performance of the public corporation. When regulators went after former HealthSouth CEO Richard Scrushy for allegedly inflating earnings at the medical rehabilitation company, they sought to freeze the assets at his private businesses, too.

另一个例子是，卡罗莱纳飓风队冰球队的老板在一场电话会议上被问及他的上市公司（Compuware）是否正在出售，如果出售的话会如何影响他对这支私有冰球队的所有权。

<!--en-->
In another example, the owner of the Carolina Hurricanes hockey team was asked questions during a conference call about whether his public company (Compuware) was for sale and, if so, how that might affect his ownership of the privately held hockey business:

在关闭部分青少年冰球业务几天后，卡罗莱纳飓风队老板彼得·卡曼诺斯表示，有人向他提议出售其软件公司Compuware的部分股份。卡曼诺斯确认自己确实与其他公司讨论过出售事宜，但他并不打算拆分Compuware。

<!--en-->
Days after shutting down part of his youth hockey operation, Carolina Hurricanes owner Peter Karmanos said he had been approached about selling part of his software company, Compuware. Karmanos confirmed he had spoken with other companies about a sale but had no interest in breaking up Compuware.

“该公司不会出售，其任何业务部门也不会出售，”卡曼诺斯在周三与分析师们讨论Compuware第四季度业绩的电话会议中表示。“有一些人询问过，仅此而已。各种各样的人都会来打听……目前并没有正在进行的正式讨论。”道琼斯新闻社报道称，BMC Software和德州太平洋集团可能是Compuware部分股份的潜在买家。

<!--en-->
"The company is not up for sale, and divisions of the company are not up for sale," Karmanos said in a conference call with analysts Wednesday to discuss Compuware's fourth-quarter earnings. "Some people have inquired. That's about it. All kinds of people inquire. . . . There's no active discussiongoing on at this point in time.” The Dow Jones news service reported that BMC Software and Texas Pacific Group were potential buyers for part of Compuware.
