<!--en-->
Public and Private and Ethics, Oh My! • 23

在过去的3年半里，由于Compuware的股价暴跌，卡曼诺斯的净资产也大幅缩水。根据美国证券交易委员会的备案信息，卡曼诺斯持有Compuware的1570万股股票，价值约7500万美元。而Compuware的整体估值约为18亿美元。

<!--en-->
Over the past 3½ years, Karmanos has seen his net worth take a beating as Compuware’s stock has plummeted. According to SEC filings, Karmanos owns 15.7 million shares of Compuware, worth about $75 million. Compuware is valued at about $1.8 billion.

1973年，卡曼诺斯与两位朋友共同创立了Compuware。作为家乡底特律青少年冰球的长期支持者，他在1994年买下了NHL的哈特福德鲸鱼队，并于1997年将该球队迁至北卡罗来纳州，改名为卡罗莱纳飓风队。¹上市公司与私有公司每天都在相互交流。上市公司向私有公司销售产品和服务，反之亦然。在很多方面，上市公司与私有公司的成败是紧密相连的。如果存在业务合作关系，一家公司就会希望其合作伙伴能够成功。如果合作方无法盈利，就可能无力支付账单，进而影响到自身。而且这两种类型的公司对美国经济都至关重要。私有公司的数量远远多于上市公司。想想一个社区里的所有小型企业，无论是个体店铺还是拥有1000名员工的工厂，几乎全是私有企业。

<!--en-->
Karmanos founded Compuware with two friends in 1973. Long a supporter of youth hockey in his hometown of Detroit, he purchased the Hartford Whalers NHL franchise in 1994 and moved the team to North Carolina to become the Hurricanes in 1997.¹
Public and private companies interact with each other on a daily basis. Public companies sell their products and services to private companies, and vice versa. In many ways, the success of public companies and private companies are intertwined. If there is a business relationship, a company will want its business partner to succeed. If the business that a company is working with does not succeed, then it may not be able to pay its bills, which could hurt the company. And both types of companies are vitally important to the U.S. economy. There are many more private companies than there are public companies. Think of all of the small businesses in a community, whether they are one-person shops or factories with 1,000 workers. Virtually all of them are private companies.

但再想想那些你最常购买产品的公司：耐克的鞋子、The Gap的服装、可口可乐的饮料、戴尔的电脑、微软的软件、通用汽车的汽车、D.R. Horton建造的住宅、雪佛龙的汽油。所有这些公司都是上市公司，其股票每天都由投资者进行交易。

<!--en-->
But think about the companies providing products you may buy the most: shoes from Nike, clothes from The Gap, drinks from Coca-Cola, computers from Dell, software from Microsoft, cars from General Motors, a home from D.R. Horton, gasoline from Chevron. All of these companies are public companies with stock that is traded by investors every day.

### 为何上市公司在报道中占据主导地位

<!--en-->
*Why Public Companies Dominate Coverage*

正如本章开头所述，大多数中大型报纸的财经报道都集中在上市公司上。MarketWatch.com和TheStreet.com等网络新闻网站以及电视台也同样关注上市公司。纽约、华盛顿等大都市地区的报纸，其大部分报道内容也是关于上市公司。原因很简单：对于记者和编辑而言，可用于撰写上市公司相关报道的信息量远多于私营企业。上市公司依法必须披露信息，而这些信息往往是一些高管不愿公开的内容。而大多数私营企业则没有此类限制。

<!--en-->
As mentioned at the beginning of this chapter, most medium- and large-sized newspapers focus their business coverage on public companies. Internet news sites, such as MarketWatch.com and TheStreet.com, and television stations also focus on public companies. Newspapers in major metropolitan areas, such as New York and Washington, spend the bulk of their coverage on public businesses. The reason behind this is simple: For the reporters and editors, there is more information available with which to write stories about public companies than there is about private companies. Public companies are required by law to disclose information. Many times, it is information that executives may not want to disclose. Most private companies are under no such restrictions.

如前所述，上市公司受美国证券交易委员会（SEC）的监管。该联邦机构成立于1934年，旨在保护投资者免受那些哄骗人们购买无价值股票的不良企业的侵害。SEC的监管方式之一是……

<!--en-->
As mentioned earlier, public companies are regulated by the SEC, a federal agency created in 1934 to provide protection for investors against unscrupulous companies who dupe people into buying worthless stock. One of the ways the

### 专家建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

*阿拉巴马州亨茨维尔《Times》报前商业版编辑谢莉·哈斯金斯给刚接触商业报道的人的建议：***要分清新闻与广告的区别：**在介绍一家企业或产品时，务必确保其中具有新闻价值。我们的广告部门靠吸引广告收入来盈利，而当你撰写关于企业的文章时，则要确保能为读者提供有价值的内容——它是如何度过艰难时期的？企业主采用了哪些策略来让员工和客户满意？同时，要谨慎报道那些全新的企业，因为它们的商业计划尚未经过时间检验。[^333]：¹ 来自L. DeCock所写的《“飓风”公司老板称其公司不出售》，发表于2003年5月9日的《The News & Observer》报，C1版。版权所有2003年《罗利新闻与观察家报》，经许可转载。

<!--en-->
*Former Huntsville (Ala.) Times business editor Shelly Haskins on newcomers to business coverage:***Know the difference between news and advertising:** When you profile a business or a product, make sure there is news value there. Our advertising side gets paid to bring in ads. When you write about a business, make sure there is something there for your readers. How did it survive rough times? What strategies do the owners use to keep their employees and customers happy? And be careful about profiling brand new businesses. Their business plan hasn’t stood the test of time.

### 专家建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

阿拉巴马州亨茨维尔《Times》报前商业版编辑谢莉·哈斯金斯给刚接触商业报道的人的建议：尽量带读者了解幕后情况：当丰田选择在亨茨维尔为其畅销的Tundra卡车生产发动机时，这项交易——如同其他所有重大经济发展项目一样——都是在保密状态下完成的。交易结束后，运用你的报道技巧还原这笔交易的来龙去脉。你可能会发现一些有趣甚至令人捧腹的轶事，比如要搞定塔吉特公司的配送中心需要多少打格林布里尔烧烤店的炸鸡，还能了解招聘流程的运作方式。

<!--en-->
Former Huntsville (Ala.) Times business editor Shelly Haskins on newcomers to business coverage:Try to take the reader behind the scenes: When Toyota chose Huntsville to build the engine for its popular Tundra truck, the deal—like all other big economic development projects—was done behind closed doors. When it’s over, use your reporting skills to reconstruct how the deal came down. You’ll get some revealing and even fun anecdotes, such as how many dozen hushpuppies from Greenbrier Barbecue does it take to land a Target Corporation distribution center, and insight into how the recruiting process works.

SEC通过要求那些股票上市的公司提供任何人都能阅读的信息，来履行保护投资者和维护股市诚信的职责。例如，公司必须每季度在指定期限内提交财务业绩报告。上市公司还须向SEC提交文件，披露重要事件，如并购或审计师变更等。此外，SEC还监管投资行业中的其他参与者，包括股票和共同基金的交易商，以及那些将股票集中购买形成基金以降低投资者风险的大型资金管理公司。这些公司同样需要向公众披露信息。

<!--en-->
SEC has gone about its job of protecting investors and maintaining the integrity of the stock markets by requiring companies with publicly traded stock to provide information that anyone can read. For example, financial performance must be filed every quarter by a certain deadline. Public companies are also required to file documents with the SEC to disclose important events, such as mergers, acquisitions, or changes in auditors. In addition, the SEC regulates other parties involved in the investment industry, including companies who buy and sell stocks and mutual funds, like large money management companies who pool stock purchases into funds to limit the risk for investors. These companies are also required to disclose information to the public.

虽然这些文件是为了让投资者决定是否投资该公司的股票而准备的，但任何人都可以在其网站上查看www.sec.gov.。越来越多的公司也开始在自己的网站上提供SEC文件查阅服务。这些将在后续章节中详细介绍的文件，对于撰写有关公司及其他商业主题报道的记者来说，是极为宝贵的信息来源。它们常常包含许多有趣的细节，比如关于诉讼以及离职高管的遣散费等信息，而这些都是公司必须详细披露的。

<!--en-->
Although these filings are intended for investors to decide whether they want to put their money in the company’s stock, the documents are available for anyone to read on the SEC’s website at www.sec.gov. Increasingly, companies have started providing access to their SEC filings on their websites as well. These documents, detailed in later chapters, can be invaluable sources of information for reporters writing stories about companies and other business topics. They are often filled with interesting revelations, such as information about lawsuits and severance packages for departing executives, both of which companies are required to detail.

如果SEC根据这些文件认为某家公司或个人违反了其规定，它就会展开调查。通常，SEC会对该企业或个人未来参与上市公司业务或股票交易的行为处以罚款或设置限制。SEC的工作人员在五名由总统任命的委员的监督下，会在认定需要新法规时制定规则。一旦提出新规，SEC会邀请各公司及其他相关方对提案发表意见。这些意见可供任何记者查阅，如果公司反对新法规，往往能构成一篇有趣的报道素材。

<!--en-->
If the SEC believes, on the basis of the filings, that a company or someone has violated its rules, it will investigate. Often, the SEC will levy fines or set restrictions on the future involvement of that business or person in public companies or trading stocks. The staff of the SEC—overseen by five commissioners who are appointed by the president—writes rules when it determines that new regulations are needed. Once a rule is proposed, the SEC invites companies and others to comment on the proposal. These comments are available for review by any reporter and can often make for an interesting story, particularly if companies are opposed to the new regulations.

近年来，美国证券交易委员会通过的最重要的规则之一——至少对撰写上市公司相关报道的记者而言——便是2000年生效的公平披露规则（Fair Disclosure，简称FD）。该规则要求上市公司必须同时向所有投资者提供信息。因此，这些公司会公开管理层与投资者及分析师通过电话或互联网进行的沟通内容，并提交更多SEC备案文件。记者可以像其他人一样收听这些业绩电话会议、参加投资者大会的演讲，并阅读相关备案文件。

<!--en-->
One of the most important rules—at least for reporters writing stories about public companies—passed by the SEC in recent years is Regulation Fair Disclosure (FD), which went into effect in 2000. Regulation FD requires public companies to provide information to every investor at the same time. This has resulted in companies providing access to discussions their managements have with investors and analysts by telephone or Internet and to more SEC filings. Reporters can listen to these earnings conference calls, attend presentations at investor conferences, and read the filings along with everyone else.

另一项重要的SEC法规为商业记者提供了了解公司内部运作的途径。每家上市公司都必须每年召开一次股东周年大会。会议邀请函以SEC备案文件的形式发送给公司的每一位股东，即便他们仅持有1股股票。事实上，过去许多商业记者或商业新闻部门会为他们所报道的每家公司购买1股股票，以确保能收到这份邀请函。

<!--en-->
Another important SEC regulation provides business reporters with access to the inner workings of a company. Each public corporation is required to hold an annual meeting of its shareholders once a year. The invitation to the meeting is in the form of an SEC filing that is sent to every shareholder of the company, even if they just own one share of stock. In fact, many business journalists or business news departments in the past would purchase one share of stock for each company they covered to make sure they received this invitation.

通常所说的股东周年大会多在该公司总部附近或总部所在地举行，但有时也会在其他办公地点召开。安海斯-布希和通用电气等大型企业会在其不同办公地点轮流举办年度股东大会。例如，安海斯-布希更倾向于在其主题公园和酿酒厂举办此类会议。

<!--en-->
The annual meeting, as it is commonly known, is often held near or at the company’s headquarters, but sometimes it may be held at another company location. Large corporations, such as Anheuser-Busch and General Electric, rotate the location of their annual meeting among their various locations. Anheuser-Busch, for example, prefers to hold its meetings at its theme parks and breweries.

公众与私营领域及伦理问题，哎呀！•25 虽然法律并未明确要求邀请记者参加股东周年大会，但实际上几乎所有上市公司都允许记者出席。

<!--en-->
Public and Private and Ethics, Oh My! • 25
Although journalists are not specifically invited to annual meetings by law, virtually every public company allows reporters to attend the meetings.

在这些会议上，公司会讨论一些业务相关事宜。例如，可能会选举审计师来审核公司的账目，或者选任新的董事会成员。即使未亲自参加会议，每位股东也可以对会议上提出的提案进行投票。股东还可以提出提案供股东大会表决，因此在会议前做好调研非常重要。这些提案会详细列在会议邀请函中，即代理委托书。在代理委托书中，股东会解释他们的提案内容以及为何认为其对公司有益。公司通常会作出回应，表明支持或反对该提案。上市公司与股东之间的此类分歧很常见，但这些提案往往能成为不错的报道素材，或是用于阐述更大趋势故事的案例。以下是可口可乐2009年致股东的邀请函中一份股东提案的示例：

<!--en-->
At these meetings, the companies discuss some of their business. For example, an auditor may be elected to review the company's books, or new board members may be chosen. Each shareholder can vote on the proposals presented at the annual meeting, even if they do not attend the meeting. Shareholders can also make proposals to be voted on at the annual meeting, so it is important to do some homework before the event. These proposals are detailed in the invitation to the meeting, which is known as the proxy statement. In the proxy statement, the shareholders explain their proposal and why they think it is good for the company. The company usually responds and states whether it supports or opposes the proposal. Such conflict is common between public companies and shareholders, but these proposals often make good stories or serve as examples and anecdotes for a larger trend story. Here is an example of a shareholder proposal in Coca-Cola's 2009 invitation to its shareholders:

国际卡车司机兄弟会普通基金，地址：华盛顿特区西北路易斯安那大道25号，邮编20001，持有100股普通股，提交了如下提案：

<!--en-->
International Brotherhood of Teamsters General Fund, 25 Louisiana Avenue, N.W., Washington D.C. 20001, owner of 100 shares of Common Stock, submitted the following proposal:

**决议：**可口可乐公司（以下简称“可口可乐”或“该公司”）的股东要求董事会制定一项政策，规定董事会主席必须是此前未曾担任过可口可乐高管职务的独立董事。该政策的实施不得违反任何合同义务。此外，该政策还应明确：(a) 若现任主席在两次股东周年大会之间不再具备独立性，应如何选出新的独立主席；以及(b) 若没有愿意担任主席的独立董事，则可免除遵守该政策的义务。

<!--en-->
**RESOLVED:** That stockholders of The Coca-Cola Company ("Coca-Cola" or "the Company") ask the Board of Directors to adopt a policy that the Board's chairman be an independent director who has not previously served as an executive officer of Coca-Cola. The policy should be implemented so as not to violate any contractual obligation. The policy should also specify: (a) how to select a new independent chairman if a current chairman ceases to be independent during the time between annual meetings of shareholders; and, (b) that compliance with the policy is excused if no independent director is available and willing to serve as chairman.

**支持声明：**董事会有责任通过对管理层进行独立监督来保护股东的长期利益。通过确定议程、优先事项和流程，主席一职在塑造董事会的工作方向方面起着至关重要的作用。因此，我们认为拥有独立主席有助于确保董事会能够客观、高效地运作。

<!--en-->
**SUPPORTING STATEMENT:** It is the responsibility of the Board of Directors to protect shareholders' long-term interests by providing independent oversight of management. By setting agendas, priorities and procedures, the position of Chair is critical in shaping the work of the Board. Accordingly, we believe that having an independent Chairman can help ensure the objective functioning of an effective board.

独立主席还能在公司高层管理层变动期间提供稳定性和连续性，而这正是我们公司极为关注的问题。仅在过去的十年里，可口可乐就更换了三位主席兼首席执行官，导致董事会和管理层出现领导真空。

<!--en-->
An independent Chairman can also provide stability and continuity during senior management transitions, a major concern at our Company. Coca-Cola has churned through three Chairman/CEOs in just the past decade, creating a leadership vacuum at the Board and management levels.

去年，可口可乐在12年内任命了第五位首席执行官，作为此次变革的一部分，公司还将主席和首席执行官的职位分开了。自2008年7月1日起，前总裁兼首席运营官穆塔尔·肯特接替伊斯德尔担任首席执行官，而伊斯德尔则继续担任主席，直至2009年的股东周年大会。

<!--en-->
This past year Coca-Cola appointed its fifth chief executive in 12 years, this time separating the positions of Chairman and CEO as part of the transition. Effective July 1, 2008, Muhtar Kent (former President and Chief Operating Officer) succeeded Isdell as CEO, and Isdell continues as Chairman until the 2009 Annual Meeting.

虽然我们认可可口可乐暂时将主席和首席执行官的职位分开的做法，但该公司尚未制定明确的公司治理政策来禁止首席执行官同时兼任主席一职。

<!--en-->
While we acknowledge Coca-Cola's temporary separation of the positions of Chairman and CEO, our Company has not adopted a clearcorporate governance policy barring the CEO from simultaneously serving as Chairman.

26 • 公众与私营领域及伦理问题，哎呀！

<!--en-->
26 • Public and Private and Ethics, Oh My!

此外，仅仅将董事长与首席执行官的职位分开并不足以确保董事会具备独立的领导力，因而也无法实现对管理层的严格独立监督。我们的公司前首席执行官、自1966年起便在可口可乐体系工作的Isdell董事长并非独立人士。

<!--en-->
Furthermore, merely separating the positions of Chairman and CEO fails to ensure independent board leadership and, therefore, stops short of instituting rigorous independent oversight of management. Chairman Isdell, our Company's former CEO who has been with the Coca-Cola system since 1966, is not independent.

## 反对关于设立独立董事会主席的股东提案的声明

<!--en-->
*Statement Against Shareowner Proposal Regarding an Independent Board Chair*

该提案旨在永久分离董事会主席与首席执行官的职责，并要求董事会主席必须是由未曾担任过公司高管职务的独立董事担任。

<!--en-->
The proposal seeks to permanently separate the roles of Chairman of the Board and Chief Executive Officer and requests that the Board Chairman be an independent director who has not previously served as an executive officer of the Company.

我们现有的治理结构允许董事会在认为情况需要且不同的领导结构更有利于股东利益时，对公司的领导架构进行调整。

<!--en-->
Our existing governance structure allows the Board to make changes in the Company's leadership structure when and if it believes circumstances so warrant and shareowner interests would be better served by a different leadership structure.

根据业务的具体需求灵活确定合适的架构至关重要，这是董事会应当行使且我们认为未来也应继续行使的判断力的一部分。

<!--en-->
This flexibility to ensure the right structure based on the specific needs of the business is critical, and it is part of the judgment a board should exercise and we believe should continue to exercise in the future.

董事会已表明，它会在最有利于股东利益的情况下审慎行使这一判断力，事实上最近也确实分离了董事长与首席执行官的职责。2007年，董事会批准了一项新的架构，根据该架构，总裁兼首席运营官Muhtar Kent于2008年7月1日接替E. Neville Isdell担任首席执行官。董事会的意图是让Isdell先生继续担任董事会主席，直至2009年4月的公司年度股东大会。

<!--en-->
The Board of Directors has demonstrated that it will prudently exercise this judgment when shareowner interests are best served and, in fact, recently separated the roles of Chairman and CEO. In 2007, the Board approved a new structure wherein President and Chief Operating Officer Muhtar Kent succeeded E. Neville Isdell as Chief Executive Officer on July 1, 2008. It is the intent of the Board that Mr. Isdell remain as Chairman of the Board of Directors until the Company's Annual Meeting of Shareowners in April 2009.

这一架构被视为推动公司发展并确保领导层顺利过渡的合适选择。它也体现了现有治理结构下董事会所拥有的灵活性。此外，董事会的董事与公司治理委员会主席James D. Robinson III先生还负责主持所有非管理层董事的会议。

<!--en-->
This was seen as the appropriate structure to take the Company forward and ensure a successful leadership transition. It also reflects the flexibility available to the Board under the existing governance structure. In addition, the Chairman of the Committee on Directors and Corporate Governance of the Board, Mr. James D. Robinson III, presides over all meetings of non-management Directors.

那种会束缚董事会手脚的、有明确规定的做法从长远来看并不会为股东带来好处。

<!--en-->
A specifically defined approach that ties the Board's hands will not serve shareowners well over time.

我们鼓励股东通过我们的网站www.thecoca-colacompany.com.了解更多关于公司治理实践的信息。

<!--en-->
We encourage shareowners to learn more about the Company's governance practices at our website, www.thecoca-colacompany.com.

**董事会建议投票反对关于设立独立董事会主席的提案。²**在阅读了可口可乐提交的这份提案后，记者可能会觉得有必要撰写一篇探讨该公司高管团队的报道。或者记者也可以利用该提案来研究该公司的高管招聘机制。[^364]：² 来自可口可乐公司于2009年3月5日提交的DEF14A表格，美国证券交易委员会公开文件编号为0001047469-09-002248，发布地：华盛顿特区，美国证券交易委员会。

<!--en-->
**The Board of Directors recommends a vote AGAINST the proposal regarding an independent board chair.²**
After reading this proposal in Coca-Cola's filing, a reporter might feel there is a story to be written examining the company's executive team. Or a reporter could use the proposal to examine the company's practice of hiring executives.
[^364]: ² From Form DEF14A, by the Coca-Cola Company, March 5, 2009, SEC Publication No. 0001047469-09-002248. Washington, D.C.: Securities and Exchange Commission.

公开与私密以及道德问题，哎呀！• 27 年度股东大会也是记者们值得参加的活动，因为首席执行官及其他高管通常会就公司的过往表现及未来发展方向进行汇报，并回答在场人员的提问。如果公司规模较小，与会股东可能不多，记者便能提出更多问题，从而获得比通过电话或联系公司公关人员时更坦诚的答复。其他公司则会在年度股东大会结束后安排时间让高管们与媒体见面。记者参加这些会议会很有价值。记者越能经常露面给高管们看，表明自己有兴趣了解公司及其运营状况，首席执行官或总裁下次接到该记者的电话时就越有可能回答问题。

<!--en-->
Public and Private and Ethics, Oh My! • 27
Annual meetings are also good for reporters to attend because the CEO and other executives will often make a presentation about the company's past performance and future direction and take questions from those in attendance. If the company is small, there might not be many shareholders in the audience and the reporter might be able to ask a lot of questions, getting more candid answers from executives than if the reporter had tried calling or going through the company's public relations staff. Other companies will set aside time after the annual meeting for its executives to meet with the media. These meetings can be valuable for a reporter to attend. The more time a reporter can show his or her face to an executive and demonstrate that he is interested in learning about a company and its operations, the more likely the CEO or president will answer questions the next time that reporter calls by phone.

股东在会议上提出的问题也能激发报道灵感。一些大型公司年度股东大会上的问答环节可能会持续数小时。有些股东可能因公司业绩不佳而感到愤怒，会向首席执行官和总裁提出尖锐的问题，询问他们将如何扭转局面。还有些股东希望公司能投身环保事业。甚至有一些股东每年会参加数十场年度股东大会，只为斥责高管并要求其提升业绩。其中最著名的是来自华盛顿特区的Evelyn Y. Davis，她为股东撰写新闻简报，曾对一位首席执行官说他的长相比他的前任更好看。

<!--en-->
Questions asked by the shareholders at the meeting can also elicit story ideas. The question-and-answer period at some large company annual meetings can last for hours. Some shareholders may be angry about a company's poor performance and may ask the CEO and president pointed questions about how they are going to turn it around. Others may want the company to take on an environmental cause. There are even shareholders who attend dozens of annual meetings a year simply to harangue executives and ask for better performance. The most famous of these is Evelyn Y. Davis, a Washington, D.C. resident, who writes a newsletter for shareholders and who once told a CEO that he was better looking than his predecessor.

此外，年度股东大会往往能反映一家公司当前的状况。如果在年度大会上出现大量负面问题，说明该公司过去业绩较好，股东希望其重回那种水平；如果负面问题较少，则表明该公司财务状况良好，且能充分照顾到股东的利益。通过观察与会者及高管的情绪，可以了解一家公司的未来走向以及过往表现。

<!--en-->
In addition, an annual meeting can often act as a barometer of a company's current standing. If there are many negative questions asked at an annual meeting, likely the business performed better in the past and shareholders would like the corporation to return to that level. If there are few negative questions, the company has likely been performing well financially and with the interest of its shareholders in the fore. Watch the mood of the attendees and the executives to get a feel for where a company is headed and where it has been.

对于任何大众媒体而言，尤其是地区性或地方性刊物，上市公司都是重要的新闻来源，因为许多当地居民可能是该公司的股东。由于许多公司会为员工提供股票持有计划，这些员工也很可能成为股东，并希望从独立渠道获取公司相关信息。例如在亚特兰大，就有数千名居民持有可口可乐的股票，而家得宝则让数百名门店员工成为了百万富翁。在全国其他地区，如西雅图，微软的股票也让除比尔·盖茨之外的许多人变得富有。查明您所在发行区域的居民持有哪些股票，这些很可能是他们会想阅读相关报道的公司。

<!--en-->
Public companies are a vital part of news for any mass communication outlet, particularly regional or local publications, because many area residents are likely shareholders of the company. Because many companies offer their employees stock ownership plans, the workers are also likely shareholders who would want to know information about the company from an independent source. In Atlanta, for example, thousands of residents own stock in Coca-Cola, and Home Depot has made millionaires out of hundreds of its store employees. The same situation exists across the country in the Seattle area, where Microsoft's stock has made many people, in addition to Bill Gates, rich. Find out which stocks are owned by residents in your circulation or distribution area. Those are likely to be the companies that they will want to read about.

### 私营企业主导着当地经济

<!--en-->
*Private Companies Dominate Local Economies*

另一方面，私营企业无需公开与股东讨论分歧，也不会举办记者可参加的年度股东大会。不过，对于报道商业新闻的任何大众媒体而言，私营企业对读者或观众来说同样至关重要。规模最大的

<!--en-->
Private companies, on the other hand, are not required to discuss disagreements with their shareholders in public, and they do not hold annual meetings that reporters can attend. Still, private companies are vital to the readers or viewers of any mass communication outlet that reports on business news. The largest

### 专家建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

*前《诺福克维吉尼亚飞行员报》商业版编辑比尔·乔伊克谈商业写作技巧：*

<!--en-->
*Former Norfolk Virginian-Pilot business editor Bill Choyke on the craft of business writing:*

**先理解再写作：**我承认有这个毛病；不幸的是我们都犯过。在写作之前务必弄清楚消息来源/专家的观点是什么。如果有疑问，就去询问。如果还是不确定，就不要使用该信息。如果您自己都不明白某个概念的含义，就不要要求读者去理解它。

<!--en-->
**Understand before you write:** I plead guilty; unfortunately we all have done it. Make sure you know what the source/expert is saying before you write it. If in doubt, ask. If still in doubt, don't use it. Don't ask the reader to understand something if you have no idea what it means.

#### 专家建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

*前《诺福克维吉尼亚飞行员报》商业版编辑比尔·乔伊克谈商业写作技巧：*

<!--en-->
*Former Norfolk Virginian-Pilot business editor Bill Choyke on the craft of business writing:*

**不要把笔记写满：**广泛收集素材，但写作时要根据新闻内容来调整——要让内容贴合新闻本身。抵制倾倒所有信息的冲动，要有选择地确定重点和目的。

<!--en-->
**Don't empty your notebook:** Report extensively, but write to fit—fit the news. Resist the urge to unload everything. Be selective with focus and purpose.

28 • 公司、私营企业与伦理问题！

<!--en-->
28 • Public and Private and Ethics, Oh My!

#### 专家建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

前阿拉巴马州亨茨维尔《时报》商业版编辑谢莉·哈斯金斯给刚接触商业报道的人的建议：

<!--en-->
Former Huntsville (Ala.) Times business editor Shelly Haskins on newcomers to business coverage:

**别忽视小型企业：**要特别努力去报道小型企业。它们提供了85%的就业岗位，却得不到像大型企业那样的关注。鼓励企业主向您提供有关近期员工培训或行业荣誉的信息——这不仅能让您了解他们的成功经验，还能为您的文章提供素材。

<!--en-->
**Don't forget small business:** Make a special effort to profile small businesses. They provide 85 percent of the jobs, but don't get as much attention as the large employers. Encourage business owners to send you information on recent employee training or industry honors—it will give you a peek into their success, as well as provide fodder for briefs.

#### 专家建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

前《诺福克维吉尼亚飞行员报》商业版编辑比尔·乔伊克谈商业写作技巧：

<!--en-->
Former Norfolk Virginian-Pilot business editor Bill Choyke on the craft of business writing:

**在报道框架内发挥创造力：**多做报道，然后再创造性地思考如何在既定的报道框架内呈现材料。美国的私营企业包括克莱斯勒这样的汽车制造商、普华永道和安永这样的会计事务所、玛氏这样的糖果制造商、玩具反斗城这样的零售商以及Publix Super Markets这样的连锁超市——这些都是以各种方式影响我们生活的企业。它们都是价值数十亿美元的大型企业，规模与许多上市公司相当甚至更大。

<!--en-->
**Be creative within the parameters of your reporting:** Report, report, report, and then think creatively how you can creatively present your material within the parameters of your reporting.
private companies in the country include businesses such as automaker Chrysler, accounting firms PricewaterhouseCoopers and Ernst & Young, candy maker Mars, retailer Toys “R” Us and grocery store chain Publix Super Markets—all businesses that have touched our lives in one way or another. These are multibillion-dollar corporations equal or larger in size to many of their public competitors.

事实上，美国有超过440家年收入超过10亿美元的私营企业。据《福布斯》杂志报道，这些企业总共拥有超过610万名员工，为其国家经济贡献了超过1.8万亿美元的产品和服务价值。

<!--en-->
In fact, there are more than 440 private companies in the United States with more than $1 billion in annual revenue. According to *Forbes* magazine, these companies have more than 6.1 million employees combined and contribute more than $1.8 trillion in products and services to the country's economy.

再想想那些存在于您日常生活中的企业，比如街角的加油站、当地的银行分行，或是您今晚可能会去吃的市中心的餐厅。这些企业很可能是私人所有的企业，可能只由一个人或少数几名投资者持有，而且他们根本不打算向公众出售股票。每有一家上市公司，就可能对应着几十家私营竞争对手。这些企业，尤其是在中小城镇，很可能是当地最大的雇主。许多当地医院也是私有的，工厂和制造企业也是如此。尽管是私营企业，它们依然能构成引人入胜的故事，让读者和观众想要了解。

<!--en-->
Think again about the businesses that are part of your everyday life, such as the corner gas station, the local bank branch, or the restaurant downtown where you might eat dinner tonight. Chances are these businesses are privately held enterprises owned by maybe just one person or a handful of investors with no intention to ever sell shares of stock to the public. For every public company, there are likely to be dozens of private competitors. These companies, especially in small- and medium-sized towns and cities, could be the largest employers in the area. Many local hospitals are privately owned, as are factories and manufacturers. Yet despite their status as private companies, they can still make for compelling stories that readers and viewers will want to know about.

然而，要获取关于私营公司的信息需要做更多的工作。事实上，许多商业新闻领域的专家认为，报道上市公司更容易，因为解释一家公司及其战略所需的大部分信息都可以在美国证券交易委员会（SEC）的文件中找到。因此，记者若想成为顶尖的商业新闻人，也可以通过报道私营公司来积累经验，因为这类公司的信息极难获取，且公司高管可能不愿被曝光。

<!--en-->
However, there is more work involved in finding information about private companies. In fact, many business journalism experts believe that it is easier to write stories about public companies because much of the information needed to explain a company and its strategy is available in SEC documents. Thus, a reporter can earn his or her stripes as a top-notch business journalist by writing a story about a private company, because the information is much harder to find and company executives may not want the exposure.

关于私营公司的公开文件中仍有很多信息。虽然这些信息不一定都在SEC手中，但也有许多私营企业必须向该联邦监管机构提交文件。例如，那些向投资者发行债券的私营企业即便仍属于私营企业，也需向SEC提交文件。不过，还有许多其他途径可以获取有关私营企业的信息。所有企业都必须在其运营所在的州进行注册登记，通常由州务卿办公室或类似弗吉尼亚州的州公司委员会这样的监管机构负责办理。这些文件往往能告诉记者企业的所有者、高管是谁以及企业位于何处。

<!--en-->
There is still a lot of information to be found in public documents about private companies. It just may not necessarily be with the SEC, although there are many private businesses that do have to file documents with the federal regulatory agency. For example, private companies that have issued bonds to investors will file documents with the SEC although they are still considered private businesses. But there are plenty of other places to get information about private enterprises. All businesses have to incorporate themselves with the state in which they are operating. This is typically done with the Secretary of State's office or a regulatory entity such as the State Corporation Commission, as it is called in Virginia. These documents will often tell a reporter who owns the business, who the executives are, and where it is located.

其他州级监管机构也掌握着大量关于私营公司的信息。从理发店到银行，大多数企业都会以某种形式受到州级机构的监管。这些州级机构的档案中通常会记载企业的经营状况。美国劳工部下属的职业安全与健康管理局以及联邦贸易委员会等联邦机构也对数千家私营企业拥有管辖权。如果你正在撰写关于非上市企业的文章，这些地方都是值得寻找信息的场所。

<!--en-->
Other state regulatory agencies also have plenty of information about private companies. Most businesses, from barbershops to banks, are regulated in some form or another by a state agency. Many of these state agencies will have information about the business's performance in their files. Federal agencies, such as the Occupational Safety and Health Administration within the U.S. Department of Labor and the Federal Trade Commission, also have jurisdiction over thousands of private companies. They are worthy places to look for information if you are writing about a business with stock that is not publicly traded.

尽管大多数小型私营企业仅由一两个人拥有，但也有一些私营公司会吸引投资者，只不过方式并非像上市公司那样向投资者出售股票。许多寻求资金扩张的私营企业会去找专门投资小型企业的投资机构，这些机构通常提供所谓的风险资本融资。

<!--en-->
Although most small private businesses are owned by only one or two people, other private companies have solicited investors, just not in the sameway that public companies sell stock to investors. Many private businesses seeking capital to expand will go to investment firms that specifically invest in small operations. These firms provide what is typically known as venture capital funding.

公共与私人企业及伦理问题，哎呀！•29 风险资本机构会向私营企业提供资金——有时甚至是数百万美元——用于扩大业务规模。作为回报，私营企业的所有者会将其企业的一部分股权交给风险资本机构。风险资本机构的高管在投入资金后可能希望对企业运营方式拥有发言权。但他们更希望企业能妥善使用他们的资金，以审慎的方式扩大业务并创造更多利润，从而提升企业的价值。通常，一家风险资本机构会在其投资的私营企业中持有股份5到7年，之后将其出售给另一位投资者，或在首次公开募股时将所持股份卖给公众投资者，从而使这家私营企业变为上市公司。

<!--en-->
Public and Private and Ethics, Oh My! • 29
Venture capital firms give private companies money—sometimes millions of dollars—to expand their operations. In return, the owners of the private company give the venture capital operation an ownership stake in their business. The venture capital executives may want to have a say in how the company operates after they invest money. But they are hoping that the business will take their money and put it to good use, expanding their operations in a prudent manner and creating additional profits, making the private business more valuable. Often, a venture capital firm will sit on its investment in a private company for five to seven years and then sell it to another investor or sell its stake in the company to public investors in an initial public offering, making the private company a public operation.

在20世纪90年代，数十家风险资本机构投入了数十亿美元到私营企业中，期望能获得巨额投资回报。其中大部分资金流向了互联网、科技和电信行业的企业。然而，由于许多这类企业倒闭，导致风险资本投资者血本无归，如今这类投资在开展时都会更加谨慎。

<!--en-->
In the 1990s, dozens and dozens of venture capital firms poured billions of dollars into private businesses in the hopes that the money would provide huge investment returns. Much of that money went into Internet, technology, and telecommunications companies. However, because many of these companies went out of business, leaving venture capital investors with nothing in return, such investments are now done with closer scrutiny.

以下是《堪萨斯城星报》的一篇报道，介绍了中西部许多私营公司为吸引风险资本机构投资而经历的过程：

<!--en-->
Below is a story from the *Kansas City Star* that explains the process many private companies in the Midwest went through to try to entice venture capital firms to invest money into their companies:

如今，钱已经不再像过去那样容易赚到了。

<!--en-->
Money doesn’t grow on trees the way it used to.

风险资本家早已不再给刚认识的公司开支票，而且在很多情况下甚至完全不再开支票了。

<!--en-->
Venture capitalists have long since stopped scribbling out checks to companies they’ve just met. And in many instances they’ve stopped writing checks altogether.

根据普华永道对风险资本投资的季度调查，第一季度仅有38亿美元的风险资本被投入市场。这一数字创下了五年来的新低，远低于2000年第一季度的286亿美元。

<!--en-->
According to a quarterly survey of venture capital investment by PricewaterhouseCoopers, only $3.8 billion in venture capital was invested in the first quarter. That’s a five-year low, and a far cry from the $28.6 billion invested in the first quarter of 2000.

但这些数据似乎并未减弱周四上午在堪萨斯城举办的“InvestMidwest”风险资本论坛上那20家企业的热情，该论坛旨在为高成长型企业与投资者牵线搭桥。

<!--en-->
But those facts didn’t seem to dampen the enthusiasm of the 20 companies on stage Thursday morning at InvestMidwest, a venture capital forum in Kansas City designed to link high-growth companies with investors.

这项在堪萨斯城和圣路易斯轮流举办的第四届年度活动吸引了30多家风险投资公司的代表参与。来自美国中西部各地的公司各有10分钟时间介绍自己，并说明为何寻求风险投资。

<!--en-->
The fourth annual event, which alternates between Kansas City and St. Louis, drew representatives from more than 30 venture capital firms. Companies from throughout the Midwest got 10 minutes each to introduce themselves and explain why they were looking for venture financing.

堪萨斯城股权合伙公司的合伙人阿贝尔·莫希卡表示：“如果去年在堪萨斯城举办这场风险投资会议，那只会是无人问津的徒劳之举。根本不会有人来倾听。”

<!--en-->
"If we would have had this venture conference last year in Kansas City, it would have been voices in the wilderness," said Abel Mojica, a partner with Kansas City Equity Partners. "No one would have been here to listen."

但周四上午，在凯悦皇冠中心酒店宴会厅的桌旁，尽管投资者们手中的笔并未放在空白支票上，他们仍在认真聆听。

<!--en-->
But Thursday morning, sitting around tables in a hotel ballroom at the Hyatt Regency Crown Center hotel, investors were listening—even if their pens weren’t poised over blank checks.

“三年来他们一直缩头缩脑，不敢露面。”

<!--en-->
"For three years they’ve hunkered down and covered their heads up

#### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

阿拉巴马州亨茨维尔《时报》前商业编辑谢莉·哈斯金斯就新手从事商业报道给出建议：

<!--en-->
Former Huntsville (Ala.) Times business editor Shelly Haskins on newcomers to business coverage:

要关注行业趋势：例如，近年来阿拉巴马州吸引了几家汽车行业企业入驻——梅赛德斯、本田、丰田以及纳维斯塔。汽车行业能提供高薪工作，但汽车和卡车销量会随经济形势起伏。你所在地区的经济是否足够多元化，足以抵御经济衰退？为什么？

<!--en-->
Keep your eye out for trends: For example, Alabama has landed several auto industry companies in recent years—Mercedes, Honda, Toyota and Navistar. The auto industry provides high-paying jobs, but auto and truck sales go up and down with the economy. Is your local economy diversified enough to survive an economic downturn? Why, or why not?

“我们只是想先保护好自己，”圣路易斯科技公司ScenarioNow Inc.的大卫·拉森比说道。

<!--en-->
30 • Public and Private and Ethics, Oh My!
and said, 'We're just going to cover ourselves,'" said David Lazenby of ScenarioNow Inc., a St. Louis technology company.

向投资者做完演讲后，拉森比表示他相信情况终于开始好转。他说资金正在不断涌入，投资者们也开始重新露面。

<!--en-->
After making his presentation to investors, Lazenby said he was confident the situation was finally beginning to turn. Money has been piling up, he said, and investors are starting to uncover their heads.

阿拉巴马州亨茨维尔的Hickory风险投资公司的合伙人托马斯·马歇尔称，他的公司依然十分谨慎，和许多风险投资机构一样，可能会继续对早期的高风险投资保持高度警惕。

<!--en-->
Thomas Marshall, a partner with Hickory Venture Capital in Huntsville, Ala., said his firm was still very cautious and, like many venture firms, was likely to continue to be much more wary of risky early-stage investments.

他的公司要求潜在投资对象至少已拥有100万美元的收入。这已经不算早期阶段了。

<!--en-->
His firm wants potential investments to already have at least $1 million in revenue. Not exactly early stage.

芝加哥Duff & Phelps资本合伙公司的合伙人道格·埃利奥特表示，风险投资机构从过去两年中吸取了教训。他们正在寻找更好的投资机会——即获得更高的持股比例，而在经济疲软时期这类机会更容易出现。

<!--en-->
Doug Elliott, a partner with Duff & Phelps Capital Partners in Chicago, said venture firms had learned from the past two years. They're looking for better deals—a bigger ownership stake for their investments—which is easier to come by in lean times.

当然，投资者也在寻找下一个伟大的成功案例。“大家都在寻找下一个微软或安进这样的企业，”埃利奥特说。

<!--en-->
Of course, investors are also looking for the next big success story.
"Everyone's looking for the next Microsoft or Amgen," Elliott said.

各家公司似乎明白投资者的需求。他们在争取200万至1200万美元的资金时，着重展示了不断增长的收入、新客户以及未来的增长预期。

<!--en-->
Companies seemed to understand what the investors wanted. They pointed to rising revenue lines, new customers and estimates for continued growth as they made their pitches for funding in sums of $2 million to $12 million.

“2年半前我们就刻意决定专注于获取客户，而非盲目扩张，”拉森比说。

<!--en-->
"We intentionally made the decision 2½ years ago to focus on getting customers rather than growing," Lazenby said.

现在该公司在与投资者交谈时，可以拿出有力的销售数据和客户数量作为依据。

<!--en-->
Now the company can pull out figures for solid sales and customers when it talks to investors.

总部位于利奥伍德的电子邮件营销公司SoftVu的总裁兼首席执行官蒂姆·唐纳利最初是在自家地下室用极少的资金创业的。他认为这是自己的优势。

<!--en-->
Tim Donnelly, president and CEO of SoftVu, a Leawood company that specializes in e-mail marketing, started in his basement on a shoestring. He points to that as an advantage.

“那些获得了2000万、3000万甚至4000万美元融资的竞争对手，发展速度有点快过了头，”唐纳利说。“我们从我家地下室里的初创公司起步，能够在面临大规模投资之前，从一些艰难处境中积累经验。”

<!--en-->
"Our competitors who received 20, 30, 40 million dollars in capital went through it a little too quickly," Donnelly said. "We went from seed company in my basement, and we've been able to learn from some tough situations' before large investments were at stake."

周四进行展示的地区企业包括SoftVu、劳伦斯的Deciphera Pharmaceuticals Inc.、莱内克萨的Felton International Inc.和Chemidex、堪萨斯城的K2B Inc.、莱内克萨的Nexgenesis以及堪萨斯城的Proteon Therapeutics。³风险投资会议是结识本地小型私营企业主并了解这些公司的绝佳场所。在这些会议上，私营企业实际上是在试图向投资者出售自己的业务，这与上市公司向公众出售股票的方式类似。如果一家私营企业能获得风险投资机构的投资，这对商业记者来说就是一篇不错的新闻素材。这家企业会如何使用这笔钱？风险投资机构又会获得多少股份作为回报？

<!--en-->
The area firms making presentations Thursday were SoftVu, Deciphera Pharmaceuticals Inc. of Lawrence, Felton International Inc. of Lenexa, Chemidex of Lenexa, K2B Inc. of Kansas City, Nexgenesis of Lenexa, and Proteon Therapeutics of Kansas City.³
Venture capital meetings are great places to meet owners of small, local, private businesses and to get a feel for the companies. At these meetings, private companies are essentially trying to sell their business to investors, much the same way a public company does when it sells stock to the public. If a private company gets an investment from a venture capital firm, it can be a story for the business reporter. What will the company do with the money? How much of an ownership stake are the venture capital investors receiving in return?

私营公司的所有权形式多种多样。与许多上市公司一样，私营公司也常常向员工发放股票。在一家保险代理店或理发店这类私营企业中，可能由一个人掌控全部所有权。除了与企业相关的故事外，这些所有者本身也是极具价值的素材。作为企业主，他们通常对经济形势十分敏感，并会每天做出决策，比如是否该投入资金扩张，还是等待时机好转。如果商业记者要撰写关于所在社区经济状况的文章，私营企业主能提供最优质的采访对象。[^423]：³ 摘自S. King所写的《Companies make pitch for venture capital funds》，2003年5月23日，《堪萨斯城星报》，第C3版。版权所有2003年堪萨斯城星报公司，经许可转载。

<!--en-->
Ownership in private companies can come in all shapes and sizes. Privatecompanies also often offer shares to their employees, just like many public companies do. One person can control ownership in a private company, such as an insurance agency or a barbershop. These owners can be valuable resources for stories—besides those about their companies. As business owners, they are often cognizant of the economy and make decisions on a daily basis such as whether they should spend money to expand or hold back until times get better. If a business reporter is writing a story about economic conditions in his or her community, private business owners can give the best interviews.
[^423]: ³ From "Companies make pitch for venture capital funds," by S. King, May 23, 2003, *Kansas City Star*, p. C3. Copyright 2003 by the Kansas City Star Company. Reprinted with permission.

公有制、私营制与伦理问题，哎呀！• 31 此外，私营企业主们常常会组成诸如当地商会之类的团体。商业记者应当参加他们的活动并与之建立联系，因为谁也不知道这些人脉何时会派上用场。如前所述，每个社区中的私营企业数量都远多于上市公司。记者应当了解这些私营企业的具体情况及其运营状况，这样就能比仅与那些可能只有本地子公司、且子公司经理需向其他州或国家的上级汇报的上市公司高管交谈，获得更全面的区域情况了解。

<!--en-->
Public and Private and Ethics, Oh My! • 31
In addition, private business owners often band together in groups such as the local Chamber of Commerce. The business reporter should attend their functions and get to know them; one never knows when those contacts will come in handy. As mentioned earlier, private businesses far outnumber public companies in every community. The reporter should find out what these private businesses are and how they are doing, and he will likely get a better picture of the area than he would by talking to executives at a public company, which may only have a local subsidiary run by a manager who reports to higher-ups in another state or country.

### 撰写与商业相关的报道

<!--en-->
*Writing Business-Related Stories*

起初，撰写商业报道似乎令人望而生畏。这类报道充斥着各种数字，还使用诸如可调整利率抵押贷款或表外融资之类的术语，普通读者可能难以理解。此外，商业记者还需要确定该从哪些人那里获取信息来撰写文章。大型企业的CEO和总裁们都很忙碌，有时因心怀其他事务——比如经营企业——而显得对提问态度生硬。商业领域的其他消息来源也很难接触，更难进行采访。他们中的许多人并不需要与记者交谈，因为这并非其工作职责范围。不过，记者不应因此气馁。这些人当初对商业世界的了解也同样有限。通过一些经验和培训，记者就能像专家一样与这些消息来源交流，让他们敞开心扉，进而写出仿佛作者比企业高管更了解铜管行业的报道。

<!--en-->
Writing business stories appears daunting at first. They are filled with numbers and use terms, such as adjustable rate mortgage or off-balance sheet financing, that the average reader may not understand. And then there is the whole idea of whom a business reporter must interview to get the information to write a story. CEOs and presidents of large corporations are busy people and sometimes appear curt in responding to questions because they have other topics on their mind—like running their company. Other sources in the business world are also difficult to reach and even harder to interview. Many of them do not have to talk to a reporter; it is not part of their job description. However, a reporter should not get discouraged. These people started out with limited knowledge of the business world as well. With a little experience and some training, the reporter will be able to talk like an expert with these sources, opening them up, and will begin writing stories that read as if the writer knows more about the copper tubing industry than the company executive does.

商业报道的素材来源多种多样。一些最优秀的商业报道，是记者或编辑通过观察趋势、分析经济数据，或是长期跟踪某家公司数月甚至数年之后在脑海中构思出来的。出色的商业报道并不总是显而易见的，它们的报道和撰写都需要时间。如今大多数商业报道都来自基础资料，比如公司新闻稿或监管机构的公告。报道素材也可以来自公司提交的监管文件，或是法院受理的诉讼案及其他相关文件。

<!--en-->
Business stories can come from a number of different places. Some of the best business stories are developed in a reporter or editor's mind by watching trends and understanding economic numbers or by tracking a company for months or years at a time. Great business stories are not always readily apparent. They can take time to report and write. The bulk of business stories written today come from basic sources, such as company news releases or releases from regulatory agencies. Stories can also come from regulatory filings made by companies or from lawsuits or other documents filed in a courthouse.

报道素材也可能来自工会官员提供的线索，或是无意中听到他人对话的人。商业报道还可以通过参加分区规划委员会等会议获得。记者应当对自己负责的新闻领域有足够的了解，这样才能写出让读者感受到他们确实懂自己在讨论什么的报道。

<!--en-->
Stories can come from source tips such as union officials or from people who overheard a conversation. Business stories can also come from attending meetings such as zoning or planning commissions. Reporters should be knowledgeable enough about their beats to write stories that show the audience that they know what they are discussing.

#### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

*阿拉巴马州亨茨维尔《泰姆斯报》前商业版编辑谢莉·哈斯金斯对刚涉足商业报道领域的新人的建议：*

<!--en-->
*Former Huntsville (Ala.) Times business editor Shelly Haskins on newcomers to business coverage:*

**了解你所在社区的商界人士：**仅仅因为参加了商会活动并主动结识他人，并不意味着你就成了商会的走狗。如果消息来源认识你，他们才会更愿意为你提供信息。试想一下，如果一个你从未见过的人突然打电话给你，把你说的一切都记录下来用于发表，你会作何感想？许多商界人士并不信任媒体，而且大多也不需要与你交谈。因此要建立关系并赢得他们的信任。

<!--en-->
**Get to know the business people in your community:** Just because you go to the chamber functions and press the flesh doesn't mean that you're a chamber lackey. You'll get better results from sources if they know you. Imagine how you'd feel if someone you'd never met called you up cold and wrote down everything you said for publication. Many business people don't trust the media, and, for the most part, they don't have to talk to you. Establish relationships and build trust.

#### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

*阿拉巴马州亨茨维尔《泰姆斯报》前商业版编辑谢莉·哈斯金斯对刚涉足商业报道领域的新人的建议：*

<!--en-->
*Former Huntsville (Ala.) Times business editor Shelly Haskins on newcomers to business coverage:*

**阅读商业刊物以获取背景知识和报道灵感：**我经常能从《商业周刊》或《华尔街日报》中获得可以结合亨茨维尔实际情况的报道灵感。至少，这些刊物能让你了解当地的经济形势，或者为商会活动提供聊天话题。

<!--en-->
**Read business publications for background and story ideas:** More often than not, I'll come away from *BusinessWeek* or the *Wall Street Journal* with a story idea that can be localized to Huntsville. At the least, it gives you an idea of the economic landscape, or just conversation fodder for those chamber functions.

#### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

*《诺福克维吉尼亚飞行员报》前商业版编辑比尔·乔伊克关于商业写作技巧的观点：*

<!--en-->
*Former Norfolk Virginian-Pilot business editor Bill Choyke on the craft of business writing:*

**乐于接受反馈：** 不要抗拒建设性的批评，主动听取来自同事、朋友、家人甚至编辑的意见与建议。

<!--en-->
**Open yourself to feedback:** Don't resist constructive criticism and open yourself to ideas and suggestions or co-workers, friends and family, and even editors.

32 • 公共事务、隐私与伦理，天哪！

<!--en-->
32 • Public and Private and Ethics, Oh My!

#### 专家建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

前《诺福克维吉尼亚人导报》商业版编辑比尔·乔伊克谈商业写作技巧：

<!--en-->
Former Norfolk Virginian-Pilot business editor Bill Choyke on the craft of business writing:

**什么才是最佳故事？** 找出最有趣的发展动态、故事情节或趋势，然后集中精力报道，但要保持开放的心态。

<!--en-->
**What's the best story?** What's the most interesting development, story line or trend, and then focus, but keep an open mind.

#### 专家建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

前阿拉巴马州亨茨维尔《时报》商业版编辑谢莉·哈斯金斯为新入行的商业新闻记者提供指导：

<!--en-->
Former Huntsville (Ala.) Times business editor Shelly Haskins on newcomers to business coverage:

**仔细阅读自己报纸的附录内容：** 报纸在附录中刊登的信息往往很有价值。尤其是建筑许可信息，能让你了解大型住宅的建设方向以及正在进行的各类项目等。破产公告可能提示你某个行业正在衰退；法律广告则能反映所有权变更或税务纠纷情况。商业执照则能帮你发现值得报道的新商业趋势。有一位《亨茨维尔时报》的记者在商业执照续期名单中发现了一家名为“Clip at your Curb”的企业，这让他发现了“上门服务”这一新兴趋势——这类企业可以提供从洗车到洗狗的各种服务。另一家报纸的记者则得到消息，他们所在的城市正在被考虑作为新的电话营销中心的选址，该中心将创造450个新就业岗位。原来这家公司投放了数百个招聘电话技能人才的匿名广告，以此测试会有多少求职者回应。该报纸对此进行了报道，后来该城市确实吸引了这家新公司。

<!--en-->
**Read your own small print:** The stuff your own newspaper runs in agate can be gold. Building permits, particularly, can give you an idea of where the biggest homes are going, what kind of projects are underway, etc. Bankruptcy listings might tip you off to a declining business segment. Legal advertising can also signal changes in ownership, or who has tax liens. Business licenses can lead you to interesting new business trends to write about. One *Huntsville Times* writer found a business called "Clip at your Curb" in the business license renewals. That turned us onto a growing trend of "come to you" businesses that will do everything from washing your car to washing your dog. Another writer at another newspaper got a tip that their city was being considered as a potential site for a new telemarketing center, with 450 new jobs. Seems the company placed a blind ad for hundreds of workers with phone skills—it was a test to see how many job seekers would respond. The newspaper did a story; the city later landed the new company.

理解公司或监管机构在新闻稿中的表述是工作的一部分。有时，最困难的部分是将这些新闻稿转化为普通读者能够理解的故事。新闻稿的问题在于它们有时由律师撰写或审核，因此语言可能不够清晰；或者其表述方式可能会淡化或掩盖真实新闻。例如，一家公司可能会发布新闻稿宣布每股派发20美分的季度股息，但却没有说明这一股息数额已低于前几个季度每股40美分的水平。又或者，一家公司可能会宣布为其主要产品推出新的广告活动，却未提及去年的广告完全失败且公司的口号也已更改。因此，任何记者都必须对其报道的主题进行深入研究。即便是最平常、最基础的声明，也可能隐藏着有待发现的新闻线索。

<!--en-->
Understanding what a company or regulatory agency is saying in a release is part of the job. Sometimes, the hardest part is translating the release into a story that the average reader can understand. The problem with news releases is that they are sometimes written or approved by lawyers, so the language may not be clear. Or the release can be written in such a way as to downplay or hide the actual news. A company could issue a release announcing its quarterly dividend of 20 cents per share. But what the release does not state is that the dividend has been reduced from the 40 cents per share the company was paying its shareholders in previous quarters. Or a company could announce a new advertising campaign for its major product without disclosing that its commercials from last year were a total flop and the company slogan has been changed. It is important, therefore, for any writer to research the topic he is writing about. Even the most mundane and basic announcements could have a hidden news peg just waiting to be found.

在与商业相关的报道中正确且有效地使用数字，也是让读者和观众理解内容的关键。在大多数情况下，应尽量少用数字。过多的数字会让文章显得冗长，从而降低读者的兴趣。如果一篇关于公司盈利情况的报道需要大量数字，应将这些数字分散开来，不要将营收和盈利数据放在同一段中，并且要解释数字变动的原因——每个数字背后都有一个故事。

<!--en-->
Using numbers effectively and correctly in business-related stories is also key to making your writing understandable to readers and viewers. Make sure that numbers are used sparingly in most cases. Numbers can bog down a story and disinterest the reader. If a story, such as one about a company's earnings, requires a lot of numbers, make sure the numbers are spread out. Do not put revenue and earnings numbers in the same paragraph. Make sure to explain why the numbers rose and fell. Behind every number is a story.

数字在其他方面也可能带来麻烦。务必确保比较的是正确的数字。例如，比较第二季度与第三季度的盈利增长是不合理的，但比较某一年第三季度与上一年同期的盈利则是可行的。季度盈利会因多种原因出现波动。比如，可口可乐在一年中的第二和第三季度营收和盈利通常更高，因为这时天气最热，消费者更想解渴。将该公司在温暖的第二季度的盈利与寒冷的第一季度的盈利作比较是没有意义的，但记者可以将今年第二季度的盈利与去年同期的数据进行对比。

<!--en-->
Numbers can be tricky in other ways. Make sure you are comparing the right numbers. For example, it is not valid to compare earnings growth from the second quarter with that from the third quarter, but it is valid to compare earnings from the third quarter of one year with those of the third quarter from the previous year. Quarterly earnings can fluctuate for a variety of reasons. For example, Coca-Cola's revenues and earnings are stronger in the second and third quarters of a year because that is when the weather is hottest and consumers want to quench their thirst. It would not be meaningful to compare the company's earnings in the warm second quarter with earnings in the chilly first quarter, but a reporter could compare earnings at the second quarter of this year with those of last year.

在商业报道中，为数字提供背景信息是绝对必要的。在报道某个月全国新增失业人数时，必须告知读者上个月的数字，这样他们才能判断人数是上升还是下降，以及上升/下降的幅度。

<!--en-->
Providing context for a number is an absolute necessity in business reporting. When writing a story about the number of newly unemployed workers in the country during a month, you must tell the reader the previous month's number so that they can determine whether and by how much the number is rising or falling.

追踪资金流向。钱是如何被使用的？钱来自哪里？谁来决定资金的分配？能够回答这些问题的商业记者才能写出有说服力的报道，帮助读者理解相关问题。因此，掌握关键的商业术语也至关重要。如果记者不清楚营收和盈利的区别，就应该去查阅相关定义。错误使用商业术语会损害媒体机构、记者以及整个新闻行业的信誉。

<!--en-->
Follow the money. How is the money being spent? Where is the money coming from? Who decides how the money gets spent? The business reporter who answers these questions will write a compelling story that will help explain an issue to readers. Thus, knowledge of key business terms is also critical. A reporter who does not know the difference between revenue and earnings should look the terms up. Misusing business terms can cost the media outlet, the reporter, and the entire journalism community credibility.

首先，负责报道和撰写商业新闻的记者应尽可能用清晰的语言进行写作。用简单的话解释正在发生的事情，避免使用当今企业界中常见的行话。不要使用“缩减员工规模”这样的表述，而应称之为“裁员”或“解雇”。当一家公司“同意出售部分资产”时，实际上就是在卖掉业务。要用读者能够理解的方式让他们知晓发生了什么。

<!--en-->
Above all, a journalist taking on the task of reporting and writing a business story should write with as much clarity as possible. Explain in simple words what is going on, avoiding the jargon permeating the corporate world today. Do not write about a "reduction in force." Call it a "layoff" or a "firing." When a company "agrees to divest certain assets," it's selling a business. Let your reader know what's happening in terms that they can understand.

公共、私营与伦理问题！• 企业在新闻稿中常用的33个术语可能需要向普通读者解释，包括：市值、收购、合资企业、费用、预测、股票分割、债务、负债、战略选择、利润率、缺口以及储备金。这些术语将在本章末尾给出定义。

<!--en-->
Public and Private and Ethics, Oh My! • 33
Terms commonly used by corporations in releases that may need to be explained to average readers include: market capitalization, takeover, joint venture, charges, forecasts, stock split, debt, liabilities, strategic alternatives, margins, shortfall, and reserves. These terms are defined at the end of this chapter.

美国的企业环境可能看起来令人生畏。但实际上，几乎所有的商业新闻都离不开金钱。企业都在试图赚取更多利润。利润越高，无论是公众公司还是私营公司的股东都会越开心。更高的利润会推高上市公司的股票价格，提升私营公司的价值，进而增加私营股东所持股份的价值。商业世界充满趣味——既有骗子，也有努力让世界变得更美好的人。记者的任务就是以能吸引最广泛受众的方式报道这两类人。

<!--en-->
Corporate America can seem daunting. However, virtually every business story comes down to money. Businesses are trying to make more money. The more money they make, the happier their shareholders—public or private—will be. Increased profits send up the stock price of public companies and make a private company more valuable, also increasing the value of a private shareholder’s stake. The business world is fascinating. There are con artists and there are people trying to make the world a better place to live. The job is to write about both in a way that will attract the widest audience possible.

#### 劳工与消费者问题

<!--en-->
*Labor and Consumer Issues*

在撰写商业新闻时，记者应考虑新闻主题会对读者或观众产生何种影响。如果新闻是关于一家亏损的大型本地企业，那可能意味着该公司不得不裁员，甚至可能面临破产诉讼。这些都是其员工和客户想要了解的信息。如果一家本地企业在工厂新增就业岗位，那就意味着当地会有更多工作机会，降低失业率，同时由于更多人有收入用于购买食品、住房及其他商品和服务，从而促进经济发展。这也是人们想了解的内容。

<!--en-->
When writing business stories, the reporter should think about the impact the topic of the story is going to have on readers or viewers. Is the story about a large, local company that has lost money? That could mean that the business might have to lay off some of its workers or that it might even be headed toward bankruptcy court. That is information that its workers and customers will want to know. Is a local company adding new jobs to its plant? That could mean more jobs for the community, improving the area’s unemployment rate and boosting the economy by adding more workers to the area who have money to spend on groceries, housing, and other goods and services. That is also information that people will want to read about.

很多时候，商业新闻会忽视员工和消费者。然而，可以说这两类群体才是报道商业和经济领域时最重要的对象。没有员工，企业就无法生产并销售产品和服务；没有每天光顾商店的消费者，企业也没有人可以销售产品和服务给。优秀的商业记者不会忽略这一重要事实，他们会为企业的员工和消费者撰写文章，确保读者理解相关影响。

<!--en-->
All too often, business journalism forgets about the worker and the consumer. Yet, arguably, these two constituents are the most vital to writing about business and the economy. Without workers, companies would not have the ability to produce and sell their products and services, and without consumers going into stores every day, these companies would not have anyone to sell their goods and services to. The best business writers do not lose sight of this important fact. They write stories for the employees and consumers of a company, making sure readers understand the ramifications.

并购新闻并非仅仅涉及A公司收购B公司。在几乎所有情况下，这些新闻也关乎员工因两家公司合并业务而失去工作——因为不再需要两位CEO的秘书，或者根本不需要两位CEO。产品召回新闻也不仅仅是关于汽车制造商需要花费数百万美元来修复最新车型中存在缺陷的安全带，它还涉及那些购买了该汽车、在事故中因安全带未能提供足够保护而受伤或死亡的消费者。关于店铺关闭的新闻也不仅仅是促销打折的消息，它们还涉及市场竞争、失业的工人，或是导致企业衰落的外部因素。以下这则来自威斯康星州斯特金湾《多尔县倡导者报》的案例就是一个典型：

<!--en-->
Merger and acquisition stories are not just about Company A purchasing Company B. In virtually every case, they are also stories about employees losing jobs as the two companies merge operations and no longer need two secretaries for the CEO—or two CEOs for that matter. A product recall story is not just about the millions of dollars an automaker will have to spend to fix a defective seatbelt on its latest model. It is also a story about the consumers who purchased that car and were injured or killed when the seatbelt did not properly protect them in an accident. Stories about store closings are not just about going-out-of-business sales. They are about competition, the workers who are losing their jobs, or the external forces that have caused a business’s decline. The beginning of this story from the *Door County Advocate* in Sturgeon Bay, Wisconsin, is a classic example:

#### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

*前《诺福克弗吉尼亚先锋报》商业版编辑比尔·乔伊克谈商业写作技巧：*

<!--en-->
*Former* Norfolk Virginian-Pilot business editor *Bill Choyke on the craft of business writing:*

**不必害怕数字：**数字往往无法揭示真相，只会带来更多的数字。不过，还是要关注数字，包括金额，这样才能让文章更具商业气息。数字并不会伤人。

<!--en-->
**Don’t be afraid of numbers:** Numbers often don’t lead to the truth, only to other numbers. Still, follow the numbers, including the money, and give the story a business feel. Numbers don’t bite.

##### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

*前《诺福克弗吉尼亚先锋报》商业版编辑比尔·乔伊克谈商业写作技巧：*

<!--en-->
*Former* Norfolk Virginian-Pilot business editor *Bill Choyke on the craft of business writing:*

**从一开始就要考虑呈现方式：**没错，《今日美国》无论人们愿不愿意，都已经改变了世界。从最初就要思考文字、图表、照片乃至设计如何相互配合。与设计/图形团队一起头脑风暴，他们能让写作更轻松。

<!--en-->
**Think presentation from the beginning:** Yes, *USA Today* has changed the world, like it or not. From the outset, think how the words, graphics, photo and even design can work together. Brainstorm with your design/graphic folks. They can make the writing easier.

##### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

*前《诺福克弗吉尼亚先锋报》商业版编辑比尔·乔伊克谈商业写作技巧：*

<!--en-->
*Former* Norfolk Virginian-Pilot business editor *Bill Choyke on the craft of business writing:*

**你自己就是最好的编辑：**大声朗读文章。如果会打扰到他人，就小声读。自我修改后，如果在提交之前有时间，再通读一遍纸质版，或者在修改后再读一遍纸质版。

<!--en-->
**You are your best editor:** Read aloud. If it distracts others, do it softly. Edit yourself and if you have time before you turn it in, read a hard copy one more time, and/or read a hard copy after the edit.

34 • 公共、私营与伦理问题！

<!--en-->
34 • Public and Private and Ethics, Oh My!

#### 专家建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

前《亨茨维尔（阿拉巴马州）时报》商业版编辑谢莉·哈斯金斯对新手报道商业新闻的几点建议：

<!--en-->
Former Huntsville (Ala.) Times business editor Shelly Haskins on newcomers to business coverage:

**了解你的受众群体：** 这完全取决于规模。判断什么才是重要的商业新闻，关键在于你的读者。在亨茨维尔或伯明翰，一家街角的杂货店倒闭或易主可能不会引起我们太多关注；但在斯科茨伯勒，当地FoodWorld变成Bi-Lo的消息却能登上头版。

<!--en-->
**Know your community:** It's all a matter of scale. Deciding what is and isn't an important business story depends on your readers. In Huntsville or Birmingham, the corner grocery store might close or change hands without us giving it much ink. In Scottsboro, the fact that the local FoodWorld is now a Bi-Lo is front-page news.

##### 专家建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

前《亨茨维尔（阿拉巴马州）时报》商业版编辑谢莉·哈斯金斯对新手报道商业新闻的几点建议：

<!--en-->
Former Huntsville (Ala.) Times business editor Shelly Haskins on newcomers to business coverage:

**为读者写作，而非为公司：** 公司会试图将信息往对自己有利的方向歪曲。你需要考虑信息来源，并寻找客观的观点。例如，如果一家公司宣布裁员，务必考虑这会影响谁——无论是被裁员工、服务可能下降的顾客，还是股价可能因公司财务状况而涨跌的投资者。

<!--en-->
**Write for the reader, not for the company:** Companies will try to spin information to their benefit. Consider the source, and seek out objective opinions. For example, if a company announces a layoff, make sure you consider whom that affects, whether it be the laid-off employees, customers who might see a decline in service, or investors, who might see their stock go up or down, depending on the severity of the company's financial picture.

密歇根街桥梁老化带来的问题，很可能是斯特金湾失去一家杂货店的最大原因。

<!--en-->
The ailments of the aging Michigan Street bridge probably are the biggest reason Sturgeon Bay is losing a grocery store.

尼克·斯威纳斯基表示虽然不愿重复老生常谈，但在这种情况下他别无选择。在斯特金湾市中心经营Nick’s SuperValu十年后，由于桥梁频繁且长时间封闭带来的压力，他不得不关闭店铺。

<!--en-->
Nick Swinarski said he hates to beat a dead horse but in this case, he can't help it. After 10 years of owning Nick's SuperValu in downtown Sturgeon Bay, Swinarski is bowing to the pressures of the long and frequent bridge closings.

桥梁问题是他和妻子辛迪决定关闭位于第三大道的杂货店的主要原因。

<!--en-->
The bridge problems are the primary reason he and his wife, Cindy, are closing their Third Avenue grocery store.

对于大多数居民来说，或许很难用具体金额来衡量密歇根大道桥梁封闭带来的不便，但对斯威纳斯基这样的商家而言却并非如此。每次桥梁封闭，Nick’s SuperValu的销售额就会下降35%。

<!--en-->
While it may be difficult for most residents to assign a dollar value to the inconvenience caused by the Michigan Avenue bridge closings, it's not difficult for business owners like Swinarski. Each time the bridge closed, Nick's SuperValu recorded a 35 percent drop in sales.

在过去三年里，斯威纳斯基被迫将巅峰时期的40名员工削减到目前的18人。这些裁员直接源于销售额下滑和利润减少，这一恶化趋势如同滚雪球一般，最初都是因为桥梁维修导致跨海交通中断而引发的。⁴ 文章还进一步说明了桥梁因维修而封闭的次数、镇上还将保留多少家杂货店——这对斯特金湾市中心的购物者来说是非常重要的信息——以及斯威纳斯基试图出售店铺却无人接盘的事实。

<!--en-->
Over the past three years, Swinarski was forced to slash his peak workforce of 40 to the 18 employees who currently work for him. The job cuts were directly attributable to eroding sales and decreased profits, a downward trend like a kind of snowball effect that all started when traffic flow across the bay was interrupted due to bridge repairs.⁴
The story goes on to explain how many times the bridge has been closed by repairs, how many grocery stores will remain in the town—a vital piece of information for downtown grocery shoppers in Sturgeon Bay—and the fact that Swinarski tried to sell his store but could not find any takers.

最优秀的商业记者在撰写此类报道时，会先设想自己作为消费者或员工时会想知道什么。那些报道固特异轮胎召回事件的记者指出，人们可以走到自家车道上，查看轮胎上的标识，以此判断自己的轮胎是否来自生产有缺陷轮胎的工厂。他们这样解释是因为考虑到了受众的需求。许多记者则会想到自己的父母或祖父母等亲属，根据他们认为这些人能够理解的信息来撰写文章。

<!--en-->
The best business writers think of what they would want to know if they were a consumer or an employee when they write such stories. The reporters who covered the Firestone tire recall pointed out how people could go out to their driveways and read the writing on their tires to determine if they had come from one of the factories that had been producing faulty tires. They explained it because they thought of their audience. Many reporters try to think of relatives, like their parents or grandparents, and write their stories on the basis of information they know those people would understand.

商业新闻中有很多能帮助消费者和工人的报道。媒体将这些报道称为“实用新闻”或个人财经报道。

<!--en-->
Business journalism is full of stories that help consumers and workers. Publications call these stories “news you can use” or personal finance reporting.

这类报道会提供如何撰写简历、如何做好面试准备以应对棘手问题的建议。它们还会告诉读者上班该穿什么，教授正确的电子邮件礼仪。但它的内容远不止于此。个人财经报道的范围很广，从经济低迷时期如何挑选合适的股票到如何理解人寿保险政策都有涉及。能为读者提供实用信息的报道是商业新闻中的宝贵资源，许多出版物和网站都专门致力于这类报道。更多关于个人财经报道的内容，请参阅第5章。

<!--en-->
This type of reporting offers advice on how to write resumés or how to go into a job interview prepared for the tough questions. It shows readers what to wear to work and teaches them proper e-mail etiquette. But, it is also much more. Personal finance journalism can run the gamut from picking the correct stocks in a down market to understanding a life insurance policy. Stories that provide a service to readers are valuable commodities in business journalism, and many publications and Web sites are devoted solely to this type of reporting. For more on personal finance stories, see Chapter 5.

商业记者还应考虑那些可能不会出现在商业版面的故事。如果一个城市能够保持较高的信用评级，它就能以比其他城市更低的利率借款，从而降低居民的税收负担，正如《北卡罗来纳州达勒姆先驱太阳报》的这篇本地新闻所解释的那样：[^485]: ⁴ 来自D.菲茨杰拉德2002年8月16日发表于《多尔县倡导报》的文章《尼克屈服于桥梁压力之下》。版权归威斯康星州多尔县《倡导报》所有，经许可转载。

<!--en-->
Business reporters should also think about stories that may not even go in the business section. If a town can maintain its high credit ratings, it can borrow money at a lower rate than other cities and keep its residents' taxes down, as this local news story from *The Herald-Sun* in Durham, N.C., explained:
[^485]: ⁴ From “Nick’s bows to bridge pressures,” by D. Fitzgerald, August 16, 2002, *Door County Advocate*. Copyright by the *Door County* (Wisconsin) *Advocate*. Reprinted with permission.

公共事务、私营企业与伦理问题 • 35 达勒姆市的财务状况良好，因此有三个国家级机构都给予其AAA级信用评级，这一评级使该市能够以更低的利率借款。

<!--en-->
Public and Private and Ethics, Oh My! • 35
The city of Durham’s financial health is good enough for three national agencies to give it their entire AAA credit rating, a status that allows the city to borrow money at lower interest rates.

实际上，在这些评级以及异常低的利率帮助下，该市最近以2.505%的利率重新融资了约4500万美元的未偿债务。此前，该市为这些债务支付的利率约为5%至6%。

<!--en-->
In fact, with the help of the ratings and unusually low interest rates, the city recently refinanced roughly $45 million in outstanding debt at 2.505 percent. Before, the city had been paying about 5 percent to 6 percent on the money.

但有一家公司警告称，该市应停止像去年那样动用储备金来支付运营成本。⁵商业记者应当思考每篇报道对员工和消费者的影响。如果记者能解释说，在可口可乐上个季度提高价格后，购买其12罐装产品的顾客变少了，那么这篇关于价格上涨导致该公司利润下降的原本较为晦涩的报道，对消费者来说就会更有意义。

<!--en-->
But one firm warned that the city should stop dipping into its savings account to cover operating costs, as it did last year.⁵
Business reporters should think about the impact of every story on employees and consumers. An otherwise arcane story about Coca-Cola’s earnings falling as a result of rising prices will have more meaning to consumers if the reporter explains that fewer grocery shoppers bought the company’s 12-packs after it raised its prices in the last quarter.

##### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

阿拉巴马州亨茨维尔《时报》前商业版编辑谢莉·哈斯金斯对新从事商业报道的人士的建议：

<!--en-->
Former Huntsville (Ala.) Times business editor Shelly Haskins on newcomers to business coverage:

**商业报道并非仅仅是对公司的报道：它关乎经济、储蓄与支出，也涉及投资。可以撰写有关如何储蓄或投资的个人理财类文章。同时要关注当地经济状况——失业率是否上升？失业者如何维持生计？在经济繁荣时期人们又如何支配自己的资金？**

<!--en-->
**Business coverage is not just company coverage:** It’s the economy, it’s saving and spending, it’s investing. Do personal finance stories on ways to save or invest money. Keep your eye on the local economy. Is unemployment up? How are workers getting by without jobs, or what are people doing with their money in boom times?

### 商业新闻业的职业道德

<!--en-->
*Business Journalism Ethics*

无论何时，任何参与新闻报道、写作或编辑工作的人都会面临道德困境。报道商业和经济话题也不例外。事实上，有人认为，由于所有参与商业报道的人都是产品投资者或消费者，他们日常生活中的每一行为都会引发道德问题。报道饮料行业的记者，如果选择喝百事而非可口可乐，是否属于偏袒行为？只在克罗格超市购物的记者，能否客观地报道总部位于辛辛那提的这家公司？这些问题看似荒谬，却曾在商业新闻研讨会和会议上被提出。

<!--en-->
At one time or another, anyone involved in the reporting, writing, or editing of news will be faced with an ethical dilemma. It is no different in reporting on business and economic topics. In fact, some argue that because everyone who is involved with business reporting is an investor or a consumer of products, everything they do in their daily lives results in ethical questions. Is a reporter covering the beverage industry showing favoritism by drinking Pepsi instead of Coke? Can a reporter who only shops for groceries at Kroger write objectively about the Cincinnati-based company? These questions may seem silly, but they have been raised at business journalism seminars and conferences.

商业记者可能面临的最大冲突领域之一就是华尔街。许多商业记者和编辑都持有相关公司的股票或共同基金份额。这是否应该阻止他们撰写关于投资或其所持有股票的公司及行业的报道？遗憾的是，这个问题并没有明确的答案。不同媒体机构的处理方式各异，有些采取逐案处理的方式。例如彭博社允许记者在向上级披露自身利益关系，并声明这种关系不会影响他们以公正态度报道相关内容的前提下，撰写涉及其有财务利益关联公司的新闻。

<!--en-->
One of the biggest potential areas of conflict for business journalists is Wall Street. Many business reporters and editors own stock in companies or shares in mutual funds. Should that prevent them from writing or editing stories about investing or stories about companies or industries in which they own stock? There is no clear-cut answer to this question, unfortunately. Media outlets handle it differently, and some handle it on a case-by-case basis. Bloomberg News, for example, allows reporters to write about events involving companies in which they have a financial interest as long as they disclose that interest to their supervisor and state that this interest will not prevent them from covering the topic in an unbiased manner.

《商业周刊》的道德准则十分严格。其规定称，员工“不得报道、撰写或编辑涉及你自己或你的直系亲属持有证券的公司的新闻——也不得报道同一行业内的其他公司”（《商业周刊》新闻职业道德准则，2005年）。该杂志表示，这一禁令还适用于记者所报道或有可能报道的行业内的公司证券，但不包括共同基金、国库券或市政债券。因此，从理论上讲，驻波士顿负责报道富达集团的该杂志的共同基金记者可以投资于该公司的一些共同基金。[^498]：⁵摘自B. Evans所写的《达勒姆获三大评级机构授予AAA信用评级》，载于2003年5月22日的《达勒姆先驱太阳报》B3版。版权归2003年达勒姆先驱公司所有，经许可转载。

<!--en-->
The ethical guidelines at *Business Week* are strict. They state that staff members “may not report, write, or edit a story about a company in which you or members of your immediate family own securities—nor about other companies in the same industry” (*Business Week* Code of Journalistic Ethics, 2005). The magazine says that its prohibition extends to securities in companies in industries that a reporter covers or is reasonably likely to cover but does not include mutual funds,treasury bills, or municipal bonds. So, theoretically, the magazine's mutual funds reporter in Boston who follows Fidelity can invest in some of that company's mutual funds.
[^498]: ⁵ From “Durham gets AAA credit rating from 3 agencies,” by B. Evans, May 22, 2003, *Durham Herald-Sun*, p. B3. Copyright 2003 by the Durham Herald Company Inc. Reprinted with permission.

36 • 公共与私人以及职业道德，哎呀！

<!--en-->
36 • Public and Private and Ethics, Oh My!

CNNmoney.com的财经新闻网站采取了更进一步的措施。在其每篇与股票相关的报道中，都会加入一段免责声明，内容大致为：“CNNmoney.com上提供的股票推荐和意见仅代表所引用分析师和专家的观点，并不代表CNNmoney关于是否买入、卖出或持有某只股票的立场”（CNNmoney.com，2003年）。

<!--en-->
CNNmoney.com's website for business news goes one step further. With each of its stock-related stories, it uses a disclaimer that reads, in part, "Stock recommendations and comments presented on CNNmoney.com are solely those of the analysts and experts quoted. They do not represent the opinions of CNNmoney on whether to buy, sell, or hold shares of a particular stock" (CNNmoney.com, 2003).

商业记者和编辑的诚信至关重要。一旦这种信任被破坏，读者和观众可能就不会再相信他们的后续报道。违反这些规则的记者和编辑要么被解雇，要么在压力之下离职。Marketwatch.com的科技专栏作家班比·弗朗西斯科因被指责投资了一家她曾撰文介绍过的科技初创企业而于2007年辞职。2005年，Marketwatch.com的前联合创始人兼评论员托姆·卡拉兰德拉因未能披露自己持有过那些他曾积极评价过的股票，且在文章发表后不久便将其卖掉，最终与美国证券交易委员会达成和解。不过，当CNBC主播玛丽亚·巴蒂罗莫被曝出2007年曾随花旗集团的一名高管乘坐该公司的飞机出行时，她的电视台给予了她支持，并为此次飞行费用向花旗集团进行了赔偿。

<!--en-->
The trustworthiness of a business reporter and editor is vital. If that trust is violated, the readers and viewers may not believe the next story. Reporters and editors who violate these rules have been fired or have left their jobs under pressure. Marketwatch.com tech columnist Bambi Francisco resigned in 2007 after criticism of her investment in a tech start-up that had clients she had written about. In 2005, former Marketwatch.com co-founder and commentator Thom Calandra settled with the SEC after it was discovered he had failed to disclose that he had held positions in stocks that he had written about in a positive fashion and had sold shortly after publishing the stories. However, CNBC anchor Maria Bartiromo was backed by her network after it was disclosed she had taken a trip on the Citigroup jet in 2007 with one of the company's executives. The network reimbursed the company for the flight.

许多新闻职业道德准则，包括《华尔街日报》的母公司道琼斯所制定的准则，都禁止其记者进行卖空操作。有些媒体甚至要求记者和编辑向上级公开自己的金融资产状况，这些资产可能包括股票、债券及其他证券；还有些媒体要求记者的配偶及直系亲属也公开投资情况。

<!--en-->
Many journalism ethics codes, including the one for Dow Jones, the parent of the *Wall Street Journal*, prohibit any of its reporters from shorting stocks. Some publications go so far as to require their reporters and editors to disclose their financial holdings to bosses. These financial holdings can include stocks, bonds, and other securities. Some even require that reporters' spouses and immediate family also disclose investments.

这种情况一定会引发道德冲突吗？并非必然。例如，我在《亚特兰大宪报》担任记者时，从祖父那里继承了Southern Co.的股票，随后我被派去报道该公司CEO关于市中心重建的演讲。我向上司说明了持股情况，并告诉编辑认为该演讲与我的持股并无关联，于是编辑允许我继续报道此次演讲。

<!--en-->
Do such situations always result in an ethical conflict? Not necessarily. For example, when I was a reporter at the *Atlanta Journal-Constitution*, I inherited Southern Co. stock from my grandfather, and I was asked to cover a speech by the company's CEO on downtown redevelopment. I went to my boss and explained the stock ownership, telling the editor that I did not think a speech on downtown development had anything to do with my ownership of stocks. The editor allowed me to cover the speech.

许多商业记者还会遇到另一个道德问题：在撰写文章时获得了他们认为一旦发表就会影响公司股价的信息。几乎所有的职业道德准则都禁止记者利用工作中获取的信息进行交易，但这种诱惑往往很大。假设微软内部有人告诉《西雅图时报》的记者，该公司本季度的业绩将远低于分析师的预期，这样的消息很可能会导致该公司股价暴跌。记者可以大量卖空该公司的股票并从中获利，但如果此事被曝光，记者和报纸都会失去读者的信任。《西雅图时报》的商业版编辑贝基·比斯比很可能会解雇这名记者。道琼斯的职业道德准则规定，其记者和编辑在文章发表后的第三个交易日之前，不得交易文中提及的任何公司的股票。

<!--en-->
Another ethical issue that many business journalists encounter is when they have obtained information during the writing of a story that they believe will move a company's stock up or down once it is published. Virtually all ethics codes prohibit reporters from acting on information that they obtain in the course of their jobs. However, the temptation can be great. Suppose someone within Microsoft told a reporter for the *Seattle Times* that the software maker would greatly miss analyst earnings projections for the quarter. Such information would likely send the company's stock crashing downward. A reporter could short a large amount of the company's shares and possibly make a profit. But the reporter and the newspaper would lose the trust of readers if the trade were disclosed. Becky Bisbee, the business editor at the *Seattle Times*, would likely fire this reporter. The Dow Jones ethics code prevents its reporters and editors from trading in the stock of any company mentioned in one of its stories until the third trading day after the article has appeared.

公共与私人领域，还有那些道德问题啊！• 37 商业领域的员工还会进行股票交易吗？很可能。但这类交易和持股应仅限于记者报道范围之外的公司和行业。不过在某些情况下，一些媒体也做出了例外规定。例如，专业投资者和资金管理人被允许为在线媒体及其他平台撰写专栏。媒体管理者认为这些人能提供记者无法具备的关于股票持有和交易的见解。在很多情况下，这些专栏或文章的末尾会披露作者的持股情况，有时作者甚至会在文章中直接说明自己持有某只股票。

<!--en-->
Public and Private and Ethics, Oh My! • 37
Does stock trading still occur among business staff personnel? Probably. But the stock trading and ownership should be confined to companies and industries outside of the reporter's beat. In some cases, however, some media outlets have made exceptions. For example, professional investors and money managers have been allowed to write columns for online publications and other outlets. Media managers argue that these people provide an insight into stock ownership and trading that journalists cannot offer. In many cases, the stock ownership of the Wall Street pro is disclosed at the end of the column or article. In many cases, the writer will even disclose that he owns a stock in the article itself.

记者在报道或撰写商业新闻时还常常会遇到其他道德困境。比如，假设你是一名记者，正在采访当地一家杂货连锁店的老板，采访结束时他给了你一些刚从门店烤好的面包让你带回家。你会接受吗？如果不接受，你觉得这位高管会生气或误解你拒绝的原因吗？大多数商业媒体都不赞成记者和编辑接受任何有价值的东西，通常这类物品的价值会被定义为超过25美元。这样做往往是为了让公关人员或其他消息来源能够请记者吃午餐，但大多数媒体希望记者下次与消息来源共进午餐时能回报这份恩情。

<!--en-->
Other ethical situations often arise when a journalist is reporting or writing business stories. For example, imagine you are a reporter interviewing the president of a local grocery store chain, and at the end of the interview, he gives you some loaves of bread, baked fresh from one of the locations, to take home. Do you take them? If you do not take them, do you think the executive would be upset or misunderstand why you are turning him down? Most business publications frown on their reporters and editors accepting anything of value, often defined as anything that is worth more than $25. In many cases, this is done to allow a public relations person or another source to buy a reporter lunch. But most media outlets would like their reporters to repay the favor the next time the staffer has lunch with the source.

绝不能为了获得报道机会而接受任何回报。财经类作家不应接受她正在采访的银行家提出的以更低利率为她重新办理抵押贷款的提议。即便是最普通的报道主题也可能出现这种情况。曾经负责制作著名AFLAC鸭子广告的广告公司的一位高管，曾提出让记者为电视体育赛事挑选下一个AFLAC知识问答题。这个请求只是出于真诚友好的意图吗？也许吧，但记者还是拒绝了，因为他不想让人觉得他对这次广告活动的报道受到了影响。此外，公司经常会随新闻稿一起将产品及宣传资料寄送给新闻编辑部，这些资料的价值往往远超25美元。例如，几年前百事公司推出“Pepsi Stuff”大型促销活动，消费者有机会赢得从T恤到皮夹克等各种奖品，当时百事公司就向数十家新闻编辑部寄去了大量宣传资料。许多记者立即将这些物品寄了回去，还有些人则将其捐赠给了慈善机构。

<!--en-->
Nothing should be accepted in return for coverage. A personal finance writer should not accept an offer to refinance her mortgage at a lower rate by a banker she is interviewing for a story. The situation can arise with even the most innocuous of stories. An executive at the advertising agency that handles the famous AFLAC duck commercials once offered to let a reporter pick the next AFLAC trivia question for a televised sporting event. Was the request just an honest, friendly gesture? Perhaps, but the reporter turned down the offer, not wanting anyone to think his coverage of the ad campaign had been tainted. In addition, companies will often send their products and promotional material to business desks along with news releases. In many cases, the material can be worth well more than $25. For example, when it announced its huge Pepsi Stuff promotion in which consumers could win everything from T-shirts to leather jackets several years ago, PepsiCo sent huge boxes of the material to dozens of newsrooms. Many reporters promptly shipped the goods back, while others donated the clothing to charity.

记者的采访与报道技巧往往也会引发问题。在商业新闻领域最著名的道德违规案例中，《辛辛那提询问报》的一名记者在花费一年时间对奇基塔国际公司进行大量报道并撰写系列文章后遭到解雇，因为他非法入侵了该公司的语音邮件系统。

<!--en-->
A journalist's interviewing and reporting tactics can often raise problems as well. In possibly the most famous case of an ethical transgression in business journalism, a reporter for the *Cincinnati Enquirer* was fired after spending a year reporting and writing a huge series of stories on Chiquita Brands International, Inc. The reporter had illegally broken into the company's voicemail system.

商业媒体不应允许其记者和编辑在获取新闻时违法。许多此类媒体要求员工在获取新闻时不得隐瞒身份或说谎。《商业周刊》的准则（2005年）规定：“这并不妨碍我们采取特殊的报道手段，但我们始终要以公开透明的方式行事，并明确表明自己是《商业周刊》的员工。任何其他做法都可能危及所收集材料的可用性，还可能引发法律诉讼。特殊的报道技巧必须获得主编的批准，并视情况与麦格劳-希尔的法律部门进行沟通。”

<!--en-->
Business publications should not allow their reporters and editors to break the law when trying to find news. Many of them do not allow their staff members to hide their identities or lie when obtaining news. "This doesn't preclude us from using extraordinary reporting efforts, but we always do so above board and as clearly identified *BusinessWeek* employees," states *BusinessWeek*'s code (2005). "Any other approach could compromise the use of the material so gathered, and could give rise to a legal claim. Unusual reporting techniques should have the approval of the editor-in-chief and be reviewed, as appropriate, with the McGraw-Hill legal department."

38 • 公私领域与伦理问题，哎呀！

<!--en-->
38 • Public and Private and Ethics, Oh My!

新闻工作的标准准则同样适用于商业报道。不得编造消息来源，也不得伪造引文。（前《纽约时报》记者杰森·布莱尔编造了数十次采访的例子足以让所有人明白这一点。）记者和撰稿人不得利用媒体身份谋取个人利益，也不得接受有偿出差。最重要的是，保持诚信是记者的职责。只要有任何可能显得不恰当的行为，记者就不应去做。正如彭博新闻社的伦理准则所言：“在揭露他人的不当行为时，我们自身应当无可指责。报道的影响力越大，我们就越有义务承受最严格的审视”（彭博，2009年，第57页）。是否存在灰色地带？当然有。任何记者在采取行动之前都应与编辑或上级讨论自己的计划。

<!--en-->
Standard rules of journalism conduct apply to business reporting. Sources should not be made up. Quotes should not be faked. (The example of former *New York Times* reporter Jayson Blair, who fabricated dozens of interviews, should make this clear to everyone.) Reporters and writers should not use their position as members of the media for personal gain. Paid trips should not be accepted. Above all, it is the reporter's job to maintain integrity. If there is anything that might give even the appearance of impropriety, the reporter should not do it. As Bloomberg News' ethics code states, "When exposing the wrongdoing of others, we should be above reproach. The greater the story's impact, the greater our obligation to withstand the most exacting scrutiny" (Bloomberg, 2009, p. 57). Are there gray areas? Of course. Any reporter should discuss what he plans to do with his editor or a superior before taking action.
