### 美国商业编辑与撰稿人协会伦理准则

<!--en-->
*Society of American Business Editors and Writers Code of Ethics*

宗旨声明：

<!--en-->
Statement of Purpose:

作为商业与财经领域的记者，我们深知自己是公众信任的守护者，绝不能滥用这一职责。

<!--en-->
As business and financial journalists, we recognize we are guardians of the public trust and must do nothing to abuse this obligation.

仅有诚实的意图是不够的；作为记者，我们必须以一种避免任何个人利益嫌疑或滥用媒体权力的方式来开展职业活动。

<!--en-->
It is not enough that we act with honest intent; as journalists, we must conduct our professional lives in a manner that avoids even the suggestion of personal gain, or any misuse of the power of the press.

基于这样的认识，我们为从事商业与财经新闻工作的人士提供以下指导原则：

<!--en-->
It is with this acknowledgment that we offer these guidelines for those who work in business and financial journalism:

*个人投资与关系：*

<!--en-->
*Personal investments and relationships:*

* 避免任何可能损害或看似损害客观性或公平性的行为。
* 绝不让个人投资影响报道内容。须向上级或直接向公众披露自己的投资状况。
* 须披露可能引发利益冲突的个人或家庭关系。
* 避免主动交易及其他短期获利行为，因为这类活动与商业记者的独立角色不相符。
* 不得利用内幕信息谋取个人利益。*信息来源：*
* 在报道过程中需确保信息的保密性，并尽一切努力在信息公之于众之前防止其落入可能借此牟利之人手中。
* 不得篡改信息、延迟或拒绝发布信息，也不得向任何政府就新闻内容作出让步。公共与私人领域与伦理问题，哎呀！ • 39

<!--en-->
* Avoid any practice that might compromise or appear to compromise objectivity or fairness.
* Never let personal investments influence content. Disclose investment positions to your superior or directly to the public.
* Disclose personal or family relationships that might pose conflicts of interest.
* Avoid active trading and other short-term profit-seeking opportunities, as such activities are not compatible with the independent role of the business journalist.
* Do not take advantage of inside information for personal gain.
*Sources:*
* Insure confidentiality of information during the reporting process, and make every effort to keep information from finding its way to those who might use it for gain before it is disseminated to the public.
* Do not alter information, delay or withhold publication or make concessions relating to news content to any government.
Public and Private and Ethics, Oh My! • 39

## *礼物与优待：*

<!--en-->
*Gifts and favors:*

* 在职业活动中，不得接受价值超过象征性意义的任何礼物或特殊待遇。
* 不得接受任何由外部机构出资的异地出差。
* 在考虑自由职业工作或演讲酬劳的邀请时，务必仔细审查，确保这些邀请并非试图影响报道内容。
* 若因记者的职业活动或人脉关系而收到任何未来就业机会或外部收入的机会，应向主管汇报。
* 只有在绝对必要的情况下，且仅在正常工作期间，方可接受价值一般的食品或饮料。

<!--en-->
* In the course of professional activity, accept no gift or special treatment worth more than token value.
* Accept no out-of-town travel paid for by outside sources.
* Carefully examine offers of freelance work or speech honoraria to assure such offers are not attempts to influence content.
* Disclose to a supervisor any offer of future employment or outside income that springs from the journalist's professional activities or contacts.
* Accept food or refreshments of ordinary value only if absolutely necessary, and only during the normal course of business.

## *新闻编辑的诚信：*

<!--en-->
*Editorial integrity:*

* 出版商、所有者及新闻编辑室管理者应制定相关政策和准则，以维护商业新闻报道的诚信性。
* 无论采用何种新闻平台，都应明确区分广告内容与新闻编辑内容。
* 由新闻编辑人员制作的素材仅可用于由编辑部门控制的版块、节目或页面。
* 由广告部门控制的版块、内容或节目，在字体、布局和设计上应与新闻版块有明显区别，且广告内容必须明确标注为广告。
* 以报道文章作为交换广告或其他利益的手段是不道德的。

<!--en-->
* Publishers, owners and newsroom managers should establish policies and guidelines to protect the integrity of business news coverage.
* Regardless of news platform, there should be a clear delineation between advertising and editorial content.
* Material produced by editorial staff should be used only in sections, programming or pages controlled by editorial departments.
* Content, sections or programming controlled by advertising departments should be distinctly different from news sections in typeface, layout and design. Advertising content should be identified as such.
* Promising a story in exchange for advertising or other considerations is unethical.

### *使用外部素材：*

<!--en-->
*Using outside material:*

* 使用非记者撰写的文章或专栏可能会具有欺骗性，并存在固有的利益冲突。但那些明确标明为观点或意见的内容，以及明确注明来自公众的投稿，如公民博客或读者来信，则不受此限制。
* 仅可接受遵守与正式员工相同道德规范的自由职业者提交的稿件。

<!--en-->
* Using articles or columns from non-journalists is potentially deceptive and poses inherent conflicts of interest. This does not apply to content that is clearly labeled opinion or viewpoint, or to submissions identified as coming directly from the public, such as citizen blogs or letters to the editor.
* Submissions should be accepted only from freelancers who abide by the same ethical policies as staff members.

## *技术：*

<!--en-->
*Technology:*

* 随着技术的不断发展和变化，商业新闻记者应率先将专业标准应用于新的新闻形式，并鼓励其他记者遵守这些标准和原则。⁶ [^533]: ⁶ 摘自美国商业编辑与作家协会的《职业道德准则》。版权归美国商业编辑与作家协会所有，经许可转载。40 • 公共与私人领域以及道德问题！

<!--en-->
* Business journalists should take the lead in adapting professional standards to new forms of journalism as technologies emerge and change.
The business journalist should encourage fellow journalists to abide by these standards and principles.⁶

## 建议练习题

<!--en-->
*Suggested Exercises*

1. 在你所在的州找出10家上市公司和10家私营公司。每家公司有哪些公开信息？这两类公司的信息有何差异？
2. 阅读美国商业编辑与作家协会的职业道德准则，讨论其中关于股票持有问题的规定。你认为自己能否客观地报道自己持有股票的公司？那对于你卖空过的公司呢？
3. 你正在撰写一篇关于所在社区汽油价格上涨的报道。你会如何寻找消费者进行采访？会问他们哪些类型的问题？
4. 讨论一下：如果你是一名报道华特迪士尼公司的报纸记者，而该公司公关部的人士为你和你的家人提供周末免费进入其主题公园的门票，你会接受吗？如果会，原因是什么？
5. 列出你认为每位商业记者和编辑都应该了解的10条重要信息或事实。你认为你所在当地报纸的商务版工作人员都了解这些信息吗？为什么或为什么不？![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/28ea43c75649b559f3d457664e5f2bf5.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T071651Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=dad81d05341e7c3dc2ac5ee5c8d19c2cba01bb2024fde22f0455cd314ab6dee1)

<!--en-->
1. Find 10 public companies and 10 private companies in your state. What information is available for each company? How does the information about the two groups compare?
2. Read the Society of American Business Editors and Writers ethics code. Discuss what it says about stock ownership. Do you think that you can write objectively about a company in which you own stock? What about a company in which you've shorted stock?
3. You're writing a story about rising gasoline prices in your community. How would you go about finding consumers to interview for this story? What types of questions would you ask them?
4. Discuss what you would do if you were a reporter for a newspaper covering Walt Disney Co. and someone from its corporate communications department offered you and your family free passes to one of its theme parks for the weekend. Would you take them? If you would, why?
5. Write down 10 important pieces of information or facts that you think every business reporter and editor should know. Do you think that every person working on the business desk at your local newspaper knows this information? Why or why not?

## 3

这就是经济

<!--en-->
It's the Economy

### 什么驱动着经济

<!--en-->
*What Drives the Economy*

在21世纪的头十年里，没有哪篇新闻比关于经济的报道对所有商业新闻读者来说更为重要。随着房价下跌、股市剧烈波动、银行被政府接管、企业倒闭以及消费者背负债务，能够清晰地报道这些问题已变得十分必要。

<!--en-->
No story at the end of the first decade of the twenty-first century has been more important to every reader of business news than that of the economy. With housing prices down, the stock market fluctuating wildly, banks being taken over by the government, businesses closing, and consumers saddled with debt, being able to report these issues clearly has become a necessity.

这并非易事。对于记者而言，任何城镇、城市、县、州或国家的经济似乎都是一个难以理解的抽象概念。究竟什么是经济？经济可以被定义为某个区域内围绕商品和服务的生产与分配而开展的各种活动。这些活动包括支付工资让工人制造产品并出售它们。支付给工人的钱会在该地区流通，用于他们购买其他生活所需的商品和服务。经济可以增长，也可以萎缩。如果一个国家或地区的经济在增长，就会创造就业机会。关注经济的商业记者可以撰写文章，介绍有哪些类型的岗位、薪资水平以及所属行业。反之亦然。当经济开始放缓或衰退时，企业对商品和服务的需求就会低于过去。面对经济放缓的情况，企业往往不得不裁员，就像2008年和2009年的美国经济所经历的那样。

<!--en-->
That's not an easy job. The economy of any town, city, county, state, or country can seem to be a nebulous concept for a reporter to grasp. What exactly makes an economy? An economy can be defined as the activities surrounding the production and distribution of goods and services for consumption in a region. Those activities include paying workers to manufacture products that are then sold. The money paid to those employees goes to work in the region as they purchase other goods and services to live. Economies can grow, and they can contract. If a country or region's economy is growing, jobs are being created. A business reporter interested in the economy could write a story about what kind of jobs are available, for what pay, and in what industries. The converse is also true. When the economy starts to slow down or decline, there is not as much demand for a company's goods and services as there was in the past. When companies are faced with such an economic slowdown, they are often forced to lay off workers, as the U.S. economy saw in 2008 and 2009.

无论是上市公司还是私营企业，无论规模大小，都会根据其对国家或地区经济走向的判断来增加或减少资本支出。如果一家公司的首席执行官及其他高管认为经济将持续增长，未来消费者的支出也会增加，他们很可能会增加资本支出。资本支出可以被定义为企业用于扩展或发展业务的资金投入。

<!--en-->
Companies—public and private, large and small—will increase or decrease their capital expenditures on the basis of where they believe the national or regional economies are headed. If the CEO and other executives at a company decide that the economy is going to keep growing and that consumers are going to spend more money in the future, they will likely increase capital expenditures. Capital expenditures can be defined as the money spent by a company to expand or build its business.

当企业认为对其产品的需求会减少时，也会削减开支。总部位于北卡罗来纳州罗利市的Martin公司……

<!--en-->
Companies will also decrease their spending when they think that there will not be as much demand for their products. Raleigh, North Carolina-based Martin

### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

麦克拉奇报业集团的经济新闻记者凯文·霍尔关于报道经济的经验：

<!--en-->
McClatchy newspapers economics correspondent
Kevin Hall on covering the economy:

**多读、再读、还得多读**：这份工作最耗费精力的是那些最终未能刊载的研究工作。要做好这份工作，就必须真正深入阅读、探究细节。因此，显而易见的参考资料就是《华尔街日报》、《金融时报》和彭博社。《华尔街日报》中真正有用的内容在于内页，那里有真实案例和实用信息。44 • 这就是经济

<!--en-->
**Read, read and read some more:** The most exhausting part of this job is all the research you do that never makes it into print. To do the job well, you have to really read and get into the weeds. So your obvious starting points are the *Wall Street Journal*, the *Financial Times* and Bloomberg. The really useful stuff in the *WSJ* is in the inside sections, where there are real-world stories and real-world information.

*Tips from the Pros*

<!--en-->

Smith, senior fellow and director of the Center for Business Forecasting at the Kenan Institute of Private Enterprise in the Kenan-Flagler Business School at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill and chief economist, Society of Industrial and Office Realtors.

1. 消费者的购买行为贡献了近70%的国内生产总值。你所在地区的消费者现在都在做什么？
2. 股价波动常成为新闻头条，但直接持有股票或共同基金的家庭还不到一半。仅有10%的家庭拥有90%的股票。采访消费者，了解股价是否会影响他们的消费计划。
3. 超过三分之二的消费者拥有住房。房价上涨带来的资本收益支撑了消费者的支出，尤其是汽车和卡车方面的支出。采访房主，了解他们对市场激励措施的反应。他们是否进行了再融资？把钱用在了哪里？
4. 失业和裁员常常成为新闻焦点，而新的就业机会却很少被报道。在同一雇主处工作十年甚至更长时间的情况几乎从不成为新闻话题。采访一部分人，找出属于后两类情况的人，并讲述他们的故事。
5. 失业的人很少会长期处于失业状态。采访一些失业者，了解他们找到新工作需要多长时间。
6. 社区学院是美国教育体系中默默无闻的英雄。在全球范围内，只有美国和加拿大设有这类院校。如果您所在地区有此类学院，可以了解一下Marietta Materials Incorporated这家公司——它生产用于建造道路、桥梁等设施的产品。2009年，由于认为经济形势，尤其是社区道路新建项目的支出增长速度将不及往年，该公司的高管们削减了资本支出。因此，任何希望了解所在地区经济状况的商业记者都会想与企业高管交谈。公司管理层会密切关注经济形势及各类经济指标：他们既不想在需求不足时让大量产品积压在仓库中，也不想在需求旺盛时生产不足，否则很可能会失去销售机会。还有些人会对企业的动向感兴趣。如果一家公司的管理团队认为经济即将比过去更强劲发展，他们就会增加产量，从而提高产品销量，进而获得更高的收入和利润。这会吸引华尔街投资者的兴趣，他们可能会购买该公司的股票。从全国层面来看，一个重要的经济指标是商务部人口普查局发布的报告，该报告会统计制造商的货物出货量、新订单量、库存水平以及未完成订单情况。如果制造商的新订单量在上升，很可能很快就会有更多货物被运出，这是经济的积极信号。相反，如果制造商的库存水平在上升，说明他们的产品销量不如从前，仓库也会逐渐填满，这是经济的负面信号。联邦储备委员会会按制造业、采矿业和公用事业等行业来观察工业生产情况，同时还会按消费品、商业设备及建筑材料等市场类别对生产数据进行分类。这些数据通常在每个月的15日左右发布，那些关心经济是处于扩张还是收缩状态的人也会密切关注这些数据。以下是美联社通常报道联邦储备委员会工业生产报告的方式：

<!--en-->
1. Consumers account for nearly 70 percent of GDP with their purchases. What are consumers doing now in your area?
2. Stock price volatility gains headlines, but less than one half of all households own a stock or a mutual fund directly. Only 10 percent of households own 90 percent of stocks. Interview consumers to see if stock prices have any impact on their spending plans.
3. More than two-thirds of consumers own a home. Capital gains from rising house prices have supported consumer spending, especially cars and trucks. Interview homeowners to see how they respond to market incentives. Have they refinanced? What did they do with the money?
4. Unemployment and layoffs grab headlines. New job creation rarely does. Working for the same employer for a decade or more almost never rates a story. Interview a sample of people to find people in the two latter categories and tell their stories.
5. People who lose their jobs are rarely unemployed for very long. Interview a sample of people who've lost their jobs to see how long it took to find a new one.
6. Community colleges are the unsung heroes of the U.S. educational system. Globally, only the United States and Canada have this type of institution. If your area has one, interview
Marietta Materials Incorporated makes products that help build roads and bridges, among other things. Company executives decreased its capital expenditures in 2009 after deciding that the economy, particularly the spending on new construction for neighborhood roads, was not going to grow as fast as it had in previous years. Thus, any business reporter looking for clues about the economy in his or her region will want to talk to business executives. Company management watch the economy and economic indicators closely. They do not want to be caught with too much of their product sitting in warehouses when there is no demand, nor do they want to be caught with too little of their goods being manufactured when demand is great because they are likely to lose sales.
Others are interested in what companies are doing. If a company's executive team decides that the economy is about to grow stronger than it has in the past, it will increase its production, raising the possibility that it will sell more of its goods. If it sells more of its goods, it might have higher revenue and profits. This will attract the interest of investors on Wall Street, who might want to buy the company's stock.
On the national level, a key economic indicator is a report from the Department of Commerce's Bureau of the Census that measures manufacturers' shipments, new orders, inventories, and unfilled orders. If new orders to manufacturers are rising, likely there will soon be more goods shipped. This is a positive indicator for the economy. Or, if manufacturers' inventory levels are going up, it means that they are not selling as many of their goods as they once were and their warehouses are filling up. This is a negative indicator for the economy.
The Federal Reserve Board looks at industrial production by industry—manufacturing, mining, and utilities. And it also breaks its production report down by market group, such as consumer goods, business equipment, and building materials. The information is typically released around the 15th of every month and is also closely watched by those interested in whether the economy is growing or contracting.
Here is how the Associated Press (AP) typically covers a story on the Fed's report on industrial production:

> 1月份，工业生产再度活跃起来，增长了0.7％；与此同时，企业在上个月增加了未售出商品的库存——这对疲软的经济而言是一对积极的信号。作为2001年经济衰退中受冲击最严重的领域，美国工厂、矿山和公用事业领域的最新运行状况显示出了令人瞩目的复苏势头。美联储周五报告称，工业活动环比增长0.7％，这与12月0.4％的大幅下滑形成了鲜明对比。1月的增长幅度是自7月以来最好的，当时工业活动也增长了0.7％。这一强劲表现令经济学家们感到意外，他们此前预计的增长率为0.3％。工业部门一直是经济全面复苏过程中的薄弱环节，但周五的报告显示，这个受损严重的行业未来或许会有更好的发展前景。企业库存的增加幅度为三个月来最大，因为零售商似乎认为谨慎的消费者在节假日期间会有更强的消费意愿。商务部在周五发布的另一份报告中指出，12月的库存增幅是11月0.3％增幅的两倍。同时，12月的企业销售额环比上升了0.2％，高于前一个月的0.1％。在华尔街，这两份经济数据推动了股市上涨。道琼斯工业平均指数在交易开始后的半小时内上涨了13点，纳斯达克指数则上涨了4点。在美联储所追踪的大部分工业产出来自的工厂领域，1月份的产量增长了0.5％，这主要得益于汽车产量的提升，较12月0.4％的产量下降有了显著改善。由于天气转冷导致需求增加，上月燃气和电力公用事业的产量增长了4％，而12月则下降了1.4％。然而，在矿山领域，产量下降了1.2％，完全抵消了12月1％的涨幅。经济一直处于增长不均衡的状态，强劲的一个季度之后便是为期三个月的疲软期。企业尤其难以在这种混乱的经济环境中判断商品的需求情况。阻碍经济复苏的最大因素在于：由于对战争可能性的担忧以及整体不确定的商业环境，企业不愿在招聘和资本支出方面做出重大承诺。¹作者展示了股市对美联储工业生产报告的积极反应。如果工业生产数据低于经济学家的预期，股价可能会下跌，因为投资者可能会担心企业没有足够多地生产产品以提升利润。还有许多来自不同机构的报告也在研究企业的生产、库存、订单和发货情况。例如，原名为全国采购经理协会的供应管理协会会发布一份关于全国制造业活动的月度报告。该报告的亮点是一个名为“采购经理人指数”（PMI）的指标，它综合考虑了新订单、产量、就业、交付和库存等情况。PMI的显著变化可能预示着经济的变动。费城储备银行也会发布一份关于该地区制造业活动的月度报告。这份基于对该地区约250家制造商的调查的报告更多是对商业活动前景的预测。所有这些关于企业生产的报告都备受关注。一些学生借此了解自己的职业目标与抱负。

<!--en-->
> Industrial production roared back to life in January, rising by 0.7 percent while businesses boosted their stockpiles of unsold goods the month before—a pair of promising signs for an ailing economy.
> The latest snapshot of activity at the nation's factories, mines and utilities—the sector of the economy hardest hit by the 2001 recession—showed an impressive rebound.
> The 0.7 percent over-the-month jump in industrial activity marked a turnaround from the steep 0.4 percent drop registered in December, the Federal Reserve reported Friday.
> January's increase marked the best performance since July when industrial activity also rose by 0.7 percent. The strong showing surprised economists, who were predicting a 0.3 percent advance.
> The industrial sector has been the weakest link for the economy's ability to get back to full throttle, but Friday's report offered hope that the battered sector may see more better days ahead.
> The increase in business inventories was the largest in three months asretailers apparently were betting that cautious consumers would have a stronger appetite to spend during the holidays.
It's the Economy • 45
December's increase was two times bigger than the 0.3 percent boost in supplies of unsold goods on shelves and back lots, which was recorded in November, the Commerce Department said in a second report Friday.
At the same time, business sales edged up by 0.2 percent in December, up from a 0.1 percent rise.
On Wall Street, the pair of economic reports gave stocks a lift. The Dow Jones industrial average was up 13 points and the Nasdaq was up 4 points in the first half-hour of trading.
At factories, which account for most industrial output tracked by the Fed, production rose by a solid 0.5 percent in January, largely reflecting a boost in automobile production. That marked a big improvement over the 0.4 percent drop in factory output registered in December.
Production at gas and electric utilities jumped by 4 percent last month, compared with a 1.4 percent drop in December, as demand was stoked by colder weather.
At mines, however, production fell by 1.2 percent, more than reversing a 1 percent gain posted in December.
The economy has been coping with uneven growth as a quarter of strength has been followed by a three-month period of weakness. And businesses have been struggling, especially, to try and gauge demand for their goods during these muddled economic times.
The biggest factor holding back the economy's recovery: Businesses have been reluctant to make big commitments in hiring and in capital spending, due in part to uneasiness about the possibility of war and also generally to an uncertain business environment.¹
The writer showed how the stock market reacted favorably to the Fed's industrial production report. If the industrial production numbers had been below what economists were expecting, stock prices might have fallen, as investors could have become worried that companies were not making as much of their goods to stimulate higher earnings.
Plenty of other reports from a variety of groups also examine companies' production, inventory, orders, and shipping levels. For example, the Institute for Supply Management, formerly the National Association of Purchasing Management, produces a monthly report on a national survey of manufacturing activity. The highlight of this report is a measurement called the Purchasing Managers' Index, or the PMI, which takes into account new orders, production, employment, deliveries, and inventories. Big moves in the PMI can signal a change in the economy. The Reserve Bank in Philadelphia also issues a monthly report that looks at manufacturing activity in the region. The survey, based on a survey sent to about 250 manufacturers in the area, is more of an outlook on business activity. All of these reports on production by companies are closely watched.

#### 专家建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

McClatchy报纸经济栏目记者Kevin Hall谈经济报道：

<!--en-->
McClatchy newspapers economics correspondent Kevin Hall on covering the economy:

**花时间阅读专业出版物和分析报告：**我会收到大量分析报告，包括富国银行的James Paulsen等看涨派人士的报告、摩根大通的James Glassman的华尔街观点，以及Ed Yardeni更为中立、专业的分析。此外还有道路建设商、承包商、设备租赁商等提供的资料，我确实会全部阅读。这类阅读内容有时会让人感到枯燥，但却是必要的，因为华尔街始终处于乐观与悲观之间的博弈之中，而双方都是基于相同的数据得出不同的结论。阅读得越多，就越能从看涨派、看跌派以及实际经济活动中找出最关键的信息。

<!--en-->
**Take the time to read specialty publications and analysis:** I get tons of analyst reports from bullish folks like James Paulsen at Wells Fargo to Wall Street views from James Glassman at JP Morgan to more centrist, wonkish views from Ed Yardeni. I get stuff from road builders, contractors, equipment lessors, etc., and I actually read all this stuff. This sort of reading can often make the eyes glaze over, but is necessary since Wall Street is a constant battle between optimism and pessimism, and each side is viewing the same sets of data to reach different conclusions. The more you read, the more you pick out what seems most salient from the bulls and the bears and underlying economic activity.

#### 专家建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

McClatchy报纸经济栏目记者Kevin Hall谈经济报道：

<!--en-->
McClatchy newspapers economics correspondent Kevin Hall on covering the economy:

**避免使用行话：**大多数人害怕自己的401(k)计划，也对信用卡账单上的细则感到困惑。在纽约或洛杉矶这样的大城市可能并非如此，但只要看看美国内陆地区关于医疗保健的那些混乱状况，就能明白在金融事务上保持通俗易懂的重要性。用简单的语言解释，不要假设读者就懂你所讲的内容。

<!--en-->
**Avoid jargon:** Most folks are afraid of their 401(k) plan and intimidated by the fine print of their credit card statement, etc. This might not be so in a big market like New York or Los Angeles, but just look at the nonsense over health care in the interior of the country and that ought to give a sense of sophistication in financial matters. Keep it simple, explain and don't assume your reader understands what you do.

尽管这些指标往往同步变动，但如果其中一个指标与其他指标走势相反，可能就是经济正在发生变化的最初迹象。

<!--en-->
Although they often move in tandem, one moving in the opposite direction to the others may be the first sign that the economy is changing.

在讨论其他重要的经济指标时，我们必须明白，全国数以百万计的企业才是推动经济的核心力量。某个县或地区的企业可能在增加产量或出货量，而该州或国家的其他地区却在减少产量和出货量。密切关注当地企业的动态总是很有帮助的。当有关工业生产的报告发布时，财经记者应务必向几家当地企业了解情况。例如，有些地方通过提供税收优惠或免税货物运输区来吸引企业迁入；还有一些地方在市中心或其他区域设立经济发展区以促进增长。这些措施也可能对当地经济产生影响，只是不会体现在这些报告中。

<!--en-->
In discussions of other important economic barometers, we must understand that the millions of businesses in the country are the driving force of the economy. Businesses in any county or region may actually be increasing production or shipments while the rest of the state or country may be decreasing production and shipments. It always helps to keep close tabs on what local businesses are doing. When a report on industrial production comes out, the business reporter should be sure to check with a few local businesses. For example, some local economies try to entice businesses to move to their regions by offering tax incentives or zones where goods can be shipped tax-free. Others have economic development areas around downtown districts or other regions to stimulate growth. These, too, may have an impact on the local economy that does not show up in these reports.

经济学并非精确的科学，关于经济的报道也是如此。经济状况可能会发出相互矛盾的信号。对于试图解读经济指标或因素的记者来说，了解自己所写的内容至关重要，否则他们的报道也会传递出混乱的信号。尽管经济形势可能十分复杂，但相关报道应当清晰明了。

<!--en-->
Economics is not an exact science, and neither is writing about the economy. The economy can send mixed signals. It is important for writers trying to make sense of economic indicators or factors to understand what they are writing about. Otherwise their stories will also send mixed signals. Although the economic picture may be cloudy, writing about it should be clear.

#### 解读经济

<!--en-->
*Making Sense of the Economy*

2008年和2009年的经济状况是媒体报道的重点话题，不仅仅是商业媒体。由房地产市场下滑等多种因素引发的经济衰退，迫使许多企业和消费者重新考虑支出规模和购买决策。巨额债务让许多家庭陷入困境，而企业则因无法获得运营所需的资金而倒闭。

<!--en-->
What happened in the economy in 2008 and 2009 was one of the dominant stories covered by the media, and not just the business media. A recession caused by many factors, including a decline in the housing market, led many businesses and consumers to reconsider how much they were spending and what they were buying. Large amounts of debt have crippled many households, while businesses have closed their doors because they have been unable to borrow the money they need to continue operating.

导致这一经济状况的最重要因素之一，是华尔街在经济中扮演的角色日益重要。华尔街越来越多地将消费者用于购买房屋、汽车等物品的贷款打包后出售给投资者。这种将贷款证券化并出售给投资者的趋势——即所谓的抵押债务证券，且不考察贷款及借款人的信用状况——是一个当时很少有人理解的问题。

<!--en-->
One of the most important factors that led to the economic situation was the increasing role Wall Street played in the economy. More and more, Wall Street bundled together and sold the loans consumers bought to purchase items such as houses and cars. The increasing trend of securitization of selling loans to investors called collateralized debt obligations—without examining the credit-worthiness of the loans and the consumers backing the investment—was an issue that few understood.

然而，诸如家庭拥有率上升、信用卡债务水平升高，以及向原本不符合贷款条件的消费者提供次级抵押贷款等趋势，最终导致了经济危机。如果经济记者能够仔细研究数据，本可以提前察觉到这些问题。

<!--en-->
Yet, many of these trends, such as the increase in household ownership, the rising credit card debt levels, and the push in sub-prime lending, which offered home loans to consumers who previously would not have been eligible for such borrowing, led to the economic troubles that economics reporters could have discerned if they had looked at numbers.

曾为彭博新闻社和《美国新闻与世界报道》负责经济报道的Noam Neusner认为，优秀的经济报道就在于能够发现这类重要的趋势。

<!--en-->
The best economics reporting, says Noam Neusner, who covered the economy for Bloomberg News and *U.S. News & World Report*, is all about spotting such important trends.

Neusner表示，虽然每位记者都需要了解用于衡量经济各领域的联邦政府报告的内容与性质，但更应关注几个核心概念。例如，通货膨胀，即商品和服务的价格水平，是重要的经济晴雨表。如果通货膨胀上升，消费者购买商品和服务的成本就会增加。但财经记者不应仅仅报道“通货膨胀正在上升”这一事实。在大多数情况下，如果记者能在杂货店或其他购物场所找到受到通货膨胀影响的消费者，报道的信息量会大得多。应当通过这些消费者的案例，让读者直观地看到像通货膨胀这样抽象的经济术语是如何改变每个人生活的。《经济学》•47 这是一篇来自MarketWatch.com的报道，内容涉及由劳工部测量的通货膨胀晴雨表——消费者价格指数（CPI），该指数并未包含消费者的相关数据：

<!--en-->
So while it is important for any reporter to understand the content and nature of reports from the federal government that gauge different parts of the economy, the bigger focus needs to be on a few big ideas, says Neusner. For example, inflation, or the price levels of goods and services, is an important economicbarometer. If inflation is rising, the cost of goods and services for consumers is going up. But the business writer should not simply report that inflation is rising. In most cases, the story will be much more informative if the reporter finds consumers who are being affected by inflation at the grocery store or someplace else they shop. Consumers should be used in the story to let a reader see first-hand how a nebulous economic term such as inflation is changing everyone's lives.
It's the Economy • 47
Here is a story from MarketWatch.com that discusses the Consumer Price Index (CPI), a barometer of inflation measured by the Labor Department, that does not include consumers:

周五公布的政府数据显示，石油和汽油价格的逆转促使4月消费者价格下降。由于能源和食品价格波动较小，零售价格自1982年以来首次连续两个月保持平稳。

<!--en-->
A reversal in oil and gasoline prices pushed down consumer prices in April. Without volatile energy and food components, retail prices were flat for a second month in a row for the first time since 1982, government figures showed Friday.

劳工部称，消费者价格指数下降了0.3%，降幅甚至超过了经济学家预计的0.1%。CBS MarketWatch.com的调查显示，核心价格指数应上涨0.1%。

<!--en-->
The consumer price index fell 0.3 percent, the Labor Department said, even bigger than the 0.1 percent drop economists expected. The CBS MarketWatch.com survey called for a 0.1 percent gain in the core rate.

价格持平甚至下降的数据令投资者担忧，在价格持续下跌的环境中投资回报将如何。CPI的下降足以使10年期国债收益率降至20世纪50年代以来的新低。

<!--en-->
The flat and falling price data spooked investors worried about returns in a declining price environment. The CPI drop was enough to push a benchmark 10-year Treasury yield to a fresh 1950s low.

周五发布的另一份报告显示，根据密歇根大学研究人员的测算，消费者情绪回升至一年来的最高水平，但这一数据对金融市场影响甚微。最新的住房开工数据也同步公布，在裁员和恶劣天气的影响下出现下滑。

<!--en-->
A separate report Friday showed consumer sentiment, as measured by University of Michigan researchers, rebounded to its highest mark in a year, but the number had little impact on financial markets. The latest housing start results were also released, falling amid job cuts and poor weather.

在周四公布的批发价格创下1.9%的纪录性跌幅之后，今日又发布了CPI数据。核心生产者价格指数下降了0.9%，为九年来单月最大降幅。

<!--en-->
The CPI results follow a record 1.9 percent drop reported for wholesale prices Thursday. The core producer price index fell 0.9 percent or the most for one month in nine years.

尽管上周美联储的会议后政策声明引发了最初的通缩担忧，但一些经济学家此后认为，实际出现持续通缩导致价格下跌的风险很小或根本不存在——尽管大多数人仍预计通货膨胀将得到控制。

<!--en-->
Despite initial worries about deflation sparked by the Fed's post-meeting policy statement last week, some economists have since been arguing they see only slim or no risks for actual deflation-sustained price drops—even though most expect inflation to remain contained.

Economy.com的Mark Zandi表示：“通缩确实是一个值得重视的威胁，主要是因为通货膨胀率已经处于极低水平，而经济依然表现疲软。不过，虽然构建通缩场景并不困难，但其发生的可能性仍然极低。”

<!--en-->
"Deflation is indeed a meaningful threat, largely because inflation is already so low and the economy continues to struggle," said Economy.com's Mark Zandi. "Still, while deflationary scenarios are not difficult to construct, they remain highly unlikely."

低水平的通货膨胀可能会持续存在，从而使美联储能够维持较低的利率。劳工部门官员证实，从同比角度来看，核心CPI仅上升了1.5%，为1966年以来的最低水平。

<!--en-->
Low levels of inflation are likely to persist, allowing the Fed to keep interest rates low. On a year-over-year comparison, core CPI is up just 1.5 percent, the lowest since 1966, Labor officials confirmed.

许多企业依然几乎没有定价能力，这可能对投资和招聘产生负面影响。更低的能源费用有望改善企业的盈利前景，大多数经济学家仍预计到今年底美国经济增长至少会有轻微改善。

<!--en-->
Many companies continue to have little to no pricing power, which could have import repercussions for investment and hiring. Cheaper energy bills should help the profit outlook and most economists are sticking with predictions for at least subtle improvement in U.S. growth by the end of the year.

Zandi表示：“近期股市和企业债市场的强劲反弹，以及企业和消费者信心的提升，都表明经济很快就能恢复稳定。预计今年的失业人数将会减少，随后会出现就业岗位的增加。”

<!--en-->
"The recent strong rallies in the stock and corporate bond markets and improving business and consumer confidence suggest that the economy should soon find its footing. The job losses are expected to abate and give way to job gains later this year," said Zandi.

ABN AMRO北美公司的首席经济学家Carl Tannenbaum表示，他认为伊拉克战争前夕的能源价格波动所带来的影响……

<!--en-->
Carl Tannenbaum, chief economist with ABN AMRO North America, said he thinks the impact from energy swings in the lead-up to war in Iraq

### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

McClatchy报纸的经济新闻记者Kevin Hall谈报道经济的方法：

<!--en-->
McClatchy newspapers economics correspondent Kevin Hall on covering the economy:

**深入研究数据：**政府每月都会发布大量报告和统计数据，但很少有记者能深入探究数据背后的细节。我喜欢仔细研究通货膨胀数据，阅读那些详细列出构成消费者价格指数的所有产品的图表。正是通过这种方式，我们在2007年就发现了食品通胀的趋势，比其他任何人都早数月。我开始追踪牛奶、鸡蛋、白面包、奶酪等日常必需品的价格走势，最终发现除了能源价格上升外，消费者在购买其他日常用品时也面临着大幅涨价。没错，牛仔裤变得更便宜了，但人们在杂货店每周都要购买的那些商品价格却在飞涨。”

<!--en-->
**Dig deeper in the numbers:** Every month, the government puts out gobs of reports and statistics and few reporters go beyond the headline numbers. I like to look closely at the inflation data, reading the lengthy charts that break down every single product that makes up the Consumer Price Index. That's how we identified the food-inflation trend in 2007 months before anyone else wrote about it. I started tracking the rise in prices on a number of staples like milk, eggs, white bread, cheese, etc., and was able to document that beyond higher energy prices, the consumer was getting socked in other daily staples. Yeah, blue jeans were cheaper, but the stuff people buy week in and week out at the grocery was soaring in price.

#### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

McClatchy报纸的经济新闻记者Kevin Hall谈报道经济的方法：

<!--en-->
McClatchy newspapers economics correspondent Kevin Hall on covering the economy:

**趋势是您的朋友：** 在 McClatchy，我们致力于挖掘趋势报道。各类通讯社已经能够很好地提供关于某个行业最新数据或进展的四张图表。但对读者而言最有用的是能够将这些点联系起来的内容。始终要从更广阔的背景思考“某件事意味着什么”：它是否预示着某种趋势或变化？在采访对象时，可以询问他们是否注意到任何有趣的趋势、变化，或是那些尚未得到财经媒体足够关注或重视的问题。

<!--en-->
**The trend is your friend:** Trend reporting is what we strive to uncover at McClatchy. The wire services do a more than sufficient job pounding out four graphs on the latest numbers or development in a sector. What's most useful for a reader, however, is something that connects the dots. Always think in terms of "what does something mean" in the broader context: does it signal a trend, a shift, etc. Ask the people you are interviewing if they are seeing any interesting trends or changes or something that isn't getting enough attention or being given enough importance by the financial media.

48 • 主题是经济状况，随后得出的较快结论是过度通缩担忧正在引发恐慌。

<!--en-->
48 • It's the Economy and then relatively quick conclusion to combat is unduly causing deflation jitters.

尽管如此，他也承认，那些此前对通缩含义不太关心或不担心的客户现在开始要求得到解释，“这对投资者情绪来说并非好事”。

<!--en-->
Still, he conceded, clients who previously cared little about what deflation means or weren't worried about it are now asking for some explanation, "and that's not good" for investor sentiment."

能源价格下跌了4.6%，这是自2001年11月以来最大的降幅，同时也完全抵消了3月时的同等幅度上涨。燃料油价格下跌了14.9%，为1990年初以来的最大跌幅。汽油价格则下跌了8.3%。

<!--en-->
Energy prices fell 4.6 percent, the biggest drop since November 2001 and completely reclaiming a like-size jump in March. Fuel oil tumbled 14.9 percent, the biggest drop since early in 1990. Gasoline prices fell 8.3 percent.

上个月，由于水果和蔬菜价格下降，食品价格下跌了0.1%。

<!--en-->
Food prices slipped 0.1 percent last month amid cheaper fruits and vegetables.

运输成本下降了1.7%，部分原因是汽车价格下跌了0.4%。不过机票价格则上涨了0.9%。

<!--en-->
Transportation costs slumped 1.7 percent, in part on a 0.4 percent drop in car prices. Airfares were 0.9 percent more expensive, however.

服装价格下降了0.6%，房价则略有下降0.1%。香烟价格上涨了0.1%。医疗保健费用上涨了0.2%，不过处方药价格则下降了0.1%。² 为什么这篇报道没有提及消费者？可能是因为 MarketWatch.com 的典型受众更多以投资者为主。那些希望快速获取经济与商业新闻的华尔街投资者、分析师及资金管理人主要阅读该网站。他们了解通货膨胀对消费者的影响，无需再被解释。虽然面向高学历读者的商业杂志也可能如此，但大多数报纸的读者未必会考虑通货膨胀对自己钱包的影响。向这些读者解释CPI表明他们购买商品和服务所需支付的费用增加了，这个概念他们是能够理解的。

<!--en-->
Clothing prices were 0.6 percent lower and housing prices eased 0.1 percent. Cigarette prices rose 0.1 percent. Medical care was 0.2 percent more expensive, although prescription drug prices eased 0.1 percent.²
Why does this story not include consumers? Probably because the typical MarketWatch.com audience is more investor focused. Wall Street investors, analysts, and money managers looking to get economic and business news fast primarily read this website. They know how inflation affects consumers and do not need it explained to them. While this may also be the case for business magazines that cater to highly educated readers, it may not be true for the readers of most newspapers, who may have never actually thought about what inflation does to their own wallets. Explain to these readers that the CPI shows that they are paying more for goods and services, and that is a concept they will understand.

大多数读者认为自己理解的经济指标是失业率，但它也容易被误解。失业率是指劳动力中那些没有工作但在寻找工作的人所占的比例。它并不包括那些没有工作但不打算找工作的人。因此，失业率并不总是能准确反映某个城镇或社区中失业人数的真实情况。

<!--en-->
An economic topic most readers think they understand is the unemployment rate, but this can also be misinterpreted. The unemployment rate is the percentage of the labor force that does not have a job but is looking for work. It does not count the number of workers without a job who are not looking to become employed. So the unemployment rate may not always be an accurate barometer of how many people are without a job in any town or community.

该国及各州都会收集失业数据。如果某个州的失业率低于全国其他地区，那么关于这一现象成因的报道就会很有价值。也许该州有更多服务行业的工作岗位，而全国其他地区的失业主要发生在制造业领域。在撰写有关就业或失业的文章时，消费者尤为重要。通常，失业者会在当地的失业办公室试图寻找工作。他们在做些什么来寻找新工作？他们是否考虑过从事与以往工作经验不同的领域的工作？他们是否需要学习新技能以提高自己在潜在雇主眼中的竞争力？

<!--en-->
Unemployment figures are collected for the country and for each state. If in one state the unemployment rate is lower than that of the rest of the country, a good story may be about why that is happening. Perhaps that state has more service-related jobs, and the bulk of job losses elsewhere in the country have occurred in manufacturing jobs. Consumers are especially important when writing about employment or unemployment. Workers without a job can typically be found at the local unemployment office trying to find work. What are they doing to find a new job? Have they considered a job in a different field from their previous work experience? Will they need to be trained with new skills to make themselves more marketable to potential employers?

有时，工人会停止寻找工作，不再计入失业率；当他们重新进入就业市场时，又会再次被统计在内。通常，失业的消费者会在认为经济状况好转、可能出现工作机会时重新开始寻找工作。具有讽刺意味的是，经济转强的第一个信号反而可能是更高的失业率。[^633]: ² 来自R. Konin于2003年5月16日发表在CBSMarketWatch.com上的文章《能源价格下跌导致CPI下降；核心指数持平》，版权归CBSMarketWatch.com所有，经许可转载。主题是经济 • 49 商业记者不应只关注低薪工作。在许多社区中，失业问题最严重的往往是那些曾经拥有六位数甚至更高薪水的人。他们往往也是最难找到新工作的群体，可能需要降低薪资才能重新就业。

<!--en-->
Sometimes, workers stop looking for jobs and are no longer counted in the unemployment rate; when they re-enter the job market, they are counted onceagain. Typically, out-of-work consumers start looking for jobs again when they believe the economy is getting better and work may have become available. Ironically, then, the first signal of a stronger economy may be a higher unemployment rate.
[^633]: ² From "CPI drops on energy drop; core flat," by R. Konin, May 16, 2003, CBSMarketWatch.com. Copyright 2003 by CBSMarketWatch.com. Reprinted with permission.
It's the Economy • 49
The business reporter should not simply focus on the low-paying jobs. In many communities, the hardest hit in the unemployment line are those who were once making six-figure salaries and higher. They are often the workers who also have the toughest time finding a new job, and they may need to take a step down in pay to become employed again.

因此，正如纽斯纳所言，商业记者应当从全局角度出发。如前所述，商业记者不应仅报道失业率上升或下降的情况，而不去分析其背后的含义。人们应当将全国及各州的统计数据应用到当地社区中。也许全国其他地区正在发生的情况现在也出现在了本地。撰写关于某家公司裁员或招人的新闻很容易，但要阐述更广泛的就业趋势则较为困难。

<!--en-->
Thus, as Neusner suggested, it behooves the business reporter to look at the big picture. As mentioned earlier, business reporters should not simply write about the unemployment rate rising or falling without looking at what it means. One should take the national and state figures and apply them to the local community as well. Maybe what has been happening in the rest of the country is now occurring locally. It is easy to write about workers getting laid off or hired at one company. It is harder to write about the broader employment trends.

生产力是另一个重要的经济因素，但很少有读者能够理解它。生产力衡量的是劳动力生产商品的能力，可以用一个简单的数学公式来表示：

<!--en-->
Productivity is another important economic factor that few readers may understand. Productivity measures how the workforce is producing goods and can be thought of as a simple mathematical equation:

$$
\frac{\text{Output (Goods and services)}}{\text{Input (Number of worker hours)}}
$$

生产力水平越高，企业在控制成本的同时生产商品的能力就越强。特别是在经济低迷时期，企业可能会试图让员工以更高的效率工作或延长工作时间，而不提高工资，以此提升生产力，正如这篇彭博新闻报道的开头所指出的那样：

<!--en-->
The higher the productivity level, the more efficient companies become in producing goods while holding down costs. Businesses may try to get away with making their workers perform at higher levels or for longer hours without raising their pay to increase productivity, particularly during an economic downturn, as the beginning of this Bloomberg News story suggests:

随着经济复苏以及企业缩减雇员人数，美国第一季度的劳动者生产力增长速度是此前三个月的两倍。

<!--en-->
U.S. worker productivity rose in the first quarter at twice the pace of the previous three months as the economy expanded and companies held down payrolls.

劳工部称，今年前三个月，衡量每工作一小时员工产出量的指标以1.6%的年增长率上升，而第四季度的增长率则为0.7%。第一季度国内生产总值的1.6%增长完全归因于生产力的提升。每单位产品的劳动力成本在上涨3.2%之后，又以1.9%的速度上升。

<!--en-->
The measure of how much an employee produces for every hour of work grew at a 1.6 percent annual pace in the first three months of the year, the Labor Department said, after 0.7 percent in the fourth quarter. The productivity gain accounts for all of the 1.6 percent increase in first-quarter gross domestic product. The cost of labor for each unit of production rose at a 1.9 percent rate after a 3.2 percent gain.

根据标准普尔500指数旗下公司截至上周的报告，受裁员推动，美国企业第一季度的利润创下2年半来的最大涨幅。过去十年的技术进步使得企业能用更少的工人生产出同样多的商品或服务，从而帮助它们度过不稳定的经济复苏期。第一季度，美国经济减少了262,000个就业岗位。

<!--en-->
U.S. corporate profits in the first quarter jumped the most in 2½ years, bolstered by job cuts, based on reports through last week by companies in the Standard & Poor's 500 Index. Technological gains in the last decade enabled companies to produce as many goods or services with fewer workers and helped them weather an uneven recovery. In the first quarter, the economy shed 262,000 jobs.

“我们需要让经济增长的速度远远超过生产力增长的速度，这样才能改善就业市场状况。”

<!--en-->

#### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

麦克拉奇报社的经济新闻记者凯文·霍尔关于报道经济的建议：

<!--en-->
McClatchy newspapers economics correspondent Kevin Hall on covering the economy:

保持谦逊，寻找比你更聪明的人：不要试图将自己的世界观强加到新闻报道中，也不要只寻找与自己观点一致的分析师。找出经济学家们认为最优秀的分析师并主动联系他们。询问你的消息来源他们尊敬谁，以及他们认为谁的观点会影响决策，然后去接触那些人。

<!--en-->
Be humble and look for people smarter than you: Resist the temptation to impose your view of the world on a story or seek out analysts who share your worldview. Identify the people economists view as the smartest analysts and seek them out. Ask your sources who they respect and whose views they think shape thinking. Then seek out those people.

If workers or readers can understand productivity and why it is important to the economy, then they can understand how an employer trying to increase productivity will affect them. That boss may ask the worker to take on additional tasks on the job. That is something that everyone can relate to and comprehend.

只要得到恰当的解释，消费者的信用状况也是大多数读者能够理解的经济因素。本章后面将会提到的联邦储备委员会会在月度报告中追踪消费者信贷情况。如果消费者越来越多地使用信用卡购物，他们将来可能难以偿还这些账单，进而损害经济。《佛罗里达州西南部的夏洛特太阳报》在其头版上报道了日益严重的信用卡债务问题，通过相关内容向任何持有维萨卡或万事达卡的读者解释这一现象。报道开头写道：

<!--en-->
A consumer's level of credit is also an economic factor that most readers can understand as long as it is explained to them properly. The Federal Reserve Board, which is discussed later in the chapter, tracks consumer credit in monthly reports. If consumers increasingly use credit cards to make purchases, they may have difficultly paying off those bills down the road, in turn hurting the economy. *The Charlotte Sun* in Southwest Florida covered the rising problem of credit card debt on its front page in a package that explained the issue to any reader with a Visa or MasterCard in his or her wallet. The story began:

> 当债务压得人喘不过气时，所有的思绪都会集中在未付的账单上。人们不再能安心入睡，而是整夜在屋里踱步。家庭争吵也愈发频繁。而最令人恐惧的声音，就是电话铃声。“我的债务管理客户们都很讨厌电话，”位于佛罗里达州西南部的消费者预算咨询公司的办公室经理伦尼·艾森伯格说道，“他们来找我时已经压力巨大。债主们日夜不停地打电话，态度极其恶劣，甚至会打到他们的工作场所。到最后，他们甚至不想接电话——因为他们感觉自己被困扰着。”根据马里兰州盖瑟斯堡的金融危机处理中心Myvesta.org的数据，美国每10名成年人中就有1人面临债务问题。而针对全国抑郁症防治运动所进行的调查中，88%的受访者表示，经济问题比死亡、家庭疾病、工作压力或婚姻问题更易引发抑郁。⁴以上内容听起来像是一篇商业新闻吗？其实并非如此。但它探讨的是困扰全国数百万消费者的一个严重经济问题。正是这类关于经济话题的报道，才能让读者更好地理解相关情况。读者能够明白家庭债务如何影响个人的消费习惯——债务越多，他们就必须将更多的收入用于偿还债务及利息。联邦储备系统会定期发布关于家庭债务负担的报告，数据显示，在21世纪的第一个十年里，这一负担达到了过去20年中的最高水平。如果记者发现有一些人的债务过重，那么他就能找到与这些统计数据相呼应的故事，从而印证全国性的趋势。商业和经济领域的记者需要拓宽对“什么是好的经济报道”的认知。很多时候，这类报道仅仅是对政府报告中的数字进行简单转述，实在乏味至极。记者需要更进一步，解释这些数字的含义，并通过采访获得的个人案例和轶事，为这些数字赋予具体的形象。[^658]：³摘自彭博新闻2003年5月1日W.爱德华兹撰写的《美国第一季度生产力增长1.6%》，版权归彭博新闻所有，经许可转载。⁴摘自2002年4月7日R.勒佩尔为《夏洛特（佛罗里达）太阳报》撰写的《痛苦与账单如影随形》，版权归《夏洛特太阳报》所有，经许可转载。这是经济板块 • 51 路透社培训编辑格雷格·麦库恩建议，记者可以通过观察朋友和邻居的购买行为，或是留意附近商场新开的店铺和关闭的店铺，来获取有助于经济报道的线索。根据《商业记者》杂志中彼得斯和祖伯（2001）的观点，他认为经济报道应该从基层出发，而非自上而下。为《吉姆·莱勒新闻一小时》节目负责商业和经济报道的保罗·索尔曼向在线新闻网站Poynter.org阐述了自己的经济报道风格：“我试图弄清楚的是，我能教给人们什么，帮助他们理解现实世界，从而让他们更像那些能够在民主社会中做出明智经济决策的公民。我会用有趣的故事作为切入点，试图向人们讲解现实世界的运作方式。由于世界上有无数的事实，因此可以创作的故事也是无穷无尽的。‘当我进行故事讲述时，我觉得自己是在揭开经济学的神秘面纱，’索尔曼补充道，‘当人们告诉我我把事情讲得如此简单，连他们都能理解时，我就觉得自己的目标达成了。’简洁性与解释力是撰写经济报道最重要的要素，没有它们，读者就会陷入困惑。”

<!--en-->
> When you're overwhelmed with debt, every thought focuses on unpaid bills.
> Instead of sleeping nights, you spend them pacing the floor. Arguments at home take place more frequently. And the most dreaded sound is the phone ringing.
> "They hate the telephone," said Lennie Eisenberg, office manager of Consumer Budget Counseling Inc. in Southwest Florida, of his debt management clients. "People come in very stressed. Creditors are calling day and night and are very nasty. They're calling people at work. It gets to the point people don't even want to answer the phone—they feel haunted."
> Debt is a problem for one out of every 10 adults in the United States, according to Myvesta.org, a financial crisis treatment center in Gaithersburg, Md. And financial problems tend to trigger depression—more than death, family illness, work worries or marital problems—according to 88 percent of people surveyed for the National Depression Campaign.⁴
Does the above read like a business story? Not really. Yet it tackles a serious economic issue that faces millions of consumers across the country. That is the type of writing about economic topics that helps bring the reporting home to readers.
Readers understand how their household debt affects personal spending habits. The more debt they have, the more of their income must go to paying off that debt plus interest. The Federal Reserve releases a quarterly report on the household debt service burden, which during the first decade of the twenty-first century was at its highest level in the past two decades. If the reporter finds some readers with too much debt, then he or she will have a story that ties nicely into these statistics and backs up a national trend.
Business and economics reporters need to expand their ideas of what makes agood story about the economy. Too often, these stories simply report the numbers from a government report. This is too boring. Reporters need to take the extra step and explain what the numbers mean and put a face to the numbers by offering the reader personal examples and anecdotes based on interviews.

⁴ From "Anguish, bills go hand in hand," by R. LePere, April 7, 2002, *The Charlotte (Florida) Sun*, p. 1-A. Copyright 2002 by *The Charlotte Sun*. Reprinted with permission.
It's the Economy • 51
Greg McCune, training editor for Reuters, suggests that reporters can get clues that will help their economics reporting by watching what friends and neighbors are purchasing or by examining the stores opening and closing at the nearest mall. He believes the economy should be covered from the bottom up, not the top down, according to Peters and Zuber (2001) in *The Business Journalist*.
Paul Solman, the business and economics correspondent for *The NewsHour* with Jim Lehrer, explained his style of economic reporting to online journalism Web site Poynter.org:
> "What I try to figure out is what I can teach people that may be useful to them in understanding the material world and thus feel more like citizens who can make educated economic decisions, as we're all supposed to be able to in a democracy. I use interesting stories as my pretext to try to teach people how the material world works. And since there are innumerable facts to the world, there's no end of stories to do.
> "When I do my storytelling, I think of myself as demystifying economics," added Solman. "When people tell me I've made things so simple that even THEY can understand it, that's when I feel I've succeeded."
Simplicity and explanation are the most important elements of writing about the economy. Without those things, the reader will be lost.

## 联邦储备系统

<!--en-->
*The Federal Reserve*

当本·伯南克发言时，所有人都会倾听——尤其是记者们。作为联邦储备委员会主席，他很可能是仅次于总统的美国最具影响力的人物。而且他是少数几个能够通过调控经济来决定总统政治命运的人之一。不过，除了知道这位有着胡子且头发渐秃的前普林斯顿大学教授的名字外，很少有美国人真正了解伯南克的职责，也不清楚通常被称为“美联储”的机构在管理国家经济方面所扮演的重要角色。

<!--en-->
When Ben Bernanke talks, people listen—especially reporters. The chairman of the Federal Reserve Board is likely the most powerful man in the country, next to the president. And he is one of the few people who can determine the political fortunes of presidents by steering the economy. But, besides knowing the name of this former Princeton University professor with the beard and balding head, few Americans fully understand Bernanke's job or the important role played by the Federal Reserve, or the Fed, as it is commonly known, in managing the country's economy.

成立于1913年的联邦储备系统是该国的中央银行。其管理委员会由七名成员组成，每位成员均由总统任命并经国会批准任职，任期为14年。该委员会的主要职责是制定国家的货币政策——这一术语看似抽象。简而言之，美联储的货币政策旨在促进经济增长，同时避免过高的通货膨胀。当委员会成员认为经济增速放缓时，他们会努力推动经济增长；而当认为经济增长过快、可能导致商品和服务价格上升速度超过工资增长速度时，则会试图放缓经济增长。美联储通过控制经济中的货币流通量及可用信贷来实现其目标。

<!--en-->
The Federal Reserve, created in 1913, serves as the country's central bank. There are seven members on the board of governors, each of whom is appointed by the president and confirmed by Congress to serve a 14-year term. The primary responsibility of the board is to set the country's monetary policy, which may seem like a vague term. Put simply, the Fed's monetary policies aim to stimulate economic growth without causing too much inflation. The Fed tries to make the economy grow when the board members believe it is slowing and slow down the growth when they believe it is growing too fast, which could cause prices of goods and services to rise faster than wages. The Fed accomplishes its goals by controlling the economy's money flow and available credit.

### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

*麦克拉奇报社的经济新闻记者凯文·霍尔谈经济报道：*

<!--en-->
*McClatchy newspapers economics correspondent Kevin Hall on covering the economy:*

**与初级工作人员及统计师交流：**这在挖掘政府数据中的趋势时尤为有用。经济分析局或劳工统计局等机构的许多研究人员和统计师都可以联系上，他们的名字通常会出现在报告上。虽然他们大多无法接受采访，但很乐意详细讲解相关数据，因为他们的日常工作就是处理这些数字，而且长期从事此类数据的跟踪工作。他们在帮助构思报道主题方面能提供很大帮助。

<!--en-->
**Talk to the junior folks and the statisticians:** This is useful, particularly when mining for trends in government data. A lot of the researchers and statisticians at the Bureau of Economic Analysis or Bureau of Labor Statistics, etc., are reachable, their names often on the reports. More often than not they can't be quoted, but they are glad to talk about the details of the numbers, since their working life is all about these numbers and they've been tracking this sort of data for quite a time. They are useful in helping to develop story ideas.

### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

*麦克拉奇报社的经济新闻记者凯文·霍尔谈经济报道：*

<!--en-->
*McClatchy newspapers economics correspondent Kevin Hall on covering the economy:*

**保持好奇心并保持怀疑态度：**好奇心或许会招致麻烦，但如果没有天生的好奇心，再多的学位和背景也毫无意义。最优秀的记者无论是对所报道领域还是更广泛的生活都充满好奇心。好奇的心思往往能揭示出各种趋势以及背后的政治操弄。52 • 经济领域这七名委员会成员构成了联邦公开市场委员会的多数派。该委员会还有另外五名成员，他们是各地区联邦储备银行的行长，包括纽约联邦储备银行行长，这些成员按轮值制产生。联邦储备银行在全国各大城市设有分支机构，如费城、芝加哥、丹佛、里士满、亚特兰大、堪萨斯城和旧金山。

<!--en-->
**Be curious and skeptical:** Curiosity might have killed the cat, but all the degrees in the world and pedigree mean nothing unless a journalist is by nature curious. The best reporters are curious, whether it is about the area they cover or life more broadly. A curious mind tends to uncover both the trends and political shenanigans.
52 • It's the Economy
The seven board members make up a majority of the Federal Open Market Committee. There are five other members of the committee, who are presidents of regional Federal Reserve Banks, including the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, selected on a rotating basis. There are Federal Reserve Bank locations in major cities across the country, including Philadelphia, Chicago, Denver, Richmond, Atlanta, Kansas City, and San Francisco.

该委员会每年召开八次会议，讨论国家经济状况，以及根据对各类经济指标的评估是否需要采取行动。如果委员会认为经济增长正在放缓，可能会降低联邦基金利率以刺激消费支出。相反，如果委员会认为经济增长过快，可能会提高联邦基金利率以抑制消费支出。联邦基金利率是指存款机构在隔夜时间内将资金借给其他存款机构的利率。它会影响其他经济因素，包括银行和其他贷款机构在消费者购买房产或汽车时收取的利率。例如，如果银行和贷款机构开始收取更高的利率，消费者可能会推迟使用贷款购买商品，从而导致经济增长放缓。

<!--en-->
This committee meets eight times each year to discuss the state of the country's economy and whether the group should take action on the basis of their assessment of various economic indicators. If the committee believes that economic growth is slowing, it might lower the federal funds rate to stimulate spending. Conversely, if, in the opinion of the committee, the economy is growing too fast, it might raise the federal funds rate to slow spending. The federal funds rate refers to the interest rate at which depository institutions lend balances at the Federal Reserve to other depository institutions overnight. It affects other economic factors, including the interest rate that banks and other lenders charge when a consumer purchases a home or a car. If banks and lenders start charging a higher interest rate, for example, consumers might hold off on purchasing an item using a loan. This could cause economic growth to slow.

美联储官员通过货币政策来预测经济的走向。由于是在进行预测，他们会持续关注各类重要经济指标的趋势——其中很多内容将在本章后面部分介绍。这些指标包括失业率、CPI、汽车和房屋销售情况以及消费者信心指数。失业率和通货膨胀是美联储最为关注的两个问题。

<!--en-->
Fed officials forecast where the economy is headed with their monetary policy. Because they are making a forecast, they are constantly looking at the trends in major economic barometers—many of which are discussed later in this chapter. Those include the unemployment rate, the CPI, auto and home sales, and consumer confidence. Unemployment and inflation are two of the Fed's biggest concerns.

每次委员会会议结束后，即使没有采取任何行动，美联储也会发布新闻稿说明委员会所采取的行动。这对各大报纸及其他大型媒体机构而言始终都是值得报道的新闻。新闻稿的内容大致如下：

<!--en-->
After each committee meeting, the Fed issues a press release stating the action taken by the committee, even if no action was taken. This is always a story, particularly for major newspapers and other large media outlets. The release would read something like this:

自9月联邦公开市场委员会会议以来收到的信息表明，经济活动仍在持续回升。在两次会议间隔期间，金融市场状况总体基本保持不变。近几个月来，房地产领域的活跃度有所上升。家庭支出似乎也在增长，但仍受到持续失业、收入增长缓慢、住房财富下降以及信贷紧张等因素的制约。企业仍在削减固定投资和员工人数，但步伐有所放缓；它们在使库存水平与销售更相匹配方面继续取得进展。尽管经济活动可能在一段时间内仍会疲软，但委员会预计，稳定金融市场和金融机构的政策措施、财政与货币刺激措施，以及市场力量，将在价格稳定的环境下助力经济增长走强，并逐步使资源利用率恢复到更高水平。

<!--en-->
Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in September suggests that economic activity has continued to pick up. Conditions in financial markets were roughly unchanged, on balance, over the intermeeting period. Activity in the housing sector has increased over recent months. Household spending appears to be expanding but remains constrained by ongoing job losses, sluggish income growth, lower housing wealth, and tight credit. Businesses are still cutting back on fixed investment and staffing, though at a slower pace; they continue to make progress in bringing inventory stocks into better alignment with sales. Although economic activity is likely to remain weak for a time, the Committee anticipates that policy actions to stabilize financial markets and institutions, fiscal and monetary stimulus, and market forces will support a strengthening of economic growth and a gradual return to higher levels of resource utilization in a context of price stability.

由于大量的资源闲置状况可能继续抑制成本压力，且长期通胀预期保持稳定，委员会预计通胀率将在一段时间内处于较低水平。

<!--en-->
With substantial resource slack likely to continue to dampen cost pressures and with longer-term inflation expectations stable, the Committee expects that inflation will remain subdued for some time.

在此背景下，美联储将继续运用多种工具来推动经济复苏并维持价格稳定。委员会将把联邦基金利率的目标区间维持在0%至0.25%之间，并继续认为，包括资源利用率低、通胀趋势温和以及通胀预期稳定在内的经济状况，将使得联邦基金利率在较长时间内需保持在极低的水平。为支持抵押贷款业务和房地产市场，并改善私人信贷市场的整体状况，美联储将购买总计1.25万亿美元的机构抵押贷款支持证券以及约1750亿美元的机构债务。虽然机构债务的购买规模略低于此前宣布的2000亿美元上限，但这与近期的购买节奏一致，也反映了机构债务供应的有限性。为促进市场平稳过渡，委员会将逐步放缓对机构债务和机构抵押贷款支持证券的购买速度，并预计这些交易将在2010年第一季度末完成。委员会将根据不断变化的经济前景及金融市场状况，持续评估其证券购买的时间安排和总量。美联储正在监测其资产负债表的大小和构成，并将在必要时调整其信贷和流动性计划。这是关于经济的报道 • 53 参与投票决定FOMC货币政策行动的人员包括：主席本·S·伯南克、副主席威廉·C·达德利、伊丽莎白·A·杜克、查尔斯·L·埃文斯、唐纳德·L·科恩、杰弗里·M·拉克尔、丹尼斯·P·洛克哈特、丹尼尔·K·塔鲁洛、凯文·M·沃什以及珍妮特·L·耶伦。⁵ 美联社对这份四段式的新闻稿进行了如下报道：

<!--en-->
In these circumstances, the Federal Reserve will continue to employ awide range of tools to promote economic recovery and to preserve price stability. The Committee will maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent and continues to anticipate that economic conditions, including low rates of resource utilization, subdued inflation trends, and stable inflation expectations, are likely to warrant exceptionally low levels of the federal funds rate for an extended period. To provide support to mortgage lending and housing markets and to improve overall conditions in private credit markets, the Federal Reserve will purchase a total of $1.25 trillion of agency mortgage-backed securities and about $175 billion of agency debt. The amount of agency debt purchases, while somewhat less than the previously announced maximum of $200 billion, is consistent with the recent path of purchases and reflects the limited availability of agency debt. In order to promote a smooth transition in markets, the Committee will gradually slow the pace of its purchases of both agency debt and agency mortgage-backed securities and anticipates that these transactions will be executed by the end of the first quarter of 2010. The Committee will continue to evaluate the timing and overall amounts of its purchases of securities in light of the evolving economic outlook and conditions in financial markets. The Federal Reserve is monitoring the size and composition of its balance sheet and will make adjustments to its credit and liquidity programs as warranted.
It's the Economy • 53
Voting for the FOMC monetary policy action were: Ben S. Bernanke, Chairman; William C. Dudley, Vice Chairman; Elizabeth A. Duke; Charles L. Evans; Donald L. Kohn; Jeffrey M. Lacker; Dennis P. Lockhart; Daniel K. Tarullo; Kevin M. Warsh; and Janet L. Yellen.⁵
The Associated Press covered this four-paragraph release this way:

<!--en-->

<!--en-->
The Fed said economic activity has “continued to pick up” and that the housing market has strengthened, a key ingredient for a sustained recovery.

但美联储主席本·伯南克及其同事警告称，未来几个月中，日益严重的失业问题以及许多企业和个人面临的信贷紧张状况，可能会阻碍经济复苏的势头。

<!--en-->
But Fed Chairman Ben Bernanke and his colleagues warned that rising joblessness and tight credit for many people and companies could restrain the rebound in the months ahead.

他们表示：“经济活动可能在一段时间内仍会疲软。”

在此背景下，美联储将其银行贷款利率的目标区间维持在0%至0.25%之间。同时，它也没有对旨在降低抵押贷款利率的计划做出重大调整。

<!--en-->
Against that backdrop, the Fed kept the target range for its bank lending rate at zero to 0.25 percent. And it made no major changes to a program to help drive down mortgage rates.

用于确定房屋净值贷款、某些信用卡及其他消费贷款利率的商业银行最优惠贷款利率将维持在约3.25%，为数十年来最低水平。

Commercial banks’ prime lending rate, used to peg rates on home equity loans, certain credit cards and other consumer loans, will remain about 3.25 percent, the lowest in decades.

尽管如此，过去几个月中仍有一些信用卡利率上升了。这部分是因为贷款机构为应对信用卡贷款违约率的上升而提高了利率。此外，在明年年初限制信用卡客户利率突然上涨的新法律生效之前，这些贷款机构也抢先提高了利率。[^692]：⁵ 来自联邦储备委员会2009年11月4日发布的联邦公开市场委员会新闻稿。54 • 关于国会经济议题，众议院周三投票决定加快制定新规则的进程，以保护消费者免受此类意外利率变动的影响。除非信用卡公司同意冻结利息和费用，否则它们必须立即遵守新规，而非从2月份开始。但该提案在参议院通过的可能性被认为很低。

Still, some credit card rates have risen over the past several months. In part, that reflects rate increases by lenders in response to escalating defaults on credit card loans. On Capitol Hill, the House voted Wednesday to accelerate the enactment date of the new rules to protect consumers from many such surprise changes. Credit card companies would have to comply immediately, rather than starting in February, unless they agreed to freeze interest rates and fees. But the proposal's chances in the Senate are considered dim.

根据Bankrate.com的统计，全国范围内浮动利率信用卡的平均利率为11.5%。由于这类债务的风险更高，贷款机构会收取更高的费用，信用卡用户的还款利率也会高于基准利率。

<!--en-->
The average rate nationwide on a variable-rate credit card is 11.5 percent, according to Bankrate.com. Lenders charge more and credit card customers pay rates higher than the prime because the debt they run up is riskier.

在华尔街，美联储宣布消息后，道琼斯工业平均指数起初仍保持了100多点涨幅。但最终在盘后交易中大部分涨幅被抹去。目前尚不清楚美联储的声明起到了多大作用。一些分析师指出，随着周五政府10月就业报告的发布临近，投资者情绪变得紧张。

<!--en-->
On Wall Street, the Dow Jones industrial average at first held onto an increase of more than 100 points after the Fed's announcement. But stocks eventually gave up most of their gains in a late-day slump. It wasn't clear how much of a role the Fed's statement played. Some analysts noted that investors are nervous as the release of the government's October jobs report on Friday approaches.

在正常情况下，美联储仅控制短期利率。但在金融危机爆发后，美联储开始购买长期国债，其购买行为使得这些长期利率保持在较低水平。

<!--en-->
In normal times, the Fed controls only short-term rates. But after the financial crisis erupted, the Fed began buying longer-term Treasuries. Its purchases kept those rates lower than they'd otherwise be.

这对拥有汽车贷款、部分学生贷款、15年期及30年期固定利率抵押贷款以及部分可调利率抵押贷款的借款人来说是好消息。但这会对储户以及那些通常能获得更高收益、依赖固定收入的人造成不利影响。

<!--en-->
This is good news for borrowers with auto loans, some student loans, 15- and 30-year fixed-rate mortgages and some adjustable-rate mortgages. But it hurts savers and people dependent on fixed incomes who would normally be enjoying higher yields.

周三，美联储重申其承诺，将利率维持在“异常低”的水平“较长时间”。大多数分析师认为，美联储要到明年春季或夏季才会开始上调利率。

<!--en-->
On Wednesday, the Fed stuck with its pledge to keep rates at "exceptionally low" levels for "an extended period." Most analysts don't think the Fed would begin to boost rates until next spring or summer.

Naroff经济顾问公司的乔尔·纳罗夫表示：“美联储的政策制定者认为，他们需要保持低利率，以确保经济复苏不会受阻。”

<!--en-->
Fed policymakers "believe they need to keep rates low to ensure that the recovery doesn't falter," said Joel Naroff of Naroff Economic Advisors.

央行希望低利率能够鼓励消费者和企业增加支出，从而推动经济复苏。由于通货膨胀几乎不存在，美联储表示可以继续维持低利率。

<!--en-->
The central bank hopes low rates will encourage consumers and businesses to boost spending, which would invigorate the recovery. The Fed signaled that it can continue to hold rates low because inflation is all but nonexistent.

美联储现已进入一个新的阶段：管理经济复苏，而非应对自大萧条以来该国遭遇的最严重的经济衰退和金融危机。

<!--en-->
The Fed has now entered a new phase: Managing the recovery rather than fighting the worst recession and financial crisis to hit the country since the Great Depression.

上个季度，经济在一年多来首次再度增长。但这一增长很大程度上来自政府支持的住房及汽车消费。一旦政府支持措施取消，复苏的强劲程度及其可持续性仍存在不确定性。

<!--en-->
The economy began growing again last quarter for the first time in more than a year. But much of that growth came from government-supported spending on homes and cars. The strength and staying power of the recovery are uncertain, especially once government supports are removed.

东京三菱银行的经济学家克里斯·鲁普基表示，在如此脆弱的复苏形势下，美联储短期内不太可能上调利率。

<!--en-->
In such a fragile recovery, a rate increase by the Fed is unlikely anytime soon, said Chris Rupkey, an economist at the Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi.

鲁普基说：“经济增长并不意味着要提高利率。”

<!--en-->
"Growth does not mean a rate hike," Rupkey said.

与以往的复苏情况类似，此次初现的复苏也不太可能阻止失业率上升。目前的失业率已达到26年来的最高值9.8%，预计在周五政府发布10月失业数据时将升至9.9%。分析师们称，失业率可能在明年年中上升至10.5%左右，之后才会下降。• 55 当经济复苏稳固之后，美联储很可能会开始释放即将提高利率的信号。一个表明未来可能加息的迹象，就是美联储改变或放弃其关于将利率维持在历史低水平“较长时间”的承诺。

<!--en-->
As with past rebounds, the budding recovery won't likely stop the unemployment rate from rising. The rate, now at a 26-year high of 9.8 percent, is expected to hit 9.9 percent on Friday, when the government releases the unemployment report for October. The jobless rate could rise as high as 10.5 percent around the middle of next year before declining, analysts said.
