the *Sarasota Herald-Tribune*, required coverage of the Port of Manatee, the boat builders in the region, orange juice maker Tropicana, and tourism as regular beats, with frequent trips to the U.S. Bankruptcy Court and attendance at downtown development authority meetings as well. There was no way to regulate when news broke either—in my office hangs a front page of a *Herald-Tribune* business section with one story about the port, two stories about Tropicana, and another about the upcoming tourist season.
Working a beat requires a number of skills and strategies that can be used for virtually any type of coverage or story. Let's examine a few of those now.

### 建立消息来源

<!--en-->
*Developing Sources*

任何优秀的商业记者都会努力在自己的报道领域建立消息来源。这需要走出办公室去结识他人，与陌生人共进早餐和午餐，探索一些独特且不寻常的联络方式。

<!--en-->
Any good business journalist will want to develop sources on their beat. This requires getting out of the office and meeting people, having breakfast and lunch with strangers, and exploring some unique and unusual ways of making contacts.

如果你的报道领域涉及一些大型企业，显然了解那里的员工非常重要。根据企业的沟通策略，公关人员可能成为极有价值的消息来源。公关人员努力在以最佳方式展示企业形象与向记者提供其撰写高质量报道所需的信息之间取得平衡。有些公关人员会向商业记者提供可能被解读为负面的企业信息，因为他们知道这样记者在后续报道中就不会对该公司过于苛刻。

<!--en-->
If your beat has some large companies, obviously it is important to know the people who work there. The public relations professionals can be, depending on the company's communications strategy, great sources. PR people strive to balance their job of presenting their company in the best possible way with giving a journalist the information he or she needs to tell a proper story. Some PR people give business reporters information about their companies that can be construed as negative, knowing that the reporter will come to respect them on future stories with less impact.

与企业高管建立关系也很关键，但若不通过公关团队很难接触到他们。有些高管愿意与新记者见面，帮助他们了解企业的运作方式及战略。可以询问是否有可能安排这样的会面；虽然很可能不会公开记录，但这有助于你更深入地理解报道内容。一些顶尖的商业记者会与他们所报道的企业高管建立更紧密的关系。例如，CNBC的查尔斯·加斯帕里诺曾与前贝尔斯登首席执行官吉米·凯恩共进晚餐。不过，这类关系可能会引发质疑，即记者能否公正地报道该企业。

<!--en-->
Developing a relationship with the company executives can also be key, but getting access to them is difficult without going through the PR staff. Some executives like to meet with new reporters on a beat to help them understand how the company works and its strategy. Ask if such a session might be available; it will likely be off-the-record, but it will help you understand what you're writing about. Some top business journalists develop closer relationships with the executives they cover. CNBC's Charles Gasparino, for example, had dinner with former Bear Stearns CEO Jimmy Cayne. But such relationships can lead to questions about whether the journalist can cover the company impartially.

企业内部的其它消息来源可能更为重要。与基层员工交谈往往能让商业记者更准确地了解企业内的实际情况。这些员工通常能提供有关CEO战略成效以及新战略能否成功的见解。他们还能提供在企业内部广泛流传的信息，比如内部通讯或高管的电子邮件，这些都可能具有新闻价值。尽管这些员工出于担心遭到企业报复通常只愿非公开交流，但他们与企业的密切联系极具价值。

<!--en-->
Other sources within a company can be even more important. Talking to lower-level employees can often give a business reporter a more accurate picture of what's going on at a company. These workers can often provide perspective on the effectiveness of the CEO's strategy and whether a new strategy has a chance of succeeding. They can also provide information that is widely disseminated within the company, such as internal newsletters or e-mail communications from executives, that could be newsworthy. While these employees will often only talk off-the-record for fear of retribution from the company, their closeness to the company can be invaluable.

在建立消息来源方面，前员工和高管同样重要。虽然他们无法再向商业记者透露企业内部情况，但他们通常仍与现职员工保持联系，能够提供关于在该企业工作的经历的一些见解。前董事会成员也同样有价值。可以查找新公司发布的新闻稿，查看其中提及的经理或高管过去的任职经历，判断他们是否曾在你报道过的企业工作过。最简单的做法是通过谷歌或Lexis-Nexis频繁搜索。报道仍在继续 • 73 还有其他一些可能有用的消息来源，可用于报道某家企业。竞争对手往往也是极为宝贵的消息来源。他们有时对自己企业的了解程度与对竞争对手的了解程度相当。任何关于企业的介绍性或战略类报道都应尝试纳入竞争对手的动态或相关信息。

<!--en-->
Former employees and executives are often just as valuable when it comes to source development. While they can no longer tell a business reporter about what's going on at a company, they often remain in contact with current employees and can provide some perspective of what it was like to work at the business. Former board members are just as valuable. Look for press releases that name managers or executives at new companies and review their past work experience to see ifthey were once employed at a company you cover. The easiest way to do this is to search frequently via Google or Lexis-Nexis.
The Beat Goes On • 73
Other sources can be developed that could be useful in covering a company. Competing businesses can often be invaluable sources. They will sometimes know as much about their competitor as they do about their own operations. Any profile or strategy story about a company should attempt to include a comment from or information about what a competitor is doing as well.

在任何商业报道领域，供应商也是不错的消息来源。供应商能告诉商业记者某家企业是否是值得合作的伙伴。他们能告知企业是在要求更多产品、要求降价或抵制涨价，还是拖欠货款。后者可能表明该企业存在财务问题。

<!--en-->
Suppliers are also good sources on any business beat. Suppliers can tell a business journalist whether a company is a good business partner. They can tell you if a company is demanding more product, asking for price breaks or resisting a price increase, or is slow to pay its bills. The latter could be an indication that a company is having some financial problems.

华尔街的分析师和投资者也是获取相关资讯的优质来源。那些关注某家公司或特定行业的分析师，往往能够对公司的战略是否有效提供见解，并对其股价发表意见。投资者也会做同样的事情。不过，对于这两类人都要有所警惕：他们都有希望公司发展的利益诉求。在投资银行工作的卖方分析师喜欢夸大公司的优势，以便吸引投资者通过他们的机构购买股票，从而让他们能从交易佣金中赚取薪水。而投资者则希望通过股价上涨获利。当然，也有一些被称为做空者的投资者，他们会在公司股价下跌时获利，这些人同样可以成为有价值的消息来源。

<!--en-->
Wall Street analysts and investors are also good sources on any beat. Analysts who follow a company or a specific industry can often provide some perspective on whether a company's strategy is working and give opinions about its stock price. Investors will do the same. A word of caution for both, however: They have a vested interest in seeing the company prosper. Sell-side analysts who work for investment banks like to pump up a company so that investors will buy the stock through their firm, helping the analyst earn his or her salary with the commissions on those trades. And an investor profits by seeing the stock price go up. Of course, there are some investors, called short sellers, who profit when a company's stock price falls, and they too can be valuable sources.

别忘了其他可能与你报道的公司或行业有过接触的专业人士，他们也是不错的资源。顾问通常专注于特定的公司或行业，或许曾为你所报道的企业提供过服务。大学教授也是如此，尤其是商学院的教授。他们在进入学术界之前可能曾在该行业工作过，也可能有过咨询经验。此外，会计和律师也可能对相关公司有所了解。在许多城市，通常会有专门处理针对大型企业诉讼的律师。

<!--en-->
Let's not forget others, primarily professionals, who may come into contact with the companies or industries on your beat and can be good resources. Consultants often specialize in specific companies or industries and may have done work in the past for businesses that you cover. The same goes for university professors, particularly those at business schools. They may have worked in the industry before joining academia, and they, too, may have performed consulting work. There are also accountants and lawyers who may know a thing or two about the company. In many cities, there's typically an attorney who specializes in lawsuits against large companies.

最后，阅读其他记者关于你所报道的行业或公司的报道。很多情况下，会有行业新闻简报或出版物介绍该行业内部的种种情况。虽然这些内容可能不会吸引你的读者，但它们能帮助你快速了解重要信息，还能为你提供写作灵感。

<!--en-->
Finally, read what other journalists are reporting about the industry or the companies on your beat. In many cases, there will be industry newsletters or publications that will write about the so-called "inside baseball" of the business. While these stories may not be of interest to your readers, they do help you get up to speed on what's important, and they can give you story ideas.

### 了解运作机制

<!--en-->
*Understanding How Things Work*

说实话，我们大多数人成为记者是因为不喜欢上数学和科学课。然而现在身为商业记者，我们却不得不学习那些曾经回避的数学技能，而且根据所报道的行业不同，还可能需要学习一些科学、医学、化学或其他领域的基础知识。我们要如何尽快掌握这些知识，才能避免在稿件中显得愚蠢呢？

<!--en-->
Let's face it, most of us became journalists because we didn't like taking math and science classes. Yet now that we're business journalists, we're forced to learn many of the math skills that we shunned, and, depending on the industry, we might be forced to learn some basics of science, medicine, chemistry, or another field. How is that going to happen soon enough for us to avoid looking like idiotic in print?

我们可以从几个方面来回答这个问题。如果你以前从未做过商业报道，那就需要快速学习如何阅读公司财务报表并解读其中的数字。别担心，大多数商业记者只需要掌握基本的加减法，或许还需要了解一些百分比知识。这些不都是我们在八年级就学过的吗？关于商业记者应如何阅读财务报表的更多内容，请参阅第9章。74 • 持续报道 如果你已经报道过一些商业新闻，现在要转向新的报道领域，那么财务方面的知识你应该已经有些了解了。

<!--en-->
Let's answer that question in a couple of ways. If you've never been a business reporter before, you're going to need a crash course in how to read company financial statements and decipher the numbers. Don't worry; all most business reporters need to do is some basic addition and subtraction, and maybe somepercentages. That’s all stuff each of us learned by the eighth grade, right? For more on how a business journalist should read financial statements, check out Chapter 9.
74 • The Beat Goes On
If you’ve already covered some business stories and are switching to a new beat, then the financial stuff should be somewhat familiar to you already.

接下来我们来看看撰写具有足够深度和分析力的报道所需的行业专业知识，这样才能让就连那些在你所报道的公司工作过的人也感到印象深刻。

<!--en-->
Let’s plow ahead though to the industry-specific knowledge that you’re going to need to write stories with enough knowledge and analysis to impress even the people who have worked at the companies you’re covering.

1994年我开始报道可口可乐公司时，原以为这会是个简单的报道领域。我以为没有什么比销售含气彩色糖水更基础的了。但我大错特错。任何想要成功深入饮料行业的记者，都必须了解饮料公司与装瓶商之间的关系——这些装瓶商往往是决定一款新饮品成败的关键因素。他们还需要意识到，这些公司在全球数十个国家开展业务，在每个国家都可能有其他产品，因此了解全球经济形势非常重要。他们还得明白，饮料公司极度依赖广告以及消费者对他们的印象，所以了解广告和媒体行业也同样关键。此外，记者还需要对自动售货机业务有所了解，因为当消费者在餐厅或便利店购买饮料时，关键在于哪家饮料公司谈成了更有利的交易条件。

<!--en-->
When I started covering the Coca-Cola Co. in 1994, I thought that this would be an easy beat. I thought that there was nothing more basic than selling carbonated, colored sugar water. I couldn’t have been more wrong. Any reporter who’s going to infiltrate the soft drink industry with any success must understand the relationship that soft drink companies have with their bottlers, who are often the reason why a new beverage succeeds or fails. They need to realize that these companies operate in dozens of countries around the world, and, in each, the company may have other products, so an understanding of the global economy is important. They have to come to grips with the fact that soft drink companies rely heavily on their advertising and the image that consumers have of them, so knowing the advertising and media world is key as well. And that reporter is going to need to know something about the fountain business, because when consumers purchase a soft drink at a restaurant or a convenience store, it’s all about which soft drink company negotiated a better deal.

换句话说，入职大约两周后，我就完全迷失了方向。我花了整整一年时间才逐渐能够自如地撰写关于这些主题以及其他相关内容的报道——同时我还在负责非饮料类的报道。要熟悉一个行业的运作方式以及其中一家公司的盈利或亏损状况需要时间。但你必须迅速学会行业术语，以便能与高管、顾问及相关人员交流，理解他们所说的话。

<!--en-->
In other words, after about two weeks on the job, I felt totally lost. It took me a good year to feel comfortable writing about all of these topics, as well as others on the beat—while I was also covering a non-beverage beat. Becoming comfortable with how an industry works and how a company in that industry makes or loses money takes time. But you’ve got to quickly learn the industry lingo to talk with the executives, consultants, and hangers on so that you’ll understand what they’re saying.

如果可能的话，看看你的新闻机构能否安排你参加行业会议或贸易展。这能让你在短短几天内掌握数年的行业知识。这类活动上的与会者和演讲者往往在该行业深耕数十年，不妨主动上前与他们交流，尽可能多提问，并做好笔记，充分吸收所学内容。如果有你负责报道的公司的人在场，可在他们不忙时跟随左右，请求他们给予简短的指导。

<!--en-->
If possible, see if your news organization can send you to an industry conference or trade show. This will give you the opportunity to cram a couple of years of knowledge into a few days. The people and speakers attending such events have often been in the industry for decades. Don’t be afraid to buttonhole them and ask as many questions as possible. Take notes and soak it all in. If there are people there from companies on your beat, follow them around and ask for some short tutorials if they’re not busy.

查看当地社区学院是否有与你所在行业相关的课程，甚至是基础会计课程。你的新闻机构甚至可能承担学费。这类课程通常在晚上开设，等你白天在新闻编辑部工作结束后再上，因此不会影响处理突发新闻。

<!--en-->
See if there is a class available at a local community college related to your industry, or even in basic accounting. Your news organization might even pay the tuition. Such courses are often offered at night, after you’ve spent the day in the newsroom, so they won’t interfere with breaking news.

同样，要阅读行业出版物。如果你是刚接触银行领域的记者，可以看看《美国银行家》；我在报道可口可乐相关新闻时，则依靠每两周发行一期 的《饮料杂志》。

<!--en-->
Again, read industry publications. If you’re new to the banking beat, check out *American Banker*. My salvation on the Coke beat was *Beverage Digest*, a newsletter that came out every two weeks.

无论哪个商业领域的学习曲线都很陡峭，尤其是当你对行业或产品不了解时。在报道初期遇到不懂的内容时不必过于焦虑。如果有人与你交谈，可以请他/她为你解释不明白的地方。因为日后你也必须为读者或观众做同样的解释，所以现在弄清楚总比盯着空白的电脑屏幕不知该如何撰写高管要求的那些晦涩文字要好。《报道进行时》• 75

<!--en-->
The learning curve on any business beat is steep, particularly if you’re unfamiliar with the industry or the products. Don’t get too worked up when you run across something that you don’t understand, particularly during the early weeks on the beat. If someone is talking to you, ask him or her to explain what you don’t understand. You’ll essentially have to do the same for your readers orviewers later on, so it's better to get it explained now than to stare at a blank computer screen wondering how to write the gobbledygook that some executive told you.
The Beat Goes On • 75

### 挖掘新闻线索

<!--en-->
*Mining For Stories*

对于新手商业记者来说，最难做到的事情之一就是想出新的新闻点子。有多年报道经验的记者知道过去报道过什么以及哪些内容具有新闻价值，但新手则缺乏这些背景信息，尤其是那些刚进入商业新闻岗位的人。

<!--en-->
One of the hardest things for a new business reporter to accomplish is to come up with new story ideas. A reporter who has been on the beat for several years knows what's been covered and what has been newsworthy in the past, but the new beat reporter has no context, particularly if he or she is new to the business desk.

新手商业记者最简单的做法之一就是与之前负责该领域的记者交流。这个人可能仍在报社工作，其对行业的了解极具价值。可以一起梳理该领域的关键消息来源，并询问前任记者这些来源过去愿意提供哪些信息。同时也可以向老记者请教应对公司的策略。

<!--en-->
One of the easiest steps for a new business beat reporter to take is to talk to the reporter who previously covered the beat. This person may still be at the paper, and their knowledge of the beat can be extremely valuable. Go over key sources on the beat and ask the previous reporter what kind of information these sources have been willing to part with in the past. Also ask the old beat reporter for strategies for dealing with companies.

新记者还应查阅前任记者在任期间撰写的报道。有些题材会反复出现，比如盈利报告和上市公司年度股东大会的相关报道，阅读这些内容能让新记者了解过去常用的报道角度。旧报道也可能为新人带来新的灵感——也许某家公司多年前曾发布过关于新产品的重大公告，读者和观众可能会想知道该新产品的发展情况。

<!--en-->
The new beat reporter should also look at the stories that the previous reporter wrote during his or her tenure. Some stories will repeat themselves, like earnings stories and stories about a public company's annual meeting, so reading these will let the new reporter know what angles have been covered in the past. Old stories could also spark new story ideas for the new beat reporter. Maybe a company on the beat made a major announcement several years ago about a new product. Readers and viewers might like to know how that new product is doing.

也别害怕向报道领域的消息来源询问新闻点子。在采访某家公司的CEO之前，可以先询问负责报道该公司的分析师，他们希望从CEO那里了解到哪些信息。还可以与竞争对手沟通，了解他们最想了解该公司的哪些方面。这类信息通常也会引起商业新闻读者的兴趣。虽然公司的公关人员很乐意提供新闻点子，但要确保这些点子是真实的，而非尚未成文的新闻稿。优秀的公关人员会提供出色的新闻点子，也能成为你构思报道的良师益友。

<!--en-->
Don't be afraid to ask sources on the beat for story ideas as well. Ask an analyst who covers a company what information they'd like to know from a CEO before you interview that CEO. Talk to competitors to find out what they're most interested in knowing about the company. This type of information is typically interesting to business news readers as well. While a company's corporate communications staff will be more than willing to provide story ideas, make sure that they're legitimate and not just a press release that hasn't been written. The best PR people will provide excellent story ideas, and they'll be a good sounding board to pitch story ideas off of.

了解你所报道的公司的高管们阅读什么，然后也去阅读那些出版物。行业出版物往往涉及只有业内核心人士才关心的深奥内容，但它们在揭示重要话题或问题方面往往比主流媒体快数月。

<!--en-->
Find out what the executives at the companies you write about read and read those publications as well. Industry publications often cover esoteric material that only the hard-core industry people care about, but they also are often months ahead of the mainstream media in exposing topics or issues that are important.

最后，与普通民众交流。你的朋友、邻居和熟人都是获取新闻线索的优质来源，尤其是当你报道那些每天与消费者互动的公司或行业时。他们可以告诉你是否对购买的产品和服务质量满意。此外，他们还常常能提供一些轶事，可用于你的报道中帮助解释相关情况。

<!--en-->
Finally, talk to average, everyday people. Your friends, neighbors, and acquaintances are prime sources to tap for story ideas, particularly if you're covering companies or industries that interact with consumers on a daily basis. They can tell you whether they're happy with the products they've purchased and the quality of the service. Plus, they often end up providing anecdotes to use in your stories to help explain what's going on.

## 常见报道领域

<!--en-->
*Common Beats*

虽然没有两个商业新闻编辑部是完全相同的，但大多数商业新闻机构都会报道一些常见的主题。这些主题包括银行与/或金融服务、制造业、科技、经济、零售业以及医疗保健领域。其他一些主题可能涉及投资/华尔街以及媒体/广告行业。最后，大多数规模尚可的商业新闻机构都会设有固定专栏作家，负责针对各种趋势和问题发表观点。76 • 新闻报道仍在继续 尽管商业新闻领域的记者可能会报道不同类型的新闻，但他们的报道与写作方式依然属于基础新闻报道：他们会提出大量问题，并尽力获取尽可能多的信息。优秀的商业记者与优秀的犯罪记者或政府记者并无不同——他们都熟悉自己的报道领域，也知道该去哪里寻找有价值的新闻素材。

<!--en-->
While it's true that no two business news desks are identical, there are some common beats that most business news organizations will cover. These include banking and/or financial services, manufacturing, technology, the economy,retail, and health care. Some others might be investing/Wall Street and media/ advertising. Finally, most decent-sized business news operations have a regular columnist who provides opinions on trends and issues.
76 • The Beat Goes On
While beat reporters on a business desk might be covering different types of stories, how they report and write those stories is still basic journalism: They ask a lot of questions and try to get as much information as possible. A good business reporter is no different than a good crime reporter or a good government reporter. Each knows their turf, and they know where to look for good stories.

事实上，新闻编辑部中的非商业报道领域也可以向商业报道领域的同行学习一些技巧。商业记者通常会询问资金的使用情况以及这些资金是否被合理使用。他们还常常关注开展业务的两方之间的关联。这些商业报道的要素——资金状况与人际关系——是所有记者在撰写新闻时都应该关注的，即便这些内容与商业领域几乎没有关联。

<!--en-->
In fact, non-business beats in a newsroom could stand to learn a few tricks from their business brethren. A business reporter commonly asks how money was spent and whether that money was spent wisely. A business reporter is also often interested in knowing the connections between two parties conducting business. Those aspects of business reporting—the money and the connections—are elements that all reporters would be wise to look for in their stories, even if they have little or nothing to do with business.

在本书的其余部分，你将了解到在任何报道领域都能出现的常见商业新闻，比如财报、新CEO的任命、并购等。在本章中，我们将探讨一些仅存在于典型商业报道领域的独特新闻。

<!--en-->
In the rest of the book, you’ll learn about basic business stories that can be found on any beat—earnings, the naming of a new CEO, a merger or acquisition, etc. In this chapter, we’ll take a look at some stories that are unique to the basic business beats.

关于商业报道还有另一点需要记住：所有企业都存在竞争。思考一下你所报道的企业竞争对手希望从你的新闻中了解什么。无论报道的内容是什么，哪怕只是关于某家本地冰淇淋店在某个周末免费派发冰淇淋的消息，你也应该采访该行业的竞争对手，看看这会对附近其他冰淇淋店的销售产生怎样的影响。

<!--en-->
Remember one more thing about business beats: All businesses have competition. Think about what a competitor to the business that you’re writing about would want to know in your story. You would do well to interview competitors on any beat for any story, even if it’s about a local ice cream store that is giving away free ice cream one weekend. How does that impact sales of the closest ice cream store?

让我们来看看这些领域的部分记者是如何覆盖他们的报道范围以及所撰写的新闻的。

<!--en-->
Let’s take a look at how some reporters on these beats cover their territory and the stories they’re writing.

## 银行业

<!--en-->
*Banking*

银行类记者负责报道某座城市内的金融机构的相关新闻。鉴于21世纪初的经济形势，联邦政府开始更加严格地监管银行，并关闭了一些银行，这一领域因此在许多社区重新引起了人们的关注。在那些拥有大型银行总部的城市里，这些银行往往也是当地最大的雇主。

<!--en-->
A banking reporter writes stories about the financial institutions in a city. Given the economic conditions during the early part of the twenty-first century, with the federal government taking a closer look at banks and shutting some down, bank coverage has taken on a renewed interest in many communities. In cities where a major bank is headquartered, it might be the largest employer in the community as well.

虽然银行领域的许多新闻与其他领域的新闻类似，比如财报或新门店的开业与关闭，但也有一些独特的报道内容。精明的银行记者会查阅联邦存款保险公司的市场份额数据，以判断该银行在当地的客户存款是在增加还是减少。此外，他们还会研究银行的贷款策略是否有效，或者是否存在不良贷款问题。这些数据同样可以从联邦政府那里获取。

<!--en-->
While many stories on the banking beat are similar to those of other beats, such as earnings and the opening and closing of new locations, there are other stories to tell. A savvy banking reporter checks a bank’s market share data with the Federal Deposit Insurance Corp. to determine whether it’s gaining or losing consumers’ deposits in the community. A banking reporter is also looking at a bank to determine whether its lending strategy is successful or if it’s making bad loans. This data can also be gathered from the federal government.

里克·罗斯哈克为《夏洛特观察家报》报道银行业新闻已近十年，2009年，他因对总部位于夏洛特的华盛顿互惠银行和美国银行的报道而获得杰拉尔德·洛布奖，这是商业新闻领域的普利策奖。罗斯哈克表示自己仍在不断学习。“尽可能多地进行采访总是好的，即使是对你不太感兴趣的话题也是如此，因为你永远不知道什么时候会再次需要与该人交谈，”罗斯哈克说。“曾经在这些银行工作过的人可以成为很有用的消息来源。作为该领域的记者，员工和其他人也知道应该联系你。不过，你始终还可以做更多工作来建立优质的信息来源。”新闻报道仍在继续 • 77 《观察家报》有两名银行类记者。罗斯哈克和另一位记者克里斯蒂娜·雷克斯罗德会根据当天的新闻动态分配报道任务，但他们也表示，即便如此也不可能覆盖所有的银行相关新闻。“我们最初的设想是克里斯蒂娜主要负责面向消费者的新闻，而我则负责更多企业相关的新闻，但由于新闻量实在太大，这种界限已经变得模糊了，”罗斯哈克说道。

<!--en-->
Rick Rothacker has covered banking for the *Charlotte Observer* for nearly a decade, and in 2009, he received a Gerald Loeb Award, the Pulitzer Prize of business journalism, for his beat coverage of banking in Charlotte, where Wachovia and Bank of America are both based. Rothacker said that he’s still learning on the beat. “It’s good to do every interview you can, even when it’s on a topic you’re lessexcited about, because you never know when you may want to talk to that person again,” said Rothacker. “People who used to work at the banks can be helpful sources. When you’re the beat reporter, employees and others also know to contact you. You always can be doing more, though, to develop good sources.”
The Beat Goes On • 77
The *Observer* has two banking reporters. Rothacker and the other reporter, Christina Rexrode, break up the beat each day depending on what’s going on, but even then, it’s impossible to cover every banking story, they say. “Our original theory had been that Christina would focus more on consumer-oriented news, while I would handle more corporate-type news, but with so much news going on, those lines blurred,” said Rothacker.

银行报道——实际上任何商业领域的报道都是如此——另一个重要的方面就是查阅监管文件。以下就是雷克斯罗德根据美国证券交易委员会的文件撰写的一篇关于美国银行的新闻的线索：

<!--en-->
Another important aspect of banking reporting—and for any business beat for that matter—is checking regulatory filings. Here’s the lead to a Bank of America story that Rexrode wrote from a Securities and Exchange Commission filing:

> 在政府监管机构的推动下，美国银行董事会的动荡于周五晚间仍在持续，该银行宣布又有三名董事辞职。威廉·巴内特、约翰·柯林斯和加里·坎特里曼是在2004年美国银行收购他们此前任职的FleetBoston Financial Corp.后加入董事会的。作为斯帕坦堡市市长的巴内特离任后，除了银行首席执行官肯·刘易斯之外，董事会中已没有与卡罗来纳州有密切关联的成员。该银行在周五下午5点后提交的监管文件中表示，每位董事辞职“并非与公司或其管理层存在分歧”，这一表述与其他近期董事离职的原因描述如出一辙。¹

<!--en-->
> The shake-up in Bank of America Corp.’s boardroom, apparently orchestrated by the hand of government regulators, continued Friday evening, when the bank announced that three more of its directors have resigned.
William Barnet, John Collins and Gary Countryman joined the board in 2004 after Bank of America bought FleetBoston Financial Corp., where they were serving as directors. The departure of Barnet, who is the mayor of Spartanburg, means there are no more directors with notable ties to the Carolinas except for bank chief executive Ken Lewis.
The bank said in a regulatory filing, made after 5 p.m. on Friday, that each director’s decision to resign “was not as a result of any disagreement with the Corporation or its management,” echoing the language of other recent board departures.¹

## 制造业

<!--en-->
*Manufacturing*

随着美国经济对工业的依赖程度降低、对服务业的依赖程度上升，对于许多新闻媒体而言，制造业领域的报道已不再那么重要。但它依然在重要性以及推动某些城镇和城市经济发展方面发挥着重要作用。

<!--en-->
As the American economy becomes less reliant on industry and more reliant on services, the manufacturing beat has become less important for many news outlets. But it can still pack a punch in terms of importance and in driving local economies of some towns and cities.

在那些拥有从钢铁、汽车到冷冻食品等各类大型工厂的社区，报道制造业状况有助于更全面地了解国家经济形势。当当地制造业发展良好时，通常意味着整个国家经济状况也不错；但当这些制造商陷入困境并被迫裁员时，往往也预示着整体经济正在面临困难。

<!--en-->
In communities where there are large plants that make everything from steel to automobiles to frozen food, covering manufacturing can give a broader glimpse of the nation’s economy. When things are going well for manufacturing locally, typically that means that the national economy is doing well. But when these manufacturers struggle and are forced to lay off workers, it’s often a sign that the broader economy is struggling as well.

制造业记者并不一定会报道这些工厂生产的产品，除非工厂主决定在某地生产新产品，而这可能会带来更多就业机会或让现有员工能够继续工作。相反，这些领域记者[^934]：¹ 来自C. Rexrode于2009年8月1日发表在《夏洛特观察家报》第1D页的文章《又有3名美国银行董事辞职：政府压力可能是这家总部位于夏洛特的银行董事们辞职的原因之一》，版权归2009年《夏洛特观察家报》所有，经许可转载。78 • 持续报道

<!--en-->
Manufacturing reporters don’t necessarily write stories about the products that are being made at these plants, unless a factory’s owner decides that a location is going to produce a new product and that might mean more jobs or that the current job force will be able to keep working. Instead, these beat reporters

78 • The Beat Goes On

### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《罗利新闻与观察家报》的零售行业记者苏·斯托克给出了以下关于采访购物者的建议：

<!--en-->
Retail reporter Sue Stock of The (Raleigh) News & Observer has these recommendations on interviewing shoppers:

1. 我知道这很基础，但当你一天要进行大约20次街头采访时，很容易对其中一些采访掉以轻心。相信我……我有八年的采访经验。**尽可能向每个人询问所有你能想到的问题。**详细记录每个人的身份信息……所在城市、年龄、职业、为他们谁购物、他们的支出与去年相比如何等等。他们和谁一起购物？也要记下那个人的姓名、年龄和身份信息。做到极度好奇真的会带来很大好处，比平常还要认真，因为你永远不知道哪个细节会是你需要的，而且几乎每年，这个细节都不是我在采访时预料的那个。
2. **也别忘了你采访的购物者的外在特征：**他们的袋子是哪家商店的？有多少个袋子？他们看起来疲惫不堪还是仍对购物充满热情？他们的口袋里有没有露出收据？他们穿什么衣服？如果你不把它们记下来，等回到办公室时就记不起是哪位购物者了。
3. **做好详细的笔记：**当笔记本上记录的人太多时，很容易把他们搞混。实际上我会把笔记本的页面折起来，以便区分不同的人。
4. **尽可能获取他们的所有电话号码：**如果他们是和姐姐、女儿或母亲一起购物，也要把那些人的号码弄到手。有相当多的购物者在离开商场后，要么把手机和所有包一起留在车里，然后倒下休息，要么因为精神疲惫而关掉手机。总会有些问题是你当时希望自己能问出口的。这类报道通常会聚焦于工厂的变动，比如是否因需求增加而增设了第三班次，或者工人是否被暂时解雇。这些工人也可能属于工会，因此工人与公司之间关于新合同的谈判也是重要的报道内容。制造业记者也可能花时间报道其他类型的新闻，比如工厂是否购置了新设备，或者公司是否出台了新的弹性工作制，让职业妈妈有机会重返工作岗位。不幸的是，由于许多制造企业的员工需要操作重型设备，这些工人在工作中受伤甚至死亡的可能性也存在。关于工作场所安全或具体伤害事件的报道通常由制造业新闻板块负责。制造商与工人之间难免会发生冲突。以下是南卡罗来纳州《格林维尔新闻报》的记者埃里克·康纳对其中一起事件的报道开头：

<!--en-->
1. I know this is elementary, but when you are doing like 20 man-on-the-street interviews in one day, you can tend to get a little lazy with some of them. Trust me . . . eight years of experience talking here. **Ask everyone everything you can think of.** Get super full IDs on everyone . . . town, age, occupation, who they are shopping for, how their spending compares to last year, etc. Who are they shopping with? Get names, ages, and IDs on them too. It really, really pays to be super, super nosy. More so than normal. Because you never know which detail is going to be the one you need, and almost every year, it's not the one I expected when I was interviewing them.
2. **Also don't forget the physical aspects of the shoppers you interview:** Which stores are their bags from? How many do they have? Do they look run down or still excited about shopping? Do they have receipts sticking out of their pockets? What are they wearing? If you don't write it down, you won't remember which shopper it was by the time you get back to your desk.
3. **Keep really good notes:** It's really easy to get the people mixed up when you have so many in your notebook. I actually fold the pages down in my notebook to separate people.
4. **Get every phone number you can out of them:** If they're shopping with [their] sister, daughter, mother, get those numbers too. A surprising number of shoppers get home from the mall and either leave their phone in the car with all their bags while they go collapse or turn their cell off because they are mentally exhausted. There is always a question you wish you'd asked.
often focus on changes at the plant, such as whether a third shift has been added due to demand or whether the workers have been furloughed. These workers might also belong to a union, so any negotiations between the workers and the company over a new contract are also major stories.
Manufacturing reporters may also spend some time on other types of stories as well, such as whether the plant is getting new equipment or whether the company has instituted a new flexible schedule that allows working moms the chance to return to the workforce. Unfortunately, because the employees of many manufacturing companies are working with heavy equipment, there's also the chance that some of these workers might get injured, or even die, while on the job. Writing about workplace safety or the specific injuries themselves commonly falls to the manufacturing beat.
Conflicts between manufacturers and their workers are bound to arise. Here's how Eric Connor, a reporter for the *Greenville News* in South Carolina, wrote a lead about one of these incidents:

> 十名前员工起诉了格林维尔的哥伦比亚农场鸡肉加工厂，称该公司拒付他们应得的加班费，还有其中一名员工因被指控伪造工伤而被解雇。该诉讼已移交联邦法院审理，与此同时，这家公司周四还因被控故意雇佣非法劳工而面临另一项刑事指控并出现在联邦法庭上。² 关于制造商的报道也应更加广泛。近年来美国汽车工业所面临的问题，正是制造商努力适应日益激烈的国际竞争的体现。许多报道都探讨了这些制造商过去本可以做出哪些改变——或做出不同的决策——以避免当前的困境。

<!--en-->
> Ten former employees have sued the Columbia Farms chicken processing plant in Greenville, alleging the company refused to pay overtime that they worked and, in one case, fired a worker after accusing her of faking a workplace injury.
> The suit, moved into federal jurisdiction, comes as the company on Thursday appeared in federal court on separate, criminal charges alleging the willful hiring of illegal workers.²
Broader stories should also be written about manufacturers. The problems of the American automobile industry in recent years have been a story of how manufacturers have struggled to adapt to growing international competition. Many stories have examined where these manufacturers could have made changes in the past—or made different decisions—to prevent their current problems.

## 零售业

<!--en-->
*Retail*

由于每个社区都有销售从服装到汽车零件的商店，零售业通常是每个商业新闻板块都会关注的领域。零售业相关的报道范围很广，包括新公司进入市场并开设分店，零售商关闭门店退出市场，已在市场上运营的零售商开设新店，现有门店在非原有地点开设分店，以及购物中心或商业街等新设施的开业。

<!--en-->
Because every community has stores that sell everything from clothing to car parts, retail is typically a beat that every business desk covers. Retail stories can include everything from a new company entering the market and opening stores, to a retailer closing its stores and exiting the market, to a retailer already in the market opening a new store, to a store that's opening a location different from its existing stores, to a new development such as a mall or strip center opening.

最优秀的零售业记者是那些走出新闻编辑室，每天大部分时间都与消费者、店员及其他相关人士交流情况的人。通过持续关注当地的零售业动态，他们能够比其他人更早发现趋势，比如当附近出现新的零售中心时，某家购物中心可能就会陷入困境。[^948]：² 来自E.康纳2009年7月31日发表于《格林维尔新闻报》第1A版的文章《哥伦比亚农场工人起诉公司：鸡肉加工厂对雇佣指控拒不认罪》，版权归2009年《格林维尔新闻报》所有。《新闻不断》•79 零售业记者需要掌握判断一家店铺或连锁店经营状况的方法。所有零售商都会关注同店销售额，即那些已经营业至少12个月的门店的销售额。同店销售额上升是店铺经营良好的迹象。另一个衡量标准是每平方英尺的销售额。通过比较同一行业不同零售商的每平方英尺销售额，可以判断哪家店的业务更兴旺。不同类型的零售商其每平方英尺销售额水平也有所不同，珠宝商的这一数值通常最高。

<!--en-->
The best retail reporters are the ones who get out of the newsroom and spend most of their days talking to shoppers, store employees, and others about what's happening. Through constant examination of the local retail scene, they're able to discern trends before others, like when a mall may be struggling because a new retail center opened up nearby.
[^948]: ² From “Columbia Farms workers sue company: Chicken processor enters not guilty plea to charges in hiring case,” by E. Connor, July 31, 2009, *Greenville News*, p. 1A. Copyright 2009 by *Greenville News*.
The Beat Goes On • 79
A retail reporter needs to know how to gauge the health of a store or a chain. All retailers look at their same-store sales, or sales of stores that have been open for at least 12 months. An increase in same-store sales is a sign of a healthy retailer. The other measure for retailers is its sales per square foot. Compare the sales per square foot of retailers in the same line of business to determine which one is getting more business from their stores. Different types of retailers will have different levels of sales per square foot. Jewelers typically have the highest level.

由于零售商遍布全国各地，即使店铺并不位于媒体所在地区，商业记者也会撰写相关报道。此外，记者还会报道零售业领域的趋势和问题，比如大型零售店开始在店内开设快餐店，或是网络购物的兴起。

<!--en-->
Retailers are located across the country, so business reporters write stories about retailers even though the retailer may not be located in the media's market. In addition, reporters write stories about trends and issues in retailing, such as when big box retailers began opening fast-food restaurants inside their stores or the rise of Internet shopping.

零售业记者几乎从不，甚至从来不会撰写零售商希望他们写的那些关于客户销售等趋势或问题的报道。许多零售商会试图推销一些纯粹为了获得免费宣传的文章。

<!--en-->
Retail reporters rarely, if ever, write about the trends or issues that retailers want them to write about, such as customer sales. Many retailers will attempt to pitch stories that are nothing more than an attempt to gain free publicity.

有一个值得注意的例外，那就是感恩节到圣诞节期间的假日购物季。零售业记者的薪资取决于他们对这一假日购物季的报道质量。

<!--en-->
There is one notable exception, and that's the holiday shopping season that occurs between Thanksgiving and Christmas. Retail reporters earn their salaries based on how well they cover the holiday shopping season.

《罗利新闻与观察家报》的零售行业记者苏·斯托克已从事该领域报道近十年，她为其他零售记者提供了许多与顾客交谈时的建议。她总是穿舒适的鞋子，并把外套留在车里，因为采访结束后她总会脱掉外套，不想在记笔记时还要兼顾拿着外套。

<!--en-->
Sue Stock, the retail reporter for *The* (Raleigh) *News & Observer*, has covered the retail beat for nearly a decade, and she has a number of recommendations for retail reporters when they're out talking to shoppers. She always wears comfortable shoes, and she leaves her coat in the car, because she always ends up taking it off and doesn't want to have to juggle it while taking notes.

斯托克建议，在进行采访时应寻找在儿童游乐区或美食广场休息的顾客。“这样你也可以坐一会儿，也不那么显眼，”斯托克说，“而且人们喜欢边吃边聊，他们会分享更多信息。”

<!--en-->
Stock's recommendation for interviews is to look for shoppers taking a break at the kid play area or at the food court. "This also allows you to sit for a minute and makes you less conspicuous," says Stock. "And people like to talk while they eat. They'll share more."

感恩节次日及整个假日购物季的零售相关报道往往千篇一律，最好尝试从新的角度来讲述这些故事。在20世纪90年代末和本世纪初，新的视角就是互联网购物的兴起。

<!--en-->
Retail stories on the day after Thanksgiving and throughout the holiday shopping season can be repetitive. It's best to try to find a new angle to tell this story. For the late 1990s and the early part of this century, the new angle was the rise of Internet shopping.

以下是我曾尝试为典型的圣诞零售购物报道带来不同视角的一些独特零售报道：

<!--en-->
Here are some offbeat retail beat stories that I once did in an attempt to bring a somewhat different perspective to the typical Christmas retail shopping stories:

1. 在为《坦帕论坛报》工作期间，我在圣诞节次日乘坐垃圾车四处行驶。为什么？因为12月26日是一年中最繁忙的垃圾清运日，就如同圣诞节前的周六是一年中最繁忙的购物日一样。我们看到了那些被丢弃的礼物——包装纸还完好地贴在包裹上。
2. 我在为《亚特兰大宪报》报道第一个圣诞购物季时，感恩节后的那个周五就开始跟踪一名塔吉特商店的经理，从她早上5点左右到店开始就跟著她。从商店经理的角度来看待第一个重要的购物日，能让你获得完全不同的视角。
3. 同样在亚特兰大，我在12月26日与两位正在为明年的圣诞节选购礼物的女士共度了一天——距离圣诞节仅有364天。这无疑为我提供了看待圣诞零售季的全新视角。80 • 报道仍在继续
4. 大学期间，我曾在一家Honey Baked Ham商店的圣诞假期期间工作，因此深知圣诞季对这类商店的重要性。它们每年约75%的销售额都来自感恩节到圣诞节这段时间。有一年，后厨的员工连续工作18小时给火腿上釉，而商店经理则为我们送来披萨。于是那一年我写了一篇关于Honey Baked Ham、Hickory Ham以及其他火腿店之间的“火腿之战”的报道。
5. 12月24日那天，我还去寻找那些典型的最后时刻才去购物的男人。那是个有趣的报道，因为我看到他们拼命地为女友、妻子、孩子等寻找礼物。我是如何找到这些人的呢？对于其中一些案例，比如12月24日的那篇报道，我只是去商场里寻找那些看起来像是逃班的人。至于其他一些案例，报纸在商业版面刊登了小块启事，邀请符合“提前364天为圣诞节购物”特征的读者与我们联系。至于垃圾车的那篇报道，只需致电当地的环卫公司即可。他们很乐意配合，不过这让我不得不在圣诞节次日凌晨4点30分就赶到垃圾场开始写作。关键在于：不要只写那种在感恩节后周五采访商店经理的典型零售报道，他们都会说销售情况很好；也不要只是重复那些用来判断圣诞销售额是上升还是下降的数字。试着以有趣的方式撰写圣诞零售报道，跳出常规思维。

<!--en-->
1. While at the *Tampa Tribune*, I spent the day after Christmas driving around on a garbage truck. Why? Dec. 26 is the busiest garbage day of the year, just like the Saturday before Christmas is the busiest shopping day of the year. We saw presents that were thrown out—with the wrapping still on the packages.
2. When I was at the *Atlanta Journal-Constitution*, the first Christmas shopping season I covered, I spent the Friday after Thanksgiving shadowing a Target store manager, beginning at about 5 a.m. when she arrived at the store. You get a much different perspective of the first major shopping day when you look at it from the store manager's perspective.
3. Also in Atlanta, I spent one Dec. 26 with two women who were shopping for next year's Christmas—only 364 days in advance. That was definitely a different perspective on the Christmas retail season.
80 • The Beat Goes On
4. Having worked at a Honey Baked Ham store during the Christmas holidays while I was in college, I knew how important the Christmas season was to ham stores. They get about 75 percent of their annual sales between Thanksgiving and Christmas. One year, the staff in the back worked 18 hours straight glazing hams, with the store managers bringing in pizzas for us. So I wrote a story one year about the “Ham Wars” between Honey Baked Ham, Hickory Ham, and the other ham store locations.
5. I also went out one December 24 to find the stereotypical guys doing their last-minute shopping. That was a fun story, as I watched them frantically try to find presents for girlfriends, wives, kids, etc.
How did I find these people? For some of them, like the December 24 story, I just went to the mall and looked for guys who appeared to be playing hooky from work. For some of the other stories, the newspaper ran a small box on the front of the business section asking for readers who might fit the profile of someone who shops 364 days in advance for Christmas to contact us. For the garbage story, it simply took calling the local sanitation company. They were more than happy to oblige, although for me it meant getting to the dump at 4:30 a.m. the day after Christmas to begin writing the story.
The point is this: Don’t just write the typical retail story that interviews store managers on the Friday after Thanksgiving. They’re all going to say that sales are good. Don’t just regurgitate the numbers that assess whether Christmas sales are up or down from the previous year. Have some fun writing Christmas retail and think outside the box.

# 医疗保健

<!--en-->
*Health Care*

几乎所有媒体都将医疗保健视为重要报道领域，原因很简单：当地医院通常是最大的雇主之一。虽然许多媒体从新发疾病（如2009年在美国肆虐的H1N1流感）或疾病治疗进展的角度报道医疗保健，但越来越多的媒体也开始撰写有关所在社区医疗保健产业的相关报道。

<!--en-->
Health care is an important beat in nearly every media outlet for the sole reason that the local hospital is typically one of the largest employers. And while many news outlets cover health care from the perspective of new illnesses, such as the H1N1 flu that swept the United States in 2009, or of advances in treating illnesses and injuries, an increasing number of them are also beginning to write stories about the business of health care in their communities.

医疗保健其实是一门庞大的生意。大多数美国医院的年度收入都超过1亿美元，但并非所有医院都被视作企业来报道。尽管其中一些是非营利机构，但商业记者仍应仔细研究它们的运营方式，因为它们实际上也是以企业模式运作的。

<!--en-->
And health care is big business. Most U.S. hospitals have more than $100 million in annual revenue, yet not all of them get covered as a business. Even though some of them are non-profit, a business reporter should take a close look at their operations, because they are run as businesses.

假设坦帕的一家医院想要增设新生儿重症监护室，但该市已有另外三家医院提供此类服务。那么，监管机构会允许这家医院扩张从而增加竞争吗？这就是值得探讨的故事，正如纳什维尔的《田纳西人报》的记者吉尔·塞西尔·威尔斯玛所做的那样。

<!--en-->
Let’s say that one hospital in Tampa wants to add a neonatal intensive care unit, but there are three other hospitals in the city that already offer such a service. So, do regulators allow that hospital to expand and increase competition? That’s a story to explore, as reporter Jill Cecil Wiersma did for the *Tennessean* newspaper in Nashville when she wrote this brief:

> 威廉姆森医疗中心与莫里地区医院于7月23日提交了申请，请求在戴维森县大法官法庭于8月19日举行的听证会上，允许媒体报道有关经济衰退、通用汽车破产、失业率预测以及当地经济的情况。《报道继续》•81 正是在那天，法庭将审议这起已持续3年的诉讼的下一轮上诉，该诉讼针对的是HCA TriStar健康系统建造一家56张病床医院的计划。这家医院已两次获得该州卫生服务发展局颁发的需求证明。³ 医疗行业板块的一则重要新闻是医疗护理成本的上升。虽然其他产品及服务的成本停滞不前，但医疗成本仍在持续上涨。部分原因在于新的治疗技术和设备延长了人们的生命；另一部分原因则是如今消费者更多地寻求医疗服务。医疗行业板块还会探讨就业问题，因为许多社区都存在护士等特定岗位的合格求职者短缺现象。我在华盛顿与李大学任教时，曾有学生写过一篇精彩的文章，讲述当地药店为吸引药剂师到弗吉尼亚州农村工作所采取的措施。医疗行业板块的记者也经常撰写关于保险的文章，内容可能涉及基本健康保险政策是否涵盖新型治疗方法，以及大型健康保险公司与医疗服务提供者（如您所在社区的医院集团或连锁诊所）之间的合同谈判。撰写医疗相关文章还意味着要关注联邦政府，因为医疗保险和医疗补助计划是医疗费用的主要支付方。医院、医生及其他医疗服务提供者能从这些计划中获得多少报销，往往决定了他们当年的盈亏状况。与其他许多服务类报道领域一样，医疗行业板块也可能涉及对欺诈行为的报道——包括消费者和医疗服务提供者的欺诈行为。可以通过查找诉讼或州级监管行动来发掘这类新闻。

<!--en-->
> Williamson Medical Center and Maury Regional Hospital filed a motion July 23 asking that media reports about the recession, General Motors’ bankruptcy, unemployment rate predictions, and the local economy be allowed for the Aug. 19 date in Davidson County Chancery Court.
The Beat Goes On • 81
That's when the court considers the next round of appeals in the 3-year-old case against HCA TriStar Health System's plans for a 56-bed hospital. The facility has twice earned a certificate of need from the state's Health Services Development Agency.³
A big story on the health care business beat is the rising cost of receiving medical care. While the costs of other products and services have stagnated, health care costs continue to rise. Some of it is due to new treatments and equipment that keep us alive longer. Some of the increase in cost is due to the fact that consumers simply use more health care providers these days.
The health care beat also explores employment, because in many communities there's a dearth of qualified applicants for specific jobs, such as nursing. When I taught at Washington & Lee University, one of my students wrote a great story about what the local drug stores were doing to recruit pharmacists to come work in rural Virginia.
The health care beat reporter often writes about insurance as well, and this can mean looking at topics such as whether basic health insurance policies cover new types of treatment, as well as contract negotiations between large health insurance companies and health care providers, such as a hospital group in your community or a chain of doctors' offices.
Writing about health care also means writing about the federal government, as the Medicare and Medicaid systems are large payers of health care. How much hospitals, doctors, and other health care providers are reimbursed by these plans often means the difference between a profit and a loss for the year.
As with many other service-related beats, the health beat can also result in writing about fraud—both by the consumer and by the provider. Look for lawsuits or state regulatory action to find these stories.

## 科技

<!--en-->
*Technology*

科技板块看似很有趣。由于每月都有各种新 gadget 和软件问世，总有新内容可写。《华尔街日报》的沃尔特·莫斯伯格和《纽约时报》的大卫·波格等记者因其能够对这些新产品进行点评，并告诉消费者其优缺点而声名鹊起，甚至出现在电视节目中。

<!--en-->
The technology beat can seem like a fun one. With all of the new gadgets and software coming out each month, there's always something new to write about. Reporters such as Walt Mossberg of *The Wall Street Journal* and David Pogue of *The New York Times* are famous and appear on television because of their ability to critique these new products and tell consumers what's good and bad about them.

大多数科技记者将自己的报道领域视为两方面内容的结合：一方面为读者提供其所报道公司推出的产品的建议，另一方面对公司的财务状况进行更客观的报道。由于每年都有许多科技公司成立，因此针对小型公司的很多科技报道都会考察这些企业是否具备成功所需的资金、商业计划以及产品。

<!--en-->
Most tech reporters look at their beat as a combination of providing advice to their readers about the products that the companies they cover are introducing and of providing more objective reporting about the financial aspects of the companies. Because many tech companies get started every year, a lot of tech coverage of smaller companies takes a look at whether these businesses have the funding, the business plan, and the products to become successful.

科技板块需要谨慎平衡，因为像微软和苹果这样的大型公司试图控制媒体对其的报道方式，而许多小型公司则愿意接受任何形式的报道。任何科技记者的目标都是提供其认为对读者最有用的报道。如果您不在加利福尼亚州或西雅图，那就多关注本地的科技企业，把全国性的新闻留给通讯社。您的读者会更想了解本地的科技企业，而关于苹果或微软的新闻他们可以从其他十几个渠道获取。[^981]：³ 摘自J.C. Wiersma于2009年7月31日在《田纳西人报》上发表的文章《医院称经济衰退是新建医院的阻碍》，第2页。版权所有2003年《田纳西人报》。82 • 报道继续 有许多博客和网站关注科技领域，包括TechCrunch、Gizmodo、Engadget、All Things Digital，以及传统的商业媒体。事实上，不少科技记者已经离开传统印刷媒体，开始运营博客或网站。虽然其中一些网站会发布传闻和来自非正式渠道的信息，从而突破了传统报道的界限，但对于科技记者来说，这些内容仍然很有价值。

<!--en-->
The tech beat is a careful balancing act in that there are many large companies, such as Microsoft and Apple, that are trying to control how they are covered inthe media, and there are many small companies that will take just about any coverage they can get. The goal of any tech writer is to provide the coverage that he or she thinks will be most useful to readers. If you're not based in California or Seattle, then focus more on your local tech companies and save the national stories for the wire services. Your readers will want to know more about the local tech guys, and they can get news about Apple or Microsoft from a dozen other sources.
[^981]: ³ From “Hospitals contend recession is factor against building new hospital,” by J.C. Wiersma, July 31, 2009, *The Tennessean*, p. 2. Copyright 2003 by *The Tennessean*.
82 • The Beat Goes On
There are a number of blogs and websites that cover the tech area, including TechCrunch, Gizmodo, Engadget, and All Things Digital, as well as the traditional business media. In fact, a number of tech reporters have left print media and started blogs or sites. While some of these sites stretch the boundaries of traditional reporting in that they post rumors and information from off-the-record sources, they are valuable to read if you're a tech reporter.

寻找科技新闻的好地方是美国专利商标局。科技公司必须在此为他们的发明提交专利和商标申请。在很多情况下，这些专利文件会详细说明他们计划何时以及如何推出新产品。

<!--en-->
A great place to look for tech stories is with the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office. This is where tech companies will have to file patent and trademark applications for their inventions. In many cases, these patents will detail how and when they plan to launch new products.

请记住，现在许多科技记者除了为出版物撰稿外，还会写博客。这些博客受到当地科技界的密切关注，是与潜在消息来源建立联系的绝佳途径。

<!--en-->
Realize that many tech reporters now blog as well as write stories for their publication. These blogs are followed closely by the local tech community and represent a great way to make connections with potential sources.

## 媒体/广告

<!--en-->
*Media/Advertising*

由于大多数公司都会利用媒体来宣传自己的产品和服务，因此本地广告行业也是许多商业新闻编辑部在报道中会涉及的领域。

<!--en-->
Because most companies use the media to advertise their products and services, the local advertising industry is also a beat that many business news desks incorporate into their coverage.

报道这一领域意味着需要与本地的广告和传播公司取得联系，了解他们何时获得或失去业务。如果一家广告代理公司为某家全国性企业获得了新客户，很可能意味着他们将招聘员工来处理这些新业务；显然，如果该代理公司把客户让给了其他公司，情况则相反。

<!--en-->
Covering this beat means getting in touch with the local advertising and communication shops and finding out when they gain or lose business. If an ad agency obtains a new account for a national company, it likely means they'll be hiring employees to take care of that new work. The opposite is true, obviously, if the agency loses an account to another firm.

在广告和媒体行业中，很多工作都依赖于人脉关系，因此如果这些公司中有企业因员工跳槽到竞争对手处或员工离职创办自己的公司而失去部分关键员工，其业务也可能会随之流失。需仔细追踪员工的流动情况。有时，一家公司更换广告代理公司只是因为其创意总监去了另一家公司。

<!--en-->
In the advertising and media business, a lot of work is based on relationships, so if one of these firms loses some of its key employees to a competitor or employees leave to start their own firm, it could mean that business will follow those workers out the door as well. Track carefully the comings and goings of staff members. Sometimes a company will change ad agencies because a creative director has gone to a new shop.

这里也可以考虑趋势类报道。如果某家航空公司开始在互联网网站上投放更多广告，那么其他竞争对手也可能效仿。同时还要观察其他新闻如何影响特定公司的广告策略。例如，在飞机失事后，航空公司的广告风格可能会发生变化，过去可能较为轻浮的广告现在可能会变得更严肃。

<!--en-->
Think about trend stories here as well. If one airline starts using more ads on Internet sites, then it could mean that competitors will follow. And look at how other news might affect a specific company's advertising. After an airplane crashes, it could mean a change in the tone of airline advertising, which might have been more flippant in the past.

美联社在MSNBC.com网站上发表的一篇报道，以一篇极具前瞻性的文章探讨了电视上广告出现的新地点。以下是文章开头：

<!--en-->
An Associated Press story, which ran on the MSNBC.com site, looked at the new places where advertising was showing up on television in a strong trend story. Here is the lead:

很快就会出现在您的电视上：更多广告，出现在您意想不到的地方。

<!--en-->
Coming soon to your TV: More advertising, in places you might not expect.

这些广告如今出现在人们以往用来避开广告的场合，比如点播视频和屏幕上的频道指南。就连因允许用户跳过电视广告而广受欢迎的那维奥（TiVo），也在开发新的广告展示方式。⁴ 这个领域的报道仍在继续 • 83 在媒体报道领域中最棘手的任务之一就是报道自己的雇主，而这项工作往往由商业记者承担。《纽约时报》决定将《波士顿环球报》出售给潜在买家时，商业记者理查德·佩雷斯-佩纳撰写了大部分相关报道。这也意味着这些报道会受到商业版编辑乃至更高层编辑的严格审查。这是一项吃力不讨好的工作，但在这类报道中做到准确公正应是理所当然的。

<!--en-->
The ads are showing up where people used to enjoy a break fromadvertising, such as video on demand and on-screen channel guides. Even TiVo, which became popular for its technology that lets people skip TV commercials, is developing new ways to show ads.⁴
The Beat Goes On • 83
One of the toughest stories on the media beat is covering your own employer, and many times that job falls to a business reporter. When the *New York Times* decided to shop the *Boston Globe* to potential buyers, business reporter Richard Perez-Pena garnered most of those bylines. It also means that the stories get close scrutiny from the business editor and potentially from editors higher up. It's a thankless job, but being accurate and fair in these types of stories should come as second nature.

## 投资/华尔街

<!--en-->
*Investing/Wall Street*

许多大型商业新闻编辑部还会指派一名记者为本地读者跟踪市场动态。这意味着该记者需要找到一种方法，用本地人能理解的方式解释华尔街的情况及其对他们的影响。

<!--en-->
Many larger business news desks will also assign a reporter to follow the markets for local readers. This means that the beat reporter needs to find a method to explain Wall Street in such a way that the locals can understand what's going on and how it impacts them.

通常，这会导致该记者每天撰写关于本地股票表现的文章，并与本地资金管理人交谈，以获取他们对特定股票或整体市场的看法。虽然这些报道确实为商业新闻受众提供了信息，但它们已经很常见，相关内容几乎可以在网络上的任何地方找到。

<!--en-->
Often, this results in the beat reporter writing a daily story about how local stocks performed and talking to local money managers to get their perspective on specific stocks or the overall market. And while these stories do perform a service for business news consumers, they're also shopworn, and the information can be found just about anywhere on the Web.

在观察报纸和其他媒体如何报道市场时，我更欣赏那些独特的报道方式。例如，《克利夫兰平原商报》会让自己的记者与当地股票经纪人一较高下，看看谁的表现更好。《亚特兰大宪报》多年来一直开设专栏，分析公司内部哪些人在买卖该公司股票——这往往是股价即将上涨或下跌的信号。

<!--en-->
When looking at how newspapers and other media follow the markets, I'm impressed more with unique ways of telling the investing story. *The Cleveland Plain-Dealer*, for example, pits one of its reporters against a local stockbroker to see who's doing better. *The Atlanta Journal-Constitution* ran a column for years that looked at who inside companies was buying and selling the company's stock—often a sign that the price might be ready to jump or fall.

如果这是您的报道领域，那就想办法以有趣的方式向读者介绍投资界的动态。如果汽油价格上涨，可以写写大宗商品市场以及那里的原油价格如何影响我们在加油站的花费。如果一家公司的季度利润持续增长，但其股价却毫无变动，可以将其表现与该行业的其他股票进行比较；也许在市场低迷时期，它的表现实际上优于竞争对手。

<!--en-->
Look for interesting ways to tell your readers what's going on in the investment world if this is your beat. If gas prices are going up, write about the commodity market and how the price of a barrel of oil being traded there affects what we pay at the pump. Has a company's stock price failed to budge despite increasing quarterly profits for the past year? Compare its performance to that of other stocks in the industry; maybe it's actually outperforming its competitors in a down market.

媒体对投资的报道往往只集中在股市上。别忘了关注债券、大宗商品和货币市场。这些都是会影响本地商业新闻受众的市场，尤其是如果您居住在大都市地区。可以为计划出国旅行的人解释哪些货币相对于美元表现较好。如果一家公司申请了破产保护，导致其股票变得一文不值，可以写写其债券的价格走势如何。

<!--en-->
Too often, a media outlet's investing coverage focuses on the stock market. Don't forget to look at bonds, commodities, and currencies as well. These are all markets that affect local business news consumers, particularly if you live in a metropolitan area. Explain to people planning to travel abroad which currencies are doing better against the U.S. dollar. If a company has filed for bankruptcy court protection, thus rendering its stock worthless, write about how the price of its bonds is holding up.

对于刚接触某个报道领域的商业记者来说，他们的优势在于拥有新鲜的视角[^1003]：⁴ 来自美联社2009年8月2日的文章《等等！还有更多！那就是电视上的广告》，下载日期为2009年8月2日，来自http://www.msnbc.msn.com/id/32259924/ns/businessmedia_biz. 84 • 这个领域的报道仍在继续

<!--en-->
What is good about any business reporter new to a beat is that they have fresh
[^1003]: ⁴ From “But wait! There’s more! Ads on TV, that is,” Associated Press, August 2, 2009. Downloaded August 2, 2009 from http://www.msnbc.msn.com/id/32259924/ns/businessmedia_biz.
84 • The Beat Goes On

## 专业人士的经验之谈

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《休斯顿纪事报》的洛伦·斯特菲分享的商业专栏写作技巧：

<!--en-->
Business column writing tips from the Houston Chronicle's Loren Steffy:

1. **别被标题误导：**优秀的商业专栏并非单纯谈论商业本身。好的专栏会针对资金流动及其对人们的影响提供评论、分析与见解。相比记者，专栏作家往往更擅长看穿公关宣传的噱头，并能通过背景介绍帮助读者理解复杂话题。
2. **多样化选题：**不要让读者或编辑限制你的报道范围。随着越来越多的新闻工作转向网络，总有人会说新闻报道必须专业化。其实并非如此。金钱以多种方式影响着人们，你的专栏应尽可能覆盖更广泛的领域。
3. **多平台创作：**除了印刷版，还要通过博客、社交媒体、播客、视频等多种渠道传播你的观点。有些专栏在特定媒介上效果更好，不妨大胆尝试。
4. **走出办公室：**写专栏并不意味着只能坐在办公室里发表意见。要亲自去实地调研，与高管、员工、个人投资者等各类人群交流。永远不要独自吃饭——商务午餐是最有用的工具。多打电话，仔细查阅文件。
5. **利用记者作为信息来源：**当然不能直接引用他们的报道，但如果我要根据报纸上的新闻故事写专栏，我会喜欢和报道该新闻的记者聊聊。他们常常能察觉到一些无法写入报道的细节，却能帮你构思专栏内容。有时还能帮你为后续报道想出更好的问题，或是提供关于如何报道该主题的建议。当类似新闻再次出现时，他们不会重复五年前写的那些内容。在负责的新闻领域，不妨尝试新方法。

<!--en-->
1. **Don't be fooled by the title:** A good business column isn't about business per se. A good column provides commentary, analysis and insight about the flow of money and how it affects people. A columnist is often better able to cut through the PR spin than a reporter and can provide context in helping readers understand complex topics.
2. **Vary your topics:** Don't allow your readers or your editors to narrow your focus. As more journalism moves to the web, you'll be told it's all about specialization. It isn't. Money affects people in many ways, and your column should cast as wide a net as possible.
3. **Write across platforms:** Spread your voice not just in print but through blogs, social media, podcasts, video. Some columns work better with certain mediums than others. Don't be afraid to experiment.
4. **Get out of the office:** Writing a column doesn't mean opining from a seated position. Do your own leg-work. Meet with executives, workers, individual investors, everyone you can. Never eat alone. The business lunch is the most valuable tool in the toolkit. Work the phones. Dig through the documents.
5. **Use reporters as sources:** You can't quote them, of course, but if I'm writing a column based on a news story in the paper, I like to chat about it with the reporter. Often, they've picked up on subtleties that they can't put in the story but can help you formulate a column. Sometimes, it helps you come up with better questions for your own reporting.
ideas on how the topic should be covered. They aren't rewriting the same story they wrote five years ago when similar news comes up. Don't hesitate to try something new on your beat.

# 其他报道领域

<!--en-->
*Other Beats*

当然，这些并非商业板块仅涉及的题材。根据读者和当地经济的关注点，你可能会发现更多报道方向。无论是商业地产还是住宅地产，在每个社区都极为重要，我们将在后面的章节专门讨论如何撰写相关报道。

<!--en-->
Of course, these aren't the only topics that a business desk covers. Depending on what's important to your readers and the local economy, you might find a few more beats. Real estate—both commercial and residential—is so important in every community that we're going to spend a later chapter talking about how it should be written about.

## 体育产业

<!--en-->
*Business of Sports*

随着球队和联赛每年创造的收入不断增加，体育产业领域的报道重要性也在提升。事实上，现在有一本名为《Street & Smith's Sports Business Daily》的刊物，专门报道体育产业相关内容。巧合的是，它的所有者正是拥有全国40份周刊商业报纸的同一家公司。

<!--en-->
The sports business beat is growing in importance as teams and leagues bring in more and more revenue each year. In fact, there's now a publication, the *Street & Smith's Sports Business Daily*, covering nothing but the business of sports. It's owned, not coincidentally, by the same company that owns 40 weekly business newspapers across the country.

体育产业相关的报道主题多种多样，从新建棒球场所需的融资，到票价的调整，再到冰球队在斯坦利杯季后赛中表现出色对当地经济带来的影响。各类体育项目，包括儿童体育赛事，都有相关的体育产业报道。几乎每个春季周末在全国各地举办的足球锦标赛都是重要的经济推动力。

<!--en-->
Sports business stories can be on a number of different topics, from the financing of a new baseball stadium, to the raising or lowering of ticket prices, to the economic impact a hockey team brings to the local community by making a deep run into the Stanley Cup playoffs. Look for sports business stories in all kinds of sports, including those for kids. Soccer tournaments held around the country almost every weekend in the spring are big economic drivers.

## 商业专栏作家

<!--en-->
*Business Columnists*

许多商业板块都会设有商业专栏作家，一些规模较大的商业新闻机构甚至会配备多名专栏作家。例如，《纽约时报》每周都会安排不同的专栏作家撰稿，每位作家负责自己感兴趣的特定领域。如果你想了解媒体行业的相关内容，那就关注每周一大卫·卡尔的专栏；如果对个人理财感兴趣，那就等待每周六罗恩·利伯的专栏。

<!--en-->
Many business desks have a business columnist. Some of the larger business news operations have several. *The New York Times*, for example, has a different business columnist for each day of the week. Each one writes a column about his specific area of interest. If you want a column on the world of media, then it's Monday with David Carr. If personal finance is your thing, then wait until Saturday with Ron Lieber.

商业专栏作家的职责是对商业领域的动态提供分析、观点——当然还有他或她的个人见解。像《休斯顿纪事报》的洛伦·斯特菲这样的专栏作家，既会探讨全国性议题，也会关注德克萨斯州的本地问题；而像《奥兰多哨兵报》的贝丝·卡萨布则更倾向于聚焦本地事务。

<!--en-->
The business columnist's job is to provide some analysis and perspective—and, hopefully, his or her opinion—to what's going on in the business world. Some business columnists, like Loren Steffy of the *Houston Chronicle*, will tackle national issues as well as those closer to home in Texas. Others, like Beth Kassab of the *Orlando Sentinel*, prefer to stick to local issues.

卡萨布在成为专栏作家之前曾是该报的商业记者，她表示自己喜欢能够自由切换不同主题进行创作的灵活性。“能够从一个热门话题跳转到另一个话题，同时探索自己感兴趣的主题，这很有趣，”她说，“我觉得如果某件事能在我和家人、朋友的饭桌上引发大量讨论，那它很可能也在佛罗里达中部其他家庭的饭桌上受到关注。”

<!--en-->
Kassab, who had been a business reporter for the paper before becoming a columnist, says she likes the freedom to move around and write about different topics with each column. “It's fun to be able to jump from one hot issue to another and also to be able to explore subjects that are interesting to me,” she said. “I figure that if there's something that's sparking a lot of conversation around the dinner table with my family and friends then it's probably also getting attention at other dinner tables across Central Florida.”

写专栏的缺点在于，即便已经没有灵感，专栏作家仍必须在规定的发布日完成文章。而且，一旦成为专栏作家，就要准备好面对不同意你观点的读者。报道持续进行 • 85

<!--en-->
The downside to column writing is that the columnist has to produce each day the column is scheduled to run, even if he or she has run out of ideas. And, if youbecome a columnist, be prepared to hear from readers who disagree with your point of view.
The Beat Goes On • 85

## 农业

<!--en-->
*Agriculture*

在农业对社会而言至关重要的社区中，农业新闻领域主导着商业新闻的报道。爱荷华州的《得梅因纪事报》就设有专门负责农业新闻的编辑，该编辑已从事这一领域的报道数十年。

<!--en-->
The ag beat dominates business news coverage in communities where farming is a vital part of society. *The Des Moines Register* in Iowa has had a farm editor who has covered the beat for decades.

农业新闻记者的报道范围极广，从大型企业集团收购或出售家庭农场，到农民所获得的农作物价格皆在报道之列。例如，在佛罗里达州的《布雷登顿先驱报》和《萨拉索塔先驱论坛报》上，纽约商品交易所的浓缩橙汁价格就是重要新闻，因为该地区最大的雇主——也是这种产品最大采购商的特罗皮卡纳公司就在当地。

<!--en-->
Ag beat writers cover everything from the buying and selling of family farms by large conglomerates to the prices that farmers are receiving for their crops. At the *Bradenton Herald* and the *Sarasota Herald-Tribune* newspapers in Florida, for example, the price of frozen concentrated orange juice on the New York Board of Trade is an important story because the largest employer in the area is Tropicana, the biggest purchaser of the product.

近年来，农业新闻领域已扩展至其他议题，比如乙醇等与环境相关的商业话题。一些商业新闻部门甚至设立了绿色商业新闻板块，用以探讨企业如何调整运营以应对全球变暖等问题。

<!--en-->
Recently, the ag beat has expanded to include other issues, such as environmental business topics like ethanol. Some business news desks have even started a green business beat to examine how companies are adapting their operations to address issues such as global warming.

## 交通运输

<!--en-->
*Transportation*

由于几乎所有消费者都会在某种程度上受到交通运输的影响，因此交通运输新闻也是商业新闻部门常见的报道主题。如果某个社区拥有由监管机构管理的重大机场或港口，这类新闻也常常会出现在新闻版面中。

<!--en-->
The transportation beat is another common assignment on a business desk because virtually every consumer is affected in some way or another by transportation. This beat often shows up on the news side as well if a community has a major airport or port governed by a regulatory agency.

交通运输领域的商业新闻可以涵盖各种内容，从联合航空公司决定在本地机场新增六班航班，到灰狗巴士公司决定减少在该州境内的停靠站点。如果该州有大型货运公司，可以询问他们观察到的货物运输量是增加还是减少。

<!--en-->
Business stories on the transportation beat can cover everything from United Airlines deciding to add six new flights at the local airport to Greyhound's decision to cut back on its bus stops within your state. If there are major trucking firms in your state, talk to them about whether they're seeing an increase or decrease in freight shipped from one place to another.

港口为交通运输新闻提供了大量素材，尤其是在经济全球化日益加剧的背景下。各类产品通过大型油轮从地球的一端运往另一端，而它们进入美国的第一站通常就是港口。这些港口会统计进出港产品的种类，分析这些数据可能会发现有趣的现象，比如从迈阿密港出口的菠萝数量大幅增加。

<!--en-->
Ports provide major transportation stories, particularly with the increasing globalization of the economy. Products are shipped via major tankers from one side of the globe to another, and their first stop here in the United States is typically at a port. These ports keep statistics on what types of products are coming and going, and analyzing these numbers may result in an interesting find, such as a dramatic increase in the number of pineapples being shipped out of the Port of Miami.

## 结论

<!--en-->
*Conclusion*

随着你对所负责的新闻领域了解得越来越深入，处理更复杂的报道也会变得更加得心应手。不过，请始终把读者或观众放在心上。最优秀的商业新闻记者，既能与行业高管交流并理解复杂的话题，又能用普通人能理解的方式将这些难以理解的问题呈现出来。撰写商业新闻的目的是传递信息、提供娱乐并活跃讨论氛围。

<!--en-->
As you learn more about your beat, you'll become more comfortable covering more complex stories. Please keep your reader or viewer in mind, however. The best business news beat reporters are ones who can talk to industry executives and understand difficult topics but who can turn around and write about those hard-to-understand issues in a way that the average person understands. The object of covering a business news beat is to inform, entertain, and enliven the conversation.

6. **设身处地为读者着想：**专栏的核心在于与读者建立联系，而实现这一目标的最佳方式就是分享个人故事。要不断寻找简单的事例来帮助读者理解复杂的内容。我就曾以自己青少年时期经营的割草业务以及儿子幼年时的发脾气事件作为写作素材（前者用于探讨非法移民问题，后者用于讨论保险费率问题）。我还曾将抵押贷款证券化和信用违约互换比作巨无霸汉堡，读者们表示这帮助他们更好地理解了抵押贷款危机。
7. **不要害怕使用幽默：**虽然需要谨慎使用，但幽默确实能起到效果。我把惠普解雇前董事长帕特里夏·邓恩的事件写成了米基·斯皮兰风格的小说，把安然公司前高管未被起诉的事件写成了苏斯博士风格的童话，并将市场形容成本·伯南克难以捉摸的约会对象。读者喜欢出人意料的内容，他们并不期望商业专栏一定很严肃。
8. **调整专栏的节奏：**有些专栏需要大量的调研工作，有些则需要更多的写作精力。例如，加入幽默元素就需要更多时间来撰写。对于那些需要大量调研的专栏，要提前做好准备，同时搭配一些能更快完成的文章，以便在中间填补时间差。
9. **接受自己的局限性：**撰写专栏的目的不是证明自己正确，而是引发人们的思考。永远不要害怕承认自己的错误，或者撰写一篇表明自己正在改变观点的专栏。当有读者打电话指出你错了时，主动提出与他们见面。通常，这样的经历能为你带来另一篇精彩的专栏。我曾经写过一篇抨击“银行家”的专栏，86 • 新闻报道仍在继续

<!--en-->
6. **Put yourself in your work:** A column is all about connecting with readers, and the best way to do that is share personal stories. Always be looking for ways to use simple anecdotes to make the complex understandable. I've used my adolescent lawn-mowing business and my son's temper tantrums when he was a toddler as leads. (The former about illegal immigration and the latter about insurance rates.) I once compared mortgage securitizations and credit default swaps to a Big Mac. Readers told me it helped them understand the mortgage meltdown.
7. **Don't be afraid to use humor:** You have to use it judiciously, but it can be effective. I turned Hewlett-Packard's firing of former Chairman Patricia Dunn into a Mickey Spillane novel, the lack of indictments against a former Enron official into a Dr. Seuss tale, and portrayed the market as a fickle date for Ben Bernanke. Readers love the unexpected, and they don't expect a business column to be funny.
8. **Vary the pace of the columns:** Some take a lot of reporting, others take more effort on the writing. Humor, for example, takes much more time to write. Always be working ahead on the columns that will take more reporting time, and balance those with quicker-hit pieces that can help meet the deadlines in between.
9. **Embrace your fallibility:** Writing a column isn't about being right, it's about making people think. Never be afraid to admit you're wrong, or to write a column in which you acknowledge that you're changing your opinion. When a reader calls to tell you you're wrong, offer to meet with them. Often, you'll get another column from the experience. I once wrote a column that blasted "bankers," and a
