## 建议练习

<!--en-->
*Suggested Exercises*

1. 除了本章提到的步骤之外，你认为还可以采取哪些措施来快速掌握对某一特定商业领域的报道技巧？
2. 你的媒体机构指派你负责报道杂货店行业。请询问五位朋友他们希望看到关于杂货店的哪些类型的报道。你觉得其中有哪些是可行的报道主题？
3. 比较本章前面列出的《亚特兰大商业纪事报》与《亚特兰大宪报》的报道领域划分。你认为从报道结构来看，哪一份在展现当地社区方面做得更好？你会对这两份报纸的商业新闻报道领域做哪些调整？
4. 想想如果你是一名商业记者，最感兴趣报道哪个领域。在美国找一家从商业角度报道该主题的媒体机构，列出你喜欢它的三点以及不喜欢它的三点。
5. 如果让你负责报道能源行业，列出10种你希望发展成消息来源的人士类型，并说明你想从每个人那里获取的信息类型。这些消息来源可以来自相关企业的内部人员，也可以来自外部人士。
6. 比较TechCrunch对科技行业的报道与《圣何塞水星报》的同类报道。哪一份做得更好？它们的报道方式有何不同？距离休斯顿约90英里的一个小镇的社区银行行长表示不满：“我本应该区分大型银行和小型银行。”我驱车去见他，最终写了一篇关于互联网如何拓展小型银行业务范围的专栏文章。
10. **回复每一位读者的邮件**：接听每一通电话。这可能会耗费大量时间，但尽可能做到这一点非常重要。这不仅能建立与读者的良好关系，还能帮助你找到消息来源并获得专栏写作灵感。我很喜欢收到读者提出话题建议或询问“你为什么还没写过这个”的邮件。把那些抱怨的人变成消息来源：“跟我讲讲那个情况吧。”这可能是用普通读者让文章更具人性化最简单的方法。
11. **专栏是一笔宝贵的财富**：不要浪费它。你已经拥有了绝佳的发表平台。不要采用“来信箱”式评论、随手记下的内容堆砌，或是用星号分隔的一堆无关紧要的新闻片段。专栏的目的不是填满版面，而是以独特的方式讲述精彩的故事。你的读者值得你付出最大的努力。
12. **看在老天的份上，享受写作过程吧**：成为一名商业专栏作家是世界上最棒的工作之一。你可以撰写关乎世界运转的核心话题，还能用自己的声音来表达。几乎没有什么比金钱更能深刻影响人们了。有人将写专栏形容为跑步机上的运动，但千万别让它变成一种机械化的例行公事。五年来，我从未缺少可写的素材，也从未感到厌倦。

<!--en-->
1. Other than the steps mentioned in this chapter, what would you consider doing to get up to speed on covering a specific business beat?
2. You have been assigned to cover the grocery store industry for your media outlet. Ask five friends what types of stories they'd like to see about grocery stores. Do you think any of them are valid story ideas?
3. Compare the beat breakdowns of the *Atlanta Business Chronicle* and the *Atlanta Journal-Constitution* listed earlier in the chapter. Which one do you think does a better job of covering the community based on its beat structure? What would you change about each paper's business news beats?
4. Think about what beat you would be most interested in covering if you were a business reporter. Find a media outlet somewhere in the United States that covers that topic from a business perspective. List three things you like and three things you dislike about its coverage.
5. List 10 types of people you would want to develop as sources if you were given the energy industry to cover and list the type of information you'd like to get from each one. These sources can be inside or outside the companies on the beat.
6. Compare the coverage on TechCrunch to the coverage of the tech industry in the *San Jose Mercury News*. Which one did a better job? How were they different in their coverage?
community bank president in a small town about 90 miles from Houston took exception. I should have distinguished between big banks and smaller ones. I drove up to meet him and wound up with a column about how the Internet was extending the reach of small-town banks.
10. **Answer every reader e-mail:** Return every phone call. It can be time-consuming, but it's important to do this as much as you possibly can. It builds reader rapport, and it develops sources and column ideas. I love to get emails where people suggest topics or say, "Why haven't you written about this." Turn the complainers into sources: "Tell me about that." It may be the easiest way to humanize your writing with people that you might never find otherwise.
11. **A column is a precious thing:** Don't waste it. You've been given prime real estate. Don't resort to "mailbag" reviews, notebook dumps or grab bags of innocuous news items separated by rows of asterisks. A column isn't about filling space, it's about telling great stories in a unique manner. Your readers deserve your best effort.
12. **For crying out loud, have fun:** Being a business columnist is one of the greatest jobs in the world. You get to write about the thing that makes the world go 'round, and you get to do it in your own voice. Few things affect people more profoundly than money. I've heard column writing described as a treadmill, but don't let it become that routine. In five years, I've never run out of things to write about, and I've never gotten bored.

## 5

人们的钱就是新闻

<!--en-->
People's Money is News

## 定义优质的个人理财报道

<!--en-->
*Defining Good Personal Finance Coverage*

每个人都关心自己的收入，但几乎没有消费者——包括商业记者在内——会在花钱或投资时仔细留意资金去了哪里。随着近年来的经济动荡，我们许多人的可支配资金都比过去少了，当我们最终坐下来查看支票簿，发现自己在下班回家途中多次光顾塔可钟，或在周五晚上请大家喝酒时，就会深刻意识到这一点。

<!--en-->
Everybody cares about the money they make, but not nearly enough consumers—and that includes business reporters—pay close attention to where the money goes when they spend or invest it. And with the economic upheaval of the past few years meaning that many of us have less money than we did in the past, it's a hard lesson when we finally sit down with our checkbooks to see how many times we've stopped at Taco Bell on the way home from work or bought a round for everyone on Friday night.

这时候就需要个人理财记者登场了。个人理财报道属于商业新闻领域的一个分支，旨在为读者和观众提供有关投资、退休、储蓄及其他金钱相关问题的建议。《金钱》和《价值》等杂志以及WalletPop等网站则专门从事个人理财报道。

<!--en-->
That's where the personal finance reporter comes in. Personal finance coverage is the segment of business journalism that aims to provide advice to readers and viewers on matters related to investing, retirement, savings, and other money-related issues. Magazines such as *Money* and *Worth* and websites such as WalletPop focus exclusively on personal finance coverage.

个人理财一直是商业新闻领域中发展迅速的板块，但也是最难撰写的领域之一。我们是记者，而非受过专业培训、了解各类人寿保险政策差异的财务顾问，谁会愿意去撰写如此复杂的主题呢？

<!--en-->
Personal finance has been a growth area in business journalism, but it's also one of the most difficult areas to write about. We're journalists, not financial advisers with training on the differences between types of life insurance policies, and who wants to write about such complicated topics in the first place?

这个问题的答案很简单。我们或许并不想撰写这类主题的文章，但商业新闻的读者却越来越需要这些信息——从如何平衡支票账户到401(k)账户中的合理投资组合规划，各种内容他们都希望得到更多。

<!--en-->
There's an easy answer to that question. We may not yearn to write about these topics, but business news consumers want this information—everything from how to balance a checkbook to the right diversification plan in a 401(k) account—in increasing doses.

对许多美国人来说，20世纪80年代和90年代那种无忧无虑的消费方式已经消失了。随着2008年股市暴跌、市场上金融产品日益复杂，以及人们对退休时社会保障体系是否依然存在的疑虑，越来越多的消费者开始亲自处理自己的财务事务。

<!--en-->
For many Americans, the carefree spending ways of the 1980s and 1990s have disappeared. With the stock market drop in 2008, more complicated financial products on the market, and doubts that the Social Security system will be around when we get ready to retire, more consumers are taking their financial matters into their own hands.

这既有好处也有坏处，尤其是对记者的就业而言。许多美国人没有足够的财力聘请财务规划师来帮助他们理清各类产品与选项带来的困惑。

<!--en-->
That's good—and bad, especially for the employment of journalists. Many Americans don't have the financial wherewithal to hire a financial planner to help them sort through the maze of products and options that are offered in certain
Tips from the Pros

《底特律自由报》专栏作家*Susan Tompor*谈个人财经报道：

<!--en-->
Detroit Free Press columnist *Susan Tompor* on covering personal finance:

**想想钱——实实在在的现金、透支的信用卡、普通的纸质支票：**我们都在以各种方式把钱花在房子、汽车、孩子、宠物、爱好上，而在花钱的同时，仍在努力想办法节省更多资金。所以当听到编辑们——我也遇到过——说个人财经是个无聊的话题时，我真不明白他们在想什么。人们同样会关注自己的金钱，就像他们关注自己的运动队或名人一样。如果你最终要写关于个人财经的内容，那就多想想钱，追踪人们的消费与储蓄方式，这样你就不会感到无聊了。88 • 人民的钱就是新闻

<!--en-->
**Think money—cold hard cash, overstretched plastic, plain-vanilla paper checks:** We're all spending it one way or another on our homes, our cars, our children, our pets, our hobbies and, as we're doing all that spending, we're still struggling with trying to figure out how to save more money, too. So when I hear editors—and I have—suggest personal finance is a dull topic, well, I wonder what in the world they are thinking. People are engaged with their money—just as they're engaged with their sports teams or their celebrities. If you end up writing about personal finance, think money, follow how people spend it and save it and you won't be bored.
88 • People's Money is News

### 专家建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《底特律自由报》专栏作家*Susan Tompor*谈个人财经报道：

<!--en-->
Detroit Free Press columnist *Susan Tompor* on covering personal finance:

**无聊并不总是坏事：**多写一些关于如何平衡支票账户，或者如何在加入401(k)计划时采用定投策略的内容并无坏处。也可以解释为什么投资时需要多元化配置，或是为何读者不应将50%甚至更多的退休资金投入某一只股票，包括所在公司的股票。美国储蓄债券听起来可能是最无趣的投资产品之一，但仍有数百万人持有它们并持续购买。储蓄债券有一长串不断变化的规则，而读者往往能从了解这些规则中找到很大价值。确实有一个政府网站www.treasurydirect.gov,介绍储蓄债券，但该网站既不易阅读也不容易理解。网络上很多其他网站和法规也是如此。

<!--en-->
**Boring isn't always bad:** It never hurts to write more about how to balance a check book or how to dollar cost average when signing up for a 401(k) plan. Or why it's necessary to diversify when investing. Or why readers do not want to put 50 percent or more of their retirement money in one stock, including stock in the company where they work. U.S. savings bonds sound like one of the dullest deals out there. However, millions of people own those bonds—they're still buying them. Savings bonds have a long list of ever-changing rules—and readers often find great value in reading about those rules. Yes, there is a government website, www.treasurydirect.gov, for savings bonds. But the website is not easy to read or really easy to understand. That's true with many websites or regulations that you can easily find on the Web.

#### 专家建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《底特律自由报》专栏作家*Susan Tompor*谈个人财经报道：

<!--en-->
Detroit Free Press columnist *Susan Tompor* on covering personal finance:

**不要在文章或专栏中堆砌大量数字：**数字或许看起来很令人印象深刻，但它们究竟意味着什么？相关问题的变化百分比或趋势是什么？这条趋势线继续下去的可能性有多大？关键是要超越单纯的数字堆砌。你需要阅读年度报告中的脚注，同时也要明白其中的警示信号。如果一篇文章里有太多数字，就删掉一些。同时也要问问自己：我真的理解我所写的内容吗？还是只是在用数字作为掩护？个人财经策略包括但不限于充分利用雇主的福利选项、规划退休生活、自律地使用信贷、挑选合适的抵押贷款买房、寻找优秀的股票经纪人，以及为未来的父母照料问题做准备。

<!--en-->
**Do not load up a story or column with a bunch of numbers:** Numbers might sound impressive, but what do they really mean? What's the percentage change or the trend with that issue? What's the likelihood that the trend line will continue? The idea is to go beyond a bunch of numbers. You need to read footnotes in annual reports. But you need to understand what the warnings signal. If you have too many numbers in a piece, take some out. But also ask yourself, do I really understand what I'm writing about? Or am I trying to hide behind the numbers?
personal finance strategies. These include but are not limited to getting the most out of an employer's benefit options, planning for retirement, using credit with discipline, picking out a mortgage to buy a home, finding a good stockbroker, and preparing for who's going to care for their parents.

商业新闻中的个人财经报道能在这些情况下提供帮助。如果个人财经记者能够向普通读者解释这些有时较为复杂的主题，并给出明智的建议，那他们就完成了工作。《纽约时报》负责个人财经报道的Ron Lieber表示：“我试图吸引那些通常不会看个人财经专栏的读者。这意味着要用通俗易懂的英语写作，像平时说话一样表达，避免使用行话，偶尔尝试幽默或小技巧，讲故事——而不是居高临下地下命令——并将个人财经的定义从单纯的投资扩展到那些会影响你钱包但可能没想到会在个人财经专栏中看到的话题。”

<!--en-->
Personal finance coverage in business journalism can help in these situations. Personal finance reporters have done their job if they can explain these sometimes complicated topics to the average reader and offer prudent advice. Ron Lieber, who covers personal finance for the *New York Times*, says: "I'm trying to get people reading who wouldn't normally look at a personal finance column. That means using plain English, writing like I talk, avoiding jargon, trying to be funny or deploying mild stunts on occasion, telling stories—instead of giving orders from on high—and redefining personal finance way beyond just investing to topics that hit you in the wallet but you might not expect to be reading about in a personal finance column."

正如Lieber所说，个人财经报道的诀窍在于讲述方式。过去二十五年中最出色的个人财经作家Jane Bryant Quinn表示，她在措辞上会反复斟酌。“我会把一句话拿开，问自己它是否清晰明了，”她这样描述自己的写作风格。“在看到成品之前，背后要付出大量心血。你不会写那些会让读者困惑的细节，但会包含关键的细节，同时提供足够的解释让专家们满意。”

<!--en-->
The trick in personal finance reporting, as Lieber suggests, is in how the story is told. Jane Bryant Quinn, the best personal finance writer of the past quarter century, says that she agonizes over how to word her columns. "I will pull back a sentence and ask myself if it's clear," she says about her writing style. "There's a lot of blood behind the keyboard before you see the finished work. You're not doing all of the details that would confuse the readers, but you're including the salient details. And you're using enough explanation to make the experts happy."

那些擅长写作与讲解的个人理财记者，比如利伯和布莱恩特·奎因，其知名度可能不亚于任何商业新闻记者。曾为《金钱》与《智能金钱》杂志撰稿的珍·查茨基如今会定期出现在《今日秀》节目中，谈论个人理财相关话题。

<!--en-->
Personal finance journalists who are good at writing and explaining, such as Lieber and Bryant Quinn, may be as famous as any business journalist. Jean Chatzky, who used to write for *Money* and *SmartMoney* magazines, now appears regularly on the *Today* show to talk about personal finance issues.

在过去几年中，尤其是2008年经济衰退开始、消费者愈发关注资金支出与储蓄方式之后，个人理财已成为商业新闻领域增长最快的领域之一。福克斯商业网络与CNN都推出了每周一次的个人理财节目。美联社也推出了系列周报及月报形式的个人理财内容，新泽西州纽瓦克的《星纪事报》以及里士满的《里士满时报-快讯》等报纸也增加了个人理财报道。

<!--en-->
Personal finance has been one of the biggest growth areas of business journalism in the last few years, particularly after the recession began in 2008 and consumers became more concerned with how they spent and saved their money. Fox Business Network launched a weekly personal finance show on Saturdays, as did CNN. The Associated Press rolled out a package of weekly and monthly personal finance content, and papers such as *The Star-Ledger* in Newark, N.J., and the *Richmond Times-Dispatch* added personal finance coverage.

伴随这一发展也出现了一些问题。全国各地的报纸都开始刊登由全国性组织“财务规划协会”撰写、却以当地财务规划师名义发表的固定个人理财专栏。（虽然这些专栏的内容尚可，但使用多个作者名义发表相同内容的做法让人对其真实性产生质疑。）此外，许多个人理财出版物与记者也因撰写并发布那些宣称某年度最优秀的10只共同基金或股票的文章而受到批评，而这些投资产品往往表现逊于市场平均水平。

<!--en-->
With that growth have come a few problems. Newspapers across the country have been running canned personal finance columns written by a national organization, the Financial Planning Association, under the bylines of local financial planners. (While the content of the columns was fine, the practice of running the same column using multiple writer names called into question their usage.) And many personal finance publications and writers have been criticized for writing and publishing stories that tout the year's 10 best mutual funds or stocks, which often then underperform the market.

布莱恩特·奎因将此类报道嘲讽为“金融色情内容”。在个人理财领域决定提供何种类型的建议颇具难度，如果信息有误，不仅会损害记者及其所在媒体的声誉。

<!--en-->
Bryant Quinn derides such coverage as "financial pornography." Deciding what type of advice to offer on the personal finance beat can be tricky and can ruin the reputation of a journalist and his or her publication if the information is wrong.

问题在于所采用的新闻报道方式。“服务型”新闻在商业与经济报道中指的是那些能够帮助读者做出资金决策的文章、图表及其他资料。这类报道能为消费者提供建议，若处理得当，既能提升读者量，也能让读者成为更精明的消费者。不过，这种新闻报道并非易事。《人们的钱就是新闻》• 89

<!--en-->
The issue is the type of journalism being practiced. "Service" journalism in business and economics reporting is stories, graphics, charts, and other materials that help readers make decisions with their money. These stories give consumersadvice and, done the right way, can increase readership and make readers smarter consumers. But, such journalism is not easy.
People's Money is News • 89

## 消费者理财与个人理财

<!--en-->
*Consumer vs. Personal Finance*

“服务型”新闻可分为两大基本类别。其一为“消费者报道”，即向读者介绍哪些产品在同类产品中最为可靠、价格最低或最受青睐。最典型的例子是绝不接受广告的《消费者报告》杂志，以及《华尔街日报》的沃尔特·莫斯伯格之类的产品评论员。这些记者与媒体都是该领域的专家，他们的专业素养源于数十年来对同一类产品的持续报道。

<!--en-->
"Service" journalism falls into two basic categories. One is "consumer reporting," which is journalism that tells readers which products are the most reliable, the cheapest, or preferred in comparison to similar products. The best examples are *Consumer Reports* magazine, which accepts no advertising, and product reviewers such as Walter Mossberg of *The Wall Street Journal*. These journalists and publications are experts in their field, with expertise that has been built up from decades of covering the same products.

不过，这种报道方式也存在问题。一个人甚至一家媒体怎么可能成为所有产品的专家呢？2007年1月，《消费者报告》被迫撤回了一篇关于儿童汽车座椅安全性的报道。该杂志的测试是由一家外部研究机构完成的，但后来被美国国家公路交通安全管理局推翻——这些测试本应模拟每小时38英里的碰撞情况，实际上却用于预测每小时70英里碰撞时的状况。

<!--en-->
This type of reporting is not without its problems, though. How can someone, or even a publication, be an expert on every product? In January 2007, *Consumer Reports* was forced to retract a story about the safety of children's car seats. An outside research firm conducted the magazine's testing, which was later refuted by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration. The tests were supposed to emulate a crash at 38 miles per hour but instead were done to predict what would happen during a crash at 70 miles per hour.

此后，《消费者报告》的几乎所有报道都经过了更为严格的审核，其声誉也得以保持。但儿童汽车座椅那篇文章的例子恰恰表明，当记者——尤其是那些无法聘请专业专家进行测试的媒体——试图就哪些产品好坏提供意见时，会存在巨大风险。

<!--en-->
Nearly all *Consumer Reports* stories have been vetted more carefully. The magazine's reputation has remained intact. But the example of the children's car seat article shows the dangers in a journalist—particularly one whose publication can't hire professional experts to conduct tests—attempting to offer advice on what products are good or bad.

本章我们将重点探讨的“服务型”新闻便是“个人理财”新闻。这一商业新闻分支旨在告诉读者如何更明智地花钱，涵盖从住房、信用卡、贷款、投资到选择汽车保险政策等多个方面。

<!--en-->
The type of "service" journalism we're going to focus on in this chapter is "personal finance" journalism. This segment of business journalism tells readers how to spend money more wisely, from homes, to credit cards, to loans, to investing, to picking out an auto insurance policy.

除了帮助个人之外，这类报道有时还会对广大消费者产生广泛影响。1990年，我为《坦帕论坛报》的商业版撰写了一篇报道，内容是关于该州最大的健康保险公司佛罗里达蓝十字蓝盾公司为何拒绝为一位不会说英语、也无法阅读英语、因而无法理解所购保险条款的坦帕本地古巴人提供保险保障。这篇报道刊出后，该公司次日便宣布将着手开发帮助说西班牙语的人购买保险的计划。仅仅一篇报道加上记者向州保险部门打的一些电话，就取得了这样的效果。

<!--en-->
Beyond helping individuals, such stories sometimes have a broad impact on consumers. In 1990, I wrote a story for the business section of the *Tampa Tribune* about how the state's largest health insurer, Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Florida, had denied coverage to a Cuban native living in Tampa because he didn't speak or read English, meaning he couldn't read the company's policies to understand what he had purchased. After the story ran, the company announced the next day that it would begin developing programs to help Spanish speakers purchase policies. All it took was one article and some phone calls by a reporter to the state insurance department.

让这个关于个人财务问题的故事如此具有说服力的原因——即大量消费者无法获得合适的健康保险——在于有真实人物亲身经历了这一问题。佩德罗·瓦尔德斯已经支付了前两个月的健康保险费，但保险公司发现他不懂英语后便退还了这笔钱。所有优秀的个人财务故事都是以一个能体现故事核心观点的人的经历开篇的。

<!--en-->
What made this story so effective in presenting a personal finance problem—a large group of consumers unable to find proper health insurance coverage—was a real person experiencing the problem first-hand. Pedro Valdes had paid the first two months of his health insurance premiums, but then the company refunded the money when it discovered that he couldn't understand English. All good personal finance stories start with a person whose experience illustrates the broad point that the story is making.

一些个人财务领域的撰稿人采用简单的问答形式，邀请读者提出问题，然后他们再进行研究并给出答案。例如，史蒂夫·布奇会在Bankrate.com上回答读者关于债务处理的疑问。最近就有位读者提出了这样的问题：

<!--en-->
Some personal finance writers use the simple Q&A format, asking their readers to send in questions, which they then research and answer. For example, Steve Bucci answers questions on Bankrate.com from readers about dealing with debt. One recently asked:

## 专家的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

美国的个人财务记者们大多错失了绝佳的报道机会。不断增长的拉丁裔人口，尤其是第一代居民，需要不同于其他消费者的个人财务教育。

<!--en-->
Personal finance journalists across the United States, for the most part, are missing great story opportunities. The growing Latino population, particularly of first-generation residents, needs personal finance education that's different from what other consumers require.

来自其他国家的拉丁裔往往不了解美国的个人财务运作方式。他们对银行心存警惕，因为在他们的祖国这些金融机构曾出现过问题。他们认为医疗保健是免费的，因为在家乡就是如此。此外，他们也不明白信用评级在申请贷款和购房时的重要性。

<!--en-->
Latinos who have come from other countries often do not understand how personal finance works in the United States. They're wary of banks because such financial institutions have failed in their homeland. They think that health care is free because that's how it was back home. And they don't understand the importance of a credit rating in terms of qualifying for a loan and buying a home.

美国有4550万西班牙裔，占全国人口的15%，他们是人口增长最快的群体。据估计，到2050年，美国的西班牙裔人数将超过1.3亿，占全国人口的30%。

<!--en-->
There are 45.5 million Hispanics making up 15 percent of the population in the United States, and they're the fastest-growing part of the population. It's estimated that by 2050, there will be more than 130 million Hispanics, or 30 percent of the population, in the United States.

然而，大多数个人财务故事并未聚焦于这一不断增长的群体。而针对拉丁裔的个人财务报道其实有很多素材可写，主要是因为这些消费者需要帮助和建议。

<!--en-->
Yet, for the most part, few personal finance stories target this growing community. And Latino-oriented personal finance coverage is ripe with stories, primarily because these consumers need help and advice.

以下是一些供个人财务记者参考的内容：

<!--en-->
Here are a few for personal finance journalists to consider:

1. 西班牙裔倾向于将资金重新投入到家族企业中，而非股票和债券。可以对比一下拉丁裔家庭通过投资企业所获得的回报，以及美国传统投资方式的回报情况。
2. 根据美国人口普查局基于2003年至2005年三年平均数据的研究，具有西班牙裔血统的人拥有健康保险的可能性最低。这种缺乏保障的情况源于他们对美国医疗保健体系了解不足。90 • 《人民的钱就是新闻》：有没有人会为第二笔抵押贷款申请再融资？我们的原始抵押贷款利率为5.625%，我们对此很满意。四年前，我丈夫去读研究生时，我不得不申请了第二笔抵押贷款，结果只能独自承担所有账单。这第二笔抵押贷款的利率高达12%，我觉得我们根本没得到任何好处。从那以后我们还产生了其他信用卡债务，虽然生活十分拮据，但还是能按时还款。请给予建议。谢谢。卡拉¹ 布奇在回答的开头就明确表达了他对卡拉债务状况的看法。他写道：“最重要的是，停下来，立刻停止，否则你会失明的。你说要停什么？停止给信用卡增加更多债务！如果你每月用信用卡消费后并不全额还款，那就很可能意味着你的生活超出了自己的承受能力。如果不学会量入为出，或者希望是远远低于自己的承受能力，想要实现财务安全是非常困难的。”还有人通过这些个人经历来讲述自己的故事，将个例作为引子，吸引读者进一步了解相关主题。《商业周刊》的克里斯·泰勒在撰写关于如何更换理财规划师的文章时，举了马萨诸塞州韦勒姆市48岁的托马斯·基廷的例子——由于他的个人退休账户价值开始下跌，他逐渐将投资转交给新的规划师。在向读者介绍基廷之后，泰勒直入主题：“由于市场剧烈波动，投资者们比以往任何时候都更愿意寻求第二种财务意见。咨询公司奥利弗·怀曼最近的一项调查发现，打算更换顾问的富裕投资者数量在一年内增长了两倍。而据Spectrem Group的调查，在过去一年的市场动荡中，只有36%的百万富翁认为他们的顾问表现良好。”通过举例说明一个普通人和你我一样的普通人是如何更换理财规划师的，泰勒让这个原本可能极其无聊的故事变得引人入胜。在个人财经类文章中，作者有时也会在故事结尾处回到自己的个人经历，让读者了解消费者所做的决定及其结果。你要如何找到这样的例子纳入文章呢？可以问问那些非记者身份的朋友。如果你正在写关于管理收支的文章，你的朋友是否有这方面的困扰？或者他们是否认识有此类问题的人？有些出版物会要求读者通过电子邮件提供特定故事。报纸、杂志或网站上可以设置一个带有电子邮件地址的邮箱框。俄克拉荷马州《塔尔萨世界报》的记者劳里·温斯洛在她正在撰写的文章中，于报纸及网站上发布了如下征集示例的启事：![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/bc1e2f4ed36aa986069e357f62bc494f.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T071651Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=9178c121a9233382ffede37e2f864eefe45b35cb42001b651ede7bcdb7758b70) 《塔尔萨世界商界版》希望了解人们在当前经济困难时期节省开支、调整预算的创新方法。当然，常见的节俭技巧包括减少外出就餐、夏季调高暖气温度、冬季调低暖气温度，以及使用优惠券。但你又有哪些不寻常、有趣或有趣的策略来让钱花得更久呢？好奇的心总想知道答案。 欢迎读者在8月21日前将他们的储蓄建议寄给我们。我们会刊登并分享部分提交的建议，以及提出这些建议的读者的姓名，以便其他人也能加以利用。² 曾为Marketwatch.com和《波士顿环球报》撰写过关于共同基金文章的Chuck Jaffe，会收集那些因过往报道而联系他的读者的姓名，名单中包含他们的电子邮件地址及其他联系方式。当Jaffe需要为即将发表的文章寻找消费者案例时，他只需向名单中的读者发送邮件，说明写作主题，并请有过相关经历的人回复。正如每周为MSN Money撰写两篇个人理财专栏的文章作者Liz Pulliam Weston所说：“人们如此渴望实用、简单的个人理财建议，以至于他们常常愿意主动提供自己作为信息来源，只为得到一些答案。”优秀的个人理财报道还会运用统计数据来支撑论点。如果您要撰写关于消费者支出的文章，可以查看劳工统计局官网上的数据，该网站地址为http://www.bls.gov/home.htm.。数据能够向读者说明您所写内容的重要性。该网站还提供了按年龄、性别、种族和就业状况划分的居民收入数据。如果在此网站上找不到所需数据，可去其他地方查找。从抵押贷款统计到信用卡欺诈，有大量数据可供用于各类个人理财报道。以下是撰写个人理财报道的一些额外建议：
1. **不要只写关于自己的内容。** 可以利用自身经历来构思故事灵感，但出于多种原因应避免直接描写个人经历。首先，你的经历可能并不代表更广泛受众的实际情况；其次，若透露过多信息，可能会让自己面临诈骗风险；第三，第一人称叙事往往会让读者感觉作者在居高临下地教导那些他试图帮助的人。不过在像 WalletPop 这样较为非正式的平台上，这种写法有时会很有效——比如布鲁斯·沃森就曾撰文讲述他与妻子因餐厅账单过高而惊讶的经历：服务员给他们上的是一瓶价值 315 美元的葡萄酒，而非他们点过的 36 美元的那款，以及他们随后如何与经理交涉。
2. **让专家为你发声。** 在挑选人寿保险产品或为初中生选择大学等具体话题上，专业人士拥有更多相关知识。作为记者，你具备撰写各类主题文章并展现权威性的能力，但你并非所有领域的**专家建议**方面的专家。

Does anybody ever refinance a second mortgage? Our original mortgage is at 5.625 percent and we are fine with it. Four years ago, I took out a second mortgage when my husband went to graduate school, and I was faced with paying all of the bills by myself. The second mortgage is at 12 percent interest, and I feel as if we are not making any gain. We have incurred other credit card debt since then but are able to make payments, although things are very tight. Please offer advice. Thank you.
Carla¹
The beginning of Bucci's answer made it clear what he thought about Carla's debt situation. He wrote, "and most importantly, stop it, stop it, stop it or you'll go blind. Stop what, you say? Stop adding debt to your credit cards! If you are making purchases with credit that are not paid in full each month, it is likely you are living beyond your means. It is very difficult to become financially secure if you don't learn how to live within, or, it is hoped, well below, your means."
Others use these personal examples to help tell their story, presenting an individual's situation as a lead anecdote to help entice the reader into learning more about the topic. Chris Taylor, writing in *BusinessWeek* about how to switch financial planners, used the example of 48-year-old Thomas Keating, of Wareham, Mass., who had been slowly moving his investments to a new planner after his individual retirement account, or IRA, started to lose value. After Taylor introduces Keating to his readers, he then gets to the heart of the matter: "Shaken to the core by a market gone wild and scrutinizing performance and fees like they never had to do in a raging bull market, investors are more open than ever to getting a financial second opinion. A recent survey by consulting firm Oliver Wyman found that the number of affluent investors looking to switch advisers has tripled in one year. According to Spectrem Group, a scant 36 percent of millionaires think their advisers performed well during the market turmoil of the past year or so."
By giving an example of how someone—an average, everyday guy just like you and me—switched financial planners, Taylor hooked readers into a story that otherwise might have been deadly boring. Sometimes in personal finance writing, the writer will also circle back to his personal anecdote near the end of the story, giving his or her readers closure on the decisions the consumer made and the results.
How do you find such examples to include in your stories? Ask your non-journalist friends. If you're writing about balancing checkbooks, do your friends have issues in this area? Or do they know someone who does? Publications will sometimes ask for readers to e-mail them for specific stories. A box with an e-mail address can be placed in the paper or magazine or on a website.
Laurie Winslow, a reporter for the *Tulsa World* in Oklahoma, wrote the following solicitation for examples, which appeared in her newspaper and on its website, for a story she was working on:

The *Tulsa World Business* section wants to hear about the inventive ways people are cutting costs and adjusting budgets during these economically hard times. Of course, there are the common saving techniques—dining out less, setting the thermostat higher in the summer and lower in the winter, or using coupons. But what unusual, interesting or fun strategies are you using to make those dollars stretch further? Inquiring minds want to know. Readers are invited to send us their savings suggestions by Aug. 21. We'll publish and share some of the submitted ideas, along with the names of those who sent them, so that others can put the tips to use.²
Chuck Jaffe, who has written about mutual funds for Marketwatch.com and the *Boston Globe*, collects names of readers who have contacted him about past stories. The list contains their e-mail addresses and other contact information. When Jaffe needs a consumer example for an upcoming article, he simply sends out an e-mail to his list explaining what he's writing about and asking those who have experienced the topic to reply back. As Liz Pulliam Weston, who writes a personal finance column for MSN Money twice a week, states, "People are so hungry for solid, uncomplicated personal finance advice that they're often willing to offer themselves as sources just so they can get some answers."
Good personal finance stories also use statistics to back up the thesis of a story. If you're writing about consumer spending, look for numbers on the Bureau of Labor Statistics home page, which can be found at http://www.bls.gov/home.htm. Numbers can tell your readers about the significance of what you're writing. The website also has data on how much people earn depending on age, sex, ethnicity, and employment. If you can't find the data that you're looking for on this site, look somewhere else. There's plenty of data available to fit any personal finance story, from mortgage statistics to credit card fraud.
Here are some other tips when reporting and writing personal finance stories:
1. **Don't write about yourself.** Use yourself and your personal experiences to come up with story ideas, but avoid writing about personal experiences for a number of reasons. First, your experience may not be typical of what a broader audience is experiencing. Second, if you divulge too much information, you may open yourself up to fraud. And third, first-person stories often come across as the writer talking down to the consumers that he or she is trying to help. It may sometimes work in a less formal format, such as WalletPop, where Bruce Watson wrote about the time he and his wife were surprised by a large restaurant bill—the waiter had given them a $315 bottle of wine, not the $36 bottle they had ordered—and how they tried to negotiate with the manager.
2. **Let the experts do the talking for you.** It's the professionals who know more about the specific topic, whether it's picking life insurance policies or picking colleges for junior. As a journalist, you have the ability to write about a number of topics and to do it with authority. But you're not an expert on all of
**Tips from the Pros**

《底特律自由报》专栏作家苏珊·汤姆波尔关于报道个人财经内容的观点：

<!--en-->
Detroit Free Press columnist *Susan Tompor* on covering personal finance:

**多样化选题：** 大学生是如何节省资金购买教科书的？青少年在商场里如何省钱？退休人员如何应对反向抵押贷款？如果预算紧张，人们为何还要使用发薪日贷款？替代性最低税对家庭有何影响？不要因为某个问题只影响小部分群体（如高收入读者）就拒绝报道它。应为不同收入阶层的读者提供多样化的财经报道内容，增强报道的经济多样性。不同的人在理财方面会面临各种不同的挑战，因此你需要面向更广泛的群体进行报道，同时也要保持趣味性。如果各家珠宝店都夸耀愿意出高价收购黄金，不妨去多家店铺看看，考虑是否出售自己的结婚戒指。[^1100]：² 摘自 L. 温斯洛所写的《商业版块征集您的省钱妙招：我们将在几周后刊登》，载于 2009 年 8 月 15 日的《塔尔萨世界报》，E2. 92 页。• 金钱即新闻。

<!--en-->
**Mix it up:** How are college students saving money buying textbooks? How are teens saving money at the mall? How are retirees dealing with reverse mortgages? Why are people using payday loans if they're on tight budgets? How is the alternative minimum tax hitting households? Do not say that you won't cover an issue because it only affects a small group, such as higher-income readers. Give some variety to your finance coverage to cover different income groups. Offer some economic diversity in your coverage. Different people face all sorts of different challenges with their money. So you need to talk to broad groups of people. But you also need to have fun. Don't be afraid to go to a bunch of jewelry stores to price selling your wedding ring if stores are bragging about paying top dollar for gold.

### 专家建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《底特律自由报》专栏作家苏珊·汤姆波尔关于报道个人财经内容的观点：

<!--en-->
Detroit Free Press columnist Susan Tompor on covering personal finance:

**建立信息来源网络：** 如果有经济学家来到当地，不妨坐下来聊聊；如果经纪人邀请你参加面向客户的晚间讲座，也别犹豫，抽时间去参加。你没有义务一定要写文章，但可以通过这些活动积累灵感或拓展信息来源网络。注意观察参加此类活动的人以及他们提出的问题。联邦储备银行在一些大城市会举办各种“财务智慧周”活动，这些都是获取灵感的良好渠道。同时也要结识为投资者服务的律师、州级监管机构人员、商业改进局的工作人员，以及你所在地区的银行家和经纪人。

<!--en-->
**Build a network of sources:** If economists come to town, be willing to sit down and chat. If brokers invite you to an evening presentation for clients, do not be afraid to take the time to attend. You're not obligated to write a story, but you may build a base of ideas or a better network of sources. Pay attention to who attends such events and the questions people are asking. The Federal Reserve banks have various "Money Smart Weeks" in some major cities and can be a good source for ideas. Get to know attorneys who represent investors; the state regulators; folks at the Better Business Bureau; your town's bankers and brokers.

#### 专家建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《底特律自由报》专栏作家苏珊·汤姆波尔关于报道个人财经内容的观点：

<!--en-->
Detroit Free Press columnist Susan Tompor on covering personal finance:

**不要被那些看似不合理的事物吓倒：** 为什么不用任何首付就买房？或者永远不偿还抵押贷款？如果某件事不合常理，就大胆挑战传统观念或提出不同的看法。仅仅引用“专家”的话，就好像他们在提供稳赚不赔的理财方法，这是不够的。2008-09 年的市场危机已经证明了传统观念的局限性。从事房地产投资并不总能盈利，股市也常常会出现长期下跌或停滞不前的情况。即使很多人从二十多岁就开始储蓄，要积累百万美元的退休基金也绝非易事。单纯重复别人的推销话术对读者或观众没有任何帮助。请记住，金融产品终究只是产品而已——有的有效，有的无效。在这些领域，很少有人能做到完美。找到该领域的专家，让他们成为向读者或观众传递信息的代言人，这样的专家也能给个人财经消费者带来更多安心感。

<!--en-->
**Don't be intimidated by things that don't seem to make sense:** Why would it make sense to buy a house with nothing down? Or never pay down your mortgage? If something doesn't make sense, don't be afraid to challenge conventional wisdom or offer another viewpoint. It's not good enough to quote the "experts" as if they're offering a sure-fire approach for making money. Conventional wisdom was tested in the market meltdown in 2008-09. You do not always make money on real estate. The stock market can have long stretches when it goes down or goes nowhere. Most people won't have an easy time building a million-dollar nest egg for retirement even if they start saving in their 20s. It does not serve readers or viewers to merely repeat someone's sales pitch. And remember financial products are just that: products. Some work; some don't.
these areas. Very few of us can be. Find the experts in the field and let them be the voice that speaks to the reader or the viewer. These experts will be more comforting to the personal finance consumer as well.

3. **不要只依赖一位专家。** 对于某个话题，务必从不同角度采访多位专家。他们可能会向消费者推荐对自己有利的内容。例如，保险代理人可能会推荐能让他获得最高佣金的保险产品，而按固定费用收费的个人理财规划师则可能会推荐更适合该人财务状况的其他产品。即便你信任消息来源，也应当注明其中的注意事项。他推荐的股票是他自己持有的吗？她在市场高点时给出过糟糕的建议吗？只要相关错误得到承认，错误的预测和其他诚实的失误并不会使该消息来源失去可信度。
4. **为读者提供从文章中能获得的收获。**这可以是某个主题的优缺点。例如，如果你正在撰写关于通过401(k)计划为退休储蓄的最佳方式，可以探讨股票与债券的利弊。理想情况下，这些内容应该是读者或观众可以剪下保存或从你的网站上打印出来的内容。
5. **不要让文章显得像是记者在直接给出建议。**我们并非财务规划师，而是引用那些提供建议的专家的观点。务必让文章清晰地表明建议的来源。太多个人理财类文章给人的感觉是作者自以为无所不知，却在不了解消费者具体情况的情况下向读者或观众提出建议。
6. **不要暗示消费者会获得特定结果。**那些告诉读者只要按照作者的建议投资就能跑赢市场的文章或标题，是个人理财写作中最严重的问题之一。如果这些建议出错会怎样？消费者很可能会远离你的媒体平台。
7. **使用图表和图形。**由于个人理财较为复杂，往往通过图形能更好地解释相关概念。图表也是展示个人理财策略重要性的好方法，比如尽早开始储蓄。此外，图表还可以为读者提供行动清单。在撰写关于购买新房的文章时，可以制作一份购房者在签约前应做的十件事的清单。图表在投资类文章中也很有用，其中可以列出专家推荐的共同基金、股票和债券的名称。
8. **绝不要使用绝对化的表述。**在经济学和金融学领域，没有任何观点是在特定情况下不能被同样有权威性和真实性的论据所反驳的。这一点在撰写有关市场与税收的内容时尤为明显。应使用“通常”或“一般而言”之类的措辞。例如：商业记者通常会将利率下降的趋势视为利好消息。的确，当市场利率下降时，企业债券等固定收益证券的价值*通常*会上升（除非该公司在利率下降的同一天突然宣布破产）。但对于依靠利息收入生活的退休者来说，较低的利率却是坏消息。另一方面，现在人们也承认，2008年开始的经济衰退部分是由低利率引发的，这种低利率催生了房地产及其他资产领域的投机泡沫。如果你不对关于经济和金融的表述加以谨慎处理，读者肯定会找尽借口批评你。《People's Money is News》• 93 像许多商业报道领域一样，要达到读者和观众所期望的水平，个人理财报道也需要特定的专业知识。但这也是最具成就感的写作类型之一，因为你的文章比出版物或网站上的其他内容更能直接影响你的受众。只需要对这个领域感兴趣即可。尽可能多地阅读关于个人理财的书籍。记者不可能成为所有领域的专家，但他们至少需要具备足够的知识，以便察觉到可疑之处或不合逻辑的解释。2002年，《华尔街日报》旗下的《Personal Journal》创刊时，罗恩·利伯被聘为撰稿人，而他当时在个人理财方面经验很少。在此之前，他曾供职于《财富》和《快公司》杂志。“我加入时对很多东西都充满热情，比如飞行里程积分，”利伯说道，“从那以后，我就顺理成章地开始撰写关于信用卡行业的文章，接着又涉足员工福利、银行业务以及其他与钱包相关的领域。”通过最后这句话，利伯总结了所有个人理财文章应该关注的重点：那些会影响你钱包的内容。

<!--en-->
3. **Don't rely on just one expert.** Make sure you interview a variety of experts on a topic from different angles. They may be telling consumers to do something that would enrich themselves. For example, an insurance agent could recommend a policy from which he or she receives the largest commission payment, but a fee-for-service personal finance planner, who is paid a flat rate, might recommend another policy that is more suited to the person's financial situation. Even if you trust your source, report the caveats. Does he own the stock he's recommending? Did she give bum advice at the market's peak? Incorrect forecasts and other honest mistakes should not disqualify your source as long as they are acknowledged.
4. **Give the reader something to take away from the story.** This can be the pros and cons of a topic. For example, if you're writing about the best way for a person to save for retirement via a 401(k) plan, you could write about the pros and cons of stocks vs. bonds. Ideally, this could be something that the reader or viewer might cut out and save or print off your website.
5. **Don't let the article seem as if the journalist is giving the advice.** We're not financial planners. We quote the experts who give the advice. Make sure the story is clear about where the advice is coming from. Too many personal finance stories appear as if it's the writer who knows everything and is making a recommendation to the reader or viewer without really knowing the consumer's specific situation.
6. **Don't imply that the consumer will have certain results.** Articles or headlines that appear to tell readers that they will be able to beat the market if they invest the way the author suggests are one of the biggest problems in personal finance writing. What happens when that advice is wrong? The consumer will likely turn away from your media outlet.
7. **Use charts and graphics.** Because personal finance is complicated, concepts can often be better explained using graphics. Graphs and charts are also a good way to show the significance of personal finance strategies, such as beginning to save at an early age. Charts can also be used to give readers a checklist of what they need to do. Writing about buying a new home? Make a chart of the ten things the buyer should do before signing the contract. Charts are also good for investment stories. They can include names of mutual funds, stocks, and bonds that your experts recommend.
8. **Never, never be absolute.** There are no statements made in the fields of economics and finance that cannot be contradicted with equal authority and truthfulness, given the right circumstances. This is especially true when writing about markets and taxes. Use words like "typically" or "usually." One example: Business journalists usually report a trend toward lower interest rates as good news. It's true that the value of fixed income securities, such as corporate bonds, *usually* increase when interest rates decline in the market (unless, for example, the corporation unexpectedly declares bankruptcy on the same day that market rates decline). But for the retiree living on interest income, lower interest rates are terrible news. On another plane, it's now conceded that the recession that began in 2008 was caused, in part, by low interest rates that prompted speculativebubbles in housing and other assets. If you don't hedge your statements about economics and finance, readers will love to nit-pick you to death.
People's Money is News • 93
Like many business beats, personal finance reporting requires specific knowledge to perform at the level that readers and viewers expect. But it can be one of the most rewarding types of writing, as your stories have a more direct impact on your consumers than does anything else in your publication or on your website. All it takes is an interest in the field. Read as many books about personal finance as you possibly can. Journalists can't be experts in everything, but they do need to know enough to smell a rat or a fishy explanation.
Ron Lieber was a business journalist with little experience in personal finance when he was hired to be part of the launch of the Personal Journal, part of *The Wall Street Journal*, in 2002. He had spent time at *Fortune* and *Fast Company* before that. “I arrived with a passion for, among other things, frequent flier miles,” said Lieber. “From there, it was a half step to writing about the credit card industry. I just sort of took it from there, wandering into employee benefits and banking and other areas that hit you in the wallet.”
With that last sentence, Lieber sums up what all personal finance stories should focus on: What hits you in the wallet.

## 个人理财主题

<!--en-->
*Personal Finance Topics*

既然我们已经讨论了个人理财报道的重要性及其背后的策略，接下来就来看看商业记者应当了解的一些不同报道领域和议题。虽然个人理财通常聚焦于投资，但实际上还有很多其他领域也能提供有价值的信息。

<!--en-->
Now that we've discussed the importance of and the strategies behind personal finance reporting, let's take a look at some of the different coverage areas and issues that a business journalist should know. While personal finance often focuses on investing, there are many other areas where stories can provide great information.

为《洛杉矶时报联合版》撰写个人理财专栏、其文章在全国多家报纸上发表的凯西·克里斯托夫表示，如今面临的挑战是如何决定写什么内容。“任何会影响你钱包的事情，从购物到工作再到投资，都属于报道范围，”克里斯托夫说，“所以最大的挑战就是要么专注于少数几个你能深入研究并成为真正专家的主题，要么找到一种方法，让自己成为多面手的同时依然保持专业水平。”

<!--en-->
Kathy Kristof, who writes a personal finance column for the *Los Angeles Times Syndicate* that runs in papers across the country, says that the issue today is deciding what to write about. “Anything that hits your pocketbook, from grocery shopping to working and investing, fits,” said Kristof. “So the big challenge is to either zero in on a handful of topics that you can learn well enough to become a true expert—or find a way to be a jack-of-all-trades, and still be an expert.”

显然，即便是最资深的个人理财记者也难以在所有领域都具备专业知识。为阐明这一点，这里有一份关于基础个人理财知识的测试，它能帮助你了解自己在报道个人理财方面的优势与不足。

<!--en-->
It's obviously difficult for even the most advanced personal finance reporter to be knowledgeable in every field. And to make that point clear, here's a test of basic personal finance knowledge. This should help you assess your strengths and weaknesses in covering personal finance.

把答案写在纸上，看看自己的表现如何。

<!--en-->
Write your answers on a piece of paper and see how you do.

1. 投资者可以通过哪三种方式来比较某只股票与另一只股票？
2. 共同基金和对冲基金之间有哪三个区别？
3. 投资股票与投资债券的主要区别是什么？
4. 消费者购房时可使用的两种基本抵押贷款类型是什么？
5. 房主通常为何要重新办理房屋抵押贷款？

<!--en-->
1. What are three ways in which investors can assess a stock relative to another stock?
2. What are three differences between mutual funds and hedge funds?
3. What is the main difference between investing in stocks and investing in bonds?
4. What are the two basic types of mortgages that a consumer can use to buy a home?
5. Why does a homeowner typically refinance his or her home mortgage?

### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《底特律自由报》*专栏作家苏珊·汤姆波尔谈个人理财报道：*

<!--en-->
Detroit Free Press *columnist Susan Tompor on covering personal finance:*

**尊重金钱——也尊重你的读者：**你无需卷入那些追求快速赚钱的炒作之中。生活并非只有发财这一条路，也不应用那些快速致富的故事浪费别人的时间。那些疯狂的财富往往只是昙花一现、极易消失的财富。我认为那些关于炒房、购买科技股之类的策略都属于此类。避免参与助长下一轮狂热。而且总会有另一轮金钱狂热出现。另外，在买卖股票时也要谨慎。如果你是负责报道银行业的记者，就不应持有所在地区银行的个股。请查阅你所在媒体的道德准则；如果媒体没有这类标准，那就去研究其他知名机构的道德规范，尽量遵循最高的标准。

<!--en-->
**Respect money—and your readers:** You do not need to get into the hype associated with making a fast buck. Life is not all about getting rich and you should not waste someone's time with fast-money stories. Crazy wealth is often just that—crazy wealth that can easily disappear. I'd put strategies for flipping houses, buying tech stocks and the rest in that category. Avoid taking part in fueling the next mania. And there is always another money mania. Also be careful about what stocks you're buying or selling. You do not want to own individual bank stocks in your community if you're the banking writer. Check into the ethical guidelines at your media outlet. Or if your outlet does not have such standards, do some research on other ethical standards at established organizations. Try to adopt the highest standard possible.

### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《底特律自由报》*专栏作家苏珊·汤姆波尔谈个人理财报道：*

**如果条件允许，去参加一些金融会议：**美国商业编辑与作家协会的会议经常会设置关于最新话题的分组讨论环节，或邀请重要演讲者出席。总部位于芝加哥的晨星公司也会在芝加哥举办年度会议，吸引金融规划师以及知名共同基金的资金管理人参加。一些金融规划师团体还会在本地社区举办活动，为会员提供持续教育。在金融相关事务上，不必害怕挑战自己。94 • 《人民的钱就是新闻》

<!--en-->
**If you can, attend some financial conferences:** The Society of American Business Editors and Writers conferences often have break-out sessions on up-to-date topics or offer key speakers. Chicago-based Morningstar has an annual conference in the Windy City that attracts financial planners and big money managers at top-name mutual funds. Some financial planner groups also have sessions in local communities to provide continuing education for members. Do not be afraid to get in over your head when it comes to finances.

#### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《底特律自由报》专栏作家苏珊·汤姆波尔谈个人理财报道：

<!--en-->
Detroit Free Press columnist Susan Tompor on covering personal finance:

别忘了税收问题：税收规则会定期变动。人们确实需要关于新税收政策或旧税收规则的清晰、易读的报道。了解一下你所在社区中为低收入家庭提供税务服务的志愿者组织，看看能否与美国国税局合作，在网上公布尚未领取的退税信息。如果能开发一个网页工具，列出那些尚未领取退税的人的名字，那将是一项非常实用的服务。也别忘了州所得税以及与之相关的各种规定。

Do not forget taxes: The tax rules change regularly. People really need clear, easy-to-read stories on new tax changes or old tax rules. See if you can work with the Internal Revenue Service to run uncollected tax refund information on the Web. It's a great service to be able to run a gadget on the Web that lists the names of people who have uncollected tax returns. Do not forget about state income taxes—and the assorted rules associated with those returns.

1. Price-to-earnings multiple, price-to-book multiple, and the net profit margin.
2. Mutual funds may advertise, while hedge funds may not. Hedge funds "short" stocks, while most mutual funds do not. (To "short" a stock means to borrow the stock, sell it, and hope the price declines before the borrowed stock must be repaid.) Hedge fund managers typically collect a percentage of the profits of their investments as a performance fee in addition to a management fee. Most mutual fund managers do not collect a separate performance fee.

### 投资与市场

<!--en-->
*Investing and the Markets*

个人财经新闻行业的兴起始于银行储蓄账户利率管制的放宽。当时通货膨胀率居高不下，普通民众急于了解如何获得最高的利率以及利率走势。通胀得到控制后，20世纪80年代和90年代股市的繁荣吸引了数百万美国普通人进入股市。与此同时，雇主们开始取消传统的养老金计划，即由雇主代为投资并从养老基金中支付退休金；取而代之的是为员工提供诸如401(k)账户之类的税收优惠型退休储蓄账户，由员工而非其雇主来决定投资方向。这样，普通人也“获得了”为自己退休储蓄的能力，尽管很少有人懂得相关技巧。回顾个人财经媒体的发展史，很多都是在这个时期成立的。CNBC成立于1989年，《聪明钱》杂志则于1992年开始出版。Marketwatch.com成立于1994年，TheStreet.com则在两年后上线。

<!--en-->
The rise of personal finance journalism began with the deregulation of interest rates that banks could pay on savings accounts. With inflation running high at that time, ordinary individuals were eager to learn how to capture the highest available rates and assess the outlook for interest rates. After inflation was tamed, a boom in the stock market in the 1980s and 1990s drew millions of ordinary Americans into the stock market. At that same time, employers began dropping traditional pension programs, in which they invested on behalf of employees and paid retirement income from the pension fund. Instead, employees were offered tax-advantaged retirement savings accounts, such as the 401(k) account, for which employees—not their bosses—made investment decisions. Ordinary people thereby were “empowered” to save for their own retirement, although few knew the ropes. If you look back at the personal finance media, many got their start during this time period. CNBC started in 1989, and *Smart Money* began publishing in 1992. Marketwatch.com got its start in 1994, and TheStreet.com launched two years later.

在整个20世纪，个人投资者的数量急剧增加。到1999年，超过一半的美国家庭在市场中有某种形式的投资。这些投资者会通过商业和财经媒体获取有关投资的信息，以及寻找优质投资机会的线索。

<!--en-->
Throughout the twentieth century, the number of individual investors increased dramatically. By 1999, more than half of all U.S. households had some sort of investment in the markets. These investors turn to the business and financial press for knowledge about their investments and for clues about where good investments might exist.

每天市场中都有数万亿美元的各种投资产品进行交易——包括股票、债券、大宗商品和货币。以普通人能够理解的方式撰写关于这些投资的文章并非易事。个人财经新闻的读者希望知道某项投资是否便宜或昂贵，以及该采取什么措施来提升自己投资组合的表现。

<!--en-->
Trillions of dollars in investments are traded each day in the markets—stock, bonds, commodities, and currencies. Knowing how to write about these investments in a way that the average person can understand is not an easy task. Consumers of personal finance news want to know whether investments are cheap or expensive and where they can take action to improve the performance of their portfolio.

许多个人理财杂志、新闻简报、电视节目、网站和博客都是通过采访专业的资金管理人来实现这一目的的，这些管理人会向记者阐述他们认为值得投资或不应投资的股票。某位资金管理人可能认为银行类股票目前价格较低，因而建议投资者将其纳入投资组合；他们也可能会认为零售业股票的估值过高，应当卖出。此时，阅读相关报道的读者或观众就需要决定是否足够信任这位资金管理人，从而采纳其建议。

<!--en-->
Many personal finance magazines, newsletters, television shows, websites, and blogs accomplish this through interviews with professional money managers who give the journalist their opinions about stocks they like and don't like. A money manager may think that bank stocks are currently cheap and may recommend that investors purchase these for their portfolio. They may also think that stocks of retailers have gotten too expensive and should be sold. Readers or watchers of this story then have to decide if they trust this money manager enough to take his or her recommendations.

个人理财记者在采访过程中应不断质疑该资金管理人的论据。如果某些股票价格低，原因何在？资金管理人应该能够以这些股票的市盈率或市净率低于整体市场水平作为依据来支撑自己的观点。这两种比率都是将当前股价与一个固定数值——即公司的每股收益或每股账面价值——进行比较。例如，如果A公司的股票每股交易价格为30美元，而该公司最近四个季度的每股收益为3美元，那么它的市盈率为10倍。个人理财记者可以将这一数值与整体市场的指数（如标准普尔500指数，其市盈率可能为18倍）或其他处于同一行业的公司（其整体市盈率为15倍）进行对比，以此向读者表明该股票相比其他股票而言价格较低。市盈率也可以根据股票分析师预测的未来收益来计算。

<!--en-->
The personal finance reporter should be questioning the money manager's rationale during the interview. If some stocks are cheap, why? The money managershould be able to back up this assertion by saying that the price-to-earnings ratio or price-to-book ratio of the stocks is low compared to the overall market. Both of these ratios compare the current stock price to a fixed number—the earnings per share of the company, or the company's book value per share.
96 • People's Money is News
For example, if Company A's stock is trading at $30 per share, and the company earned $3.00 per share during its most recent four quarters, it is trading at a P/E ratio of 10. The personal finance reporter can compare this number to an index of the overall market, such as the Standard & Poor's 500 index, which may be trading at 18 times earnings, or to other companies in Company A's industry, which collectively are trading at 15 times earnings, to show the reader that this stock is cheap compared to other stocks. Price-to-earnings ratios also may be calculated based on future earnings, as estimated by stock analysts.

同样的方法也可用于解释为何某只股票可能估值过高。假设某家公司的股票每股交易价格为50美元，而该公司的账面价值——即资产价值除以在外流通股数——为10美元，这意味着该公司的股票交易价格是其账面价值的5倍。但如果整体市场的股票交易价格仅为账面价值的1.8倍，而同行业其他公司的股票交易价格则为账面价值的2.5倍，那么个人理财记者就有充分理由认为该股票价格偏高。

<!--en-->
The same technique can be used to explain how a stock may be too expensive. Let's say that a company's shares are trading at $50 a share, and the company's book value—or the value of its assets divided by the number of outstanding shares—is $10. That means that this company is trading at five times its book value. But if the overall market is trading at 1.8 times book value and other companies in this industry are trading at 2.5 times book value, a personal finance reporter can make a good argument that the stock is expensive.

这些报道技巧同样适用于其他类型的投资。记者可以查看某只共同基金过去一年或五年的表现，并将其与采用类似投资策略的其他共同基金进行对比——比如那些投资小型企业股票或拉丁美洲企业股票的基金。由于对冲基金基本上不受监管，相关的数据与对比信息较难获取。此外，对冲基金要求投资者拥有远超大多数共同基金投资者的财富，因此可能只有少数人对对冲基金感兴趣。

<!--en-->
The same reporting techniques can be used for other investments. A reporter can check out a mutual fund's performance for the last year or the last five years and compare those numbers to other mutual funds using a similar investment strategy—such as buying stocks of small companies or buying stocks of companies based in Latin America. Because hedge funds are largely unregulated, numbers and comparisons are harder to come by. Hedge funds require that their investors have a lot more wealth money than most mutual fund investors hold, so fewer readers may be interested in hedge funds.

与投资相关的个人理财报道还可以探讨不同的投资策略。负责撰写此类报道的记者必须先成为这些投资概念的学习者，最终成为客观的批评者，而非盲目支持者。投资者是否应该考虑在投资组合中加入看跌期权或看涨期权？股票期权赋予投资者在特定时期内以特定价格买入或卖出股票的权利。那么卖空又是什么呢？即投资者在股票价格下跌而非上涨时获利。其运作方式如下：投资者从经纪人处借入股票，然后在公开市场上卖出。如果他们能以更低的价格买回这些股票，就能获得利润。如果某投资者卖空了100万股每股价值10美元的股票，他需要准备1000万美元的资金。如果股价跌至8美元，这些股票的价值就变为800万美元，投资者买回股票后就能盈利200万美元。当然，投资始终存在风险。如果股价涨至12美元，投资者就需要支付1200万美元买回股票，从而损失200万美元。

<!--en-->
Personal finance stories related to investing can also look at different strategies. A reporter covering the personal finance beat must become a student and, ultimately, an objective critic of these concepts but never an advocate. Should an investor consider put or call options as part of his or her portfolio? Stock options convey a right to buy or sell stock at a specific price during a specified period. And what about short selling, which is when an investor makes money when the price of a stock falls instead of rises? Here's how that works: An investor borrows shares of a stock from a broker and then sells them on the open market. They make money if they can buy back the shares at a lower price. If an investor shorts 1 million shares of a $10 stock, they put $10 million in their wallet. If the stock drops to $8, the shares are now worth $8 million. The investor can buy back the shares and profit $2 million. Of course, there's always a risk in investing. If the stock rises to $12 a share, the investor has to pay $12 million to buy back the shares and loses $2 million.

关于投资的个人理财报道还可以探讨其他概念，比如在首次公开募股时或私人公司通过上市出售股票时买入股票。许多投资者主张只购买那些会派发股息的股票，即公司定期向股东支付的现金或股票。投资者可以通过两种方式获利：股息收入以及期望中的股价上涨带来的收益。投资类报道还可以关注投资领域的从业者。例如，可以通过分析分析师的建议，来判断谁能为客户提供更好的投资建议。一些个人理财媒体会将不同分析师的观点进行对比，让一位推荐某只股票，另一位则建议投资者避开它。还有些个人理财刊物则会聚焦于共同基金经理的简介，分析他们的投资策略。

<!--en-->
Personal finance stories about investing can also take a look at other concepts, such as buying stocks at the time of initial public offering or when a private company goes public by selling stock on the market. Many investors advocate buying only stocks that pay dividends, which are cash or shares of stock that companies pay their shareholders on a regular basis. The investor can make money two ways: the dividend payments and, hopefully, gains in the stock price.
People's Money is News • 97
Investment stories can also look at the people in the investing business. The recommendations of analysts, for example, can be examined to see who is providing better advice for their clients. Some personal finance media will match analysts against each other, with one recommending a stock and the other telling investors to avoid it. Other personal finance publications focus on profiles of mutual fund managers that examine their investment strategies.

除了股票之外，还有其他投资品种。个人财经记者可以从多个角度审视债券，包括当发行方的债务评级上升或下降时是否值得购买。虽然大多数消费者对商品市场的了解有限，但他们知道购买一加仑汽油或一壶橙汁——这两种每天都会交易的商品——会对自己的钱包产生何种财务影响。从个人财经的角度撰写关于商品的文章，有助于向读者或观众解释价格为何上涨或下跌，从而帮助他们更明智地规划投资组合和家庭预算。

<!--en-->
Then there are the other investments beside stocks. A personal finance reporter can look at bonds from a number of perspectives, including whether they're a good buy when the issuer's debt rating gets raised or lowered. While most consumers are limited in their knowledge of the commodities market, they know the financial impact on their wallet when they go to purchase a gallon of gas or a jug of orange juice—two products traded every day. Writing about commodities from a personal finance standpoint helps explain to the reader or viewer why prices are rising or falling and can help them make informed decisions with their investment portfolios and with their family budgets.

关于投资的个人财经话题数不胜数，唯一的限制就是想象力。不过在撰写投资相关内容时，请记住：如果鼓吹频繁交易，其实并没有为消费者带来任何好处，因为这只会让从中获取佣金的经纪商受益。最优秀的投资者往往是那些长期持有股票、债券、商品或其他投资品种的人。

<!--en-->
There are countless other personal finance stories to write about investing. The only limit is your imagination. When writing about investing, however, remember this: You're not doing your consumers any favors if you're advocating heavy trading. That only helps the brokers who receive the commissions on such actions. The best investors are the ones who have held their stocks, bonds, commodities, or something else for a long time.

#### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《底特律自由报》专栏作家*Susan Tompor*谈个人财经报道：

<!--en-->
Detroit Free Press columnist *Susan Tompor* on covering personal finance:

**伯尼·马多夫并非唯一的诈骗犯：**了解你所在州的监管机构，以便掌握该州有哪些骗子正在活动。有关各类消费者或投资者警示信息，请参阅www.finra.org或www.sec.gov。注意分类广告或Craigs List上宣传的内容，有些居家工作骗局确实存在。人们不仅需要知道如何保护自己的钱，也需要知道如何赚更多的钱。也可参阅www.ftc.gov。

<!--en-->
**Bernie Madoff isn't the only guy to run a scam:** Get to know your state regulators to discover what con artists are doing in your state. See www.finra.org or www.sec.gov for various consumer or investor alerts. Pay attention to what's being marketed in classified ads or on Craigs list. Some real scams exist when it comes to working-at-home schemes, etc. People need to know how to keep their money—as well as how to make more money. See www.ftc.gov too.

## 福利保障

<!--en-->
*Benefits*

个人财经报道还涵盖福利保障方面，比如健康保险、人寿保险、残疾保险，以及雇主为激励员工留任或入职而提供的其他福利。

<!--en-->
Personal finance coverage also extends into benefits, such as health insurance, life insurance, disability coverage, and other options that employers offer their workers as an incentive to stay with or join the company.

大多数雇主都会为员工提供某种形式的健康保险。关于这类福利的个人财经报道通常会探讨对员工而言最合适的选项。大多数医疗保健计划会在年底附近设置开放注册期，此时消费者可以更改保险选项，调整需支付的费用，通常是通过工资扣款的方式实现。

<!--en-->
Most employers offer some form of health insurance to their workers. Personal finance reporting regarding this benefit typically discusses the most effective option for the employees. Most health care plans have open enrollment periods near the end of the year, when consumers can change their options, raising or lowering the price they're paying, typically through some sort of payroll deduction.

在自主选择型医疗计划中，员工可以自行挑选医生或其他医疗服务提供者。由于选择范围广泛，费用通常较高。而在管理式医疗计划（如健康维护组织或优选医疗服务提供者组织）中，保险公司会为就诊协商固定费用。但对部分消费者来说，缺点是他们必须去计划内的医院就诊，否则就要支付更高费用。

<!--en-->
In an indemnity plan, the employee chooses which doctor or other health care provider they use. Because their options are unlimited, the cost is typically higher. But with a managed care plan, such as a health maintenance organization or a preferred provider organization, the insurer has negotiated a flat rate for visits. The downside for some consumers is that they have to go to the doctors in the plan, or they will pay more.

选择雇主提供的健康保险方案几乎总是一种明智的财务决策，因为它能降低员工的医疗支出。在大多数情况下，员工为雇主赞助的健康保险计划支付的保费是可以抵税的。但许多员工并未意识到，通过选择特定的保险选项，他们实际上可以影响自己需要支付的金额。个人财经记者可以通过讲解这些选项——比如弹性支出账户的利弊，或者消费者是否应该选择牙科护理、眼科护理甚至宠物保险等附加保障——为这类消费者提供有价值的帮助。98 • 《人民金钱即新闻》个人财经记者也经常撰写有关人寿保险的文章。虽然有些雇主会将人寿保险作为福利提供，但许多消费者仍需将其视为整体财务策略的一部分来考虑购买。应向他们解释不同类型保险计划的优缺点及各自相关的费用。在什么情况下，终身人寿保险会比定期人寿保险更具优势？

<!--en-->
Choosing the health insurance option offered by an employer is almost always a financially smart move because it will likely limit the health care expenses that employees have to pay. In most cases, the insurance premiums the employee pays to an employer-sponsored health insurance plan are tax-deductible. But what many employees don't realize is that they can affect the amount they pay by picking certain options. A personal finance reporter can perform a valuable service for such consumers by explaining these options, such as the pros and cons of a flexible spending account or whether the consumer should opt for add-on coverage for items such as dental care, eye care, and even pet insurance.
98 • People's Money is News
Personal finance journalists also frequently write about life insurance. While some employers offer life insurance as a benefit, many consumers need to consider purchasing policies as part of their overall financial strategy. Explain to them the advantages and disadvantages of the different types of policies and the costs associated with each one. When would a whole-life insurance policy be more advantageous than a term-life insurance policy?

在福利保障方面，还有许多其他类型的保险值得报道。残疾保险能在员工受伤无法工作时，帮助他们支付房租、电费等账单。许多雇主都会为员工提供此类福利，且成本相对较低，但很少有人会利用这一选项。此外还有长期护理保险，可在人退休后支付养老院护理及其他相关费用。当然，这类保险的缺点是，如果人在需要护理之前就去世了，缴纳的保费就会白费。

<!--en-->
There are also plenty of other types of insurance to write about when it comes to benefits. Disability insurance helps pay for an employee's bills, such as their rent and electricity, when they are injured and can't work. Many employers offer such a benefit to their workers, and it's relatively cheap, yet few take advantage of the offer. There's also long-term care insurance, which can pay for nursing home care and other expenses when a person retires. The downside to such coverage, of course, is that the premiums will be wasted if the person dies before they need such care.

个人理财报道甚至可以探讨那些很少有雇主提供保障的保险类型，比如汽车险和房屋险。不过，关于如何在不提高保费的情况下充分利用这类保单的内容，对消费者来说同样具有很高的价值。许多消费者并不完全清楚自己的汽车险或房屋险涵盖哪些内容、不涵盖哪些内容。你可以向他们解释，例如如何在房屋险中添加附加条款——即一种能提供额外保障的特殊保险条款——来为他们的棒球卡收藏或珍贵艺术品收藏购买保险。

<!--en-->
Personal finance reporting can even take a look at types of insurance, such as auto and home coverage, that few, if any, employers cover. But stories about how to get the most out of such policies—without increasing the price—can be just as valuable to consumers. Many consumers don't fully understand what their auto or home policy does and does not cover. You can explain to them how, for example, to get a rider—a special insurance policy provision that provides additional benefits—on their home policy to cover their baseball card collection or their prized art collection.

## 退休规划

<!--en-->
*Retirement Planning*

随着人们对社会保障体系长期可持续性的质疑日益增多，以及企业们在养老金计划资金筹措方面面临困难，个人理财新闻开始更深入地探讨消费者们是如何规划退休生活的费用的。《财富》杂志2009年8月17日的文章详细分析了社会保障体系存在的问题及其可能对每个美国人的影响。

<!--en-->
As questions arise about the long-term viability of the Social Security system and companies struggle to properly fund their pension plans, personal finance journalism has been taking a closer look at how consumers are planning to pay for their retirement years. The August 17, 2009 issue of *Fortune* magazine took a long look at the problems of Social Security and what it might mean for every American.

目前，最受关注的退休规划话题就是由雇主资助的401(k)退休计划。该计划得名于美国国税局法规中的某一部分，允许雇主在员工工资税前提取部分资金并存入其退休账户。通常，雇主还会匹配一定数额的资金。

<!--en-->
Currently, the biggest retirement planning story is the employer-sponsored retirement plan known as the 401(k). Named after a section of the Internal Revenue Service Code, a 401(k) plan allows an employer to take money out of a worker's paycheck before tax and put it in a retirement account. The employer will often match the money up to a certain amount.

这是如何运作的呢？假设你在撰写一篇关于某位每周收入1,000美元的消费者的故事。此人选择每周将10%，即100美元，存入401(k)计划。其雇主会匹配前6%的金额，这意味着每周还会再投入60美元。这些钱实际上是由公司直接给予员工的。此外，该员工的应税收入减少到900美元，因此每周需缴纳的税款也会相应减少。如果他将这笔钱一直留在401(k)计划中直到达到退休年龄，就可以免税提取。但如果他提前取出这笔钱用于购房或其他用途，则必须缴纳税款并支付罚款。

<!--en-->
How does this work? Let's say you're writing a story about a consumer who makes $1,000 a week. This person opts to have 10 percent, or $100, a week put into the 401(k) plan. His employer matches the first 6 percent, which means it is putting an additional $60 in every week. That's money that's essentially given to the employee by the company. In addition, the worker's taxed income decreases to $900, which means he is paying less in taxes every week. If he keeps the money in the 401(k) plan until reaching retirement age, he can withdraw it without having to pay taxes. However, if he takes it out early to purchase a home or do something else, he has to pay taxes and penalties.

关键问题——也是许多个人理财记者重点关注的一点——是员工必须自行决定这笔钱的投资方向。雇主通常会提供多种选择，包括公司股票、采用不同投资策略的共同基金、货币市场账户以及债券。员工该怎么办呢？很多人会向个人理财记者寻求建议，而记者们通常会建议他们分散投资。安然公司倒闭、其股票价格跌至零时，一些前安然员工就吃了苦头，因为他们把所有的401(k)资金都投在了安然公司的股票上。《人们的钱就是新闻》•99位个人理财记者会撰写有关退休规划策略的文章，比如建议每季度查看401(k)账户对账单以了解投资表现，并给出何时应该考虑调整计划内投资组合的指导。他们还会介绍员工离职后如何处理401(k)计划，以及如何将计划中的资金转入新雇主的401(k)选项或投资到个人退休账户（IRA）中。

<!--en-->
The catch—and what many personal finance reporters focus on—is that the employee has to pick where the money is invested. The employer will typically provide a number of options, including company stock, mutual funds withvarious investment strategies, money market accounts, and bonds. What is the employee to do? Many of them look for advice from personal finance journalists, who regularly advise them to diversify their investments. Some former Enron employees learned this the hard way when the company collapsed and the stock price fell to nothing. They had put all of their 401(k) into the Enron stock options.
People's Money is News • 99
Personal finance journalists write about retirement planning strategies, such as checking your 401(k) statement every quarter to make sure the investments are performing, and provide guidelines on when a consumer should consider changing their investment portfolio in the plan. They also write about how workers can take their 401(k) plan when they leave their employer and how they can roll the money from the plan into their new employer's 401(k) option, or invest it in an individual retirement account (IRA).

这一领域还有其他值得撰写的主题，包括IRA账户和罗斯IRA计划。消费者可以通过在IRA中存钱，在401(k)之外节省更多资金。根据收入和纳税状况，这些存款可能可享受税收减免，且当人们停止工作、税率降低时即可提取这笔钱。对于罗斯IRA而言，至少在账户建立五年后提取的资金是免税的。这类信息正是个人理财记者乐于提供给读者的。

<!--en-->
Other topics to write about in this area include IRA accounts and Roth IRA plans. Consumers can save additional money outside their 401(k) by putting money into an IRA. The contributions may be tax deductible based on income and tax-filing status, and the money is withdrawn when the person stops working and their tax rate is lower. With a Roth IRA, distributions are tax-free at least five years after the account has been established. That's the kind of information that personal finance reporters love to provide readers.

### 大额消费

<!--en-->
*The Big Purchase*

大多数消费者在人生中的某个阶段都会购买房产。而对大多数人来说，这将是他们一生中最大的一笔消费，因此非常适合从个人理财的角度进行报道。

<!--en-->
Most consumers, at some point in their lives, will purchase a house. And for most consumers, it's the largest purchase they will ever make, which lends itself well to writing about it from a personal finance perspective.

关于买房与租房哪个更划算的问题由来已久，不同年龄段的人在不同情况下会有不同的选择。此外，抵押贷款利息可抵扣税款这一点，以及房产增值有助于家庭积累财富的问题也备受关注。近年来，一个热门话题是利用房产的净值贷款来偿还利率更高的贷款，比如信用卡债务。事实上，关于房产的购买、出售和再融资的内容充满了个人理财层面的视角。

<!--en-->
There's the age-old question of buying vs. renting and which is more advantageous for a consumer at certain ages. There's also the issue of mortgage interest payments being tax deductible and the appreciation of the value of a home in terms of helping a family create value. In recent years, a hot topic was using equity loans on a home to pay off higher interest loans, such as credit card debt. Indeed, writing about the buying, selling, and refinancing of a home is full of personal finance angles.

个人财经作家还可以探讨固定利率抵押贷款与浮动利率抵押贷款的优缺点。对于计划长期居住在该房产的人而言，前者更为合适；而对于打算在三到五年内出售房屋的人来说，后者则可能更适用。对于需要建立信用记录的首次购房者而言，浮动利率抵押贷款也可能是个不错的选择。另一种选择是按月调整利率的浮动利率抵押贷款，不过这类产品的风险更高，消费者应当了解其可能带来的高昂成本。

<!--en-->
Personal finance writers can also explore the advantages and disadvantages of fixed-rate mortgages and adjustable-rate mortgages. The former is preferable to home buyers who plan to stay at the location for a long time, while the latter can work well for someone who plans to sell the home in three to five years. Adjustable-rate mortgages can also be preferable to first-time buyers needing to establish credit. Another consideration is an option adjustable-rate mortgage, where the interest rate rises every month. These are more risky, and consumers should be made aware of how expensive such deals can be.

接下来要考虑的是贷款期限——购房者应该选择30年还是15年的还款期？同样，这取决于消费者的财务状况，两者各有利弊。

<!--en-->
Then there's the length of a loan. Should a buyer go for a 30-year or a 15-year term? Again, both have plusses and minuses, depending on the consumer's financial situation.

近年来，次级抵押贷款的概念日益受到关注，因为它们是2008年经济危机的原因之一。贷款机构向那些原本可能不符合抵押贷款条件的消费者提供贷款，而且往往没有充分评估这些人的还款能力，也没有向购房者充分解释相关风险，导致他们可能失去住房。如今，抵押贷款机构已收紧了此类贷款的资格要求，这为个人财经报道提供了很好的素材。《人民金钱即新闻》：另一个与抵押贷款相关的个人财经话题是，当利率下降时是否应该重新申请贷款。虽然重新申请贷款需要花费费用，但可以降低每月的还款额，而且如果消费者有其他资金需求，还可以提取房屋的部分资产价值。

<!--en-->
In recent years, the concept of sub-prime mortgages has gained prominence, as they were one of the reasons for the economic meltdown in 2008. Lenders gave home loans to consumers who otherwise might not have qualified for a mortgage. In doing so, they often didn't perform enough due diligence on the customer'sability to repay the mortgage, and they also may not have explained what the consumer was purchasing well enough for buyers to understand the risk of losing their homes. Now, mortgage lenders have tightened their restrictions on who qualifies for such loans, making it a great personal finance story.
100 • People's Money is News
Another personal finance topic related to mortgages is whether to refinance the loan when interest rates fall. Refinancing costs money, but it can cut the amount of the monthly payment, and consumers can take some equity out of the home if they need money for another purpose.

我们也不应忽视购房以及其他个人财经报道领域中存在的骗局。我的一位前学生安德鲁·邓恩在《夏洛特观察家报》的商业版实习期间撰写了一篇相关报道，讲述了一家公司向消费者露丝·巴伯承诺收购她的房子却从未履行承诺的事件。邓恩写道：

<!--en-->
Let's not forget the scams out there in home purchasing—and in other areas of personal finance reporting. One of my former students, Andrew Dunn, wrote this story while interning on the business desk of the *Charlotte Observer*. It's about a company that told consumer Ruth Barbour it would buy her house but never did. Dunn writes:

> 和北卡罗来纳州的其他人一样，她也成了某种越来越常见的抵押贷款骗局的受害者，这类骗局多针对那些急于脱手房产的房主。夏洛特地区的涉案人员中包括一名曾因抵押贷款欺诈入狱的男子。有研究这一现象的律师估计，已有数千人上当受骗。这些声称能快速收购并完成房屋交易的机构已经引起了州监管机构和立法者的注意，他们正在考虑出台相关法律以更方便地追踪此类案件。“很多房主正面临被收回房产的风险，他们的处境十分脆弱，”共同推动相关追踪法案的韦克县民主党议员詹妮弗·韦斯表示，“还有许多毫无戒心的民众正在被利用。”³ 购买和出售房屋对消费者来说可能是最令人沮丧的经历之一，有一些个人财经记者专门从事房地产领域的报道，他们擅长用通俗易懂的方式解释相关流程，告诉消费者需要注意什么、该争取什么以及该避免什么。

<!--en-->
> Like others across North Carolina, she fell victim to a type of mortgage scheme that's become more common as businesses target homeowners desperate to get out of their houses. The major Charlotte players include a man who spent time in prison for mortgage fraud. One lawyer studying the trend estimates several thousand people have been taken in. The businesses, which say they buy and close on homes quickly, have captured the attention of state regulators and legislators, who are now considering legislation that would make tracking these cases easier. "A lot of homeowners are facing foreclosure, and they're very vulnerable," said N.C. Rep. Jennifer Weiss, a Wake County Democrat who is cosponsoring legislation to track the cases. "There are a lot of unwary folks out there who are being taken advantage of."³
Buying and selling a house can be one of the most frustrating experiences for a consumer, and there are personal finance journalists who focus solely on writing about real estate. Their expertise is in explaining the process in a way that anyone can understand, telling consumers what to watch out for, what to push for, and what to resist.

## 信用评分

<!--en-->
*Credit Scores*

决定一个人能否购买房屋的因素之一就是其信用记录，然而包括一些个人财经作家在内，很少有人完全了解信用评分的评定方式。因此，这在几乎所有媒体上都是一个很适合做个人财经报道的主题。

<!--en-->
One of the issues that determines whether someone can purchase a house is their credit history, yet few people—including some personal finance writers—fully understand how a person's credit score is determined. That makes it a great personal finance story in virtually any publication.

信用报告记录了一个人的信用活动情况，其中列出了该人可能拥有的任何信用卡账户和贷款、欠款金额以及还款频率，还会显示因未付款而产生的任何处理措施。负责收集这些信息的有三家公司——Equifax、Experian和TransUnion。它们会对这些信息进行整理，为该人生成一个信用评分。[^1193]：³ 摘自A.邓恩2009年8月16日发表于《夏洛特观察家报》第1D版的文章《房屋骗局让房主受害：这些企业以买家身份招揽业务，虽取得房屋产权但并未承接抵押贷款，部分甚至会让陷入困境的房主面临房屋被收回的风险》，版权归2009年《夏洛特观察家报》所有。《人民金钱即新闻》•101 该信用评分基于五个类别——还款历史、欠款金额、信用记录时长、新信用业务以及所用信用类型。

<!--en-->
A credit report is a record of a person's credit activities. It lists any credit card accounts and loans the person may have, the balances, and how regularly the person makes payments. It also shows any action because of unpaid bills. There are three companies—Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion—that collect this information. They tabulate the information and create a score for that person.
[^1193]: ³ From "Home scam stings owners: Businesses advertise as buyers. They take over a home's title but not the mortgage, and some can leave distressed owners in foreclosure," by A. Dunn, August 16, 2009, *Charlotte Observer*, p. 1D. Copyright 2009 by *Charlotte Observer*.
People's Money is News • 101
The score is based on five categories—payment history, amount owed, length of credit history, new credit, and type of credit used.

许多消费者并未意识到，其实有很多人能够查看他们的信用评分。显然，那些考虑向某人提供贷款的债权人可以获取其信用评分，但其他人也能做到。考虑招聘、晋升或调岗的人士可以获取信用报告，打算为消费者办理新保险或续保的保险公司同样可以。政府机构为评估民众是否符合领取福利的条件而会查阅信用报告，潜在房东或有正当业务需求的人也可能会查看。害怕了吗？我敢打赌，你们很多人希望知道自己的当前信用评分是多少，以及谁查过它。

<!--en-->
What many consumers don't realize is who can get their credit score. Obviously, creditors who are considering granting a loan to a person can obtain his or her score. But so can others. Employers considering someone for a job, a promotion, or a reassignment can acquire a credit report, as can insurance companies considering a consumer for a new policy or a renewal. Government agencies can review a credit report to assess someone's financial status for government benefits, as can a potential landlord or anyone with a legitimate business need for the information. Scared yet? I bet many of you wish you knew what your current credit score was and who has been looking at it.

而这正是个人财经新闻的意义所在。你需要提供信息，让读者了解到那些影响他们生活却尚未知晓的事情，帮助他们掌握改善自身状况所需的细节。

<!--en-->
And that's the point of personal finance journalism. You want to provide information that tells the reader something about their lives that affects them but which they don't know. You want to arm them with the details they need to make themselves better.

### 预算与支出

<!--en-->
*Budgeting and Spending*

尤其是在最近几年，个人财经报道中增长最快的领域是与人们日常生活相关的内容，比如帮助他们控制日常开支，以及提供避免过度消费的建议。

<!--en-->
The fastest growing area of personal finance reporting, particularly in the last few years, has been content related to people's everyday lives, such as taking control of their day-to-day expenses and providing tips on how not to overspend.

这些个人财经类文章的内容涵盖从如何减少家庭年末税负到为子女上社区大学做储蓄的各种建议。其中还包括如何与信用卡公司协商降低年利率的文章，以及“财务改造”类故事——在这些故事中，个人财经记者会将消费者的财务状况交给专业财务规划师，然后再撰写相关建议。

<!--en-->
These personal finance stories range from tips on what to do to lower your family's tax bill at the end of the year to saving for junior's college. They include stories on how to negotiate with a credit card company to lower your annual interest rate and stories on money makeovers, where the personal finance journalist takes a consumer's financial situation to a professional financial planner and then writes about the advice.

《雅基马先驱共和报》的记者Mai Hoang在学年开始前撰写了关于如何理性购物、控制服装开支的文章。她采访了购物者，听取了他们的策略，并获得了专家的建议。她的文章里还附有一系列购物时的注意事项，以及排队结账时该怎么做。

<!--en-->
Reporter Mai Hoang, of the *Yakima* (Wash.) *Herald-Republic*, wrote about shopping for clothes on a budget right before the start of the school year. She talked to shoppers about their strategies and got advice from experts. Her story included a box of tips to consider while shopping and what to do while standing in the checkout line.

《罗利新闻与观察家报》的零售行业记者Sue Stock将预算意识提升到了新的高度。她运营着一个名为“Taking Stock”的博客，在其中记录自己每年通过优惠券和促销活动节省的金额，还会每周整理一份当地可找到并使用的优惠券清单。她在最近的一篇博文中写道：“我经常听到不使用优惠券的人说，使用优惠券太耗时间了，剪贴、分类这些步骤让人觉得负担太重。但我的答案是：如果你每周能花一两个小时来剪贴、分类并查看促销传单，就能节省不少钱，大概每周至少20美元。每周20美元，一年就是1000多美元，而且这是税后金额，都是实实在在的钱。”

<!--en-->
Sue Stock, the retail reporter for *The* (Raleigh) *News & Observer*, takes budget awareness to the next level. She writes a blog called “Taking Stock” where she chronicles her savings each year using coupons and sales and compiles a list every week of where local coupons can be found and used. A recent blog entry stated, “One of the most common things I hear from non-couponers is that it simply takes too much time to use coupons. All the clipping and sorting makes people feel like it's too much of a commitment. Well here's my answer. If you can devote one to two hours a week to clipping, sorting and reviewing the sales fliers, you will be able to save a substantial amount. Probably at least $20 a week. $20 a week is more than $1,000 a year. And those are post-tax dollars, too, so that's some real money.”

美联社商业记者Sarah Skidmore根据一项调查数据拓展了话题，给出了如何协商更低价格的建议。根据消费者调研机构American Research Group的调查，过去几个月里约有72%的美国消费者曾要求商家降低购买价格，而且他们有大约80%的成功率。102 • 人民的金钱就是新闻

<!--en-->
AP business reporter Sarah Skidmore took some data from a survey and expanded the topic to provide some advice on how to negotiate lower prices. About 72 percent of American consumers have asked for a lower price on their purchases in the past few months, according to consumer survey organization American Research Group. And they were successful about 80 percent of the time.
102 • People's Money is News

#### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《底特律自由报》的专栏作家Susan Tompor谈个人财经报道：

<!--en-->
Detroit Free Press columnist Susan Tompor on covering personal finance:

留意你自己的账单、对账单以及寄到家的邮件：仔细阅读那些细则——你会发现一些有趣的故事或专栏素材。早在国会开始关注信用卡费用之前，我在20世纪90年代中期就写过关于信用卡还款何时会被视为逾期的奇怪规则和特殊时间的文章。这些内容藏在细则里，很适合作为专栏素材。如果你阅读银行或其他机构发送的信息，就能提醒读者注意存在的问题、异常规则或费用。礼品卡早期也是如此。很多人没有意识到某些礼品卡的有效期有多短——或者这种“礼物”并不会一直有效。不过，只要阅读细则，你就能写出很多好的文章，提醒赠送礼品卡和接收礼品卡的人。

<!--en-->
Pay attention to your own bills, statements, the mail you receive at home: Read that fine print—you can uncover some fine stories or columns. Long before Congress started looking at credit card fees, I wrote columns in the mid-1990s about some strange rules and oddball times when a credit card payment could be viewed as late. It was buried in the fine print and made interesting reading for a column. You can alert readers to problems or unusual rules or fees if you read what banks or others are sending. The same was true early on for gift cards. Many people didn't realize how quickly some cards could expire—or how this gift did not keep on giving. If you read the fine print, though, you could write a lot of good pieces warning people who gave gift cards and people who received them.

于是Skidmore提出了六条关于如何巧妙讨价还价的建议，这些建议被全国各地的报纸采用。这些建议基于谈判专家的建议，包括保持礼貌、练习推销话术，以及利用自己作为消费者的优势。

<!--en-->
So Skidmore provided six recommendations on how to haggle with class that were picked up by papers across the country. Her suggestions, based on advice from negotiating experts, included being polite, practicing your pitch, and using your leverage as a shopper.

## 结论

<!--en-->
*Conclusion*

请记住，个人理财故事几乎可以涉及任何主题。仅仅因为某些内容没有在这里被提及，并不意味着它不能成为个人理财故事。1993年，我为《商业周刊》的“个人业务”栏目写了一篇关于收集棒球卡的文章；同年晚些时候，我又写了一篇关于买卖稀有汽车的文章。虽然这些内容看似不属于典型的个人理财故事，但它们在读者中极为受欢迎。那篇关于棒球卡的文章如此受欢迎，以至于我受邀登上CNBC节目讨论这一话题。

<!--en-->
Remember that personal finance stories can be about virtually anything. Just because something wasn't mentioned here doesn't mean that it can't be a personal finance story. In 1993, I wrote a story for *BusinessWeek*'s "Personal Business" section about collecting baseball cards. Later that year, I wrote another story about buying and selling exotic cars. While these may not seem like your basic personal finance stories, they were extremely popular with readers. The baseball card story was so popular that I was invited to appear on CNBC to discuss the topic.
