## 建议练习

<!--en-->
*Suggested Exercises*

1. 为自己制定一份基本预算，列出你的各项开支和收入——即便这些钱来自父母。然后把这两类金额加总。完成后，与另一位同学交换预算表，探讨彼此如何减少开支。还有哪些节钱策略你还没有采用？
2. 拿出最近几期的信用卡账单，仔细查看你的消费记录。账单上是否有你几乎没用过的商品？如果是这样，这能反映出你使用信用卡的习惯如何？
3. 查找有关美国消费者每月还清信用卡比例的统计数据，并与你同学们的简短调查结果进行对比。你是否会每月还清信用卡账单？这能说明你的个人财务状况如何？
4. 学期快结束时，再做一次本章中的个人理财测试。第二次测试的成绩是更好了还是更差了？你认为成绩变化的原因是什么？
5. 您认为大学生最感兴趣阅读哪类个人理财故事？您会采访谁来撰写这些故事，又会如何进行写作？请为您的指导老师或编辑准备一份简短的一页纸故事构思，并向他们展示。![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/28ea43c75649b559f3d457664e5f2bf5.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T071651Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=dad81d05341e7c3dc2ac5ee5c8d19c2cba01bb2024fde22f0455cd314ab6dee1)

<!--en-->
1. Write out a basic budget for yourself, listing your expenses and your income—even if the money comes from your parents. Then total up the two categories. When you are done, swap your budget with another classmate and talk about how each of you can lower your expenses. What are some money-saving strategies that you're not implementing?
2. Pull out the last few statements of your credit card bill and review your purchases. Are there items on the statements that you've barely used? If so, what does that say about your credit card habits?
3. Find statistics that detail what percentage of U.S. consumers pay off their credit cards each month and compare that to a quick survey of your classmates. Do you or do you not pay off your credit card statements every month? What does that say about your personal finances?
4. Near the end of the semester, go back and take the personal finance quiz in this chapter again. Did you do better or worse the second time you took the test? Why do you think your performance changed?
5. What type of personal finance stories do you think college students would be most interested in reading about? Who would you interview for those stories, and how would you write them? Come up with a short, one-page story pitch to your instructor or an editor and present it to them.

The Ins and Outs of Company News Stories

## SEC备案文件是记者的最佳帮手

<!--en-->
*SEC Filings are a Reporter's Best Friend*

在互联网出现之前，很难说服一些上市公司向记者提供其SEC备案文件的副本。许多公司知道，如果记者不在华盛顿特区或纽约，往往很难拿到这些文件。那些负责复制备案文件并寄送至新闻编辑部的服务通常每份收费25美元。对于许多吝啬的报纸来说，这笔钱实在太高了，尤其是对于那些可能根本不会成为报道内容的枯燥监管文件。

<!--en-->
Before the Internet, it was tough to convince some publicly traded companies to provide copies of their SEC filings to reporters. Many companies knew that if reporters were not in Washington, DC, or New York, it was often hard for them to get their hands on these documents. Services that would make copies of filings and mail them to newsrooms typically charged $25 a pop. For many penny-pinching newspapers, that was a lot of money for a boring regulatory filing that might not have contained news that would end up in the paper.

然而，商业版编辑从未反对在8-K表格上花钱。这是因为8-K表格所包含的实际新闻内容比公司向SEC提交的任何其他表格都要多。用法律术语来说，8-K表格是一种针对公司生活中“极其重要”事件的“即时事件报告”。这意味着8-K表格几乎可以披露任何信息。SEC规定有16种事件需要通过8-K表格披露，它们分别是：

<!--en-->
Never, however, did a business editor object to spending money on a Form 8-K filing. That is because Form 8-Ks contain more actual news than any other form companies file with the SEC. In legal lingo, a Form 8-K is a “current event report” for a “materially important” occurrence in the life of a corporation. This means that the 8-K may disclose just about anything. The SEC has determined that 16 events require disclosure in an 8-K. They are:

1. 控制权变更；
2. 资产的收购或处置；
3. 破产法庭起诉或监管行动；
4. 会计事务所更换；
5. 董事辞职；
6. 财务报表及附表；
7. 财年变更；
8. 签署或终止重大最终协议；
9. 表外财务安排；
10. 与业务处置或退出相关的成本；
11. 任何加速或增加财务义务的事件；
12. 重大资产减值；
13. 股票退市通知；
14. 未经注册的股票出售；106 • 公司新闻故事的方方面面

<!--en-->
1. Change in control;
2. Acquisition or disposition of assets;
3. Bankruptcy-court filing or regulatory action;
4. Change in accounting firm;
5. Resignation of directors;
6. Financial statements and exhibits;
7. Change in fiscal year;
8. Entering or terminating a material definitive agreement;
9. An off-balance sheet financial arrangement;
10. Costs related to the disposal or exiting of a business;
11. Any event that accelerates or increases a financial obligation;
12. Material impairments;
13. Notice of delisting of the stock;
14. Unregistered sale of stock;
106 • The Ins and Outs of Company News Stories

### 专业人士的经验分享

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

路透社记者Karey Wutkowski谈SEC备案文件：

<!--en-->
Reuters reporter Karey Wutkowski on SEC filings:

**要意识到自己正在玩一场猫捉老鼠的游戏：**监管备案文件中存在着根本性的矛盾。通常，企业以及对冲基金等大型投资者会试图尽可能少地披露信息，同时仍需满足华盛顿证券交易委员会设定的披露要求。你的任务就是找出那些隐藏的有用信息，以及提交文件方对其业务表现、高管薪酬以及公司财务前景的真实看法。

<!--en-->
**Realize that you are engaged in a game of cat and mouse:**
There is a fundamental tension in regulatory filings. Oftentimes, companies and big-time investors such as hedge funds are trying to reveal as little information as possible, while still meeting the disclosure requirements set by the Securities and Exchange Commission in Washington. It is your job to find where the good information is hiding, and what the filer is REALLY saying about the performance of their business lines, how they are paying their executives and what the financial outlook is for their companies.

#### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

路透社记者Karey Wutkowski谈SEC备案文件：**监管备案文件可能是令人生畏的文件，**其中充斥着法律术语和大量数字，往往让人难以理解。但对于那些愿意突破形式主义障碍、挖掘其中信息的记者来说，它们却是无价工具。商业记者几乎每天都会查看SEC备案文件，以判断公司高管是否在买入股票以表达信心，对冲基金是否正在透露恶意收购的初步计划，或者某家大公司是否已成为联邦机构调查其财务作假的对象。

<!--en-->
Reuters reporter Karey Wutkowski on SEC filings:
**Regulatory filings can be intimidating documents,**
chock full of legalese and so many numbers that they tend to blur. But they are also an invaluable tool for reporters willing to get past the veil of formality and discover just how much information is at their fingertips. Business reporters use SEC filings almost every day to see if a company's executives are buying up stock as a vote of confidence, if hedge funds are disclosing the first steps of a hostile takeover, or if a major corporation has become the target of a federal probe about cooking their books.

15. 运营或财务业绩；或
16. 任何其他公司认为重要的事件。通常情况下，提交的8-K文件只是公司发布的新闻稿的副本。不过，有时8-K文件会包含新闻稿中未提供的额外信息；而有时则会在没有发布新闻稿的情况下提交8-K文件。这类情况往往最适合作为新闻素材。一般来说，当一家公司提交8-K文件但不发布新闻稿时，该公司必须——但可能并不愿意——披露其中的信息。许多8-K文件都是在周五下午提交的，尤其是当消息不佳时。公司希望商业记者会忘记去查找这些文件，转而考虑周末的事情。然而，随着越来越多的记者意识到这些文件的存在，这样的策略通常会失败。此外，那些能在所报道的公司向SEC提交文件时及时提醒记者的服务，也有助于防止新闻被忽视。公司必须向SEC提交数十份文件，以披露对记者而言至关重要的信息。第9章介绍了10-Q和10-K文件所能提供的宝贵信息。本章则探讨了在委托书以及高管买卖公司股票时提交的表格中所披露的重要信息。简而言之，SEC文件可以是记者最好的帮手。尽管这些表格大多现在都是以电子方式提交的，但这些纸质文件仍能披露新闻与信息，让人们对上市公司及部分私营公司的运营状况有宝贵的了解。虽然这些文件中的很多都使用晦涩的法律术语，难以理解，但只要记者能够明白其中的内容，它们往往就能揭示企业内部运作及重要决策的关键细节。与20年前相比，如今可以通过多种途径获取公司的SEC文件。许多公司在其网站上公布了最新的SEC提交文件，如10-Q、10-K和委托书，但往往不会提供高管的内幕交易申报文件或投资者的申报文件。查看一家公司所有SEC提交文件的最简单方法，是访问该机构的网站www.sec.gov，然后点击“搜索公司文件”。之后只需输入公司名称并点击“查找公司”链接即可。另一家许多记者用来查阅SEC文件的平台是http://freeedgar.com,，该平台由总部位于康涅狄格州诺沃克的EDGAR Online Incorporated公司运营。该网站要求用户注册。这家公司还运营着一些付费网站，利用SEC文件中的信息和数据。有趣的是，EDGAR Online本身也是一家上市公司，其SEC文件可在其网站上查看。还有一些资深商业记者会使用Morningstar Document Research这一平台，它之前名为10Kwizard.com。许多记者选择这项服务，是因为它能让记者在特定公司的文件中搜索特定的单词或短语。例如，如果一名记者想查看可口可乐的所有提交文件，看看其中是否提到了百事可乐，那么在该网站上进行搜索就能告诉他或她竞争对手的相关内容出现在何处。（SEC的网站现在也有类似功能，允许记者搜索特定的单词或短语，比如“重大减值”。）不过，与EDGAR的某些服务一样，该网站也会对详细搜索收取费用。公司新闻报道的方方面面 • 107 阅读SEC文件对记者来说是一份宝贵的工具，尤其是对于那些刚接触相关报道领域的记者，因为他们需要了解并熟悉自己将要撰写报道的公司。阅读SEC文件并不每次都能产生新闻线索。事实上，即便有一半的时间，阅读SEC文件也不太可能带来新闻。但记者养成阅读所报道公司相关文件的习惯，仍然是一种良好的做法。 当某篇报道确实隐藏在厚厚的档案之中时，这种勤奋就会得到回报。而通读所有档案有助于勾勒出公司的全貌，从而让记者能够写出体现其专业素养的报道。

<!--en-->
15. Operational or financial results; or
16. Any other event deemed important to the company.
Quite often, the 8-K filed is simply a copy of the news release issued by a company. However, sometimes the 8-K will contain extra information not provided in the release. And at other times, the 8-K will be filed without a release being issued. Those are, quite often, the best for news. As a general rule of thumb, when a company files an 8-K but does not issue a news release, the company must—but may not want to—disclose the information therein.
Many 8-Ks are filed on Friday afternoons, particularly if the news is bad. Companies hope that the business reporter will forget to look for the filing and is instead thinking about the weekend. With more and more reporters becoming aware of these filings, however, such moves typically fail. In addition, services that alert reporters whenever a company on their beat files a document with the SEC help prevent news from flying below the radar.
Companies must file dozens of documents with the SEC that disclose information vital to reporters. Chapter 9 explains the valuable information that a 10-Q and a 10-K can provide. This chapter discusses the important information that gets disclosed in proxy statements, as well as forms filed by executives whenever they purchase or sell company stock.
Simply put, SEC documents can be a reporter's best friend. These pieces of paper—although most of these forms are now filed electronically—disclose news and information that can provide valuable insight into how public companies and some private companies operate. Although many of these documents are written in legalese that can be hard to understand, they often disclose the key details of the inner workings and important decisions made in a business, as long as the reporter understands what is being explained.
In stark contrast to 20 years ago, SEC documents for companies can now be obtained in a variety of ways. Many companies make their most recent SEC filings, such as the 10-Q, 10-K, and proxy statement, available on their websites. But they often do not provide insider trading filings made by executives or filings made by investors.
The easiest way to review all of a company's SEC filings is by going to the agency's website at www.sec.gov and clicking on "Search for Company Filings." From there, reviewing filings is as easy as typing in the name of the company and clicking on the "Find Companies" link. Another site that many reporters use to read SEC filings is http://freeedgar.com, a site run by a Norwalk, Connecticut-based company, EDGAR Online Incorporated. This site requires the user to register. The company also runs pay sites that use information and data from SEC filings. Interestingly, EDGAR Online itself is a public company, and its SEC filings are available on its website. A third site that some advanced business reporters use to examine filings is Morningstar Document Research, formerly 10Kwizard.com. Many reporters use this service because it allows a journalist to search a specific company's filings for certain words and phrases. For example, if a reporter wants to review all Coca-Cola filings to see if they mention Pepsi, a search on this website could tell him or her where the competitor is discussed. (The SEC's website now has a similar function that allows reporters to search for specific words and phrases, such as "materialimpairment.”) Like some of EDGAR’s services, however, this site charges for detailed searches.
The Ins and Outs of Company News Stories • 107
Reading SEC filings can be a valuable tool for reporters, particularly those new to their beats, because these new journalists need to learn about and understand the companies on which they are going to be writing stories. Reading an SEC filing may not result in a story every time. In fact, it is unlikely that reading SEC filings will result in a story even half of the time. But it is good practice for reporters to read the filings of companies on their beats. Such diligence pays off when a story does appear buried in the back of a filing. And reading all of the filings will help paint a picture of the company that will give the reporter the understanding needed to produce stories that show the writer knows his or her stuff.

### 必须披露的内容

<!--en-->
*Required Disclosures*

近年来，上市公司提交8-K表格的频率大幅增加。首先，了解公司必须提交8-K表格的各种原因以及提交时间非常重要。根据美国证券交易委员会的现行规定，公司必须在四个工作日内提交8-K表格；若为满足公平披露规则的要求，则还需更早提交。有时，公司会在事件发生的当天就提交8-K表格，但很多时候也会等待数天甚至一周。这一点尤其重要，尤其是当公司发布新闻稿时：在相关文件中可能还藏着后续报道的线索。

<!--en-->
In the past few years, public companies have dramatically increased the number of times they file 8-Ks. First, it is important to know the various reasons that a company must file a Form 8-K and when it must be filed. According to current SEC regulations, companies are required to file 8-Ks within four business days. If the filing is to satisfy compliance with Regulation Fair Disclosure, then the document must be filed even earlier. Sometimes, companies file 8-Ks on the day the event occurs. But many times, companies wait a few days or even a week. This is important to note, especially if the company issues a news release: A follow-up story may be waiting in the filing.

公司运营中的某些事件要求必须提交8-K表格。这些事件大多属于公司的重要变动，监管机构认为投资者有权知晓。财经记者应以监管要求为指引——这类披露内容往往是媒体应当报道的重要新闻。其中一种事件就是公司任命新领导层。由于新CEO或总裁的任命几乎总通过新闻稿公布，因此包含此类信息的8-K表格很少会成为值得报道的新闻。不过，有时关于高管变动的8-K表格会涉及重要信息。例如，请注意Chubb Corporation在2003年1月21日提交的这份8-K表格中所披露的细节，内容涉及其几个月前才被任命的新CEO的薪酬构成：

<!--en-->
Certain events in a company’s operations require that an 8-K be filed. Many of these events are important changes in a company that regulators have determined investors have a right to know about. Business writers should take their cues from the regulators—these disclosures are often important news that should be reported by media outlets. One of these events is when the company names a new leader. Because a new CEO or president is almost always announced by a news release, the filing of an 8-K with this information rarely becomes a newsworthy event. However, sometimes an 8-K about an executive change discusses important information. For example, note the details filed in this 8-K by Chubb Corporation on January 21, 2003, about the pay package of its new CEO, who had been named to the post months earlier:

1. 他的基本起薪为120万美元；
2. 他可获得的奖金最高可达其薪水的2.5倍；
3. 他持有的股票期权目前价值600万美元；
4. 他可使用公司配发的汽车、司机以及公司飞机出差，还可享受某家乡村俱乐部的会员资格及会费优惠，并获得免费的财务咨询服务。对于财经记者而言，新CEO的薪酬结构是非常重要的报道内容，因为这类披露有助于投资者和员工判断公司是否合理使用资金。此外，每当公司进行资产收购或处置——即买卖业务时——都必须提交一份详细说明该交易的8-K表格。通常，这类交易相关的8-K表格会披露

<!--en-->
1. His starting base salary is $1.2 million;
2. He may receive bonuses up to 2.5 times his salary;
3. His stock options are currently worth $6 million;
4. He may use a company car and driver and a company aircraft for business travel. He will be provided with a membership and club dues at one country club, and he will receive free financial counseling.
The new CEO’s compensation package is important for the business reporter to write about because this disclosure can help investors and employees determine whether a company is spending money wisely. In addition, whenever a company acquires or disposes of assets—buys or sells a business—it is required to file an 8-K detailing the transaction. Quite often, the 8-K about a transaction discloses

### 专家建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

路透社记者Karey Wutkowski谈SEC文件披露：

<!--en-->
Reuters reporter Karey Wutkowski on SEC filings:

**新一代正在崛起：** SEC文件格式一直在不断发展，从过去难以在互联网上检索的静态文档，演变为如今可通过数百种方式搜索的交互式文档。越来越多的公司、共同基金以及大型投资者开始使用可扩展商业报告语言（XBRL）来提交文件。这种格式会为每一个财务数字和文字信息加上电子“标签”，从这些标签中收集到的数据可以被导入电子表格或其他文档中，让用户能够快速比较和分析数据，从而进一步提升公司账目和运营的透明度。请持续关注这些变化，并学会如何利用它们更好地报道商业动态。

<!--en-->
**The next generation is coming:** The SEC filing is an evolving creature, going from a static document that can be difficult to call up on the Internet to an interactive document that can be searched in literally hundreds of ways. Companies, mutual funds, and big-time investors are increasingly filing their documents in eXtensible Business Reporting Language, or XBRL. This format will essentially tag every financial number and piece of written information with an electronic “tag.” The data collected from these tags can be brought into a spreadsheet or other document that will quickly let users compare and decipher data, bringing even more transparency to companies’ books and operations. Keep on top of the changes and learn how to use them to better report the business landscape.

#### 专家建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

路透社记者Karey Wutkowski谈SEC文件披露：

<!--en-->
Reuters reporter Karey Wutkowski on SEC filings:

**熟悉各类表格格式：** 如果不懂语言，就无法阅读书籍。同样，你也必须熟悉不同披露文件的格式。许多这类文件充斥着各种代码和正式术语，因此你必须深入了解它们的结构，才能迅速从中获取信息。

<!--en-->
**Know the forms:** You can’t read a book if you don’t know the language. Similarly, you must familiarize yourself with the format of different disclosure documents. Many of them are riddled with codes and formal terms, so you must intimately learn what these documents look like so you can quickly glean information from them.

#### 专家建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

路透社记者Karey Wutkowski谈SEC文件披露：

Reuters reporter Karey Wutkowski on SEC filings:

注意查看修订版文件：修订后的文件往往能提供大量有用信息，尤其是公司的季度报告。它可能是重大会计变动的首个迹象，也能反映公司的真实财务状况。此外，修订后的首次公开募股申请文件会补充有关发行定价的关键细节，从而显示该次IPO在投资者群体中引发的兴趣程度。修订后的股权结构文件则能显示是否有大型投资者在买入或卖出股票，以此体现其对公司的信心。即便文件经过了修订，所披露的信息依然具有时效性和参考价值。其他内容可能还包括合并协议、股票期权协议（如有）、对合并协议的任何修订或修改、交易完成情况、被收购公司的财务报表以及合并后公司的财务报表。

<!--en-->
Check for amendments: An amended filing can be a very revealing document, especially for a company's quarterly filings. It can be the first glimpse into a major accounting change, and can show the true financial condition of a company. Also, amended IPO filings fill in critical details on the pricing of the offering, which shows how much interest the IPO is garnering among the investing public. Amended ownership documents show if a major investor is selling or buying up stock, indicating his or her confidence in the company. Just because a document is amended, it does not mean the material revealed is not fresh and informative.
financial details of the deal not included in the release. Other items may include the merger agreement, including the stock option agreement if there is one, any amendments or modifications to the merger, the closing of the deal, financial statements of the company being acquired, and financial statements of the combined operations.

有时，8-K文件甚至会披露潜在的收购计划。例如，请参阅《丹佛邮报》上的这篇报道开头：

<!--en-->
Sometimes an 8-K may even disclose a potential acquisition. For example, note the beginning of this story from the *Denver Post*:

能源交易商及管道运营公司Williams Cos.可能会参与对Barrett Resources Corp.的竞购——这一动向是在周二“外部人员”接入Williams董事们的电话会议时被披露的。

<!--en-->
Williams Cos., an energy trader and pipeline operator, may jump into the bidding for Barrett Resources Corp.—a move disclosed Tuesday when “outside individuals” got onto a conference call among Williams directors.

总部位于丹佛的Barrett公司在周一拒绝了皇家荷兰壳牌集团旗下子公司提出的24亿美元的高价收购提议，并决定将公司挂牌拍卖。

<!--en-->
Denver-based Barrett on Monday rejected a sweetened $2.4 billion takeover bid by a unit of Royal Dutch/Shell Group and has put itself up for auction.

根据该公司向美国证券交易委员会提交的文件，总部位于俄克拉荷马州塔尔萨的Williams公司在周二通过电话召开了董事会会议，以考虑收购Barrett的事宜。文件中并未提及具体条款。该文件称，周二“电话会议服务提供商错误地将外部人员接入了公司的董事会会议”，从而无意间披露了Williams可能提出收购的消息。

<!--en-->
Williams, based in Tulsa, Okla., held a board meeting by telephone Tuesday to consider a bid to buy Barrett, the company disclosed in a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission. Terms weren't specified. Disclosure of a possible Williams bid was made unintentionally when “outside individuals were mistakenly connected by a conference call vendor” to the company's board meeting Tuesday, the filing said.

这份提交给SEC的8-K报告称：“在发现这一错误之前，Williams的高管们表示召开董事会会议是为了探讨Williams可能提出的收购Barrett的方案。”

<!--en-->
“Before this error was discovered, officers of Williams stated that the board meeting had been called to consider Williams' potential proposal to acquire Barrett,” said the filing, an 8-K report to the SEC.

Barrett公司表示将继续接受收购要约直至今日。该公司在PR Newswire上发表的声明称，由于价格上升，其第一季度的利润增长了六倍多。

<!--en-->
Barrett has said it will continue to accept bids until today. The company reported first-quarter profit rose more than sixfold because of higher prices.

Barrett公司在一份声明中表示，其净收入为5700万美元，稀释后每股收益为1.67美元，而去年同期分别为780万美元和每股24美分。公司的销售额则增长了一倍多，达到1.614亿美元。

<!--en-->
Denver-based Barrett posted net income of $57 million, or $1.67 a diluted share, up from $7.8 million, or 24 cents a share, a year ago, the company said in a statement on PR Newswire. Sales more than doubled to $161.4 million.

Barrett公司的股价上涨了52美分，至64.87美元——这表明投资者认为该公司很可能会收到比壳牌勘探生产公司每股60美元的报价更高的出价。Williams公司的股价则上涨了1.21美元，至43.38美元。¹如果没有提交8-K文件，关于Williams公司可能收到收购要约的这一重要消息很可能要等到官方新闻稿发布后才会被媒体报道。

<!--en-->
Barrett shares rose 52 cents to $64.87—an indication investors consider it likely the company will receive a higher offer than Shell Exploration and Production Co.'s bid of $60 per share.
Williams shares rose $1.21 to $43.38.¹
Without the filing of the 8-K, it is unlikely that this important news of an offer for Williams would have been disclosed in the media until a news release was issued.

当一家公司申请破产法院保护或面临监管机构的调查时，就必须提交8-K文件。对于那些业务遍布其他州或总部位于某州但在其他州注册成立的公司的记者来说，这些文件往往包含宝贵的信息。例如，由于特拉华州的公司法律较为友好，数千家公司在那里注册成立，因此该州有大量的破产案（以及诉讼案件）。因此，比如位于波特兰的记者很可能无法了解全国各地的公司或监管机构在特拉华州法院提交了哪些文件。[^1272]：¹摘自J. Beauprez所写的《Liberty takes On Command reins; Hotel room movie firm may be merged with rival》，发表于2001年5月2日的《丹佛邮报》，C-1版。版权归《丹佛邮报》所有，经许可转载。

<!--en-->
When a company files for bankruptcy-court protection or is the recipient of regulatory action, it must file an 8-K. These filings often contain valuable information for reporters covering companies with operations in other states or companies incorporated in states other than the one in which their headquarters are located. For example, thousands of companies are incorporated in Delaware because of its friendly corporation laws, so a large number of bankruptcies (and lawsuits, for that matter) are filed in that state. Thus, a reporter in Portland, for example, probably will not know what has been filed in Delaware courts by companies or by regulators across the country.
[^1272]: ¹ From “Liberty takes On Command reins; Hotel room movie firm may be merged with rival,” by J. Beauprez, May 2, 2001, *Denver Post*, p. C-1. Copyright 2001 by *Denver Post*. Reprinted with permission.

公司新闻报道的方方面面 • 109 基于这类文件撰写报道属于基础新闻报道，因为这些披露的内容已经说明了公司的最新状况。例如，当提供互联网、语音及传真通信软件的CyNet Incorporated申请第11章破产保护时，记者们便根据其提交的8-K文件对此事进行了报道。其他8-K文件可能还包括监管机构发给公司的信件，其中详细规定了对公司未来运营的限制，或是要求公司停止业务的禁令。在许多此类情况下，这些公司并不会发布新闻稿，因此记者们仔细阅读8-K文件就显得至关重要。

<!--en-->
The Ins and Outs of Company News Stories • 109
Writing stories from these types of filings should be basic reporting, because the disclosures spell out what is going on at a company. For instance, when CyNet Incorporated, a provider of Internet, voice, and fax messaging software, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection, reporters covered the event, detailed in its 8-K filing. Other 8-K filings might include documents such as letters from regulators to companies detailing limits placed on their future operations or restraining orders preventing companies from continuing to do business. In many of these cases, the companies do not issue news releases, which makes it vitally important for reporters to read 8-K filings.

当公司更换会计事务所时，也会提交8-K文件。其会计师可能已经辞职，也可能被解雇。无论哪种情况，这一事件都会导致文件提交，即便双方的离职是和平的。需要指出的是，通常当公司的财务报表存在分歧或差异时，会计事务所就会终止与客户的关系。鉴于安然公司与其前会计事务所安达信之间发生的事情，记者们可以预期会有更多公司认真审视其与审计师之间的关系。此外，还会有更多会计事务所重新评估与存在矛盾的客户的合作关系。

<!--en-->
Companies also file an 8-K when they change their accounting firm. Their accountants may have resigned, or they could have been fired. In either case, this event leads to a filing, even if the parting is amicable. It should be noted that an accounting firm often ends its relationship with a client when there is a disagreement about or a discrepancy in the company's financial statements. Given what happened between Enron and Arthur Andersen, Enron's former accounting firm, reporters should expect more companies to take a closer look at their relationships with their auditors. In addition, look for more accounting firms to re-assess relationships with clients with whom there has been friction.

撰写一篇关于某公司更换审计机构的新闻稿，在新闻编辑部看来或许算不上什么值得关注的头条。但此类变动可能暗示该公司内部存在更多问题，尤其是当其经营状况不佳时。企业所使用的会计事务所需在公司的年度股东大会上获得批准。如果某会计事务所决定不在年会上寻求连任，这一决定可能表明双方存在分歧。报纸上关于审计机构更替的简短报道，可能会引来该公司或该会计事务所相关人士的电话，希望向记者透露更多内幕信息。可查阅该公司的委托书或DEF 14A文件，了解年会上是否有新的会计事务所候选者。

<!--en-->
Writing a story about a company changing its auditors may not seem like an exciting day in the newsroom. But a change such as this may hint at further problems within the company, particularly if the business is struggling. Accounting firms used by companies are approved each year at the company's annual meeting. If an accounting firm declines to put itself up for re-election at the annual meeting, that decision could be a sign that there has been a disagreement. A small story in the newspaper about a change in auditors could lead to a call from a source—either at the company or at the accounting firm—who wants to tell the reporter more about what happened. Check the company's proxy statement, or DEF 14A, to see if there are new accountants up for election at the annual meeting.

董事会成员辞职时也必须提交8-K表格。除非该董事颇具知名度且在董事会中拥有较大影响力，否则这通常也不会成为商业版面的头版新闻。这类辞职消息通常只会有两三句话的简短描述。不过，董事会成员的突然辞职仍可能预示着董事会与公司管理层之间的矛盾日益加剧。多名董事会成员同时辞职则可能表明董事会与公司管理层之间存在冲突。2006年惠普公司一名董事会成员的辞职促使该公司披露了其曾暗中监视商业记者，以查明是哪位董事会成员泄露了信息的事实。这名董事因反对这种做法而辞职，最终董事会主席也跟着辞职了。

<!--en-->
An 8-K must also be filed when a member of the board of directors resigns. This is not typically a front-page story for a business section either, unless the board member was well known and carried some clout on the board. Typically such resignations are simply a brief, no more than two or three sentences. But again, the sudden resignation of a board member may signal growing discord between the board and the executive team at the company. Several board members resigning at the same time may also indicate conflict between the board and company management. The resignation of a Hewlett-Packard board member in 2006 led to the disclosure that the company was spying on business journalists to determine who on the board was leaking information. The board member resigned because he disagreed with the tactic, and the chairwoman of the board ended up resigning as well.

当公司变更财年时，也需要提交包含财务报表及附表的8-K表格。这类披露很少能成为新闻头条，但也有可能。例如，附表中可能包含与新高管签订的雇佣协议，如果相关细节此前未公开，记者就可以据此撰写新闻。财务报表通常是最近一个季度的，如果它们没有出现在公司的盈利公告中，就应当予以核查。

<!--en-->
A company also files an 8-K for its financial statements and exhibits and when it changes its fiscal year. Rarely do these disclosures result in a story, but they could. For example, an exhibit could be something such as an employment agreement with a new executive, and if the details have not been disclosed before, a reporter could write a story. The financial statements are typically from the most recent quarter, and if they were not included in the company's earnings release, they should be reviewed.

#### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

路透社记者Karey Wutkowski谈SEC文件：

<!--en-->
Reuters reporter Karey Wutkowski on SEC filings:

**别忘了脚注：**细节决定成败，而对于SEC文件而言，关键细节往往隐藏在脚注中。脚注是隐藏重要信息的常见地方，只要仔细研读文件，就能发现有关SEC对违规行为的调查、账外隐藏的有问题资产，以及会严重影响公司盈利的会计变更等信息。

<!--en-->
**Don't forget the footnotes:** The devil's in the details, and for SEC filings, those details are hidden in footnotes. The footnotes are a common place to hide critical details, and if you carefully comb the documents, you can find disclosures about SEC probes into wrongdoing, troubled assets that are parked off the books, and accounting changes that will significantly affect a company's bottom line.

#### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

路透社记者Karey Wutkowski谈SEC文件：

<!--en-->
Reuters reporter Karey Wutkowski on SEC filings:

**学会识别关键信息：**监管文件中有一些披露内容应引起警惕。你应该能够分辨出哪些是常规表述，哪些是公司的重大变化。如果审计机构表示怀疑该公司是否具备“持续经营能力”，这对该公司而言往往等同于死刑判决。如果公司宣布正在寻找“战略替代方案”，那就意味着它在寻求合作伙伴或其他公司收购自己以求生存。如果公司收到SEC的“威尔斯通知”，或者监管机构将其调查升级为正式调查，都会立即打压该公司的股价。熟悉这些术语，才能快速理解它们的影响。

<!--en-->
**Learn what matters:** There are a few disclosures housed in regulatory filings that should set off alarm bells. You should be able to recognize what is boilerplate language and what is a significant change at a company. A notice that an auditor has expressed doubts that a company is a "going concern" is often a death sentence for that company. A revelation that a company is seeking "strategic alternatives" means that company is looking for a partner or another company to acquire it in order to survive. A disclosure that a company has received a "Wells Notice" from the SEC or that a regulator has upgraded its probe into a formal investigation can immediately hammer a company's stock price. Familiarize yourself with these terms, so you can quickly interpret their impact.

110 • 公司新闻报道的方方面面

<!--en-->
110 • The Ins and Outs of Company News Stories

#### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

路透社记者Karey Wutkowski谈SEC文件：

<!--en-->
Reuters reporter Karey Wutkowski on SEC filings:

**要彻底深入：**这些文件页数可从一页到数百页不等。通读这些文件虽费时费力，但回报颇丰。许多记者只会匆匆浏览公司的文件，如果没有发现什么特别突出的新信息就会继续下一项工作。但若花时间挖掘其中隐藏的要点，就能率先报道出其他人忽略的新闻。

<!--en-->
**Be thorough:** These filings can vary from a single page to hundreds of pages. It can be a slog to make it through any of these documents, but there is pay-off. Many reporters will take a quick glance at a company's filings, and move on if nothing glaringly new jumps out at them. But taking the time to find the nuggets buried within these filings can put you in a position to reveal news that has escaped others' attention.

美国证券交易委员会还要求，任何对该公司业务具有重大影响的其他事件都必须在8-K文件中披露。究竟某一事件是否“重要到”需要披露，由公司高管自行判断。但由于2008年和2009年美国发生的经济危机等近期事件，许多公司因未及时披露信息而受到批评，这反过来又促使不少企业为符合联邦监管要求而主动提交8-K文件。例如，总部位于纽约的热狗连锁店Nathan's Famous Incorporated就提交了一份8-K文件，称家得宝终止了其旗下所有门店的8家餐厅经营许可协议，而这些门店的销售额约占该公司总销售额的15%。这一信息的重要性甚至被《亚特兰大宪报》负责报道家得宝的记者所关注。

<!--en-->
The SEC also requires that other events material to a company's business be disclosed in an 8-K filing. Whether an event is “material” enough to be disclosed is up for interpretation by company executives. But, as a result of recent events such as the economic crisis that occurred in the United States in 2008 and 2009, many companies have been criticized for not disclosing information, which, in turn, has caused a number of businesses to file 8-Ks just to be on the safe side of federal regulation. For example, Nathan's Famous Incorporated, a New York-based hot dog restaurant chain, filed an 8-K noting that Home Depot terminated eight restaurant license agreements at stores in which Nathan's operated, accounting for about 15 percent of the company's total sales. This information was valuable enough to be picked up by a reporter covering Home Depot for the *Atlanta Journal-Constitution*.

其他时候，公司会提交8-K文件来预测下一季度或下一年的业绩。这些预测通常会在各类会议或演示活动中向分析师和投资者公布。因此，在这种情况下提交8-K文件是为了让所有人能同时获取这些信息。

<!--en-->
Other times, companies file 8-Ks projecting earnings for the next quarter or for the next year. Many times, these projections are given to analysts and investors at conferences or presentations. Thus, in these instances, 8-Ks are filed so that the information is given to everyone at the same time.

2003年1月16日，总部位于纽约的人寿保险公司及资产管理公司MONY Group Incorporated提交8-K文件时，同时向美国证券交易委员会提供了当天晚些时候将向投资者和分析师展示的演示文稿幻灯片。通讯社记者及其他人士立即查阅了该文件，以判断幻灯片中是否有值得报道的消息。

<!--en-->
When MONY Group Incorporated, New York-based life insurer and asset manager, filed an 8-K on January 16, 2003, it provided the SEC with the slides from a presentation that it was giving to investors and analysts later that day. Wire service reporters and others immediately reviewed the filing to determine whether there was news in the slide show.

这就是在线新闻网站Insurance Investor Interactive负责跟踪MONY动态的迈克尔·克里滕登当天撰写报道的方式：

<!--en-->
This is how Michael Crittenden, who followed MONY for the online news site Insurance Investor Interactive, led his story that day:

> 人寿保险公司MONY Group Inc.在1月16日提交的监管文件中称，其第四季度的营业利润很可能超出华尔街的预期。这家总部位于纽约的公司在该8-K表格中表示，初步的第四季度业绩显示，税前营业利润在800万美元至1300万美元之间，即每股收益11美分至18美分。这一数值远高于Thomson First Call给出的3美分/股的共识预期，其中最高预期为11美分，最低预期为盈亏平衡。MONY Group称，第四季度的初步净收入应在900万美元至$14 million, or 12 cents to 19 cents per share.² Interestingly, that same day, Dan Lowrey, a reporter for Dow Jones, chose to focus on other disclosures in the filing. His lead noted the company's earnings estimates for 2003—$.30美元至$.35美元/股之间——而华尔街分析师的平均预期则为$.33美元/股。两位记者都仔细阅读了这份长达30多页的完整文件，并都发现了对读者有重要意义的新闻内容。其他情况下，8-K文件也可能披露有助于评估公司运营状况的财务数据。例如，美联社报道称，网络设备制造商Cisco Systems Incorporated在一份8-K文件中指出，其2.75亿美元的季度亏损准备金中有5%与客户账户相关。该公司为可疑账户损失计提了1400万美元的准备金，而去年同期仅为500万美元。在报道这一信息时，记者将Cisco本季度的亏损准备金与上一年度同期的数字进行了对比，让读者了解到该公司为处理逾期账款所预留的资金几乎是之前的三倍，这可能表明其客户存在还款困难。[^1298]：²摘自M. Crittenden于2003年1月16日在Insurance Investor Interactive上发表的文章《MONY预计第四季度业绩将超预期，与2003年水平相当》，版权所有2003年SNL Financial，经许可转载。《公司新闻报道的方方面面》•111 2002年，《匹兹堡邮报》的一篇短文利用Adelphia Communications Corporation提交的8-K文件中的信息，指出这家有线电视公司正在流失用户，因此预计收益会下降。该短文分析了Adelphia的收益预测，并说明了该公司为何要下调预期。任何基于8-K文件撰写报道的商业记者都必须解释这一情况发生的原因，以便为报道提供背景信息。此外，所有作为例子的报道都会注明信息的来源文件，这不仅提升了报道的可信度，也向读者展示了记者对该公司情况的密切关注。通常，记者需要通读文件中的大量内容才能找到有价值的新闻线索，然后将这些信息整合成一篇引人入胜的报道。他们必须将数千字的信息浓缩到通常不超过300至400字的文章中。普通投资者可能无法理解这类信息，但商业记者在专家的帮助下，凭借对自己报道主题的充分了解，能够正确分析这些信息，并撰写出向投资者说明该披露内容重要性的文章。

<!--en-->
> Life insurer MONY Group Inc. suggested in a Jan. 16 regulatory filing that its fourth quarter operating earnings could easily beat Wall Street expectations.
> In the Form 8-K, the New York-based company said that its preliminary fourth quarter results yielded pretax operating earnings in a range of $8 million to $13 million, or 11 cents to 18 cents per share. That range is well ahead of the Thomson First Call consensus estimate of 3 cents per share, with a high estimate of 11 cents and a low estimate of breakeven.
> MONY Group said preliminary net income for the fourth quarter should be between $9 million and $14 million, or 12 cents to 19 cents per share.²
Interestingly, that same day, Dan Lowrey, a reporter for Dow Jones, chose to focus on other disclosures in the filing. His lead noted the company's earnings estimates for 2003—$.30 to $.35 per share—compared with the average earnings estimate by Wall Street analysts, which was $.33 per share. Both reporters reviewed the entire filing, which, in this case, was more than 30 pages. And in both cases, the reporters found news important to their readers.
Other times, the 8-K may disclose financial results that can be important in assessing how a company is performing. For example, the Associated Press reported that computer networking equipment maker Cisco Systems Incorporatednoted in an 8-K filing that 5 percent of its $275 million quarterly loss provision was related to customer accounts. The company set aside $14 million for losses on doubtful accounts, up from $5 million in the same quarter the previous year. In writing about this disclosure, the reporter nicely compared Cisco's first quarter loss provision with the loss provision for the first quarter of the previous year. That comparison shows the reader that the company is setting aside nearly three times as much money to pay for overdue payments than it had previously, an indication that maybe its customers are having trouble paying their bills.
[^1298]: ² From “MONY sees fourth-quarter results ahead of estimates, in line 2003,” by M. Crittenden, January 16, 2003, Insurance Investor Interactive. Copyright 2003 by SNL Financial. Reprinted with permission.
The Ins and Outs of Company News Stories • 111
A 2002 brief in the *Pittsburgh Post-Gazette* used information from an 8-K filed by Adelphia Communications Corporation to show that the cable company was losing subscribers and thus projecting lower earnings.
The brief story took the earnings projections for Adelphia and showed why the company was lowering its estimates. It is important for any business reporter writing a story based on an 8-K to explain why the news is happening to give it context.
Also note that all of the stories used as examples cite the documents from which the information was obtained. Doing so lends credence to the report and to the reporter by showing readers that he or she is tracking the company closely. Often, a reporter must read through numerous pages in the filing to find snippets of news and then combine that information into a compelling story. A reporter has to condense thousands of words and numbers into a story that often is no longer than 300 to 400 words.
An individual investor may not be able to assess this kind of information. But a business journalist, with the help of experts and a proper understanding of what he or she is writing about, can properly assess the information and write a story telling the investor why the disclosure is important.

#### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

路透社记者Karey Wutkowski谈SEC文件：

<!--en-->
Reuters reporter Karey Wutkowski on SEC filings:

**了解公司的“性格”：**公司提交的SEC文件中包含大量能反映其企业文化的信息，这对撰写该公司相关报道的记者而言至关重要。公司支付给高管的薪酬数额，以及这些薪酬是以延期股权形式还是现金形式发放，都能体现这些高管对该公司未来的投入程度。关于公司董事会的详细信息，以及他们与其他公司或个人之间的利益关联或冲突，也能帮助人们了解公司信任谁来监督公司运营。你越深入研究这些文件，就会越清楚地看到不同公司所采取的透明度程度各异。一家公司对投资者的开放程度，能反映出它的经营方式以及所处的竞争市场环境。

<!--en-->
**Get to know a company's personality:** There is a lot of information in a company's SEC filings that reveals its corporate culture, an important aspect for a reporter telling that company's story. How much a company pays its executives and if that compensation is in the form of deferred equity or immediate cash says a lot about how invested those executives are in the company's future. Details about a company's board of directors and what entanglements, or conflicts of interest, they have with other companies or people can provide insight into who the company trusts to watch the shop. And the more you look at filings, the more you will realize the range of transparency that companies adopt. How open a company is to its investors says a lot about how it does business and the type of competitive market in which it competes.

#### 董事会成员和高管辞职

<!--en-->
*Resignations of Board Members and Executives*

前一节提到，公司需要在多种情况下提交8-K文件，包括高管变动或董事会成员辞职时。可以说，根据SEC规定，这些是最重要的披露内容，因为高管团队和董事会正是负责管理公司并确保其盈利的核心力量。不过，即便有其中一人或多人离职，也不应直接认为公司出了问题。

<!--en-->
The previous section mentioned that an 8-K must be filed on numerous occasions, including when a company changes its executives and when a board member resigns. These are, arguably, the most important disclosures under the SEC rule, because the executive team and the board are the people in charge of running the company and ensuring that the business is making money. However, if one or more of them leaves, you should not automatically assume that something is wrong.

很多时候，公司高管的更替与公司的经营状况毫无关系。CEO或董事会成员可能到了退休年龄。在某些情况下，CEO会因健康原因离开公司，或者认为该让更年轻的人来掌管公司了。董事会成员则可能因为其他商业机会而承担新责任，觉得自己没有足够时间投入董事会工作。

<!--en-->
Many times, company executives change for reasons that have nothing to do with the company's performance. A CEO or board member may reach retirement age. In some cases, a CEO will leave a company for health reasons or decide that it is simply time to let someone younger have a chance to run the shop. A board member may take on a new commitment with another business opportunity and feel that he or she does not have the proper time to devote to the board.

这些都是公司高层更迭的合理原因。但在越来越多的案例中，CEO或董事会成员的离职可能预示着公司内部存在动荡。

<!--en-->
These are all good reasons for a changing of the guard at a company. But in an increasing number of cases, a CEO or a board member moving on may be an indication that there is unrest.

商业记者首次意识到安然公司存在问题，是在其会计问题曝光前不久，该公司CEO杰弗里·斯克林格突然辞职。当时，斯克林格在声明中表示，他因个人原因离开公司，而这些原因与公司事务无关。

<!--en-->
The first time business journalists might have thought there was trouble at Enron was when its CEO, Jeffrey Skilling, abruptly resigned shortly before its accounting problems were disclosed. At the time, Skilling said in a statement that he was leaving the company for personal reasons that had nothing to do with the

##### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

路透社记者凯瑞·伍特科夫斯基谈SEC文件：

<!--en-->
Reuters reporter Karey Wutkowski on SEC filings:

**如果不确定，就询问：**许多监管文件都可能令人困惑。如果解读有误，记者就可能传播不准确的信息，进而影响大型公司的股价。如果您对文件中的内容有疑问，请致电该公司。相关官员通常无法透露文件中未公开的具体细节，但他们可以准确描述文件的内容。如果从公司那里得不到满意答复，可联系分析师或SEC本身，以彻底了解文件所传达的信息。

<!--en-->
**If you don't know, ask:** Many regulatory documents can be confusing. If read the wrong way, a reporter can disseminate inaccurate information that can move the stock of a major company. If you have a question about what is being revealed in a document, call the company. The officials are often limited in what they can say about a document because they cannot reveal details beyond what is disclosed in the filing, but they can describe exactly what the document says. If you do not get a satisfactory answer from the company, call an analyst or the SEC itself to fully understand what a document is telling you.

112 • 公司新闻报道的方方面面。虽然“个人原因”在很多情况下确实是一种合理的解释，但遗憾的是，这也正是许多公司用来掩盖紧张局势的借口——从董事会对CEO表现不满到直接发动政变迫使高管退休不等。

<!--en-->
112 • The Ins and Outs of Company News Stories company. Although “personal reasons” may be a valid explanation in a number of cases, it is also the terminology, unfortunately, that many companies use to mask tense situations ranging from a board becoming dissatisfied with the CEO’s performance to an outright coup forcing executives into retirement.

在很多案例中，董事会内部的纷争是商业记者最感兴趣的故事素材。高管和董事也是人，他们的性格难免会发生冲突。这些性格差异往往会影响公司的运营，公司也会呈现出高管们的个人风格和行事方式。仅根据新闻稿或文件中的辞职信息撰写的报道，可能只是更大故事的开始，后续还会涉及诸多其他问题，比如谁将接替被罢免的高管，以及该董事会成员为何离开。

<!--en-->
In many cases, boardroom intrigue is one of the most fascinating stories for a business reporter. Executives and directors are only human, and they have personalities that can clash. These personalities often drive a company, which takes on the personal styles and mannerisms of its executives. Writing a story about a resignation from a news release or a filing may just be the beginning of a bigger story that delves into a number of other issues, such as who will replace the deposed executive or why the board member left.

富有好奇心的记者在阅读CEO离职相关的8-K文件说明时，应该会产生进一步了解该高管工作表现的兴趣。事实上，《坦帕论坛报》关于某CEO辞职的报道就暗示，背后其实存在着不为人知的复杂情况：

<!--en-->
An enterprising reporter reading the 8-K explanation of a CEO’s departure should become curious enough to want to find out more about the executive’s performance. In fact, the following story from the *Tampa Tribune* about the resignation of a CEO implies that more than meets the eye was going on behind the scenes:

> 最近，热带运动服装国际公司首席执行官威廉·康普顿宣布辞职，这一事件引发了关于上市公司应向监管机构和股东披露多少信息的疑问。企业治理专家表示，虽然无需公开企业内部的所有事务，但必须向证券交易委员会报告“重大事件”。特拉华大学企业治理中心主任、前海湾波特斯特森大学法学院教授查尔斯·埃尔森指出，这意味着要披露“合理投资者在做出投资决策时会认为重要的信息”。对于重大事件，相关文件需在事件发生月份的月底后10天内以8-K表格的形式提交，同时还需向公司股票交易的证券交易所提交类似文件。在热带运动服装公司的案例中，该公司在康普顿辞职的次日，即11月19日提交了8-K表格，其中披露了康普顿的辞职情况，以及他的离职补偿协议，还有一份公司新闻稿称，康普顿是在“董事会一个委员会对近期与他会面相关的管理问题进行审查后”同意辞职的。该新闻稿并未详细说明导致康普顿离职的管理问题，仅表示这些问题“并非公司整体性问题，也不会导致公司财务报表的任何调整或重述”。多年来，法院根据具体案件不断细化了何为重大事件以及何种信息必须披露的标准。罗德岛州普罗维登斯的阿德勒·波洛克&希恩律师事务所证券法合伙人、曾任美国证券交易委员会新英格兰地区主管的威利斯·里奇奥表示，这“给公司在决定需报告哪些内容时留下了很大的自主空间”。里奇奥称：“他们可以基于诚信原则，判断所发生的事情是否属于需要披露的重大事件。”他同时指出，国会推出的各项改革，包括近期通过的《萨班斯-奥克斯利法案》，很可能会缩短企业进行信息披露的时间。如果企业获得了有关重大事件的新的重要信息，还有义务对已提交的文件进行补充。“很明确的是，一旦他们发表声明，就必须在所有关键方面都准确无误，”埃尔森说道。除了阐明必须披露的内容外，这篇报道还提出了一个疑问：康普顿为何离开热带运动服装公司？显然，许多投资者都希望得到这个问题的答案，因此这也是记者应当询问的问题。在其他情况下，相关文件可能会揭示董事会想要解雇高管的具体原因，正如《丹佛邮报》的以下报道中所描述的这家科罗拉多州公司的情形：本周提交给证券交易委员会的几位董事的辞职信显示，由于该公司长期存在的会计问题，这些阿勒帕霍县的科技公司董事建议公司的高层管理人员辞职。周三接受《丹佛邮报》采访的激光技术公司首席执行官大卫·威廉姆斯称，大家都在过度反应一个问题——这个问题是由于一笔交易被记入1993财年，但实际上可能应记入1994财年而引发的。1月11日的辞职信中表示，在公司全体董事会拒绝这些建议后，理查德·B·塞福德、R·詹姆斯·林奇和威廉·R·卡尔退出了激光技术公司的董事会。 这家生产激光速度与距离测量设备的公司本周提交了相关文件，作为对其8-K表格的修订。这三位董事的建议源于他们从10月开始对公司会计处理方式的调查。根据这些文件中的建议，威廉姆斯、首席财务官帕梅拉·塞维、董事H·德沃思·威廉姆斯以及秘书兼董事丹·N·格罗特都应辞职。文件还要求大卫·威廉姆斯“支付其欠公司的所有款项（如有）”，公司应从外部聘请新的首席执行官和首席财务官，同时Laser应立即聘请一家独立于公司任何高管和董事的知名会计事务所。当被问及是否最终会辞职时，威廉姆斯表示：“今天不会。”这是Laser持续动荡的最新进展，而这场动荡始于12月21日，当时该公司的会计事务所——总部位于芝加哥的BDO Seidman——退出了工作，并声明不再对1993至1997财年的Laser财务报表进行审计。自12月22日起，Laser的股票便不再在美国证券交易所交易。[^1340]：³ 摘自G. Haber所著《企业披露信息基于其对投资者的相关性》，2002年12月10日，《坦帕论坛报》第4版。版权所有2002年《坦帕论坛报》，经许可转载。114 • 公司新闻报道的方方面面 威廉姆斯告诉《邮报》，这场争议的核心是一笔被记入1993财年的销售交易，但实际上可能应计入1994财年。他拒绝透露细节。“如果不做大量解释的话，我很难深入讨论这个问题，可惜我无法这么做，”威廉姆斯说。然而，当这一情况对Laser造成困扰时，BDO Seidman向美国证券交易委员会表示：“EDO已收到一些信息，表明他们不能再依赖管理层的陈述。”虽然赛福德周三拒绝对此发表评论，但他表示仍坚持自己辞职信中的说法。卡尔也拒绝置评，林奇则无法联系上。赛福德、林奇和卡尔在10月组建了一个特别审计委员会，开始调查Laser的会计处理方式。这三位董事各自聘请了法律顾问、会计事务所和临时首席财务官，他们都直接向特别委员会汇报。BDO Seidman在调查进行期间退出了。股票交易随之停止，特别委员会继续工作，并于1月7日向董事会全体成员建议，仅让威廉姆斯和塞维留任到找到新首席执行官和首席财务官为止，同时要求威廉姆斯支付其欠公司的任何款项。威廉姆斯称，“是否存在公司欠我钱的问题，或者我是否可能欠公司少量款项”，都源于那笔有争议的销售交易。他说，问题只是记账上的误解，而非舞弊行为。“我不会说这是个小问题，但它确实被夸大成了大问题，其实并没有一些人想象的那么严重，”他说。威廉姆斯表示，无论是会计纠纷还是近一个月的股票交易暂停，都没有对公司业务产生负面影响。“业务进展顺利，公司状况很好，”他说。尽管1993年和1994年的财务数据可能会被重新表述，但他称公司在这五年期间的整体业务规模数据仍然是准确的。他还表示，公司最近公布的截至1998年6月30日的九个月净利润为738,508美元，即每股15美分，销售额为810万美元，这一数据是准确的；同时公司预计截至9月30日的整年销售额将达到1170万美元，这一预测也同样准确。 威廉姆斯表示，激光公司上周仍聘请了琼斯、詹森合伙事务所作为新审计师，希望能在两三周内整理好账目，之后便可恢复交易。⁴ [^1355]：⁴ 摘自L. Kokmen和E. Hubler于1999年1月21日发表在《丹佛邮报》上的文章《呼吁激光科技公司高管离职》，版权所有1999年《丹佛邮报》，经许可转载。《公司新闻故事的内幕与细节》•115 董事会成员与高管之间发生冲突可能有多种原因。公司盈利可能未达到董事会的预期；或者CEO和总裁的管理风格令其他员工不满，从而降低士气并损害公司业绩，因为员工缺乏改善业务的动力。高管也可能有理由对董事会成员感到不满。可口可乐公司的CEO道格·艾维斯特在任职仅两年后便于1999年离开公司，因为他觉得董事会干预了他的管理权。由于高管负责公司的日常运营，他们可能比董事会更清楚公司需要什么。无论哪种情况，关注高管层与董事会之间的此类分歧都是明智的，即便这些内容并未在8-K文件中披露。无论公司规模大小，内部纷争都可能演变成关于企业控制权的精彩故事，往往会成为商业版中最受关注的报道。只要记者知道该查找什么，就能从8-K文件中找到相关线索。许多投资者——也就是读者——想知道解雇一名高管的成本是多少。在某些情况下，8-K文件会提供详细信息；如果没有，第10章将详细介绍的下一份委托书则可能提供相关数据。以下摘录展示了《劳德代尔堡太阳哨兵报》如何报道一家公司解雇首席运营官的代价：总部位于劳德代尔堡的招聘巨头Spherion Corp.周二宣布，将在本财年早些时候已核销的6.92亿美元基础上，再核销2.5亿至3亿美元的收购商誉价值。在同一公告中，Spherion称首席运营官罗伯特·利沃尼乌斯已离开公司，这一变动将导致公司在第四季度再承担350万美元的费用。Spherion在股市开盘前向证券交易委员会提交了8-K报告，披露了这两件事。该公司的股价收盘下跌42美分，至6.21美元。公司发言人帕特里夏·约翰逊表示，取消利沃尼乌斯的职位是为了减少管理层级、简化组织结构。利沃尼乌斯自1991年起就在该公司工作，1997年在前任CEO雷蒙德·马西的领导下被任命为执行副总裁兼首席运营官。他的年薪为495,000美元外加期权，是公司中仅次于首席执行官的第二高薪高管。公司将为他提供350万美元的遣散费。CEO兼总裁辛达·A·霍尔曼在关于利沃尼乌斯离任的声明中表示，她将直接负责业务运营。“我们衷心感谢鲍勃为公司做出的诸多贡献，并祝愿他未来一切顺利，”她补充道。⁵ [^1368]：⁵ 摘自J. Fleischer Tamen于2003年1月8日发表在《南佛罗里达太阳哨兵报》上的文章《Spherion核销2.5亿美元商誉；为削减成本取消首席运营官职位》，版权所有2003年《南佛罗里达太阳哨兵报》，经许可转载。116 • 《公司新闻故事的内幕与细节》上述示例第二段中提到的费用实际上意味着该高管获得了350万美元才同意离职。过高的离职补偿常常遭到投资者和高管薪酬专家的批评。 此类披露信息应当被报道，因为公司的投资者和员工希望了解公司是否在明智地花钱。因此，报道此类事件的商界记者应查明：由于解雇该高管，公司所获得的好处是否超过了相应的遣散费。

<!--en-->
> The recently announced resignation of Tropical Sportswear International Corp. Chief Executive Officer William Compton raises the question of how much publicly traded companies are required to disclose to regulators and shareholders.
> Although they don’t have to disclose everything that goes on within the business, companies must notify the Securities and Exchange Commission of “material events,” corporate governance experts said.
> That means disclosing information “a reasonable investor would deem important in making an investment decision,” said Charles Elson, director of the University of Delaware’s Center for Corporate Governance and a former professor at Stetson University College of Law in Gulfport. In the case of a material event, the filing, on a document known as Form 8-K, must be made within 10 days after the close of the month in which the event occurred. A similar filing must also be made with the stock exchange on which the company’s shares are traded.
> In Tropical Sportswear’s case, the company filed a Form 8-K on Nov. 19, the day after Compton’s resignation.
> It disclosed Compton’s resignation and included his severance agreement and a company press release announcing that Compton had agreed to resign “following a review by a committee of the board of directors of recent management issues related to Mr. Compton.”
> The release did not elaborate on the management issues leading to Compton’s departure other than to say they were “not systemic to the company and will not result in any adjustments to or restatements of the company’s financial statements.”
> The definition of what is material, and required to be disclosed, has been refined by the courts over the years on a case-by-case basis.
> It “leaves a lot of latitude in the judgment of the company” about what it must report, said Willis Riccio, a securities law partner with Adler Pollock & Sheehan in Providence, R.I., and a former New England regional administrator for the SEC.
The Ins and Outs of Company News Stories • 113
"They can make a good-faith judgment about whether what has occurred is material, in terms of disclosure" Riccio said.
Reforms in Congress, including the recently enacted Sarbanes-Oxley Act, are likely to shorten the amount of time companies have to make disclosures, Riccio noted.
Companies also have a continuing duty to supplement their filings if they obtain important new information about a material event.
"What is clear, is that when they say something, it has to be correct in all material respects," Elson said.³
In addition to explaining what must be disclosed, this story raises the question of why Compton left Tropical Sportswear. It is a question that many investors would obviously like to have answered; thus, it is a good question for reporters to be asking. Other times, the filing may show the specific reasons why board members want to get rid of executives, as was the case with this Colorado-based company in the following story from the *Denver Post*:
Three directors of an Arapahoe County technology company recommended that the company's top managers resign as a result of long-term accounting problems in the firm, according to the directors' letters of resignation, filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission this week.
Laser Technology Inc.'s chief executive officer, David Williams, who spoke to *The Denver Post* on Wednesday, said everyone's overreacting to a problem caused when a sale was logged as having occurred in the 1993 fiscal year but possibly should have been recorded in fiscal 1994. He wouldn't give details,
Richard B. Sayford, R. James Lynch and William R. Carr quit the board of Laser Technology after the company's full board of directors rejected the recommendations, the Jan. 11 letters said. The company, which makes laser speed- and distance-measuring devices, filed the letters this week as an amendment to its form 8-K. The three directors' proposals came out of their investigation, begun in October, into the company's accounting practices.
The recommendations, according to the letters, called for the resignations of Williams, Chief Financial Officer Pamela Sevy, Director H. DeWorth Williams and Secretary and Director Dan N. Grothe.
They also stated that David Williams "pay all amounts, if any, that are due from him to the company," that the company hire a new CEO and CFO from outside the company, and that Laser immediately retain a reputable accounting firm that's independent from any of the company's officers and directors.
Asked if he planned eventually to resign, Williams said: "Not today."
It's the latest installment of Laser's turmoil, which began when the company's accounting firm, Chicago-based BDO Seidman, quit Dec. 21 anddisclaimed its audits of Laser's financial statements for fiscal years 1993 through 1997. Laser's stock has not traded on the American Stock Exchange since Dec. 22.
[^1340]: ³ From "Firms base disclosure on relevance to investors," by G. Haber, December 10, 2002, *Tampa Tribune*, p. 4. Copyright 2002 by *Tampa Tribune*. Reprinted with permission.
114 • The Ins and Outs of Company News Stories
At the heart of the dispute, Williams told *The Post*, is a sale that was logged as having occurred in the 1993 fiscal year but possibly should have been recorded in fiscal 1994. He wouldn't give details.
"It's difficult for me to get into that without going into a lot of explanation, which unfortunately I can't do," Williams said.
When it stopped working for Laser, however, BDO Seidman told the SEC, "Information has come to EDO's attention which indicates that they can no longer rely on management's representations."
While Sayford declined to comment Wednesday on the situation, he said he stands by the statements in his letter of resignation. Carr declined comment and Lynch could not be reached.
Sayford, Lynch and Carr formed a Special Audit Committee in October to begin investigating Laser's accounting practices. The three directors brought in their own legal counsel, accounting firm and interim CFO, all of whom reported directly to the special committee.
BDO Seidman quit in the midst of the investigation.
Trading in the stock halted and the special committee continued its work, recommending to the full board on Jan. 7 that Williams and Sevy be retained only long enough to find a new CEO and CFO, and that Williams pay what—if anything—he owes the company.
"There is an issue as to whether the company owes me some money or whether I would potentially owe the company a small amount of money" stemming from the disputed sale, Williams said.
The matter in question is a bookkeeping misunderstanding, he said, not malfeasance.
"I wouldn't say it's a small issue, but it's an issue that has kind of blown up into a big deal and it's not as big an issue as some people would think that it is," he said.
Neither the accounting dispute nor the nearly month-long trading halt has had a negative impact on the company's business, Williams said. "Business is proceeding well. The company is doing very well," he said.
Though the company's results for 1993 and 1994 may end up being restated, Williams said the aggregate amount of business the company reported for the entire five-year period remains accurate. He also said the company's recent announcement of net income of $738,508, or 15 cents per share, on sales of $8.1 million for the nine months ended June 30, 1998, is accurate, as is its prediction of record sales of $11.7 million for the full year ended September 30.
Laser retained the firm Jones, Jensen & Co. as new auditors last week and hopes to have its books in order in two or three weeks, Williams said, after which trading could resume.⁴
[^1355]: ⁴ From "Laser Technology execs' exit urged," by L. Kokmen and E. Hubler, January 21, 1999, *Denver Post*, p. Cl. Copyright 1999 by *The Denver Post*. Reprinted with permission.
The Ins and Outs of Company News Stories • 115
Clashes between board members and executives can occur for several reasons. The company may not be making as much money as the board expects. Or the CEO and president may be running the company with a style that upsets other employees, lowering morale and hurting the company's performance because the workers have no incentive to better the business. Executives may also have reasons to be upset with board members. Coca-Cola CEO Doug Ivester left the top spot at the company in 1999 after only two years on the job because he felt board members interfered with his ability to run the company. Because executives run the company on a day-to-day basis, they may have a better feel than the board for what the company needs.
In either case, it is wise to watch for such disagreements between the executive suite and the boardroom, even if they are not events disclosed in an 8-K. Infighting, no matter what size the company, can turn into a gripping story about the control of a business that often becomes the best-read story in the business section. The clues can be found in 8-K filings as long as the reporter knows what to look for.
Many investors—and therefore readers—want to know the price of getting rid of an executive. In some cases, the 8-K provides the details. If not, the next proxy statement, discussed in more detail in Chapter 10, could provide the information.
The following excerpt shows how a story in the *Sun-Sentinel* in Fort Lauderdale handled the price of a company getting rid of its chief operating officer:
Fort Lauderdale-based staffing and recruitment giant Spherion Corp. said Tuesday it will write off an additional $250 million to $300 million for the value of goodwill in acquisitions—on top of the $692 million it wrote off earlier in the fiscal year.
In the same announcement, Spherion said Chief Operating Officer Robert Livonius has left the company, a departure that will cause the company to take an additional $3.5 million charge in the fourth quarter.
Spherion filed an 8-K report with the Securities Exchange Commission disclosing both events before the market's opening. Its stock closed down 42 cents at $6.21.
Company spokeswoman Patricia Johnson said Livonius' position was eliminated in an effort to reduce layers of management and to flatten the organization. Livonius had been with the company since 1991 and was appointed executive vice president and COO in 1997 under former CEO Raymond Marcy.
Livonius, with an annual salary of $495,000 plus options, was the second highest paid executive in the organization, after the chief executive. The company will give him a $3.5 million severance agreement.
CEO and President Cinda A. Hallman said in a statement on Livonius' departure that she will assume direct responsibility for business operations.
"We sincerely appreciate Bob's many contributions to the company and wish him well in the future," she added.⁵
[^1368]: ⁵ From "Spherion taking $250 m goodwill charge; COO post eliminated to cut costs," by J. Fleischer Tamen, January 8, 2003, *South Florida Sun-Sentinel*, p. 10. Copyright 2003 by *South Florida Sun-Sentinel*. Reprinted with permission.
116 • The Ins and Outs of Company News Stories
The charge mentioned in the second paragraph of the example above essentially states that the executive received $3.5 million to leave the company. Exorbitant pay to leave a company is often criticized by investors and executive pay experts. Disclosures like this should be reported, because investors and employees of the company want to know if it is spending money wisely. Thus, business reporters covering events such as these should find out whether the company will receive benefits totaling more than the severance package as a result of getting rid of the executive.

### 当企业与会计师发生冲突时

<!--en-->
*When Companies and Accountants Collide*

近年来，企业与其会计事务所之间的关系越来越受到关注。在安然、世界通信等公司倒闭之前，企业与其审计师之间存在着紧密的联系。企业会支付数百万美元给会计事务所，让其审核财务记录，并在向美国证券交易委员会提交的文件中出具无问题的审计报告。会计行业的职责是为投资者及其他与该公司有业务往来的各方提供一定的安心感。

<!--en-->
The relationship between a company and its accounting firm has come under increasing scrutiny in recent years. Before the collapses of Enron, WorldCom, and other companies, a company and its auditor were closely tied. A company would pay its accounting firm millions of dollars to audit its financial records and to provide a statement in its SEC filings giving it a clean bill of health. The accounting industry's role was to provide some sense of comfort to investors and others who did business with the company.

实际上，会计事务所之所以会在营收、销售额及其他财务数据方面顺从企业高管的意愿，是因为他们担心拒绝就会失去收入来源。在其他情况下，企业则向审计师隐瞒其真实的经营状况，这使得会计师几乎无法正常履行职责。

<!--en-->
What actually happened, it turns out, was that accounting firms went along with what company executives wanted as far as reporting revenues, sales, and other financial numbers because they feared losing their income if they said no. In other cases, companies hid the actual financial performance of their operations from their auditors, making it nearly impossible for the accountants to properly do their job.

尽管如此，审计师也难辞其咎。根据总部位于佛罗里达州的Weiss Ratings公司的一项研究，后来被发现有会计违规行为的公司中，超过90%都获得了会计事务所出具的无问题审计报告。Weiss的研究还显示，那些宣布存在会计问题的公司中，很少有能得到审计师表达担忧的声明。在这些公司的会计违规问题被揭露之前，它们在华尔街的市值已超过1.9万亿美元；之后，其市值又下跌了1.2万亿美元以上。这对商业记者来说是个重大新闻，也凸显出了解企业与会计师之间关系的重要性。

<!--en-->
Still, the auditors must take some blame. According to a study by Weiss Ratings, a Florida-based firm, accounting firms gave a clean bill of health to more than 90 percent of companies that later had accounting irregularities uncovered. The Weiss research also disclosed that few companies that announced accounting problems had a statement from their auditors expressing concern. These companies had a market capitalization of more than $1.9 trillion on Wall Street before their accounting irregularities were uncovered. Afterward, their value on Wall Street fell by more than $1.2 trillion. That is a huge story for business journalists and shows how important it is to understand the relationship between companies and accountants.

在这种情况下，商业记者也处于两难境地。如果连企业自身的审计师都没有被告知真相，商业记者又该如何相信企业的数据或揭露不当行为呢？为判断企业与其会计师之间的关系是否正当，记者仍需查看许多文件。最重要的是，应仔细阅读企业提交给美国证券交易委员会的10-Q和10-K文件中的审计师声明。有时，审计师的声明会提及对企业持续经营能力的担忧，这样一来，记者不仅能为明天的报纸或晚间新闻撰写报道，还能明确看出企业与其会计师之间的关系是正常的。以下摘自《圣何塞水星报》的案例便说明了审计师对企业未来表示担忧如何成为一篇新闻：这家美国最大的高速互联网服务提供商At Home因沉重的债务和运营亏损而面临破产风险，该公司在周一向美国证券交易委员会提交的更新版年度报告中如此表示。

<!--en-->
In these circumstances, business reporters are also put in a difficult position. How can a business journalist trust a company's numbers or uncover a wrongdoing if the company's own auditors are not being told the truth? There are still a number of documents that a journalist should examine to determine whether the relationship between a company and its accountants is legitimate. Most importantly, the reporter should review the accountant's statement in a company's 10-Q and 10-K filings. Sometimes the auditor's statement discusses concerns about a company's continuing ability to operate, in which case the writer has not only a story for tomorrow's newspaper or evening newscast but also a clear indication that the relationship between the company and its accountants is legitimate. The following excerpt from the *San Jose Mercury News* illustrates how an auditor statement expressing concern about the future of a company is a story:At Home, the nation's largest provider of high-speed Internet access, is at risk of being buried under its heavy debt and operating losses, the company said in an updated annual report filed Monday with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

企业新闻报道的方方面面 • 117 这家曾是互联网经济领域佼佼者的红木城公司称，审计师安永对其作为“持续经营企业”的能力表达了“重大疑虑”。

<!--en-->
The Ins and Outs of Company News Stories • 117
The Redwood City company, once a high-flying player in the Internet economy, said auditors Ernst & Young have expressed “substantial doubt” about its ability to continue as a “going concern.”

周一，At Home的股价下跌了近一半，从每股47美分降至46美分。

<!--en-->
Shares of At Home lost nearly half their value Monday, falling 46 cents to 47 cents a share.

这家以Excite@Home为名称运营的公司可能面临从纳斯达克股市摘牌的风险，届时将不得不向其可转换债券持有人支付1亿美元。分析人士指出，截至6月30日，At Home仅有1.834亿美元的现金，若必须支付这笔款项，很快就会资金耗尽并被迫申请破产。

<!--en-->
The company, which does business as Excite@Home, faces a possible delisting from the NASDAQ stock market, which would trigger a $100 million payment to its convertible bondholders. With only $183.4 million in cash as of June 30, At Home would soon run out of money and be forced to declare bankruptcy if it had to make the payment, analysts said.

6月，At Home通过可转换债券从两家专门为陷入困境的企业提供融资的投资机构那里获得了1亿美元的关键资金支持。该笔交易要求该公司必须继续在某个主要证券交易所上市。

<!--en-->
In June, At Home obtained through a convertible bond a crucial $100 million injection from two investment firms that specialize in financing struggling companies. That deal included a requirement that the company stay listed on one of the major stock exchanges.

目前，At Home未能满足纳斯达克要求的持续上市最低标准。其股价已跌至3美元以下，这一数值低于纳斯达克规定允许的最低买入价。At Home的发言人艾莉森·鲍曼表示，该公司尚未收到纳斯达克的退市通知。⁶ 阅读审计师的报告始终非常重要，尤其是当该公司近年来一直处于亏损状态时。大多数公司都能从会计师那里获得无问题的审计报告，因此一旦报告对该公司提出质疑，便属于重大事件。另一些公司则会收到有保留意见的审计报告，这通常意味着该公司的财务账目存在问题。此外，如果会计师对公司的未来生存能力存疑，记者应查看10-K或10-Q文件中的报告内容，看相关表述是否有所变化。如果有变化——无论好坏——那么就有必要撰写一篇更新该公司状况的报道。当出现此类持续关注声明时，可能会像下文《丹佛邮报》报道的波士顿炸鸡案那样，通过8-K表格进行披露：

<!--en-->
At Home currently fails to meet NASDAQ's minimum requirements for continued listing. Its stock price has dropped below $3, the lowest bid price allowed under one of NASDAQ's standards. Alison Bowman, an At Home spokeswoman, said the company has not received a delisting notice from NASDAQ.⁶
It is always important to read the auditor's statement, particularly if the company has been losing money for the last few years. Most companies receive a clean bill of health from their accountants, so it is a major development when the statement raises questions about the company. Other companies receive qualified opinions, which typically means the company's financial books are not up to par. In addition, if its accountants question a company's future viability, reporters should check the statements in the 10-K or 10-Q to see if the language in the statement has changed. If it has—for better or worse—then a story updating the company's condition is likely warranted. When the ongoing concern statement is made, it may be filed in an 8-K, as in the case of Boston Chicken, disclosed in the following *Denver Post* story:

波士顿炸鸡公司的审计师已向美国证券交易委员会提交一份声明，称该连锁餐厅“极有可能”无法继续经营。

<!--en-->
Boston Chicken Inc.'s auditor has filed a statement with the federal Securities and Exchange Commission saying there is “substantial doubt” that the restaurant chain can stay in business.

这份日期为5月19日、周三提交的SEC文件中，审计机构安达信有限责任合伙公司详细阐述了波士顿炸鸡的财务困境。

<!--en-->
In the SEC document, dated May 19 and filed Wednesday, auditor Arthur Andersen LLP gives a detailed account of Boston Chicken's financial woes.

审计师指出，波士顿炸鸡的财务问题可能导致数亿美元债务的违约。文件中表示，无法“保证”该公司能够“履行其财务义务”。在8-K表格中，安达信称其在1997年的审计报告中加入了一段内容，指出“对（波士顿炸鸡）作为持续经营实体的能力存在极大疑虑。”[^1386]：⁶ 来自J. Kwan所写的《At Home警告称可能面临资金短缺》，发表于2001年8月21日的《圣何塞水星报》第1C版。版权所有2001年《圣何塞水星报》，保留所有权利。经许可转载。

<!--en-->
The auditor describes how Boston Chicken's money problems could trigger default on hundreds of millions of dollars in debt. There can be “no assurance,” the document says, that the company will be able to “meet itsfinancial obligations.” On the 8-K form, Arthur Andersen says it has included a paragraph in its 1997 audit report that “there is substantial doubt about (Boston Chicken’s) ability to continue as a going concern.”
[^1386]: ⁶ From “At Home warns it may run out of cash,” by J. Kwan, August 21, 2001, *San Jose Mercury News*, p. 1C. Copyright 2001 by *San Jose Mercury News*. All rights reserved. Reprinted with permission.

118 • 公司新闻报道的方方面面 安达信在对波士顿炸鸡的特许经营者——即区域开发商——的评估中也包含了同样的表述。负责为这些特许经营者进行审计的安达信，也对每家特许经营者“作为持续经营实体”的能力提出了质疑。

<!--en-->
118 • The Ins and Outs of Company News Stories
The same statement is included in Arthur Andersen’s assessment of Boston Chicken’s franchisees—called area developers. Andersen, the company that also audited each of the franchisees, questions each franchisee’s ability to continue “as a going concern.”

8-K是一种上市公司向SEC提交的表格，用于报告可能影响其财务状况或股票价值的各类事件。

<!--en-->
An 8-K is a form a publicly held company files with the SEC to report on any events that might affect its financial situation or the value of its shares of stock.

据全国性审计机构毕马威·皮特·马威克的一位合伙人所说，审计师在财务审计中加入“持续经营”相关表述是“非常严重的”行为。⁷ 商业记者最好还能咨询了解该公司运营情况的供应商、竞争对手及政府机构。竞争对手往往能察觉到其他公司是否遇到困难或正在失去市场份额。在报道许多公司时，供应商是尤为重要的信息来源，因为他们可以告知该公司是否按时支付账单。如果一家公司延迟付款，这可能表明存在审计师尚未发现或在文件中未提及的财务问题。此外还应查看是否有诉讼案件，以判断该公司是否因拒付款项而面临诉讼。

<!--en-->
An auditor’s inclusion of the “going concern” statement in a financial audit is “serious,” according to a partner at KPMG Peat Marwick, a national auditing firm.⁷
It is also wise for a business reporter to check with the suppliers, competitors, and government agencies who know a company’s operations. Competitors often know if another company is experiencing difficulty or losing market share. In writing about many companies, suppliers are particularly important sources because they can tell you if the company pays its bills on time. If a company pays late, that may be an indication that there are financial problems that the accountants have not uncovered or mentioned in the filings. One should also look for lawsuits to see if a company is being sued for nonpayment.

有时，SEC会针对那些涉嫌虚报财务问题的公司展开调查或采取行动。SEC的调查结果可能会通过8-K表格或10-K、10-Q等文件公开。

<!--en-->
Sometimes, the SEC initiates investigations or actions against companies that it believes may have improperly stated financial problems. The results of SEC actions can be disclosed in 8-Ks or filings such as the 10-K or 10-Q.

以下是彭博新闻社报道某公司账目审查情况的一个示例：

<!--en-->
The following is an example of how Bloomberg News reported the disclosure of a look into a company’s books:

阿尔法制药公司表示，美国证券交易委员会已开始对其收入确认方式展开正式调查。该公司的股价下跌了13%，从27.5美元降至17.90美元。

<!--en-->
Alpharma Inc. said the Securities and Exchange Commission has begun a formal investigation of the company’s methods for recognizing revenue. Alpharma shares declined 13 percent, falling $2.75 to $17.90.

这家位于新泽西州福特李市的仿制药及动物保健产品制造商去年11月重新公布了其盈利数据。根据向SEC提交的文件，此次调查涉及与数据重述相关的两项收入确认做法。

<!--en-->
The Fort Lee, New Jersey, manufacturer of generic drugs and animal health products last November restated its earnings. The investigation, reported in a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, involves two revenue recognition practices connected with the restatement.

该公司今日称，股东们曾在集体诉讼中指控其在巴西的动物保健业务中采用了不当的收入确认政策。新泽西地区美国地方法院已驳回了该集体诉讼。

<!--en-->
Shareholders had alleged in a class action lawsuit that the company used improper revenue recognition policies in regard to its animal health business in Brazil. The U.S. District Court for the District of New Jersey dismissed the class action suit, the company reported today.

阿尔法制药公司在10月表示，由于部分动物产品的销售是在确认订单时而非实际发货时才入账，因此将修改其盈利报表。该公司此前称，这一问题已在去年第三季度得到解决。

<!--en-->
Alpharma in October said it would revise its earnings statements because some sales of animal products were billed when the orders were recognized, not when they were actually shipped. The problem was corrected by the third quarter of last year, the company had said.

Alpharma在11月重新公布了2001年上半年的业绩，净收入增长了59%，达到3570万美元，这一数值低于此前三年报告的数字。[^1399]：⁷ 来自P. Parker于1998年5月29日发表在《丹佛邮报》A1版的文章《Boston Chicken的困境日益严重》，版权归《丹佛邮报》所有，经许可转载。

<!--en-->
Alpharma in November restated earnings to report 59 percent more netincome, or $35.7 million, for the first half of 2001, and lower earnings than reported for the previous three years.
[^1399]: ⁷ From “Boston Chicken woes mount,” by P. Parker, May 29, 1998, *The Denver Post*, p. A1. Copyright 1998 by *The Denver Post*. Reprinted with permission.

公司新闻报道的方方面面 • 119 Alpharma称2000年的净收入为5550万美元，而非之前报告的6110万美元；1999年的实际盈利为2990万美元，比报告的数字少700万美元；1998年的盈利则为2280万美元，而之前报告的是2420万美元。一旦监管机构批准启动正式调查，工作人员便有权要求提供相关资料。

<!--en-->
The Ins and Outs of Company News Stories • 119
Net income in 2000 was $55.5 million, Alpharma said, not $61.1 million as it had reported. In 1999, the company earned $29.9 million, $7 million less than reported, and in 1998, it earned $22.8 million. It had reported $24.2 million for that year. Once the commission approves the opening of a formal examination, staff members have the authority to subpoena information.

根据相关文件，Alpharma预计会配合SEC的调查。⁸ 这类调查可能会迫使企业重新公布财务数据，从而降低其营收或利润。一旦出现这种情况，企业实际上就是在承认自己的会计工作存在问题。不过投资者对此并不会感到满意，他们通常会抛售该公司的股票，导致股价下跌。正因如此，财经记者应始终留意企业财务报表中可能存在的任何异常迹象。率先报道相关调查或问题的记者，能为读者提供极大的帮助。

<!--en-->
Alpharma anticipates cooperating with the SEC investigation, according to the filing.⁸
An investigation like this can lead a company to restate its financial results, lowering its revenue or its earnings. When this happens, a company is essentially admitting that its accountants fooled. However, investors are not humored by the event. They will usually dump the stock, sending its price downward. That is why a business reporter should always be on the lookout for any hint of impropriety in a company's financial statements. The writer who is first to report an investigation or a problem does his or her readers a great service.

早前“强制披露”部分提到，企业在与审计师解除合作关系时必须提交8-K文件。需要特别强调的是，企业解雇审计师或审计师拒绝继续为该公司服务，往往是未来可能出现问题的重要信号。（例外情况是像安达信这样的会计事务所倒闭，导致其所有原有客户都必须寻找新的审计师来审核账目。）8-K文件往往会披露企业与会计师之间存在分歧，才导致了合作关系破裂；有时则不会说明具体原因。这仍是一件值得关注的重要事件，记者应密切跟踪，并可能联系消息来源以查明更换审计师的真实原因。

<!--en-->
Earlier, the “Required Disclosures” section mentioned that companies must file an 8-K when they part ways with auditors. It cannot be emphasized enough that a company firing an auditor or an auditor declining to work with a company is one of the best indicators that there may be some future problems. (An exception to this is when an accounting firm such as Arthur Andersen goes out of business, forcing all of its former clients to find a new auditor to review its books.) Often, the 8-K discloses that there was a disagreement between the company and its accountants that led to the parting. Other times, a reason is not given. It is still an important event, one that a reporter should watch closely and perhaps even call sources to determine the real reason for the switch.

下面这篇来自《坦帕论坛报》的报道详细介绍了某家破产企业如何在破产法庭上选择新的审计师。报道暗示，选择新审计师是为了能从新的角度审视该企业的财务状况：

<!--en-->
A story from the *Tampa Tribune* below details how a company in bankruptcy court picked a new auditor. The story implies that the new auditor was selected to provide a fresh look at the company's financial situation:

Anchor Glass Container Corp.已解聘安达信作为其独立公共会计师，但表示这一决定与安达信近期的麻烦无关。

<!--en-->
Anchor Glass Container Corp. has dismissed Andersen as its independent public accountant but said the decision has nothing to do with Andersen's recent troubles.

证券交易委员会的记录显示，这一损失使得安达信失去了这家2001年向其支付了503,000美元服务费的坦帕湾客户。

<!--en-->
The loss deprives Andersen of a Tampa Bay client that paid $503,000 in fees in 2001, Securities and Exchange Commission records show.

根据4月15日提交的SEC 8-K文件，Anchor在2002年聘请了普华永道。

<!--en-->
Anchor retained PricewaterhouseCoopers for 2002, according to an SEC 8-K filing April 15.

“这与安达信毫无关系；即便没有这些情况，我们也会这么做，”Anchor Glass的首席财务官Dale Buckwalter说道。“这反映出我们有新的所有者以及新的律师事务所，”坦帕的Carlton Fields补充说。

<!--en-->
“It has nothing to do with Andersen; we would have done this regardless,” said Dale Buckwalter, chief financial officer for Anchor Glass. “It reflects we have a new owner and a new law firm,” Carlton Fields in Tampa.

SEC的文件指出，Anchor的董事会是在4月11日做出这一决定的。

<!--en-->
The SEC filing states Anchor's board made the decision April 11.

SEC的文件中表示：“在会计原则或实务、财务报表披露以及审计范围或程序等方面，我们与安达信之间不存在任何分歧。”[^1412]：⁸ 来自M. Weiss于2002年6月3日发表在彭博新闻上的文章《Alpharma称SEC正在调查其营收方式》，版权归彭博社所有，保留所有权利，经许可转载。

<!--en-->
“There were no disagreements with Arthur Andersen on any matter ofaccounting principle or practice, financial statement disclosure or auditing scope or procedure,” the SEC filing states.
[^1412]: ⁸ From “Alpharma says SEC investigating its revenue methods” by M. Weiss, June 3, 2002, Bloomberg News. Copyright 2002 by Bloomberg L.P. All rights reserved. Reprinted with permission.

120 • 公司新闻报道的方方面面 公司官员称，由于母公司总部位于多伦多的Consumers Packing Inc.申请了破产保护，Anchor不得不在4月15日申请破产保护。

<!--en-->
120 • The Ins and Outs of Company News Stories
Anchor was forced to file for protection from bankruptcy April 15 because its parent company, Toronto-based Consumers Packing Inc., filed for bankruptcy protection, company officials said.

Anchor的首席运营官Richard M. Deneau上周表示，这家总部位于坦帕的子公司的生意状况是二十年来最好的。获得Anchor业务合作的普华永道是坦帕湾规模最大的会计事务所。

<!--en-->
Business at the Tampa-based subsidiary is the best it’s been in two decades, Anchor Chief Operating Officer Richard M. Deneau said last week. PricewaterhouseCoopers, which gains Anchor’s business, is the largest accounting firm in Tampa Bay.

“显然，Anchor Glass对我们来说是一家规模庞大且重要的客户，”普华永道中佛罗里达业务部的办公室管理合伙人Andrew McAdams说道。

<!--en-->
“Obviously, Anchor Glass is a large and important client for us,” said Andrew McAdams, office managing partner for PricewaterhouseCoopers’ Central Florida practice.

在3月14日的起诉书中，联邦大陪审团指控安达信在Enron Corp.财务危机期间销毁了大量纸质文件并删除了电脑文件。⁹ 随着人们对企业与其会计师之间关系的关注度不断提高，许多人希望审计师能在审查客户财务报表时更加谨慎。这样的发展或许会让更多审计师公开披露企业存在的问题。

<!--en-->
In an indictment March 14, a federal grand jury accused Andersen of destroying “tons of paper” and deleting computer files in the financial collapse of Enron Corp.⁹
With the increasing scrutiny of the relationships between companies and accountants, many hope that auditors will become more vigilant in reviewing the financial statements of their clients. Such a development could lead to more auditors making disclosures about problems at companies.

美国证券交易委员会似乎在以下两方面采取了更为强硬的立场：(a)审查审计师与公司之间的业务往来；(b)对那些行为可能影响其作为审计师独立性的会计师处以罚款并予以谴责。对商业记者而言，另一项可能很有价值的举措是加强公司董事会中审计委员会权力的措施。审计委员会负责审查公司与其外部会计师之间的关系。许多公司会从与之有业务往来的会计事务所聘请首席财务官，一些研究企业治理的专家曾批评过这种关系。

<!--en-->
The SEC appears to be taking a more aggressive stance in (a) reviewing business dealings between auditors and companies, and (b) fining and censuring accountants whose dealings call into question their independence as auditors. Another important step that could prove valuable for business reporters is a measure designed to increase the clout of the auditing committee on a company’s board of directors. The auditing committee reviews the relationship between a company and its outside accountants. Many companies hire CFOs from accounting firms with which they do business. Some reviewing corporate governance have criticized that relationship.

在公司与审计师关系方面的另一个有趣进展是，现在规模最大的公司的高管必须证明其财务报表尽可能准确无误。尽管这一要求适用于资产规模超过12亿美元的900家最大公司，但其他规模较小的公司的高管也需对其业绩数据进行确认。这意味着，公司高管现在有责任向审计师及公众提供能够真实反映公司状况的准确财务报表。

<!--en-->
One more interesting development in the relationship between companies and auditors is that executives at the largest companies are now required to certify that their financial statements are as correct and accurate as possible. Though this certification applies to the 900 largest companies, or those with more than $1.2 billion in assets, other smaller companies have also had executives attest to their results. This means that the onus is now on company executives to provide accurate financial statements that reflect the true picture of the company to auditors and the general public.

大多数公司都会尽力提供尽可能准确的财务业绩信息。但总会有少数企业为了显得比实际更好而试图突破会计规则的界限。对于商业记者来说，了解公司与其外部会计师之间的关系尤为重要，这样他们才能判断该公司是否诚实，或者是否需要进一步调查。[^1422]：⁹摘自T. Jackovics所写的《Anchor Glass解雇Anderson，继续聘用普华永道》，2002年4月23日，《坦帕论坛报》，第5页。版权所有2002年《坦帕论坛报》，经许可转载。

<!--en-->
Most companies give as accurate a picture of their financial results as possible. But there will always be a few businesses that stretch the limits of accounting rules in a bid to make themselves appear better than they actually are. The relationship between a company and its outside accountants is important to understand, particularly for the business journalist, so he or she can assess whether the business is being truthful or if it needs closer examination.
[^1422]: ⁹ From “Anchor Glass drops Anderson, retains PricewaterhouseCoopers” by T. Jackovics, April 23, 2002, *Tampa Tribune*, p. 5. Copyright 2002 by *Tampa Tribune*. Reprinted with permission.

公司新闻报道的方方面面 • 121

<!--en-->
The Ins and Outs of Company News Stories • 121

### 公平披露规则与电话会议

<!--en-->
*Regulation FD and Conference Calls*

还记得本章前面提到的MONY集团在8-K文件中披露预期收益的例子吗？该公司为何要公开此类信息？

<!--en-->
Remember the example earlier in this chapter where MONY Group disclosed its projected earnings in an 8-K filing? Why did the company disclose such information?

在提交文件前两天发布的新闻稿给出了线索。其中提到该公司将召开面向投资者和分析师的年度会议，管理层将介绍“公司及其业务部门的整体情况与未来展望”（MONY集团，2003年）。该新闻稿还指出，人们可以通过公司的网站在线收听此次会议。因此，在提交8-K文件的同时，该公司还召开了会议来讨论文件中的内容。MONY集团的这次会议、新闻稿以及8-K文件的提交，都是为了遵守2000年生效的公平披露规则（Regulation FD），该规则极大地改变了华尔街和商业媒体获取公司信息的方式。

<!--en-->
A news release issued two days before the filing provides a clue. It mentioned that the company was going to hold its annual meeting with investors and analysts and that its management team would provide an “overview and outlook for the company and its business units” (MONY Group, 2003). The release also mentioned that the meeting could be heard via the Internet from its website. So, at the same time the 8-K was filed, the company held a meeting to discuss the information in the filing. The meeting, the release, and the 8-K filing by MONY Group were done to comply with a set of SEC rules called Regulation Fair Disclosure (Regulation FD) that went into effect in 2000 and profoundly changed how Wall Street and the business media obtained information from companies.

在企业和华尔街机构的反对声中，公平披露规则得以出台，旨在为投资界创造公平的竞争环境。监管机构认为，此前有些公司会向特定的分析师和投资者提供有关自身财务表现和业务运营的信息，让这些人在信息公开给其他人之前就能买卖相关股票。公平披露规则如今禁止公司向华尔街的少数人提供信息，公司或高管必须同时向所有人公开信息。

<!--en-->
Amid opposition from companies and Wall Street firms, Regulation FD was enacted to bring a level playing field to the investment community. Regulators saw companies providing information about their financial performance and their business operations to favored analysts and investors, allowing them to trade in the company’s stock before the information was shared with others. Regulation FD now prevents companies from providing information to a select few on Wall Street. A company or executive must now provide the information to everyone at the same time.
