公司通过多种方式选择遵守公平披露规则。其中一种方式是通过提交8-K文件来披露信息；另一种方式则是通过电话会议，向任何希望通过互联网或免费电话号码收听的人介绍季度业绩或其他重要进展，这包括媒体和小型投资者。过去，公司通常只允许分析师和投资者参加这些电话会议，虽然有些公司允许记者旁听，但像安海斯-布希这样的公司则不允许。如果记者在电话会议进行期间注意到某家公司的股价上涨或下跌，他们就必须等到会议结束，再联系他们知道正在收听的分析师和投资者，以查明股价变动的原因。

<!--en-->
Companies have chosen to comply with Regulation FD in a number of ways. One of these ways has been through filing information in an 8-K. Another way has been to open conference calls discussing quarterly earnings or other important developments to anybody who wants to listen via the Internet or a toll-free telephone number. This includes the media and small-time investors. In the past, companies limited who could listen to these conference calls to analysts and investors. Although some companies allowed reporters to listen to these calls, others, such as Anheuser-Busch, did not. If a reporter noticed a company’s stock rising or falling while a conference call was ongoing, he or she would have to wait until the call was over to call analysts and investors he or she knew were listening to find out what had caused the stock to move.

商业新闻界大力支持《FD法规》。彭博新闻社撰写了大量关于那些不愿让公众广泛收听其电话会议的公司的报道。美国商业编辑与作家协会也致信支持该立法。其理由很简单：除了帮助投资者外，《FD法规》还能为记者提供更多信息。如今，记者可以收听过去只有华尔街内部人士才能接触的会议内容。虽然商业记者在会议期间并不总能提问，但他们可以利用高管、分析师和投资者之间的对话来完善报道内容，解释华尔街人士为何对某家公司的业绩感到愤怒或满意。这样一来，报道内容便更加详尽，而收听电话会议也成了商业记者日常工作中的重要环节。有些记者

<!--en-->
The business journalism community rallied strongly behind Regulation FD. Bloomberg News wrote countless stories about companies that did not allow broad access to their conference calls. The Society of American Business Editors and Writers wrote letters in support of the legislation. The reasoning was simple: In addition to helping investors, Regulation FD gave reporters more information as well. Reporters can now listen to the calls that were previously just the territory of Wall Street insiders. Though business journalists cannot always ask questions during the calls, they can use the conversations among executives, analysts, and investors to improve the content of their stories, explaining why people on Wall Street are angry or happy with a company’s performance. The result has been more detailed stories, making listening to the conference call an important part of the business journalist’s daily routine. Some reporters

#### 专业人士的经验之谈

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

路透社记者Karey Wutkowski谈SEC文件：

<!--en-->
Reuters reporter Karey Wutkowski on SEC filings:

**IPO申请规则：**通常来说，偏袒某家公司是不可取的，但一份IPO申请文件却极具吸引力。这是公司首次被迫向公众公开其内部运作情况，其中蕴含着大量信息。这份文件能让人们初步了解公司的财务历史、投资者情况、可能在未来带来问题的“风险因素”，以及任何未了结的法律问题。同时还需关注申请中关于“资金用途”的说明。如果公司打算将资金用于再投资以扩大业务规模，那就表明其前景不错；但如果大股东利用IPO套现，那很可能存在严重问题。

<!--en-->
**IPO filings rule:** Generally it’s not acceptable to pick your favorite child, but an initial public offering filing is an exciting document. It is the first time a company is forced to reveal its inner workings to the public, and it contains a treasure trove of information. The document provides the first glimpse into a company’s financial history, its investors, the “risk factors” that could pose problems down the road, and any outstanding legal matters. It is also important to pay attention to the “use of proceeds” from the offering. If a company is using the funds to reinvest in and expand the company’s operations, that indicates decent prospects. If the major shareholders are using an IPO to cash out of the company, there may be a significant underlying issue.

122 • 公司新闻报道的方方面面 在财报季期间，记者往往需要在一天内收听多场电话会议。而且大多数公司都会通过新闻稿的形式，直接向记者提供如何收听这些电话会议的信息。

<!--en-->
122 • The Ins and Outs of Company News Stories often have several conference calls to listen to in a single day, particularly during earnings season. And most companies provide information about how to access their conference calls directly to journalists in the form of releases.

有人认为，《FD法规》导致电话会议数量增加，却并未达到提供更多信息的预期效果。如今的高管们只会照着精心准备的讲稿念稿，谈论公司时不会透露任何非同寻常的信息。而跟踪该公司的知名分析师和投资者仍会在会议上提出大部分问题。许多公司还限制了单个人在会议中可提问的次数，再加上准备好的发言有时长达30分钟，而在通常仅限一小时的会议中几乎没时间回答所有问题。尤其是关于季度业绩的电话会议，如果公司的业绩与华尔街预期一致且不会在会议上公布任何意外消息，往往会极其乏味。只有那些多年来一直关注该公司的老练记者，才能通过聆听这样的会议来判断是否有新消息披露。很多时候，这类会议上的唯一新闻出现在问答环节。不过，越来越多的分析师和投资者不愿提出可能会被竞争对手听到的深入问题。那样的话，通常只有公司在会议上给出业绩指引时才有新闻价值。即便如此，公司通常也会在新闻稿或8-K文件中提前披露此类信息。此外，如果公司高管在回答会议中的问题时提供了其认为对业绩有重大影响的消息，公司日后通常会提交8-K文件。

<!--en-->
The increase in conference calls as a result of Regulation FD, some argue, has not had the intended effect of providing more information. The executives now read from carefully worded scripts and do not provide any out-of-the-ordinary information when discussing their companies. And the major analysts and investors who follow that company still ask the bulk of the questions on the call. Many companies limit the number of questions that a single person can ask during the call, and with prepared remarks sometimes lasting as long as 30 minutes, there is little time to answer all questions on a call that is usually limited to an hour. Conference calls about quarterly earnings results, in particular, can be extremely boring, especially if the company reported earnings in line with Wall Street estimates and is not expected to reveal any surprises on the call. It takes a savvy reporter who has followed a company for years to listen to such a call and determine whether there has been any news disclosed. Many times, the only news on such calls comes during the question-and-answer period. But increasingly, analysts and investors do not want to ask probing questions for their competitors to hear. Then, the news is typically if a company provides any sort of earnings guidance during its call. If that happens, the company has usually provided the news in a release and in an 8-K filing. Often, if a company executive, in answering a question on the call, provides information that the company determines is material to its performance, the company will later file an 8-K.

尽管如此，即使收听电话会议后无法写出报道，对商业记者而言仍是一次宝贵的经历。记者可以通过观察问题是带有敌意还是友好态度，来评估CEO或CFO与分析师及投资者的互动方式。问题的语气和回应能告诉记者华尔街人士对公司是满意还是不满。高管对问题的回答也能反映出他们对公司业务表现或未来前景的看法。

<!--en-->
Still, listening to conference calls can be a valuable experience for business reporters, even if the time spent on the call does not result in a story. The journalist can assess how the CEO or CFO interacts with analysts and investors by noting whether the questions are hostile or friendly. The tone of the questions and the responses can tell the reporter whether Wall Street is happy or upset with the company. How an executive responds to a question can also be an indicator of how he or she thinks the business is performing or what he or she thinks about the company's future prospects.

任何回过头去收听现已破产的能源巨头安然公司2001年第一季度业绩电话会议的人，都会听到Highfields Capital Corporation的分析师Richard Grubman与CEO Jeff Skilling之间关于为何公司未在业绩报告中同时公布资产负债表的那段对话：

<!--en-->
Anyone who went back and listened to the first-quarter 2001 earnings conference call for now-bankrupt energy giant Enron would have run across this exchange between Highfields Capital Corporation analyst Richard Grubman and CEO Jeff Skilling on why the company had not released a balance sheet along with its earnings statement:

Grubman：早上好。您能告诉我们，截至季度末，价格/风险管理方面的资产和负债情况如何？具体数值是多少？

<!--en-->
Grubman: Yes, good morning. Can you tell us what the assets and liabilities from price/risk management were at quarter-end, what those balances were?

Skilling：我们的资产负债表还没完成。很快就会搞定。

<!--en-->
Skilling: We don't have the balance sheet completed. We'll have that done shortly.

Grubman：但你是唯一一家无法提供包含盈利信息的资产负债表或现金流量表的金融机构。

<!--en-->
Grubman: But you're the only financial institution that can't produce a balance sheet or a cash flow statement with their earnings.

公司新闻背后的种种真相 • 123 Skilling：您——非常感谢，我们很感激。Grubman：不胜感激。¹⁰随后Skilling低声骂了一句脏话。不到六个月后，他便从该公司辞职，而该公司随后重新核算了盈利数据并申请破产保护。Skilling与Grubman之间那段紧张的对话，足以让任何旁听者意识到或许有人需要仔细审视安然公司的经营状况。

<!--en-->
The Ins and Outs of Company News Stories • 123
Skilling: You—thank you very much. We appreciate it.
Grubman: Appreciate it.¹⁰
Skilling then muttered an expletive. Less than six months later, he resigned from the company, which then restated its earnings and filed for bankruptcy-court protection. The tense conversation between Skilling and Grubman could have been an indicator to anyone listening that maybe someone needed to take a closer look at Enron's performance.

有时，电话会议可能会带来一些意想不到的结果。以下这篇彭博新闻报道就展示了这样一起案例：股东在电话会议上披露了公司与其首席执行官之间的利益关系。

<!--en-->
Sometimes, the conference call can provide some unintended results. The following Bloomberg News story illustrates a case in which shareholders disclosed information on a conference call about a relationship between the company and its CEO:

Insignia Financial Group Inc.的首席执行官Andrew Farkas的薪酬遭到了该房地产经纪公司两大投资者的批评，他们认为他正在以股东的利益为代价从公司合作项目中获利。

<!--en-->
Insignia Financial Group Inc. Chief Executive Andrew Farkas' compensation was criticized by two of the property broker's biggest investors, who said he is profiting from company partnerships at shareholder expense.

Third Point Partners LP的Daniel Loeb在一场电话会议上表示，那种规定Farkas在某项投资回报达标后即可获得该公司管理投资基金22%利润的安排，并不符合股东的最佳利益。

<!--en-->
An arrangement giving Farkas a 22 percent share of profits from a company managed investment fund after a certain return is met isn't in the best interests of shareholders, Daniel Loeb of Third Point Partners LP said on a conference call.

Loeb还表示，Insignia也不应为其CEO使用其个人拥有的飞机和游艇而支付95万美元的费用。他称，这些薪酬安排使得这家纽约最大规模的经纪公司Insignia/ESG部门面临股东“强烈反对”的风险，毕竟该公司的股价今年以来已下跌24美分；截至3月底，Loeb的机构持有Insignia 4.9%的股份。

<!--en-->
Insignia also shouldn't have paid Farkas $950,000 for company use of a personal plane and boat he owns, Loeb said. The compensation arrangements put Insignia, whose Insignia/ESG unit is New York's biggest broker, at risk of "a major backlash" from shareholders at a time when the company's shares are down 24 cents for the year, said Loeb, whose firm had a 4.9 percent stake in Insignia at the end of March.

“现在你的股票表现低迷，却还能赚很多钱。”Loeb在电话中对Farkas说道。

<!--en-->
"Right now you're in a position to make a lot of money while your stock is languishing," Loeb told Farkas on the call.

该公司官方拒绝立即置评。在这场旨在讨论Insignia第二季度业绩的电话会议上，Farkas称Loeb的分析“并不完全准确”。

<!--en-->
Company officials declined immediate comment. On the call, which was held to discuss Insignia's second-quarter results, Farkas said Loeb's analysis wasn't "entirely accurate."

他说：“我认为，股东的利益与管理层以及所有参与激励计划的人的利益其实是高度一致的。”

<!--en-->
I "believe that the interests of shareholders and the interests of management, including all those who participate in promote programs, are in fact very much aligned," he said.

Farkas表示，Insignia的顾问团队及薪酬委员会——该委员会由Related Cos.的董事长Stephen Ross以及前贝塔斯曼AG旗下BMG娱乐音乐部门负责人H. Strauss Zelnick组成——会定期重新评估相关“激励计划”。

<!--en-->
Insignia's counsel and compensation committee, which consists of Related Cos. Chairman Stephen Ross and H. Strauss Zelnick, former head of Bertelsmann AG's BMG Entertainment music unit, reevaluate its "programs on a regular basis," Farkas said.

Insignia昨日宣布，其第二季度净收入为318万美元，即每股12美分；而去年同期持续经营业务则出现175万美元的亏损，即每股9美分。该公司称，互联网相关业务带来的亏损使得本季度的业绩又减少了260万美元。

<!--en-->
Insignia yesterday said it had second-quarter net income of $3.18 million, or 12 cents a share, compared with a loss from continuing operations of $1.75 million, or 9 cents, a year earlier. Losses on Internet-related ventures reduced results for the latest quarter by $2.6 million, Insignia said.

该公司的股价在纽约证券交易所下跌30美分，至8.20美元。另一位股东，即Greenlight Capital LLC的对冲基金经理David Einhorn也在电话会议上加入了Loeb的批评行列。截至3月底，Greenlight持有Insignia 7.4%的股份，是该公司的第三大股东。[^1455]：¹⁰摘自M. Marbaro于2002年10月6日发表在《华盛顿邮报》上的文章《还有问题吗？公司电话会议仍让投资者被排除在外》，版面位置H1。版权所有2002年《华盛顿邮报》。经许可转载。

<!--en-->
The company's shares fell 30 cents to $8.20 on the New York StockExchange. Another shareholder, hedge fund manager David Einhorn of Greenlight Capital LLC, joined Loeb in his criticism on the call. Greenlight owned a 7.4 percent stake in Insignia at the end of March, making it the company's third-largest shareholder.
[^1455]: ¹⁰ From "Any more questions? Company conference calls still leave investors out," by M. Marbaro, October 6, 2002, *Washington Post*, p. H1. Copyright 2002. *Washington Post*. Reprinted with permission.

124 • 公司新闻背后的种种真相 “我们的看法和他一样，”Einhorn说，“我们认为公司应该尽快说明如何解决其企业治理问题，以免事态演变成一场媒体闹剧。”

<!--en-->
124 • The Ins and Outs of Company News Stories
"We feel similarly to him," Einhorn said. "And we think the company should come back promptly with how to fix its corporate governance issues before this turns into some sort of media circus."

Loeb表示，Farkas在从新业务中获取个人利益之前，应先确保Insignia能够弥补损失。由于Farkas推动的包括EdificeRex.com在内的多项互联网业务失败，Insignia已经为此承担了3470万美元的亏损。EdificeRex.com原本旨在为公寓租户提供服务。

<!--en-->
Before taking personal benefits from new ventures, Farkas should first make sure Insignia recoups its losses, Loeb said. Insignia has taken $34.7 million of charges for failed Internet ventures spearheaded by Farkas, including EdificeRex.com, which sought to provide services to apartment renters.

“看起来你可以接连不断地建立各种合作伙伴关系，如果其中一个不成功，那就换下一个，”Loeb说，“我更希望看到的是我们所有人坐在一起，共享同一份资源。”¹¹一个月后，Insignia Financial提交了8-K文件，宣布不再为CEO使用其个人游艇支付费用，也将停止为他共同拥有的飞机付费。（这一举动又为负责报道该公司的彭博记者提供了新的素材。）这正是公司股东而非高管利用电话会议制造新闻的一个案例。

<!--en-->
"It seems like you can keep setting up these partnerships one after another and if one doesn't work well, so be it," Loeb said. "You go on to the next one. What I'd rather see is us all sitting at the same table and eating from the same trough, if you will."¹¹
A month later, Insignia Financial filed an 8-K disclosing that it would no longer reimburse its CEO for the company's use of his personal boat and would stop paying for the plane he co-owns. (That resulted in another story for the Bloomberg reporter covering the company.) This is a case in which the investors in a company, not the executives, used the conference call to make news.

对于大多数财经记者而言，获取这些电话会议内容就像找到公司网站一样简单。大多数公司都会在网站上提供互联网电话会议的链接，还有一些公司则会在新闻稿末尾给出可直接拨打的电话号码。不过也有一些专门提供公司电话会议访问服务的网站，其中最好的免费网站之一就是http://seekingalpha.com.；另一家不错的网站——虽然是付费的——则是www.bestcalls.com，因为它还提供会议记录。

<!--en-->
For most business reporters, accessing these calls is as simple as finding the company's website. Most companies include a link to the conference call via the Internet. Others provide the phone number that can be called at the end of a news release. But there are also websites that specialize in providing access to company conference calls. One of the best free sites is http://seekingalpha.com. Another good site—although it is a pay site—is www.bestcalls.com because it also provides transcripts of calls.

自美国证券交易委员会实施FD法规以来已经过去十年了。监管机构花了两年多时间才开始打击涉嫌违反该规定的公司。即便如此，这些公司所受到的处罚也大多只是轻微的警告，正如以下《圣何塞水星报》的报道所描述的那样：

<!--en-->
It has now been a decade since the SEC imposed Regulation FD. It took regulators more than two years to crack down on companies suspected of violating the rules. Even then, the companies received little more than slaps on the wrist, as the following *San Jose Mercury News* story explains:

Siebel Systems同意就其违反证券交易委员会相关法规的行为达成和解，该法规禁止公司在向普通投资者披露消息之前，选择性地向某些华尔街分析师透露信息。

<!--en-->
Siebel Systems agreed to settle a federal charge that it had violated a Securities and Exchange Commission regulation prohibiting companies from selectively disclosing information to favored Wall Street analysts before releasing the news to ordinary investors.

与这家圣马特奥软件公司的和解案，标志着首起为执行FD法规（即公平披露法规）而提起的诉讼。该法规于2000年8月出台，旨在确保公众能够平等获取重要的投资信息。

<!--en-->
The agreement with the San Mateo software company marked the first litigation brought to enforce Regulation FD (for Fair Disclosure), which was adopted in August 2000 in order to ensure the public equal access to important investment information.

美国证券交易委员会还在周一宣布，已对圣何塞的安全软件制造商Secure Computing以及马萨诸塞州列克星敦的国防承包商Raytheon结束了行政程序。[^1466]：¹¹ 来自Bloomberg News 2002年7月25日D. Levitt撰写的文章《股东批评Insignia Financial首席执行官的薪酬方案》，版权归Bloomberg L.P.所有，经许可转载。

<!--en-->
The SEC also announced Monday the settlement of administrative proceedings against Secure Computing, a San Jose security-software maker, and Raytheon, a Lexington, Mass., defense contractor.
[^1466]: ¹¹ From "Insignia Financial CEO's pay package criticized by shareholders," by D. Levitt, July 25, 2002, Bloomberg News. Copyright 2002 by Bloomberg L.P. All rights reserved. Reprinted with permission.

公司新闻报道的方方面面 • 125 这三家公司均同意今后不再违反FD法规，且既不承认也不否认有任何不当行为。Siebel Systems还同意支付25万美元的民事罚款。

<!--en-->
The Ins and Outs of Company News Stories • 125
All three companies agreed to cease and desist from any future violations of Regulation FD without admitting or denying any wrongdoing. Siebel Systems also agreed to pay a civil penalty of $250,000.

总部位于硅谷、以科技业务见长的律师事务所Fenwick & West的董事长Gordy Davidson表示：“他们试图传达一个信号，即美国证券交易委员会在严格执行FD法规方面是认真的。”

<!--en-->
"They are trying to send a message that SEC is serious about enforcing the Regulation FD," said Gordy Davidson, chairman of Fenwick & West, a Silicon Valley law firm that emphasizes its technology practice.

这三个案例展示了FD法规在多大程度上影响了公司与投资者之间的沟通方式。在该法规出台之前，分析师们通常依靠与高管们的私下交谈来判断一家公司的财务前景，那些规模更大、知名度更高的机构的分析师往往还能获得额外的指导。

<!--en-->
The three cases illustrate how broadly Regulation FD has affected the way companies communicate with investors. Before it was adopted, analysts generally relied on private conversations with executives to form an opinion about a company's financial prospects. Analysts at larger, more prestigious firms often received special guidance.

美国证券交易委员会东北地区办公室的副区域主任Mark Schonfeld称：“这些案例，尤其是Raytheon的案例，正好体现了FD法规本应防范的那种行为。”

<!--en-->
"These cases, and Raytheon in particular, describe the kind of conduct that Regulation FD was supposed to prevent," said Mark Schonfeld, associate regional director of the SEC's Northeast Regional Office.

根据美国证券交易委员会的文件，Raytheon的首席财务官Franklyn Caine在2001年2月的财报电话会议之后，致电个别分析师，告知他们对该公司第一季度盈利的预估“过高”或“过于乐观”。

<!--en-->
According to SEC documents, Raytheon Chief Financial Officer Franklyn Caine called individual analysts following a February 2001 earnings call to let them know their estimates for first-quarter earnings were "too high" or "very aggressive."

在与被列为美国证券交易委员会诉讼当事人的Caine交谈后，这些分析师下调了他们的预估，使得Raytheon在三个月后公布财报时，每股的盈利数据比市场普遍预期高出1美分。

<!--en-->
After speaking with Caine, who was named as a party in the SEC action, analysts lowered their estimates, enabling Raytheon to beat the consensus estimate by a penny a share when it announced financial results three months later.

监管机构表示，摩托罗拉之所以没有成为类似诉讼的对象，是因为该公司的内部法律顾问告诉一位高层管理人员，可以给选定的分析师打电话。

<!--en-->
Regulators said Motorola avoided becoming the subject of a similar action because the company's in-house legal counsel told a senior executive it was OK to telephone selected analysts.

在涉及Secure Computing的案例中，根据美国证券交易委员会文件（该文件也将McNulty列为诉讼当事人），该公司首席执行官John McNulty在发布新闻稿之前，就曾向选定的分析师透露了公司计划将自家软件与Cisco Systems的产品捆绑销售的消息。

<!--en-->
In the case involving Secure Computing, Chief Executive John McNulty told selected analysts about a deal the company had made to bundle its software with products made by Cisco Systems before it issued a press release, according to SEC documents which named McNulty as a party.

旧金山地区办公室的助理地区主管Robert Mitchell表示，尽管监管机构认定最初的披露属于意外，但当公司员工正在准备新闻稿时，McNulty仍继续向更多分析师谈论这笔交易。“这对他们来说是个特别的问题，”Mitchell说道。

<!--en-->
Though regulators determined the initial disclosure was accidental, McNulty continued to talk about the deal with still more analysts as his employees prepared a press release, said Robert Mitchell, assistant district administrator of the San Francisco District Office. "That was a particular problem for them," Mitchell said.

Siebel Systems的首席执行官Tom Siebel并未被列入针对其公司的诉讼名单，不过该诉讼与他2001年11月在高盛科技会议上发表的言论有关。

<!--en-->
Tom Siebel, CEO of Siebel Systems, was not named in the action brought against his company, though it concerned statements he made during a Goldman Sachs technology conference in November 2001.

在会议前三周的一次公开财报电话会议上，Siebel曾悲观地谈到“异常疲软的市场”和严峻的商业环境。但在会议前几天，该公司的投资者关系主管却向高盛的一位分析师表示，公司业务状况正在好转。当Siebel在上午10点的演讲中转为乐观态度时，该公司的股价便大幅上涨，收盘价较前一日高出16%以上。

<!--en-->
On a public earnings call three weeks before the conference, Siebel had spoken pessimistically about "an exceptionally soft market" and a tough business environment. But a few days before the conference, the company's director of investor relations told a Goldman Sachs analyst that business was looking up. When Siebel struck an optimistic tone during his 10 a.m. presentation, the company's stock took off. It closed more than 16 percent above the previous day's close.

根据美国证券交易委员会的文件，会议开始时，与会者甚至在西贝尔发言结束前就开始交易该公司的股票，而高盛是当天交易西贝尔系统股票最活跃的机构。

<!--en-->
According to SEC documents, attendees at the conference began trading the stock even before Siebel finished speaking, and Goldman Sachs was the most active firm trading Siebel Systems stock that day.

该公司周一发布的新闻稿称，西贝尔的讲话“被视为违反了《公平披露规则》，因为该演讲并未通过网络直播或其他方式向公众同步播出”。该公司表示，西贝尔并不知道此次会议没有在互联网上转播。

<!--en-->
A company press release Monday said Siebel's remarks "were deemed tobe in violation of Regulation FD because the presentation was not Webcast or otherwise simultaneously broadcast to the general public.” The company said Siebel did not know the conference was not being transmitted on the Internet.

126 • 公司新闻报道的方方面面 “这对各地的管理层来说是一个很好的提醒：他们在会议上的问答环节及分组讨论中应当更加谨慎地发言，”JMP证券的分析师帕特里克·沃尔拉文斯说道。¹²

<!--en-->
126 • The Ins and Outs of Company News Stories
“This is a great reminder to management teams everywhere that they better be careful what they say in question-and-answer sessions and in breakout sessions at conferences,” said Patrick Walravens, an analyst at JMP Securities.¹²

## 结论

<!--en-->
*Conclusion*

《公平披露规则》确实为公司应向公众提供何种信息以及如何提供信息提供了一些指导。随着企业界逐渐更深入地理解这些规定，它们又回到了《公平披露规则》实施之前的做法，在电话会议上提供信息时变得更加主动和坦诚。

<!--en-->
Regulation FD did give companies some guidance about the “what and how” of information they are supposed to provide to the public. As the corporate world has moved forward and begun to understand these regulations better, companies have moved back to pre-Regulation FD days and become more comfortable and forthcoming in providing information during conference calls.

了解公司如何制作和传播新闻，有助于财经记者更专业地报道相关新闻。对于财经记者而言，最糟糕的情况莫过于无法准确解释董事会成员辞职或审计师对一家公司未来发展表示怀疑意味着什么。

<!--en-->
Understanding how companies make and disseminate news can help business reporters cover that news competently. Nothing hurts a business journalist more than botching an explanation of what it means for a board member to resign or for an auditor to express doubt about a company’s future.

## 建议练习题

<!--en-->
*Suggested Exercises*

1. 找出10个提交8-K文件的原因的实例，以及基于这些文件撰写的报道。这可以是一个贯穿整个学期的项目。
2. 撰写一篇500字的文章，解释由于《联邦披露规则》而导致的8-K文件提交量增加的原因。阐述《联邦披露规则》的内容，并举例说明由此提交的8-K文件类型及其为何属于新闻报道。
3. 找一家近期有高层管理人员离职或被替换的公司，比较该公司新闻稿中披露的信息与8-K表格中披露的信息。
4. 收听某家公司的电话会议，根据会中透露的新闻内容撰写一篇报道。提交报道后，将会议开场的准备发言与会议结尾的问答环节进行对比。![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/28ea43c75649b559f3d457664e5f2bf5.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T071651Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=dad81d05341e7c3dc2ac5ee5c8d19c2cba01bb2024fde22f0455cd314ab6dee1)

<!--en-->
1. Find examples of 10 of the reasons an 8-K is filed, along with stories that were written from those filings. This could be a project that is spread out across an entire semester.
2. Write a 500-word essay explaining the increase in 8-K filings due to Regulation FD. Explain Regulation FD and give examples of the types of 8-Ks being filed as a result and why they're stories.
3. Find a company where a top-ranking executive has recently left or been replaced. Compare the information disclosed in the company's news release to the information disclosed in the Form 8-K.
4. Listen to a company's conference call and write a story based on what news you thought was disclosed during the call. After you turn the story in, compare the prepared remarks at the beginning of the call to the Q&A session at the end of the call.

让我们来做个交易

<!--en-->
Let's Make a Deal

### 企业为何互相收购

<!--en-->
*Why Companies Buy Each Other*

几乎每位商业记者都曾撰写过关于一家公司收购另一家公司的报道，这就好比警察记者撰写谋杀案报道一样，这类新闻事件频发。根据Mergermarket的数据，2009年前九个月共有1,896起并购案，总价值超过4715亿美元。尽管这些数字看似庞大，但相比2008年前九个月，分别下降了41%和34%。

<!--en-->
At some point in time, virtually every business reporter will write a story about one company buying another. It is like a police reporter writing a story about a murder. Both of these news events happen with regularity. In the first nine months of 2009, there were 1,896 mergers or acquisitions, valued at a total of more than $471.5 billion. Although these numbers seem large, they are actually down 41 percent and 34 percent, respectively, from the first nine months of 2008, according to data from Mergermarket.

简而言之，并购活动如此频繁，以至于已成为商业报道中的常见内容。鉴于其高频率，记者们有必要了解并购发生的机制与原因，以及哪些信息对读者和观众而言至关重要。几乎所有大型企业，还有许多小型企业，都是通过一次或多次并购形成的。花旗集团是由原花旗银行和旅行者集团合并而成的；AOL时代华纳则是美国在线与时代华纳的合并产物，而时代华纳本身又是时代公司与华纳兄弟公司交易的成果；迪士尼则收购了电视网络ABC，从而使ESPN也并入这家新公司。

<!--en-->
Simply put, mergers and acquisitions occur with such regularity that they have become a staple of business reporting. Because of their frequency, it is important for journalists to understand how and why M&A occur and what information is important for readers and viewers to receive. Virtually every huge company, and plenty of small ones, too, were created by one or more mergers or acquisitions. Citigroup is the combination of the former Citibank and Travelers; AOL Time Warner was created by the merger of America Online with Time Warner, itself the creation of a deal between Time and Warner Brothers; and Disney bought television network ABC, which brought ESPN into the new company.

近期的经济危机迫使一些公司为维持经营而出售自身。联邦政府也在并购活动中发挥了作用，有时会为陷入困境的公司寻找合适的收购方。2008年9月，政府支持花旗集团收购瓦乔维亚公司，但后来又因富国银行出价更高而支持其收购瓦乔维亚公司。同月，联邦政府接管了华盛顿互惠银行，并将其大部分资产出售给了摩根大通。

<!--en-->
The recent economic crisis has forced some companies to sell themselves to remain in business. The federal government has played a part in mergers and acquisitions as well, sometimes finding suitable acquirers to purchase companies in trouble. In September 2008, the government backed Citigroup Incorporated's purchase of Wachovia Corporation but later backed Wells Fargo & Company's acquisition of Wachovia because Wells Fargo & Company offered a higher price. In the same month, the federal government seized Washington Mutual Incorporated and sold the bulk of its assets to J.P. Morgan Chase & Company.

无论是上市公司还是私营企业，大多都希望扩大规模。许多企业之所以选择并购，是因为认为规模更大的企业能更高效地分摊各项开支。例如，既然两家公司可以合并为一家，为何还要设置两位首席执行官和两位首席财务官？为何要130 • 让我们来做个交易

<!--en-->
Most companies, whether they are public or private, like to get bigger. Many of them make acquisitions under the belief that a larger company can spread its expenses around more efficiently. For instance, why have two CEOs and two CFOs when two companies can be combined to only have one of each? Why
130 • Let's Make a Deal

### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《The Deal》*编辑罗伯特·泰特尔曼关于报道并购案的技巧：*

<!--en-->
The Deal *editor Robert Teitelman's tips on covering mergers and acquisitions:*

## 其经济逻辑是什么？

<!--en-->
*What's the economic logic?*

这是简单的业务整合、试图抢占市场份额的行为，还是所谓的“转型型”并购？是为了摆脱业务衰退，还是为了提升市场主导地位？收购方只是想获得新产品（较容易），寻求新技术（较困难），还是进行彻底的自我重塑（最困难）？这一逻辑应体现在价格和溢价上。有些公司总是为技术支付过高代价；有些则反复尝试实现转型；还有少数公司在收购企业并成功整合方面有着悠久的历史。请考察收购方的过往记录。为何要设立两个总部，而一个就足够了？这正是大多数公司的期望，但实际上，并购并不总如愿以偿。

<!--en-->
Is this a bolt-on, an attempt to buy market share or a so-called "transformational" merger? Is it an attempt to escape a declining business or one that attempts to create greater dominance? Is the buyer simply getting new products (easy), seeking access to new technologies (more difficult), or remaking itself (most difficult)? This logic should be reflected in price and premium. Some companies consistently overpay for technology; others make repeated stabs at transformation. A few have long track records of buying companies and successfully integrating them. Check the buyer's track record.
operate two headquarters when one would suffice? That is what most companies hope for. But, in reality, mergers and acquisitions do not always work out that way.

首先，需明确相关条款。尽管“并购”这两个词有时会被混用，但两者之间存在很大差异。“合并”指的是两家公司同意将业务整合为一家公司。在真正的合并中，两家公司的原所有者将在新公司各持有50%的股份。合并后的公司董事会通常也会由两家原公司的董事会成员共同组成。在很多情况下，两家原公司的管理团队也会合并，形成一个新的管理团队。这便是应有的运作方式。

<!--en-->
First, the terms should be defined. Although the terms merger and acquisition are sometimes used interchangeably, there is a big difference. Merger refers to when two companies agree to combine their operations into one company. In a true merger, the past owners of the two companies will each own 50 percent in the new company. In a merger, the combined company's board of directors is also typically split among the board members of the two old businesses. In many cases, the management teams of the old companies also combine to form one new executive team. That is how it is supposed to work.

然而，尽管公司努力让并购双方处于平等地位，但通常仍有一方占据优势。例如，其总部会成为合并后公司的新总部，其CEO会接管新公司的运营，或者其股东最终可能持有新公司55%的股份。

<!--en-->
However, despite how hard companies try to make mergers equal, one company typically has the upper hand. For example, its headquarters becomes the new headquarters for the combined operation, its CEO takes over running the new company, or its shareholders may end up owning 55 percent of the new company.

“收购”则指一家公司购买另一家公司的控股权。收购并不一定意味着一家公司要买下另一家公司的100%股份。有时，一家公司只需购买51%的股份，因为只要成为多数股东，就能掌控整个公司的运营。

<!--en-->
Acquisition refers to when one company buys a controlling interest in another company. An acquisition does not always mean that one company purchases 100 percent of another company. Sometimes, a company will just purchase 51 percent because if one company becomes the majority owner, it can control how the entire company is operated.

公司出于各种原因收购其他企业，其中之一可能是CEO希望推动公司发展。有时候，扩张公司的最简单方法就是收购另一家公司。但有时收购并非明智之举——被收购的公司可能在运营模式或企业文化上与现有业务不匹配。不过，在大多数情况下，并购都是出于特定目的而进行的。某次收购可能是公司扩张战略的一部分。例如，在20世纪90年代中期，可口可乐希望完善其饮料产品线。其产品线中最缺少的就是根啤酒。该公司曾在少数地区销售名为Ramblin' Root Beer的品牌，但其竞争对手都拥有更知名的品牌，如Mug、Dad's和A&W。于是可口可乐四处寻找可收购的根啤酒公司，最终在1995年买下了总部位于新奥尔良的Barq's公司。

<!--en-->
Companies buy other companies for various reasons, one of which may be because the CEO wants to see the company grow. Sometimes, the easiest way to grow a company is to acquire another company. But sometimes an acquisition is not a smart move. The acquired company may not fit in with the business, either operationally or culturally. In most cases, however, mergers or acquisitions take place for specific reasons. An acquisition may be part of a company's expansion strategy. For example, in the mid-1990s, Coca-Cola wanted to round out its portfolio of beverages. One of the biggest holes in its product line was in root beer. The company sold a brand called Ramblin' Root Beer in a handful of locations, but its competitors all had better-known brands, such as Mug, Dad's, and A&W. So Coca-Cola looked around until it found a root beer company it could buy. In 1995, it purchased Barq's, a New Orleans-based company.

其他时候，公司通过收购进入新的地理区域。也许该公司的业务主要集中在中西部和西部，但它希望拓展到中大西洋地区。《华盛顿邮报》曾报道过一家公司通过收购进入新市场的故事：

<!--en-->
Other times, companies make acquisitions to expand into new geographic territories. Maybe the company's operations are primarily in the Midwest and the West, but it would like to expand into the Mid-Atlantic. The following is a story from *The Washington Post* written about one company's acquisition that helped it move into new markets:

弗吉尼亚州最大的健康保险公司Trigon Healthcare Inc.昨日同意被美国第五大上市健康保险公司Anthem Inc.以38亿美元的现金和股票收购。

<!--en-->
Trigon Healthcare Inc., the largest health insurance company in Virginia, agreed yesterday to be acquired by Anthem Inc., the fifth-largest publicly traded U.S. health insurer, for $3.8 billion in cash and stock.

这两家Blue Cross Blue Shield公司此前均为非营利性质，后来转为股东所有制企业。近年来，许多地区的Blue Cross计划宣布打算与规模更大的“Blue”保险公司合并，以便更好地与Aetna Inc.和UnitedHealth Group Inc.等大型保险公司竞争。

<!--en-->
Both Blue Cross Blue Shield companies formerly operated on a not-for-profit basis but converted to stockholder-owned enterprises. In recent years, many regional Blue Cross plans have announced plans to merge with larger "Blues" to better compete with big insurers such as Aetna Inc. and UnitedHealth Group Inc.

总部位于印第安纳波利斯的Anthem公司为八个州的800万客户提供服务。如果该并购获得批准，Anthem公司将拥有弗吉尼亚州及华盛顿特区的220万会员，并在其尚未布局的东南部和中大西洋地区站稳脚跟。根据交易条款，Trigon的股东每持有一股Trigon股票，将获得30美元现金和1.062股Anthem股票。按周五的收盘价计算，这对Trigon的股东而言相当于每股105.08美元的收益。Let's Make a Deal • 131 昨日，纽约证券交易所上Trigon的股票股价上涨14.62美元，涨幅达17.4%，至98.87美元。Anthem的股票则下跌4.05美元，跌幅为5.7%，至66.65美元。

<!--en-->
Indianapolis-based Anthem serves 8 million customers in eight states. If approved, the merger would give Anthem 2.2 million members in Virginia and the District and a foothold in the Southeast and Mid-Atlantic,where it does not have a presence. Under terms of the deal, Trigon stockholders would receive $30 in cash and 1.062 Anthem shares for each Trigon share they own. Based on Friday's closing prices, the package is worth $105.08 a share to holders of Trigon.
Let's Make a Deal • 131
Trigon stock surged $14.62 a share, or 17.4 percent, to $98.87 yesterday on the New York Stock Exchange. Anthem shares fell $4.05, or 5.7 percent, to $66.65.

Trigon的首席执行官小托马斯·G·斯尼德表示，该交易不会立即影响公司客户所支付的保费。他预计“至少在未来几年内”，保费还将出现两位数的上涨。

<!--en-->
Trigon chief executive Thomas G. Snead Jr. said the deal would have no immediate impact on premiums the company's customers pay. He said he expected double-digit premium increases "for at least the next couple of years."

“保险费是根据提供该产品所需的医疗成本以及相关管理成本来确定的，”他说。

<!--en-->
"Premiums are set as a result of the underlying medical costs and administrative costs that are required to service the product," he said.

但他表示，随着时间的推移，这次合并将造就一家拥有更雄厚资金实力和技术能力的更强健的保险公司。

<!--en-->
But over time, he said, the merger would create a stronger health insurer with greater financial resources and technological capabilities.

“这是一次战略联盟，”斯尼德说，“双方坐下来共同探讨了合作与分开各自的局面，我得说……这非常有道理。”

<!--en-->
"This is a strategic alliance," Snead said. "Both parties sat down and figured out what we could look like together versus separate and, I got to tell you . . . this makes an awful lot of sense."

该合并协议尚需获得弗吉尼亚州保险监管机构的批准。¹ 需要注意的是，这篇报道的开篇首先提到的是被收购方Trigon，而非收购方Anthem。这是因为记者清楚读者最关心什么。由于大量读者位于弗吉尼亚州，《华盛顿邮报》在报道此次收购时重点关注这家总部位于弗吉尼亚的公司。开篇段落还详细说明了收购该公司的价格。在任何并购新闻中，价格都是最重要的细节——支付金额决定了交易的估值。如果一家公司不公开其收购另一家公司的金额，记者应当追问。对于涉及上市公司的并购，监管机构要求公司必须披露价格；而私营公司虽无需披露价格，但也可选择公开相关信息。

<!--en-->
The merger agreement is subject to approval by Virginia insurance regulators.¹
Note that the lead paragraph of this story first mentions the company being acquired, Trigon, not the company making the acquisition, Anthem. That is because the reporter knows what his readers will care about the most. With a large contingent of readers in Virginia, the *Post* focuses its coverage of this acquisition on the Virginia-based company. The lead paragraph also details how much money is being paid for the acquired company. The price is the most important detail in any merger and acquisition story. The money being paid places a value on the transaction. If a company does not disclose how much it is paying for another company, the reporter should ask. For mergers and acquisitions involving public companies, regulators require the company to disclose the price. Private companies conducting transactions are not required to disclose the price, but they may choose to release that information.

报道还说明，该公司是通过现金加股票的方式被收购的。这也是大多数并购新闻中应披露的另一个重要细节，它能让读者了解用于收购的资金来源。上市公司通常会用股票来支付交易费用。

<!--en-->
The story also explains that the company is being purchased with a combination of cash and stock. This is another important detail that should be disclosed in most merger and acquisition stories. It lets the reader know where the money to fund the acquisition is coming from. Public companies often use their stock to help pay for a deal.

这篇报道还详细说明了换股比例。在涉及股票交换的并购中，这是至关重要的信息——它能让被收购公司的股东知道在合并后的公司里他们能获得多少股份。在Trigon/Anthem的案例中，除了现金外，每持有1股Trigon的股票还能获得略多于1股的Anthem股票。[^1526]：¹ 来自B.布鲁贝克2002年4月30日发表于《华盛顿邮报》E1版的文章《印第安纳公司拟收购Trigon：保险公司同意38亿美元的交易》，版权归2002年《华盛顿邮报》所有，经许可转载。132 • 让我们达成交易

<!--en-->
The exchange ratio is also detailed in this story. For mergers and acquisitions in which stock is being used, this is vital information. It informs the shareholders of the company being acquired how many shares they will receive in the combined company. In the case of the Trigon/Anthem deal, it was slightly more than one share in Anthem for every share of Trigon stock owned, in addition to cash.
[^1526]: ¹ From "Indiana company to buy Trigon: Insurers agree to $3.8 billion deal," by B. Brubaker, April 30, 2002, *Washington Post*, p. E1. Copyright 2002 by *Washington Post*. Reprinted with permission.
132 • Let's Make a Deal

### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《The Deal》杂志编辑罗伯特·泰特尔曼关于报道并购的建议：

<!--en-->
The Deal *editor Robert Teitelman's tips on covering mergers and acquisitions:*

**薪酬问题：**交易的核心驱动力是金钱。高管和董事会成员的薪酬情况总是值得关注且很有意思。在某些情况下，处于巅峰或开始走下坡路的公司的高管会出售股份，以最大化包括自己在内的股东的收益。在其他情况下，奖金会与股价挂钩，在某些市场里，一旦宣布交易消息，股价就会随之上涨。不过情况并非总是如此。在熊市中，投资者甚至会拒绝看似不错的交易，导致股价下跌，进而使管理层不愿进行交易。通常来说，判断一笔交易合理性的关键在于谁从中获利。可问的问题是：谁在盈利？

<!--en-->
**Compensation:** Deals are driven by money. How senior executives and board members are paid is disclosed and always interesting. In some cases, executives of a company hitting its peak, or beginning to fade, will sell out to maximize returns to shareholders, including themselves. In other cases, bonuses will be tied to stock prices, which, in certain markets, will reflexively boost the share price upon the announcement of a deal. That's not always the case. In bear markets, investors will reject even compelling deals, hammering the share price and making management deal averse. Mostly, the underlying rationalization for a deal can be found in who's cashing out. Question to ask: Who's profiting?

#### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《The Deal》杂志编辑罗伯特·泰特尔曼关于报道并购的建议：**节省的成本在哪里？**新合并实体何时能开始为盈利做出贡献？两家公司之间是否存在可以减少管理开支和员工人数的重叠部分？还是说这两家公司是互补关系，虽然整合起来更容易，但产生“协同效应”——即降低成本——则更为困难？削减成本可能成就一笔交易，也可能毁掉它，尤其是在大公司收购具有独特文化的较小公司时。为抬高价格而削减成本可能会招致人才流失。涉及人才或知识产权的并购最难整合。

<!--en-->
The Deal *editor Robert Teitelman's tips on covering mergers and acquisitions:*
**Where are the savings?** How quickly will the new unit be “accretive,” that is contribute to earnings? Is there overlap between the two companies that can produce reductions in overhead and headcount? Or are the two companies complementary, which makes integration easier, but “synergies”—or cost reductions—tougher? Cost cutting can make or wreck a deal, a particular issue when a large company buys a smaller one with a unique culture. Cost cutting to justify price can drive away talent. Deals that involve talent or intellectual property are hardest to integrate.

在并购中，这种换股比例通常是1股对1股，或接近1:1的比例。

<!--en-->
With mergers, this exchange ratio is often one share for one share, or a ratio close to 1:1.

这篇报道还向读者说明了该交易是如何按每股价格来评估被收购公司的价值的。对于同时持有Trigon股票的《华盛顿邮报》读者而言，这是重要信息——它告诉他们每持有一股股票能获得多少钱，从而帮助他们判断这笔交易是否划算。在这起案例中，Trigon的大多数投资者很可能对Anthem给出的价格感到满意。在交易宣布之前，Trigon的股价约为84美元，而Anthem却以每股105美元的价格收购了该公司，为投资者带来了25%的收益。这25%的差额就被视为Anthem为Trigon支付的溢价。溢价指的是收购方愿意为一家公司支付的金额超过该公司当前价值的部分。

<!--en-->
This story also informs readers how the deal values the acquired company on a per share basis. For readers of the *Post* who also owned Trigon stock, this is important information. This tells them how much money they will receive for each share of stock they own, and it enables them to assess whether the deal is a good one. In this case, most investors in Trigon likely were happy with the price Anthem paid. Trigon stock was trading for about $84 before the deal was announced, yet Anthem paid $105 per share for the company, a 25 percent gain for investors. This 25 percent is considered the premium paid by Anthem for Trigon. A premium is how much more the acquirer is willing to pay for a company than the company's current value.

企业出于各种原因支付溢价收购其他公司，但其中很多都与它们的整体并购战略密切相关。或许收购方的管理层认为自己能够更好地运营被收购公司，从而提升其销售额和利润。如果收购方的判断正确，那么被收购公司的实际价值可能高于目前的估值。又或者，收购方的高管们认为通过整合两家公司的业务可以削减成本，进而降低公司运营开支。这种现象就被称为协同效应。

<!--en-->
Companies pay premiums to acquire other companies for various reasons, but many are tied into their overall merger and acquisition strategies. Maybe the management of the acquiring company thinks it can do a better job of running the acquired company, increasing its sales and profits. If the acquiring company is right, the company being acquired is probably worth more than it is currently valued. Or maybe the executives at the purchaser think that they can cut costs at the acquired company by combining the two operations, thus lowering the expenses related to running the company. This is called synergy.

此前提到的那些收购案例通常属于所谓的友好收购，即收购方会与被收购公司的董事会进行谈判，并在宣布收购之前就收购价格达成一致。但这种情况并非总是发生。有时，一家公司想要收购另一家不愿出售的公司；或者有时，虽然双方进行了收购谈判，但最终未能达成协议。在这种情况下，试图进行收购的公司往往会采取所谓的恶意收购手段。

<!--en-->
The acquisitions that have been referenced so far are what are typically called friendly takeovers, which means the acquiring company negotiates with the board of the company being sold, and they come to an agreement on the purchase price before the acquisition is announced. But this does not always happen. Sometimes a company will want to acquire another company that does not want to sell. Or sometimes, a company will negotiate to acquire another company, but those talks will end without an agreement. When that happens, sometimes the company wanting to make the acquisition launches what is called a hostile takeover.

即便公司之间已经达成协议，也可能会出现恶意收购的企图。第三家公司可能会介入，提出比最初报价更高的金额或不同的收购方案。2000年和2001年在美国东南部就发生过这样的事件：Wachovia和First Union同意合并成一家银行，但另一家银行SunTrust对这笔交易不满，于是向First Union提出了独立的收购报价。最终，Wachovia赢得了这场竞争。这类恶意收购是商业记者们喜爱的新闻素材，因为它们通常涉及竞争对手以及愤怒的CEO，这些CEO希望借助媒体宣传自己的立场。在许多情况下，CEO们为了说服人们他们的报价更优，会通过媒体直接向目标公司的股东发表意见。

<!--en-->
A hostile takeover attempt can even occur when companies have reached an agreement. A third company may enter the fray, offering more money or a different structure than the original offer. Such an event occurred in the Southeast in 2000 and 2001, when Wachovia and First Union agreed to merge and create one bank. However, another bank, SunTrust, became upset with the transaction and made a separate offer for First Union. In the end, Wachovia won the battle. Such hostile takeovers are great news stories for business reporters because they typically involve competitors and angry CEOs who want to talk to the media to get their side of the takeover out for discussion. In many cases, CEOs, in the hopes of convincing people their bid is better, use the media to speak directly to the shareholders of the company up for sale.

这只是关于并购报道的众多类型之一。大型并购交易通常在周末谈判结束后，于周日晚上或周一早间宣布。之所以如此，是因为参与交易的各方都希望获得尽可能多的媒体报道。由于周末几乎没有商业新闻，这些公司知道自己的交易很可能会被报道出来。他们还意识到，专门报道并购领域的《华尔街日报》记者能够为该交易带来更多关注。《华尔街日报》周日不出版，因此其编辑们会在周一寻找最新的新闻素材。以下这篇《纽约时报》的文章有助于解释为何企业在尝试恶意收购时会利用宣传来为自己辩护：

<!--en-->
This is just one of the many types of stories that can be written about mergers and acquisitions. Large acquisitions typically are announced on late Sunday or early Monday after negotiations are finalized during the weekend. This often happens because the companies involved in the deal want as much coverage from the media as possible. Because little business news occurs during a weekend, the companies know that they are likely to get stories written about their deal. They also realize that *The Wall Street Journal* reporters who specifically cover mergers and acquisitions could give the deal good play. The *Journal* does notpublish on Sunday, so its editors look for the latest news for its sections on Monday.
Let's Make a Deal • 133
The following *New York Times* story helps explain why companies sometimes use publicity to make their case in a hostile takeover attempt:

大规模的恶意收购正在卷土重来，只不过这次的方式更为隐蔽巧妙。人们甚至将其称为“熊抱式收购”。

<!--en-->
The big hostile takeover is coming back, but it is warmer and fuzzier this time. They even call it the bear hug.

根据汤森金融证券数据，今年迄今为止，未经请求的收购报价占所有交易总价值的19.5%，而去年同期这一比例仅为2.9%。过去，这类报价大多以要约收购的形式出现，即投标方直接面向目标公司的股东提出报价。但最近，许多备受关注的报价并非针对股东，而是针对公司管理层，部分原因是他们无法直接联系到股东。不过，与那些低调的幕后收购谈判不同，这种“熊抱式收购”是以非常公开的方式进行的。

<!--en-->
So far this year, unsolicited offers account for 19.5 percent of the value of all deals, compared with only 2.9 percent during the corresponding period a year ago, according to Thomson Financial Securities Data. In past years, many of these offers came in the form of tender offers, in which the bidder went straight to the shareholders of a company. But recently, many of the most publicized bids have been made not to shareholders but to the companies' managements, in some cases because they could not go directly to shareholders. But unlike quiet, behind-the-scenes takeover talks, these "bear hugs" are made in a very public way.

本周EchoStar Communications向Hughes Electronics提出的300亿美元未经请求的收购报价就是一个例子。Comcast对AT&T有线电视业务发起的收购尝试也是另一个例子。第三个例子则是工具制造商Danaher Corporation向竞争对手Cooper Industries提出的55亿美元未经请求的收购报价，后者昨日已拒绝了该提议。

<!--en-->
EchoStar Communications' unsolicited $30 billion offer this week for Hughes Electronics, is one example. Comcast's takeover bid for AT&T's cable-television business is another. A third is the toolmaker Danaher Corporation's unsolicited $5.5 billion bid for a rival, Cooper Industries, which rejected it yesterday.

在每一个案例中，投标方都清楚自己获胜的概率极低。但他们也明白，即便失败，在很多方面他们依然算是“赢家”。

<!--en-->
In each of these cases, the bidders knew they stood little chance of winning. They also knew that even if they lost, in many ways they would still win.

以EchoStar的收购案为例，其董事长Charles Ergen公开提出该提案，部分目的是吸引Hughes的母公司通用汽车董事会的注意。他曾与Hughes的高管们进行过讨论，但他担心通用汽车的董事会尚未审查该提案。

<!--en-->
Take EchoStar's bid. The chairman, Charles Ergen, took his proposal public partly to get the attention of the board of General Motors, parent of Hughes. He had held discussions with executives at Hughes, but said he was worried that G.M.'s board had not reviewed the proposal.

昨日，在通用汽车董事会于周二决定重新审视该收购提议后，埃尔根表示：“通用汽车如此认真地对待我们的提案，这让我们感到鼓舞。”这种公开表达支持的态度也是为了敦促股东向公司董事会施加压力。自EchoStar提出收购意向以来，已有四起针对通用汽车的诉讼由股东提起，这些诉讼实际上迫使该公司考虑EchoStar的报价。康卡斯特对AT&T宽带业务的公开收购方案迫使AT&T推迟了该业务的分拆计划，从而使该业务重新进入谈判范畴。虽然库珀工业公司可能已拒绝丹纳赫的报价，但该公司表示会考虑各种提升股东价值的替代方案，实际上相当于将公司挂牌出售。库珀还推迟了将公司迁往百慕大的投票，因为在百慕大进行收购将困难得多。

<!--en-->
Yesterday, Mr. Ergen said he was "encouraged that G.M. is taking our proposal very seriously," after a decision by G.M.'s board on Tuesday to review the offer. The publicity of a bear hug is also meant to stir shareholders to apply pressure to the company's board. Since EchoStar made its bear hug, four lawsuits have been filed against G.M. by shareholders effectively pushing the company to consider EchoStar's offer. Comcast's public offer for AT&T Broadband forced AT&T to postpone spinning off the unit, putting the business in play. And while Cooper Industries may have rejected Danaher's offer, Cooper did say it will consider a variety of alternatives to increase shareholder value, effectively putting the company up for sale. Cooper also postponed a vote to move the company to Bermuda, where a takeover would be much more difficult.

进行此类公开收购的最大问题在于，它降低了收购方在没有竞争的情况下与目标公司谈判的机会。自从康卡斯特提出对AT&T宽带的收购意向后，已有六家左右的潜在收购方开始围拢该业务，其中一些甚至讨论组建联合体来购买该业务，只为阻止其落入康卡斯特手中。

<!--en-->
The biggest problem with making such a public offer is that it reduces a suitor's chance of being able to negotiate for the target without competition. Since Comcast made its offer for AT&T Broadband, half a dozen suitors have begun circling the business, some discussing forming consortiums to buy the business simply in an effort to keep it from Comcast.

在另一起案例中，荷兰皇家壳牌集团的美资子公司壳牌石油公司对巴雷特资源公司提出了收购报价。巴雷特拒绝了壳牌的报价，但认为已有足够的……

<!--en-->
In another situation, the Shell Oil Company, the United States arm of the Royal Dutch/Shell Group, made an offer for the Barrett Resources Corporation. Barrett rejected Shell's offer, but decided there was enough

## 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《The Deal》杂志编辑罗伯特·泰特尔曼关于报道并购案的技巧：*

<!--en-->
The Deal *editor Robert Teitelman's tips on covering mergers and acquisitions:*

## 人格契合度如何？

<!--en-->
*What's the personality fit?*

人是决定并购成败的关键因素，而核心就在CEO身上。除非在特殊情况下，双CEO制往往会引发决策瘫痪。另一个危险信号是：高层管理者的任命基于政治考量而非能力——试图平衡两家公司的人才力量。从积极的角度看，有些并购案会包含继任计划：某公司的CEO打算退休且没有接班人，于是与另一家拥有年轻CEO的公司合并，后者随后接掌公司。最后还有企业文化的问题。有些并购案，比如时代华纳与AOL的合并，就因文化冲突而无法挽回。而在其他案例中，一种文化会吸收另一种文化——即便经历了激烈的收购斗争之后。文化契合度很难预测。

<!--en-->
People make deals successes or failures. The key: The CEO. Except in unusual cases, co-CEOs suggest potential paralysis. Another danger sign: Decisions on senior executives based on politics, not competence—balancing off talent from each company. More positively, some mergers may involve a succession plan: The CEO of one is planning to retire, lacks a successor, and merges with another with a younger CEO, who will then take over. Finally, there's the matter of culture. Some deals, like Time Warner and AOL, never recover from culture clashes. In others, one culture absorbs the other—even after a contentious takeover struggle. Culture fit is hard to predict.

134 • 让我们达成交易——股东的压力促使该公司考虑出售。最终，能源贸易商及管道运营公司威廉姆斯公司获得了对巴雷特的控制权。

<!--en-->
134 • Let's Make a Deal pressure from shareholders to put itself up for sale. In the end, the Williams Companies, an energy trader and pipeline operator, won control of Barrett.

企业也喜欢采用这种公开表达支持的方式，因为相比需要耗费大量成本、耗时漫长的方式向数千名股东发出收购要约，这种方式更简单、成本更低。只需要一份新闻稿和一张邮票，就能将提议寄送给公司董事会。

<!--en-->
Companies also like the bear hug because it is easier and cheaper than a tender offer, which can involve a costly, lengthy appeal to thousands of shareholders. All it requires is a press release and a postage stamp to send the proposal to the company's board.

有些企业也更愿意公开宣布自己的收购意向，因为它们并不担心失败。“过去那条‘不能公开开始的事情也无法公开完成’的经验法则似乎不再适用了，”瑞士信贷第一波士顿的全球并购负责人唐纳德·梅尔策说道，“越来越多的收购方愿意公开出价并承担失败的风险，以此表明他们对自己愿意支付的价格有明确的规划。”

<!--en-->
Some companies are also more comfortable about going public with their offers because they aren't worried about losing. "The old rule of thumb that you don't start something publicly you can't finish doesn't seem to hold anymore," said Donald Meltzer, global head of mergers and acquisitions at Credit Suisse First Boston. "More acquirers are prepared to go public with an offer and take the risk of losing, demonstrating they are disciplined about the price they are willing to pay."

当太阳信托银行在与第一联合银行争夺瓦乔维亚银行的控制权失败后，太阳信托银行的董事长L·菲利普·胡曼表示接受这一结果。

<!--en-->
When SunTrust lost its fight against First Union for control of Wachovia, SunTrust's chairman, L. Phillip Humann, said the loss was acceptable.

“显然我们希望这场竞争能有不同的结局，但如果这意味着放弃我们的商业纪律，以对股东不利的低价进行收购，那是不可取的，”他说，“现在我们会按照之前所说的做法——就此了结这件事。”² 就像雪花一样，每笔交易都是独一无二的。但关于并购的报道应该回答以下问题：

<!--en-->
"Clearly we would have preferred a different outcome to this contest, but not if it meant abandoning our business discipline to pursue an acquisition at a price that did not make sense for our shareholders," he said. "Now we'll do just what we said we would in this situation—close the book."²
Like snowflakes, every transaction is different. But stories about mergers and acquisitions should answer these questions:

1. 这笔交易的总价格和每股价格是多少？
2. 此次收购是用现金、股票、债务还是多种方式共同支付的？
3. 如果是股票交易，交换比例是多少？
4. 该价格与行业内类似交易的价格相比如何？
5. 交易何时完成？谁需要批准这笔交易？
6. 进行这笔交易的理由是什么？它能否让该公司成为所在行业或业务领域的最大企业？
7. 投资者对这项收购公告有何反应？
8. 这次并购是否会影响到特定的竞争对手？
9. 在交易宣布前不久，参与该交易的公司的股票交易活跃度是否有所上升？
10. 这项交易会对收购方公司产生增值效应还是稀释效应？每当有交易宣布时，记者都应思考为何该交易对收购方和出售方都有意义。很多时候，相关公司的高管会召开电话会议，向华尔街及其他人士解释他们认为此项举措为何是正确的选择。务必收听这些电话会议。如果分析师和投资者对该交易持怀疑态度，你也有充分的理由保持警惕。[^1563]：²摘自A.R. Sorkin所著《敌意收购的温和版本》，2001年8月9日，《纽约时报》，C1版。版权归《纽约时报》所有，经许可转载。Let's Make a Deal • 135

<!--en-->
1. What is the total price and per share price of a deal?
2. Is the acquisition being paid for with cash, stock, debt, or a combination?
3. If it's a stock transaction, what is the exchange ratio?
4. What is the price compared to that of similar transactions in the industry?
5. When will the deal be completed and who must approve the transaction?
6. What is the reason for this deal? Does it make the company the largest in its industry or business line?
7. How did investors react to the acquisition announcement?
8. Will the merger or acquisition affect specific competitors?
9. Did the trading activity of the stocks of the companies involved in the transaction increase shortly before the deal was announced?
10. Will the deal be accretive or dilutive to the acquiring company?
Any time a deal is announced, the reporter should ask him or herself why the transaction makes sense for both the acquiring company and the selling company. Many times, executives at the companies will hold a conference call to explain to Wall Street and others why they think the move is a good one. Always listen to these calls. If the analysts and investors are skeptical about the deal, there's probably a good reason you should be also.
[^1563]: ² From "The warm and fuzzy version of the hostile takeover bid," by A.R. Sorkin, August 9, 2001, *New York Times*, p. C1. Copyright 2001 by *New York Times*. Reprinted with permission.
Let's Make a Deal • 135

## 交易的资金来源

<!--en-->
*Funding the Deal*

企业会采用多种方式来为收购另一家公司筹集资金。最常见的三种支付方式是现金、股票和债务。企业也可以结合两种或更多种方式来筹集购买另一家公司所需的资金。

<!--en-->
Companies use various ways to fund the purchase of another business. The three most common methods of payment are cash, stock, and debt. A company can also use a combination of two or more of these methods to raise the cash needed to buy another company.

现金是最容易理解的支付方式。基本上，如果一家公司的银行账户中有足够的现金用于收购，那就意味着它有足够的资金来完成这笔交易。财经撰稿人可以通过查看企业随季度或年度财务报表一同提交的现金流量表，来判断该公司是否有足够的现金来实施拟议中的交易。有时，企业会宣称将用现金支付收购款项，但实际上其账户中并没有相应现金。这些资金可以来自债券、债务或融资，具体内容详见第8章。这类似于向银行借款。

<!--en-->
Cash is the easiest method of payment to understand. Basically, if a company has enough cash sitting in its banks to make an acquisition, it has enough money to pay for the acquisition. Business writers can look at the company's cash flow statement filed with its quarterly or annual financial statements to determine whether a company has the cash to do a proposed deal. Sometimes companies announce that they will use cash to pay for an acquisition, even though they do not actually have that cash in their accounts. The money can come from bonds, debts, or offerings, as discussed in Chapter 8. This is similar to borrowing the money from a bank.

有时，企业会用股票来支付收购费用。这意味着企业会将股票分发给被收购公司的所有者。为此，收购方通常需要向美国证券交易委员会提交文件以出售新增的股票。这些文件会披露大量关于该交易的信息。当企业的股价高于其历史估值时，企业往往更倾向于用股票来支付收购费用。此类交易的逻辑在于：股价越高，企业为完成收购所需发行的股票数量就越少。如果A公司同意以1亿美元的价格收购B公司，它就需要以每股10美元的价格发行1000万股股票。但如果其股价为20美元，那么它只需发行500万股股票即可完成收购。这对许多企业及其现有股东来说是一个重要考量因素，因为他们不希望因企业发行更多股票而导致自身持股被稀释。

<!--en-->
At other times, a company will pay for an acquisition using its stock. This means that the company will give the owners of the company it is acquiring shares of stock. To do so, the acquirer will often have to file documents with the SEC to sell the additional shares. These filings disclose lots of information about the transaction. Companies often like to use stock to pay for acquisitions when their stock price is high compared to its historical valuation. The rationale behind such transactions is this: The higher the stock price, the fewer shares a company has to issue to fund an acquisition. If Company A agrees to buy Company B for $100 million, it would have to issue 10 million shares at $10 each. But if its stock is trading at $20, then it would only have to issue 5 million shares to fund the deal. That is an important consideration for many companies and their existing shareholders, who do not like to see their holdings diluted by the company issuing more stock.

企业也可以将债务纳入收购价格之中。如果被收购公司在账面上欠银行或其他贷款机构的钱，它可能希望收购方能承担这些债务并作为收购的一部分偿还这些贷款。如果收购方不承担卖方的债务，而卖方账面上仍有债务，负责报道该事件的记者就需要弄清楚这些债务将如何偿还，尤其是当报道的重点更多放在卖方而非买方时。被承担的债务通常被视为企业收购价格的一部分。如果一家企业用1.5亿美元现金加上5000万美元的债务承担额来收购另一家公司，那么总收购价格通常被视为2亿美元。这就是收购方最终需要为该交易支付的全部金额。

<!--en-->
Companies can also factor in debt as part of the purchase price. If the company being acquired owes money to banks or other lenders on its books, it may want the acquiring company to assume the debt and pay off those loans as part of the acquisition. If the acquirer is not assuming the debt from the seller and there are debts on the seller's books, it is important for a reporter covering the story to find out how this debt will be repaid, particularly if the coverage is focused more on the seller than the buyer. Assumed debt is often considered part of the purchase price of a company. If a company buys another company for $150 million in cash plus the assumption of $50 million in debt, the total purchase price is often considered to be $200 million. That is the total amount of money the acquiring company will eventually have to pay for the deal.

并非所有的收购价格都是如此明确。在Anthem/Trigon的收购案中，Anthem同意以现金和股票相结合的方式收购Trigon。其他情况下，收购可能是仅用现金，或是用股票加债务承担；还有些交易则可能是三者的混合。显然，收购方希望以最有利的方式安排收购资金的支付方式。如果企业的股价较低，它可能不想使用股票，尤其是当它认为股价很快会上涨时。股票也可能被用来吸引被收购公司的管理层继续留在公司工作。如果被收购公司的管理层也是股东的话……

<!--en-->
Not all acquisition prices are this cut and dried. In the Anthem/Trigon acquisition, Anthem agreed to purchase Trigon for a combination of cash and stock. Other times, an acquisition will be for cash and assumed debt or stock and assumed debt. Other deals could be a mix of all three. Obviously, what the buying company wants to do is structure how it pays for an acquisition in the most advantageous way. If the company's stock price is low, it may want to avoid using stock, particularly if it thinks that the stock price is going to go up soon. Stock may also be used to entice the management of the selling company to remain with the operation. If the management of the selling company are shareholders and

## 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《交易》杂志编辑Robert Teitelman关于报道并购案的建议：

<!--en-->
The Deal editor Robert Teitelman's tips on covering mergers and acquisitions:

## 这笔交易将如何获得资金支持？

<!--en-->
*How will it be financed?*

现金、股票、债务，还是三者结合？最理想的交易方式是用现金收购另一家公司。但很多时候，用股票支付或举债会更高效或更必要。通过贷款或债务市场为交易融资会带来风险。这里存在几个问题：这笔交易能否获得融资？融资成本是否不会在未来限制买方的经营？债务会带来多大的负担？买方是否需要艰难地偿还债务，从而给业务运营带来更多压力？买方是否会受到银行契约的约束，进而限制其灵活性或迫使它削减研发等投资？

<!--en-->
Cash, stock, debt, a combination? The cleanest deals involve the purchase of another company with cash. But it's often efficient or necessary to pay in stock, or raise debt. The need to finance a deal in the loan or debt markets adds risk. There are several issues here. Can the deal be financed, or at a price that won't limit the buyer in the future? How onerous a burden will the debt prove to be? Will the buyer have to struggle to pay down debt, putting more pressure on operations? Will the buyer find itself restrained by bank covenants that will limit its flexibility or force it to reduce investments like R&D?

136 • Let's Make a Deal：在交易中，买方会获得被收购公司的股票，这会激励他们留在公司里，努力通过改善业绩来推高股价。而如果卖方股东认为买方的股价不会再上涨，他们可能会与买方协商，要求获得更多现金；如果他们认为股价很快会上涨，则可能会要求获得更多股票。

<!--en-->
136 • Let's Make a Deal they receive stock in the acquired company as part of the deal, then they have an incentive to remain with the company to try to drive the stock price higher by improving the results. Shareholders of the selling company, in turn, may negotiate to receive more cash from the acquirer if they believe that the stock price of the buyer is not going to get any higher. Or they may ask for more stock if they believe that the stock price could rise soon.

现金、股票和债务之间的平衡是买方与卖方谈判的一部分。此外，税收也会影响交易是采用现金、股票还是债务形式。许多小型企业的所有者选择以现金出售资产，这类收入会被视为资本利得并征税。尽管如此，私人企业的所有者仍可能寻求纯现金交易，因为他们不想继续成为被收购公司的股东。如果他们确实获得了股票，往往会在交易后一两年内卖掉所持股份。

<!--en-->
The balance between cash, stock, and debt is part of the negotiating process between the buyer and the seller. In addition, taxes may play a part in whether a transaction uses cash, stock, or debt. Many owners of small companies sell for cash, which is taxed as a capital gain. Despite this, owners of private companies may look for strictly cash deals because they do not want to remain stockholders in the purchasing company. If they do receive stock, many times the owners will sell their holdings within a year or two of the deal.

通常，一家公司会在投资银行的帮助下确定愿意出多少钱来收购另一家公司。投资银行会对比被收购企业与其所在行业其他公司的表现，同时评估目标企业的未来前景以及行业内的其他收购案例，从而为潜在的收购方提供一个价格范围。一般来说，收购方的董事会会根据投资银行提供的信息，向目标公司的董事会提出收购报价。这种报价通常以信件的形式呈现，如果相关公司是上市公司，该信件后来还会被披露在SEC的文件中。偶尔，买方会在信中提出所谓的“价格区间保障”。这种保障旨在确保向卖方支付最低金额，也可作为激励管理层/所有者留任、而非离开去创办竞争性企业的手段。

<!--en-->
Often, a company determines what it is willing to pay to buy another company with the help of an investment banker. An investment banker reviews the performance of the business being acquired compared to other companies in the same industry. The bankers also review the target's future prospects and other acquisitions in the industry and give the potential acquirer a range of prices to pay. Typically, the board of the acquiring company, on the basis of the information from its investment banker, makes an offer to the board of the company it wants to buy. This can often be in the form of a letter, often later released in SEC filings if the companies are public. Occasionally, in the letter, a buyer will offer what is known as a collar. A collar is often offered to guarantee a minimum payment to the seller and can be used as incentive for management/owners to stay on board rather than to leave to perhaps start a competing business.

目标公司可以选择接受报价，也可以拒绝并等待更高的价格。当两家公司最终就价格达成一致时，通常会发布新闻稿，大肆赞扬合并后的企业将在未来多年取得成功。但正如任何持怀疑态度的商业记者所知，真正的考验是在一两年后的实际业绩。

<!--en-->
The target can choose to accept the offer or to reject it and hold out for a higher price. When the two companies finally agree on a price, a news release is typically issued with glowing praise about how the combined operations will be a success for many years to come. But, as any skeptical business writer knows, the proof is in the results a year or two later.

## 好交易与坏交易

<!--en-->
*Good Deals and Bad Deals*

如前所述，并非所有的并购都能让收购方和被收购方都受益。只要具备基本的并购运作知识，商业记者就能判断某笔交易是好是坏。

<!--en-->
As mentioned earlier, not every merger or acquisition works for both the acquiring and selling company. And with just a basic knowledge of how mergers and acquisitions work, a business reporter can determine if the deal is good or bad.

判断一笔交易对收购方而言是成功还是失败的首要指标，是其是否能立即提升或稀释收购方的每股收益。能够提升每股收益的并购，会直接增加收购方的每股盈利。这种情况发生在收购方的市盈率高于被收购企业时。例如，如果收购方的市盈率为18，而被收购企业的市盈率为14，那么这就是一项能提升每股收益的并购。（关于市盈率的详细内容，请参见第9章。）而能稀释每股收益的并购，则会导致收购方的每股盈利下降。这种情况发生在收购方的市盈率低于被收购企业时。通常，公司在宣布并购的新闻稿中会说明该并购是能提升还是稀释每股收益。如果新闻稿中没有这些信息，分析师或投资者很可能会在讨论该交易的电话会议上提出这个问题。Let's Make a Deal • 137 通常，投资者希望并购能够提升或至少保持每股收益不变。毕竟，他们购买一家公司的股票正是基于对公司盈利增长的预期。而能稀释每股收益的并购则会导致盈利下降。为了安抚投资者，进行此类并购的公司往往会声称，这项交易将在明年或后年开始为盈利做出贡献。通过改善被收购企业的业绩，他们甚至可以将原本能稀释每股收益的并购转变为能提升每股收益的并购。

<!--en-->
The first indicator of whether a transaction is going to be successful or unsuccessful for the acquirer is if it is immediately accretive or dilutive to the acquiring company's earnings. An acquisition that is accretive immediately adds to the acquiring company's earnings per share. This happens when the price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio is higher at the acquiring firm than at the business being purchased. If the acquiring company has a P/E ratio of 18, but the company being acquired has a P/E ratio of 14, then it is an accretive acquisition. (For a review of P/E ratio, see Chapter 9.) A dilutive acquisition is one in which the acquiring company's earnings per share decrease as a result of the deal. This happens when the P/E is lower at the company making the purchase than at the company being sold. Typically, a company will state in the release announcing the acquisition whether the acquisition is accretive or dilutive. If this information is not in therelease, an analyst or an investor will likely ask this question on a conference call discussing the transaction.
Let's Make a Deal • 137
Investors typically want mergers and acquisitions to be accretive, or at least neutral, to earnings. After all, these are the people who buy a company's stock believing that earnings will rise. A dilutive acquisition makes earnings go down. To appease its investors, a company making a dilutive acquisition will often state that the deal will begin to add to earnings in the next year or the year after that. It can turn a dilutive acquisition into an accretive acquisition by improving the results of the acquired company.

收购完成后，记者应持续关注该公司将所购业务整合进自身运营的进展。需通过其季度财报来判断该收购是否真正提升了盈利水平。通常，企业会在财报中夸耀其并购活动的成功。如果财报中没有相关信息，分析师或投资者往往会要求在财报电话会议上了解收购进展的最新情况。若仍无回应，记者可直接向公司询问。如果本应提升盈利的并购并未达到预期效果，那便是一个值得深入调查的选题。

<!--en-->
After the acquisition is complete, a reporter should follow the company's progress in integrating the purchased business into its own operations. Watch its quarterly earnings for any indication of whether the acquisition actually was accretive to earnings. Often, companies trumpet the success of their deal-making in earnings releases. If that information is not in a release, an analyst or investor will typically ask for updates on an acquisition's progress during an earnings conference call. If that does not happen, a reporter can always ask the company. If a deal that was supposed to be accretive has not been, that is a potential story and warrants further investigation.

有些并购也会失败，原因是战略匹配度不佳。企业认为必须扩张业务才能保持成功，因而选择收购其他公司。但事实并非总是如此。一家企业在某个业务领域取得成功，并不意味着它能将这种成功复制到其他业务上。

<!--en-->
Deals also go bad because they are a bad strategic fit. Companies acquire other companies believing that they need to expand their operations to continue to be successful. But that is not always true. Just because a company has been successful in one business does not mean it can translate that success into another operation.

正如本章前文所述，以夏洛特为总部的第一联合银行在与华盛顿互惠银行合并之前就遭遇了困境。1998年，第一联合银行决定扩大贷款业务并成为该领域的领军者，于是收购了“货币商店”公司。然而两年后，它便关闭了贷款业务，这实际上意味着对“货币商店”的收购彻底失败。《商业周刊》的希瑟·蒂蒙斯（2000年）在收购公告发布后不久的文章中解释了这一失败的原因。她指出，第一联合银行为关闭这家消费贷款机构而计提了26亿美元的费用，同时透露该银行每股34美元的收购报价比该公司原本愿意接受的报价高出25%。此外，第一联合银行支付的金额约为“货币商店”盈利的20倍，而竞争对手美国银行收购类似公司的价格仅为其盈利的8倍左右。此次收购失败的原因是第一联合银行为“货币商店”支付的价格远高于其他竞争对手的报价。蒂蒙斯利用市盈率来对比第一联合银行的支付金额与其他公司的支付水平，还指出该银行低估了面向低收入群体的贷款业务价值。

<!--en-->
Consider what happened to First Union, the Charlotte-based bank, before it merged with Wachovia, as was noted earlier in this chapter. In 1998, First Union decided it wanted to expand its lending operations and become a major player in that business, so it purchased The Money Store. Two years later, however, First Union shuttered its lending business, effectively saying that the acquisition of The Money Store was a colossal flop. Heather Timmons (2000) of *BusinessWeek* explained why this deal failed in a story soon after the announcement. She noted that First Union took a $2.6 billion charge to earnings to shut the consumer lender, and her reporting disclosed that First Union's $34-a-share offer for the company was 25 percent more than what the company would have accepted. In addition, First Union paid about 20 times The Money Store's earnings, whereas rival Bank of America paid about eight times earnings for a similar company. This deal failed because First Union paid much more for The Money Store than competitors were paying for similar operations. Timmons used P/E ratios to compare what First Union paid to what others paid. She also noted that First Union underestimated the business of lending to low-income consumers.

在撰写报道时，始终要将某家公司为并购支付的金额与其他公司收购类似业务所支付的金额进行比较。通过对比市盈率等指标，就能让读者判断该公司是否支付过高。安森保险收购特里贡公司就是另一个例子。在医疗管理行业，企业会根据医疗计划中每位成员的成本来决定收购价格。安森保险为特里贡公司的业务支付的费用，高于其他竞争对手收购类似公司时的价格。意识到这种对比重要性的记者会及时向读者披露这一高昂的收购价格。

<!--en-->
In a story, it is always important to compare what a company is paying in acquisition to what other companies have paid to acquire similar businesses. Such a comparison of P/E multiples, or other barometers, gives the reader an indication of whether a company is overpaying. Another example of this is illustrated by the Anthem acquisition of Trigon. In the managed care business, companies base their acquisitions on the price per member in the managed care plans. Anthem paid more per member for Trigon's operations than competitors had paid for similar companies. Reporters who knew the importance of such a comparison dutifully reported the high price for their readers.

## 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《交易》栏目编辑罗伯特·泰特尔曼关于报道并购案的技巧：

<!--en-->
The Deal editor Robert Teitelman's tips on covering mergers and acquisitions:

**价格与溢价？**与价格相关的关键指标包括目标公司盈利的倍数以及股价的溢价幅度。不同行业的倍数存在差异：快速增长的技术公司的收购倍数会高于增长缓慢的制造企业。为了击败竞标者或说服不愿出售的公司，溢价可能会上升。大型企业有能力为小型目标公司支付更高的溢价，尤其是涉及技术领域的收购，但过高的价格和溢价会加大财务上的合理性论证难度，这也解释了为何在牛市中会出现更多定价过高的并购案。需要思考的问题是：目标公司的内在价值是多少？138 • 让我们达成交易。《商业周刊》的文章提到了资产减值，即对盈利的扣除，这对于任何希望判断并购是否成功的财经记者来说都是一个重要因素。对买方而言成功的并购不会产生任何资产减值，顾名思义，资产减值是指企业因某项资产的市场价值高于其账面价值，而将其价值在财务报表中下调的做法。这通常会作为一项费用体现在利润表上，从而降低净利润。

<!--en-->
**Price and premium?** The key metrics on price involve the multiple of price to the target's earnings and premium over the stock price. Multiples vary depending on industry; an acquisition of a fast-growing tech company will be larger than a slow-growing manufacturer. Premiums may rise with cost reductions, to beat out a bidder or convince an unwilling seller. Larger companies may pay a larger premium for smaller targets, particularly if technology is involved, because they can afford to. But a higher price and premium makes it tougher to justify financially, which explains why in a bull market more overpriced deals occur. Question to ask: What's the intrinsic value of the target?
138 • Let's Make a Deal
The *BusinessWeek* story mentions a writedown, or a charge to earnings, which is an important factor for any business writer looking to determine whether a merger or acquisition was successful. A deal that worked for the buyer will not have any writedowns, which are exactly what they sound like. A writedown is when a company reduces the value of an asset on its financial statement because that asset is overvalued compared to market values for similar assets. This typically shows up on the income statement as an expense, thereby lowering net income.

在并购案例中，被减值的资产往往是被收购企业的资产。当这些资产被减值时，公司实际上是在表明自己为该企业支付了过高的价格，因此不得不降低所购资产的估值。换言之，这笔交易是失败的。商业报告应将任何公司减值资产的行为视为其近期并购失败的表现。相反，如果一家公司没有对资产进行减值，那就意味着它可能完成了与自身业务高度契合的并购。这种减值通常被称为商誉减值损失，因为被减值的正是所购买的商誉价值。当企业为某企业支付的金额高于仅根据其资产和负债价值所能估算的金额时，就会产生商誉。商誉可被视为公司客户群体的忠诚度或门店所在地的优势。

<!--en-->
In the case of acquisitions, the assets that get written down are often the assets of the business that was purchased. When the assets are written down, what a company is essentially saying is that it paid too much for the business and is now being forced to lower the value of the assets it purchased. In other words, the deal was a flop. Business reports should look at any company writing down its assets as a sign that an acquisition it made in the recent past failed. Conversely, if a company is not writing down its assets, that means it probably made an acquisition that fit nicely into its operations. Writedowns are commonly called goodwill impairment charges because what is being written down is the value of the goodwill purchased. Goodwill arises when more was paid for the business than would be expected from just looking at the value of its assets and liabilities. Goodwill can be considered to be the loyalty of a company's customers or the locations of its stores.

《旧金山纪事报》上的以下文章很好地解释了为何企业会将商誉损失计入利润，以及这如何影响公司的业绩：

<!--en-->
The following article in the *San Francisco Chronicle* does an excellent job explaining why companies take goodwill charges to earnings and how this affects a company's performance:

如果在鸡尾酒会上想赶走某人，“商誉减值”似乎是个不错的话题。

<!--en-->
"Goodwill impairment" sounds like a good topic to bring up if you want to shoo off somebody at a cocktail party.

这与追加保证金和资本利得税一样，都是股票投资者不愿去考虑的话题之一。

<!--en-->
It's one of those subjects stock investors would rather not think about, right up there with margin calls and capital gains taxes.

但随着一家又一家公司核销数十亿美元的减值商誉，人们不禁要问到底发生了什么，自己是否应该关心？

<!--en-->
But as one company after another writes off billions of dollars worth of impaired goodwill, you have to ask yourself what the heck is going on here, and should I care?

JDS Uniphase上周宣布了创纪录的448亿美元商誉减值，这一数额仅比加利福尼亚州明年在K-12教育上的支出少10亿美元。

<!--en-->
JDS Uniphase last week announced a record-breaking goodwill write-down of $44.8 billion, which is less than a billion shy of the amount California will spend on K-12 education in the next year.

在最近一个季度中，其他出现巨额商誉减值的公司还包括北电网络（124亿美元）、康宁（48亿美元）和VeriSign（99亿美元）。但迄今为止我们所看到的减值可能只是冰山一角。

<!--en-->
Other companies taking large goodwill charges in the latest quarter include Nortel Networks ($12.4 billion) Corning ($4.8 billion) and VeriSign ($9.9 billion). But the write-downs we've seen so far might be the tip of the iceberg.

雷曼兄弟的税务与会计分析师罗伯特·威伦斯表示：“明年的第一季度——哇，你肯定不会相信，会有数千亿美元的商誉减值。”原因如下：

<!--en-->
"In the first quarter of next year—wow, you won't believe it. There will be hundreds of billions of dollars" in goodwill write-downs," says Robert Willens, a tax and accounting analyst with Lehman Bros.
Here's why:

当一家公司以高于其可辨认资产价值减去债务后的金额收购另一家公司时，就会产生商誉。商誉被认为代表着公司那些无法明确计量的无形资产，如声誉、客户群和员工队伍。

<!--en-->
Goodwill is created when a company buys another firm for more than the value of its identifiable assets minus its debts. Goodwill supposedly represents a company's unidentified intangible assets, such as its reputation, customer base and workforce.

财务会计准则委员会的项目经理金·佩特罗内说：“正是这些无形资产让整个公司的价值超过各部分之和。”财务会计准则委员会最近改变了企业核算商誉的方式。在旧规则下，企业必须随着时间推移逐步“摊销”或核销固定比例的商誉，这种减值会减少企业的营业利润。人们希望合并后产生的利润能够弥补额外的费用。

<!--en-->
"It's what makes the whole worth more than the sum of the parts," says Kim Petrone, a project manager with the Financial Accounting StandardsBoard. The FASB recently changed the way companies must account for goodwill.
Let's Make a Deal • 139
Under the old rules, a company has to “amortize” or write off a fixed portion of goodwill over time. This write-down reduces a company’s operating earnings. The hope is that the merger will create enough earnings to exceed the added charge.

每当企业发现其商誉已出现“减值”，即被收购公司的实际价值低于最初预估时，就必须进行进一步的减值处理。

<!--en-->
Companies are supposed to take an additional write-down any time they discover their goodwill has become “impaired,” which means the purchased company isn’t worth as much as they originally thought.

由于商誉减值并不涉及工资或超级碗广告等现金支出，分析师在评估企业的业绩和前景时常常忽略它。但这并不意味着你就应该忽略它。

<!--en-->
Because goodwill charges don’t represent cash outlays such as salaries or Super Bowl ads, analysts often ignore them when valuing a company’s performance and prospects. But that doesn’t mean you should.

购买与权益合并：只有当企业在会计处理上将某项并购视为“购买”交易时，才会产生商誉。

<!--en-->
PURCHASE VS. POOLING: Goodwill is only created when a company treats an acquisition, for accounting purposes, as a “purchase” transaction.

根据会计规则，被视为“权益合并”的并购不会产生商誉。尽管权益合并存在弊端，但许多企业仍更倾向于采用这种方式，因为可以避免商誉减值。

<!--en-->
Under accounting rules, acquisitions treated as “pooling of interests” do not generate goodwill. Although pooling deals have drawbacks, many companies have preferred them because they could avoid goodwill charges.

为了创造更加公平的竞争环境，财务会计准则委员会最近出台了新规则——第141号准则，禁止权益合并。6月30日之后宣布的所有并购都必须按照购买法进行核算，这意味着所有合并都可能产生商誉。

<!--en-->
To create a more level playing field, the FASB recently adopted a new rule—Statement 141—that outlaws pooling. All acquisitions announced after June 30 must be accounted for under the purchase method, which means all mergers will potentially create goodwill.

财务会计准则委员会的另一个新规则——第142号准则规定，企业不再需要按固定时间表对商誉进行摊销。

<!--en-->
The FASB’s other new rule—Statement 142—says companies will no longer have to amortize goodwill on a fixed schedule.

取而代之的是，企业只需根据第142号准则中规定的新方法，在确定商誉已出现减值时才进行减值处理。这一新方法取代了企业目前使用的多种不同核算方式。

<!--en-->
Instead, they will only have to take write-downs when they determine goodwill has become impaired under a new method spelled out in Statement 142. The new method replaces several different methods companies use now.

那些并购并未失败的公司的确能从新规则中受益，因为它们无需再计提季度商誉减值准备。基因泰克、万豪等公司早已估算出这一会计政策变动将如何影响其明年的盈利水平。³在评估并购时，除了战略不匹配、价值增值/稀释以及资产减记之外，商业记者还需考虑其他几方面因素。有时，并购的架构设计对其未来的成败具有至关重要的意义。

<!--en-->
Companies whose acquisitions haven’t gone sour will benefit from the new rule because they won’t have to take quarterly goodwill charges. Genentech, Marriott and other companies have already estimated how much the accounting change will add to earnings next year.³
There are a couple of other things for business reporters to consider, in addition to bad strategic fits, accretion/dilution, and writedowns, when assessing acquisitions. Sometimes, how the acquisition is structured can be vitally important to its future success.

20世纪80年代，许多公司都是通过所谓的杠杆收购方式被收购的。杠杆收购通常是指公司将自身出售给管理层及其他投资者，这些投资者承担部分收购成本，而剩余资金则通过借贷或发行债券等债务工具来筹集。随后，管理层希望通过对公司进行有效管理来赚取足够现金，以偿还债务或债券。

<!--en-->
In the 1980s, many companies were acquired in what is called a leveraged buyout, or an LBO. An LBO typically occurs when the company is sold to its management and other investors, who put up part of the cost to buy the company but fund the rest of the acquisition by borrowing money, or issuing debt such as bonds. The management then hopes that it can raise enough cash by managing the company to repay the debt or bonds.

为了筹集现金，管理层常常会出售公司的部分业务。20世纪80年代的一些杠杆收购项目最终失败了，原因就是相关公司无法

<!--en-->
Often, the management sells parts of the company to help raise the cash. Some of these LBOs of the 1980s failed when the company was not able to

## 专家建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《The Deal》杂志编辑罗伯特·泰特尔曼关于报道并购的建议：**该交易是复杂还是简单？**在大多数情况下，简单的交易——即用现金完成收购，没有诉讼或监管问题，且双方企业文化相似——比复杂的交易更容易达成。潜在问题的一个迹象是：存在可能用于避税或旨在安抚重要利益方的复杂架构。在经济或金融环境动荡时，诸如约束条款、分手费、禁止竞争条款或认股权证之类的机制变得越来越重要。它们是降低风险的尝试，也是通过谈判达成的，但其存在本身就表明存在潜在的不确定性。需要问的问题是：为何要采用某些特定的架构？

<!--en-->
The Deal *editor Robert Teitelman’s tips on covering mergers and acquisitions:*
**Is it complex or simple?** In most cases, a simple transaction—cash, a takeover, no litigation or regulatory issues, similar cultures—is easier to close than a more complex deal. One sign of underlying issues: A complex structure that may involve tax avoidance or be designed to placate major interests. Devices like collars, breakup fees, no-shop provisions or warrants grow more important in volatile economic or financial conditions. They represent attempts to reduce risk, and are arrived at by negotiation, but their presence suggests an underlying uncertainty. Question to ask: Why are certain structures employed?

### 专家建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《The Deal》杂志编辑罗伯特·泰特尔曼关于报道并购的建议：**这是哪种类型的并购：恶意收购、平等合并还是收购？**它是通过债务融资的私募股权收购，还是单纯的收购？许多战略性收购由于业务存在重叠，因此能够实现“更轻松”的成本削减。而杠杆收购往往缺乏这种优势，由此产生的债务会给企业带来更大的压力，迫使它们寻找其他方式来降低成本或增加现金流。（有些收购属于附加式收购，这类收购可能更容易实现成本削减。）负责设计杠杆收购的财务赞助方通常需要三到七年的时间才能看到回报。需要问的问题是：卖方选择了哪种方式——收购还是企业合并？[^1624]：³摘自K. Pender于2001年8月2日发表在《旧金山纪事报》B1版的文章《大规模商誉减值表明公司进行了糟糕的收购；JDS Uniphase位居计提减值的公司榜单之首》，版权归2001年《旧金山纪事报》所有，经许可转载。140 • 让我们达成交易

<!--en-->
The Deal *editor Robert Teitelman’s tips on covering mergers and acquisitions:*
**What kind of merger is it: a hostile takeover, a merger of equals or an acquisition?** Is it a private equity acquisition, which involves financing with debt, or a straightforward takeover? Many strategic acquisitions involve “easier” cost reductions because of overlapping operations. An LBO will often lack these, and the resulting debt will put pressure to find other ways to cut costs or boost cash flow. (Some buyouts are bolt-ons, which may have easier cost reductions.) The firm that engineers an LBO, a financial sponsor, will usually have from three to seven years to see a return. Question to ask: What did the seller opt for—either a buyout or a corporate acquisition?
