## 经济形势发生变化的概率有多大？

<!--en-->
*What are the odds of economic change?*

市场状况是动态变化的。人们往往倾向于将当前的状况推演到未来，这正是企业陷入沉重债务或抱有过于乐观预期的原因。根据不同情况，并购交易可能需要八个月甚至一年的时间才能完成，在此期间股市、资本市场和监管环境都可能发生变化。那些成本高昂、结构复杂且需要多年整合的交易，其经济风险更大。而转型型交易从定义上就是面向未来的——也是所有交易中风险最高的类型（可参考AOL与时代华纳的案例）。需要问的问题是：在经济状况急剧恶化的情况下，这项交易还会是原来的样子吗？企业可以通过削减广告开支、裁减门店员工等手段来控制成本，但这样做的结果可能是门店销售额下降。如果记者正在撰写关于某次并购的文章，尤其是涉及管理层参与收购的情况，他或她应当始终关注该交易的架构设计。并非所有的杠杆收购都会失败，但很多此类收购最终导致企业破产或被迫出售业务以筹集资金。

<!--en-->
Conditions are dynamic. There's a tendency to extrapolate current conditions into the future, which is how companies get caught with crushing debt or wildly optimistic assumptions. M&A deals can take up to eight months or a year to close, depending on various issues, in which time the stock market, capital markets and regulatory climate can change. An expensive, complex deal that will require years of integration involves greater economic risk. A transformational deal is by definition future oriented— and the riskiest deal of all (see AOL and Time Warner). Question to ask: What will the deal look like in a dramatically worse economy?
generate the cash to repay the debt. This can happen if a company cuts expenses, such as advertising and store employees, in a bid to control costs, but the result is lower sales in its stores. If a reporter is writing about an acquisition, particularly one in which the management has been involved in buying the business, he or she should always look at how the transaction is structured. Not all LBOs failed. But many resulted in companies that ended up in bankruptcy court or were forced to sell operations to raise money.

杠杆收购之所以流行，是因为管理团队可以先掌管公司数年，之后通过首次公开募股出售公司股票——实质上就是将公司卖给公众。如此一来，许多高管就能通过出售股票变得富有。尽管杠杆收购已不像过去那样频繁发生，但仍有部分收购案的设计能让管理层从中获利。有些公司会在公司章程中加入所谓的“黄金降落伞”条款，规定若公司被出售，管理层可获得数百万美元的补偿。公司通常会设置黄金降落伞以抵御不希望出现的收购，比如恶意收购。但如果公司决定出售自己，且章程中包含此类条款，那么在交易过程中失去工作的高管仍能获得股票期权、奖金或一次性付款。在某些案例中，高管们获得的补偿高达数千万美元。商业记者应在美国证券交易委员会的文件中寻找黄金降落伞相关条款；如果发现此类协议，便有了报道素材。

<!--en-->
LBOs became popular because management teams could run the companies for several years and then offer stock in the company in an initial public offering— essentially selling the company to the public. In doing so, many executives became rich by selling their stock. Although LBOs do not occur with as much regularity as they used to, some acquisitions are still structured in ways that allow management to gain financially. Some companies add so-called “golden parachute” language into their corporate bylaws that allows management to receive millions of dollars should the business be sold. A company often implements a golden parachute to fend off an unwanted takeover, such as a hostile takeover. But should a company decide to sell itself and its bylaws contain this language, its executives would receive stock options, bonuses, or lump-sum payments if they lost their jobs as part of the transaction. In some cases, executives have received tens of millions of dollars. Business reporters should look for golden parachute language in the SEC filings. If reporters find such agreements in the filings, they have got a story.

这些交易还包含了所谓的解约费。解约费是指在收购交易因某种原因失败时，参与收购的公司必须向另一家公司支付的费用。在某些情况下，解约费会被设定得很高，以此阻止公司破坏交易。与黄金降落伞类似，这些解约费也常常会在与交易相关的美国证券交易委员会文件中被披露。存在解约费或黄金降落伞并不意味着该交易好或坏，但它们都是可能涉及巨额款项的重要支付项，足以成为报道的素材。

<!--en-->
Transactions also have what are called break-up fees built into them. A break-up fee is money that a company involved in an acquisition must pay to the other company should the transaction fall through for some reason. In some cases, the break-up fee is set high to discourage a company from breaking the deal. Like golden parachutes, these break-up fees are often disclosed in the SEC filings related to a deal. The existence of a break-up fee, or of a golden parachute for that matter, does not mean that a deal is bad or good. But they are important potential payments of large sums of money that could result in stories.

另一个需要考虑的重要因素是该公司是否制定了毒丸计划。如果公司不想被收购，毒丸计划能帮助其抵御来自其他公司的收购。该计划允许除潜在收购方之外的公司股东以更低价格购买更多公司股份，迫使潜在收购方支付远高于其原本期望的价格。

<!--en-->
Another important factor to consider is whether a company has adopted a poison pill statement. This allows a company to fend off an acquisition from another company if it does not want to sell. The poison pill allows a company's shareholders, other than the potential acquirer, to purchase additional shares in the company at a lower price. This forces the potential acquirer to have to pay much more than it would typically want to.

有时交易在完成前就会破裂。可能会有其他买家介入并出更高的价格，导致原买家退出协议；或者进行收购的公司遇到财务困难，不得不放弃交易。在其他情况下，政府监管机构也可能叫停交易。在某些情形下，如果被收购公司的经营状况发生巨大变化，收购价格也可能会重新协商。这些细节同样可以在公司的文件中找到。

<!--en-->
Sometimes deals fall apart before they are completed. Another buyer may step in and offer more money, and the original buyer may bow out of the agreement. Or a company making an acquisition may run into financial difficulty and be forced to back away from a transaction. In other instances, government regulators may scuttle a deal. In some cases, the purchase price may be renegotiated if the performance of the company being sold changes dramatically. These are also details that reporters can find in a company's filings.

## 交易的谈判过程

<!--en-->
*How the Deal was Negotiated*

《旧金山纪事报》关于惠普收购康柏的报道开头讲述了一则趣闻：一位金融分析师问惠普总裁迈克尔·卡佩拉斯是否会跳舞，这暗指这位高管为确保公司能够收购康柏而做出的种种巧妙周旋。“我向来会不惜一切代价，”卡佩拉斯回答后便开始跳舞。这个故事源自公司高管、分析师和投资者之间的一次私人会议。这类分析师、股东、投资组合经理与公司高管之间的会议通常不对公众或记者开放。但聪明的商业记者还是有办法了解这些会议的内容，尤其是涉及并购的会议。《纪事报》的记者在第二段的末尾简要提到了获取这些信息的地方（Pimental, 2001, p. E1）。许多商业记者和编辑在看到公司向美国证券交易委员会提交的S-4文件时会忽略它，但他们应该予以重视。这些文件的重要性在于，它是所有美国证券交易委员会文件中最能讲述完整故事的。当公司希望增发股票并需要股东批准时，就会提交S-4文件。公司想要增发股票的最常见原因是为了进行收购。例如，总部位于伊利诺伊州的亚瑟·J·加拉格尔公司在2008年提交了S-4文件，打算再增发1000万股股票。这家在全国范围内运营保险代理机构的公司在过去几年里一直积极收购小型代理机构：2007年它完成了或宣布了20笔收购，前一年则完成了或宣布了9笔。在提交这份文件后，加拉格尔公司在2008年底前完成了对10家代理机构的收购。因此，加拉格尔公司的S-4文件中包含以下内容也就不足为奇了：

<!--en-->
A story in the *San Francisco Chronicle* about the acquisition of Compaq by Hewlett-Packard leads with an anecdote of a financial analyst asking Hewlett-Packard President Michael Capellas if he could dance, a reference to the fancy footwork done by the executive to ensure his company's acquisition of Compaq. "I have been known to do whatever it takes," replied Capellas before breaking into a dance. This anecdote came from a private meeting between company executives, analysts, and investors. These meetings between analysts, shareholders, portfolio managers, and company executives are not typically open to the public or to reporters. But there is a way for a savvy business reporter to find out what was said during those meetings, particularly if they involve a merger or acquisition. The *Chronicle* reporter makes a brief mention of where this information can be found at the end of his second paragraph (Pimental, 2001, p. E1).
Let's Make a Deal • 141
Many business reporters and editors ignore S-4s when they are filed with the SEC, but they should pay attention to them. These documents are important because they do the best job of any SEC filing at telling a story. An S-4 is filed when a company wants to sell more shares of its stock and needs shareholder approval to do so. The most common reason a company would want to sell more stock is that it wants to make an acquisition. For example, Illinois-based Arthur J. Gallagher & Company filed an S-4 in 2008 to sell an additional 10 million shares of its stock. Gallagher, which operates insurance agencies across the country, has been an active acquirer of smaller agencies in the past few years. In 2007, it made or announced 20 deals. The year before, it made or announced nine deals. After this filing, Gallagher completed deals to buy 10 agencies before the end of 2008. So it should come as no surprise that Gallagher's S-4 filing contains the following language:

> 我们预计将在未来两年内，通过未来的收购活动来发行并出售本招股说明书所涉及的股份。我们预计未来的收购对象主要会是更多的保险经纪业务及相关业务。此类收购的对价可能包括现金（含分期付款）、普通股股票、其他证券（包括可转换为普通股的证券）、担保、负债承担，或上述各项中的任意两项或更多项，具体由我们与拟收购企业或资产的所有者或控制人通过协商确定。此外，我们还可能与被收购企业的前所有者及核心高管人员签订雇佣合同和竞业限制协议。目前，我们正在与多个潜在的收购目标进行初步洽谈。总体而言，每项未来收购的条款将由我们的代表与拟收购企业或资产的所有者或控制人通过协商确定。在确定收购条款时需考虑的因素可能包括拟收购企业的现有质量与声誉及其管理团队、其总佣金收入、盈利能力、现金流、增长潜力、拟收购企业及资产的位置，以及我们预计通过此次收购实现的地域和服务多元化程度。我们预计，在任何未来的收购中发行的普通股，其定价都将与股份交付时纽约证券交易所公布的该股票当时的市场价值保持合理关联。除了被收购公司的现金余额外，我们不期望从此类发行中获得任何其他现金收益。142 • 让我们达成交易（S-4表格，Arthur J. Gallagher & Co.，第11页）诚然，这并非海明威的作品，单凭这一点或许还不足以成为任何出版物刊登故事的依据。但它确实为我们了解Gallagher的收购策略以及其与潜在被收购方谈判的思路提供了一些线索。同时它也向读者表明，该公司很可能在不久的将来宣布更多收购计划。商业记者在与Gallagher的首席执行官讨论其收购策略时，可以利用这些信息。其他S-4表格的披露内容可能更为丰富。以Pulte Homes Incorporated为收购另一家住宅建筑商Centex Corporation而提交的S-4表格为例，其中包含了许多此前未公开的关于该交易的背景信息。据此，《Big Builder News》——一家追踪住宅建筑行业的网站——的记者Sarah Yaussi撰写了一篇精彩的报道。Yaussi的报道涵盖了Centex与Pulte之间的谈判情况，以及还有另外两家有意竞标的公司这一事实。她的报道摘录如下：3月11日，Eller在面对B公司的首席执行官时提出了一种所谓的“平等合并”方案。然而，根据该方案，合并后的公司中Centex的股东将持有51%的股份，而B公司的股东则持有剩余的49%。此外，合并后的公司董事会将由Centex和B公司各选出的成员平分席位，Eller将成为新公司的首席执行官，而公司总部则设在达拉斯。不到一周后，B公司提出了反制方案，使得这种所谓的“平等合并”真正实现平等，即Centex和B公司的股东各持50%的股份。 此外，埃勒将担任合并后公司的首席执行官，但公司总部将迁至B公司的办公地点。⁴ 需要注意的是，S-4申报文件往往是了解收购方与被收购方谈判细节的唯一信息来源。很多时候，公司高管不愿谈论这些谈判内容，有时会以交易尚未完成为借口。对于试图撰写有关收购过程报道的记者而言，S-4申报文件是获取相关背景信息及谈判细节的最佳途径。如果高管们仍不愿开口，应礼貌地提醒他们，这些信息会在S-4文件提交后公开。令人惊讶的是，届时会有许多高管突然愿意透露信息。有时，S-4文件中关于谈判细节和背景的描述，能够揭示本应在数月前就报道的消息。[^1650]：⁴ 摘自莎拉·雅乌西2009年5月11日发表于《Big Builder News》的文章《Pulte S-4：Centex与另外两家竞标方探讨过可能的收购事宜》，2009年10月11日从http://www.bigbuilderonline.com/industry-news.asp?sectionID=363&articleID=963768.检索。版权所有2009年Hanley Wood LLC，经许可转载。《让我们达成协议》•143。美国国际集团为收购HSB集团而提交的用于出售股份的S-4申报文件并未引发众多商业记者的报道，但实际上或许应该有相关报道。该文件包含了此前未公开的细节，例如HSB集团的首席执行官理查德·布斯实际上只是为了推动公司出售才被任命为首席执行官的。然而，在一年前获任该职位后接受记者采访时，布斯并未向媒体透露这一事实。以下的S-4文件详细记载了布斯与AIG首席执行官汉克·格林伯格会面的时间、地点以及交谈内容：作为其推进计划的一部分，布斯与HSB集团当时已有或可能建立战略关系、合资企业或其他联盟的多家机构进行了接洽。其中一次会面发生在2000年4月13日，地点在纽约的AIG总部，参与者为布斯与AIG的董事长兼首席执行官莫里斯·R·格林伯格。他们讨论了行业状况、AIG与HSB集团正在实施的策略，以及两家公司在其各自市场中的优势。在这次会面之前和之后，布斯还与其他行业高层高管会面，探讨能为HSB集团带来战略突破的潜在合作方式。在2000年6月5日的会议上，布斯向HSB集团董事会汇报了迄今为止的调研结果、该集团可选择的各类战略方案，以及对面临的各种运营风险的评估。高盛的代表则与HSB集团董事会探讨了各种关乎股东价值的问题。经过充分讨论后，HSB集团董事会指示并授权布斯探索所有战略选项，包括出售HSB集团的可能性。2000年6月14日，HSB集团聘请高盛作为其财务顾问，协助处理包括可能的出售在内的各类战略交易事宜。高盛联系了九家机构，了解它们对与HSB集团开展战略交易的兴趣程度。在2000年7月24日的会议上，布斯向HSB集团董事会更新了战略选项的相关情况，高盛则与董事会一起分析了股东价值评估问题。经过反复讨论后，基于价格和货币因素，AIG表现出的兴趣被认为优于其他潜在竞标方的兴趣。于是HSB集团董事会授权布斯继续与AIG展开谈判。 2000年7月26日，布斯先生、HSB公司高级副总裁兼财务总监索尔·L·巴斯奇先生，以及HSB公司高级副总裁兼全球保险业务负责人诺曼德·梅尔西埃先生在纽约与格林伯格先生及AIG高层管理人员会面，商讨公司战略以及业务合并可能带来的益处。此后，AIG与HSB展开了尽职调查。HSB向AIG提供了一份拟议的合并协议草案。经过从2000年8月13日那一周初期开始的数天密集谈判，双方最终就交易的核心要素及相关文件达成了共识。⁵ 144 • 让我们立即达成协议 除非CEO允许记者旁听会议，否则商业记者无法从其他渠道获得关于像汉克·格林伯格这样的CEO与谁会面以及讨论了什么内容的第一手信息。不幸的是，这份申报文件并未像某些S-4文件那样详细记载关于收购价格的谈判过程。这类信息有时会在申报文件中出现，有时则不会；而在这份文件中并未提及。撰写并购报道的记者务必留意S-4文件的提交情况。通常，这些文件中所包含的关于交易的细节远多于企业自己在公告中披露的内容。很可能这些文件会透露出该公司的其他竞购方是谁，以及收购价格在谈判过程中是有所上调还是下调。此外，记者还可能由此了解到并购交易的具体架构。然而，那些不知道该查找这类文件的记者往往会对S-4文件视而不见。而那些了解其存在及其所含信息的记者则很可能会让他们的编辑满意。与并购相关的所有公司申报文件都应予以审阅，而不仅仅是S-4文件。一项并购可能会令部分股东不满，他们可能会通过申报文件表明自己打算反对这笔交易。惠普收购康柏时就出现过这样的情况：该公司一位创始人的亲属认为这笔交易对该公司不利。他向美国证券交易委员会提交的申报文件引发了如下彭博新闻社的报道：根据一份监管申报文件，惠普公司董事、公司联合创始人威廉·惠普的儿子沃尔特·惠普将游说股东反对计划中的康柏电脑公司收购案。该申报文件还称，股东兼惠普前首席财务官埃德温·范·布龙克霍斯特、惠普的两位姐妹以及威廉·R·惠普可撤销信托基金也将参与这场代理权争夺战。惠普及其另一位联合创始人的儿子戴维·帕卡德曾批评这笔价值233亿美元的收购，称其会加剧惠普对个人电脑业务的依赖，并导致大量裁员。预计明年年初将举行股东投票。“惠普公开反对这笔交易无疑引发了许多疑问，”持有惠普股票且反对此次收购的Matrix Asset Advisors Inc.公司的首席投资官大卫·卡茨说道，“显然，他会试图阻止这笔交易。”上周，惠普聘请了代理征集机构MacKenzie Partners Inc.，这一举动引发了人们关于惠普会主动出击以争取其他股东支持的猜测。惠普的发言人托德·格拉斯表示，惠普也可能决定不进行代理权争夺战。格拉斯称，提交那份申报文件是为了给惠普留下选择空间，并补充说“惠普先生尚未决定采取何种行动”。[^1666]：⁵ 来自美国国际集团公司于2000年9月15日提交的S-4表格，美国证券交易委员会出版物编号为0000950123-00-008562，第26-30页。华盛顿特区：美国证券交易委员会。 让我们达成协议 • 145 Van Bronkhorst曾是戴维与露西尔·帕卡德基金会的托管人，该基金会持有惠普10.4%的股份，但尚未表明将如何投票决定这笔交易。这两位惠普姐妹分别是埃莉诺·惠普·吉蒙和玛丽·惠普·贾菲。总部位于加利福尼亚州帕洛阿尔托的惠普股价下跌59美分，至21.50美元。总部位于休斯顿的康柏股价则下跌40美分，至10.30美元，这一价格比惠普的收购要约对应的每股价值低24%。弗里德曼·弗莱舍尔与洛威公司以及帕特农集团共同撰写的报告指出，收购康柏“缺乏吸引力”，因为这会令惠普的业务组合变得更差，战略问题无法得到解决，整合风险将“相当大”，而且还会损害股东利益。这份由惠普委托撰写的报告今日已随惠普向美国证券交易委员会提交的文件一同提交。惠普首席执行官卡莉·菲奥莉娜正在努力说服投资者接受她收购康柏的计划。她表示，此次合并将拓宽惠普的产品线，并更注重咨询等利润更高的服务。“我们依然坚信，这项交易是为股东、员工和客户创造价值的最佳方式，”惠普发言人雷贝卡·罗博伊说道。康柏发言人阿奇·柯里德拒绝就惠普向美国证券交易委员会提交的文件发表评论。⁶ 当一家公司参与收购时，商业记者务必仔细审查任何可能与该交易有丝毫关联的内容，因为他们可能会发现一些令人惊讶的信息。

<!--en-->
> We expect to offer and sell the shares covered by this prospectus in connection with future acquisitions within the next two years. We anticipate that our future acquisitions will consist principally of additional insurance brokerage and related businesses. The consideration for such acquisitions may include cash, including installment payments, shares of common stock, other securities including securities which may be converted into common stock, guarantees, assumptions of liabilities, or any two or more of the foregoing, as determined from time to time by negotiations between us and the owners or controlling persons of the businesses or properties to be acquired. In addition, we may enter into employment contracts and non-competition agreements with former owners and key executive personnel of acquired businesses. At this time we are engaged in preliminary discussions with a number of candidates for possible future acquisitions.
In general, the terms of each future acquisition will be determined by negotiations between our representatives and the owners or controlling persons of the businesses or properties to be acquired. The factors taken into account in determining the terms of an acquisition may include the established quality and reputation of the business to be acquired and its management, its gross commission revenues, earning power, cash flow, growth potential, the location of the business and properties to be acquired and the geographical and service diversification we anticipate as a result of the acquisition. We anticipate that shares of our common stock issued in any future acquisition will be valued at a price reasonably related to the then current market value of our common stock as reported on the New YorkStock Exchange at or about the time or times of delivery of the shares. We do not expect to receive any cash proceeds, other than cash balances of acquired companies, in connection with any such issuances.
142 • Let's Make a Deal
(Form S-4, Arthur J. Gallagher & Co., p. 11)
True, this is not Hemingway. And it is probably not enough by itself to warrant a story in virtually any publication. But it does give some insight into Gallagher's acquisition strategy and how it goes about negotiating deals with potential acquirees. It also tells readers that it is likely to announce more deals in the near future. A business reporter can use that information whenever he or she talks to Gallagher's CEO about its acquisition strategy.
Other S-4 filings can be juicier. Consider the S-4 filed by Pulte Homes Incorporated regarding the stock it was issuing as part of its acquisition of fellow homebuilder Centex Corporation. It gave the reader a lot of background about the deal that had not been previously disclosed. The result was a nice story written by Sarah Yaussi, a reporter for *Big Builder News*, an online site that tracks the home building industry.
Yaussi's story covered Centex and Pulte's negotiations, as well as the fact that there were two other interested bidders. The following excerpt from her story reads:
On March 11, Eller presented to Company B's CEO in an in-person meeting a so-called "merger of equals." However, the proposed deal would give Centex shareholders 51% ownership of the combined company and Company B stockholders the remaining 49%. In addition, the combined company board would be an even split between Centex and Company B picks, Eller would be the new company's chief executive, and the combined company's headquarters would be in Dallas.
A little less than a week later, Company B came back with a counteroffer that made the so-called merger of equals actually equal, with ownership split down the middle between Centex and Company B shareholders. Moreover, Eller would assume the combined company's chief executive role but that corporate headquarters would shift to Company B's corporate offices.⁴
Note that the S-4 filing can often be the only source of information detailing the negotiations between acquirer and acquiree. Many times, company executives are not willing to talk about these negotiations. Sometimes, they will give the excuse that the transaction has not yet closed.
For the reporter trying to write a story about how an acquisition came about, the S-4 is the best place to look for background information and details about the negotiations. If executives are not willing to talk, they should be politely reminded that the information will come out when the S-4 is filed. It is surprisinghow many executives suddenly want to talk. Sometimes the level of detail about the negotiations and the background in an S-4 can reveal stories that should have been reported months earlier.
[^1650]: ⁴ From "Pulte S-4: Centex discussed possible acquisition with two other bidders," by Sarah Yaussi, May 11, 2009, *Big Builder News*. Retrieved October 11, 2009 from http://www.bigbuilderonline.com/industry-news.asp?sectionID=363&articleID=963768. Copyright 2009 by Hanley Wood LLC. Reprinted with permission.
Let's Make a Deal • 143
The S-4 filed by American International Group Incorporated to sell shares as part of its acquisition of HSB Group Incorporated did not engender stories from many business reporters, but maybe it should have. The filing included previously undisclosed details, such as the fact that HSB CEO Richard Booth was basically installed as the company's CEO just to sell the company. However, Booth neglected to reveal this to reporters when he was interviewed after being named to the position a year earlier. The following S-4 goes into detail about when and where Booth and AIG CEO Hank Greenberg met and what they talked about:
As part of the process Mr. Booth undertook, he met with a number of entities with which HSB then currently had or might form strategic relationships, joint ventures or other alliances. One such meeting occurred on April 13, 2000, between Mr. Booth and Mr. Maurice R. Greenberg, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of AIG, at AIG's headquarters in New York. They discussed industry conditions, strategies being pursued by AIG and HSB and the competencies of each company in their respective marketplace. Both prior and subsequent to this meeting, Mr. Booth met with other industry senior executives to discuss potential relationships which could provide a strategic breakthrough for HSB.
At a June 5, 2000 meeting, Mr. Booth discussed with the HSB Board the results of his review to date, the various strategic options available to HSB and an evaluation of the various operating risks facing HSB. Representatives of Goldman Sachs discussed various shareholder value issues with the HSB Board. After a thorough discussion, the HSB Board instructed and authorized Mr. Booth to explore all strategic options, including the possible sale of HSB. On June 14, 2000, HSB engaged Goldman Sachs as its financial advisor in connection with possible strategic transactions, including a possible sale of HSB. Goldman Sachs contacted nine entities regarding potential interest in a strategic transaction with HSB. At a July 24, 2000 meeting, Mr. Booth updated the HSB Board on strategic options and Goldman Sachs reviewed shareholder valuation issues with the HSB Board. After considerable discussion, an indication of interest from AIG was judged to be superior, based on price and currency, to indications of interest from other potential bidders. The HSB Board authorized Mr. Booth to proceed with discussions with AIG.
On July 26, 2000, Mr. Booth, Mr. Saul L. Basch, Senior Vice President, Treasurer and Chief Financial Officer of HSB, and Mr. Normand Mercier, Senior Vice President and Chief Global Insurance Officer of HSB, met with Mr. Greenberg and other members of AIG senior management in New York to discuss corporate strategies and the potential benefits of a business combination. Thereafter, AIG and HSB conducted due diligence. AIG was provided with a form of proposed merger agreement by HSB. Following several days of intensive negotiations, commencing early in the week ofAugust 13, 2000, the principal elements of a transaction and related documentation were agreed upon.⁵
144 • Let's Make a Deal
Nowhere else can a business reporter get a first-hand account about with whom a CEO of Hank Greenberg's stature met and what was discussed, except if the CEO lets the reporter sit in on the meetings. Unfortunately, this filing does not detail the haggling about the purchase price, as some S-4s do. Sometimes that information is in the filing, and sometimes it is not.
In this case, it was not there. It is vital that the reporter writing about a merger or acquisition be on the lookout for the filing of the S-4. Often the filing contains many more details about the transaction than the companies will have released in their announcements of the deal. Likely, the filing will divulge who the other bidders for the company were and whether the purchase price was negotiated higher or lower during the process. In addition, the reporter can likely get an important glimpse into the process of how the merger or acquisition was structured. However, reporters who do not know to look for them often ignore S-4s. Those that do know what they are and the information they contain will likely make their editors happy.
All company filings related to an acquisition should be reviewed, not just the S-4. An acquisition could upset some shareholders, who could make it known through filings that they intend to fight the deal. Such a case occurred with Hewlett-Packard's acquisition of Compaq, when a relative of one of the company's founders decided the deal was bad for the company. His filings with the SEC led to stories like the following Bloomberg News report:
Hewlett-Packard Co. director Walter Hewlett, the son of company co-founder William Hewlett, will lobby shareholders to fight the planned acquisition of Compaq Computer Corp., according to a regulatory filing.
Edwin van Bronkhorst, a shareholder and Hewlett-Packard's former chief financial officer, two sisters of Hewlett and the William R. Hewlett Revocable Trust also will participate in the proxy fight, the Securities & Exchange Commission filing said.
Hewlett and David Packard, the son of the company's other cofounder, have criticized the $23.3 billion purchase, saying it would make Hewlett-Packard more reliant on personal-computer sales and require too many layoffs. A shareholder vote is expected early next year.
"Hewlett coming out against the deal definitely raised a number of questions," said David Katz, chief investment officer at Matrix Asset Advisors Inc., which owns Hewlett-Packard shares and opposes the purchase. "Clearly, he is going to try to stop the deal."
Last week, Hewlett hired proxy-solicitation firm MacKenzie Partners Inc., which started speculation that Hewlett would go on the offensive to try to lure other shareholders to his side.
Hewlett may decide not to pursue a proxy fight, said Hewlett spokesmanTodd Glass. The filing was meant to keep Hewlett's options open, Glass said, adding that "Mr. Hewlett has not decided on a course of action."
[^1666]: ⁵ From Form S-4, by American International Group Incorporated, September 15, 2000, SEC Publication No. 0000950123-00-008562, pp. 26-30. Washington, DC: Securities and Exchange Commission.
Let's Make a Deal • 145
Van Bronkhorst is a former trustee of the David and Lucile Packard Foundation, which owns 10.4 percent of Hewlett-Packard's shares and hasn't said how it will vote on the deal. The two Hewlett sisters are Eleanor Hewlett Gimon and Mary Hewlett Jaffe.
Shares of Palo Alto, California-based Hewlett-Packard fell 59 cents to $21.50. Houston-based Compaq fell 40 cents to $10.30, 24 percent less than the per-share value of Hewlett-Packard's acquisition offer.
The acquisition of Compaq is "unattractive" because Hewlett-Packard's business portfolio will become worse, strategic problems won't be solved, integration risks will be "substantial" and the deal will hurt shareholders, a report prepared by Friedman Fleischer & Lowe and The Parthenon Group said. The report, commissioned by Hewlett, was filed with Hewlett's SEC statement today.
Hewlett-Packard Chief Executive Carly Fiorina is pushing investors to accept her plan to acquire Compaq. She has said the combination would broaden Hewlett-Packard's product line and emphasize more-profitable services such as consulting.
"We remain convinced the transaction is the best way to create value for shareholders, employees and customers," said Hewlett-Packard spokeswoman Rebeca Robboy. Compaq spokesman Arch Currid declined to comment on Hewlett's SEC filing.⁶
When a company is involved in an acquisition, it is extremely important that business writers review anything that might seem remotely involved with the deal. They may be surprised at what they find.

## 交易的法律监管

<!--en-->
*Regulatory Oversight of Deals*

尽管收购方与被收购方的董事会都同意了这项收购，但这并不意味着交易就已经完成。在几乎所有情况下，交易的其他参与方也必须批准该交易。例如，在交易最终确定之前，股东们会投票决定是否赞成或反对该交易。通常，公司管理层会争取大股东的同意，让他们投票支持该交易。当惠普宣布收购康柏时，其管理层便花费了大量时间游说股东投票支持这笔交易。

<!--en-->
Just because the board of directors of both the buying and selling companies have agreed on an acquisition does not mean that the transaction is complete. In virtually every case, other participants in the deal must also approve the transaction. For example, shareholders vote whether to approve or turn down a deal before it goes through. Often, a company's management will line up agreements from large shareholders to get them to vote for a deal. When Hewlett-Packard announced its acquisition of Compaq, its management then spent a lot of time wooing shareholders to vote for the deal.

不过，还有另一个重要角色对许多并购案拥有最终决定权，尤其是那些涉及某个行业或业务领域内两大公司的并购案。州级和联邦级的监管机构每年都会审查大量并购案，以判断该交易是否会阻碍某一领域的竞争，或者是否会导致消费者因不公平行为而受损。[^1677]：引自彭博新闻2001年11月16日P. Horvitz撰写的《惠普高管发起并购代理权争夺战》，版权归彭博新闻所有，经许可转载。146 • 让我们达成交易

<!--en-->
But there is another important player that has the final say on many mergers and acquisitions, particularly those that involve the two biggest companies in a certain industry or business. State and federal regulators review many acquisitions each year to determine whether the deal will hinder competition in a certain field or whether consumers will be hurt by a transaction through unfair or
[^1677]: ⁶ From "Hewlett-Packard director to wage merger proxy fight," by P. Horvitz, November 16, 2001, Bloomberg News. Copyright 2001 by Bloomberg News. All rights reserved. Reprinted with permission.
146 • Let's Make a Deal

### 专家建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

*The Deal*杂志编辑罗伯特·泰特尔曼关于报道并购案的技巧：***监管方面：**是否存在可能引发司法部或联邦贸易委员会关注的反垄断问题？或者，像保险、赌场或公用事业领域的交易那样，是否需要逐州获得批准，而这可能会十分复杂且耗时，尤其是在涉及裁员的情况下。如果出现外国买家，该交易是否可能被视为国家安全问题，进而陷入美国外国投资委员会（CFIUS）的审批程序，甚至更糟地被提交给国会处理？多年来，银行类交易一直受到活动人士利用当时尚不为人知的《社区再投资法案》来威胁并购或迫使企业让步的影响。此外还有诉讼——环境诉讼、集体诉讼、员工相关诉讼或股东诉讼。诉讼对规模较小的交易威胁更大。还有欺骗性行为，比如因竞争对手被淘汰而抬高价格。

<!--en-->
The Deal *editor Robert Teitelman's tips on covering mergers and acquisitions:***Regulation:** Is there an antitrust problem looming that may attract the Department of Justice or the Federal Trade Commission? Or might it, like insurance, casino or utility deals, involve state-by-state approvals, which can be difficult and time consuming, particularly if job cuts are involved. If a foreign buyer appears, can the deal be construed as a national security matter, in which case it may get bogged down in the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States (CFIUS), or (worse yet) dragged into Congress. For years, bank deals were hit by activists that used the then-obscure Community Reinvestment Act to threaten mergers or extract concessions. Finally, there's litigation—environmental, class action, employee related or shareholder. Litigation threatens smaller more than larger deals.
deceptive acts or practices, such as higher prices because of the elimination of a competitor.

无论涉及哪个行业，联邦贸易委员会（FTC）都必须对所有并购案进行审查。当一笔交易被宣布后，FTC和司法部有30天的时间来审查该交易。如果交易较为复杂，他们还可以要求再延长30天的审查期。正因如此，在许多宣布交易的新闻稿中，通常会出现“该交易需获得股东及监管机构的批准”这样的表述。FTC的审查包括提交一份哈特-斯科特-罗迪诺报告，这份报告是保密的，几乎总只是走形式而已。

<!--en-->
The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) must review all mergers and acquisitions, no matter what industry the companies are involved in. When a deal is announced, the FTC and the Department of Justice have 30 days to review the transaction. They can request an additional 30-day review period if the deal is complicated. That is why it is typical to see the statement “The transaction is subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals” in many news releases announcing transactions. A review by the FTC involves the filing of a Hart-Scott-Rodino report, which is confidential and almost always a formality.

尽管如此，FTC在交易审查中仍起着重要作用。从1996年到2009年8月31日，FTC共对319起并购案提出了异议。如果FTC审查某项收购并决定反对该交易，它可以在联邦法院申请针对相关企业的初步禁令。从1996年到2009年8月31日，FTC共做了34次这样的申请。法院随后可以颁布临时限制令，阻止交易完成，直到FTC提交行政投诉或启动行政程序为止。有时，FTC只需向交易各方暗示该交易很可能不会获得批准，这一暗示就足以破坏交易——同时也能为跟踪并购进展的财经记者提供素材。

<!--en-->
Still, the FTC plays an important part in reviewing deals. From 1996 through August 31, 2009, the FTC challenged 319 mergers and acquisitions. If the FTC reviews an acquisition and decides to oppose a deal, it can seek a preliminary injunction against the companies in federal court. From 1996 to August 31, 2009, it did so 34 times. The court can then grant a temporary restraining order preventing the deal from being completed until the FTC files an administrative complaint or begins an administrative proceeding. Sometimes, the FTC can simply imply to the companies involved in a transaction that the deal is unlikely to be approved. That nudge can scuttle a deal—and create a story for a business writer tracking the progress of a merger or acquisition.

以下是2009年6月《罗利新闻观察家报》报道的一起案例，该案例中正是由于联邦监管机构的质疑，导致一笔交易失败：

<!--en-->
The following shows a case reported in the *The* (Raleigh) *News & Observer* in June 2009 in which questions about a deal by the federal agency ended a transaction:

周一，随着一家澳大利亚公司31亿美元的收购计划被取消，Talecris Biotherapeutics的高层誓言将继续拓展公司业务。

<!--en-->
The top executive at Talecris Biotherapeutics vowed to continue expanding the company's business, after its $3.1 billion buyout by an Australian company was scrapped Monday.

去年8月宣布的与CSL Ltd.的拟议交易本将成为三角地区规模最大的企业合并之一。Talecris的总部位于研究三角园，在克莱顿还拥有一座大型药品制造工厂。

<!--en-->
The proposed deal with CSL Ltd., announced last August, would have been one of the Triangle's largest corporate marriages. Talecris is based in Research Triangle Park and has a large drug manufacturing plant in Clayton.

但该交易引起了美国联邦贸易委员会的警惕，他们担心这种合并会损害竞争，并推高血浆制剂的价格。上个月，FTC请求联邦法官阻止这笔收购。

<!--en-->
But the deal raised red flags at the U.S. Federal Trade Commission, which worried that the combination would hurt competition and raise prices for medicines made from blood plasma. Last month the FTC asked a federal judge to block the buyout.

CSL和Talecris的官员们表示原本计划通过法律途径对抗FTC，但在周一宣布放弃抗争。关注CSL的分析师们此前就预测，该公司不愿与FTC展开漫长且成本高昂的诉讼。

<!--en-->
CSL and Talecris officials said that they planned to fight the FTC in court but announced on Monday that they were throwing in the towel. Analysts who follow CSL had predicted the company didn't want to wage a long, costly legal battle with the FTC.

这一举措很可能为当地创造就业机会。分析人士原本预计，合并后的公司会在削减成本的过程中裁减部分岗位，尤其是位于Talecris的RTP总部。Talecris在全球拥有约4,750名员工，其中2,000多名在三角地区工作。

<!--en-->
The move likely saves local jobs. Analysts had expected the combined company would eliminate some positions as it reduced costs, especially at Talecris' RTP headquarters. Talecris employs about 4,750 worldwide, including more than 2,000 in the Triangle.

“我们 simply认为继续前行符合所有利益相关方的最佳利益，”Talecris首席执行官Lawrence Stern表示，“我们可以花些时间来评估下一步该采取什么行动。”

<!--en-->
"We simply felt it was in the best interest of all our stakeholders to move on," Talecris CEO Lawrence Stern said. "We can take some time and evaluate what our next best step is."

他补充说，Talecris的财务状况十分稳健，“我们无需采取任何特定措施”。该公司去年报告的营收为14亿美元，较2007年增长了15%以上。Let's Make a Deal • 147 该公司仍在研发新药物，扩大其遍布美国的66家血液血浆中心网络，并招聘新员工。自今年年初以来，Talecris已在北卡罗来纳州新增了222个就业岗位。

<!--en-->
Talecris is in solid financial shape and "we don't need to take any specific action," he added. The company reported revenue of $1.4 billion last year, up more than 15 percent from 2007.
Let's Make a Deal • 147
The company continues to research new medicines, expand its chain of 66 blood-plasma centers across the United States and hire new workers. Since the beginning of the year, Talecris has added 222 jobs in North Carolina.

Stern称，在未来几年内，该公司还计划将一种用于治疗罕见血液凝固疾病的药物的生产地从加州的伯克利转移到克莱顿的工厂。这一举措将为克莱顿带来数量不详的新增就业岗位。

<!--en-->
Over the next several years, the company is also planning to shift production of a drug to treat a rare blood-clotting disease from Berkeley, Calif., to its Clayton plant, Stern said. That move will add an undetermined number of workers in Clayton.

他补充说：“在过去的10个月里，我们持续对业务进行投资，我们认为自己为未来做好了充分准备。”

<!--en-->
"Over the past 10 months, we've continued to invest in the business and we feel we're very well-positioned for the future," he added.

不过，Talecris的股东们很可能会寻找新的买家，或重新考虑首次公开募股的计划。Talecris成立于2005年，当时两家投资公司以3.035亿美元的价格收购了拜耳的血液血浆业务。这两家机构分别是纽约的Cerberus Capital Management和马萨诸塞州韦尔斯利的Ampersand Ventures，它们或许会暂时持有Talecris，但最终仍希望套现。

<!--en-->
Still, Talecris' owners will likely seek another buyer or revive plans for an initial public offering of stock. Talecris was formed in 2005 after two investment firms bought Bayer's blood-plasma business for $303.5 million. Those firms, Cerberus Capital Management of New York and Ampersand Ventures of Wellesley, Mass., could decide to simply hold Talecris for now, but will want to cash out their investment at some point.

Stern说：“只有我们的股权所有者才能决定他们想做什么。”周一尝试联系Cerberus未获回复。

<!--en-->
"Only our equity owners can determine what they want to do," Stern said. Calls to Cerberus weren't returned on Monday.

Stern表示，他在周一通过群发语音邮件和一封书面信件，将CSL交易失败的消息告知了Talecris的员工。“人们为促成这笔交易付出了巨大努力，”他说，“我们的团队已经开始了新的工作。”

<!--en-->
Stern said he notified Talecris employees about the canceled CSL deal on Monday with a mass voice mail message and a letter. "People worked very hard to consummate this transaction," he said. "Our team has already moved on."

尽管交易失败，但对Talecris来说也有积极的一面。根据协议，CSL需向Talecris支付7500万美元的解约费，同时还会继续为Talecris供应血浆。

<!--en-->
The failed deal has a bright spot for Talecris. As part of their agreement, CSL will pay Talecris a $75 million break-up fee. CSL will also continue to supply plasma to Talecris.

美国联邦贸易委员会反对这笔交易，原因是担心合并后的公司会掌控过多的血液血浆药品市场。该委员会在一份法庭文件中写道，此次合并会将生产血液血浆药品的公司数量从5家减少到4家。

<!--en-->
The FTC objected to the deal because of worries that the combined companies would control too much of the market for blood-plasma medicines. The merger would have reduced the number of companies that make medicine for blood plasma from five to four, the FTC wrote in a court filing.

美国联邦贸易委员会写道，这笔交易“有可能大幅削弱几种用于治疗罕见疾病的药品市场的竞争”，“其后果将是供应进一步紧张……价格进一步上涨——甚至可能让重症患者无法获得他们最需要的治疗手段”。

<!--en-->
The deal "threatens to substantially lessen competition in the markets for several" drugs to treat rare diseases, the FTC wrote. "The effect will be further tightening of supply . . . and steeper price increases—potentially leaving critically ill patients without treatments they need most."

CSL和Talecris的官员则持不同意见，他们称合并带来的成本节约将用于研发新药物以及扩大现有工厂的产能。

<!--en-->
CSL and Talecris officials disagreed, saying the cost savings from their merger would be invested in developing new medicines and expanding capacity at existing plants.

CSL首席执行官Brian McNamee在一份事先准备的声明中表示：“虽然我们依然相信这笔交易能给客户带来诸多好处，并产生显著的财务协同效应，但CSL董事会认为，与联邦贸易委员会展开漫长的诉讼程序——鉴于其中存在的风险、高昂的成本，以及会长时间分散CSL管理层和员工的精力，使其无法专注于企业的规划与运营——并不符合我们利益相关方的最佳利益。”⁷ [^1704]: ⁷ 摘自A. Wolf于2009年6月9日发表在《罗利新闻观察报》上的文章《Talecris和CSL Ltd.停止收购尝试》，第E6版。版权归《罗利新闻观察报》所有，经许可转载。148 • Let's Make a Deal 美国司法部也会审查大型并购案，并可能通过向联邦法院申请禁令来阻止这些交易。当交易完成后，司法部可能会要求某家公司剥离或出售部分业务。司法部通常会与联邦贸易委员会共同审查并购案，而且往往会在交易完成前要求做出调整。例如，当埃克森公司与美孚公司合并业务时，联邦监管机构迫使他们在东北部、中大西洋地区、加利福尼亚州和得克萨斯州出售2,400多家加油站，因为认定合并后的公司在这些市场的汽油业务占比过高。BP公司与阿莫科公司合并时也被要求出售部分加油站。

<!--en-->
"Although we continue to believe in the many customer benefits and significant financial synergies that supported the transaction, CSL's Board of Directors did not believe that entering into a protracted litigation process with the FTC, with its inherent risks, substantial costs, and lengthy distraction of CSL management and staff from planning and running our businesses would be in the best interests of our stakeholders," said CSL chief executive Brian McNamee, in a prepared statement.⁷
[^1704]: ⁷ From "Talecris and CSL Ltd. halt buyout attempt," by A. Wolf, June 9, 2009, *The* (Raleigh) *News & Observer*, p. E6. Copyright 2009 by *The* (Raleigh) *News & Observer*. Reprinted with permission.
148 • Let's Make a Deal
The Department of Justice also reviews large mergers and acquisitions and may challenge them by seeking an injunction in federal court. When a deal has been completed, the Department of Justice may require a company to divest, or sell, some of its operations. The Justice Department often works with the FTC in reviewing mergers and acquisitions, and quite often it does require changes in a deal before it can be completed. When Exxon and Mobil combined operations, federal regulators forced them to sell more than 2,400 gas stations in the Northeast, Mid-Atlantic, California, and Texas because it was determined that the resulting company would have too much of the gasoline business in those markets. BP and Amoco were also required to sell some of their gas stations when they merged.

还有其他监管机构负责审查并购交易。例如，联邦通信委员会会审核涉及广播和电视电台的并购案。联邦储备委员会以及货币监理署则对涉及银行和储蓄机构的交易拥有决策权。欧洲的监管机构也会审查美国公司收购其在当地有大规模业务的公司的交易。一般来说，如果美国并购后该公司在欧州的年度收入超过2.25亿美元，那么该交易就属于欧洲竞争事务专员的管辖范围。正因如此，尽管美国监管机构已批准通用电气拟以450亿美元收购霍尼韦尔国际公司的计划，该交易最终还是被叫停了。

<!--en-->
There are other regulatory agencies that look at mergers and acquisitions. The Federal Communications Commission, for example, reviews deals that involve radio and television stations. The Federal Reserve Board has a say in transactions involving banks and thrifts, as does the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency. Regulators in Europe also review transactions that involve a U.S. company buying another company with large operations there. In general, American mergers and acquisitions that would result in a company with more than $225 million in annual revenue from Europe fall under the domain of the European competition commissioner. That is how General Electric's proposed $45 billion acquisition of Honeywell International was scuttled, even though U.S. regulators had approved the deal.

州级监管机构通常也会对交易是否通过发表意见。州保险专员依然在很大程度上负责监管保险行业。银行进行并购也必须获得州级监管机构的批准。

<!--en-->
State regulators also often have a say in whether a transaction goes through. State insurance commissioners still largely regulate the insurance industry. Banks also must receive state regulatory approval for mergers and acquisitions.

财经记者应当了解哪些监管机构需要批准某项交易，并查明这些监管机构是否计划就该并购案举行公开听证会。此类听证会往往在州级而非联邦层面召开。在安泰姆与特里贡的合并完成之前，特里贡总部位于弗吉尼亚州，该州的州企业委员会举行了公开听证会，多名医生在会上反对这项交易。出席听证会的记者本可以写出一篇不错的报道。

<!--en-->
Business reporters should know the regulators that must approve any deal and should find out if these regulators plan to hold a public hearing on a merger or acquisition. Such hearings often occur at the state, not federal, level. Before the Anthem/Trigon deal was completed, the State Corporation Commission—a regulatory agency in Virginia, where Trigon was based—held a public hearing in which a number of doctors spoke out against the deal. A reporter attending the hearing would have ended up with a nice story.

如果没有公开听证会，记者应查明有关该交易的哪些文件是可获取的。当某一行业发生并购时，联邦贸易委员会和司法部常常会征求其他企业的意见。当可口可乐宣布同意收购巴克公司时，A&W公司的母公司负责人在向联邦贸易委员会提交的声明中反对这笔交易。对于负责报道可口可乐相关情况的《亚特兰大宪报》记者来说，吉百利施维普斯美国软饮料业务负责人约翰·布罗克的言论便成了一篇报道的素材。

<!--en-->
If there are no public hearings, reporters should find out what documents about the transactions are available. The FTC and the Department of Justice often ask for comments from other companies when an acquisition occurs in their industry. When Coca-Cola announced its agreement to purchase Barq's, the head of the company that owns A&W opposed the deal in a statement to the FTC. For the reporter at the *Atlanta Journal-Constitution* covering Coca-Cola, the comments made by John Brock, president of the U.S. soft drinks business of Cadbury Schweppes, turned into a story.

如果无法获取公众对该交易的意见，记者可以直接联系最大的竞争对手。该公司发言人很可能会透露其是否曾向联邦监管机构反对过该交易，以及反对的理由是什么。

<!--en-->
If the public comments on a transaction are unavailable, the reporter can simply call the biggest competitors. A company spokesman will likely be able to divulge whether it has opposed the deal with federal regulators and, if so, on what grounds.

与任何其他商业新闻一样，记者应思考谁可能会受到并购的影响。在很多情况下，就是该行业内的其他公司。如果记者能预见到某笔交易可能带来的影响，他或她就能比其他报纸的同行领先一步。Let's Make a Deal • 149

<!--en-->
As with any other business story, reporters should think about who might be affected by a merger or acquisition. In many cases, it is the other companies in that business. If a reporter can think about the effects of a deal, he or she is one step ahead of competitors at another newspaper.
Let's Make a Deal • 149

## 建议练习题

<!--en-->
*Suggested Exercises*

1. 找一份你所在地区近期发生的并购新闻稿。回答以下问题：该公司披露了关于售价的哪些信息？关于被收购公司如何融入收购公司的信息有哪些？你认为收购公司为何决定进行此次收购？
2. 找一份涉及股票收购的S-4表格。阅读S-4中关于收购谈判过程的章节，撰写一篇500字的分析报告，内容包括是否存在其他潜在竞购方，以及被收购公司是否能够争取到更高的股价。
3. 与另一位同学讨论增值型并购与稀释型并购之间的区别，并列出公司选择进行稀释型并购的原因。
4. 分析一家正在进行并购的公司其股价近期的涨跌情况。他们将这种涨跌归因于这次并购吗？关于此次并购的哪些细节让投资者感到担忧或欣喜？
5. 找一例收购方使用全部股票或全部现金支付被收购公司款项的案例。如果该公司使用了现金，请将该公司在收购时的股价与历史水平进行对比。如果股价已低于其历史最高点，探讨股价是否影响了此次并购的融资方式。如果该公司使用了股票，则进行同样的分析，并说明为何不选择现金支付。这项练习可能需要查看收购方的现金流量表。

<!--en-->
1. Find a news release for a recent merger or acquisition in your area. Answer the following questions: What information did the company disclose about the sale price? What information was released about how the acquired company will be integrated into the purchasing company? Why do you think the purchasing company decided to buy the acquiring company?
2. Find a Form S-4 for an acquisition involving stock. Review the section of the S-4 that discusses how the negotiations for the acquisition occurred. Write a 500-word analysis of the negotiations, including whether there were any other potential suitors and whether the acquired company was able to negotiate a higher stock price.
3. Discuss the differences between accretive acquisitions and dilutive acquisitions with another student. List reasons why a company would make a dilutive acquisition.
4. Assess the recent rise or decline in the stock price of a company making an acquisition. Do they attribute the rise or fall to the acquisition? What details about the acquisition are making investors nervous or happy?
5. Find an acquisition where the acquiring company used all stock or all cash to pay for the acquired company. If the company used all cash, assess the company's stock price at the time of the acquisition to historical levels. If the stock is down from its all-time high, discuss whether the stock price played a part in how the acquisition was funded. If the company used stock, do the same assessment and ask why cash was not used. This exercise might require reviewing the acquiring company's cash flow statement.

## 8

华尔街与普通大众市场

<!--en-->
Wall Street Meets Main Street

### 街头漫步

<!--en-->
*A Walk Up and Down the Street*

在大众媒体中，没有什么比华尔街更能主导商业新闻的报道了。白天，CNBC、Fox Business Network和Bloomberg TV的观众会不断收到来自纽约证券交易所交易大厅的实时报道，屏幕底部还会滚动显示股价。然而，很少有经验丰富的记者，更不用说初出茅庐的商业记者了，能够充分理解市场动态，从而写出关于某一天股市表现或特定公司股价涨跌原因的连贯清晰的报道。

<!--en-->
Nothing dominates business coverage in mass communication like Wall Street. During the day, viewers of CNBC, Fox Business Network, and Bloomberg TV are bombarded with live reports from the trading floor of the New York Stock Exchange, along with a rolling tape of stock prices on the bottom of the screen. Yet few experienced journalists, let alone beginning business reporters, understand enough about what is happening to be able to write a cohesive and clear story about how the stock market performed in a single day or why the stock prices of particular companies might have risen or fallen.

实际上，华尔街背后的基本原理并不复杂。记者们应当将华尔街视为一个巨大的市场，全世界的投资者每天都会聚集在这里买卖股票。虽然确实存在华尔街这个地方，但很多交易都是通过全球各地的办公室通过计算机完成的。尽管美国的纽约证券交易所、美国证券交易所和纳斯达克从周一到周五上午9:30至下午4:00开放交易，但如今美国公司的股票几乎可以在海外交易所及盘后市场中通过计算机实现全天24小时的交易。

<!--en-->
In actuality, the basic principle behind Wall Street is not that complicated. Reporters should think of Wall Street as a huge marketplace, where investors from all over the world gather each day to buy and sell stocks. Although there is an actual Wall Street, a lot of the trading occurs via computer from offices around the globe. And though the U.S. exchanges—New York Stock Exchange, American Stock Exchange, and NASDAQ—are open Monday through Friday from 9:30 a.m. to 4 p.m. for trading, trading in stocks of American companies now occurs virtually 24 hours a day in overseas exchanges and after-hours markets using computers.

投资者买卖股票是基于他们对一家公司未来表现的预期。如果某位投资者认为“香草可乐”能提升可口可乐的销售额和利润，那么即使该股票上午的开盘价为58美元，他或她也可能愿意以60美元的价格买入该公司的股票。未来的盈利越高，股价上涨的空间可能就越大。如果另一位投资者试过“香草可乐”后不喜欢其口味，他或她可能会认为这款产品会失败，进而卖出部分股票。（关于公司业绩如何影响股价的更多内容，请参见第9章。）

<!--en-->
Investors buy and sell stocks on the basis of how well they believe a company will perform in the future. If an investor believes that Vanilla Coke is going to boost Coca-Cola's sales and profits, he or she might be willing to buy the company's stock at $60, even if it began trading in the morning at $58. The higher the earnings in the future, the higher the stock price might rise. If another investor samples Vanilla Coke and does not like the taste, he or she may believe the product could be a failure and might sell some stock. (For a refresher on how a company's performance affects its stock price, see Chapter 9.)

“低买高卖”这句老话源自华尔街，因为每位投资者买卖股票及其他投资品的目的都是为了赚钱。那位以每股40美元价格买入可口可乐股票的投资者，可能会愿意卖出其中一部分股票。

<!--en-->
The old adage “buy low and sell high” was created on Wall Street because every investor buys and sells stocks and other investments to make money. The investor who purchased Coca-Cola stock at $40 per share may be willing to sell some of it

### 专家建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《商业周刊》资深撰稿人Roben Farzad谈华尔街报道技巧：

<!--en-->
BusinessWeek senior writer
Roben Farzad on covering
Wall Street:

**记住长线投资的重要性：** 用杰克·博格尔的名言来说，从长远来看，市场就像一台称重机。尽管短期内股市可能显得混乱、波动剧烈且难以预测（比如那些“互联网流量”之类的因素），但股票最终必须反映企业的核心指标——盈利情况。在此期间，要对那些主张相反观点的新理论（及相关指标）保持警惕。

<!--en-->
**Remember the long haul:** In the immortal words of Jack Bogle, over the long run, the market is a weighing machine. However messy, volatile and unpredictable they may be in the short run (Internet eyeballs, anyone?), stocks do ultimately have to reflect a bottom line—earnings. In the interim, be leery of new paradigm arguments (and associated metrics) to the contrary.

152 • 当股价达到60美元时，华尔街与普通投资者利益一致。此时，该投资者将实现50%的投资回报。但那些在每股58美元时买入可口可乐股票的投资者或许会选择再持有一段时间，期望股价能涨到60美元以上。若如此，他们的回报率仅为3.4%。

<!--en-->
152 • Wall Street Meets Main Street at $60. In doing so, he or she will have realized a 50 percent return on his investment. But the investor who bought Coca-Cola stock at $58 per share may want to hold onto it a little bit longer, hoping that it will rise above $60. At that price, he or she will have realized a return of only 3.4 percent.

当然，对投资者而言，关键在于并非所有股票价格都会上涨。许多在20世纪80年代末进入华尔街，并在90年代乃至21世纪初享受大幅涨幅的投资者，早已习惯每年都能获得两位数的投资回报。但2008年底股市的表现表明，华尔街并不总是会上涨，只有经验丰富且聪明的投资者才能持续发现并投资于那些会上涨的股票。

<!--en-->
The trick for investors, of course, is that not all stock prices rise. Many investors who entered Wall Street in the late 1980s and rode the spectacular gains throughout the 1990s and into the 2000s came to expect double-digit gains in their stock portfolios every year. But the performance of the stock market at the end of 2008 shows that Wall Street will not always go up, and only the experienced and smart investor can continue to find and invest in stocks that will rise.

用于买卖股票的交易所就像巨大的杂货店，提供各种可能的食品和饮料。唯一的区别在于，消费者即投资者决定了他们愿意支付的价格。每天，都有投资者来到交易所进行股票交易，但他们中的许多人心中已有固定的价格预期。如果他们想购买微软的股票，却认为该公司的股价仅值50美元/股，那么只要股价高于50美元，他们就不会购买。每有一个卖股者，就必然有一个买股者。因此，股市遵循供求关系的经济原理运作。如果某家公司的股票需求旺盛，那么低价可买的股票供应量可能会很少。但如果由于种种原因许多投资者都想卖出该公司的股票，导致股票供应量很大，他们可能不得不以低于预期的价格出售。

<!--en-->
The exchanges where stocks are bought and sold are like huge grocery stores that offer every possible food and drink available. The only difference is that the consumers, or investors, are determining how much they are willing to pay. Each day, investors come to the exchange, wanting to buy and sell stocks. But many of them have a set price for those stocks. If they want to buy Microsoft stock but think that the company's shares are worth only $50 per share, then they will not purchasing any stock if the price is above $50. There must be a buyer for every seller of stock. Thus, the stock market operates under the economic idea of supply and demand. If there is a demand for stock in a company, then the supply of stock available to purchase at a low price might be minimal. But if the supply of stock in a company is large because many investors want to sell the stock for one reason or another, they may have to sell it at a lower price than they had hoped.

股票让投资者拥有发行股票的公司的部分所有权。企业通过出售股票来筹集资金，以便建造新工厂或收购其他公司以实现扩张。股票被卖给投资者，是希望投入企业的资金能够得到有效利用，从而带来更高的利润和更多的销售额，进而推动股价上升，因为其他投资者看到企业的成功后也会想要购买其股票。

<!--en-->
Stock gives an investor a piece of ownership in the company that is selling the stock. Businesses sell shares to raise money so that they can expand by building a new plant or buying another company. The stock is sold to investors with the idea that the money given to the company will be put to good use, resulting in higher profits and more sales that will, in turn, make the stock price go up because other investors will see the company's success and want to buy the stock, too.

然而，情况并不总是如此。有些公司在业务扩张策略上失败了，这时股价也会开始下跌。例如，某家零部件公司向多名投资者以每股20美元的价格出售了100万股股票。按此价格，该公司筹集了2000万美元用于业务扩张。假设其中一名投资者购买了10万股，花费了200万美元。这名投资者现在拥有该公司10%的股份，根据规定他需要向美国证券交易委员会提交相关披露文件（详见第10章）。作为10%股份的持有者，如果该公司清算，他有权获得公司资产的10%。

<!--en-->
This is not always the case, however. Some companies fail in their strategies to expand their business. And when that happens, stock prices begin to fall as well. For example, a widget company sells 1 million shares of stock at a price of $20 per share to a number of investors. At that price, the company has raised $20 million to expand its business. Imagine that one of those investors bought 100,000 shares, spending $2 million. That investor now owns 10 percent of the company, which would require him to file certain disclosures with the SEC (which are discussed in Chapter 10). As the owner of 10 percent of the stock, the investor would be entitled to 10 percent of the company's assets should it be liquidated.

股票价格的涨跌取决于多种因素，而这些因素归根结底都源于一个核心原因：投资者情绪。如果投资者认为某只股票无论出于何种原因都会上涨，他们就会愿意为这只股票支付更高价格。反之亦然。投资者可能认为某只股票会下跌，因为该公司不太可能实现比过去更高的利润，或者因为其首席执行官要离职去管理另一家公司。

<!--en-->
The prices of stocks rise and fall on the basis of a number of factors that all boil down to one overriding reason: investor sentiment. If investors believe that a stock is going to go up for whatever reason, they are willing to pay more for that stock. The opposite also holds true. Investors may believe a stock will fall because the company is unlikely to report higher profits than in the past or because the CEO is leaving to run another company.

投资者在判断某只股票是否值得购买时会考虑诸多因素。其中一些是基本面数据，比如第9章中提到的市盈率（P/E）和市净率（P/B）。另一些投资者则会关注季度盈利情况或分析师对未来几个季度或几年的盈利预测。还有一些人则基于主观原因进行股票买卖，比如他们是否喜欢该公司的CEO，或是他们购买该公司产品的频率如何。《华尔街与主流市场》•153：负责撰写关于股市在一天、一周、一个月、一个季度或一年内的表现报道的财经记者，需要探究导致股价上涨或下跌的各种因素。许多报纸要求其市场记者重点报道本地股票的走势。但即便如此，股价的涨跌仍可能由多种因素引发，而这些因素很多可能与该公司本身并无直接关联。也许投资者对经济形势感到担忧，或者担心与伊拉克的战争会切断中东的石油供应，从而提高许多企业的运营成本；又或许政府发布的支出或消费者信心报告数据低于预期；又或者总统呼吁通过减税措施，让更多资金流入消费者手中，希望他们能将这些钱用于购买商品和服务。

<!--en-->
Investors look at a number of factors in determining whether a stock is worth buying. Some of these factors are fundamental numbers, such as the price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio and the price-to-book (P/B) value discussed in Chapter 9. Others may look at quarterly earnings results or earnings projections from analystsfor future quarters or years. Still others use qualitative reasons for buying and selling stocks, such as whether they like the CEO or how often they purchase the company's products.
Wall Street Meets Main Street • 153
A business reporter asked to write a story about the stock market's performance during a day, week, month, quarter, or year will want to look at the factors that caused stocks to rise or fall. Many newspapers ask their markets reporters to focus their stories on how local stocks performed. But even in those cases, stocks could go up or down on the basis of a number of factors, many of which may not be directly related to the company. Maybe investors have become skittish about the economy or fear the war with Iraq may cut off oil supplies from the Middle East, raising the cost of doing business for many companies. Maybe the government has released a report on spending or consumer confidence that came in below projections. Or maybe the president urged the passage of a tax cut designed to put more money into the pockets of consumers, hoping that they will go out and spend it on goods and services.

要理解特定日子里整体股市为何上涨或下跌，并不像评估单只股票或某个行业内多家公司的表现那么简单。不过，往往某只个股或某个板块中的几只个股就可能导致整个市场下跌。例如，道琼斯工业平均指数或许是华尔街最著名的股市表现指标。每天都有数百名记者报道道指的涨跌情况。但道指仅包含30只股票，尽管这些都是像可口可乐和华特迪士尼这样知名企业的股票。如果道指中的某只股票在某天出现大幅下跌，整个指数也可能会随之下降。

<!--en-->
Understanding why the broader stock market rises or falls on a given day is not as easy as assessing the performance of a single stock or the stocks of companies in a specific industry. But often, a single stock or a few stocks in a sector may cause the overall market to fall. For example, the Dow Jones Industrial Average is perhaps the best-known barometer of stock performance on Wall Street. Every day, hundreds of reporters detail how the Dow moved up or down. But the Dow includes just 30 stocks, albeit 30 stocks of well-known companies, such as Coca-Cola and Walt Disney. If one of the stocks in the Dow happens to fall dramatically one day, the overall index could drop.

其他指数则不会因为单只股票的走势而出现如此大的波动。标准普尔500指数由500只股票组成，而罗素2000指数则涵盖2000家小型公司的股票。此外还有针对特定行业或特定市场的其他指数存在。

<!--en-->
Other indexes may not fluctuate as much on the basis of the performance of a single stock. The Standard & Poor's 500 Index is made up of 500 stocks, while the Russell 2000 Index includes the stocks of 2,000 small companies. Other indexes exist for certain industries and for specific markets.

以下是彭博新闻社一篇解释部分指数为何下跌的文章片段：

<!--en-->
The following excerpt is an example of a Bloomberg News story that explains why some of these indexes declined:

彭博社为记者编写的指南《彭博报道法》列出了在撰写市场相关报道时应尽早回答的四个问题，具体如下：

<!--en-->
Bloomberg's handbook for reporters, called *The Bloomberg Way*, lists four questions that should be answered early in a story about the market. Those questions are the following:

我的投资今天发生了什么变化？为什么会发生这种变化？（当日主题）今天的走势与过去相比如何？谁说了什么？（关键引语）（彭博社，1995年，第100页）这些问题的答案都在文章开头给出。直到第四段，读者才会看到说明各大指数当日具体下跌幅度的数字。《彭博报道法》还建议，在回答第三个问题时，记者可考虑以下对比：

<!--en-->
What happened to my investments today?
Why did it happen? (theme of the day)
How does today's move compare with the past?
Who said what? (key quote)
(Bloomberg 1995, p. 100)
Each of these questions is answered early in the story. It is not until the fourth paragraph that the reader is given the specific numbers indicating how the broad indexes fell on the day. *The Bloomberg Way* later advises reporters in answering the third question to consider the following comparisons:

自何时以来最大的涨幅/跌幅是多少？连续上涨/下跌/波动不大的天数有多少？在此期间价格/收益率变化了多少？自何时以来达到最高/最低水平？自何时以来波动幅度最窄/最宽？（彭博社，1995年，第101页）彭博新闻在报道市场方面表现极为出色，因为其主要受众是每天进行股票买卖的交易员和投资者。其记者和编辑深知，他们的读者要求以清晰简洁的方式了解市场动态及其成因。太多关于股市的报道只是泛泛提及“原因”，却未能充分解释市场的走势。

<!--en-->
Biggest advance/decline since when?
How many days in a row up/down/little changed?
How much have prices/yields changed in that time?
Highest/lowest level since when?
Narrowest/widest range since when?
(Bloomberg 1995, p. 101)
Bloomberg News does one of the best jobs in writing about the market because its primary audience is the traders and investors buying and selling stocks every day. Its reporters and editors know they have demanding readers who want to know what is happening and why in a clear and concise manner. Too many stories about the stock market dance around the "why" without fully explaining the market's movement.

二三十年前，许多媒体机构并不认为报道股市很重要。但随着全国越来越多的人将退休储蓄投入投资华尔街的401(k)计划和变额年金产品，更多读者希望了解股市的表现。如今，报道华尔街已成为当今大众传媒中最重要的内容之一。[^1775]：¹ 来自彭博新闻2002年12月24日S. Fu撰写的《耐用品及零售数据疲软，美国股市下跌：花旗集团股价下滑》，版权归彭博社所有，经许可转载。《华尔街与普通民众的交汇》•155。投资者不仅可以购买公司股票，还可以购买另一种名为债券的投资产品。债券被视为投资者向公司提供的贷款——投资者购买债券后，资金就会流入该公司。作为回报，公司会向投资者支付债券利息，并在债券期限结束时偿还本金。例如，某公司发行了价值1亿美元的债券，利率为6.75%，期限为30年。该公司每年都会向投资者支付利息，30年后再偿还1亿美元本金。该公司希望利用这段时间的资金将业务扩展到新领域，从而获得的收益远超过支付的利息成本。债券期限越长，公司需要支付的利率就越高。比如，一年期的债券可能仅为投资者带来3%的收益，而30年期的债券则能提供6.75%的年收益。所谓垃圾债，是由标准普尔或穆迪等评级机构给予低信用评级的公司发行的债券。由于评级较低，这些公司必须提供更高的收益率才能吸引投资者，有些此类公司发行的债券甚至能带来超过10%的回报。

<!--en-->
Twenty or thirty years ago, reporting about the stock market was not considered important to many media outlets. But as more people across the countrypoured their retirement savings into 401(k) plans and variable annuities that invested in Wall Street, more readers wanted to know how the stock market was performing. Now, writing about Wall Street is one of the most important stories in mass communication today.
[^1775]: ¹ From "U.S. Stocks fall as durable, retail data lag: Citigroup drops," by S. Fu, December 24, 2002, Bloomberg News. Copyright 2002 by Bloomberg L.P. All rights reserved. Reprinted with permission.
Wall Street Meets Main Street • 155
Investors do not just buy stocks in companies. They can also purchase another investment called bonds. A bond is considered a loan given to a company by an investor. An investor purchases the bond, and the money goes to the company. In return, the company pays the investor interest on the bond, and at the end of the bond's term, pays the balance of the bond. To illustrate, a company sells $100 million in bonds at an interest rate of 6.75 percent over a 30-year period. Each year, the company pays the interest to investors, and at the end of 30 years, pays the $100 million back. A company hopes to recoup the $100 million and the interest paid by using the money during that time period to expand its operations into new businesses that will bring in much more than the cost of the interest. The longer the time period for the bond, the higher the interest rate the company will pay. For example, a one-year bond may only give an investor a 3 percent yield. But the 30-year bond would pay 6.75 percent a year. So-called junk bonds are issued by companies that have low credit ratings from companies such as Standard & Poor's or Moody's. Because of their low ratings, these companies must offer higher yields to attract investors. Some bonds issued by these companies may offer returns of more than 10 percent.

债券和股票一样，在市场上每天都会进行交易。但通常让财经记者困惑的是，当债券价格上升时，其收益率反而下降，反之亦然。例如，如果一名投资者以7%的收益率从一家公司购买价值1000美元的债券，那么在债券到期前，他每年可从该公司获得70美元的利息，到期时还能拿回1000美元本金。但如果该投资者以999美元的价格出售这只债券，其收益率就会略有上升，因为新的债券持有人在债券到期时不仅能获得利息，还能拿回比原来购买价更高的1000美元本金。

<!--en-->
Bonds are traded every day in the market, just like stocks. But what usually trips up business reporters is that when the price of a bond goes up, the yield declines, and vice versa. For example, if one investor buys a $1,000 bond from a company with a 7 percent return, he would receive $70 a year from the company until the bond matures, when he would receive his $1,000 back. But if the investor sells that bond for $999, the yield goes up slightly because the new bondholder would get the $1,000 back when the bond expired—more than what he originally paid—in addition to the interest payments.

当一家公司申请破产保护时，债券和股票之间存在一个重要区别：在这种情况下，债券持有人通常会优先获得应得的偿付，而股票持有者在破产程序中几乎永远无法得到任何补偿。（有关破产法院的更多信息，请参见第13章。）

<!--en-->
One important distinction between bonds and stocks occurs when a company files for bankruptcy court protection. When this happens, a bondholder is usually first in line to be repaid what he is owed. But a stockowner rarely, if ever, gets anything in a bankruptcy proceeding. (For more on bankruptcy court, see Chapter 13.)

债券与股票在本质上有相似之处：它们都是由华尔街的大型机构——即经纪公司或投资银行所出售。这些机构中的许多都与那些向投资者出售股票和债券的公司保持着长期的合作关系。它们在全国各地设有办事处，其股票经纪人会努力说服投资者购买这些公司的股份。当投资者想要购买股票时，他们会通过经纪人下订单。这些订单通常指定特定数量的股份（例如1,000股）以及特定的价格（例如每股20美元）。随后，经纪人会去寻找愿意以该价格出售这些股份的买家。这些机构并不购买股票和债券，只负责销售，并从所售股份中获取佣金。他们卖出的股份越多，获得的收入就越高。正因如此，这些公司才会配备股票经纪人以及被称为卖方分析师的人员，负责向投资者推销这些股票。而本地股票经纪人主要致力于向本地的中小投资者销售股票，分析师则专注于向那些被称为

<!--en-->
Bonds and stocks are alike in a fundamental manner: They are both sold by large Wall Street firms known as brokerage houses or investment banks. Many of these firms have long-standing relationships with the companies whose stocks and bonds they are selling to investors. And they have offices across the country where their stockbrokers try to get investors to purchase shares in these companies. When investors want to purchase stock, they place orders with their stockbrokers. The orders are typically for a set number of shares (e.g., 1,000) at a specific dollar amount (e.g., $20 per share). The broker then goes out to find a buyer willing to sell those shares at that price. These firms do not buy stocks and bonds; they only sell and receive commission fees on the shares they sell. The more shares they sell, the more money they make. That is why these companies have stockbrokers and people called sell-side analysts who peddle these stocks to investors. Whereas local stockbrokers primarily spend their time selling stocks to local, small-time investors, analysts focus on selling these stocks to large investors known as

#### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《商业周刊》资深撰稿人罗本·法尔扎德谈华尔街报道：

<!--en-->
BusinessWeek senior writer
Roben Farzad on covering Wall Street:

**账目的两面性：**优秀的市场记者能够仔细审查损益表。顶尖的市场记者则深入了解收益、现金流以及常被忽视的资产负债表。可以去社区学院修习会计课程，学会欣赏像CreditSights和Gimme Credit这类小型机构所做的细致资本结构研究。债务与股权领域之间存在着紧密的联系。

<!--en-->
**Both sides of the ledger:**
Good market reporters can scrutinize an income statement. Great market reporters know the ins and outs of earnings, cash flow and the all-too-neglected balance sheet. Take an accounting class at a community college and learn to love the granular capital structure research of small outfits such as CreditSights and Gimme Credit. The worlds of debt and equity are all too interrelated.

156 • 华尔街与普通市场的机构投资者。机构投资者是指以买卖股票为职业的人，他们可能为保险公司或共同基金机构工作。他们的任务是在股价上涨之前买入股票，在股价下跌之前卖出。有时机构投资者能成功完成这一目标，但有时则不然。

<!--en-->
156 • Wall Street Meets Main Street institutional investors. An institutional investor is someone who buys and sells stocks for a living. He or she may work for an insurance company or a mutual fund operation. The job is to find stocks before they go up in price and sell them before they fall. Sometimes institutional investors are successful in accomplishing that task, but other times they are not.

在过去的二十年里，另一种名为抵押债务证券的投资产品也进入了市场。这类也被称作资产支持证券的投资产品被视为2008年市场崩盘的罪魁祸首。抵押债务证券是一种以债券或贷款组合作为支撑的投资证券。例如，抵押抵押贷款证券就是以抵押贷款作为支撑的。到2006年，仅这类投资产品的发行规模就已超过5000亿美元。2008年和2009年房地产市场价值下跌后，房产所有者开始拖欠贷款，于是问题便出现了——没有资金用来支付购买了这些证券的投资者。

<!--en-->
In the past two decades, another type of investment, called collateralized debt obligations, has also entered the market. These investments, also known as asset-backed securities, have been blamed for the market's fall in 2008. A collateralized debt obligation is an investment security backed by a pool of bonds or loans. For example, a collateralized mortgage obligation is backed by mortgages. By 2006, more than $500 billion worth of these investments alone had been issued. Problems arose when the property owners began defaulting on their loans when the real estate market declined in value in 2008 and 2009. There was no money to pay the investors who had purchased these securities.

股票经纪公司或评级机构的分析师会对其所在机构正在销售证券的公司进行调研，以确定哪些是最佳投资标的。然而，最近对这种做法的调查揭示了一个华尔街大多数专业投资者早已知晓的秘密：分析师们会受到所在机构的影响，倾向于推荐那些他们已有业务往来的公司的股票，比如帮助这些公司寻找潜在的收购对象或促使它们出售更多股票和债券。在抵押债务证券的案例中也是如此，许多此类证券都被赋予了投资级评级。但当房价开始下跌后仔细审查才发现，这些抵押贷款具有极高的投机性，且被销售给了极有可能拖欠贷款的消费者。

<!--en-->
The analysts at a stock brokerage house or a rating agency will research the companies in which their firm is selling securities and determine which ones are the best investments. Recent investigations into this practice, however, discovered the secret that most professional investors on Wall Street already knew—that analysts were influenced by their firms to push stocks of companies with which they already did business, such as helping them find potential acquisitions or sell more stock and bonds. This occurred with the collateralized debt obligations. Many were sold with investment-grade ratings. A closer inspection when real estate prices started falling revealed that the mortgages were highly speculative and had been sold to consumers with a high potential of defaulting on the loans.

因此，华尔街在许多消费者以及商业记者眼中的可信度受到了损害。一些媒体现在会仔细审查支撑某项投资的资产情况。还有些媒体要求其记者在引用分析师的观点时，披露评级机构或投资银行公司的分析师与其其他业务之间可能存在的利益冲突。现在的报道通常会类似这样写道：

<!--en-->
As a result, the credibility of Wall Street has suffered in the eyes of many consumers, as well as business reporters. Some media outlets now closely examine the assets backing an investment. Others now require their reporters to divulge the potential conflicts of interest between a rating agency or an investment banking firm's analysts and its other businesses when quoting the analyst. Stories now typically read something like the following:

> “Widget公司的盈利状况远好于其竞争对手，因为它生产的部件质量更优，”持有该公司股票的所罗门史密森巴尼公司分析师弗雷德·J·穆格斯说道。不过，他的公司并未为这家公司提供过投资银行服务。商业记者需要了解分析师与其所关注的投资产品——无论是股票、债券、大宗商品还是其他类型的产品——之间的关系，以此来判断该分析师是否尽可能保持客观。关于卖方分析师及其在商业报道中所扮演角色的更多内容，请参阅本章后面的“卖方分析师与买方分析师”部分。

<!--en-->
> "Widget Co.'s earnings were much stronger than its competitors' because it's built a better widget," said Fred J. Muggs, an analyst at Salomon Smith Barney who owns shares in the company. However, his firm has not done investment-banking business for the company.
A business reporter needs to know the relationship between an analyst and the investments—whether they're stocks, bonds, commodities, or something else—he or she is following to help determine whether the analyst is as objective as possible. See the “sell-side and buy-side analysts” section later in this chapter for a closer look at sell-side analysts and the role they play in business reporting.

## 买卖

<!--en-->
*Buying and Selling*

某只股票的需求可能一天之内就上下波动。但经过数月乃至数年，仍有一些股票始终受到投资者青睐。并非所有股票都同等，发行这些股票的公司表现如何，通常决定了哪些投资者愿意购买以及愿意支付的价格。《华尔街遇见主街》•157：投资者形形色色，他们对哪些股票表现更佳也各有先入之见。对于商业记者而言，理解一家公司的业务战略、规模、管理团队、历史背景与投资者购买其股票的意愿之间的关联至关重要。有些投资者可能希望投资那些未来增长潜力巨大的公司股票。

<!--en-->
Demand for a stock can rise and fall from one day to the next. But over months and years, there are some stocks that are constantly in demand by investors. All stocks are not created equal, and how the companies that issue these stocksperform typically determines which investors are willing to buy them and what price they are willing to pay.
Wall Street Meets Main Street • 157
Investors come in all shapes and sizes, and with all kinds of preconceived ideas about which stocks perform better than others. It is important for a business reporter to understand the connections among a company's business strategy, its size, its management team, its past history, and investors' willingness to purchase its stock. Some investors may want to acquire stocks in companies where there is great potential for future growth.

20世纪90年代中期，亚特兰大的一家杂货店连锁企业Harry’s Farmers Market Incorporated上市，向投资者出售股票，并承诺将以类似Home Depot Incorporated改变自助零售业的方式彻底革新杂货行业。1981年Home Depot上市后，由于其快速成长并成为全球十大零售商之一，早期投资者因此获得了数倍于初始投资的财富。但Harry’s未能兑现其承诺，从未将业务扩展到亚特兰大以外的地区，许多投资者因此亏损。

<!--en-->
In the mid-1990s, a grocery store chain in Atlanta called Harry's Farmers Market Incorporated went public, selling shares to investors with the promise that it was going to revolutionize the grocery industry in much the same way that Home Depot Incorporated had changed the do-it-yourself business. Early investors in Home Depot, after it went public in 1981, became millionaires many times over as a result of the company's rapid growth, which made it one of the top ten retailers in the world. But Harry's was not able to follow up on its promise. It never expanded outside of the Atlanta market, and many of its investors lost money.

然而，每有10家Harry’s，就有一家Home Depot或Microsoft Corporation。那些喜欢投资增长潜力大的公司股票的投资者会寻找所谓的成长股。这类投资者的期望是，由于公司扩张计划带来的营收和利润增长，股价会上涨。大多数成长股不会向投资者派发股息。成长型公司是指那些营收或利润通常以远高于行业平均水平的速度增长的 Unternehmen。其营收可能每季度增长30%，利润则可能增长25%甚至更多。

<!--en-->
For every ten Harry's, however, there is a Home Depot or a Microsoft Corporation. Investors who like to buy stocks in companies in which there is a lot of growth potential look for what are called growth stocks. Investors in growth stocks are looking for the price of the stock to rise because of the increase in the company's revenue profits as a result of an expansion plan. Most growth stocks do not pay dividends to their investors. Growth companies are businesses in which revenues or profits are typically increasing at multiples of the rest of the company. Revenues may be rising by 30 percent every quarter, and profits may be increasing by 25 percent or more.

与以成长为导向的投资策略相反的是另一种策略，即根据公司的价值来选择股票进行投资。所谓的价值投资就是将股价与其定量指标进行对比。例如，价值投资者可能会选择那些市净率较低的股票进行购买。

<!--en-->
The opposite of a growth-oriented investment strategy is one that focuses on buying stocks in companies on the basis of their value. So-called value investing looks at the worth of the stock price compared to quantitative barometers. For example, a value investor may look to purchase stocks that appear cheap on the basis of the P/B value.

如果一家公司的市净率低于其竞争对手或整个市场的水平，投资者可能会认为该股票价格偏低。价值投资者还会根据市盈率来评估股票。如果某家公司的股价约为其盈利的10倍，而其他股市股票的股价约为其盈利的15倍，那么这家公司的股票就可能被认为具有投资价值。

<!--en-->
If a company's P/B value is below that of its competitors or the overall market, then an investor may consider it to be cheap. A value investor may also look at a stock on the basis of its P/E ratio. If a stock price of a company is trading at around 10 times its earnings but the rest of the stock market is trading at around 15 times earnings, that stock may be considered to have value.

反之亦然。如果一家公司的市净率或市盈率高于其竞争对手或整个市场的水平，投资者可能会考虑抛售所持股票。对于记者来说，跟踪所报道公司的这些指标，寻找股价上涨或下跌背后的原因，是明智之举。

<!--en-->
The opposite is also true. If the P/B or P/E of a company gets to be higher than that of competitors or the rest of the market, an investor may consider selling his holdings. It is wise for reporters to track these values of the companies on their beats to look for potential stories about why the stock price is rising or falling.

还有些价值投资者更倾向于购买那些会向投资者派发股息的公司股票。股息是定期（通常为季度）向投资者支付的款项，旨在激励他们持有该股票。例如，总部位于亚特兰大的电力公司Southern Company，目前会为其股票持有者每股支付约0.44美元的季度股息。许多投资者购买股票只是为了获得公司发放的季度股息。正因如此，当一家公司决定削减股息时，总会有新闻价值。

<!--en-->
Other value investors prefer to purchase stocks in companies that pay dividends to their investors. A dividend is a payout to investors, often done on a quarterly basis, that serves as an incentive to own the stock. For example, Atlanta-based Southern Company, a power company, currently pays the people who own its stock about $.44 as a quarterly dividend for every share they own. Many investors purchase stocks just to receive the quarterly dividend check from a company. That is why it is always a story when a company decides to cut its

### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《商业周刊》资深撰稿人Roben Farzad谈报道华尔街：

<!--en-->
BusinessWeek senior writer
Roben Farzad on covering Wall Street:

**说到这里，来认识一下EBO：**任何优秀的市场记者都需要能够穿透数千字的财报冗文，提炼出符合标准、可辩护且经GAAP认可的最终财务数据。没错，首席财务官先生，您提到在扣除各项杂项费用前的营业利润持续上升，这确实不错。但归根结底，这会给您的股东带来多少实际收益或损失呢？一些粗俗的老手可能会称其为“剔除废话后的利润”；而我则称之为“剔除混淆因素后的利润”。

<!--en-->
**Speaking of which, meet EBO:** Any good markets reporter needs to be able to cut through thousands of words of earnings release fluff to get to a standardized, defensible, GAAP-recognized bottom line. Yes, Mr. CFO, it's great that you posted a sequential rise in operating profit before amortization and special one-time charges related to jibba-jabba. But what is the gain or loss that will actually accrue to your shareholding owners when all is said and done? A crasser veteran might call this earnings before bullcrap; I opt for earnings before obfuscation.

158 • 《华尔街遇见主街》：股息，然后把这笔钱用在其他地方。削减股息会导致投资者抛售股票，进而使股价下跌。

<!--en-->
158 • Wall Street Meets Main Street dividend and use that money elsewhere. Cutting a dividend will cause investors to sell the stock, leading to a drop in the stock's price.

总体而言，采取成长型投资策略的投资者所承担的风险要高于价值型投资者。成长意味着企业正在扩张，而扩张本身就始终存在出问题的可能性。比如，某零售商可能将门店开在了错误的位置。总体来说，价值型投资的风险较低，因为这类企业通过缓慢、稳健的增长来吸引投资者。不过，如果企业能够实现快速成长，成长型投资策略也可能为投资者带来更高的回报。

<!--en-->
For the most part, investors who take a growth-oriented strategy to investing are taking a greater risk than value investors. Growth means that a company is expanding, and growing means that there is always the chance of something going wrong. Maybe a retailer is putting its stores in the wrong place. There is less risk with value investing, in general, because these are companies looking to entice investors with their slow, methodical growth. However, a growth-investing strategy may also pay greater rewards for the investor if the company is successful in growing itself at a fast rate.

对许多投资者而言，股票的声誉与稳定性非常重要。在20世纪90年代的大部分时间里，通用电气公司和可口可乐公司都是深受投资者青睐的股票，因为它们公布的盈利水平通常能达到或超出华尔街的预期。尽管这些公司有时会被指责利用会计手段操控盈利增长，但投资者仍看重它们能够符合华尔街预测的能力。投资者不喜欢出现负面意外，如果一家公司能公布与预期相符的盈利数据，其股价就不太可能下跌。

<!--en-->
The reputation and reliability of a stock are important to many investors. For most of the 1990s, General Electric Company and Coca-Cola Company were attractive stocks to own for many investors because they routinely reported earnings that met or beat Wall Street expectations. Although these companies were criticized for sometimes using accounting changes to control their earnings growth, investors appreciated their ability to match what Wall Street predicted. Investors do not like negative surprises, and if a company can report earnings that are in line with estimates, then the stock price is unlikely to fall.

投资者和财经记者只需通过对比数据就能衡量这种稳定性。如果X公司公布的第二季度每股收益为0.25美元，而市场预期为0.27美元，投资者可能会因此却步；但如果市场预期仅为0.24美元，投资者则更有可能感到满意。这一点对财经记者尤为重要，尤其是在撰写关于公司盈利表现的报道时。强劲的盈利表现可能推动股价上涨，而疲软的业绩则可能导致股价下跌。无论出现哪种情况，最好联系相关投资者，与其探讨股价的变动情况。

<!--en-->
Investors and business reporters can measure this reliability simply by comparing the numbers. If Company X reports second-quarter earnings of $.25 per share but was expected to report earnings of $.27 per share, investors may be scared off. But if the company was expected to report earnings of $.24 per share, then investors are more likely to be happy. This last point is an important one for business reporters to consider, particularly when they are writing stories about a company's earnings performance. A strong earnings performance could cause its stock price to rise, but weak results could lead to a drop in the stock price. If either one of these is the case, it is good to call an investor and talk to him or her about the stock's movement.

公司的规模也是决定投资者是否购买其股票的一个因素。有些投资者甚至拒绝考虑市值低于10亿美元的公司股票。市值是指公司在华尔街上的估值，计算方法是将当前股价乘以已发行股数。另一些投资者则喜欢购买市值较小的公司股票。例如，有些共同基金专门投资于市值低于5亿美元的公司。

<!--en-->
The size of a company can also be a determining factor in whether an investor purchases its stock. Some investors refuse to even look at the stock of any company that has a market capitalization of less than $1 billion. The market capitalization is the value of the company on Wall Street and is computed by multiplying the current stock price by the number of shares outstanding. Other investors like to purchase stock in companies that have small market capitalizations. Some mutual funds, for example, specialize in investing in companies with market caps, as they are called, of less than $500 million.

还有些投资者只关注公司的战略或结构。有一些投资者的策略就是购买那些从由储户持有转变为在市场上出售股份并由股东持有的储蓄机构的股票。这些投资者过去曾从这类转型中获利，因此他们相信其他人也能从中赚钱。

<!--en-->
Other investors may be looking solely at the company's strategy or structure. There are a number of investors whose strategy is simply to purchase stock of thrifts that convert from being owned by the depositors into having the thrift's shares sold on the market and being owned by stockholders. These investors have made money in the past on these conversions, and they are willing to bet that others will also make them money.

许多投资者还会考察公司的业务战略，尤其是其产品或服务的销售方式。如果投资者自己也在使用该公司的产品，他们往往更愿意购买该公司的股票。许多投资者会观察产品的销售情况或公司旗下的实体店。例如，一位投资者走进盖璞门店，看到店内顾客众多，但如果发现其中有不少人没买东西就离开了，他可能会考虑抛售部分股票。另一位投资者则可能因为每天都要排长队才能买到一杯咖啡而想购买星巴克的股票。许多投资者还会考虑公司管理层的实力这一定性指标。与财经记者一样，投资者也喜欢与公司的首席执行官和首席财务官会面交谈。投资者如何看待管理层运营公司以及制定连贯战略的能力，会在很大程度上决定他们是否购买该公司的股票。如果投资者在与首席执行官会面后认为该公司领导者对其业务缺乏清晰的认识，他就不太可能购买该股票；相反，如果首席执行官能够有条理地阐述自己对公司的愿景，投资者就更有可能购买该股票。

<!--en-->
Many investors also look at the company's business strategy with regard to how it sells its products or services. Investors are often more willing to purchase a stock in a company if they use that company's product. Many investors look at how a product is sold or at a company's local store. For example, an investor may go into a Gap store and see many customers, but if he or she notices that a number of those shoppers walk out without buying clothes, the investor may think aboutselling some of his or her stock. Another investor may want to buy stock in Starbucks because he or she has to wait in long lines every day for a cup of coffee.
Wall Street Meets Main Street • 159
Another qualitative measure that many investors consider is the strength of a company's management. Like business reporters, investors like to meet and talk with the CEO and a CFO of a company. How an investor perceives management's ability to run the company and espouse a coherent strategy can go a long way in determining whether he purchases stock. If an investor comes away from a meeting with a CEO thinking that the company leader does not have a firm grasp on its operations, he is unlikely to buy the stock. Conversely, if the CEO can explain his vision for the company in a way that makes sense, investors will be more likely to purchase the stock.

还有其他一些投资者，他们只寻找可能被其他公司收购的企业。由于收购方支付的金额往往高于目标公司股票的当前交易价格，因此那些能够找到正在出售或只要出现合适买家就能被收购的公司的精明投资者，便能赚得盆满钵满。1999年国会通过《格拉姆-里奇-布莱利法案》后，许多投资者开始考虑购买保险公司和金融服务公司的股票，因为这项新法律首次允许银行持有这些企业。如果记者能意识到这一事件的重要性，通过采访那些会根据新情况决定买卖股票的投资者，就能写出有价值、能帮助读者了解情况的报道。

<!--en-->
There are other investors who simply look for companies that might be acquired by other companies. Because acquiring companies often pay more than the value at which a selling company's stock is currently trading, a savvy investor who can find companies that are for sale or could be bought if the right buyer came along can make a lot of money. After Congress passed the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act in 1999, many investors looked to purchase stock in insurance companies and financial services companies because the new law allowed banks to own these companies for the first time. A reporter who recognizes the significance of such an event can find a nice story that will inform readers by interviewing investors who will make decisions on buying and selling stocks on the basis of new developments.

规模最大的投资者是那些管理共同基金和对冲基金的机构。这类投资者通常掌管着数十亿美元的资金，其对市场的影响力有时极为巨大。共同基金是一种投资工具，消费者将资金汇集起来交给基金经理，期望其以能为他们带来回报的方式投资这些资金。这类基金可能有特定的投资策略，比如本节前面提到的那些策略。例如，某只基金可能专门投资市盈率较低的股票或零售业企业的股票。共同基金起源于20世纪20年代，如今总数已超过8,000只，管理的投资资产总额超过12万亿美元。

<!--en-->
The biggest investors are those who manage mutual funds and hedge funds. These investors often oversee billions of dollars, and their influence in the market can sometimes be tremendous. A mutual fund is an investment tool where consumers pool their money, giving it to the fund's manager with the understanding that he or she will then invest the money in a way that will provide them a return. The fund may have a specific investment strategy, such as those mentioned earlier in this section. For example, a fund may focus solely on stocks with a low P/E multiple or stocks of companies in the retail industry. Started in the 1920s, mutual funds now total more than 8,000, and they have more than $12 trillion in investments to manage.
