最后一种债券是美国国债。这类债券有不同的面额和到期日，由联邦政府发行用于资助美国政府项目。国库券的到期日不超过1年，面值为1万美元；国库票据的到期日为1年至10年，面值为1000美元；国库债券的到期日为10年至30年，可按1000美元的面额购买。到期日越长，收益率越高。由于美国联邦政府从未出现过违约行为，这类债券被视为世界上最安全的投资品种之一。

<!--en-->
The last type of bond is a U.S. Treasury bond. These come in different denominations with different maturity dates and are issued by the federal government to help fund U.S. government projects. Treasury bills are issued with a maturity date of a year or less and have a price of $10,000. Treasury notes are issued with a maturity date ranging from one year to 10 years and have a value of $1,000. Treasury bonds have a maturity date ranging from 10 years to 30 years and can be purchased in $1,000 denominations. The later the maturity date, the bigger the yield. These bonds are considered some of the safest investments in the world because the U.S. federal government has never defaulted on a payment.

在评估各类债券时，考虑经济因素非常重要。如果利率上升，企业和政府可能会因为成本增加而减少债券发行。

<!--en-->
It is important to assess economic factors with all types of bonds. If interest rates are rising, corporations and governments may issue fewer bonds because their cost will increase.

企业债与国债之间也存在关联，以下报道对此进行了说明：

<!--en-->
There is also a connection between corporate bonds and Treasuries, as the following story explains:

随着经济复苏迹象增多，美国国债本周可能出现两多月来的最大单周跌幅。

<!--en-->
U.S. Treasuries headed toward their biggest weekly decline in more than two months on increasing signs the economy is gaining strength.

在商务部宣布11月建筑支出连续第三个月上升后，今日市场对国债的需求下降。昨日，作为基准的10年期国债出现了去年以来最大的跌幅，结束了为期四周的上涨势头。此前有行业报告显示制造业指数创下11年来最大涨幅，同时股市也大幅上涨。[^1981]：⁹摘自E. Baeb于2002年12月27日在彭博新闻发表的文章《马萨诸塞州动用储备金、提高利率并解雇50人》。版权所有2002年彭博公司，经许可转载。“华尔街与普通民众”•175“今年前六周的经济形势可能较为乐观，这对企业债有利，但对国债则不利，”位于巴尔的摩的T. Rowe Price集团负责管理60亿美元债券投资的丹·沙克尔福德说道。他表示，该公司已减少国债投资，转而增加收益率较高的企业债和资产支持债券的投资。

<!--en-->
Demand for Treasuries fell today after the Commerce Department said construction spending rose for a third month in November. The benchmark 10-year note had its largest drop in more than a year yesterday, ending afour-week rally, after an industry report showed the biggest increase in a manufacturing index in 11 years and as stocks surged.
[^1981]: ⁹ From "Massachusetts water taps reserves, raises rates and fires 50," by E. Baeb, December 27, 2002, Bloomberg News. Copyright 2002 by Bloomberg L.P. All rights reserved. Reprinted with permission.
Wall Street Meets Main Street • 175
"The tone for the first six weeks of this year could be positive for the economy, which is good for corporate bonds and not so positive for Treasuries," said Dan Shackelford, who helps invest $6 billion of bonds at T. Rowe Price Group Inc. in Baltimore. He said the firm has added higher-yielding corporate and asset-backed debt at the expense of Treasuries.

截至纽约时间下午3点15分，本周作为基准的2012年到期、票面利率为4%的债券，每1000美元面值下跌了1¾，即17.50美元，这是自10月18日那周以来的最大跌幅。该债券的收益率上升了22个基点，达到4.03%。2004年到期、票面利率为1¾%的债券则下跌了约3/8，其收益率上升了18个基点，达到1.77%。1个基点等于0.01个百分点。当日，这些债券的价格基本持平，10年期债券价格上涨了1/32，2年期债券价格则保持不变。

<!--en-->
The benchmark 4 percent 2012 note this week lost 1¾, or $17.50 per $1,000 face amount, to at 3:15 p.m. in New York, its biggest slump since the week ended Oct. 18. The note's yield rose 22 basis points to 4.03 percent. The 1¾ percent 2004 note fell about 3/8 as its yield grew 18 basis points to 1.77 percent. A basis point is 0.01 percentage point. On the day, prices were little changed. The 10-year note rose 1/32 while the two-year note was unchanged.

本周，这两种证券之间的利率差扩大了5个基点，达到2.26个百分点，为两周来的最大值。更宽的利差表明交易员认为联邦储备委员会设定的1.25%这一41年来的最低隔夜贷款利率有助于经济复苏。

<!--en-->
The interest-rate differential between the two securities grew 5 basis points this week to 2.26 percentage points, the widest in two weeks. A wider gap suggests traders see the Federal Reserve's target overnight lending rate, at a 41-year low of 1.25 percent, underpinning an economic recovery.

分析师称，一些投资者本周抛售了国债，以便在投资组合中为预期中的企业债务供应增加腾出空间。特朗普酒店与赌场度假村公司以及欧洲第四大债券发行商Kreditanstalt für Wiederaufbau等公司都计划在未来几天内出售约40亿美元的债券。根据美林公司的债券指数，普通投资级企业债券的收益率比国债高1.81个百分点。¹⁰由于国债的收益率低于企业债券，因此当企业债券被出售时，一些投资者会抛售国债来购买它们。这是债券市场中的一个趋势，商业记者应当关注，因为它可能会影响他们所报道公司的债券发行情况。

<!--en-->
Some investors sold Treasuries this week to make room in their portfolios for an expected increase in the supply of corporate debt, analysts said. Trump Hotels & Casino Resorts Inc. and Kreditanstalt für Wiederaufbau, Europe's fourth-largest seller of debt, are among companies slated to sell about $4 billion of bonds in coming days. The average investment-grade corporate bond yields 1.81 percentage points more than Treasuries, according to a Merrill Lynch & Co. bond index.¹⁰
Treasury bonds provide a lower yield than corporate bonds, so when corporate bonds are sold, some investors dump Treasuries to purchase them. This is a trend in the bond market that business reporters should watch because it might affect the bond issue of companies they cover.

尽管华尔街的大部分报道都集中在股票涨跌上，但任何商业记者了解债券市场依然至关重要。债券往往能更全面、更清晰地反映一家公司或政府机构的状况。如果一家公司发行大量债券，可能是在为大规模扩张做准备，也可能是准备进行收购。无论出于何种原因，它都需要资金。商业记者的任务就是查明原因。

<!--en-->
Although the majority of Wall Street coverage focuses on the rise and fall of stocks, it is still vitally important for any business reporter to understand the bond market as well. Bonds can often tell a broader and clearer story about a company or government body. If a company is issuing a large amount of bonds, it may be gearing up for a large expansion, or it may be getting ready to make an acquisition. For one reason or another, it needs money. It is the business reporter's job to find out why.

### 钱，就是燃料

<!--en-->
*Money, it's a Gas*

本章将解释企业为何以及如何通过股市和债市筹集资金，以及这一过程对企业成功的重要性。那些通过提升利润和销售额表现良好的企业，其股价很可能会上涨，这使它们能够出售更多股票，并用这些股票来奖励员工。[^1991]：¹⁰摘自2003年1月3日彭博新闻社H. Bandur撰写的《因预期经济增速加快，国债价格下跌》，版权归2003年彭博L.P.所有，保留所有权利。经许可转载。176 • 华尔街与普通市场的交汇 但是，从股市和债市筹集到的资金进入企业账户后究竟去了哪里？企业有时并不会向股东明确说明打算如何使用这些资金。通常，这些资金会被用于以下四类用途之一：偿还过往贷款和债务；收购另一家公司或业务；建造新工厂或总部等设施；或者直接存放在企业银行账户中，以备必要时支付各项开支。

<!--en-->
This chapter explains why and how companies raise money through the stock market and the bond market and how this process is important to the success ofthe business. Companies that perform well by increasing profits and sales will likely see their stock price rise, allowing them to sell additional stock and use the stock to compensate their employees.
[^1991]: ¹⁰ From "Treasuries fall in week on expectations economy growing faster," by H. Bandur, January 3, 2003, Bloomberg News. Copyright 2003 by Bloomberg L.P. All rights reserved. Reprinted with permission.
176 • Wall Street Meets Main Street
But where does this money that's raised in the stock and bond markets go once it gets into the bank accounts of the companies? Companies are sometimes not specific in telling their shareholders what they plan to do with the money. Typically, the money goes to one of four uses: to pay off past loans and debt; to acquire another company or business; to build something, such as a new plant or headquarters; or simply to sit in the company bank account and be used to fund expenses when necessary.

如前所述，通过上市，企业向投资者出售股权。通常，S-1文件会说明企业打算如何使用这些资金。例如，总部位于纽约的休闲餐饮连锁店Cosi Incorporated于2002年上市。在其提交的文件摘录中，该公司大致说明了计划如何使用股票销售所得的资金，内容如下：

<!--en-->
As mentioned earlier, by going public, companies sell shares of ownership to investors. Often, the S-1 will explain what the company intends to do with that money. For example, New York-based Cosi Incorporated, a casual restaurant chain, went public in 2002. In the following excerpt from its filings, it explained how it intended to use the money from the sale of its stock in broad terms, explaining that:

> 对于如何使用此次募资所得的净款项，我们的管理层拥有广泛的自主决定权。我们无法保证管理层会有效运用这些资金，也无法保证这些募资款项会被投资于能够带来理想回报的项目。¹¹ 这段表述已经尽可能模糊了。但在申报文件的其他部分，该公司提供了更多细节，说明了资金的使用方式——即开设新餐厅：从历史上看，新增餐厅一直是我们业务增长的主要动力，我们预计在短期内它仍将是主要增长来源。我们认为自己采取了可控的增长策略，计划在现有市场开发众多新餐厅，并有选择地进入新市场，以此提升运营效率、为顾客提供更多便利并提高品牌知名度。由于我们不采用中央厨房模式，因此扩张不会受到地理位置的限制。我们的选址标准十分灵活，能够适应各种不同的房地产环境，包括商业中心、城市及郊区住宅区以及郊区购物中心。我们计划在2002财年开设约25家新餐厅，2003财年则计划开设约53至59家新餐厅。我们预计未来开业的大多数餐厅都将采用Cosi全天候经营模式。¹² [^1998]：¹¹ 来自Cosi Incorporated于2002年4月17日提交的S-1表格，美国证券交易委员会公开文件编号：0000950123-02-003869，第12页，华盛顿特区：美国证券交易委员会。¹² 来自Cosi Incorporated于2002年4月17日提交的S-1表格，美国证券交易委员会公开文件编号：0000950123-02-003869，第3页，华盛顿特区：美国证券交易委员会。《华尔街与普通街头的交汇》•177 另一家在2002年底发行股票的加州公司Impac Medical Systems，对其从募资中获得的数百万美元的用途也表述得同样含糊。它提到了几种可能的使用方式，如下文摘录所示，但并未给出具体细节：我们的管理层可能会以股东可能不希望的方式使用这些募资款项，或者以无法带来理想回报的方式使用它们。作为对我们普通股的投资者，您将无法影响这些募资款项的使用方式。目前我们打算将这些募资款项用于一般企业用途及营运资金。未来我们也可能会将这些款项用于战略性的收购或投资，但目前还没有具体的收购或投资计划。在需要使用这些募资款项之前，我们计划将其投资于投资级的有息证券，但这些投资可能不会产生收益，甚至可能贬值。¹³ 总之，许多公司筹集资金只是因为有能力这么做。通常它们并没有特定的资金使用计划，只是希望在需要时有钱可用。每当一家公司宣布一项需要资金的重大计划——无论是新的全国性广告活动、新建工厂还是收购其他公司——财经记者都应该询问资金来源。如果公司没有说明该计划的成本，记者应要求其给出估算值；如果公司仍不给出估算，就应寻找该领域的专家来提供一个大致数字。随后再查看公司的财务报表，判断其是否有足够的资金支持该项目。如果不够，公司就可以向银行借款或出售股票或债券。企业扩张所需的资金总得有个出处。 通常，这些资金来源于在华尔街买卖股票和债券的投资者。那些能够追踪资金流向——从资金如何筹集到将如何使用——的商业记者，可以通过撰写相关报道来帮助读者和听众了解这些资金是否被明智地使用，从而为他们提供宝贵的服务。追踪资金流向是商业记者工作中最重要的一环。本章将解释资金是如何从投资者流向企业的，以及企业为何有时需要资金。后续章节则会探讨企业资金的其他使用方式。

<!--en-->
> Our management has broad discretion as to the use of the net proceeds that we will receive from this offering. We cannot assure you that our management will apply these funds effectively, nor can we assure you that the net proceeds from this offering will be invested in a manner yielding a favorable return.¹¹
This statement is about as nebulous as it can get. But elsewhere in the filing, the company provided more detail that explained how the money was going to be spent—that is, opening new restaurants:
> The addition of new restaurants has been our primary source of growth historically and we anticipate that it will be the primary source of growth in the near term. We believe that we have adopted a manageable growth strategy and intend to develop many of our new restaurants in our existing markets, and selectively enter new markets, to gain operational efficiencies, enhance convenience for our customers and increase brand awareness. We do not utilize a commissary system and thus our expansion is not restricted by geographic proximity to commissary kitchens. Our site selection criteria is flexible and allows us to adapt to a wide variety of real estate paradigms including central business districts, urban and suburban residential locations and suburban shopping centers. We plan to open approximately 25 new restaurants during fiscal 2002, and approximately 53 to 59 new restaurants in fiscal 2003. We expect the majority of our restaurants to be opened in the future will be in the Cosi all-day format.¹²
[^1998]: ¹¹ From Form S-1, Cosi Incorporated, April 17, 2002, SEC Publication No: 0000950123-02-003869, p. 12. Washington, DC: Securities and Exchange Commission.
¹² From Form S-1, Cosi Incorporated, April 17, 2002, SEC Publication No: 0000950123-02-003869, p. 3. Washington, DC: Securities and Exchange Commission.
Wall Street Meets Main Street • 177
Another company that sold stock in late 2002, California-based Impac Medical Systems, was also similarly vague about its intended usage of the millions of dollars it received from its offering. It mentioned a number of potential possibilities, shown in the following excerpt, but gave no specifics:
Our management could spend the proceeds from this offering in a manner that our stockholders may not desire or that does not yield a favorable return. You will not have the opportunity, as part of your investment in our common stock, to influence the manner in which the net proceeds of this offering are used. We currently intend to use the net proceeds from this offering for general corporate purposes and working capital. We may also use the net proceeds in future strategic acquisitions or investments, but currently we do not have any specific acquisitions or investments planned. Until we need to use the net proceeds of this offering, we plan to invest the net proceeds in investment grade, interest bearing securities, but these investments may not produce income or may lose value.¹³
The bottom line is that many companies raise money because they can. Often, they do not have a specific usage for the money, but they want to have the money available when they need it.
Anytime a company announces a major initiative that will cost money—everything from a new national advertising campaign to the construction of a new factory to the acquisition of another company—a business reporter should ask where the money is coming from. If the company does not say how much the new initiative is going to cost, the reporters should ask for an estimate. If it does not give you an estimate, find an expert in that business to provide a ballpark figure. Then look at the company's financial statements to see if it has enough money to fund the project. If it does not, then the company could borrow the money from a bank or sell stock or bonds.
The money for businesses to expand has to come from somewhere. Most often, it comes from investors buying and selling stocks and bonds on Wall Street. A business reporter who can follow the money trail from how the cash was raised to how it will be spent can provide a valuable service to readers and listeners by writing stories that help explain if the money is being spent wisely.
The money trail is the most important aspect of being a business journalist. This chapter explains how money flows from investors into companies and why companies sometimes need money. Later chapters discuss other ways companies spend their money.

**Remember the little guy:** For as much as market reporting indulges the minute-to-minute play by play of earnings guidance and buy & hold carnival barking, today's stock market is ultimately the province of tens of millions of individual investors who dutifully contribute to their retirement plans. ## 建议练习

<!--en-->
*Suggested Exercises*

1. 编制一份本地股票的清单，并全天跟踪其表现。根据各个股及指数的涨跌情况撰写一篇报道，然后将你的报道与当地报纸上的股市报道进行对比。
2. 查阅卖方分析师为某家本地公司发布的调研报告。撰写一篇250字的分析文章，探讨该分析师对该公司的评级是否合理。
3. 讨论卖方分析师与买方分析师之间的差异。分别列出卖方分析师能帮助商业记者的五种方式以及买方分析师能帮助商业记者的五种方式。同时思考两种类型的分析师都可能试图利用记者为自己谋利的方式。
4. 查阅一家近期上市的公司的S-1注册文件。评估其融资规模及初始股价。列出该文件中五项具有新闻价值、适合纳入有关此次股票发行报道的内容。
5. 你是一家专注于银行股领域的杂志的编辑。你计划安排一次与一只投资银行股的共同基金经理的问答采访。该共同基金是该杂志401(k)退休计划的一部分，而你也参与了该计划。你应该亲自进行这次采访，还是找一位未参与该退休计划的员工来负责？如果选择让其他员工进行采访，你是否需要参与编辑访谈记录？![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/28ea43c75649b559f3d457664e5f2bf5.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T071651Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=dad81d05341e7c3dc2ac5ee5c8d19c2cba01bb2024fde22f0455cd314ab6dee1)

<!--en-->
1. Compile a list of local stocks and monitor their performance throughout the day. Write a story based on the gains and losses in the individual stocks and the indexes. Then compare your story to the stock market story in the local newspaper.
2. Review a research report for a local company issued by a sell-side analyst. Write a 250-word analysis of the analyst's rating for the company, discussing whether you believe the rating is justified.
3. Discuss the differences between sell-side analysts and buy-side analysts. Compile a list of five ways a sell-side analyst can help a business reporter and five ways a buy-side analyst can help a business reporter. Think of ways both analysts might try to use reporters to their advantage.
4. Review the S-1 registration statement for a company that has recently gone public. Assess the size of the offering and the initial stock price. List five items in the filing that are newsworthy and should be included in a story about the stock offering.
5. You are the editor of a magazine that follows bank stocks. You arrange a Q&A interview with the manager of a mutual fund that invests in bank stocks. The mutual fund is part of the magazine's 401(k) retirement plan, and the editor is part of the plan. Should you conduct the interview, or should you find a staff member who has not invested in the retirement plan to conduct the interview? If you find a staff member to conduct the interview, should you be involved in editing the transcript?

### 9

财务数据可以成为你的帮手

<!--en-->
Financial Numbers Can Be Your Friend

#### 利润表与资产负债表

<!--en-->
*Income Statements and Balance Sheets*

公司运营的目的是盈利。如果无法盈利，就需要做出调整以实现盈利。但如何判断一家公司是否在盈利呢？上市公司和私营企业都会向美国证券交易委员会及州级监管机构提交重要的财务数据报表，这些报表值得仔细阅读和分析。其中一种称为利润表，另一种称为资产负债表。两者所含信息及其所反映的公司运营状况都具有同等价值。然而，商业记者往往只关注利润表，而忽视了资产负债表以及现金流量表。

<!--en-->
A company is in operation to make money. If it is not making money, it needs to change its business in a way that enables it to be profitable. But how does one determine whether a company is making money? Public and private companies provide charts of financial numbers to the SEC and state regulatory agencies that are important to read and analyze. One is called the income statement, and the other is called the balance sheet. Both are equally valuable in the information they contain and the story they convey about a company's performance. Yet, too often, business writers focus on the income statement and ignore the balance sheet, as well as the cash-flow statement.

利润表是一种记录公司财务表现的报表。对于经验丰富的读者而言，利润表能讲述众多信息，为了解公司的财务状况提供大量线索。它详细列出了公司的销售收入、各项支出以及利润情况。公司通常会提供一个为期三个月的利润表，即一个会计季度，并将该季度的业绩与上一年的同期进行比较。分析师不应将一个季度与上一个季度直接对比，因为这种对比可能并不准确，尤其是当公司的业务具有季节性特征时。例如，可口可乐在每年的第二和第三季度销售的软饮料量会比第一和第四季度更多。为什么呢？因为第二和第三季度天气更热，人们会更倾向于购买软饮料。

<!--en-->
An income statement is a chart that records a company's financial performance. To the experienced reader, the income statement tells dozens of stories and gives plenty of clues about a company's financial performance. It details a company's sales, its expenses, and its profits. A company typically provides its income statement for a three-month period, known as a fiscal quarter, and compares the performance in that time with the same three months of the previous year. Analysts should not compare one quarter with the previous quarter. The comparison may not be valid, particularly if a company's business is seasonal. For example, Coca-Cola sells more soft drinks in the second and third quarters of the year than it does in the first and fourth quarters. Why? It is hotter in the second and third quarters, so people purchase more soft drinks.

利润表是衡量一家公司发展状况与健康程度的重要指标。财经记者应当仔细分析利润表中的各项数据，并比较收入、支出及利润的增长速度。如果收入的增长速度快于利润，这可能意味着该公司正在降低产品成本；如果利润的增长速度快于收入，则说明该公司可能在削减开支；而如果支出增长速度超过收入或利润，那么这家企业或许

<!--en-->
An income statement is an important barometer of a company's success and health. A business reporter should review the performance in the income statement and compare the growth rates of revenues, expenses, and profits with each other. If revenues are growing faster than profits, one interpretation of those two numbers could be that a company is cutting the cost of its products. If profits are increasing faster than revenue, then a company could be cutting expenses. If expenses are rising faster than revenues or profits, then a business might

#### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

路透社记者Joe Rauch关于报道盈利情况的见解：

<!--en-->
Reuters reporter Joe Rauch on covering earnings:

**多读、再读、反复阅读：**这是最简单的方法，虽然需要大量耐心，但通读年度报告、季度报告以及盈利报告的内容对于了解一家公司至关重要。你可能会惊讶地发现，只需完整阅读一份报告就能找到许多有价值的信息。这些文件中往往隐藏着适合第二天报道或深度报道的素材。此外，这样还能帮助你建立关于该公司的知识库，从而在撰写文章时无需再逐份查找所需信息。遗憾的是，略读是不起作用的——企业总喜欢在文件中隐藏信息。随着你越来越熟悉企业在季度报告和年度报告中放置信息的习惯，可以跳过一些格式化的常规章节，但这些部分若有所变动也值得仔细阅读。

<!--en-->
**Read, read, read and read some more:** It's the simplest approach and involves a lot of drudgery, but reading annual reports and quarterly reports, along with earnings reports, from cover to cover is invaluable in learning about the company. You'd be amazed what nuggets you can find just by reading a full report from cover to cover. Buried in the filings are often nuggets for second-day or enterprise stories. It also creates your own knowledge base about the company, so you don't need to hunt through every filing in your search for that one fact you need before you can file a story. Sadly, skimming doesn't count. Companies love to hide things in filings. As you get more familiar with where companies put information in their quarterly and annual reports, you can gloss over some boilerplate sections, but even those can be worth a read for any changes.

<!--en-->

表9.1展示了一个财季典型财务报表的样式。

<!--en-->
Table 9.1 shows what a typical financial statement for a fiscal quarter might look like.

像可口可乐这样的公司的利润表结构相当简单，只要知道要看什么内容，任何人都能理解。该报表的最上方一行被称为“净营业收入”。对于可口可乐而言，这意味着在2009年的4月、5月和6月期间，它共售出了价值83亿美元的经典可乐、无糖可乐、芬达、Mr. Pibb及其他饮料。这一数值较2008年同期的90亿美元软饮销售额下降了8.6%。

<!--en-->
The income statement of a company such as Coca-Cola is basic enough for anyone to understand if they know what they are looking at. The top line in this statement is called “Net operating revenues.” What this means for a company such as Coca-Cola is that during the months of April, May, and June of 2009, it sold $8.3 billion worth of Coke Classic, Diet Coke, Fanta, Mr. Pibb, and other drinks. That is a decrease of 8.6 percent from the $9.0 billion worth of soft drinks it sold during the same three months of 2008.

下一行被称为“销售成本”。这一项包括了可口可乐为生产用于制造软饮的浓缩液和糖浆所花费的成本。在本季度，该公司的此项支出为29亿美元，较2008年同期的近32亿美元下降了8.5%。需要注意的是，该公司生产软饮的成本下降幅度与销售额的下降幅度几乎一致。如果供应商为其饮料所需的原料（如人工甜味剂）收取更高的价格，那么销售成本的下降幅度可能会更小，比如在5%左右。明白增长率的变化总是有其背后的原因，有助于财经记者向公司高管和华尔街专家提出恰当的问题。

<!--en-->
The next line is called “Cost of goods sold.” This line includes how much money it cost Coca-Cola to make the concentrates and syrups used to make the soft drinks. For this quarter, it cost the company $2.9 billion, down 8.5 percent from the nearly $3.2 billion it cost in the same quarter of 2008. Note that the cost to make the soft drinks for the company declined at nearly the same rate as sales. If Coca-Cola were charged more by its suppliers for the cost of the ingredients, such as artificial sweeteners, used to make its drinks, then maybe the decline in the cost of goods sold would have been smaller, such as around 5 percent. Understanding that a change in growth rates always has an underlying reason enables the business writer to ask the right questions of executives and Wall Street experts.

接下来是“毛利润”。这一数值本质上是销售收入减去产品生产成本，其中不包含企业运营所需的各项支出，*表9.1 可口可乐公司及其子公司简明合并利润表（未经审计）*

<!--en-->
Next is “Gross profit.” This figure is essentially sales minus the cost to produce the product. It excludes company expenses for running the business, which

财务数字可以成为你的帮手 • 183 这一数值出现在下一行，即“销售、一般及行政费用”项。该项目也常被称为SG&A。这些费用涵盖从广告支出到高管及员工薪资，再到公司总部的供暖成本以及电话费等各种开支。在可口可乐公司，本季度的SG&A费用为28亿美元，较上一年度同期下降了8.1%。

<!--en-->
Financial Numbers Can Be Your Friend • 183
appear in the next line, called “Selling, general, and administrative expenses.” This line is also commonly called SG&A. These expenses include everything from advertising to executive and employee salaries to the cost of heating corporate headquarters and the company’s telephone bill. At Coca-Cola, during this quarter, the SG&A costs were $2.8 billion, down 8.1 percent from the same quarter the previous year.

为了快速对比损益表中的各项数据，公司在向SEC提交的前三个财季后的10-Q报表背面设有“经营成果”一节。在该部分中，公司会回顾该时期的经营表现，并通常会对损益表中列出的各项数据的增减原因进行说明。

<!--en-->
For a quick comparison of the numbers on an income statement, the back of the 10-Q—a document filed with the SEC by a company after the first three fiscal quarters—contains a section called “Results of Operations.” Here, a company will review its performance for the time period, typically explaining the increase or decrease in each number listed in the income statement.

以某家公司为例，其营收或销售额下降了8.6%，产品制造成本下降了8.5%，而SG&A费用则下降了8.1%。通过比较这三项数据的变动幅度，财经记者便能大致了解该公司该季度的情况。在可口可乐公司的案例中，营收的下降速度快于SG&A费用的下降速度，这表明该公司失去销售额的速度快于其削减费用的速度。理想情况下，当销售额下降时，投资者希望看到公司能够控制的费用（如差旅费和薪酬）有更大幅度的下降。显然，在某些方面，公司的支出下降速度并未跟上销售额的下降速度。

<!--en-->
To review, we have a company for which revenue, or sales, decreased by 8.6 percent, the cost of making its product fell 8.5 percent, and its SG&A expenses dropped 8.1 percent. By comparing the growth rates of these three figures, the business reporter should begin to understand what happened at the company that quarter. In the case of Coca-Cola, revenue declined faster than its SG&A expenses. That is an indication that the company lost sales faster than it could decrease its expenses. Ideally, when sales decline, investors would like to see a larger decline in expenses that the company can control, such as travel and pay. Somewhere, spending did not fall as fast as sales.

通过用营收或销售额减去商品成本及SG&A费用，公司即可得出营业利润，即其在缴税及其他会计处理影响之前的盈利或亏损额。营业利润这一数据能让财经记者了解公司的核心业务运营状况。在本案中，可口可乐公司本季度的营业利润较去年同期下降了9.0%，由于SG&A费用的下降幅度较小，这一降幅甚至超过了营收的下降幅度。

<!--en-->
By taking the revenue, or sales figure, and subtracting the cost of the goods and the SG&A expenses, a company arrives at its operating income, or the amount of money it made or lost before paying taxes and before other accounting effects. The operating income figure gives a business reporter an indication of how the company’s core business is performing. In this case, Coca-Cola’s operating income fell 9.0 percent when compared to the same quarter of last year. This decline is more than its revenue decline because of the lower rate of decline in SG&A expenses.

损益表中的接下来几行反映了公司从投资活动以及银行账户存款中获得的收益或损失。这类信息通常不会对大多数公司的盈利产生重大影响，但在某些行业中却可能产生影响。例如，保险公司通常会从消费者那里收取保费，并将这些资金投资于股票和债券，随后会在此处记录这些投资的收益或损失。需要注意的是，此处显示的损失是以括号形式呈现的，而非在数字前加负号。如果某个公司的盈利数据被放在括号内，则表示其为负数。在可口可乐公司的案例中，2008年第二季度该公司因对全球各地的装瓶商等公司的投资而出现了8.43亿美元的损失；但在2009年的同三个月里，这些投资则带来了3.1亿美元的收益。2008年的损失主要是由于可口可乐持有股份的一家大型装瓶公司——可口可乐企业公司的资产价值缩水所致。

<!--en-->
The next few lines in the income statement reflect the money the company made or lost from its investments and from money it holds in bank accounts. This information typically does not heavily influence most companies’ earnings. However, in some industries, it can have an impact. For example, insurance companies typically take premiums from consumers and invest that money in stocks and bonds. They then record income or losses from those investments here. Note that the losses reflected here are in parentheses instead of having a minus sign before a number. Don’t report that a number from a company’s earnings was positive when it has parentheses around it. A number inside parentheses means that it’s a negative number. In the case of Coca-Cola, it reported an $843 million loss in the second quarter of 2008 on its investments in other companies, primarily bottlers around the world. But in the same three months of 2009, those investments led to a $310 million gain. The 2008 loss was primarily the result of the writedown of the value of assets at Coca-Cola Enterprises Incorporated, a large bottler in which Coca-Cola holds an ownership stake.

在计入利息收入与支出以及投资收益与损失之后，公司就能得出税前利润。随后再减去该季度已缴纳的税金，即可得到净利润。对于财经记者而言，这一数字或许是最为重要的，因为它反映了公司在该季度的盈利或亏损情况。可口可乐公司报告的净利润为20亿美元，较上一年度同期的净利润增长了42%。

<!--en-->
After adding and subtracting interest income and expenses, as well as income and losses from investments, the company arrives at an earnings figure before paying taxes. It then subtracts the amount of taxes paid in the quarter to arrive at a net income amount. This is the number that is arguably most important for the business reporter to assess, because it reflects how much money a company made or lost during the quarter. Coca-Cola reported net income of $2.0 billion, a gainof 42 percent above the net income figure it reported in the same quarter the previous year.

184 • 财务数据可以成为你的助力 像可口可乐这样的上市公司会拆解其净利润数据，以显示每股已发行股票所创造的收益。在表9.1中，这被称为“稀释后每股收益”，但通常简称为每股收益，即EPS。该数值是通过将净利润除以已发行股票总数计算得出的。以可口可乐为例，其净利润为20亿美元，除以23.2亿股已发行股票，得出的每股收益为88美分。

<!--en-->
184 • Financial Numbers Can Be Your Friend
Public companies such as Coca-Cola break down their net income figures to show how much money was made for each share of outstanding stock. This is called “Diluted net income per share” in Table 9.1, but it is typically known simply as earnings per share, or EPS. This number is calculated by dividing the net income by the total number of shares outstanding. The math for Coca-Cola is $2.0 billion in net income divided by the 2.32 billion shares outstanding, or 88 cents per share figure.

每股收益是华尔街用来衡量公司盈利情况的指标。在公司正式公布数据之前，许多华尔街分析师会根据预测和计算机模型来估算公司的EPS。如果公司的实际EPS高于分析师的预期，其股价可能会上涨；反之，若EPS低于预期，则股价可能下跌。

<!--en-->
Earnings per share is a barometer for Wall Street to measure a company’s earnings. Many Wall Street analysts estimate a company’s EPS on the basis of projections and computer models before a company actually reports the figure. If the company’s actual EPS beats Wall Street analysts’ estimates, then the company’s stock could rise. If its EPS is lower than the estimate, the stock price could fall.

以下这段虚构摘录说明了上述数据如何被用于向读者解释可口可乐的盈利情况：

<!--en-->
The following fictional excerpt explains how the above numbers could have been used to help explain Coca-Cola’s earnings to readers:

可口可乐公司报告称，得益于新产品以及北美以外地区的强劲销售表现，抵消了美元走弱的负面影响，其第二季度盈利增长了44%。

<!--en-->
The Coca-Cola Co. reported second-quarter earnings that rose 44 percent as new products and strong sales outside North America overcame a weak dollar.

总部位于亚特兰大的这家公司报告称，其净利润为20亿美元，即每股88美分，而2001年同期的净利润为14.2亿美元，即每股61美分。这一业绩符合华尔街分析师的预期。由于汇率疲软，公司的营收从90亿美元下降了9%，至83亿美元。

<!--en-->
The Atlanta-based company reported net income of $2 billion, or 88 cents a share, compared with $1.42 billion, or 61 cents a share, in the quarter in 2001. The results were in line with Wall Street analyst expectations. Revenue fell 9%, to $8.3 billion from $9.0 billion, due to the weak currency exchange rates.

由于营收低于预期，投资者感到担忧，该公司的股价下跌了1.3%，至每股50.35美元，分析师们指出正是这一点导致了股价下跌。

<!--en-->
The company’s stock fell 1.3%, at $50.35 a share as investors worried about the lower revenue number, which missed projections, analysts said.

需要注意的是，开头部分的重点在于盈利或净利润的增长情况。直到第二段，记者才会给出实际的净利润数字，并评估EPS与预期的差距。如需更深入地了解如何撰写盈利相关报道及盈利预测内容，请参阅本章的“撰写盈利报道”部分。

<!--en-->
Note that the emphasis in the lead is on the growth in earnings, or net income. The actual net income numbers are not included until the second paragraph, in which the reporter also assesses where the EPS was in relation to estimates. For a more in-depth treatment of writing earnings stories and earnings estimates, see the “Writing the Earnings Story” section of this chapter.

资产负债表也是衡量公司财务状况的重要指标，但很少能看到记者撰写关于公司资产负债表的报道。其实他们应该这么做，因为资产负债表能显示公司的资产和债务情况。尽管公司会公布净利润，但其负债可能超过资产——这或许更能反映该公司的真实健康状况。通过分析资产负债表，你可以获取关于一家公司的重要信息。

<!--en-->
Balance sheets are also important barometers of a company’s financial status, but rarely do you see reporters writing stories about the company’s balance sheet. They should, because the balance sheet shows the company’s assets and debts. Though a company reports net income, it could have more liabilities than assets—possibly a truer reflection of that company’s health. You can find out important information about a company by assessing the balance sheet.

资产负债表的名字正如其名。公司资产负债表上的资产应等于其负债与公司股东权益之和。资产通常分为三类：流动资产、物业、厂房及设备，以及无形资产。在查看一份示例资产负债表之后，我们将对这些类别进行更详细的说明。

<!--en-->
The balance sheet is just what its name implies. The assets of a company on its balance sheet should be equal to the sum of its liabilities and the shareholders’ equity in the company. Assets are typically divided into three areas: current; property, plant, and equipment; and intangible assets. These will be explained in more detail after we look at a sample balance sheet.

既然之前已经讨论过可口可乐，那我们就来看看同一季度末该公司的资产负债表。

<!--en-->
Since we discussed Coca-Cola earlier, let’s look at its balance sheet at the end of the same quarter.

表9.2列出了截至2009年7月3日该公司的全资产情况。这些资产的价值每天都在变化，尤其是现金这类资产。《财务数据可以成为你的助力》• 185 *表9.2 可口可乐公司及其子公司简明合并资产负债表（未经审计）*

<!--en-->
Table 9.2 reflects the listing of the company’s total assets as of July 3, 2009. The worth of these assets can change every day, particularly for items such as cash and

cash equivalents, so it is important to view these numbers as a snapshot of a company's assets on just that day.

列表的上半部分列出了截至7月3日可口可乐银行账户中的现金数额，同时还详细说明了该季度末公司所拥有的软饮料原料及其他材料的库存价值，这部分被称为“存货”。该部分的另一项重要内容是“预付费用及其他资产”，这类项目可能包括可口可乐已为电视广告支付但尚未使用的费用。

<!--en-->
The top section lists how much cash Coca-Cola has in its bank accounts as of July 3. It also details the value of the inventory of soft drink ingredients and other materials the company had at the end of the quarter. This is called “Inventories.” Another large item in this section is “Prepaid expenses and other assets.” This line could include items such as money Coca-Cola has paid for advertising on television but has not yet used.

资产列表的下一部分称为“投资及其他资产”，其中列出了可口可乐在世界各地对其他公司进行的投资，这些投资是通过购买股票或向相关公司注资实现的。可口可乐的投资对象多为负责为其软饮料装瓶并将其运送给零售商的公司，例如，Coca-Cola Enterprises是美国最大的软饮料装瓶商，而Coca-Cola Amatil则是澳大利亚的大型装瓶商。

<!--en-->
The next section of the list of assets is called “Investments and other assets.” These columns list investments Coca-Cola has made in other companies around the world, either by purchasing stock or by adding money into the company. The investments listed by Coca-Cola are in companies that bottle and ship its soft drinks to retailers. Coca-Cola Enterprises, for example, is the largest soft-drink bottler in the United States. Coca-Cola Amatil is a large bottler in Australia.

为什么可口可乐要投资这些公司？或许是因为公司管理层意识到这些企业的成功与可口可乐自身的成功息息相关。此类投资对公司而言极为重要，这也是商业记者必须仔细分析资产负债表中这一板块的原因。如果一家公司对其业务无关的公司进行投资，那么这些资产或许需要进一步审视。（例如，一家饮料公司为何要投资软件开发商？这种投资必定存在合理的商业理由。）商业记者还想了解这些投资是否为该公司带来了价值增长，如果没有，或许就需要重新评估该公司对外投资的策略，这样的分析或许能成为一篇报道的素材。

<!--en-->
Why does Coca-Cola invest in these companies? Maybe it is because company executives know that the success of these businesses is intertwined with Coca-Cola's own success. Such investments can be very important for a company —which is why it is vital for a business reporter to evaluate this section of the balance sheet. If a company is making investments in other companies that have nothing to do with its business, maybe those assets need closer examination. (Why would a beverage company invest in a software developer, for example? There should be some valid business reason for the investment.) A business reporter also wants to see whether these investments are increasing in value for the company. If they are not increasing, maybe the company's strategy of investing in other companies needs to be assessed. That review could turn into a story.

在列出投资之后，可口可乐还会说明其不动产、厂房及设备的价值，这些包括公司总部的土地、其他建筑物、电脑、公司车辆、卡车以及自动售货机等物品。由于会计上的折旧机制，这些物品的价值会定期下降。折旧可以这样理解：当消费者购买汽车后，汽车一离开销售场地，其价值就会立即开始下降，这就是汽车的折旧。如果是奔驰汽车，其价值下降的速度可能不如雪佛兰汽车快。电脑和自动售货机等其他物品也会出现同样的价值折旧现象。

<!--en-->
Following its investments, Coca-Cola lists the value of its property, plant, and equipment. This is the land its headquarters is on, its other buildings, itscomputers, company cars, trucks, and other items, such as vending machines. The value of these items decreases regularly as a result of an accounting measure called depreciation. Depreciation can be thought of this way: When a consumer buys a car, the worth of that car immediately declines as it is driven off the lot. That is the depreciation of the value of the car. If it is a Mercedes, its value may not decrease as fast as a Chevrolet's. The same depreciation in value happens with other items, such as computers and vending machines.

186 • 财务数据可以是你的助力 最后，该公司会列出其商标及其他无形资产的价值。在此，可口可乐会评估其授予装瓶商的特许经营权价值，这些资产的明细也可以在相关文件中找到。

<!--en-->
186 • Financial Numbers Can Be Your Friend
Last, the company lists the value of its trademarks and other intangible assets. Here, Coca-Cola assesses the value of the franchise rights it grants to bottlers. A breakdown of these assets can also be found in the filing.

截至6月30日，扣除折旧后的所有这些资产总额为460亿美元，这意味着2008年前六个月该公司的资产增加了55亿美元。尽管这个数字看起来相当可观，但了解资产增减的原因始终是明智之举。通常，公司会在财务报告中对此作出解释，对于可口可乐而言，资产增加的部分原因在于其不动产、厂房及设备的增值。

<!--en-->
All of these assets, minus depreciation, totaled $46 billion as of June 30. That is an increase of $5.5 billion in assets for the company in the first six months of 2008. And although this number may seem impressive, it is always smart to find out why assets are rising or falling. Typically, a company will explain this somewhere in the financial filing. In the case of Coca-Cola, the increase in assets is partly attributed to an increase in its property, plant, and equipment.

现在，让我们来看看资产负债表的另一面——负债及股东权益（表9.3）。资产负债表的这一面应当与公司的资产相等。

<!--en-->
Now, let's look at the other side of the balance sheet, the liabilities and shareowners' equity (Table 9.3). This side of the balance sheet should equal the company's assets.

资产负债表负债方的“应付账款及应计费用”部分列出了公司为生产软饮料及其他产品而欠各类供应商和卖家的款项，“应付贷款及票据”则详细说明了公司欠银行及其他贷款机构的款项。

<!--en-->
The "Accounts payable and accrued expenses" section of the liabilities side of the balance sheet lists the money that the company owes various suppliers and vendors for the ingredients to make its soft drinks and other items. "Loans and notes payable" details the money that the company owes banks and other lenders.

财务数据可以成为您的帮手 • 187 这两项均属于流动负债，即短期债务，通常是指企业必须在一年内偿还的款项。在这一部分中，可口可乐公司列出了其长期债务的数额。长期债务一般需要在一年以后才需要偿还。需要注意的是，在这六个月的时间里，该公司的长期债务增加了一倍多。每当看到某个数字出现大幅上升时，都应探究其原因。对于可口可乐而言，其长期债务增加的部分原因在于该公司发行债券以替代短期债务。

<!--en-->
Financial Numbers Can Be Your Friend • 187
These are both included in current liabilities, or short-term debts, which are generally obligations that a company must pay within a year. Under this section, Coca-Cola lists how much long-term debt it owes. Long-term debt is typically payable in more than a year. Note that the long-term debt for the company more than doubled during the six-month timeframe. Whenever you see a number increase by a significant amount, you should look into the reasons. In the case of Coca-Cola, part of the reason for the increase in long-term debt was its issuing of bonds to replace short-term debt.

最后，公司会列出股东权益的数值，这也被称为公司的账面价值。从本质上讲，如果公司变卖所有资产、停止运营并将资金支付给投资者，股东们能得到的金额就是这个数。同样，大多数公司会在后续的财务披露中说明这些数值的增减情况。但将资产负债表中的“流动资产总计”项目与“流动负债总计”项目进行对比非常重要，因为公司通常会用资产来偿还负债。如果负债超过资产，那么公司可能就需要借款来偿还部分负债。显然，关注这些资产负债表数值中的大幅变动也很重要，因为这可能是公司内部存在其他问题的信号，进而有可能成为新闻素材。

<!--en-->
Finally, the company lists the value of the shareowners' equity, which is also commonly referred to as the book value of the company. This is essentially how much money shareholders would receive if the company sold everything in its possession, went out of business, and paid its investors the money. Again, most companies discuss the increase or decrease in each of these numbers later in their financial disclosures. But it is important to compare the "Total current assets" side of the balance sheet with the "Total current liabilities" side primarily because companies typically pay the liabilities with the assets. If liabilities are exceeding assets, then a company may have to borrow money to pay some of those liabilities. Obviously, it is important to look at these balance sheet numbers for any large increases or decreases that might be a signal of something else going on at the company that could result in a story.

由于安然公司的倒闭，许多偶尔阅读财经版面的读者可能听说过“表外交易”。这类交易是指企业进行的、未计入资产负债表中的业务。它们可能是与另一家公司共同创建合资企业，也可能是向另一家公司提供贷款以帮助其起步。例如，石油公司会设立表外子公司来勘探新的油井。公认会计原则允许将这些项目从企业的资产负债表中剔除，但大多数此类项目都必须在附注中详细说明。由于这些附注是由会计师撰写并经过律师审核的，因此往往难以阅读，更难理解。如果您遇到表外交易的附注，最好将相关内容交给会计师、律师或其他能明白其中披露内容的专家。在安然的案例中，该公司正是利用表外交易来虚增利润，掩盖其在多个业务领域的巨额亏损。

<!--en-->
Because of the failure of Enron Corporation, many casual readers of the business page may have heard of an "Off-balance sheet transaction." These are deals that a company enters into that are not included on a balance sheet. They may be the creation of a joint venture with another company, or they may be a loan to another company to help it get started. For example, oil companies create off-balance sheet subsidiaries to explore for new oil wells. Generally accepted accounting rules allow for these to be excluded from a company's balance sheet, but most of them must be detailed in the footnotes. These footnotes can be difficult to read and even harder to understand because they are written by accountants and reviewed by attorneys. If you encounter footnotes for an off-balance sheet transaction, it would be wise to take the information to an accountant, lawyer, or another expert who understands what the disclosure is stating. In the case of Enron, the company was using the off-balance sheet transactions to pump up its earnings and mask enormous losses in many businesses.

## 私营公司的财务报表

<!--en-->
*Financial Statements for Private Companies*

本章的第一部分评估了一家上市公司的财务表现。可口可乐的股票在纽约证券交易所（NYSE）交易。由于任何人都可以购买其股票，因此它被视为一家上市公司。然而，可口可乐的财务报表编制方式与私营公司的财务报表非常相似。正因如此，了解一家公司是如何得出其损益表和资产负债表中的数据的，对于各类企业报告而言都十分重要——无论该公司是上市公司还是私营企业。

<!--en-->
The first part of this chapter assessed the financial performance of a public company. Shares of Coca-Cola are traded on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE). Because anyone can purchase its stock, it is considered a public company. Yet, Coca-Cola's financial statements are constructed very similarly to financial statements for a private company. That is why understanding how a company derives the numbers in its income statement and balance sheet can be important for any type of business reporting—whether the company is public or private.

许多刚入行的商业记者都认为，私人公司就是所谓的“私人所有”的企业。他们觉得既然投资者不持有其股票，该公司就无需公开财务状况。但事实远非如此。许多商业记者在得知诸如银行和保险公司等数千家私人公司实际上必须向州级及联邦监管机构提交财务报告时感到十分惊讶。

<!--en-->
Many beginning business reporters operate under the assumption that a private company is just that—private. They think that because investors do not own its stock, it is not required to divulge its financial performance. Nothing could be further from the truth. Many business reporters are surprised to learnthat thousands of private companies, such as banks and insurance companies, are required to file documents disclosing their financial performance with state and federal regulators.

188 • 财务数据可以是你的好朋友 例如，当美国最大的杂货连锁店之一——Publix Super Markets Incorporated在20世纪90年代开始将业务从佛罗里达州向北扩展到乔治亚州、阿拉巴马州和南卡罗来纳州时，这些州的聪明记者们便深入研究了该公司向美国证券交易委员会披露的财务表现，尽管这家总部位于佛罗里达州莱克兰的公司被视为私人企业。为什么Publix要公开这些信息？因为资产价值超过1000万美元且股票持有者超过500人的公司必须提交年度报告及其他定期报告。Publix就符合这一条件——其股票由数百名门店员工以及詹金斯家族持有。当Publix公布财务信息时，这就会成为新闻。该公司的竞争对手想要了解其经营状况，成千上万的员工也是如此。然而却很少有记者愿意去查找这些信息。以下是彭博新闻社报道的相关内容：

<!--en-->
188 • Financial Numbers Can Be Your Friend
For example, when Publix Super Markets Incorporated, one of the country's largest grocery store chains, began expanding its operations out of Florida northward into Georgia, Alabama, and South Carolina in the 1990s, smart newspaper reporters in those states delved into the company's financial performance as disclosed to the SEC, even though the Lakeland, Fla.-based company is considered to be private. Why did Publix provide this information? Because companies with more than $10 million in assets with securities that are held by more than 500 owners must file annual and other periodic reports. Publix fits this description. Its stock is held by hundreds of store employees and by the Jenkins family. When Publix files financial information, it is news. The company's competitors want to know how it is performing, and so do its thousands of employees. Yet few reporters bother to look for this information. Here is a story from Bloomberg News that provided the results:

这家属于封闭式管理的超市公司表示，去年的利润仍为5.304亿美元，没有变化。

<!--en-->
Publix Super Markets Inc., a closely held supermarket company, said its profit last year was unchanged at $530.4 million.

由于流通在外的股数减少，每股收益从上一年的2.52美元上升至2.62美元。Publix在一份声明中表示，销售额从2000年的146亿美元增长了4.8%，达到153亿美元，2000年的统计周期多了一周。

<!--en-->
Per-share earnings rose to $2.62 from $2.52 a year earlier, as the company had fewer shares outstanding. Sales rose 4.8 percent to $15.3 billion from $14.6 billion in 2000, which had an extra week in the period, Publix said in a statement.

同店销售额增长了3.2%。对于零售商而言，经营至少一年的门店的销售额是衡量其业务状况的关键指标，因为这类数据排除了新开门店和已关闭门店的影响。

<!--en-->
Same-store sales rose 3.2 percent. Sales in stores open at least a year are a key indicator of a retailer's business because they exclude new and closed locations.

总部位于佛罗里达州莱克兰的Publix在佛罗里达州、乔治亚州、南卡罗来纳州和阿拉巴马州拥有691家门店，其股票由公司家族成员、员工及董事持有。这些股票的价值为41.1美元。这篇关于私人企业的报道中所提供的信息与公开上市公司的信息并无不同。报道重点强调了该公司的利润，这一点与关于可口可乐盈利情况的报道类似。对于私人企业和上市公司而言，销售额或营收都是同样重要的衡量指标。无论是否为上市公司，所有企业都在努力增加盈利额。如果一家企业能够持续提升销售额和利润，无论其性质如何，都可被视为运营良好的企业。

<!--en-->
Shares of Lakeland, Florida-based Publix, with 691 stores in Florida, Georgia, South Carolina and Alabama, are owned by family members and Publix employees and directors. The shares are valued at $41.¹
The information in this story about a private company is the same as it would be for a public company. The lead emphasizes the company's profit, similarly to the lead in the story on Coca-Cola's earnings. Sales, or revenue, are just as important a barometer for private companies as for public ones. All companies, whether they are public or private, strive to keep increasing the amount of money they make. A company, public or private, is considered healthy if it continues to increase its sales and profits.

其他行业的私人企业也可以从其他监管机构那里获取类似的财务信息。例如，各州监管机构负责管理保险行业——在该州开展业务的保险公司必须向监管机构提交财务信息。（有关监管机构能提供哪些信息的更多信息，请参见第15章。）

<!--en-->
Similar financial information can be obtained from other regulatory agencies for private companies in other industries. For example, state commissioners regulate the insurance industry. Insurance companies that do business in a state are required to file financial information with the commissioner. (For more information about what is available from regulatory agencies, see Chapter 15.)

尽管上市公司和私人企业提交的财务信息类似，但记者应采用不同的方式解读这些数字。上市公司的核心目标是提升股价以造福股东，为此它们往往会采取削减销售、一般及行政费用等手段来提高利润。而私人企业可能并不那么重视提升利润。私人企业的管理层往往由那些无意让企业上市的老板掌控，他们甚至可能会故意降低一两年的利润，然后将这些资金用于建造新工厂或新增公司总部大楼。许多私人企业，尤其是股东较少的私营企业，并不关心每股收益（EPS）的情况。而对于规模极小的私人企业来说，可能只有一名所有者。[^2091]：¹ 来自彭博新闻社2002年3月1日S. Elam撰写的《Publix Super Markets年度利润仍为5.304亿美元》，版权归彭博新闻社所有，经许可转载。

<!--en-->
Although public and private companies report similar financial information,reporters should interpret the numbers differently. Public companies are in the business of increasing the stock price for their shareholders. To do that, many of them engage in practices such as cutting SG&A expenses to increase their profits. A private company, however, may not be as interested in improving profits. Management at private companies, often run by owners that have no interest in making the company public, may actually lower earnings for a year or two and use that money to build a new plant or add a new corporate headquarters building. Many private companies, particularly private businesses that have few shareholders, do not worry about earnings per share (EPS). And for very small private companies, there may be only one owner.
[^2091]: ¹ From “Publix Super Markets annual profit unchanged at $530.4 million,” by S. Elam, March 1, 2002, Bloomberg News. Copyright 2002 by Bloomberg News. All rights reserved. Reprinted with permission.

财务数据可以是你的好朋友 • 189

<!--en-->
Financial Numbers Can Be Your Friend • 189

### 企业为何要公开财务信息

<!--en-->
*Why Companies Disclose Financial Information*

想象一下，如果没有任何一家企业，无论是上市公司还是私人企业，都从不透露自己的盈利情况、亏损情况，或是季度间、年度间的销售额变动情况，潜在投资者要如何判断是否应该购买这些公司的股票？他们难道只能相信企业告诉他们的内容吗？对于消费者来说，要决定是购买A公司的产品还是B公司的产品又该如何选择？显然，有些企业的言论是不可信的。企业高管们明白，通过公开自身的财务表现，可以增强客户对其不会倒闭的信心；如果能够证明自己有能力提升营收和利润，还能说服投资者购买股票。

<!--en-->
Imagine for a minute that no company, public or private, ever divulged how much money it was making, how much money it was losing, or how its sales rose or fell from quarter to quarter or from year to year. How would potential investors assess whether to purchase stock in such companies? Would they just have to believe what the company told them? What about consumers deciding whether to buy a product from Company A or Company B? Obviously, there are some companies whose word is not to be trusted. Company executives know that by releasing financial information about their performance, they build confidence among their customers that it is not going to go out of business, and they may convince investors to buy stock if they can demonstrate an ability to increase revenue and profits.

商业环境的运作方式要求企业向众多受众公开其财务表现的详细信息。在交易所上市的上市公司会定期向美国证券交易委员会提交文件，披露其利润、亏损、销售额以及其他诸多财务指标。私营公司也会公开财务信息，尽管获取这些信息可能更为困难。许多私营公司会向美国证券交易委员会汇报数据，这一做法令不少记者感到意外。还有些私营公司则向贷款机构、评级机构以及州级监管部门披露其财务表现。简而言之，所有企业都会密切关注自身的支出与收入情况。商业记者只要仔细阅读提交给美国证券交易委员会及州级监管机构的财务报表，就能获取数千家企业的此类信息。

<!--en-->
The business world is set up in a way that requires companies to release detailed information about their financial performance to a multitude of audiences. Companies with stock that is traded on an exchange regularly file documents with the SEC that disclose their profits, losses, sales, and many other financial measures. Private companies also disclose financial information, although it may be tougher to obtain. Many of them provide results to the SEC, which surprises many reporters. Other private companies disclose their financial performance to lenders, rating agencies, and state regulators. In short, all companies keep close tabs on where they are spending and where they are making their money. The business reporter can find this kind of information for thousands of companies by carefully reading the financial statements filed with the SEC and with state regulatory agencies.

能够阅读并分析企业的财务报表是商业记者工作的核心。记者需要具备分析企业运营状况及其与竞争对手相比表现的能力。可以说，评估企业的财务数据是商业记者工作中所有其他重要工作的基础。若不能正确理解利润、销售额、营收等指标，商业记者就无法：(a) 采访CEO了解其公司的运营情况；(b) 正确理解企业为何想要收购竞争对手；或(c) 理解董事会成员关于需更换管理层的观点。

<!--en-->
Being able to read and assess a company's financial statement is the cornerstone of a business reporter's job. The writer needs to be able to analyze how a company is performing and how its performance compares with that of its competitors. It can be argued that assessing a company's financial numbers is the root of everything else important in a business reporter's job. Without a proper understanding of profits, sales, revenue, and other measures, a business reporter cannot (a) interview a CEO about his or her company's performance, (b) begin to properly understand why a company might want to acquire a competitor, or (c) comprehend a board member's opinion that management needs to be changed.

如前所述，美国证券交易委员会负责监管所有定期交易股票或债券的企业。由于该机构的职责是保护投资者，因此它有诸多要求。

<!--en-->
As mentioned above, the SEC regulates all companies that regularly trade stocks or bonds. Because the SEC is there to protect the investor, it requires a lot

### 专家建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

*路透社记者Joe Rauch谈财报报道：*

<!--en-->
*Reuters reporter Joe Rauch on covering earnings:*

**一站式信息来源——年度报告：**在截止日期临近时，年度报告能为记者提供有关高管或企业的关键信息，具有极高的价值。根据美国证券交易委员会的规定，年度报告必须全面展示企业当年的整体情况。虽然这类报告往往极为详尽，但这反而对记者有利——报告中会包含一些在企业官网的公司历史介绍或个人简介中找不到的细节。有时这些信息可能会被更近期的季度报告所取代，但年度报告仍能让人大致了解企业的整体发展态势。

<!--en-->
**Your one-stop shop—the annual report:** Annual reports can be invaluable for finding quick tidbits about executives or the company you may need while pressed on deadline. The reports are mandated by the SEC to provide a comprehensive look at the company for the given year. Annual reports are often exhaustingly thorough, but that plays to your advantage. You'll find details about the company buried in the filing you'd never find on their corporate history or corporate bio posted to their official website. Sometimes this information can be superseded by information in more recently quarterly reports, but the annual report is the broad view of where the company is.

#### 专家建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

*路透社记者Joe Rauch谈财报报道：*

<!--en-->
*Reuters reporter Joe Rauch on covering earnings:*

**数据并不能反映全部真相：**企业发布的财报向来以呈现最理想的季度业绩而著称。毕竟，这是企业试图从最佳角度展示相关数据。但财报新闻稿中的前几句话往往并非真实情况。例如，美国银行在2009年第二季度的财报显示，在经历金融危机的艰难一年后实现了净利润，甚至出现了该公司历史上的首次季度亏损。大多数媒体都报道了这一净利润，但《纽约时报》的Floyd Norris在当天晚些时候的文章中分析了这一利润实际上只是源于一次性收益以及特殊的经营环境，并不能反映企业核心业务的真实状况——后者实际上损失了数十亿美元。

<!--en-->
**The numbers don't tell the whole story:** Company earnings releases are notorious for telling the best possible version of the company's quarterly results. After all, it's the company trying to present the best possible perspective on the numbers. But those first few sentences of the earnings press release often aren't the real story. For example, Bank of America's second quarter 2009 earnings reported a net profit after a rough year during the financial crisis, including posting the first quarterly loss in company history. Most outlets reported the net profit, but Floyd Norris of the *New York Times*, in a story later that morning, picked apart why the profit was the result of one-time gains and extraordinary business conditions that didn't reflect the true health of the core business, which actually lost billions.

#### 专家建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

路透社记者Joe Rauch谈财报报道：

<!--en-->
Reuters reporter Joe Rauch on covering earnings:

阅读管理层讨论与分析部分：管理层讨论与分析章节，以及企业与分析师（有时还包括媒体）进行的业绩电话会议，是了解企业管理层对公司运营看法的主要途径。这固然只是某一种视角——毕竟这是管理层的观点——但它通常比业绩电话会议中的内容更为坦诚，还会包含关于该季度业务发展的各种有趣信息。请务必每个季度都仔细阅读。

<!--en-->
Read the MD&A: The Management's Discussion & Analysis sections, along with the earnings call companies have with analysts (and sometimes media) are the primary means by which you can see management's view of the company's performance. It's a certain perspective—this is management's view after all—but it is often more candid than what you'll hear in the earnings call, and it has all sorts of interesting items about the business, as it happened in the quarter. Read through it carefully every quarter.

190 • 财务数据可以成为你的帮手：这些需公开披露的信息对于商业记者而言堪称宝库——只要他们知道该寻找什么以及去哪里找。

<!--en-->
190 • Financial Numbers Can Be Your Friend of information to be filed for public dissemination. This can be a treasure trove for business reporters—if they know what they are looking for and where to find it.

为什么美国证券交易委员会要求企业提交这些文件？如果该机构要求企业定期公开运营相关信息，投资者和潜在投资者就能自行判断企业的业绩是在好转还是恶化。如果负面信息通过美国证券交易委员会的文件而非新闻稿披露，企业的股价很可能会下跌；而正面信息，即便是通过大肆宣传的新闻稿披露，也往往会推动股价上涨。

<!--en-->
Why does the SEC require these filings? If the SEC requires companies to file information about their operations on a regular basis, investors and potential investors will be able to assess for themselves whether the company's performance is improving or waning. If bad information is disclosed, usually in an SEC filing and not in a news release, a company's stock price will likely fall. Good information, likely disclosed in a release with horns blaring and whistles blowing, will send the stock price up.

华尔街的专业投资者每天都会查看这类文件以获取此类信息。正因如此，优秀的商业记者也会阅读SEC提交的文件。如果记者能比其他人更快找到这些信息并据此撰写报道，他就能获得独家新闻。不过这并不总是那么容易。商业记者需要能够理解所读内容，并判断其重要性。最后也是最重要的一点是，他们还需要能够将这些有新闻价值的信息转化为文章，让那些没有时间仔细查阅SEC文件的读者也能看懂。

<!--en-->
Professional investors on Wall Street review these filings every day for this type of information. That is why good business reporters also read the SEC filings. If a reporter can find this information before anyone else and write a story about it, he has a scoop. It is not always that easy, however. Business reporters need to be able to understand what they are reading, and they need to be able to analyze its importance. Lastly and most importantly, business reporters need to be able to then take that newsworthy information and write a story that makes sense to a reader who may not have the time to go looking through the SEC filings.

### 评估公司的财务状况

<!--en-->
*Evaluating a Company's Financial Health*

本章及前几章介绍了如何以及从何处入手来判断一家公司是在盈利还是亏损。一般来说，无论是一家上市公司还是一家私营企业，只要其报告的利润和收入都在上升，通常就被视为经营状况良好。本节将探讨公司公开的一些财务信息，这些信息可以被用来作为判断公司健康状况的指标。

<!--en-->
This chapter and the previous chapters outline the basics of how and where to look to assess whether a company is making or losing money. Essentially, a company that reports increasing profits and rising revenues is generally considered to be healthy, whether it is public or private. This section discusses some of the financial information a company discloses that can be manipulated to determine barometers of health or sickness.

现金流量表是每家公司在SEC文件中必须披露的另一份财务信息表，与损益表和资产负债表一同呈现（见表9.4）。这份报表有助于商业记者分析公司的资金来源及其使用方式。

<!--en-->
The cash-flow statement is another table of financial information that every company discloses in its SEC filings, along with its income statement and its balance sheet (Table 9.4). This statement helps a business reporter analyze where a company is getting its money and how that money is being used.

正如本章第一节所示，评估损益表和资产负债表只需要简单的加、减、除运算即可。无需掌握复杂的公式或算法就能了解公司的运营状况。现金流量表也是如此。它只是一张简单的表格，显示公司从经营活动、投资活动和融资活动中获得了多少资金。衡量公司健康状况的基本标准是其是否拥有正向的现金流，也就是说，流入公司的资金是否多于流出的资金？如果公司的收入大于支出，那就表明该公司经营状况良好。

<!--en-->
As the first section of this chapter shows, assessing the income statement and balance sheet requires only simple addition, subtraction, and division. There is no need to know complicated formulas or to understand algorithms to assess how a company is performing. The same holds true for a cash-flow statement. It is a simple table that shows how much money a company is getting from its operations, investments, and financing. The basic test of health is whether a company is generating positive cash flow. That is, is more money coming into the company than flowing out? If the company is generating more money than it is spending, this is the sign of a healthy company.

表9.4再次展示了可口可乐公司的现金流量表样式。

<!--en-->
Table 9.4 shows what the cash-flow statement would look like, again for Coca-Cola.

经营活动产生的现金流反映了公司通过销售产品或服务获得的资金。如果该数值在上升，说明公司经营状况良好；如果下降，则可能意味着公司在销售产品或服务方面存在问题。这可能会促使商业记者进一步调查该公司。

<!--en-->
The cash flow from operations is an indication of the money the company is receiving from selling its product or services. If the cash flow from operations is increasing, that is a sign of a healthy company. If it is decreasing, the company may be having some problems selling its goods or services. That could be a sign to a business reporter to check into the company further.

What is the new business opportunity that was not available at the same time last year?

现金流量表的最后一部分显示了用于融资的现金支出。这部分内容反映了企业如何获得额外资金以发展业务，以及它们是否在偿还债务。对企业而言，偿还债务至关重要，否则利息会不断累积，使债务规模越来越大。债务越高，偿还难度就越大。那些持续通过发行债券借款的企业最终必须偿还这些债务。若无法偿债，一些企业甚至会陷入破产程序。

<!--en-->
The last section of the cash-flow statement shows cash spent on financing. This shows how companies get extra money to grow their businesses and whether they are paying off their debts. It is vital for a company to pay its debts or interestkeeps adding to the total, making the debt higher and higher. The higher the debt gets, the more difficult it becomes to pay off. Companies that keep borrowing money by issuing debt will eventually have to pay it off. Some companies wind up in bankruptcy court if they cannot pay off their debt.
