## 建议练习

<!--en-->
*Suggested Exercises*

1. 找一家当地的上市公司。如果所在地区没有本地上市公司，可以选择麦当劳或沃尔玛等总部位于该地区的上市公司。阅读该公司的10-Q文件，撰写一篇400字的分析报告，内容涉及其利润表和资产负债表。随后在课堂上共同讨论这份分析报告。
2. 查看同一家公司的现金流量表。轮流解释现金流量表中每一行的含义，然后投票决定该公司的财务状况是在好转还是恶化。
3. 在该公司的网站上找到其盈利新闻稿以及10-Q文件，对比两者披露的财务信息。如果可能的话，找一份不包含资产负债表或现金流量表的新闻稿。
4. 比较同一时期该公司在盈利新闻稿与10-Q文件中对自身业绩的描述，是否存在新闻稿中未提及的问题？
5. 计算一家公司的利润率、营业利润率、市净率以及市盈率。用10分钟时间完成计算，再将这些数值与竞争对手的数值进行对比。
6. 阅读某家公司的10-Q和10-K文件，根据文件中的叙述信息列出三个可能的新闻选题。![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/28ea43c75649b559f3d457664e5f2bf5.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T071651Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=dad81d05341e7c3dc2ac5ee5c8d19c2cba01bb2024fde22f0455cd314ab6dee1)

<!--en-->
1. Find a local public company. If your area doesn't have public companies based locally, it may have a location of a public company such as McDonald's or Wal-Mart that would suffice. Read the 10-Q filing for the company and write a 400-word analysis of its income statement and balance sheet. Then review this analysis in class together.
2. Review a cash-flow statement of the same company. Take turns explaining what a line in the cash-flow statement means. Then vote as to whether the cash-flow statement is from a company whose health is improving or declining.
3. Find the earnings press release and a Form 10-Q for the same company on its website. Compare the financial information disclosed in both. If possible, find a press release that does not include a balance sheet or cash-flow statement.
4. Compare and contrast a company's analysis of its performance in an earnings news release and in the Form 10-Q for the same time period. Are there issues in the filing that aren't discussed in the news release?
5. Calculate the profit margin, operating margin, price-to-book ratio and price-to-earnings ratio for a company. Take 10 minutes, and then compare the numbers with a competitor.
6. Read the 10-Q and 10-K filings for a company. List three potential news stories from the narrative information provided in the filing.
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/28ea43c75649b559f3d457664e5f2bf5.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T071651Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=dad81d05341e7c3dc2ac5ee5c8d19c2cba01bb2024fde22f0455cd314ab6dee1)

## 10

高管办公室

<!--en-->
The Corner Office

### CEO作为摇滚明星

<!--en-->
*The CEO as Rock Star*

在20世纪90年代，撰写关于大型企业CEO的特写文章变得流行，这些人被比作电影明星或摇滚偶像。商业媒体纷纷赞扬微软的比尔·盖茨、通用电气的杰克·韦尔奇以及可口可乐的罗伯托·戈伊苏埃塔等人的成就。尽管这些企业的成功离不开数千名员工的努力，但许多CEO仍因之获得赞誉。当时的报道或许有些过度夸张，也远未达到应有的批判性。如今，商业记者们开始更客观地审视CEO在管理企业方面的成败。

<!--en-->
During the 1990s, it became popular to write profiles about the CEOs of major corporations, treating them like movie stars or rock icons. The business media lauded the exploits of Microsoft's Bill Gates, GE's Jack Welch, and Coca-Cola's Roberto Goizueta, to name a few. Many CEOs received the credit for the companies' successes, even though they oversaw operations with thousands of employees who contributed to the companies' positions as industry leaders. The coverage was perhaps a bit over the top. Certainly, it was not nearly as critical as it should have been. We now see business reporters taking a harder look at the successes and failures of CEOs in running their companies.

泰科国际的丹尼斯·科兹洛夫斯基在20世纪90年代就被视为这类“摇滚明星”之一。他的照片出现在众多商业杂志的封面上，而他构建企业集团的策略也备受赞誉。如今，科兹洛夫斯基已不再领导泰科公司。他在2002年因逃税罪被起诉前不久便辞职了，目前正在狱中服刑。此外，他还被指控挪用公司6亿美元用于维持奢侈的生活，比如购买价值15,000美元的雨伞架和价值6,000美元的淋浴帘。奥兹·奥斯本或许也有这样的奢侈品，但当企业高管用公共公司的资金来购买这些东西时，无异于玩火，理应受到商业媒体的严密关注。

<!--en-->
Tyco International's Dennis Kozlowski was considered one of these rock stars in the 1990s. His face adorned the cover of many business publications, and his strategy of building a conglomerate was praised. Now, Kozlowski no longer leads Tyco. The disgraced executive resigned from the company shortly before he was indicted for tax evasion in 2002 and now sits in prison. In addition, he stands charged with looting the company of $600 million to sustain an extravagant lifestyle that included a $15,000 umbrella stand and a $6,000 shower curtain. Ozzy Osbourne likely lives with such amenities, but when a corporate executive uses money from a public corporation to buy them, he is playing with fire and should draw the scrutiny of the business media.

科兹洛夫斯基曾经极佳的商业声誉如今已荡然无存。在科兹洛夫斯基的领导下，为了筹措资金，泰科公司以远低于几年前收购价格的一半价格出售业务。商业媒体并未给予足够多的批评。就在他被捕前几个月，《商业周刊》还将他评为该国最优秀的经理人之一。

<!--en-->
Kozlowski's business reputation, once excellent, is now in tatters. Under Kozlowski's direction, to raise cash, Tyco sold operations at less than half of what it paid a few years earlier. The business media was not critical enough. Just months before his arrest, Kozlowski was named one of the country's best managers by *BusinessWeek*.

不幸的是，科兹洛夫斯基并非个例。前安然公司首席执行官肯尼思·雷显然曾使用公司飞机运送自己女儿的家具。前阿德尔菲通信公司负责人约翰·里加斯则从这家有线电视公司获取了1300万美元用于建造高尔夫球场。就连韦尔奇和戈伊苏埃塔这样的昔日风云人物也在面临困境。208 • 高层办公室

<!--en-->
Kozlowski is not alone, unfortunately. Former Enron CEO Kenneth Lay apparently used the corporate jet to transport his daughter's furniture. Ex-Adelphi Communications head John Rigas took $13 million from the cable company to build a golf course. Even former icons such as Welch and Goizueta are facing
208 • The Corner Office

### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《克雷恩纽约商业报》资深记者亚伦·埃尔斯坦关于报道高管薪酬的观点：在撰写有关高管薪酬的文章时，始终要给公司一个解释的机会。先致电公司，同时也要联系董事会中的薪酬委员会成员。大多数情况下，公司和董事们会拒绝与你交谈，这当然会为你提供更多独立撰写的空间。但当他们开口时，你总会听到一些有趣的内容，比如他们对自身业绩的重新评估。韦尔奇虽然从通用电气退休，但即便在2008年经济衰退开始之前，该公司也难以维持他在任时的增长速度。这主要是因为该公司再也无法进行足以推动更高收益的大规模收购，同时也无法像韦尔奇当年那样从现有业务中削减过多开支。而韦尔奇本身也有其不当行为——他的离婚谈判披露，通用电气为他提供了丰厚的退休待遇，包括支付曼哈顿公寓的费用以及乡村俱乐部的会员费。

<!--en-->
Crain's New York Business senior reporter Aaron Elstein on covering executive compensation:Always give the company a chance to explain itself when doing an exec pay story. Call the company, but also reach out to the compensation-committee members of the board. Most of the time, the company and its directors will refuse to talk to you, which of course gives you more room to write on your own. But when they do talk, you invariably hear something interesting.
re-evaluations of their performances. Welch retired from GE, but the company has since struggled to maintain the growth rate it had under his reign, even before the start of the recession in 2008. This is primarily because it can no longer make acquisitions big enough to fuel higher earnings, and also because it can only squeeze so much excess spending out of its existing businesses—strategies that Welch used to grow the company. And Welch had his excesses, too. His divorce negotiations disclosed that GE had given him a generous retirement package, including paying for items such as a Manhattan apartment and country club fees.

1997年作为可口可乐首席执行官去世的戈伊苏埃塔的业绩如今也正被以新的视角重新审视。这位能够轻松与世界各国总统会面的人领导可口可乐进行了改革，旨在确保公司未来数十年的成功。然而，在接替戈伊苏埃塔仅两年多后，道格·艾维斯特便辞去了可口可乐首席执行官一职。这位出生于乔治亚州的会计师——戈伊苏埃塔亲自挑选的继任者——无法承受种族歧视诉讼、欧洲市场的操作违规风波以及销售疲软所带来的巨大压力。1999年12月《亚特兰大宪报》的一篇报道将艾维斯特的辞职称为“意外”，并指出他担任公司领导期间的表现“动荡不安”（昂格，1999年，第1A页）。该报道还提到，艾维斯特抵制了董事会要求他指定副首席执行官的压力。此后十年间，可口可乐又经历了三位首席执行官更迭以及其他种种困境。

<!--en-->
The performance of Goizueta, who died as Coca-Cola's CEO in 1997, now is also being examined in a new light. A man who easily obtained meetings with presidents of countries around the world, Goizueta led Coca-Cola in an overhaul that was supposed to ensure its success for decades to come. Just more than two years after taking over from Goizueta, however, Doug Ivester resigned as Coca-Cola's CEO. The job was too much for the Georgia-born accountant, Goizueta's hand-picked successor. He was unable to withstand the spotlight brought on by a racial discrimination lawsuit, a tampering scare in Europe, and sluggish sales, as suggested in a December 1999 story in the *Atlanta Journal-Constitution*, which called Ivester's resignation a "surprise" and noted that his tenure as leader of the company was "tumultuous" (Unger, 1999, p. 1A). The story also noted that Ivester resisted pressure from the board of directors to name a No.2 executive. Coke has since been through three more CEOs in the past decade and other tribulations.

在许多此类案例中，商业记者在记录公司业绩时似乎都过于愿意给首席执行官们留有余地。有权势的首席执行官及其公关团队常常用未来企业辉煌发展的美好愿景来讨好记者，声称这些愿景最终会让股东们变得极其富有。然而，他们的承诺很少能实现。很少有公司能够长期保持那种能让股东们暴富的持续增长势头。近年来，美林和花旗集团等曾经的蓝筹公司也因各种问题而迫不得已更换首席执行官。在衍生品和抵押贷款支持证券出现问题之后，华尔街几乎所有的首席执行官都遭到了批评。

<!--en-->
In many of these cases, business reporters appear to have been all too willing to give CEOs the benefit of the doubt when documenting their companies' performances. Powerful CEOs and their public relations staffs often coddle reporters with grand visions of future corporate glory that will ultimately result in shareholders becoming unbelievably rich. Their promises are seldom realized, however. Few companies have been able to sustain the kind of repeated growth over a long period of time that makes their shareholders wildly rich. In recent years, former blue-chip companies such as Merrill Lynch and Citigroup have forced out their CEOs amid problems. Virtually every CEO on Wall Street has come under criticism in the wake of the problem with derivatives and mortgage-backed investments.

健谈且性格独特的首席执行官也会获得相当多的关注。但这真的有必要吗？在很多情况下，或许并非如此。《TheStreet.com》——一家在线商业新闻网站——的资深撰稿人达根·麦克道威尔在该网站上写道：

<!--en-->
Talkative and quirky CEOs also get a fair amount of attention. But is it warranted? In many cases, it may not be. A senior writer for TheStreet.com, an online business news service, Dagen McDowell, wrote on the site:

> 如果一家公司由性格鲜明的人物掌管，他/她甚至可以成为原本枯燥的财经报道中的有趣人物，那么这家公司就会获得媒体更多的关注……一个直率、敢言、观点鲜明，甚至有点疯狂的企业高管，比那些乏味的人能获得更多的媒体报道时间。但对投资者来说，过于鲜明的个性并不一定意味着出色的企业领导者。（McDowell, 2002）每位摇滚明星都有批评者，企业界也是如此。商业记者应当从近期揭露的种种过度行为中吸取教训，让高管为他们的行为负责。当然，也有一些CEO和其他高层管理人员确实是在为股东和员工谋福利，但还有不少人并非如此，值得记者进一步调查。记者可以深入企业内部，撰写文章揭露高管层和董事会里的真实情况。法律要求上市公司每年公开其高层管理人员的薪资、奖金以及股票期权等其他福利。对于一些私人公司，薪资、奖金及其他报酬会向州监管机构披露，只要记者知道去哪里查找或询问谁，就能获取这些信息。问题在于：为什么董事会会任由CEO将公司资金用于个人用途？答案是，包括泰科公司的董事会成员在内的许多董事会都声称对CEO的所作所为不知情。如今许多董事会开始严格审查此类支出，这对希望获取这类信息的商业记者来说是个好消息。友善的董事会成员可能会提供相关文件用于报道。另一个问题是：为什么董事会会同意给高管如此高额的薪酬？在很多情况下，为了留住优秀的高管，企业会给他们高达数百万美元的薪资和奖金。但高管薪酬已成为一个越来越有争议的话题，商业记者现在也更加认真地报道这一话题。后续章节将通过房地产记录和法庭文件详细说明如何查明高管与其公司相关的财务持有情况。但在任何记者开始采访高管并撰写相关报道之前，了解公司的架构是非常重要的。

<!--en-->
> A company also will get a lot more attention from the media if it's run by a colorful personality who could serve as an engaging character in an otherwise dry financial story. . . . A corporate executive who is blunt, outspoken, opinionated and maybe even a little nuts will get a lot more media time than someone who is, well, boring. Unfortunately for investors, an outsize personality doesn't always mean a great corporate leader.
(McDowell, 2002)
Every rock star has his or her critics. The same should hold true in the corporate world. Business journalists should learn from the recent disclosures of excess and hold executives accountable for their actions. To be sure, some CEOs and other
The Corner Office • 209
executives act in the best interests of their shareholders and their employees. But there are enough who do not to merit more scrutiny by reporters.
Reporters can dig into the world of corporations and write stories that expose what is going on inside the executive suite and the boardroom. Laws require public companies to disclose the salaries and bonuses, as well as stock options and other perks, of their top executives every year. In the case of some private companies, salaries, bonuses, and other compensation are disclosed to state regulators, and that information can be obtained if a reporter knows where to look or whom to ask.
The question is: Why have boards allowed their CEOs to get away with spending corporate money on personal items? The answer is that many boards, including members of the Tyco board, have professed ignorance as to what their CEOs have done. Many boards now aggressively look at such spending, which can be good news for business reporters looking to find such information. A friendly board member might provide the documents for a story.
Another question might be: Why do boards agree to pay executives such large sums of money? In many cases, successful executives receive seven-figure salaries and bonuses to keep them at the company. But executive compensation has become an increasingly controversial topic that business reporters now cover with more diligence. Later chapters detailing real estate records and court filings explain how to uncover an executive's financial holdings as they relate to his company. But before any reporter begins to interview executives and write stories about what they are doing, it is important to understand how a company is structured.

### 谁负责什么？

<!--en-->
*Who Does What?*

无论企业规模大小，CEO都是其中最重要的人物。CEO是制定公司战略的高管，组织结构图上的所有人最终都必须向CEO汇报工作。

<!--en-->
The CEO is the most important person in any business, no matter the size. The CEO is the executive who sets the strategy for the company, and everyone on the organizational chart must eventually answer to the CEO.

在许多公司中，CEO还可以拥有其他头衔。很多时候，CEO同时也是董事会主席。许多公司都设有董事会，旨在为高管团队提供指导。

<!--en-->
In many companies, the CEO can hold other titles. A lot of times, the CEO is also the chairman of the board of directors. Many companies have boards, which are set up to provide guidance to the executive team.

在一些公司里，当CEO同时担任董事会主席时，此人似乎拥有绝对权力。但并非总是如此。以可口可乐近期的一位CEO道格·达夫特为例，他和他的前任一样也担任董事会主席。但当时的可口可乐董事会中有世界首富之一沃伦·巴菲特，他持有该公司8%的股份。许多人认为，由于巴菲特的影响力更大，他在为可口可乐做出重要决策时的权力超过了持有较少股份的达夫特。有报道称，2001年巴菲特和其他董事会成员拒绝了达夫特收购包含佳得乐在内的奎克燕麦公司的提议（Valdmanis and Howard, 2000），最终是竞争对手百事公司买下了这家公司。

<!--en-->
At some companies, when a CEO is also chairman, that person can seem to have absolute power. But not always. Consider the story of one of Coca-Cola's recent CEOs, Doug Daft. Daft also held the title of chairman of the board, as did his predecessors. But the Coca-Cola board at the time included Warren Buffett, one of the richest men in the world, who owns 8 percent of the company's stock. Many believe that Buffett's stature gave him more power in making important decisions for Coca-Cola than Daft, who owns much less of the company. There were reports that Buffett and other board members turned down Daft's request to buy Quaker Oats, which included Gatorade, in 2001 (Valdmanis and Howard, 2000). Instead, rival Pepsi bought the company.

董事会通常由其他公司的CEO和高管、公司CEO的朋友，或是与该公司及高管有业务往来的人士组成。在监管机构和希望拥有更独立、敢于发声并让高管为过度支出及其他可能存在的问题负责的投资者的推动下，许多董事会都在做出改变。

<!--en-->
A board of directors is typically made up of other CEOs and executives at other companies, friends of the company CEO, or people who have business relationships with the company and executives. Many boards, spurred by regulators and investors seeking more independent boards who are willing to speak up and hold CEOs accountable for excessive spending and other decisions that may

### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《Crain’s New York Business》资深记者亚伦·埃尔斯坦关于报道高管薪酬的观点：

<!--en-->
Crain's New York Business senior reporter Aaron Elstein on covering executive compensation:

请记住，一篇出色的高管薪酬报道的关键通常不单单在于涉及的金额大小，而在于这笔钱与公司业绩的对比关系。当鲍勃·纳尔德利在家得宝获得巨额薪酬时，让这篇报道极具冲击力——并激怒了许多股东，最终导致他被罢免——的原因是他将一家非常成功的公司带入了歧途。210 • The Corner Office

<!--en-->
Remember that the key to a great exec pay story is generally not just the sheer amount of money involved, but how the money compares to the company's performance. When Bob Nardelli got paid a huge amount at Home Depot, what gave the story real bite—and drove so many shareholders nuts that he got pushed out—was that he'd driven a very successful company astray.
210 • The Corner Office

#### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《Crain’s New York Business》资深记者亚伦·埃尔斯坦关于报道高管薪酬的观点：

<!--en-->
Crain's New York Business senior reporter Aaron Elstein on covering executive compensation:

同样值得记住的是，有时“高薪者”的定义就是任何收入比你高的人。在探讨这些故事时，至少要愿意接受存在那些值得高薪的人才这一观点。如果你一开始就打算全盘否定他们，就有可能错过让这些故事更具吸引力的细微之处。这些人会影响公司的未来，有的会从公司外部招募与CEO毫无关联的新成员，还有的人则会引入少数族裔和女性董事会成员以带来不同的视角。

<!--en-->
It's worth remembering, too, that sometimes the definition of overpaid is anyone who gets paid more than you. As you approach these stories, try to be at least open to the idea that there are people worth a lot of money. If you go in ready to hang 'em all, you risk missing the nuances that make these stories sing.
affect the company's future, are adding members from outside the company who have no ties to the CEO. Others are adding minority and female board members to add different perspectives.

如果CEO并非董事会主席，那么这两人之间保持良好的工作关系非常重要。董事长本质上就是CEO的上司，如果董事长对CEO的工作表现没有信心，他或她可能会要求其他董事会成员帮忙寻找新的CEO。

<!--en-->
If the CEO is not the chairman of the board, it is important for these two people to have a good working relationship. The chairman is essentially the CEO's boss, and if the chairman does not have confidence that the CEO is doing the job well, he or she may ask the other board members to help find a new CEO.

CEO与董事会之间另一种有趣的关系出现在CEO卸任但仍保留董事会主席头衔的情况下。许多从CEO转任为主席的人无法放手，不让继任者有机会不受干涉地管理公司。记者在审查董事会构成时，需要留意是否有前公司高管仍在其中。

<!--en-->
Another interesting relationship between CEOs and boards sometimes occurs when a CEO retires from that position but maintains the title of chairman of the board. Many former CEOs-turned-chairmen have been unable to let go of the reins and allow their successors a chance to run the company without interference. When reviewing a board's composition, it is important for a journalist to see if there are former company executives lingering.

即便是上市公司，其董事会会议也对记者开放。不同公司的董事会平均每月或每两个月召开一次会议，且会议时长往往长达一整天。他们会听取关于公司运营状况的报告，并讨论管理层变动事宜。董事会还会投票决定是否批准公司的重要决策，比如建设新工厂或聘请新的CFO。此外，董事会还会就是否拆分公司股票或提高对投资者的股息等事项进行表决。公司通常会通过新闻稿公布董事会会议中决定的重要事件。

<!--en-->
Board meetings for companies, even public companies, are not open to reporters. Depending on the company, boards get together on average about once a month or every other month and often meet for an entire day. They hear reports on the performance of the company's operations and discuss managerial changes. Boards vote to approve major company moves, such as building a new plant or hiring a new CFO. Boards also vote on matters such as whether to split a company's stock or to raise the dividend paid to investors. Companies will typically disclose newsworthy events decided at board meetings via a news release.

财经记者了解所报道公司的董事会成员情况是明智的。大多数公司都会在网站及年度报告的末尾列出董事会成员名单。董事会成员经常会向记者谈论CEO的工作表现，也能提供有关并购相关董事会讨论的见解。本章将详细介绍如何获取更多关于董事会成员的信息。

<!--en-->
It is smart for business reporters to know the board members of the companies they are writing about. Most companies provide a list of board members on their websites and at the back of their annual reports. Board members may often speak to reporters about the CEO's job performance, and they often can give insights into boardroom discussions related to acquisitions. This chapter details how to find more information about board members.

公司的最高执行长官CEO也可能同时担任总裁一职。公司的总裁通常负责日常运营，监管各个主要部门及生产环节。如果这两个职位分开设置，总裁通常向CEO汇报工作。如果由不同的人担任这两个职位，其主要区别在于CEO往往更关注公司的整体规划，而总裁则负责管理当前的日常业务。

<!--en-->
The CEO, the top executive of a company, may also hold the title of president. The president of a company typically is the person in charge of the day-to-day operations, overseeing major divisions and manufacturing. If the two jobs are split, the president typically reports to the CEO. The major difference in these two jobs—if held by separate people—is that the CEO is often more focused on a company's plans, whereas a president oversees the current, running business.

图10.1展示了一家制造公司的典型组织结构图。这家公司的董事长同时也是CEO。

<!--en-->
Figure 10.1 is a typical organizational chart for a manufacturing company. The chairman in this company is also the CEO.

如果一家公司没有总裁，那么它可能会有首席运营官，即COO。这两个职位相似，通常由同一人兼任。公司有COO而没有总裁并不重要。不过，既有COO又有总裁的公司内部可能会出现权力斗争，或者让这两位高管展开竞争以取代现任CEO。这种情况值得关注，也可能成为新闻素材。

<!--en-->
If a company does not have a president, it may have a chief operating officer, or COO. These jobs are similar, and often one person may hold both titles. It is not significant if a company has a COO but not a president. However, a company with a COO and a president may have a power struggle near the top. Or it could be setting up those two executives in a horse race to replace the current CEO. That is something that bears watching and could lead to a story.

公司总裁/COO与CEO之间的关系十分重要。CEO往往会挑选合适的人选担任这一职务，因为他需要一位能够高效、迅速执行命令的二号人物。CEO与总裁通常会定期会面，讨论公司战略及运营状况。在20世纪90年代的可口可乐公司，CEO与总裁每周都会与其他高管一起共进午餐商讨业务。

<!--en-->
The relationship between the president/COO and the CEO of a company is important. A CEO will often pick someone as his right hand for the slot, knowing that he needs a No. 2 executive who can execute orders effectively and quickly. CEOs and presidents often meet regularly to discuss corporate strategy and a company's operations. At Coca-Cola in the 1990s, the CEO and president got together weekly with other executives at lunch to discuss business.

通常与总裁和COO处于同一层级的是CFO，他负责管理公司的账目。相比其他大多数高管，CFO通常更清楚公司的财务表现。CFO会参与编制公司的季度财报，并在公司为分析师和投资者举行电话会议时经常介绍这些数据。《高层办公室》• 211

<!--en-->
Typically at the same level as the president and COO is the CFO, who is incharge of keeping the company's books together. The CFO typically has a better handle on the financial performance of the company than most other executives. The CFO is involved in preparing a company's quarterly earnings statement and will quite often discuss those results when the company holds a conference call for analysts and investors.

***图10.1** 制造企业的典型组织结构图。*在总裁和首席运营官之下，根据企业架构的不同，可能设有多个职位。像可口可乐这样极度重视市场营销与区域业务的公司，可能会设置负责北美、欧洲、中东、南美、非洲及亚洲业务的高管，以及一名首席营销官。所有这些高管都向总裁汇报工作。而另一类企业的架构则可能不同，由负责制造或特定产品的高管直接向总裁汇报。

<!--en-->
***Figure 10.1** Typical organizational chart for a manufacturing company.*
Below the president and COO can be a number of positions, depending on how the company is structured. A company like Coca-Cola that is heavily focused on marketing and geographic operations might have executives in charge of its North American, European, Middle Eastern, South American, African and Asian operations, as well as a chief marketing officer. All of these executives report to the president. Another company may be structured differently and have executives in charge of manufacturing or specific products reporting directly to the president.

记者应当了解这些高管之间的相互关系。公司的首席营销官与某个业务部门的负责人可能需要频繁沟通。当公司推出新产品时，会希望尽可能多地销售产品，因此业务部门负责人需要与首席营销官探讨该产品的卖点。

<!--en-->
A reporter should understand the relationships among these executives. A chief marketing officer and the head of an operating unit at a company may need to spend a lot of time together. When a company unveils a new product, it wants to sell as much as it can. So the operating executive will need to discuss the selling points for the new product with the chief marketing officer.

企业内部还存在其他重要的关系。业务部门负责人可能需要资金来扩建工厂或开发新产品，为此他必须向总裁或首席执行官申请。在沃尔玛这样的公司，山姆俱乐部业务部的负责人可能希望为门店配备新电脑以追踪各类产品的销售情况，要获得这些新电脑，他则需要向信息系统负责人——有时也称为首席信息官——提出请求。212 • 高层办公室

<!--en-->
Other important relationships exist in a company. An operating executive may need money to expand a plant or to develop a new product. To get that money, he will have to go to the president or the CEO. At a company like Wal-Mart, the head of the Sam's Club division may want to install new computers in the stores to track the sales of various products. To get those new computers, he will need to ask the head of information systems, also sometimes called the chief information officer.
212 • The Corner Office

#### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《克雷恩纽约商业报》资深记者亚伦·埃尔斯坦关于报道高管薪酬的建议：在查看薪酬委员会的报告后，要注意董事会用来确定首席执行官薪酬的“同业群体”情况。这一点很重要，因为董事会总是以其他公司的薪酬制度作为自己决策的依据。这个同业群体是否现实？其中是否包含规模更大甚至属于不同行业的公司？小型企业往往倾向于将自己的薪酬制度与大型企业相比，因为一般来说大型企业的薪酬水平高于小型企业。（我发现薪酬与业绩之间的关联远不如薪酬与公司规模之间的关联重要。）

<!--en-->
Crain's New York Business senior reporter Aaron Elstein on covering executive compensation:After you examine the compensation committee's report, check out things like the "peer group" of companies that the board used to help it determine the CEO's pay. This is important because boards always point to the pay practices of others to justify their actions. Is the peer group realistic? Does it include companies that are much larger or even in different businesses? Small companies have a tendency to compare their pay practices to larger ones, because big companies generally pay more than smaller ones do. (I've found the correlation between pay and performance to be much less important than the correlation between pay and company size.)

或者，如果沃尔玛要开设新门店，就需要招聘新员工。人力资源副总裁需要从零售业务部门负责人那里了解门店的位置、预计开业时间，以及需要多少全职和兼职员工。

<!--en-->
Or, if Wal-Mart is opening a new location, it will need to hire new employees. A vice president of human resources will need to know from the head of the retail division where the store is located, when it is expected to open, and how many full-time and part-time employees will be needed.

了解每位高管的职责非常重要。对于撰写关于微软在巴西业务的报道的记者来说，与其采访现任首席执行官史蒂夫·鲍尔默，不如采访该公司南美业务部的负责人。大多数企业还有其他对商业记者而言同样重要的高管。负责报道葛兰素史克这类制药公司的记者，或许应该与研发负责人建立联系，因为此人可能愿意谈论正在研发的未来上市产品。而撰写关于银行自动取款机故障报道的记者，则应采访该银行的首席信息官或信息系统副总裁。

<!--en-->
It is important to know the responsibilities of each executive. For a reporter writing a story about Microsoft's business in Brazil, it is probably better to interview the head of the company's South American operations than to talk to Steve Ballmer, the current CEO. Most companies have other executives who can also be important for a business reporter. A reporter covering a drug company such as GlaxoSmithKline may want to cultivate a relationship with the head of research, a person who might be willing to talk about drugs being developed for future sale. A reporter writing a story about how the automated teller machines failed at a bank may want to interview its chief information officer or vice president of information systems.

规模较大的企业设有专门处理媒体询问的企业公关团队。优秀的公关团队会努力促成商业记者与高管之间的交流，而非自行发言。他们明白，只有高管才能比任何人都更清楚地了解企业内部情况，从而给出更准确的答复。在大多数情况下，这些高管都接受过以特定方式回答问题的培训。

<!--en-->
Larger companies have corporate communications staffs that handle media requests. The better corporate PR staffs work to put the business reporter and executives together, rather than talking themselves. They realize that it is the executives who know what is going on at the company better than anyone else and can give better answers. In most cases, these executives are trained to answer questions in a specific manner.

记者在采访时应认真细致，确保问题能得到满意的解答。有时高管们会像政客一样：试图回答一个并未被提出的问题，而不是实际被问到的那个问题。记者在采访过程中应注意倾听对方的回答，并针对未得到解答的问题再次提问。通常只需重复提问一次就能得到答案，有时则需要两三次。

<!--en-->
Reporters should be diligent in their interviews to ensure that questions are answered satisfactorily. Sometimes executives can be like politicians: They try to answer a question that was not asked, not the one that was. It is important for reporters to listen to the answers during the interview and return to questions that go unanswered. Often, just asking the question again will get an answer; sometimes it takes two or three times.

高管们都是非常忙碌的人。在很多情况下，他们还要管理价值数十亿美元的企业，因此对于表述不清的问题往往会失去耐心。记者应在采访前对相关高管进行背景调查，避免在基础问题上浪费时间。记者应该询问该高管为公司的战略规划，而非其担任首席执行官的时间长短。那些表现出已做好准备且熟悉行业情况的记者，下次更有可能获得采访机会。

<!--en-->
Executives are busy people. In many cases, they have multibillion dollar corporations to manage. They tend to get impatient with poorly framed questions. A reporter should prepare for interviews by conducting background research on the executive so that time is not wasted on basic questions. A reporter should ask about the executive's strategy for the company, not how long he or she has been CEO. The reporter who shows that he or she is prepared and knows the business will be more likely to get an interview the next time.

图10.2是另一份典型的公司组织结构图。（在某些国家，CEO被称为执行董事。）请注意，这家公司的公关负责人直接向公司领导汇报工作，但其权力层级低于运营总监或首席财务官。通常，企业公关副总裁会直接与总裁或CEO合作，共同制定公司应对媒体请求的战略。

<!--en-->
Figure 10.2 is another typical organizational chart for a company. (The CEO in some countries is called the executive director.) Note that the head of communications for this company reports directly to the company leader but is at a lower level of power than the director of operations or the CFO. Often, a vice president of corporate communications will work directly with a president or CEO in setting the company's strategy toward handling media requests.

## 薪资、奖金与股票期权

<!--en-->
*Salaries, Bonuses, and Stock Options*

企业的核心目标是盈利，其高管们也是如此。公司CEO明白，公司越成功，他就越有可能获得加薪或更高的奖金。他会选择那些最有可能成功并实现盈利的项目或业务机会，因为他知道自己的收益也会随之增加。《角落办公室》• 213

<!--en-->
Companies are in the business of making money. So are their executives. A company CEO knows that the more successful he makes his company, the more likely he is to get a pay raise or a higher bonus. A CEO will take on projects or business ventures for a company that have the best possibility of succeeding and being profitable, knowing that his wallet stands to benefit as well.
The Corner Office • 213

<!--en-->
***Figure 10.2** Another typical company organizational chart.*
The SEC requires every public company and some private companies to disclose information about their operations to investors. This disclosure of information includes the compensation packages of top executives. Increasingly, the disclosure of this information is becoming a major business story because of some of the examples of excess described at the beginning of this chapter. The Obama administration also moved in 2009 to limit executive compensation at companies that accepted bailout money during the economic crisis.

商业记者可以从多个渠道获取这些薪资信息。每年，在年度股东大会召开前约六周，上市公司会向每位注册股东寄送一份名为代理投票表或DEF 14A表格的文件。另一张投票卡则要求股东对代理投票表中列出的各项内容进行投票。对于财年与日历年一致的公司，这种寄送通常在2月底或3月初进行。商业记者应主动联系自己跟踪的公司，了解他们预计何时发布代理投票表。通常，代理投票表中会包含记者所在报纸次日商业版面想要刊登的新闻。

<!--en-->
A business reporter can find this salary information in several places. Every year, public companies send a filing called a proxy, or a DEF 14A filing, to every registered shareholder of that company about six weeks before the annual meeting. A separate voter card asks shareholders to vote on various items detailed in the proxy. This mailing typically happens in late February or early March for companies whose fiscal year coincides with the calendar year. A business reporter should check with the companies that he or she tracks to see when they expect to release the proxy. Often, the proxy contains news that the reporter's newspaper will want in the next day's business section.

通常会有多名董事会成员参与选举。董事会成员往往以交错任期方式选出，因此一年内董事会的多数派很少发生变化。公司通常会要求股东批准

<!--en-->
Typically, several members of the board of directors are up for election. Board members are often elected in staggered terms, so the majority of a board rarely changes in a year. Often, companies will ask shareholders to approve

### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《克雷恩纽约商业报》资深记者亚伦·埃尔斯坦关于报道高管薪酬的经验：众议院最近通过了一项法案，要求公司让股东对其薪酬制度进行投票。参议院很可能也会通过类似的法案。许多公司——比如所有获得救助的银行——已经在进行此类投票。在未来数月乃至数年中，值得密切关注这些投票，因为它们将成为公众向公司表达对其薪酬制度看法的新途径。通常，公司还会要求股东否决由持不同意见的股东（如工会）提出的提案，这些提案可能限制高管对公司事务的控制权。常见的反对提案是要求公司增加董事会中的外部董事人数，同时减少公司内部高管在董事会中的比例。这些信息往往能为商业记者提供优质的报道素材。

<!--en-->
Crain's New York Business senior reporter Aaron Elstein on covering executive compensation:The House of Representatives recently passed a bill that would require companies to let shareholders vote on their pay practices. The Senate will probably pass a similar bill. Many companies—such as every bailed-out bank—hold these votes already. It's worth keeping an eye on these votes in the coming months and years because they will be a new tool for the public to let companies know what they think about their pay practices.
executive option plans. Typically, companies also ask shareholders to vote against proxy proposals presented by dissident shareholders—such as unions—that they think could limit executive control over the company's affairs. A common dissident shareholder proposal is to ask a company to increase the number of outside directors on the board and decrease the number of company executives on the board. This information can often result in good stories for business reporters.

以下这篇报道展示了《芝加哥论坛报》的比尔·巴恩哈特是如何审视与公司审计师相关的各类反对提案，并将其转化为一篇关于这一趋势的深度报道的：

<!--en-->
The following story shows how Bill Barnhart of the *Chicago Tribune* looked at a variety of dissident shareholders proposals related to corporate auditors and turned them into a broad story about this trend:

能源交易商安然公司的倒闭将为今年的股东大会带来新的活力。

<!--en-->
The implosion of energy trader Enron will provide new vigor to this year's round of shareholder meetings.

维持现状的支持者会将安然的现任及前任高层管理者指责为疏忽大意或欺诈行为——即所谓的“害群之马理论”。但股东活动家则会利用安然案，要求对企业治理流程进行系统性改革。

<!--en-->
Proponents of the status quo will finger Enron's current and former senior management as negligent or fraudulent—the so-called bad apple theory. But shareholder activists will use the Enron case to demand systematic reforms in corporate governance procedures.

通过这种方式，那些正在为4月和5月达峰的年度股东大会做准备的活跃分子，将在此前教育股东并维护其权利所取得的成果基础上继续努力。

<!--en-->
In doing so, activists preparing for the annual meeting season, which peaks in April and May, will build on gains made last year in educating shareholders and asserting their rights.

一项重大进展是美国证券交易委员会出台了一项新规定，要求上市公司披露支付给独立审计师的款项，需分别列出用于审计服务的费用以及用于咨询服务等“其他”工作的费用，因为后者可能与审计工作存在利益冲突。这项于去年实施的规定的出台，体现了那些希望保持现状的人与那些希望禁止审计师为客户从事非审计工作的人之间的妥协。

<!--en-->
A major advance was a new rule by the Securities and Exchange Commission requiring public companies to disclose payments to their independent auditors, broken down into money paid for audit services and money paid for “other” work, such as consulting services, which could pose a conflict of interest with the audit. The requirement, adopted during the past year, represents a compromise between those who wanted no change and those who wanted to ban auditors from engaging in non-audit work for their clients.

总部位于芝加哥、为工会养老金计划提供咨询服务的Marco咨询集团在其关于股东权利问题的年度报告中指出：“鉴于Sunbeam、MicroStrategy、Cendant和Waste Management此前出现的审计丑闻，以及Enron倒闭带来的持续冲击，股东们自然而然地开始质疑其审计师的‘独立性’究竟如何。”

<!--en-->
“In view of past auditing scandals at Sunbeam, MicroStrategy, Cendant and Waste Management and the ongoing horror of Enron's collapse, shareholders naturally began to question how 'independent' their auditors were,” Chicago-based Marco Consulting Group, a consultant to union pension plans, said in its annual review of shareholder rights issues.

这或许将成为一种趋势：积极分子在向娱乐巨头华特迪士尼提出质疑之外，还采取了更多行动。该公司2月19日会议的代理声明中包含一项股东提案，要求禁止目前为迪士尼提供审计服务的普华永道再为其承接其他业务。除了会计舞弊问题外，股东积极分子仍对高管薪酬表示担忧。许多研究都表明，首席执行官的薪资与公司股价的表现并无关联。

<!--en-->
In what could become a trend, activists are doing more than asking questions at entertainment giant Walt Disney. The proxy statement for the company's Feb. 19 meeting contains a shareholder proposal asking that independent auditors, currently PricewaterhouseCoopers, be barred from performing other work for Disney. In addition to accounting shenanigans, shareholder activists remain concerned about executive compensation. Many studies have demonstrated that what the chief executive is paid bears no relation to how well the company's stock performs.

根据Marco集团的分析，去年至少有13次，股东们否决了管理层提出的可能稀释股东权益的股票期权计划。在某些情况下，这些期权计划允许以低于期权授予时股票市场价值的价格行权。去年，股东积极分子利用互联网成功在多家公司争取到了反对派董事会成员的席位。Marco的报告提到了LoneStar Steakhouse & Saloon、Alltrista、Hercules、Willamette Industries和ICN Pharmaceuticals。¹ The Corner Office • 215 本文着眼于日益高涨的股东维权趋势，探讨未来为何股东会提出更多限制，以约束公司对于审计师选聘和高管薪酬确定的控制权。资深商业记者Barnhart充分利用了自己对代理声明及其中股东诉求的了解。每当商业记者在代理声明中发现此类提案时，都应对其加以报道。

<!--en-->
At least 13 times last year, shareholders defeated management-proposed stock option plans that threatened to dilute the stakes of shareholders. In some cases, the options proposals allowed options to be exercised at prices below the market value of the stock at the time of the options grant, according to the Marco Group analysis. Using the Internet, shareholder activists were successful last year in rallying votes for dissident board members at several companies. The Marco report mentions LoneStar Steakhouse & Saloon, Alltrista, Hercules, Willamette Industries and ICN Pharmaceuticals.¹
The Corner Office • 215
This story takes the trend of increasing shareholder agitation and focuses on why shareholders may be proposing more limits on company control of selecting auditors and determining executive compensation in future years. Barnhart, a long-time business journalist, put his knowledge of proxy statements and the shareholder requests in them to good use. Those types of proposals should be written about every time a business reporter finds them in a proxy.

代理声明中还有许多其他信息能引起商业读者的兴趣。大多数商业记者收到代理声明后首先会查看其中的薪酬表格。首席执行官的薪资或奖金在过去一年中上升或下降了多少，显然都是值得关注的新闻。难点在于解读这些数字并向读者解释清楚，因为那些没有拿到代理声明的读者或尚未收到代理声明的投资者同样希望了解这些信息。

<!--en-->
There is plenty of other information in a proxy filing to interest business readers. Most business reporters immediately turn to the compensation chart of a proxy when they receive it. How much a CEO's salary or bonus rose or fell in the past year is obviously news. The hard part is deciphering the numbers and explaining them to readers, who also want to know this information but do not have access to the proxy, or to investors who have not yet received their proxy.

关于薪酬的报道是商业版块中最受关注的类型之一。其他公司的高管想知道同行们的收入水平，公司员工则想了解自己上司的薪资状况，而公司股东则想知道高管是否物有所值。通常可以通过比较某一年首席执行官薪酬包的增减幅度与该年公司股价的增减幅度来判断这一点。大多数投资者希望看到的是，高管的整体薪酬包——包括薪资、奖金、股票期权及其他报酬——能与公司当年的业绩变化保持一定程度的同步。例如，如果在一个公司股价下跌40%、利润下降50%的年份里，首席执行官的薪资却增长了75%，投资者很可能会感到不满，并在年度会议上提出质问。

<!--en-->
Compensation stories are among the most widely read in the business section. Executives at other companies want to know what their counterparts are making down the street. Employees of the company want to know what their boss is pulling in. And company shareholders want to know whether the executive is worth his salary. This can often be determined by comparing the percentage increase or decrease in the CEO's compensation package in any given year with the percentage increase or decrease in the company's stock price for the same year. What most investors would like to see is an executive's total compensation package—his salary, bonus, stock options, and other pay—change somewhat in line with how the company performed for the year. For example, if a CEO's pay increased 75 percent during a year in which the company's stock price fell 40 percent and profits dropped 50 percent, an investor is likely to be upset and could ask questions at the annual meeting.

近年来，美国证券交易委员会对代理声明的披露要求进行了调整，使得记者更容易查明高管的薪资水平。此前，记者必须将薪酬包的各个组成部分加总才能得出总薪酬额，这有时会导致错误。现在，公司必须披露总薪酬额，但不同媒体在报告总薪酬时仍可能存在差异。例如，美联社在2008年出台了相关指南，规定其报道中的高管薪酬计算方式将与代理声明中的薪酬表格有所不同。

<!--en-->
In recent years, the SEC has made changes to the disclosure requirements of proxy statements, making it easier for reporters to ascertain how much an executive was paid. Previously, a journalist would have to add up each part of the compensation package to obtain the total compensation amount. That sometimes led to mistakes. Now, companies have to disclose a total compensation amount. Still, there can be some differences in how total compensation is reported. The Associated Press, for example, issued guidelines in 2008 in which it said its stories would calculate executive compensation differently than in the compensation table in a proxy statement.

此外，新的SEC规则还为记者提供了更多信息。关于高管奖金的确定方式有更清晰的披露，高管持有的所有股票期权也得到了更全面的公开。同时，还有更多信息说明高管离职后会获得多少薪酬，以及其养老金计划的金额。

<!--en-->
In addition, the new SEC rules provide more information for reporters. There is better disclosure as to how an executive's bonus was determined and more complete disclosure of all of the stock options that an executive holds. There's also more information about how much an executive would be paid if he left the company and how much he receives in his pension plan.

代理声明是上市公司每年公布高管薪酬的唯一渠道，它说明了谁获得了高额薪酬，奖金数额是多少。

<!--en-->
The proxy is the only place in which public companies annually release executive compensation. It explains who is making the big bucks, how much of a bonus

### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

道琼斯通讯社副主编Michael Reid谈如何报道高管薪酬：

<!--en-->
Dow Jones Newswires deputy managing editor Michael Reid on covering executive compensation:

不要被巨额数字吓到、激怒或影响判断：高管们与华尔街的精英们生活在另一个世界，他们所获得的薪资、奖金及股票奖励在普通职场看来简直高得离谱。但请记住，在这些人所处的特殊环境中，这些数字应当结合具体背景来评估。也就是说，不要被表面上的民粹主义言论左右。人们很容易认为任何超过100万美元的薪酬都过高，但实际上，业绩表现、职位职责、目标设定，以及竞争对手、前任、股价表现和利润状况等都是帮助你公正准确地评估薪酬的重要因素。

<!--en-->
Don't be spooked, angered or swayed by big numbers: Executives and Wall Street stars live in a different world where the sorts of salaries, bonuses and stock plans they get seem obscene on Main Street, but remember, in the rarefied air in which these people operate, the numbers should be simply assessed contextually. That is, don't be swung by blatant populism. It would be easy to consider any $1 million-plus compensation package excessive, but performance, job, goals and the context of rivals, predecessors, stock performance and profit are all important ingredients to help you report fairly and accurately about compensation.

### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《克雷恩纽约商业报》资深记者亚伦·埃尔斯坦关于报道高管薪酬的观点：

<!--en-->
Crain's New York Business senior reporter Aaron Elstein on covering executive compensation:

阅读薪酬表可了解公司薪酬最高的五名员工名单。这份名单中是否有你原本认为不应获得与CEO同等或更高薪酬的人？不过，标明“总薪酬”的数字并非高管实际总收入的真实数值。要得到准确数字，必须进一步查看年度委托书，查找该年度授予高管的股票和期权价值，并将其加到“总薪酬”上。最简单的办法是咨询像Equilar或Salary.com这样的研究机构，它们以分析薪酬数据为业，能够为你提供相关数据。[^2373]：¹ 摘自B. Barnhart所著《激进股东推动变革》，2002年1月8日，《芝加哥论坛报》，第8页。版权所有2002年《芝加哥论坛报》，经许可转载。

<!--en-->
Read the compensation table to get a list of the company's five best-paid people. Does this list include anyone who you wouldn't expect to get paid as much (or more) than the CEO? However, the table that reads "total compensation" is not the true number for the executives' total pay. To get that figure, you must go further into the proxy and look up the value of the stock and options that were granted to the executive during the year and add that figure to the "total compensation." The easiest solution is to ask a service like Equilar or Salary.com, which are research firms that crunch pay data for a living, to tell you what their reading is of the numbers.
[^2373]: ¹ From "Activist shareholder forcing change," by B. Barnhart, January 8, 2002, *Chicago Tribune*, p. 8. Copyright 2002 by *Chicago Tribune*. Reprinted with permission.

216 • “总裁办公室”奖项是在过去一年中颁发的，同时还会注明是否授予了股票期权。“其他所有薪酬”这一类别往往是最有趣的部分。

<!--en-->
216 • The Corner Office was awarded in the past year, and whether stock options were granted. A category called “All other compensation” is often the most interesting section.

### 专家建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

道琼斯通讯社副主编Michael Reid关于报道高管薪酬的观点：

<!--en-->
Dow Jones Newswires deputy managing editor Michael Reid on covering executive compensation:

### DEF 14A表格就是关于薪酬的“圣典”：

<!--en-->
*The DEF 14A is your “Holy Book” of compensation:*

每年，上市公司都必须公开披露其高管薪酬的完整明细。为此，证券申报文件DEF 14A堪称核心文件。它通常会在公司年度股东大会前的规定期限内提交给美国证券交易委员会（从而成为公开文件）。（由于许多财年与日历年一致，3月是最常见的DEF 14A提交时间。）该文件会详细列出前一年最高级别高管的薪酬情况，而各种支付形式（工资、奖金等）的完整分类则可在“薪酬汇总表”中找到。“计划奖励授予”表格也会显示高管所获得的股票和期权奖励的价值。现有薪酬的变动信息也可以在常规的8-K文件中找到，因此也要留意这些文件。不过务必学会如何查阅这些文件。关于薪酬的诸多细节可能出现在脚注、表格、盈利报告及其他文件中。仔细研究这些内容往往能获得比单纯阅读14A表格更多的细节和分析。218 • 《The Corner Office》

<!--en-->
Each year, publicly traded companies must disclose their full menu of executive compensation. For this, the securities filing DEF 14A is the Holy Grail. It's usually filed with the Securities and Exchanges Commission (and therefore becomes a public document) within a set period before the company's annual general meeting with shareholders. (Given that many fiscal years are also calendar years, March is the most common period for DEF 14As.) This filing provides details of the previous year's compensation for the highest ranking executives and a full breakdown of the various forms of payment (salary, bonus, etc.) is best found in the section “Summary Compensation Table.” The “Grants of Plan-Based Awards” table also gives the value of stock and option awards to the executive. Changes to existing compensation may also be found in a regular 8-K filing, so keep an eye out for those, too. But make sure you learn to find your way through filings. There are a number of issues relating to compensation which can be found in footnotes, tables, earnings reports and other filings. Poring over them can produce more detail and analysis than simply reading the 14A.
218 • The Corner Office

#### 专家建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

道琼斯通讯社副主编Michael Reid关于报道高管薪酬的观点：

<!--en-->
Dow Jones Newswires deputy managing editor Michael Reid on covering executive compensation:

**工资与薪酬并非同一概念：** 如今，工资已不像过去那样令人瞩目，但它却掩盖了高管可能获得的全部薪酬。那些在文件中显示年薪为845,000美元的首席执行官，实际上很可能还能获得2000万美元的“其他薪酬”。日益强烈的反华尔街情绪催生了一个专门的“薪酬顾问”行业。这些人想出了各种巧妙的办法来设计多元化的薪酬方案（他们也是值得关注的消息来源）。其中包括工资、奖金、股票奖金、股票期权、受限股票、各项费用，还有臭名昭著的“税前加算额”（一种帮助高管缴纳税款，使其实际拿到手的薪酬达到面值的方式）。而这还只是开始。所有这些内容都可以在美国证券交易委员会的详细文件中找到，但有时在其他文件中也能发现一些有价值的信息。

<!--en-->
**Salary and compensation aren't the same thing:** These days, salaries aren't as impressive as they once were, but they mask the full payout an executive can receive. A CEO whose salary is listed in filings as $845,000 a year can easily be awarded $20 million in "compensation." The rising anti-Wall Street sentiment has spawned an entire industry of "compensation consultants." These people have dreamt up ingenious ways of creating multi-pronged compensation packages (and they're also good sources to cultivate). There's salary, bonus, stock bonus, stock options, restricted stock, expenses and the notorious "gross-ups" (a way of paying the executive's tax so he gets face value for his pay package). And that's just for starters. All of these will be found in the detailed part of Securities and Exchange Commission filings, but sometimes you can find nuggets of information in other documents.

艾尔斯的奖金比上一年高出许多。薪酬委员会的报告对此作出了解释，内容如下：

<!--en-->
Ailes's bonus is much larger than it was the previous year. The compensation committee report explains why, stating the following:

根据此项安排，薪酬委员会向艾尔斯先生发放了550万美元的现金形式的FOX新闻频道奖金，这一数额反映了FOX新闻频道在2009财年的业绩表现，其EBITDA数值处于该区间的高水平。此外，根据他之前的雇佣协议条款，当FOX商业频道的公允市场价值达到雇佣协议规定的成本两倍时，艾尔斯先生在2008年10月获得了333,333股我们的A类普通股。

<!--en-->
Pursuant to this arrangement, the Compensation Committee awarded Mr. Ailes a FOX News Channel Bonus of $5.5 million in cash, reflecting FOX News Channel's performance in fiscal 2009 which was at the highest end of the EBITDA range. In addition, pursuant to the terms of his prior employment agreement, in October 2008, Mr. Ailes received 333,333 shares of our Class A Common Stock when the fair market value of the FOX Business Network reached two times its cost as determined pursuant to the terms of the employment agreement.

（新闻集团，DEF 14A表格，2009年，第25页）在阅读了足够多的委托书后，记者会开始发现一些规律。其中之一就是许多公司会将股票期权作为高管薪酬包的一部分。股票期权是一种激励手段，旨在促使CEO及其他高管提升公司业绩，进而推动股价上涨——从而让CEO获得更高的资产收益。

<!--en-->
(News Corporation, Form DEF 14A, 2009, p. 25)
After reading enough proxy statements, the reporter will begin to establish some patterns. One is that many companies give stock options to their executives as part of their compensation packages. The stock options are a way of providing an incentive to the CEO and other executives to improve the company's performance, which should lead to a higher stock price—and higher assets for the CEO.

假设有一家名为ACME Inc.的虚构公司。ACME的薪酬委员会决定为其高管们提供一些股票期权。CEO获得了100,000份股票期权，有权以每股25美元的价格购买股票。无论股票价格如何上涨，他通常都有大约10年的时间，可以按每股25美元的价格行权。CEO想要做的是在股票价格远高于25美元时行权并买入股票，因为他只需支付事先约定的25美元价格。他这么做的原因是，如果他能将ACME的股票价格抬高到每股50美元，那么这100,000股股票的价值就将高达500万美元。根据与薪酬委员会达成的协议，CEO只需花费250万美元就能以每股25美元的价格买下这些股票。通过这笔交易，他在扣除税费后便已赚取了250万美元的利润。很多时候，高管们在行权后会立即以更高的价格卖出股票。这正是商业记者应该报道的内容。

<!--en-->
Consider a fictitious company called ACME Inc. ACME's compensation committee decides to give its executives some stock options. The CEO is granted 100,000 stock options, allowing him to purchase the stock at $25 per share. He typically has a certain amount of time, perhaps 10 years, to exercise those options at $25 per share, regardless of how high the stock is valued. What the CEO wants to do is exercise his options and buy the stock when it is at a price much higher than $25 per share because he will only be paying the prearranged $25 price. He wants to do this because if he can get ACME's stock price up to $50 per share, those 100,000 shares of stock are now worth $5 million. Mr. CEO will spend $2.5 million to buy those shares at $25 per share, on the basis of the agreement struck with the compensation committee. He has just pocketed a profit of $2.5 million, minus taxes, in this transaction. Many times, executives turn around and sell the stock at the higher price immediately after exercising the options. That is a story for a business reporter.

当然，情况也常常相反。CEO及其他高管可能无法将股价抬高至期权行权价以上，导致期权变得一文不值。如果股票价格仅为15美元，还有谁会愿意以25美元的价格购买呢？不过，有些公司有时会修改股票期权协议，降低高管们购买股票的价格。这会令投资者不满，理应成为头版新闻。

<!--en-->
Of course, the opposite often happens. The CEO and other executives can be unsuccessful in raising the stock price above the option price, making the options worthless. Who would purchase stock for $25 per share if it were trading at $15 per share? However, companies sometimes change the stock option agreement, lowering the price at which executives can purchase shares. This upsets investors and should be front-page news.

期权到期时同样具有重要意义。如果到期日即将到来，而公司的股票价格仍未达到期权行权价水平，CEO可能会寻找另一家愿意以高于期权行权价的价格收购整个公司的企业。这样，他或她就可以在期权到期前行权。

<!--en-->
It is also significant when the options expire. If the expiration date is coming up soon and the company's shares have not yet reached the option price level, the CEO may seek to find another company willing to purchase the entire company at a price tag above the option price. That way, he or she can exercise the options before they expire.

了解高管们是否在行权非常重要。如果在行权价低于当前股价时他们并未行权，那就表明他们更倾向于将资金投入其他领域。本章后面将会介绍如何判断高管是在买入还是卖出股票。这些内容尤为重要，因为期权是公司在给高管发放工资和奖金之外，用于提供额外“补偿”的一种方式。股东权利活动人士也批评向高管授予大量股票期权的行为过于奢侈，因为公司高管本就已经获得了数百万美元的薪酬包。《高管办公室》•219家公司还会向高管提供所谓的受限股票。受限股票相比股票期权有更多限制。大多数向高管提供受限股票的公司都会设定规定，要求高管在退休前不得出售这些股票。如果高管在退休年龄之前离职，这些受限股票将被没收。不过，在大多数情况下，尽管高管实际上并不控制这些股票，他们仍能获得股票的股息分红。向高管授予受限股票和股票期权往往会让其薪酬包增加数百万美元。这同样是值得报道的新闻。

<!--en-->
It is important to know whether executives are exercising options. If they are not exercising options when the exercise price is below the current price, that is a sign that they feel more comfortable putting their money elsewhere. Later, this chapter examines how to find out if an executive is buying or selling stock. These items are of particular interest because options are a way for companies to paytheir executives additional “compensation” in addition to salary and bonuses. Shareholder rights activists also criticize large stock option awards to executives as being excessive because company executives are already being paid multimillion-dollar compensation packages.
The Corner Office • 219
Companies also give executives what is called restricted stock. Restricted stock has more limits than stock options. Most companies that give executives restricted stock set limits that the executive cannot sell the stock prior to retirement. If the executive leaves the company before retirement age, the restricted stock is forfeited. In most cases, however, the executive receives dividends paid on the stock, despite the fact he or she does not actually control the stock. The granting of restricted stock and stock options to executives often adds millions of dollars to an executive’s compensation package. That is news.

记者应在委托书中其他地方寻找有关薪酬以及高管为何会获得股票期权和受限股票的解释。最好的信息来源是所谓的“薪酬委员会报告”。薪酬委员会由董事会成员组成。这份关于高管薪酬的报告通常与高管薪酬图表放在一起。记者应查找那些担任薪酬委员会成员、负责决定高管薪酬数额的董事会成员所撰写的报告。

<!--en-->
A reporter should look elsewhere in the proxy for explanations about compensation and why executives are receiving stock options and restricted stock. A reporter’s best bet is what is called the “Compensation Committee Report.” The compensation committee is composed of board members. This report on executive compensation is usually found with the chart on executive compensation. A reporter should look for the report from the members of the board of directors who sit on the compensation committee and who decide how much or how little executives get paid.

例如，新闻集团薪酬委员会的报告向读者披露了以下内容：

<!--en-->
For example, the News Corporation compensation committee report informs readers of the following:

该公司与罗杰·艾尔斯于2008年11月签订了修订后的雇佣协议，该协议取代了他此前的雇佣协议。艾尔斯此前雇佣协议的期限原定于2010年8月到期，而新的雇佣协议则延长至2013年6月30日。根据新协议，在截至2011年6月30日、2012年6月30日及2013年6月30日的财政年度中，艾尔斯可获得的最低年度奖金从1,000,000美元提高到了1,250,000美元。与之前的雇佣协议一样，艾尔斯在新的雇佣协议有效期内也有资格获得福克斯新闻频道的奖金。2009财年支付给艾尔斯的福克斯新闻频道奖金在0美元至550万美元之间，且这一上限每年都会上升，到新雇佣协议的最后一个财政年度时已达到1,000万美元。

<!--en-->
The Company and Roger Ailes entered into the Amended and Restated Employment Agreement in November 2008, which replaced his then current employment agreement. The term of Mr. Ailes’ prior employment agreement was scheduled to expire in August 2010, and the new employment agreement extends through June 30, 2013. The new employment agreement increases the minimum annual bonus Mr. Ailes is entitled to receive from $1,000,000 to $1,250,000 for the fiscal years ending June 30, 2011, June 30, 2012 and June 30, 2013. As with his prior employment agreement, Mr. Ailes is also eligible to receive a FOX News Channel Bonus during the term of his new employment agreement. The FOX News Channel Bonus payable to Mr. Ailes in fiscal 2009 ranged from $0 to $5.5 million, with the high end of the range increasing each year up to $10 million in the final fiscal year of the new employment agreement.

（新闻集团，DEF 14A表格，2009年，第27页）该报告指出，尽管艾尔斯在2008年的奖金已经很高，但在未来几年还可能进一步增加。一篇关于新闻集团代理声明的报道可能会这样开头：

<!--en-->
(News Corporation, Form DEF 14A, 2009, p. 27)
The report tells how Ailes’ bonus, while already large in 2008, could increase even more in future years. A story written about the News Corporation proxy might begin the following way:

根据新闻集团向其监管机构提交的代理声明，由于公司财务状况有所改善，福克斯新闻频道的首席执行官在2008年获得了更高的奖金。

<!--en-->
The chief executive officer of Fox News Channel received a higher bonus in 2008 due to the company’s improved financial performance, according to a proxy statement filed by parent News Corporation with regulators.

#### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《克雷恩纽约商业报》资深记者亚伦·埃尔斯坦谈报道高管薪酬的经验：

<!--en-->
Crain’s New York Business senior reporter Aaron Elstein on covering executive compensation:

显然，高管的薪酬容易引发公愤，但无法脱离具体背景来评判薪酬。必须考察该公司与往年的表现对比——其股价走势如何？这又是一家怎样的公司？我的意思是，它是由一位创始人/企业家为了回报多年前所冒的风险而管理的公司，还是由一群人在接管之前就已成功的业务基础上从中牟利？公司是否因某次并不理想的并购而快速发展，进而提升了首席执行官的薪酬？通过提出这类问题，你的报道才能更有深度。220 • 高管办公室

<!--en-->
Obviously executive pay lends itself to outrage, but you can’t judge pay in a vacuum. You have to look at how the company fared compared to prior years. How did its stock price perform? And what kind of company is this? By that, I mean is it a place run by a founder/entrepreneur rewarding himself for taking a chance years ago? Or is management a bunch of guys milking a business that was successful before they took over? Did the company grow fast—and boost the CEO’s pay—based on a merger that isn’t panning out? Asking questions like that along the way will give your story depth.
220 • The Corner Office

#### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

道琼斯新闻专线副主编迈克尔·里德谈报道高管薪酬的经验：

<!--en-->
Dow Jones Newswires deputy managing editor Michael Reid on covering executive compensation:

**重复计数的风险：**在DEF 14A表格中，你经常会看到附有估值的期权或限制性股票奖励。该估值是基于布莱克-斯科尔斯模型得出的。但对于薪酬领域的初学者来说，这里存在一个风险：那只是名义价值（即在授予高管时对该奖励价值的最佳估算）。换句话说，它并不能反映高管最终能从这些期权或限制性股票中获利多少。由于这些权益在未来才会逐步归属，如果在评估高管整体薪酬时同时计入其早年已归属期权在同一年可能获得的收益，那就既不公平也不准确。换言之，这就是重复计数。请选择其中一种方式，并用精确的措辞表述。

<!--en-->
**The danger of double counting:** In the DEF 14A you will often see an options or restricted stock award with a value attached. The value is based on the Black-Scholes method of determining what an award is worth. But here's the danger for the compensation novice: That is a nominal value only (that is, a best guess of what the award is worth at the time it's given to the executive). In other words, it doesn't reflect how much the executive may eventually recoup from those options or restricted stock. Because it vests some time in the future, it's unfair and inaccurate to include this amount in valuing an executive's package if you also include the amount he/she may receive in the same year from vested options awarded years earlier. In other words, it's double-counting. Pick one or the other and word your phrasing precisely.

##### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《克雷恩纽约商业报》资深记者亚伦·埃尔斯坦谈报道高管薪酬的经验：

<!--en-->
Crain's New York Business senior reporter Aaron Elstein on covering executive compensation:

公司必须公开其为高管提供的各种福利及其金额。这些福利可能包括使用公司专机、汽车和司机、协助办理税务、为住所安装防盗系统、提供豪华公寓等。这些福利通常会在薪酬表的脚注中列出。请仔细阅读脚注，因为有趣的信息往往就在那里。

<!--en-->
Companies must disclose the perks they dole out to execs and the dollar value of these items. They can include personal use of the corporate jet, car and driver, help with preparing their taxes, a burglar alarm at their home, a fancy apartment, etc. These goodies are typically broken out in footnotes to the compensation table. Read the footnotes carefully, because this is where this juicy stuff lies.

### 特殊交易与董事会成员

<!--en-->
*Sweetheart Deals and Board Members*

代理声明中另一个引人注目的部分通常位于董事会成员名单之后，名为“某些关系及相关交易”。该部分详细说明了董事会成员与公司之间的业务关系。例如，如果某位董事会成员是律师，该部分会以具体金额说明公司每年向其律所支付的费用。

<!--en-->
Another eyebrow-raising section of the proxy, normally found right after the list of the members of the board of directors, is a section called “Certain Relationships and Related Transactions.” It details business relationships between board members and the company. For example, if a board member is an attorney, this section will detail, in dollar amounts, how much the company is paying his or her law firm in annual fees.

赫布·艾伦是纽约的一名投资银行家，他所在的艾伦公司也为可口可乐公司提供服务。在2009年的代理声明中，该公司公开了二者之间的关系：

<!--en-->
Herb Allen is an investment banker in New York, and his firm Allen & Company does work for the Coca-Cola Company. In this section of the 2009 proxy, the company discloses that relationship:

我们的董事之一赫伯特·A·艾伦同时也是艾伦公司（“ACI”）的总裁、首席执行官兼董事，以及该公司母公司的主要股东。ACI是艾伦有限责任公司（“ACL”）的间接股权持有者。ACI已于2002年9月将其投资和财务咨询业务转移给了ACL。

<!--en-->
Herbert A. Allen, one of our Directors, is President, Chief Executive Officer and a Director of Allen & Company Incorporated (“ACI”) and a principal shareowner of ACI’s parent. ACI is an indirect equity holder of Allen & Company LLC (“ACL”). ACI transferred its investment and financial advisory services business to ACL in September 2002.

自1977年起，ACI一直在我们一家子公司拥有的位于纽约州纽约市第五大道711号的建筑内租赁并转租办公空间。2005年6月，ACI将该租赁权及转租权转让给了ACL。2008年，ACL支付了约480万美元的租金及相关费用；根据现有租赁条款，预计2009年ACL仍将支付类似金额。管理层认为，该租赁条款在2002年经过修改后依然公平合理，且与签订租赁合同时能从无关第三方处获得的条款相比对本公司十分有利。

<!--en-->
ACI has leased and subleased office space since 1977 in a building owned by one of our subsidiaries and located at 711 Fifth Avenue, New York, New York. In June 2005, ACI assigned the lease and sublease to ACL. In 2008, ACL paid approximately $4.8 million in rent and related expenses and it is expected that ACL will pay a similar amount in 2009 under the terms of the current lease. In the opinion of management, the terms of the lease, which were modified in 2002, are fair and reasonable and as favorable to the Company as those that could have been obtained from unrelated third parties at the time of the execution of the lease.

2008年，本公司就一项潜在交易向ACL支付了150万美元，作为其提供的财务咨询服务费。管理层认为，该财务咨询服务的条款公平合理，且与从无关第三方处获得的条款相比对本公司同样有利。

<!--en-->
In 2008, the Company paid ACL $1.5 million for financial advisory services it provided in connection with a potential transaction. In the opinion of management, the terms of the financial advisory services arrangement are fair and reasonable and as favorable to the Company as those which could be obtained from unrelated third parties.

（可口可乐公司，2009年DEF 14A表格，第25页）鉴于Allen & Company数十年来一直为可口可乐提供服务，单凭这一点可能并不值得报道。（商业记者可以通过查阅旧年的委托书来了解相关情况。）不过，如果记者遇到涉及可口可乐及其律师的报道，这一信息还是值得记住的。

<!--en-->
(Coca-Cola Company, Form DEF 14A 2009, p. 25)
On its own, this is probably not something worth reporting, given that Allen & Company has done work for Coca-Cola for decades. (A business reporter can look this up by going back and reading old proxies.) Still, it is worth remembering should the reporter run across a story involving Coca-Cola and its attorneys.

可口可乐的委托书中有更详细的关于其与沃伦·巴菲特旗下公司关系的说明。巴菲特是伯克希尔·哈撒韦的董事长，这家总部位于奥马哈的公司拥有众多子公司，业务范围从地毯制造到珠宝销售不等。披露内容如下：

<!--en-->
The section in Coca-Cola’s proxy detailing its relationships with Warren Buffett’s companies is more detailed. Buffett is chairman of Berkshire Hathaway, an Omaha company that owns dozens of companies, from carpet makers to jewelers. The disclosure states the following:

McLane Company, Inc.（“McLane”）是伯克希尔·哈撒韦的全资子公司。2008年，McLane在日常业务中为购买喷泉糖浆及其他产品而向本公司支付了总计约1.37亿美元的费用。同年，McLane还因在日常业务中向客户销售本公司产品而获得了约780万美元的代理佣金、营销费用及其他相关款项。在伯克希尔·哈撒韦于2003年收购McLane之前，这种业务关系已存在多年，且条款公平合理，与本公司与其他客户之间的业务关系基本相似。The Corner Office • 221 International Dairy Queen, Inc.（“IDQ”）也是伯克希尔·哈撒韦的全资子公司。2008年，IDQ及其子公司在日常业务中为购买其门店所需的喷泉糖浆及其他产品，直接或通过装瓶商及其他代理商向本公司支付了总计约200万美元的费用。特许经营店的付款不包含在内。同年，IDQ及其子公司还因企业店和特许经营店的销售规模获得了促销及营销奖励，总计从本公司及其子公司处获得了约170万美元的款项。在伯克希尔·哈撒韦收购IDQ之前，这种业务关系已存在多年，且条款公平合理，与本公司与其他客户之间的业务关系基本相似。

<!--en-->
McLane Company, Inc. (“McLane”) is a wholly owned subsidiary of Berkshire Hathaway. In 2008, McLane made payments totaling approximately $137 million to the Company to purchase fountain syrup and other products in the ordinary course of business. Also in 2008, McLane received from the Company approximately $7.8 million in agency commissions, marketing payments and other fees relating to the sale of the Company’sproducts to customers in the ordinary course of business. This business relationship was in place for many years prior to Berkshire Hathaway's acquisition of McLane in 2003, is fair and reasonable, and is on terms substantially similar to the Company's relationships with other customers.
The Corner Office • 221
International Dairy Queen, Inc. ("IDQ") is a wholly owned subsidiary of Berkshire Hathaway. Payments from franchised stores are not included.
