This business relationship was in place for many years prior to Berkshire Hathaway's acquisition of IDQ, is fair and reasonable, and is on terms substantially similar to the Company's relationships with other customers.

FlightSafety International, Inc.（“FlightSafety”）是伯克希尔·哈撒韦的全资子公司。2008年，本公司因其在日常业务中为本公司提供飞行员、空乘人员及机械师培训服务而向其支付了约854,000美元。管理层认为，提供这些服务的FlightSafety协议条款公平合理，且与签订协议时能从无关第三方处获得的条款相比对本公司十分有利。

<!--en-->
FlightSafety International, Inc. ("FlightSafety") is a wholly owned subsidiary of Berkshire Hathaway. In 2008, the Company paid FlightSafety approximately $854,000 for providing pilot, flight attendant and mechanic training services to the Company in the ordinary course of business. In the opinion of management, the terms of the FlightSafety agreement under which these services are provided are fair and reasonable, and as favorable to the Company as those which could have been obtained from unrelated third parties at the time of the execution of the agreement.

XTRA Lease LLC（“XTRA”）是伯克希尔·哈撒韦的全资子公司。2008年，本公司为在日常业务中使用用于运输和储存产品的拖车而向XTRA支付了约187,000美元的租金。管理层认为，该租赁条款公平合理，且与签订租赁合同时能从无关第三方处获得的条款相比对本公司十分有利。

<!--en-->
XTRA Lease LLC ("XTRA") is a wholly owned subsidiary of Berkshire Hathaway. In 2008, the Company paid approximately $187,000 to XTRA for the rental of trailers used to transport and store product in the ordinary course of business. In the opinion of management, the terms of the lease are fair and reasonable, and as favorable to the Company as those which could have been obtained from unrelated third parties at the time of the execution of the lease.

（可口可乐公司，2009年DEF 14A表格，第25–6页）同样，可口可乐与巴菲特旗下公司的所有这些关系似乎都是正当的。但对于任何商业记者而言，这部分委托书都是必读内容，因为它可能会详细列出一些可能引发疑问的商业交易。记者还会发现一些有趣的交易，比如下面这个在Progressive Corporation 2000年的委托书中有所记载的交易。在该文件提交时，彼得·刘易斯是该公司的首席执行官。

<!--en-->
(Coca-Cola Company, Form DEF 14A, 2009, pp. 25–6)
Again, all of these relationships between Coca-Cola and Buffett's companies seem legitimate. But this section of the proxy is required reading for any business reporter because it could detail business dealings that might raise questions. A reporter will also find interesting transactions such as the one below, which was detailed in Progressive Corporation's 2000 proxy. At the time this document was filed, Peter Lewis was the company's CEO.

1999年4月23日，该公司将其公司专机——一架Canadair Challenger 601-1 A型飞机——卖给了由彼得·B·刘易斯独立拥有的公司。根据独立飞机评估机构JetPerspectives, Inc.确定的公允市场价值，该飞机以1210万美元的价格卖给了刘易斯先生。在出售当日，该飞机的账面净值约为690万美元。该飞机的运营由两名飞行员和一名机械师负责，他们均为该公司一家子公司的雇员。刘易斯先生会为这些雇员的工资及其他所有薪酬支出向该公司进行补偿。

<!--en-->
On April 23, 1999, the Company sold its corporate airplane, a Canadair Challenger 601-1 A, to a company independently owned by Peter B. Lewis. The airplane was sold to Mr. Lewis for $12.1 million, the fair market value as determined by JetPerspectives, Inc., an independent aircraft appraiser. The net book value of the airplane was $6.9 million at the date of the sale. Operation of the airplane is supported by two pilots and a mechanic, who are employees of a subsidiary of the Company. Mr. Lewis reimburses the Company for the salaries and all other payroll costs of such employees

#### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

道琼斯通讯社副主编迈克尔·里德谈高管薪酬报道：

<!--en-->
Dow Jones Newswires deputy managing editor Michael Reid on covering executive compensation:

**精确性至关重要：**与商业新闻领域的任何主题一样，用词精确非常重要。现金总额并不等同于总薪酬，而总薪酬又可能与总报酬有所不同。现金即工资加奖金，总薪酬则是现金加上股票价值，总报酬则还包括其他非股票形式的福利。请记住，高管被授予的权利并不一定意味着他们最终能得到相应的东西。期权价值是波动的。事实上，如果股价长期下跌，期权的价值可能会大幅降低甚至归零；而如果股价飙升，基于布莱克-斯科尔斯模型的股票授予估值很可能远低于高管实际获得的收益。

<!--en-->
**Precision is vital:** As with any theme in business journalism, precise wording matters. Total cash is not the same as total compensation and total compensation can be different from total remuneration. Cash is cash (salary plus bonus), total compensation is total cash plus the value of stock and total remuneration includes other non-stock benefits. And remember, what an executive is granted is not necessarily what he will get. The value of options fluctuates. Indeed, if the stock declines over a long period, the options and stock may have little or less value. If the stock soars, the Black-Scholes estimate of a stock grant will likely be a fraction of what the executive gleans.

222 • The Corner Office会直接支付或补偿该公司因飞机的储存、维护、使用及运营而产生的所有运营费用及其他成本。对于刘易斯先生因执行与公司相关的业务或担任董事会成员而使用该飞机的情况，该公司会按照JetPerspectives, Inc.挑选的三家飞机包租公司提供的报价，以每小时3,567美元的标准（即同类飞机的包租价格）向其进行补偿。

<!--en-->
222 • The Corner Office and pays directly or reimburses the Company for all operating and other costs that the Company incurs in connection with the storage, maintenance, use and operation of the airplane. The Company reimburses Mr. Lewis at the rate of $3,567 per hour, the air charter rate for comparable aircraft (based on the quotes obtained from three air charter companies selected by JetPerspectives, Inc.), for his use of the airplane on Company-related business or as a member of the Board of Directors.

（Progressive Corporation，2000年DEF 14A表格，第5页）至少乍看之下，这似乎是一种合理的安排。这份声明明确了公司在飞机出售事宜上与首席执行官之间的关系，以防出现疑问。但好奇的记者可能会打电话了解这种型号飞机的价值以及飞机包租的市场行情。

<!--en-->
(Progressive Corporation, Form DEF 14A, 2000, p. 5)
This seems like a reasonable arrangement, at least at first reading. The statement clarifies the relationship between the company and the CEO in case questions should arise regarding the airplane sale. But an inquisitive reporter may want to make a few phone calls on the value of this model of airplane and the going rate for chartering planes.

医疗保健服务提供商Aetna Incorporated在其2000年的委托书中也披露了董事会成员伦纳德·阿布拉姆森与其亲属之间的一些有趣关系。

<!--en-->
Health care provider Aetna Incorporated also disclosed some interesting relationships among board member Leonard Abramson and his relatives in its 2000 proxy statement.

该公司的一家子公司根据1999年签订的独立承包协议，向阿布拉姆森先生的女婿理查德·沃尔夫森支付了150,469美元，作为对其所提供服务的报酬。

<!--en-->
A subsidiary of the Company paid Richard Wolfson, a son-in-law of Mr. Abramson, $150,469 under an independent contractor agreement for services rendered in 1999.

1999年间，该公司及其子公司根据服务协议向Criterion Communications, Inc.支付了7,068,958美元。玛西·舒梅克（阿布拉姆森先生的女儿）持有Criterion公司全部已发行有表决权证券的100%股份。

<!--en-->
During 1999, the Company and its subsidiaries paid $7,068,958 to Criterion Communications, Inc. pursuant to a service agreement. Marcy Shoemaker (a daughter of Mr. Abramson) owns 100 percent of the outstanding voting securities of Criterion.

（Aetna Incorporated，2000年DEF 14A表格，第16页）这或许是个值得报道的故事。这类财务安排显然属于最恶劣形式的裙带关系。当阿布拉姆森从董事会辞职后，美联社和《费城问询报》都对此类关系进行了报道。《费城问询报》文章的第四段内容如下：

<!--en-->
(Aetna Incorporated, Form DEF 14A, 2000, p. 16)
This may be a story. Such financial arrangements smack of nepotism at its worst. And when Abramson resigned from the board, these relationships were reported in an Associated Press story and in a *Philadelphia Inquirer* story. The fourth paragraph of the *Inquirer* story stated the following:

据美联社援引该公司向美国证券交易委员会提交的财务报表称，自1996年以来，阿布拉姆森的两个女儿和女婿也从这家保险公司获得了超过1800万美元的款项。（Stark，2000）随后，该报道还引用了批评这些咨询费用安排的股东意见。委托书的其它部分也能提供线索，帮助了解某些董事会成员究竟拥有多少权力。了解哪些董事会成员属于哪个委员会非常重要，因为担任诸如薪酬委员会之类的委员会成员可能会导致权力滥用。

<!--en-->
Abramson's two daughters and son-in-law also were paid more than $18 million by the insurer since 1996, according to the Associated Press, which cited financial statements filed by the company with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.
(Stark, 2000)
Later, the story quotes shareholders criticizing the consulting fee arrangements. Other sections of the proxy can provide clues as to how much power certain board members have. It is important to see which board members belong to which committees. Membership on certain committees, such as the compensation committee, can result in abuses of power.

对于商业记者而言，查看列有公司最大股东名单的“主要股东表”也很重要。该列表应包含每位董事会成员、每位高层管理人员以及最大机构投资者的持股数量。董事会成员持有的股份越多，其在会议中行使权力的可能性就越大。

<!--en-->
It is also important for a business writer to review the “Chart of Principal Ownership,” which lists the largest shareholders of the company. The list should include the number of shares owned by every board member, every top executive, and the largest institutional investors. The more shares owned by a board member, the more power he or she is likely to wield at meetings.

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/d27eb2f79eb9e612bd2d130c81025f08.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T071651Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=bcd52538383b26551770d8cba17a22a5d417f17b056a8bef05a75093802abb15)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/d27eb2f79eb9e612bd2d130c81025f08.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T071651Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=bcd52538383b26551770d8cba17a22a5d417f17b056a8bef05a75093802abb15)

The Corner Office • 223通常情况下，公司的首席执行官或前任首席执行官应当是最大的个人股东之一。此外，董事会成员的持股量也应逐年增加。记者应将当年的持股情况表与上一年的表格进行对比，以判断董事会成员是否在增持股票。如果他们没有增持，或许应该询问原因。如果某位董事会成员的持股量在上升，那可能预示着公司未来前景向好。

<!--en-->
The Corner Office • 223
The company CEO or a former CEO should be, typically, one of the largest individual shareholders. In addition, board members should increase their stock ownership annually. A reporter should check the stock ownership chart for the current year with the one from the previous year to determine if board members are buying more stock. If they are not, then maybe they should be asked why. If a board member's stock holdings are going up, that could indicate a bullish future.

这张图表还有另一个重要价值：它列出了那些既非公司高管也非董事会成员的最大股东名单。如果公司出现危机，记者应联系这些股东。该部分的脚注有时会包含这些股东的家庭住址，这有助于记者找到他们的电话号码。

<!--en-->
This chart is also valuable for another reason. It lists the largest shareholders who are not company executives or board members. Reporters should call them if the company implodes. Sometimes the footnotes of this section contain home addresses for these shareholders, which should help reporters dig up some phone numbers for them.

## 内幕交易

<!--en-->
*Insider Trading*

如果你询问普通路人关于内幕交易的看法，他们很可能会给出未经了解的评论，认为这是不道德的行为，政府应当更积极地介入并严厉打击此类案件。或许很多人都知道，家居专家玛莎·斯图尔特因在调查ImClone股票内幕交易时作伪证而被判有罪，而她可能是从该公司前首席执行官萨姆·瓦克斯尔那里获得了内幕消息，后者已离职并承认了自己从事内幕交易的行为。

<!--en-->
Ask the average person on the street about insider trading, and he will make the uninformed comment that it is immoral and that the government should step in and be more aggressive in prosecuting cases. Many people probably know that home maven Martha Stewart was convicted of perjury in an investigation into insider trading of ImClone stock based on a tip she might have gotten from the company's former CEO, Sam Waksal, who stepped down from the company and pleaded guilty to insider trading.

人们没有意识到的是，超过99%的内幕交易其实是完全合法的。对于财经记者而言，内幕交易记录是了解公司高管、董事会成员或投资者对该公司看法的绝佳途径。

<!--en-->
What people do not realize is that more than 99 percent of all insider trading is perfectly legal. And insider trading records are an excellent way for a business reporter to assess what a company executive, board member, or investor thinks about a company.

根据美国证券交易委员会制定的投资监管规则，内幕人士被定义为上市公司的官员或董事，或是持有该公司任何类别股份10%及以上的个人或实体。在玛莎·斯图尔特的案件中，她之所以被视为内幕人士，是因为据称她从另一名内幕人士瓦克斯尔处获得了信息，并据此采取了行动。

<!--en-->
According to the rules used by the SEC to govern investing, an insider is defined as an officer or director of a public company or an individual or entity owning 10 percent or more of any class of a company's shares. In Martha Stewart's case, she would be considered an insider because she allegedly received information from an insider—Waksal—and acted upon that information.

这些高管、董事会成员及机构投资者只要在交易后向美国证券交易委员会提交4号表格，就可以买卖这些公司的股票。如果内幕人士在公开市场上买卖股票，必须在交易发生后的当月第十天之前向美国证券交易委员会提交报告。只有当高管、董事或外部投资者利用可能被视为重大信息的非公开信息来买卖公司股票时，内幕交易才会变成违法行为——通常这类信息会导致公司需要按照第6章的要求提交8-K表格。

<!--en-->
Those executives, board members, and institutional investors are allowed to buy and sell stock in these companies as long as they file a Form 4 with the SEC following the transaction. If an insider buys or sells stock in the open market, he or she must file with the SEC by the tenth day of the month following such a trade. Insider trading becomes illegal when the executive, director, or outside investor buys or sells stock in the company on the basis of nonpublic information that is, or could be, considered material in nature—generally anything that would require the company to file a Form 8-K, covered in Chapter 6.

例如，如果HSB集团公司在1999年春季告知某位投资者，该公司将被美国国际集团以每股60美元的价格收购，而该投资者出于从中获利的意图购买了股票，那么联邦执法部门就会立即对其采取行动。

<!--en-->
For example, if an executive at HSB Group Incorporated told an investor in the spring of 1999 that the company would be acquired by American International Group Incorporated for $60 a share and the investor bought the stock with the intention of profiting from this information, the feds would be coming after him or her with handcuffs.

以下就是大多数普通财经杂志读者所认为属于内幕交易的报道类型：

<!--en-->
The following is the type of story that most casual business section readers equate with insider trading:

圣路易斯的投资者约翰·D·韦尔同意支付93,424美元，以了结美国证券交易委员会提起的内幕交易诉讼。

<!--en-->
Investor John D. Weil of St. Louis has agreed to pay $93,424 to settle an insider trading suit brought by the Securities and Exchange Commission.

### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

道琼斯新闻专线副主编迈克尔·里德谈如何报道高管薪酬问题：

<!--en-->
Dow Jones Newswires deputy managing editor Michael Reid on covering executive compensation:

**控制权变更条款**：需特别留意这些条款。许多关于公司战略方向以及董事会真实想法的精彩报道，都可能隐藏在控制权变更条款之中。这类条款规定，如果公司被其他公司合并或收购，首席执行官和高管们就能获得相应报酬。在并购活动频繁的行业里，实力较弱的公司可能会设有丰厚的控制权变更条款。同样，被聘请来改善公司状况并推动其出售的首席执行官，也很可能会要求为此获得补偿。有时候，在漫长的并购谈判过程中，如果管理层和董事会调整控制权变更条款，那就意味着交易即将达成。更有趣的情况是，有些控制权变更条款设置得极为宽松，以至于高管们在并未真正失去控制权时也能获得报酬。此外，即便看似已经发生收购，相关条款仍未触发，也可能会让高管们感到不满，从而愿意开口谈论情况。224 • 高管办公室 美国证券交易委员会指控韦尔利用纽约的一家保险经纪公司Kaye Group Inc.可能被收购的内幕消息非法获利。

<!--en-->
**Change-of-control clauses:** Watch out for these. Many great stories about a company's strategic direction and what a board's really thinking may be revealed in change-of-control clauses. This is the payments which are triggered to a CEO and executives in the event the company is merged with, or taken over by, another company. A weak company in an M&A-frenzied industry may have lucrative change-of-control clauses. Likewise, a CEO brought in to polish up and sell the company would likely demand compensation for doing just that. Sometimes, in a prolonged merger battle, if management and a board tweak its change-of-control clauses it's a sure sign a deal's in the offing. Even better are stories where change-of-control clauses are so lukewarm that executives have payouts triggered when they don't actually lose control. Likewise, plans which aren't triggered despite an apparent takeover can make executives angry and willing to talk.
224 • The Corner Office
The SEC alleged that Weil had profited illegally from a tip that Kaye Group Inc., an insurance brokerage based in New York, might be acquired.

韦尔既未承认也未否认这些指控，但同意放弃46,712美元的利润，并缴纳同等数额的民事罚款。目前无法联系到韦尔以获取其意见。

<!--en-->
Without admitting or denying the allegations, Weil agreed to give up $46,712 in profits and pay a civil fine of an equal amount. Weil could not be reached for comment.

美国证券交易委员会费城分部助理局长大卫·霍洛维茨表示，纳斯达克股市在日常监控过程中发现了Kaye股票的交易异常情况，随后便通知了美国证券交易委员会。

<!--en-->
David Horowitz, assistant district administrator for the SEC in Philadelphia, said the NASDAQ Stock Market became aware of suspicious trading in Kaye's stock as part of its normal surveillance process. The NASDAQ then alerted the SEC, he said.

根据美国证券交易委员会的说法，韦尔在2000年11月底或12月初得知另一家公司有意收购Kaye集团，这一消息来自Kaye集团的董事内德·L·谢尔伍德。

<!--en-->
According to the SEC, Weil learned in late November or early December of 2000 that another company was interested in buying Kaye Group. The information came from Ned L. Sherwood, a director of Kaye Group.

美国证券交易委员会称，持有Kaye集团10%股份的韦尔经常与谢尔伍德讨论该公司的相关情况，并向谢尔伍德保证这些对话是保密的。

<!--en-->
The SEC says that Weil, who owned 10 percent of Kaye Group's stock, talked regularly with Sherwood about the company, and had assured Sherwood that the conversations were confidential.

韦尔利用其未来妻子的经纪账户，在2000年12月28日至2001年1月17日期间以每股7.44美元至7.94美元不等的价格购买了7,400股凯伊集团股票。

<!--en-->
Using brokerage accounts in his future wife's name, Weil bought 7,400 shares of Kaye Group between Dec. 28, 2000, and Jan. 17, 2001, at prices ranging from $7.44 to $7.94 a share.

2001年1月20日，凯伊集团宣布已接受另一家保险经纪公司Hub International Ltd.提出的每股14美元的收购要约。美国证券交易委员会还指控来自佛罗里达州奥兰多的兰德·E·夏皮罗通过凯伊集团股票获得了35,804美元的非法利润。美国证券交易委员会称，夏皮罗获取内幕信息的方式是另一位董事霍华德·A·凯伊。与韦尔一样，夏皮罗也同意认罪、退还非法所得并缴纳罚款。

<!--en-->
Kaye Group announced on Jan. 20, 2001, that it had accepted a $14-a-share buyout offer from Hub International Ltd., another insurance brokerage. The SEC also accused Rand E. Shapiro of Orlando, Fla., of making $35,804 in illegal profits on Kaye Group's stock. Shapiro's inside information came from another director, Howard A. Kaye, the SEC said. Like Weil, Shapiro agreed to settle the charges, return his profits and pay a fine.

霍洛维茨表示，凯伊集团的董事们并未被指控有不当行为，因为他们认为自己的对话属于保密内容，且没料到会有人利用这些信息进行交易。

<!--en-->
The Kaye Group directors weren't accused of wrongdoing because they thought their conversations were confidential, and they didn't expect anyone to trade on the information, Horowitz said.

美国证券交易委员会的指控被纳入了周二在奥兰多联邦法院提起的民事诉讼中。² 在报道商业新闻时，这类故事具有很高的价值且非常重要。不过，这类故事的事实并非来自美国证券交易委员会的公开文件，而是来自该机构的投诉书，这类投诉书通常可以在其网站上的www.sec.gov.处找到（有关从网站上获取信息的更多信息，请参阅第16章）。

<!--en-->
The SEC's allegations were included in a civil lawsuit filed Tuesday in federal court in Orlando.²
These stories are valuable and important to write when covering business news. But the facts for such stories do not come from SEC filings. Instead, they come from an SEC complaint, which is often available on the agency's website at www.sec.gov. (For more information about obtaining information from websites, see Chapter 16.)

同样，公司高管、董事会成员或其他投资者进行的几乎所有股票交易都是完全合法的，通常并不值得报道。但如果某位董事会成员或高管出售其持有的大部分公司股份，或大量购入公司股票，那就成了值得报道的新闻。

<!--en-->
Again, virtually all stock trades done by company executives, board members, or other investors are perfectly legitimate and typically are not worth writing about. But it is a story if a board member or company executive is selling the majority of his or her stock holdings in the company or buying a large chunk of stock.

高管或董事会成员出售股票是有合理理由的。可能是到了支付大专学费的时候，或者他正在购买度假屋。也可能是时候对投资组合进行多元化配置，避免将过多净资产集中在某一只股票上。这些都是内幕人士出售股票的正当理由。但商业记者应留意内幕交易行为。一旦发生此类情况，记者应致电该公司了解原因。如果高管能给出合理的出售理由，那就不太可能成为新闻；但如果没有合理理由，或许意味着他认为股价短期内不会上涨。高管比任何人都更了解公司的未来前景。此外，记者还应留意高管大量购入公司股票的情况，这可能表明这些高管对公司未来前景持乐观态度，认为股价很快就会上升。那么，记者从哪里可以获取这些信息呢？还是美国证券交易委员会能提供帮助。

<!--en-->
There are legitimate reasons for an executive or board member to sell stock. It might be time to pay for junior's college tuition. Or maybe he is buying a vacation home. It might even be time to diversify the investment portfolio and not hold
**Tips from the Pros**

*道琼斯新闻专线副主编迈克尔·里德谈如何报道高管薪酬问题：*

<!--en-->
*Dow Jones Newswires deputy managing editor Michael Reid on covering executive compensation:*

**入职奖金与“金色降落伞”：**问问大多数人，他们都会认为入职奖金或“金色降落伞”（一种离职补偿方案，绝非那种普通的“请离开”的握手礼）简直荒谬至极。在报道这类话题时，还需考虑行业特性。公平地说，入职奖金既不是礼物也不是奖励，而是对高管放弃其在原职位所应获得的报酬的一种补偿。许多公司只允许员工在职期间才能获得股票期权和其他股票授予。一旦离职，未来的福利就随之丧失，连工牌和订书机也一并没了！同样，“金色降落伞”也是高管面临无法长期任职风险的一种补偿措施。虽然听起来很诱人，但由于股东的压力和季度财报的要求，高管的平均任期往往只能以棒球赛季来计算，而非总统任期——也就是说非常短暂！[^2481]：² 来自D.尼克劳斯2002年12月14日发表在《圣路易斯邮报》上的文章《圣路易斯投资者约翰·D·韦尔就SEC内幕交易案达成和解》，第2页。版权归《圣路易斯邮报》所有，经许可转载。《The Corner Office》•225

<!--en-->
**Sign-ons and golden parachutes:** Ask most people and they'll tell you the mere notion of a sign-on bonus or a golden parachute (a severance package but not your average "please leave" handshake) are obscene. Again, consider the industry when reporting on these. Sign-ons, to be fair, are neither a gift nor a bonus. They are payments for surrendering what remuneration an executive was promised at the job he's leaving. Many companies only allow stock options and other stock grants to vest if you are still an employee. Leave, and you leave your future benefits at the door, thanks, along with your name-tag and stapler! Likewise, golden parachutes are a product of the risk an executive takes of not being in the job long. Sounds-cushy, but the demands of shareholders and quarterly earnings reports mean the average tenure of an executive can be measured in baseball seasons, not presidential terms—i.e., short!
[^2481]: ² From "St. Louis investor John D. Weil settles SEC insider trading suit," by D. Nicklaus, December 14, 2002, *St. Louis Post Dispatch*, p. 2. Copyright 2002 by *St. Louis Post Dispatch*. Reprinted with permission.
The Corner Office • 225
too much of his net worth in one stock. These are all valid reasons for an insider to sell stock. But business reporters should watch for insider selling. When it happens, a reporter should call the company to find out why. If the executive can give a good reason for selling, then it is not likely a story. But if there is no good reason, it might mean that he does not think the price is going to get higher anytime soon. Executives know more about the future prospects of a company than anyone else. Also, reporters should watch for executives buying large amounts of company stock. That could be an indication that these executives think good things about the company's future prospects and believe the stock price is going higher sooner rather than later. Now, where can a reporter find this information? Again, the SEC comes to the rescue.

需要指出的是，商业记者可能会受到诱惑，根据所获信息去购买股票。这种行为必须避免，因为这很可能会导致记者被解雇。没有任何媒体机构允许其记者主动买卖所报道公司的股票。

<!--en-->
It should be noted that business reporters might be tempted to act on information they find and buy stock. This must be avoided, because it will likely result in the reporter being fired from his job. No media outlet allows its reporters to actively buy and sell stocks of companies they are reporting on.

美国证券交易委员会要求高管、董事会成员及其他投资者以多种形式披露其交易情况。Form 4是一种两页长的文件，由持有公司10%以上股份的董事、高管或股东提交。该报告包含有关计划购买和出售特定股权证券的信息，以及报告人与公司之间的关系。此外，该表格还会说明是买入还是卖出股票、买卖的股数以及价格，同时还会注明此人目前还持有多少股股票。

<!--en-->
The SEC requires executives, board members, and other investors to disclose their transactions in a variety of forms. The Form 4 is a two-page document filed by directors, officers, or owners of more than 10 percent of the stock in a company. The report contains information on planned purchases and sales of certain equity securities. The form also contains information on the reporting person's relationship to the company. In addition, the form will disclose whether shares were bought or sold, how many shares were bought or sold, and the price. The form will also state how many shares the person still owns.

阅读这些表格很有价值，因为其中通常会包含提交人的街道地址。如果记者难以找到公司董事会成员，这些表格能提供帮助。不过有时，高管或董事会成员在提交4表时仅使用公司的邮寄地址。对于记者而言，追踪这类交易还有一个问题：内幕人士必须在交易发生后的下个月第十天之前提交4表，而到那时，导致买卖的种种条件可能已经发生变化。

<!--en-->
Reading these forms can be valuable because they also typically contain street addresses for the filer. If a reporter is having trouble tracking down a company board member, this form can help. Sometimes, however, executives or board members simply use the company's mailing address when they file Form 4s. Another problem for reporters in tracking these trades is that insiders have until the tenth day of the month following their trades to file their Form 4. By that time, the conditions causing the buying or selling may have changed.

每当记者撰写有关公司战略或首席执行官的文章时，核查内幕交易情况都是明智之举。如果首席执行官大肆吹嘘某款新产品或公司即将带来的更好业绩，他们就应该愿意用实际行动来证明自己的说法。如果首席执行官并未基于这些前景购买自家公司的股票，记者就应该追问原因。

<!--en-->
Anytime a reporter is writing a story about a company's strategy or the CEO, it is wise to check insider trading. If CEOs gush about a new product or a change in a company that is expected to produce better results, they should be willing to put their money where their mouth is. If a CEO is not buying his or her own company's stock on the basis of those prospects, a reporter should ask why.

从更广泛的角度来看，监控内幕交易也很有帮助。追踪内幕交易的华尔街专家希望了解买入量是否多于卖出量。如果是这样，这可能预示着整体股市有望上涨。

<!--en-->
Watching insider trading is also helpful in a broader sense. Wall Street experts who track insider trading want to know if more buying than selling is occurring. If that is the case, it may be an indication that the broader stock market could be headed higher.

以下是记录投资者内幕交易行为的一篇报道的部分内容：

<!--en-->
The following is part of a story that documents insider trading by investors:

根据美国证券交易委员会的文件显示，近几个月来有多家机构投资者增持了Trenwick的股票。在第三季度，总部位于纽约的Jennison Associates LLC购买了超过100万股股票；另一家纽约的资产管理公司Trainer Wortham & Co.则购买了超过686,000股股票。在同一时期，总部位于孟菲斯的New South Capital Management Inc.进一步增持了股票，成为Trenwick最大的机构投资者，又额外购买了**专业人士的建议**

<!--en-->
A number of institutional investors have been adding to their positions in Trenwick in recent months, according to SEC filings. During the third quarter, New York-based Jennison Associates LLC purchased more than 1 million shares. Trainer Wortham & Co., another New York-based money manager, purchased more than 686,000 shares. Over the same period, Memphis-based New South Capital Management Inc. added to its position as Trenwick's largest institutional investor, purchasing an additional
**Tips from the Pros**

*道琼斯新闻专线副主编迈克尔·里德谈报道高管薪酬的话题：*

<!--en-->
*Dow Jones Newswires deputy managing editor Michael Reid on covering executive compensation:*

**职位最高并不代表薪酬最高：**2009年，由于美国财政部不得不接连救助多家银行，限制高管薪酬成为一个重大议题。结果就是出现了要求限制高管薪酬的民粹主义呼声，政府官员也承诺削减银行高层员工的薪酬。但有一个问题：一家公司，尤其是金融机构中职位最高的100名管理人员，往往并非薪酬最高的100人。这是一个依赖人才的行业。与棒球、橄榄球、电视业以及许多其他行业一样，这里的“明星”们的年度薪酬往往远高于管理层，甚至高于首席执行官。这是报道薪酬时的一个关键点。过去几年，高盛的一位明星银行家的薪酬曾是首席执行官的两倍。226 • 高管办公室

<!--en-->
**Most senior doesn't mean most highly paid:** Curbs on executive pay became a huge issue in 2009 after the U.S. Treasury had to bail out bank after bank. The upshot was the populist demand for a curb on executive pay, and therein followed promises by government officials to cut the pay of a bank's most senior staff. One problem though: the most senior 100 managers at a company, and particularly at financial institutions, are often not the 100 most highly paid. It's a talent-driven industry. Like baseball, football, television and many other industries, the "stars" can earn much more in annual compensation than management, even the CEO. This is a key point when reporting on compensation. In past years, a star banker at Goldman Sachs has earned twice that of the CEO.
226 • The Corner Office

### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

道琼斯新闻专线副主编迈克尔·里德谈报道高管薪酬的话题：

<!--en-->
Dow Jones Newswires deputy managing editor Michael Reid on covering executive compensation:

**选对时机，选对背景：**在准确、公正地报道高管薪酬时，需考虑整个行业状况、竞争对手以及规模大小不同的同行。同时还要思考，一家公司的良好表现究竟是因为个别首席执行官的功劳，还是仅仅因为整个行业正处于繁荣期。以20世纪90年代末英国制药公司史克利恩·比彻姆的首席执行官简·莱施利为例，当时该公司实现了强劲的增长，利润上升，股价也随之上涨。他还因拥有英国最高的薪酬包之一而闻名，据不同人士的说法，其薪酬总额约为9000万英镑（公平地说，其中大部分是股票和期权）。然而当该公司与葛兰素史克合并后，新任首席执行官让-皮埃尔·加尼耶却因高额的“金色降落伞”计划而遭到严厉批评，并引发了股东抗议。为什么？部分原因是加尼耶接手的是一家处于行业困境中的公司——研发成本上升、监管更加严格、还有仿制药品的竞争——而这些都不是他的过错。在当时的环境下，几乎所有制药公司都在快速发展，莱施利正是身处正确的时间、正确的位置，领导了史克利恩的崛起。简而言之，尽管加尼耶被广泛认为是制药行业中最有才华的高管之一，但莱施利与加尼耶的业绩（以及相应的薪酬）却引发了截然不同的反应。

<!--en-->
**Right time, right place:** When writing accurately and fairly about executive compensation, consider the wider industry, rivals, and both larger and smaller peers. And also consider whether a company's strong performance is down to the individual CEO, or simply the result of an industry going through a boom. Take the example of Jan Leschly, CEO of British drug maker SmithKline Beecham in the late 1990s during which the company produced solid growth, profit and a rising stock price to match. He was also famous for having one of the biggest compensation packages in the UK, valued (depending on who you talked to) at around 90 million pounds sterling (to be fair that was mostly stock and options). Yet when the company was merged with Glaxo Wellcome, it was the new CEO Jean-Pierre Garnier who drew huge criticism, and a shareholder revolt, for a generous "golden parachute." Why? Partly because Garnier inherited a company at a tough point in the industry—higher R&D costs, tougher regulation, generic competition—that was none of his fault. Leschly oversaw SmithKline's rise during a period when almost all drugmakers grew fast given the circumstances. In short, Leschly was in the right place at the right time. His and Garnier's performance (and therefore compensation) drew drastically different responses despite the fact that Garnier was widely considered to be one of the most talented executives in the pharmaceutical industry.

457,915股。作为该公司的长期投资者，New South目前持有超过350万股股票。

<!--en-->
457,915 shares. New South, a long-term investor in the company, now owns more than 3.5 million shares.

最近，Lord Abbett & Co.在第四季度购买了超过240,000股股票，使其在Trenwick的总持股量超过100万股。德克萨斯州教师退休系统购买了97,000股，使其总持股量达到240,000股。Palisade Capital则又增加了43,400股股票。

<!--en-->
More recently, Lord Abbett & Co. purchased more than 240,000 shares in the fourth quarter, bringing its total holdings in Trenwick to more than 1 million shares. The Teacher Retirement System of Texas bought 97,000, bringing its total position to 240,000 shares. And Palisade Capital added 43,400 shares to its position.

根据这些公司最新的美国证券交易委员会备案文件，特伦威克公司前10大机构股东中仅有两家在过去六个月内减持了持股。第三季度，Reich & Tang公司卖出了51,525股股票，占其总持股量的不到4.0%。总部位于纽约的Royce & Associates Inc.在第四季度减持了289,600股特伦威克公司的股票，但其仍持有超过905,000股股票。

<!--en-->
According to the most recent SEC filings for the firms, only two of Trenwick's top 10 institutional shareholders have lowered their holdings in the past six months. In the third quarter, Reich & Tang sold 51,525 shares, less than 4.0% of its total holdings. New York-based Royce & Associates Inc. trimmed 289,600 shares from its Trenwick holdings in the fourth quarter, but the firm still owns more than 905,000 shares.

然而，尽管特伦威克公司的市值已接近10亿美元，华尔街的卖方分析师群体对其兴趣依然寥寥。目前跟踪该公司的五位分析师中有三位给予“持有”评级。³这类内幕交易行为正是商业新闻读者想了解却往往没时间自行查询的内容。如果记者能在报道中提供更多此类信息，就能更好地服务于读者。此外，这也能向公司高管表明他们明白衡量公司表现的最重要标准——即投资者是否愿意购买其股票。这些备案文件数量的增减可以反映出华尔街专业人士对某只股票的看法。

<!--en-->
Yet as Trenwick's market capitalization nears $1.0 billion, the company still attracts little interest from the sell-side analyst community on Wall Street. Three of the five analysts who follow Trenwick currently give it a "hold" rating.³
This is the kind of insider trading activity that readers of business stories want to know about but quite often do not have the time to look up themselves. If reporters can provide more such information in their stories, they will better serve their readers. In addition, they will show company executives that they know the most meaningful measure of performance—whether investors are willing to buy stock. An increase or decrease in these filings can be an indicator of what Wall Street pros think about a certain stock.

还有几份关于股票交易的重要的备案文件值得注意，尽管它们并不直接涉及公司高管或董事会成员。与该公司无关的投资者在买卖公司股票时也必须向美国证券交易委员会提交相关文件。

<!--en-->
There are several other important filings about stock trades worth noting, although they do not directly involve company executives or board members. Investors who are not connected to a company are also required to file documents with the SEC when they purchase and sell company stock.

当某位股东或一组股东持有某家公司5%以上的股票时，就需要提交13D表。这些文件必须在投资后的10天内提交。此外，提交13D表的人通常希望对公司进行某些改变，这类人往往是不满的股东。由于投资者在持有某公司5%的股票时就必须提交13D表，他们很多时候会先购买4.9%的股份，这样其他投资者就不会知道他们对这家公司的兴趣，从而避免股价上涨。

<!--en-->
A Schedule 13D is filed when a shareholder or a group of shareholders acquires more than 5 percent of a company's stock. These filings must be made within the first 10 days of the investment. In addition, someone filing a 13D typically wants to effect a change at the company. These are most often disgruntled shareholders. Because investors have to file a 13D when they acquire 5 percent of a company's stock, many times they will purchase shares up to 4.9 percent so that other investors do not know of their interest in the company, which might drive the price up.

对于商业记者来说，还有另一种重要的表格。当机构投资者和专业投资者出于业务需求而非意图改变公司控制权而购买股票时，美国证券交易委员会会对此进行记录。此时，机构投资者需要提交13G表。13G表也必须在交易发生所在季度结束后的10天内提交。[^2504]：³摘自C. Roush于2001年3月发表在《保险投资者》杂志第1页的文章《特伦威克集团的快速增长：这家再保险公司通过收购拓展新业务并寻求更多交易。首席执行官吉姆·比莱特能否让股价持续上涨？》，版权所有2001年SNL Financial，经许可转载。The Corner Office • 227。虽然13G表的提交速度不如某些其他文件快，但它仍然能提供有价值的信息。

<!--en-->
There is another form that is also important for business reporters. The SEC notes when institutional investors and professional investors acquire stock in the course of their business and not with the idea of changing the control of the company. When this happens, an institutional investor files a Schedule 13G. A Schedule 13G must also be filed within 10 days of the end of the quarter when the transaction occurred.
[^2504]: ³ From "Trenwick Group's growth spurt: The reinsurer has added new businesses through acquisition and is seeking more deals. Can CEO Jim Billett keep the stock price rising?" by C. Roush, March 2001, *Insurance Investor*, p. 1. Copyright 2001 by SNL Financial. Reprinted with permission.
The Corner Office • 227
Even though they are not filed as quickly as some other documents, a 13G can still provide good information.

这些文件到底有多有价值呢？13G表和13D表通常会包含投资者所在公司的名称、购买的股票数量、购买日期和价格，而且往往还会列出负责该项具体投资的机构投资者的姓名及电话号码。

<!--en-->
How much of a treasure trove are these files? Schedule 13Gs and Schedule 13Ds typically include the name of the investor's company, how many shares were purchased, purchase dates and prices, and, quite often, the name and the phone number of someone at that institutional investor who is in charge of the specific investment.

例如，下面这段摘自13G表的文字。一位记者在为一篇关于总部位于密歇根州的American Physicians Capital Incorporated公司的文章做调研时发现了这份备案文件。记者只需查到Greenlight Capital的电话号码，接电话的就是大卫·艾恩霍恩，他非常乐意交谈，尽管他从未听说过该记者所撰写的刊物。

<!--en-->
For example, consider the excerpt from the Schedule 13G below. A reporter found this filing while doing research for an article about American Physicians Capital Incorporated, a Michigan-based company. All the reporter had to do was look up the phone number for Greenlight Capital and had David Einhorn on the other end, more than happy to talk, even though he had never heard of or seen the publication for which the reporter was writing.

**Item 2(e) CUSIP Number.**
**Item 3 Reporting Person.** Inapplicable.

**第4项：股权归属。** (a) Greenlight以及Einhorn先生和Keswin先生是990,000股普通股的实益拥有者。 (b) Greenlight以及Einhorn先生和Keswin先生持有该公司已发行普通股总数的9.9%的实益权益。该比例是基于发行人初始公开募股（即“IPO”）时所发行的10,000,000股股份计算得出的。Keswin先生被告知，由于IPO的承销商选择额外认购部分股份，截至2000年12月14日，已发行股份数量已增至11,450,254股。按照这一调整后的已发行股份数计算，Greenlight以及Einhorn先生和Keswin先生的持股比例应为8.6%。 (c) Greenlight拥有对其实益拥有的990,000股普通股进行投票和处置的唯一权力。作为Greenlight的负责人，Einhorn先生和Keswin先生可以指导Greenlight对这990,000股普通股的投票及处置事宜。

<!--en-->
**Item 4 Ownership.** (a) Greenlight and Messrs. Einhorn and Keswin are the beneficial owners of 990,000 shares of Common Stock.
(b) Greenlight and Messrs. Einhorn and Keswin are the beneficial owners of 9.9 percent of the outstanding shares of Common Stock. This percentage is based upon the outstanding shares of the Issuer equaling 10,000,000 shares, the amount of shares initially offered in connection with the Issuers initial public offering (the "IPO"). Mr. Keswin has been informed that underwriters of the IPO have elected to subscribe for an additional amount of shares causing the outstanding shares to equal 11,450,254 as of December 14, 2000. Based on this revised number of outstanding shares, Greenlight's and Messrs. Einhorn's and Keswin's percentage ownership would be equal to 8.6 percent.
(c) Greenlight has the sole power to vote and dispose of the 990,000 shares of Common Stock beneficially owned by it. As the principals of Greenlight, Messrs. Einhorn and Keswin may direct the vote and disposition of the 990,000 shares of Common Stock beneficially owned by Greenlight.

(Greenlight Capital L.L.C., 2000年13G表)

<!--en-->
(Greenlight Capital L.L.C., Schedule 13G, 2000)

228 • The Corner Office 这篇报道探讨了American Physicians Capital提升业绩的策略。而相比公司的大量股东，最能对这一策略作出准确评价的，恐怕非该公司首席执行官本人莫属。记者通过这份文件中的有用信息找到了Einhorn——包括他的公司名称Greenlight Capital、公司的邮寄地址以及Einhorn本人的姓名。记者还通过快速拨打电话查询服务获取了该公司的电话号码。

<!--en-->
228 • The Corner Office
The story was a look at American Physicians Capital’s strategy for improving its performance. And, likely, the only person better to quote assessing that strategy than an investor who has purchased a large amount of stock in the company is the CEO himself. The valuable information in this filing that allowed the reporter to find Einhorn was the name of his company, Greenlight Capital, its mailing address, and Einhorn’s name. The reporter obtained the firm’s phone number with a quick call to directory assistance.

撰写关于公司高管、董事会成员及投资者的文章，需要详细呈现商业报道中最引人入胜的人际关系之一。这些人都是普通人，都会受到某些因素的驱使。首席执行官或许会被对权力的渴望，或是为员工创造良好工作环境、为投资者带来丰厚回报的愿望所驱动。董事会成员往往也受这些因素影响。而投资者则只有一个目标——赚钱。这三方之间的互动往往能催生出精彩的故事。

<!--en-->
Writing about company executives, boards, and investors involves detailing one of the most fascinating relationships in business reporting. These people are all human, and they are all driven by certain factors. The CEO may be driven by the need to have power or by the desire to provide a good working environment for his employees and a favorable return for his investors. Board members are often driven by the same factors. Investors are driven by one factor—to make money. How the three interact often results in compelling stories.

## 建议练习

<!--en-->
*Suggested Exercises*

1. 查看两家不同公司的组织结构图。撰写一篇500字的分析，说明为何这两家公司的组织结构存在差异，重点探讨职位名称及上下级汇报关系，尤其要关注CEO、总裁与执行副总裁或部门总裁之间的关系。
2. 查阅一家上市公司的高管薪酬情况。将该公司CEO和总裁的奖金及薪资涨幅与同一财年的净收入及股价涨幅进行比较。探讨为何薪酬与公司业绩之间可能存在差距。
3. 研究一家公司的董事会。列出那些可能与该公司有财务关联的董事以及没有关联的董事。讨论这些财务联系是否可能影响董事的决策。
4. 查看一家公司的前十大股东名单。用30分钟时间判断哪些是外部投资者，哪些是董事会成员，哪些是现任或前任高管。比较董事会成员与外部股东持有的股票数量，并讨论是否有大型外部股东应获得董事会席位。
5. 查看某家公司的高管及董事会成员在过去12个月内的内幕买卖情况。将整个群体的卖出股数与买入股数相加。该公司过去一年的内幕交易能否反映其未来的表现？![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/28ea43c75649b559f3d457664e5f2bf5.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T071651Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=dad81d05341e7c3dc2ac5ee5c8d19c2cba01bb2024fde22f0455cd314ab6dee1)

<!--en-->
1. Review the organizational charts of two different companies. Write a 500-word analysis of why the organizational structures differ, focusing on job titles and who reports to whom, with emphasis on the relationship between the CEO, president, and executive vice presidents or division presidents.
2. Review the executive compensation for a public company. Compare the bonus and salary increase for the CEO and president of the company to the increase in net income and stock price for the same fiscal year. Discuss why there may be a discrepancy between the compensation and the company's performance.
3. Examine a company's board of directors. List the directors who may be considered to have financial ties to the company and those who don't. Discuss whether the financial connections might have a bearing on the decisions made by the board member.
4. Review a list of the top shareholders for a company. Take 30 minutes to determine which shareholders are outside investors, which ones are board members, and which ones are current or former executives. Compare the amount of stock held by board members to the amount of stock held by outside shareholders. Discuss whether a large outside shareholder deserves a seat on the board.
5. Examine the insider buying and selling by a single company's executives and board members for the past 12 months. Total the number of shares sold by the entire group to the number of shares purchased. Is the insider trading for the company in the past year a reflection of the company's future performance?
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/28ea43c75649b559f3d457664e5f2bf5.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T071651Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=dad81d05341e7c3dc2ac5ee5c8d19c2cba01bb2024fde22f0455cd314ab6dee1)

### 11

规模虽小，新闻价值却大

<!--en-->
Small in Size, Large for News

#### 地方经济的重要组成部分

<!--en-->
*A Vital Part of Local Economies*

私营企业和小企业是国家经济的支柱。没有它们，许多城镇和社区将无法存在。它们为数百万人提供稳定的就业机会，还能在大型企业陷入困境或倒闭时助力经济增长或保持稳定。

<!--en-->
Private and small businesses are the backbone of the nation's economy. Without them, many towns and communities would not exist. They provide stable jobs for millions and help the economy grow—or remain stable when larger companies struggle or go out of business.

然而，阅读国内报纸、网站和杂志，收听广播或观看电视新闻，会发现大部分商业报道都忽视了小型企业和私营企业。部分原因在于许多记者认为这类企业规模太小，不值得报道，或者不够有趣。

<!--en-->
Yet read the nation's newspapers, Internet sites, and magazines; listen to its radio; or watch its television news, and the bulk of the business coverage ignores small and private businesses. Part of the reason is that many reporters believe that these companies are too small to be making news or that they are not interesting enough.

乍看之下，这些记者的观点或许正确。那些产品和服务被全国乃至全球数百万人使用的大型企业，对更多人的影响更大。而小型企业并不销售能产生巨大影响的产品。

<!--en-->
At first glance, these reporters may be correct. Big companies whose products and services are used by millions around the country—and the world—have a bigger impact on more people. Small businesses do not sell products that have a huge impact.

但如果一家小型企业开发出能影响大量人群的产品，它就会成为那样的大型企业。比尔·盖茨是在车库里创立了自己的公司，如今微软已成为全球最大的企业之一，主导着计算机软件行业。沃尔玛最初只有一家门店，可口可乐最初是在一家药店售卖饮料，福特最初也是销售第一辆汽车。这些公司并非一开始就是拥有数万员工的数十亿美元企业，而是怀揣成为更伟大企业的梦想从微小的业务起步的。

<!--en-->
But if a small business develops a product that is going to have an impact on a large part of the population, it will become one of those big companies. Bill Gates started his company in his garage, and now Microsoft is one of the biggest companies in the world, dominating the computer software industry. Wal-Mart started with one store. Coca-Cola started by selling its soft drinks at one drug store. Ford started by selling its first car. These companies were not created as multibillion-dollar operations with tens of thousands of workers. They began as tiny operations with dreams of becoming something bigger.

反对媒体报道小型及私营企业的另一个理由是，很难找到关于它们的客观信息。例如，几乎没有任何私营企业，也只有少数小型企业需要向美国证券交易委员会提交能够显示其收入和利润的财务信息。当一家小型企业的首席执行官声称其公司去年的收入增长了50%时，除非该高管向记者出示账本，否则记者似乎无从验证这一信息。不过，还是有许多方法可以找到相关资料。232 • 规模虽小，新闻价值却高

<!--en-->
The other argument against covering small and private businesses in the media is that it is tough to find objective information about them. Virtually no private and few small companies are required to file financial information with the SEC, for example, that would reveal their revenues and profits. When the CEO of a small company says that his or her company's revenues grew by 50 percent in the past year, it would seem that a reporter has no way of verifying that information unless the executive shows him the books. But, there are plenty of ways to find
232 • Small in Size, Large for News

#### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

私营企业的公开记录：需关注哪些内容：

<!--en-->
Public records for private companies: What to look for:

1. **地方政府：**房地产交易记录；地契登记处记录、卫生部门记录、规划部门记录、财产评估师或税务评估员的相关记录；民事与刑事诉讼记录。
2. **州政府：**州务卿办公室的注册记录；《统一商法典》相关备案文件、经济发展相关记录；州立法机构；专业执照管理委员会；负责保险和银行业监管的州级机构。
3. **联邦政府**：消费者产品安全委员会、环境保护局、平等就业机会委员会以及负责工作场所相关记录的职业安全与健康管理局；联邦贸易委员会、专利商标局；以及负责能源、航空等特定行业的联邦机构。此外还有全国范围内小型企业及私营企业的财务信息。正如本章将展示的那样，只需稍加思考与研究即可找到相关线索。没有哪家企业是完全隐秘的，也没有任何一家企业，无论规模多小，能完全不留痕迹。相关报告其实是可以完成的，只是很多人不知道如何操作。还有一个更为重要的原因，解释了为什么大众媒体应当更加关注小型企业及影响其运营的各种问题。如前所述，小型企业对经济至关重要，当经济遭遇困境时，小型企业也会和其他企业一样受到影响。2008年上半年流失的763,000个就业岗位中，超过一半来自小型企业；未注册的个体经营者数量从2007年的平均1040万降至2008年的平均1010万，到2008年11月和12月则进一步降至960万。自20世纪90年代中期以来，小型企业通常每年创造60%至80%的净新增就业岗位，但在2008年却出现了310万个岗位的净损失。虽然目前还无法确定小型企业失去了多少就业岗位，但这一数字很可能相当可观。一些媒体——尤其是那些位于大都市地区的媒体——几乎忽视了那些雇佣了全国半数以上劳动力、创造了私营部门半数以上产值的企业。当然，也有一些报纸和其他媒体设有专门报道小型企业问题的记者。比如北卡罗来纳州西部的《斯塔茨维尔记录与地标报》，在这样一个几乎所有新闻都与小型企业相关的社区里，也有专门的商业记者。但总体而言，与对上市公司和知名私营企业的报道相比，商业新闻领域往往忽视了许多小型企业。尽管根据华盛顿美国企业研究所的一项调查，美国人对小型企业的评价高于对知名企业和工会的评价。该调查显示，90%的美国人对小型企业持积极态度，这一比例在过去25年间一直保持在84%至94%之间。相比之下，最新的哈里斯民意调查显示，66%的人对工会有较高的信任度，而对大型公司的信任度为72%。一个多世纪以来，小型企业一直受到这个国家的推崇。19世纪，国会首次通过反垄断法，就是为了保护小型企业。1953年，美国小型企业管理局成立，旨在为小型企业提供援助。由于利益一致，小型企业已逐渐成为州立法机构和国会中强大的游说力量。全美独立企业联合会拥有60多万名会员，在50个州都设有办事处，其游说人员会与州级及联邦政府机构为小型企业的权益而斗争。MarketWatch.com上的以下报道展示了过去监管机构是如何迎合小型企业利益的，不过也存在一个显著的例外：不妨称之为“繁文缛节之战”。政府制定的各种规则和法规是大多数小型企业的噩梦。20多年来，它们一直在与联邦官僚们为应对华盛顿方面颁布的繁杂法规而持续抗争。 体积虽小，新闻价值却大 • 233 不容忽视的是，小型企业早已在诸多战役中取得过重大胜利。然而，这场斗争依然以令人沮丧的方式持续着。最新一轮冲突上周在众议院小型企业委员会上爆发，针对对象正是美国国税局。背景是，早在1980年，繁文缛节相关的争斗本应达成停战协议。当时，白宫小型企业会议推动了三项重要新法律的出台——《监管灵活性法案》、《司法平等准入法案》以及《文书简化法案》。这些法律本应确保政府机构考虑到所有受联邦法规影响的人的诉求。尤其是《监管灵活性法案》至关重要，它要求各机构在颁布新规之前先对其可能对小型企业造成的影响进行评估，旨在找到办法减少法规对小型企业的过度冲击。众所周知，似乎没有哪个联邦机构比国税局更热衷于增加文书工作。但在遵守自身法规方面，美国的税收体系却表现出极强的抗拒变革的特性。“如果避开《监管灵活性法案》是国税局的隐秘目标，那他们无疑已经成功了；但对于那些关心该法案效力的人来说，整体情况实在糟糕，”总部位于亚利桑那州菲尼克斯、为小型企业提供保险服务的Argus集团负责人丹·马斯特朗科说道。经过四年的激烈立法斗争，国会最终在1996年进一步收紧了《监管灵活性法案》的法律标准。或许并不意外，国税局在推出看似无害的工资税缴纳系统变更时，引发了改革浪潮。“他们提出的规则简直就是胡言乱语，”曾参与这场斗争的前国会议员安迪·爱尔兰表示，“我根本看不懂，而且当我去国税局局长办公室作证时，他的手下似乎也都不明白。”他向委员会透露：“然而这些人却坚信普通小型企业主不会有遵守上的困难。”印第安纳波利斯Baker & Daniels律师事务所的合伙人弗兰克·斯韦恩称，不幸的是，国税局对《监管灵活性法案》的轻视态度至今依然明显。根据该机构12月发表在《联邦公报》上的最新半年度监管计划，目前国税局正在推进286项监管项目，但仅称其中两项值得进行监管灵活性分析。“无论国税局如何解读法律，在现实世界中，声称在286项监管事项中只对其中两项认为需要此类分析，显然是不可信的，”曾任小型企业管理局首席法律顾问的斯韦恩说。要了解国税局那些看似无害的提案为何常常会带来广泛的负面影响，可以看看去年6月国税局提出的一项提议：取消免除某些移动机械（如起重机）部分燃油及其他消费税的法规。这项被称为234 1. **Local government:** Real estate transaction records; register of deeds, health department records, planning department records, property appraiser or tax assessor; civil and criminal litigation.
2. **State government:** Secretary of State's office for incorporation records; Uniform Commercial Code filings, economic development records; state legislature; professional licensing boards; state regulatory agencies for insurance and banking.

financial information about small and private companies across the country. All it takes is some thinking and research, as this chapter will demonstrate. No company is completely private. And no business, no matter how small, leaves a cold trail. The reporting can be done. Many just do not know how to do it.
There is another, more important, reason why mass communication outlets should likely pay more attention to small and private businesses and the issues that affect their operations. As mentioned earlier, small and private businesses are vital to the economy, and when the economy suffers, small businesses are affected just like everyone else. More than half of the 763,000 jobs lost in the first half of 2008 were lost in small firms, and unincorporated self-employment fell from an average of 10.4 million in 2007 to an average of 10.1 million in 2008—and to 9.6 million by November and December 2008. Since the mid-1990s, small businesses have generally created 60 to 80 percent of the net new employment each year, but in 2008 there was a net loss of 3.1 million jobs. While it is not yet possible to know how many jobs were lost in smaller businesses, it is likely that the number is significant.
Some media outlets—particularly those in large metropolitan areas—virtually ignore businesses that collectively employ more than half of the country's workforce and account for more than half of all private sector output. To be sure, a number of newspapers and other media outlets do have a reporter assigned to cover small business issues. And small-town newspapers, such as the *Statesville Record & Landmark* in western North Carolina, have a business reporter in a community where virtually all news is small business news. But for the most part, business journalism has overlooked many small and private businesses compared with the coverage of public companies and well-known private corporations.
This is despite the fact that Americans have a higher opinion of small businesses than they do of better-known corporations and labor unions, according to a survey by the American Enterprise Institute in Washington. Ninety percent of Americans have a favorable opinion of small business, according to the survey, and the figure has hovered between 84 percent and 94 percent for the last quarter century.
In comparison, the latest Harris poll showed that 66 percent of people have a great deal of or some confidence in labor unions. The confidence level for large companies was 72 percent.
Small businesses have been revered in this country for more than a century. When Congress first passed antitrust laws in the nineteenth century, it did so to protect small and private businesses. The U.S. Small Business Administration was created in 1953 to aid and assist small companies.
Because of their collective interests, small businesses have grown into a powerful lobbying force in state legislatures and in Congress. The National Federation of Independent Business has more than 600,000 members and offices in all 50 states. Its lobbyists fight for small business rights with state and federal authorities.
The following story from MarketWatch.com shows how regulatory agencies have catered to small business interests in the past, with one notable exception:
Call it the red tape wars. Rules and regulations churned out by the government are the bane of most small businesses. For more than 20 years,they've fought a running battle with federal bureaucrats over the daunting process of complying with the edicts emanating from Washington.
Small in Size, Large for News • 233
Make no mistake; small businesses have won a significant round or two along the way. Yet the war continues in all its pencil-snapping frustration. The latest skirmish unfolded last week before the House Committee on Small Business. The target: the Internal Revenue Service.
By way of background, an armistice in the red tape wars was supposed to have been reached back in 1980. That's when the White House Conference on Small Business served as a catalyst for three significant new laws—the Regulatory Flexibility Act, the Equal Access to Justice Act and the Paperwork Reduction Act.
Together they were supposed to insure that government agencies took the concerns into account of anyone afflicted by federal rule making. The Regulatory Flexibility Act, in particular, was key. It exacted a pledge that agencies would study proposed regulations—before they were issued—to assess how they affected small businesses. The goal was to find ways to limit the impact, if regulation hit small firms disproportionately.
As we all know, no federal agency seems to pile on the paperwork quite like the IRS. Yet when it comes to complying with regulations itself, the nation's tax revenues have proved to be particularly resistant to change. "If avoidance of the RFA has been the Service's implicit goal, they have been unquestionably successful; but for those who care about the efficacy of the RFA, the overall record has been dismal," said Dan Mastromarco, Principal of The Argus Group, a Phoenix, Ariz., company that provides insurance to small businesses.
Congress last tightened the RFA's legal standards in 1996, following a bruising four-year legislative battle. Perhaps not surprisingly, the IRS triggered the reform effort when it issued supposedly innocuous changes to the payroll tax deposit system. "What they put out as a proposed rule can best be described as gibberish," said former Congressman Andy Ireland, who was involved in the fight. "I couldn't understand it. And, when I went to testify at a hearing before the staff of the IRS Commissioner none of his people seemed to understand it," he told the committee. "Yet these same people were confident that the average small businessperson would have no problem complying."
Unfortunately, the IRS's disdain for the RFA is still evident, said Frank Swain, a partner in the law firm of Baker & Daniels in Indianapolis. In fact, of the 286 regulatory projects it's working on right now, the IRS says that only two merit a regulatory flexibility analysis, according to the agency's most recent semi-annual regulatory agenda, which it published in the Federal Register in December. "Whatever the IRS's reading of the law is, in the real world it defies credibility to say that [it] is only working on two of 286 regulatory matters that it believes merit a regulatory flexibility analysis," said Swain, a former Chief Counsel for the Small Business Administration.
To understand how seemingly innocuous IRS proposals often have broad overreaching consequences, consider an IRS proposal last June to eliminate a regulation exempting certain mobile machinery, such as cranes, from certain fuel and other excise taxes. Although the measure, known as the

#### 专家建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

### 十二个关键问题：给小型或私营企业主的建议

<!--en-->
*The Dirty Dozen: 12 questions for the small or private business owner*

许多小型企业主对记者的提问十分警惕，尤其是那些从未接受过采访的人。这些问题能向企业主表明，您确实是真心希望向读者介绍他的公司。

<!--en-->
Many small business owners are wary of questions from reporters, particularly when they've never been interviewed before. These questions will show the owner that you're genuinely interested in telling readers about his or her company.

1. 您是何时萌生创业想法的？您的背景如何与这个创业理念相契合？
2. 您是如何为这家企业筹措资金的？资金来自储蓄还是亲友？
3. 店铺开业后多久就实现了盈利？您是如何庆祝的？
4. 在创业初期，最难克服的障碍是什么？
5. 您认为谁是您最大的竞争对手？原因是什么？
6. 您是如何发展企业的？是通过广告还是客户推荐？
7. 您最大的客户是谁？如果失去这位客户，您会怎么做？
8. 您的热销产品是什么？
9. 如果附近开了类似的企业，您会作何反应？如何应对加剧的竞争？
10. 您预计未来五年、十年内，您的公司规模会发展到多大？
11. 什么情况会促使您将企业出售给其他公司？
12. 您的员工是如何参与企业日常决策制定的？对于“移动机械免税”政策，由于该政策自1977年起就已存在，美国国税局称其对小型企业的影响微乎其微。斯韦恩表示，国税局从未费心进行过相关影响分析。斯韦恩指出，事实上，许多受影响的行业——包括建筑、打井与相关服务行业以及移动起重机操作行业——中都包含大量小型企业。¹ 报道小型私营企业与报道大型上市公司有所不同。首先，许多小型私营企业并不寻求宣传来提升股价，而且它们也不希望有记者四处打探新闻线索。而许多上市公司都有公关人员负责处理媒体询问，但大多数小型私营企业则没有。当有记者来电时，通常由老板或首席执行官亲自接听。商业记者并不一定非得报道小型私营企业的具体情况才能涉及相关内容。例如，报道圣诞促销的零售记者既可以联系私人店铺主，也可以联系上市百货连锁店和沃尔玛。而银行记者则会想报道某家私人社区银行如何增设分行以与美国银行和BankOne竞争。有些私人企业主和高管愿意接受采访，谈论当地及区域经济状况，或是分析诸如熟练工人短缺问题以及新法律将给他们带来的影响。通过每一篇报道，记者并非只是在记录企业情况，而是在赢得这些小型私营企业主或高管的信任。这样，当有与该企业相关的重大新闻值得报道时，企业主就更有可能敞开心扉。与大多数企业一样，小型私营公司也需要了解媒体的作用。他们中的许多人期望获得正面或积极的报道，如果未能如愿就会生气，甚至有人认为正面报道是作为其投放广告的交换条件。记者应当明确基本原则：对于任何企业相关报道，记者和媒体机构的职责都是向公众传递信息。只有当某些小型私营企业的情况在市场上具有独特性时，才会被报道。例如，威斯康星州斯特金湾的《Door County Advocate》就报道了该县斯特金湾以北第一家汽车洗车店的开业情况，那是因为它确实独一无二——方圆数英里内仅有这家洗车店。应当明确的是，由媒体机构来决定什么才是新闻。报道小型私营企业可以展现它们是如何随着社区的发展而变化和进步的。密苏里州卡普吉拉尔多市的《Southeast Missourian》曾在头版刊登了一篇关于移民小型企业主及国际劳工涌入该地的报道，帮助读者理解为何这些企业会在当地开设分店。许多小型企业记者更关注各种问题与趋势，而非对企业进行深度剖析。他们会探讨小型企业在商界生存的艰难处境，撰写关于为企业员工提供健康保险及其他福利的决定，以及相关成本如何可能拖垮一家小型企业；还会讲述一位企业主在经营40年后将企业交予下一代的艰辛历程。此外，他们还会评估新开的Home Depot会对那些已在当地经营了半个世纪的五金店产生的影响。[^2567]: ¹ 摘自K. Girard所著《战斗仍在继续：小型企业与美国国税局的规则制定博弈》，2003年5月5日，CBSMarketWatch.com。版权所有2003年MarketWatch.com，经许可转载。 体量虽小，新闻价值却大 • 235 报道小型及私营企业往往极具吸引力，因为这要求记者更深入地分析企业的状况。他们不能仅依赖美国证券交易委员会的文件来获取事实，而必须采访竞争对手、客户以及业务对象，评估市场环境，并寻找线索，以了解为何某家小型企业能够成功发展，或是为何难以维持运营。记者应当把自己视作一家小型企业：他们有收入——即工资——也有租金、电费、燃气费等开支，就像普通小型企业一样。剩余的资金可用于扩大业务，比如购买新电视、家具，甚至是新车。工资结余越多，记者就能“扩展”自己的“生意”。但如果没有剩余资金，那么这个“生意”就会陷入困境，可能不得不负债度日，甚至需要用信用卡消费或向银行贷款买车。小型及私营企业的运营方式大致如此，遇到困难时也会借贷。如果情况持续恶化，它们可能被迫停业。同样，如果记者的财务状况持续不佳，也可能被迫“停业”并寻找薪水更高的工作。与所有企业一样，小型及私营企业也会经历起伏，而这些起伏本身就可以成为新闻素材。

1. Where did you get the idea to start your business? How does your background fit into the company idea?
2. How did you fund the business? Did the money come from savings or relatives?
3. How soon after you first opened your doors did your business make a profit? How did you celebrate?
4. What was the hardest obstacle to overcome in getting the business off the ground?
5. Whom do you consider to be your biggest competitor and why?
6. How have you grown the business? Has it been through advertising or customer recommendations?
7. Who is your biggest customer? What would you do if you lost that customer?
8. What is your best-selling item?
9. How would you react if a similar business opened nearby? How could you handle the increased competition?
10. How big do you foresee your company becoming in the next five years? In the next 10 years?
11. What would make you sell your business to another company?
12. How are your employees involved in the day-to-day decision making of the business?
