It never bothered to conduct an RFA analysis, said Swain. As it turned out, many affected industries, including construction, well digging and services, and mobile-crane operators, include a significant number of small businesses, Swain said.¹
Writing about small and private businesses can be different than covering large, public companies. For one, many small and private businesses are not seeking publicity to help pump up their stock price. Many of them do not want a reporter poking around, looking for stories. Whereas many public companies have public relations personnel to handle media inquiries, most small and private businesses do not. When a reporter calls, the president or CEO often takes the call.
Business reporters do not necessarily have to write stories about what is going on at small and private businesses to write stories that include them. A retail reporter writing about Christmas sales can call the private storeowner as well as the publicly traded department store chain and Wal-Mart. A banking reporter will want to write about how a private community bank is adding branches to compete against Bank of America and BankOne.
Private business owners and executives are sometimes willing to grant interviews to talk about the local and regional economy or to assess issues such as a shortage of experienced workers or how they will be affected by new laws. With each story, the reporter is not writing about the business but is gaining the trust of the small and private business owner or executive. Then, when news specifically about the company merits coverage, the owner will be more likely to open up.
Like most businesses, small and private companies need to understand the role of the media. Many of them expect to receive glowing or positive coverage, and when they do not get it, they are mad. Some of them may even believe that positive coverage is a quid pro quo in exchange for their advertising.
The reporter should make the ground rules clear. With any business story, the job of the reporter and of the media outlet is to inform the public. Some stories are written about small and private businesses if they are unique to the market. The *Door County Advocate* in Sturgeon Bay, Wisconsin, covered the opening of the first car wash in the county north of Sturgeon Bay. But that was because of its uniqueness—it was the only car wash for miles. It should be clear that the media outlet decides what is news.
Writing about small and private businesses can show how they are changing and evolving with the community. The *Southeast Missourian* in Cape Girardeau, Missouri, published a story about the influx of immigrant small business owners and international workers in a front-page story that helped explain to its readers why these businesses were opening around town.
Many small business reporters focus on issues and trends instead of profiling companies. They look at how small companies struggle to make it in the businessworld. They write about the decision to provide health insurance and other benefits to workers and how the cost of doing so can cripple a small operation. They write about the struggle of a small business owner to hand his operation to the next generation after 40 years of running the company. They assess the impact of the new Home Depot on the local hardware stores that have been part of the community for half a century.
[^2567]: ¹ From “The battle rages on: Small business squares off against IRS rulemaking,” by K. Girard, May 5, 2003. CBSMarketWatch.com. Copyright 2003 by MarketWatch.com. Reprinted with permission.
Small in Size, Large for News • 235
Writing about small and private businesses can be fascinating because it forces the reporter to dig deeper into analyzing a company's situation. He or she cannot rely on SEC filings to provide the facts. He or she must interview competitors, customers and clients, assess the market, and look for clues as to why a small business is successful—or struggling to make ends meet.
The reporter should think of him- or herself as a small business. The reporter has revenue—a paycheck—and expenses, such as rent, electricity, and gas, just like a small business. What is left over is used to expand operations by buying a new television or some furniture or even a new car. The more money left over from the paycheck, the more the reporter can expand his or her “business.” But if there is no money left over, then the “business” is struggling and may have to go into debt to make ends meet. That may mean making purchases with credit cards or asking the bank for a loan to buy that car.
Small and private businesses operate much the same way. And when they struggle, they borrow money, too. If they continue to struggle, they may be forced to go out of business. If the reporter's financial situation continues to flounder, he or she, too, may be forced to go out of “business” and find a new job that pays more money.
Small and private businesses have ups and downs, just like any business. Those ups and downs can be news.

## 获取信息

<!--en-->
*Finding Information*

许多记者误以为私营企业就只是“私有的”而已。虽然私营企业很少主动公开其运营信息，但仍有许多其他途径可以获取这些信息。

<!--en-->
Many reporters mistakenly believe that private companies are just that—private. And while private companies rarely hand out information willingly about their operations, there are plenty of other places to get that information.

记者应先考虑了解小型或私营企业的哪些信息较为重要，然后再向该公司请求这些信息。有一次我提出要求，钟表品牌Timex的首席执行官便向我提供了该公司最近一年的营收与利润数据。北卡罗来纳州规模最大的私营企业则公开了自20世纪30年代成立以来的每年营收与利润情况。如果该公司拒绝提供信息，那就需思考这些信息可能存在于何处。

<!--en-->
Reporters should consider what information would be good to know about a small or private business and then ask the company for that information. The CEO of watchmaker Timex once gave me the private company's revenues and profits for the most recent year because I asked. The largest private company in North Carolina provides its revenues and profits for each year dating back to its founding in the 1930s. If the business declines to provide the information, then think about where that information might be found.

有些私营企业会主动向本地商业杂志等媒体提供营收和利润的区间数据。在其他情况下，则可根据对该公司运营情况的了解来估算其营收和盈利水平。当记者使用这类数据时，必须确保注明信息来源。

<!--en-->
Some private companies willingly give a range of revenue and profits to publications such as the local business journal. In other cases, revenue and earnings may be estimated on the basis of knowledge of the company's operations. When reporters use numbers like these, they must make sure to attribute them to the source.

即使企业不愿透露信息，要获取小型和私营企业的信息也相对容易。政府机构是获取此类信息的最佳渠道。关于小型和私营企业的基本信息，如公司章程，都存放在州务卿办公室。

<!--en-->
Still, it is relatively easy to find information about small and private businesses if the company is not forthcoming. Government agencies are the best places to look for most of this information. Basic information about small and private companies, such as articles of incorporation, is filed with the Secretary of State's

## 专家建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《新奥尔良时代-皮卡尤恩报》商业版编辑Kim Quillen关于报道小型和私营企业的建议：

<!--en-->
New Orleans Times-Picayune business editor Kim Quillen on covering small and private companies:

**建立人脉：** 有很多途径可以与小型企业建立联系，包括商会午餐会、小型企业研讨会以及各类社交活动。花时间与当地小型企业的经营者交流，了解他们的业务情况。

<!--en-->
**Network:** There are a number of places you can go to interact with small businesses, including chamber of commerce luncheons, small business seminars, and networking events. Spend time rubbing elbows with the operators of local small firms and learning about their operations.

### 专家建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《新奥尔良时代-皮卡尤恩报》商业版编辑Kim Quillen关于报道小型和私营企业的建议：

<!--en-->
New Orleans Times-Picayune business editor Kim Quillen on covering small and private companies:

**开业/周年纪念/新产品发布：** 作为小型企业记者，我可以向你保证，你会收到大量来自当地企业的请求，希望你能为其新店开业、企业周年纪念或新产品发布撰写报道。最好尽早明确自己针对这类事件的报道原则（或了解所在报社的政策），以便始终如一地回应。

<!--en-->
**Grand openings/anniversaries/new products:** As a small business reporter, I can assure you that you will receive numerous pitches from local firms seeking write-ups about stores they are opening, business anniversaries and new products. It's a good idea to think through early on what your policy will be on covering these events (or find out what your paper's policy is) so that you can respond consistently.

#### 专家建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《新奥尔良时代-皮卡尤恩报》商业版编辑Kim Quillen关于报道小型和私营企业的建议：

<!--en-->
New Orleans Times-Picayune business editor Kim Quillen on covering small and private companies:

**不要害怕提问：** 小型私营企业无需公开财务信息。不过，通常更容易接触到这类企业的所有者或高层管理人员。充分利用这一机会，直接询问所有者是否愿意与你分享相关数据。236 • 规模虽小，新闻价值巨大

<!--en-->
**Don't be afraid to ask:** Small private firms are not required to disclose their financial information. However, you usually get better access to the owner or top executive at a smaller firm. Make the most of that access and ask the owner directly if he'll share relevant data with you.
236 • Small in Size, Large for News

#### 专家建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《新奥尔良时代-皮卡尤恩报》商业版编辑Kim Quillen关于报道小型和私营企业的建议：

<!--en-->
New Orleans Times-Picayune business editor Kim Quillen on covering small and private companies:

**利用州务卿办公室的资源：** 一些州的州务卿会维护一个可搜索的在线数据库，收录该州所有注册的企业信息。如果你需要在最后一刻报道一家你不太了解的公司，这里是个快速获取基本信息的好地方，包括公司的高层管理人员是谁以及公司何时注册的。公司章程中会列明高管和所有者的姓名，以及电话号码和邮寄地址。这是研究小型或私营企业时的首要查询途径。不过有时注册记录可能并非最新，也可能该州已将该企业标记为经营状况不佳，这可能是企业存在财务问题的迹象。

<!--en-->
**Use your Secretary of State's Office:** Some Secretaries of State maintain a searchable online database of all the businesses incorporated in the state. If you're doing last-minute coverage of a company you know little about, this is a good place to quickly find out basic information, including who the top officers are and when the company was incorporated.
office. The articles of incorporation will provide the names of the executives and owners, as well as phone numbers and mailing addresses. That is the first place to start when researching a small or private business. Sometimes the incorporation records may not be up to date, and maybe the state has listed the company as not in good standing. This could be a sign that the business is having financial trouble.

另一个获取信息的良好途径是当地政府档案。例如，当地的建筑部门会保存建筑许可和检查记录。县书记员或土地登记处则会有有关房地产契据、抵押贷款协议以及假名注册的信息。当一家企业以某个名称开展业务，但在州级层面以另一个名称注册时，这些名称可能会非常重要。

<!--en-->
Another good place to find information is local government records. The local building department will have building permit and inspection records, for example. A county clerk or register of deeds will have information about real estate deeds, mortgage agreements, and fictitious name registrations. The names may be important when a company is operating its business under one name but is incorporated at the state level under another name.

在法院时，记者不应忘记查看该企业此前是否曾遭遇诉讼。记者应阅读相关诉讼文件，并确认起诉该公司的律师姓名，随后致电他们询问其与该企业的往来情况。如果某公司在过去几个月或一年中面临大量诉讼，这可能表明该公司存在偿债困难。同时也要查明该企业自身是否也在提起诉讼。诉讼记录能够提供关于那些否则可能不为人知的小型及私营企业的信息。

<!--en-->
While at the courthouse, a reporter should not forget to check whether the business has been sued in the past. The reporter should read the lawsuits and check the names of the lawyers suing the company. The reporter should call them and ask about their dealings with the business. If there are a lot of lawsuits against a company in the last few months or year, that could be a sign that the business is having trouble paying its debts. Also check to see if the business is litigious itself and is filing lawsuits against others. Lawsuits can provide information about small and private businesses that may have otherwise gone undisclosed.

记者还应查看法院的刑事案件相关记录。如果首席执行官或小型企业主被捕，这通常都是新闻素材。首席执行官及企业高管偶尔也会卷入与业务无关的民事诉讼，而这些诉讼会披露有关其公司的信息。离婚申请就是一个典型例子——配偶可能会要求分得企业一半的价值，并在申请材料中详细列出企业的财务状况。

<!--en-->
Reporters should check the criminal side of the courthouse, too. If a CEO or small business owner has been arrested, that is often news. CEOs and company executives also occasionally find themselves in civil suits unrelated to their business in which information about their company is disclosed. Divorce filings are a prime example. A spouse may be seeking half of the worth of the business and may file detailed information about its financial performance in the filings.

在地方层面也有大量可用信息。当地卫生部门会保存卫生检查记录及部分许可证。对于餐厅等许多行业而言，卫生记录非常重要。例如，科罗拉多州的《洛夫兰报道先驱报》每周都会公布全州范围内的餐厅及食品服务行业检查结果，按“优秀”“一般”“不合格”等等级进行排序。

<!--en-->
There is lots more information also available at the local level. The local health department will have health inspection records and some permits. Health records are important for many industries, such as restaurants. The *Loveland Reporter-Herald* in Colorado, for example, lists restaurant and food service inspections throughout the county every week, ranking them from those that received “excellent” ratings to those that received “marginal” and “inadequate” ratings.

规划或分区管理部门会存有有关建设许可以及用于担保施工的保证金的相关信息。这类信息对撰写关于当地商业或住宅开发商报道的记者很有帮助。此外，房产评估师或税务评估办公室可以提供房产的评估价值以及房产和建筑的相关描述。

<!--en-->
The planning or zoning department will have information about development permits and bonds posted to guarantee construction. Such information can be helpful for reporters writing about a local commercial or residential developer. In addition, the property appraiser or tax assessor's office can provide the assessed value of a property as well as property and building descriptions.

当地的房地产交易情况也能为了解小型或私营企业提供线索。记者应查看该公司近期是否有任何购置行为。如果有，土地位于何处，该公司打算如何使用这些土地？如果购置地点靠近其当前所在地，该公司可能在计划扩张。另外，还需查明小型或私营企业是否在购买住宅物业。如果是，居住在这些房子里的人是谁？如果这些居民是该公司的员工或高管，为何能享受这种特殊待遇？规模虽小，新闻价值却高 • 237 小型及私营企业还会与可能提供信息的州级监管机构有接触。除了州务卿办公室外，其他可能掌握企业相关记录的州级机构还包括总检察长办公室——该办公室可能曾调查针对该企业的消费者投诉或对该企业提起过诉讼；还有经济发展办公室，其目标是让州内的企业满意并吸引新企业入驻。如果某家企业曾获得税收减免或其他财政优惠，经济发展办公室会有相关记录。

<!--en-->
Local real estate transactions can also be telling for a small or private business. Reporters should check to see if the company has been making any purchases recently. If so, where is the land, and what does the company plan to do with it? If the purchases are near its current location, the company could be planning an expansion. It is also important to check to see if a small or private business is purchasing residential property. If it is, who is living in the houses? If the residents are employees or executives of the company, why are they receiving this special treatment?
Small in Size, Large for News • 237
Small and private businesses also come into contact with state regulatory agencies that could provide information. In addition to the Secretary of State's office, other state agencies that might have records on a business include the attorney general's office, which might have investigated consumer complaints against the business or prosecuted the company, and economic development offices, which have the goal of keeping businesses happy in the state and attracting new companies. If a business has ever received a tax break or other financial enticement, the economic development office would have a record.

《哈特福德信使报》报道称，康涅狄格州官员曾协助一家宾夕法尼亚州的小型企业申请州政府资金以助其扩张。此外，这些官员的近亲还参与了这家私营公司的投资，此后他们的投资价值迅速飙升。这一报道正是通过查阅州经济发展机构的信息得出的。

<!--en-->
The *Hartford Courant* reported that Connecticut officials assisted a small Pennsylvania company seeking state funding to help it expand. In addition, the company helped close relatives of those officials invest in the private company. The value of their investment skyrocketed shortly thereafter. That story came from looking at the state economic development agency.

州级许可机构也是小型及私营企业的重要信息来源。它们负责监管从理发店到医生等各类企业，而且其许多记录都是公开信息。例如，在某些情况下可以获取针对医疗行业的罚款及吊销执照的相关记录。

<!--en-->
State licensing agencies are also an important source of information for small and private businesses. They regulate businesses ranging from barbershops to doctors, and many of their records are public information. Fines and suspensions against the medical profession, for example, can be obtained in some cases.

记者还应查看州立法机构的记录，看是否有与该企业或其所在行业相关的听证会记录。州环境保护机构可能有该企业污染情况的记录，而劳工部门则可能透露该公司是否曾裁员。州采购办公室可以告知该企业是否与州政府有合同关系，若有，涉及哪些商品或服务。

<!--en-->
Reporters should also check the state legislature to see if there have been any hearings related to the company or its industry. The state environmental protection agency may have records of pollution on the business, whereas the department of labor may be able to tell whether the company has been laying off workers. The state purchasing office can tell whether the business has any contracts with the state, and if so, for which goods or services.

《统一商法典》（UCC）的备案文件也是重要资料，能够帮助了解小型或私营企业的状况。该法典的法规几乎已被美国所有州采纳。当一家企业以赊销方式向另一家企业出售商品时，就需要进行UCC备案。例如，将拖拉机卖给农夫的企业会提交一份UCC表格，说明该拖拉机是贷款的抵押物。如果购买拖拉机的企业未能偿还贷款，另一家企业就可以收回拖拉机。UCC表格还能显示一家企业是否为采购而借贷了大量资金，这可能是该公司计划扩大业务的迹象。

<!--en-->
Uniform Commercial Code (UCC) filings are also important documents that can help tell a story about a small or private business. The UCC has a body of laws that has been adopted in virtually every state in the country. A UCC filing occurs when one business sells something to another business on credit. The business that sold the tractor to the farmer, for example, filed a UCC form showing that the tractor was collateral for the loan. If the business that purchased the tractor fails to pay the loan, the other business can repossess the tractor. UCC forms can show whether a business is borrowing a lot of money to make purchases. This could be a sign that the company plans to expand its operations.

负责监管银行和保险行业的州级监管机构同样是重要的信息来源，即便是像保险机构这样的小型企业也不例外。他们掌握着在该州运营的每一家银行和保险公司的财务报告。即便某家银行或保险公司是私营性质且不愿向记者披露其收入和利润，这些信息也应能轻易获取，因为它们早已将相关数据交给了监管机构。记者应提前告知该公司自己将获取并使用这些信息。在记者与州级监管机构取得联系后，该公司可能会更愿意透露信息。电力、水务等公用事业公司也是如此，它们由州公共服务委员会监管，该委员会会保存相关的财务记录。

<!--en-->
State regulators tracking the banking and insurance industries can also be important sources of information, even for small businesses like insurance agencies. They will have financial reports for every bank and insurance company operating in the state. If the bank or insurer is private and not willing to disclose its revenue and profits to a reporter, the information should still be readily available because it has given this information to regulators. Reporters should let the company know they are going to get the information and use it. The company might open up more after the reporter makes a few calls to the state. The same goes for utility companies, such as electricity and water operations. They are regulated by a state public service commission, which keeps financial records.

州级税务记录同样具有价值。纽约WABC电视台的吉姆·霍弗通过查询州级税务记录，发现曼哈顿的许多餐厅拖欠数千美元的税款。“从快餐店到城里一些最优秀的餐厅，我们的调查共发现了近200家店铺，它们从顾客那里收取的税款总计约1000万美元，”霍弗指出，“这些钱是通过8.25%的销售税征收的，但这些餐厅并未将其上缴给市政府和州政府，而是据为己有。”掌握了这一信息后，霍弗找上了其中一些餐厅老板——他们都是小型私营企业主。许多人声称正在努力偿还债务，还有一个人表示自己将销售税用作贷款，以帮助度过2001年9月11日恐怖袭击后的难关，同时他也清楚自己需要为此支付罚款（霍弗，2003年）。238 • 规模虽小，新闻价值巨大。根据职能不同，联邦机构也可能掌握有关小型和私营企业的信息。例如，环境保护局会向排放环境敏感液体的企业发放许可证，并对泄漏事件进行调查；如果某公司的产品因安全问题被召回，消费品安全委员会也会保留相关记录。（有关监管机构的更多信息，请参见第15章。）

<!--en-->
State tax records can also be valuable. Jim Hoffer, of WABC in New York, searched state tax records and discovered that many Manhattan restaurants owed thousands in back taxes. "From fast food to some of the city's finest restaurants, our investigation found nearly 200 establishments that have collected from their customers a combined total of about $10 million," noted Hoffer. "It's moneycollected through the 8.25 percent sales tax. But instead of passing it on to the city and state, these restaurants kept it.” Armed with this information, Hoffer confronted some of these restaurant owners, all small, private businesses. Many claimed to be working to pay off the debt. One said he used the sales tax as a loan to help make it through the aftermath of the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks, fully understanding he would pay a penalty (Hoffer, 2003).
238 • Small in Size, Large for News
Federal agencies might also have information on small and private businesses, depending on their operations. The Environmental Protection Agency, for example, issues permits to businesses that discharge environmentally sensitive liquids, and it also investigates spills. The Consumer Product Safety Commission will have records on a company if it has ever had a product recalled because of safety concerns. (For more information about regulatory agencies, see Chapter 15.)

在涉及员工事务方面，平等就业机会委员会和职业安全与健康管理局是查询信息的绝佳途径。这些机构会调查关于工作歧视、骚扰以及恶劣工作条件的投诉。如果某家企业有员工在工作中受伤，或者曾面临员工提出的不公平待遇指控，那么就会有关于对此事进行调查的记录。如果该企业有工会成员，可向国家劳工关系委员会查询，看看该公司是否因操纵工会投票而陷入麻烦。

<!--en-->
For employee-related matters, the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission and the Occupational Safety and Health Administration are excellent places to check for information. These agencies investigate complaints of job discrimination and harassment and unsafe working conditions. If the business has had a worker injured on the job or has ever faced a claim from an employee alleging unfair treatment, there is a record of an investigation into the matter. Check the National Labor Relations Board if the business has unionized workers to see if the company has gotten into trouble for tampering with union votes.

如果该公司从事科技或其他专业领域业务，它可能拥有用于盈利的发明专利。专利商标局会保存该公司获得的每一项专利的记录。如果该公司不愿谈论其产品，这或许是一种获取相关信息的途径。不过，可能需要工程师或科学家的帮助才能解释这些专利的含义。

<!--en-->
If the company is involved in technology or another specialized business, it may have patents on inventions being used to help it make money. The Patent and Trademark Office will have a record of every patent issued to the company. If the company does not want to talk about its products, this could be a way of getting information about them. However, it may take an engineer or a scientist to help explain what the patent means.

联邦机构还会对特定行业进行监管。例如，关于信用合作社的财务信息可从国家信用合作社管理局获取。许多记者并不知道这一点，他们误以为信用合作社是由储户拥有的非营利组织。但实际上，很多信用合作社都盈利能力很强。记者应查明所在地区信用合作社的盈利情况，这或许就是一篇值得撰写的报道素材。

<!--en-->
Federal agencies also regulate specific industries. For example, financial information about a credit union is available from the National Credit Union Administration. Many journalists do not know this, rightfully thinking that credit unions are nonprofit organizations owned by the depositors. Yet, many credit unions are very profitable. A reporter should find out the profitability of the credit unions in his or her town. That may be a story waiting to be written.

美国联邦航空管理局会收集与机场相关的信息，这些信息对撰写报道非常有帮助，尤其是对于那些关注交通或旅游领域的记者而言。该机构还掌握着针对航空公司、飞行员、机械师以及行业内其他人员的监管记录，同时还有全国所有飞机的登记信息。美国联邦通信委员会则拥有关于国内每一家广播电台和电视台的大量信息，以及电话公司和有线电视公司的相关文件。

<!--en-->
The Federal Aviation Administration collects information about airports that can be useful in writing a story, particularly for a reporter interested in transportation or tourism. The agency has enforcement information against airlines, pilots, mechanics, and others in the industry, as well as a registry of all aircraft owned in the country. The Federal Communications Commission has tons of information about each and every radio and television station in the country, as well as documents on telephone and cable companies.

想要了解私营矿业公司信息的记者可以咨询矿山安全与健康管理局。而核管理委员会则保存着核电站运营方的记录。从这两个例子可以看出，几乎每种类型的行业都有相应的监管机构。对于打算撰写关于当地枪店故事的记者来说，酒精、烟草及火器局维护着一份全国范围内获得联邦批准的枪支经销商数据库。如果那家枪店不在名单上，那么记者得到的素材可能比最初预想的还要好。规模虽小，新闻价值却高 • 239 或者，记者可能在撰写关于某家从小企业管理局（SBA）获得贷款担保支持的小企业的故事。SBA拥有一个数据库，其中详细记载了贷款金额、审批时间、贷款是否已偿还或出现逾期情况、提供贷款的银行名称、该公司因该贷款承诺新增的就业岗位数量以及其他相关信息。SBA还负责推行一项计划，鼓励联邦政府将项目合同授予小型企业和少数族裔企业，这类合同上也会有类似的信息。如果你所撰写的对象的企业提到曾为联邦政府工作，那么应该能找到很多信息，包括该企业的营收情况及其收入来源——即便是私营企业也是如此。

<!--en-->
Reporters looking for information about private mining companies can check with the Mine Safety and Health Administration. And the Nuclear Regulatory Commission has records about operators of nuclear plants. As these two examples show, there is likely a regulatory agency for almost every type of industry. For the reporter trying to write a story about a gun store in town, the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, and Firearms maintains a database of federally approved gun dealers across the country. If the gun store is not on that list, then the reporter has a better story than he or she may have originally thought.
Small in Size, Large for News • 239
Or maybe a reporter is writing about a small business that has gotten some help from the Small Business Administration (SBA) in the form of a loan guaranteed by the agency. The SBA has a database that details the size of loans, when the loan was approved, whether the loan has been paid or become delinquent, which bank made the loan, the number of jobs the company promised to add to its employee base because of the loan, and other information. The SBA also administers a program that encourages the federal government to award contracts for work to small and minority businesses. Similar information is available on these contracts. If the business you are writing about mentions that it has done work for the federal government, a lot of information should be available, including revenue for the company and where the revenue is coming from—even for private businesses.

其他渠道也能获取有关小型企业和私营企业的有用信息。例如，可以付费购买邓白氏等公司提供的信用报告，这些报告有时能告诉记者该公司是否存在债务偿还问题。

<!--en-->
Other good information about small and private companies is available from other sources. For example, credit reports from companies such as Dun and Bradstreet can be purchased for a fee. These reports can sometimes tell a journalist if the company has had problems repaying its debt.

一家私营企业可能曾面临债务问题。如果确实如此，它可能已向美国证券交易委员会提交相关资料。此外，债券评级机构很可能会对这一债务问题进行评估并给出债券评级，同时也可能撰写关于该公司及其财务状况的报告。

<!--en-->
A private company may have made a debt issue. If it has, then it may have filed information with the SEC. In addition, bond rating agencies will likely have reviewed the debt issue and issued a rating on the bonds. The rating agency may have also written a report about the company and its financial status.

小型企业在向美国证券交易委员会申请成为上市公司时，并不总是需要遵循与大企业相同的流程。如果该企业的营收低于2500万美元，或其股票市值不超过2500万美元，就可以提交SB-1表格来筹集1000万美元或更少的资金。该表格允许企业以问答形式提供信息。当小型企业希望通过股票发行筹集无限额资金，但又希望披露的信息少于美国证券交易委员会对大企业要求的程度时，则会使用SB-2表格。例如，小型企业只需提供两年的经审计财务报表，而大企业则必须提供三年的经审计财务报表。

<!--en-->
Small companies do not always have to go through the same steps as larger companies when filing documents with the SEC to become public companies. If it had less than $25 million in revenue or its stock is worth no more than $25 million, the company can file a Form SB-1 to raise $10 million or less. This form allows the business to provide information in a question-and-answer format. A Form SB-2 is used by a small business when it wants to raise an unlimited amount of cash in a stock offering but still requires less disclosure than the SEC requires for larger companies. For example, small businesses have to provide two years of audited financial statements, whereas large companies must provide three years of audited financial statements.

还有其他途径可以获取有关小型或私营企业的信息。如果该企业发布了任何新闻稿，相关文件应可在PR Newswire或Business Wire上找到。记者应查看所在媒体的档案库，看看过去是否有过关于该企业的报道，或者可以在LexisNexis等数据库中进行更广泛的搜索，查找其他相关文章或提及。如果这家小型或私营企业属于某个有专业出版物（如通讯或月刊）的细分行业，记者也应查阅这些刊物，看是否有过对该企业的提及。在试图获取一家不愿公开信息的企业的相关线索时，每一个细节都可能起到重要作用。

<!--en-->
Other sources exist for ferreting out information about a small or private business. If the business has issued a news release about anything, the document should be available from PR Newswire or Business Wire. Reporters should check their media outlet's library to see if it has done a story on the company in the past or should do a broader search on a database such as LexisNexis to check for other articles or mentions. If the small or private business is part of a niche industry with a specialty publication, such as a newsletter or monthly magazine, reporters should check it to see if the business has ever been mentioned. Every little bit helps when you are gathering string on a company that is not divulging any information.

同样，竞争对手也可能提供有价值的信息。诸如广告公司以及该公司产品或商品的经销商等供应商，能够提供与该企业合作的相关体验信息。公共利益团体也可能掌握相关信息。可以咨询当地的商会或商业改进局，了解是否有过针对该企业的投诉记录。

<!--en-->
Again, competitors may be able to provide valuable information. Suppliers such as advertising firms and distributors of the company's products or goods can provide information as to what it is like to do business with the company. Public interest groups may also have information. Check with the local Chamber of Commerce or Better Business Bureau to see if there have been complaints filed against the business.

另一个宝贵的信息来源是员工。他们可能心怀不满或不开心。虽然出于担心丢掉工作的顾虑，他们可能不会公开谈论自己的雇主，但可能会通过提供可能造成损害的内部文件或公司信息来报复恶劣的待遇。记者在此时应谨慎行事。如果员工有所顾虑，他可能会向上级告发有记者在打探消息。240 • 体量虽小，新闻价值巨大 最近对《福布斯》杂志网站访问者的一项调查显示，53%的受访者认为不应要求私营企业披露收入、利润、资产和员工人数，而29%的人则认为应当如此。很可能不会出台要求私营企业这样做的法律。但那种认为小型私营企业在信息方面是封闭状态的观念应该被打破。其实可以获取大量信息。当然这需要付出一些努力，而且大部分努力可能无法得到可用于报道的信息，但只要有一条有用信息，就能让报道变得有价值。

<!--en-->
Another valuable source is employees. They may be disgruntled or unhappy. Although they may not talk on the record about their employer for fear of losing their jobs, they may seek retribution for bad treatment by providing internaldocuments or company information that could be damaging. Reporters should tread lightly here. If an employee balks, he may go to his superior and tell him that a reporter has been snooping around.
240 • Small in Size, Large for News
A recent survey of visitors to the *Forbes* magazine website resulted in 53 percent of the respondents replying that private businesses should not be required to disclose revenue, profits, assets, and employees, whereas 29 percent believed they should. It is unlikely that any laws will be passed requiring private companies to do so. But the notion that small and private businesses are closed doors when it comes to information should be dispelled. Plenty of information can be obtained. It certainly takes some legwork, and most of the legwork may not result in any information that will make it into the story. But the one fact that does makes the story worthwhile.

### UCC登记文件

<!--en-->
*UCC Code Filings*

UCC登记文件是小型私营企业的信息来源，这一点再怎么强调都不为过。

<!--en-->
UCC filings are a source of information for small and private businesses. This cannot be emphasized enough.

对于记者而言，UCC登记文件是最有价值的资料之一，但却很少被用来讲述一家企业——无论是公营还是私营、大型还是小型——或个人的状况。这实在令人遗憾，因为这些登记文件能为记者提供关于公司或个人的重要信息。记者在撰写有关公司或个人的报道时，应每次都查看UCC登记文件。

<!--en-->
UCC filings are some of the best documents available to a reporter, but they are seldom used to tell the story of a business—public or private, big or small—or an individual. That is disappointing, because these filings help tell the reporter vital information about a company or a person. A reporter should look at UCC filings each time he or she writes a story about a company or a person.

各州的州务卿办公室都提供UCC登记文件。其中很多文件都可以在线查询，可以通过贷款方名称或借款人的身份进行检索。

<!--en-->
UCC filings are available from the Secretary of State's office in each state. Many of these are available online and can be searched by lender name as well as by the borrower's identity.

如前所述，UCC登记文件是向州政府提交的，用于说明资金是因购买物品还是其他原因而被借出的。这些登记文件能显示哪家公司或企业对某家公司的资产或房屋拥有留置权。有时，登记文件还会披露贷款金额以及用作贷款抵押的物品。没人愿意购买带有前业主债权人留置权的房子。UCC登记文件可以揭示这些信息，还能让企业主了解潜在合作伙伴有多少笔贷款，以及贷款金额大概是多少。许多企业主在签订合同之前会查看其他企业的UCC登记文件，他们想确保对方有能力履行合同义务。

<!--en-->
As mentioned earlier, UCC filings are made with the state to show when money has been borrowed to make a purchase or for another reason. UCC filings show which company or business holds a lien on a corporation or a home. Sometimes, the filing will disclose the amount of the loan and what was used as collateral for the loan. No one would want to buy a house that has a lien on it from a creditor of the previous owner. A UCC filing can disclose this information, and it can tell a business owner how many loans, and sometimes for what amounts, a potential business partner has. Many business owners check the UCC filings of other businesses before they sign a contract. They want to know that the company is going to be able to fulfill its end of the deal.

北卡罗来纳州州务卿办公室对查阅UCC登记文件的价值作了如下解释：

<!--en-->
The North Carolina Secretary of State's office explains the usefulness of reviewing UCC filings in the following way:

> 此类信息可用于判断贷款机构是否有意向小型企业主提供信贷，例如为其购买设备或原材料提供资金。小型企业主则可通过该部门的记录，决定是否以待售成品作为担保来向客户提供信贷。如果没有《统一商法典》相关条款提供的服务，贷款机构或小型企业主可能不得不查询多个县的留置权记录，才能全面了解参与潜在交易的人员或企业的财务状况。（北卡罗来纳州州务卿部，2003年）规模虽小，资讯量大 • 241 这些登记信息在多方面都很有用。在报道某家企业或个人时，记者可以查明该人或公司欠款的金额及欠款对象。《今日美国》在调查声名狼藉的前世界通信公司高管伯尼·埃伯斯时，查阅了全国各地的《统一商法典》登记记录，从而得到了他过去十年间所有投资和购买项目的详细清单，这有助于向读者展示他从世界通信公司获得的资金去向了何处。《匹兹堡邮报》对一家希望重新开发购物中心的教堂进行的调查也体现了查阅《统一商法典》登记信息的益处：记者通过查看该教堂的登记记录，发现尽管它拖欠税款和其他债务，银行及其他贷款机构仍向其提供了七笔贷款。《统一商法典》登记信息主要分为两类。第一类称为UCC-1，是首次记录的原始财务声明；UCC-3则是用于延续、终止、修改或免除债务或贷款的声明。虽然《统一商法典》登记信息看起来可能令人生畏，但实际上它们只是记录简单的商业交易。记者应充分利用这些信息。当小型或私营企业主——或者任何人——发现记者花时间查看了其《统一商法典》登记信息时，就会立刻意识到该记者是真心想要获取信息。《圣彼得堡时报》就利用《统一商法典》登记信息查找为里奇港市供水的公司的相关信息，该公司老板对自己被找到感到十分惊讶。

<!--en-->
> Such information may be used to determine whether a lender would be interested in extending credit to the small business owner to, for example, provide capital for purchasing equipment or raw materials.
> The small business owner may, in turn, access the Section's records to determine whether to extend credit to customers by taking a security interest in the finished product to be sold. Without the services offered by the UCC Section, the lender or small business owner might be required to check county lien records in several counties in order to get a true financial picture of the person or business involved in the potential transaction.
*(North Carolina Department of the Secretary of State, 2003)*
Small in Size, Large for News • 241
These filings can be helpful in a number of ways. When writing about a business or an individual, reporters can find out how much and to whom the person or company owes money. When *USA Today* researched disgraced former WorldCom leader Bernie Ebbers, it pored through UCC filings around the country to get a detailed list of everything he had invested in or purchased during the last decade. That helped show readers where the money he had made from WorldCom had gone. Another example of the benefits of looking at UCC filings is illustrated by the *Pittsburgh Post-Gazette* investigation into a church that wanted to redevelop a shopping center. The reporter looked at the church's UCC filings and discovered that banks and other lenders had given it seven loans despite the fact that it had fallen behind in paying its taxes and other debts.
There are two main types of UCC filings. The first one is called a UCC-1 and is the original finance statement being recorded for the first time. A UCC-3 filing is a statement that continues, terminates, amends, or releases the debt or loan.
UCC filings may seem intimidating, but all they are doing is recording simple business transactions. Reporters should use them to their advantage. When a small or private business owner—or anyone, for that matter—discovers that a reporter has taken the time to look at its UCC filings, he or she suddenly realizes that that reporter is serious about finding information. The *St. Petersburg Times* used UCC filings to track down information about a company providing water to the city of Port Richey. The owner of the company was surprised that she had been found.

### 私营公司的所有权与结构

<!--en-->
*Private Company Ownership and Structure*

了解小型或私营公司的所有权结构，与了解该企业的业务状况及运营情况同样重要。公司的所有权能告诉你谁才是企业的决策者。如果一家企业由一个人拥有，那么很可能是这个人同时担任总裁或首席执行官，并负责做出所有重大决策。

<!--en-->
Knowing the structure of small or private company ownership is as important as knowing the facts about the business and its operations. The company's ownership will tell you who is calling the shots for the business. If a business is owned by one person, it is likely that he or she is also the president or CEO and is making all of the major decisions for the business.

独资企业通常会随着业务的发展而改变所有权结构。例如，如果小型企业需要资金扩张，独资经营者可能会决定将其初创公司的部分股份出售给投资者以换取现金。这些投资者现在可能会希望对公司的运营方式发表意见，以此提升自己在公司中的股权价值。或者，企业也可能直接被出售给其员工。因此，员工也同样关心企业的经营状况。

<!--en-->
Sole proprietorships often change ownership structure as the business becomes more successful. For instance, if the small business needs money to expand, the sole owner may decide to sell a stake in his or her fledgling company to investors in return for the cash. These investors now may want a say in how the company operates so as to boost the value of their ownership in the company. Or a business may actually sell itself to its employees. Thus, the employees have a vested interest in how the business performs as well.

会计事务所普华永道近期针对私营企业开展的一项研究显示，典型的私营企业拥有约200名员工，年度收入约为4700万美元。对于小镇上的记者来说，普通的小型或私营企业可能没有这么大规模，不过大城市的私营企业规模可能会更大。

<!--en-->
A recent study on private businesses by accounting firm PricewaterhouseCoopers discovered that the typical private company has about 200 employees and annual revenues of about $47 million. For a reporter in a small town, the average small or private company may not be that big. Private companies in larger cities may be much bigger than that, however.

在普华永道的调查中，大约一半的私营企业属于封闭式公司，即这类企业的股东数量很少，通常不超过50人。这类企业的股票也没有现成的市场，而且大多数股东都积极参与公司的管理。

<!--en-->
About half of the private companies in the PricewaterhouseCoopers survey were close corporations, meaning that the businesses only have a small number of shareholders, usually no more than 50. These businesses also have no ready market for the corporation's stock, and a majority of the shareholders are active in the management of these corporations.

### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《新奥尔良时代-皮卡尤恩报》商业版编辑金·奎伦关于报道小型及私营企业的经验：

<!--en-->
New Orleans Times-Picayune business editor Kim Quillen on covering small and private companies:

**请告诉我这家公司是如何创立的：** 这是我最喜欢的关于小型企业主的问题之一。通常，背后都有一个有趣的故事等待讲述。而企业主们往往会因为您表现出的兴趣而感到受宠若惊。这是我用来打破紧张氛围、与焦虑的企业主展开对话的首选问题。242 • 规模虽小，新闻价值却大。调查显示，约40%的私营企业属于所谓的S类公司，这类公司享有公司注册带来的好处，同时避免了双重征税——即公司的利润先作为公司收入征税，然后再作为公司股东的个人收入征税。S类公司的股东人数不得超过100人。

<!--en-->
**Tell me about how this company got started:** That's one of my favorite questions for small business people. More often than not, there's an interesting tale waiting to be told. And small business people are usually flattered by the interest you're expressing. That's my go-to question for breaking the ice with a nervous business owner and getting the conversation going.
242 • Small in Size, Large for News
The survey found that about 40 percent of the private businesses are what are called S corporations, which provide the benefits of incorporation but eliminate double taxation, which can occur when the profits of a company are taxed as a corporation and then as income for the shareholders of the corporation. An S corporation is limited to no more than 100 shareholders.

调查还发现，约4%的私营企业为合伙制企业，如有限责任公司。这种企业结构能为合伙人提供有限责任，同时像合伙企业一样缴税，从而避免双重征税。这类企业多为律师事务所或会计事务所。另外约3%的私营企业为个体经营企业，即只有单一的所有者。

<!--en-->
The survey also found that about 4 percent of private businesses were partnerships, such as limited liability corporations. This business structure provides limited liability to the members and also pays taxes like it is a partnership, eliminating double taxation. These businesses are often law firms or accounting businesses. And about 3 percent of private businesses are sole proprietors, meaning there is just one owner of the company.

其他小型私营企业则采用员工持股计划（ESOP）这一策略，将公司股权分配给员工。目前约有11,500家企业实施了ESOP计划，覆盖超过1000万名员工，约占私营部门劳动力的10%。

<!--en-->
Other small and private businesses take the strategy of offering ownership in the company to employees through a program called employee stock ownership plans, or an ESOP. About 11,500 companies now have ESOPs covering more than 10 million employees, or about 10 percent of the private sector workforce.

员工可以通过多种方式获得ESOP计划中的股票。他们可以直接购买股票，也可以作为奖金获得股票；此外还可以通过利润分享计划获得股票，在该计划中公司的利润会在股东之间分配。

<!--en-->
Employees can receive stock in an ESOP in a variety of ways. They can purchase the stock directly or be given the stock as a bonus. They can also obtain stock through a profit sharing plan in which the profits of the company are divided up among shareholders.

私营企业普遍使用ESOP计划，以便让所有者出售其持有的公司股份，同时激励剩余的员工。在几乎所有的ESOP计划中，21岁以上的所有全职员工都会参与该计划。他们根据薪资水平或其他计算公式获得公司股票。员工将在5到7年的时间内逐步拥有这些股票——即实现股权归属。如果员工离职，企业会根据外部对股票的估值买回这些股票。有时这种估值可由企业自身或员工提供。

<!--en-->
ESOPs are commonly used by private companies to allow the owners to sell their stake in the company and to motivate their remaining employees at the same time. In almost every ESOP, all full-time workers above the age of 21 participate in the plan. They receive stock in the company on the basis of their pay rate or another formula. Employees are then vested—which means they then own the stock—within a five- to seven-year time frame. If an employee leaves the company, then the business buys back the stock on the basis of an outside valuation of the shares. Sometimes this valuation can be obtained from the company or from employees.

ESOP计划的初衷是鼓励员工为企业的最佳利益着想，但实际情况并非总是如此。有些ESOP计划未能帮助陷入困境的公司扭转局面。1994年至2000年间，联合航空公司的员工为了换取总计48亿美元的薪资和福利削减，获得了其母公司55%的股份。但批评者指出，该ESOP计划最终失败是因为它排除了空乘人员，且不允许持有股票的员工投票选举董事；此外2000年后加入公司的员工根本无法加入ESOP计划，这导致了员工之间的分歧。不过，也有成功的ESOP案例。床垫公司Simmons曾由ESOP计划持有大部分股份长达十年，之后才以盈利价格出售给其他投资者。对于私营企业而言，ESOP结构的风险在于员工将所有退休保障都寄托在这一项上。如果公司经营不善开始亏损，该计划中的股票价值就会下降，就像上市公司业绩不佳时华尔街的股票价值会下跌一样。

<!--en-->
ESOPs are designed to encourage employees to consider the best interests of the business, but that is not always how it works. Some ESOPs have failed to turn struggling companies around. Between 1994 and 2000, workers at United Airlines accumulated 55 percent of the stock in its parent company in exchange for pay and benefit cuts totaling $4.8 billion. But critics say that the ESOP eventually failed because it excluded the flight attendants and did not allow employees who owned the stock to vote for directors. And employees who joined the company after 2000 were not allowed to join the ESOP at all, which created a rift between employees. But, other ESOPs have been successful. Simmons, the mattress company, was majority owned by an ESOP for a decade before selling to other investors for a profit. The risk of an ESOP structure to a private business is that the employees are putting all of their retirement eggs in one basket. If the company should struggle and begin to lose money, then the value of the stock in the plan will go down, just as the value of stocks traded on Wall Street declines when a public company performs badly.

以下故事展示了私营企业的所有权结构如何发生变化以及变化背后的原因。

<!--en-->
The following story illustrates how the ownership structure of a private company can change and the causes behind that change.

Alion Science and Technology Corp.昨日表示，其员工利用自己的退休基金中的1.3亿美元从伊利诺伊理工学院手中买下了该公司，从而创建了一家独立的国防承包商。规模虽小，新闻价值却大 • 243 总部位于麦克莱恩的Alion公司拥有1,650名员工，曾为五角大楼提供军事战略咨询，还为士兵使用新武器时的训练开发了建模软件。

<!--en-->
Alion Science and Technology Corp. said yesterday that its employees bought the company from the Illinois Institute of Technology, using$130 million from their retirement funds to create an independent defense contractor.
Small in Size, Large for News • 243
McLean-based Alion, with 1,650 employees, has been a consultant to the Pentagon on military strategy and has developed modeling software for soldiers training on new weapons.

公司高管称，所有权的变更将使Alion在日益激烈的市场竞争中更具优势，因为它能留住优秀人才，而竞争对手包括Science Applications International Corp.和Booz Allen Hamilton Inc.等行业巨头。

<!--en-->
Company executives said the change in ownership will give Alion an edge in keeping talented employees in an increasingly competitive market where it faces industry giants such as Science Applications International Corp. and Booz Allen Hamilton Inc.

“当IIT的教授们在经济大萧条时期创办这家企业时，那可是研发领域的另一个时代，”Alion公司总裁Bahman Atefi说道。

<!--en-->
"When IIT professors launched this venture during the Depression, it was a different era in research and development," said Bahman Atefi, president of Alion.

“如今，研发资金和人才的竞争异常激烈。为了避免让一些核心人才流失到私营企业，我们自己转变为私营营利企业至关重要，这样才能留住最优秀的人才。”

<!--en-->
"Nowadays, competition for R&D dollars and people is fierce. Rather than face losing some of our key people to private companies, it's critical that we ourselves become private and for-profit, as a way to retain the best and brightest."

Alion的科技系统部门经理巴里·沃森表示，该公司将放弃非营利性质，通过股票激励那些拥有军事经验或科研背景的员工。

<!--en-->
Alion, shedding its nonprofit status, will use stock to lure employees with military experience or a scientific and research background, said Barry Watson, Alion's technology systems sector manager.

沃森称，由于2001年9月11日的袭击，多个项目的工作量增加，该公司去年加快了招聘速度。Alion最近还获得了国防部的合同，负责开发与化学和生物武器、军控以及国土防御相关的技术。

<!--en-->
The company accelerated hiring last year when work on several projects stepped up because of the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks. Alion recently won a Defense Department contract to develop technology concerning chemical and biological weapons, arms control, and homeland defense, Watson said.

他说，该公司目前有大约100个职位空缺。

<!--en-->
The company has about 100 job openings, he said.

在大部分发展历程中，这家公司名为IIT研究机构，业务主要面向政府。随着新所有权的出现，该公司更名并将总部迁至弗吉尼亚州北部，那里它已设有办事处多年。

<!--en-->
For most of its history the company was known as IIT Research Institute and did most of its business with the government. With the new ownership, the company changed its name and moved its headquarters to Northern Virginia, where it had offices for several years.

其他几家大型国防承包商也是员工持股的企业，包括雷斯顿的DynCorp和SAIC。计算机科学公司计划以9.5亿美元的现金和股票收购DynCorp。

<!--en-->
Several other major defense contractors are employee-owned, including Reston's DynCorp and SAIC. Computer Sciences Corp. plans to buy DynCorp for $950 million in cash and stock.

沃森表示，处理这笔交易的律师们未能找到另一例由大学创建的非营利实体转变为私人员工持股公司的案例。Alion在2002财年的营收为2.01亿美元，利润为470万美元。

<!--en-->
Lawyers working on the deal could not find another instance of a nonprofit entity created by a university becoming a private, employee-owned company, Watson said. Alion reported $201 million in revenue during fiscal 2002 and $4.7 million in profit.

Alion的一位发言人称，该公司超过20%的营收来自与国防部签订的一份合同，该合同要求其在安纳波利斯运营一处设施，为该部门管理无线服务，包括为通信寻找可用频率。

<!--en-->
More than 20 percent of its revenue is from a single contract with the Defense Department to run an Annapolis facility that manages wireless service for the agency, including finding available frequencies for communications, an Alion spokesman said.

根据美国证券交易委员会的文件，15%的营收来自为军方开发建模与仿真软件的合同。

<!--en-->
Fifteen percent of revenue is from a contract to develop modeling and simulation software for the military, according to a Securities and Exchange Commission filing.

芝加哥伊利诺伊理工学院的校长卢·科伦斯表示，对于该校而言，这次出售能为学校的捐赠基金提供资金，而在交易前该基金的规模为1.5亿美元。科伦斯还说，交易还包括一份价值1亿美元的认股权证，如果Alion达到某些财务目标，该校可在五年后行使该权利。

<!--en-->
For the Illinois Institute of Technology, the sale provides money for its endowment, which stood at $150 million before the deal, said Lew Collens, the Chicago university's president. The deal also includes a warrant, worth $100 million, that the university could exercise in five years if Alion meets certain financial goals, Collens said.

科伦斯说：“我们讨论过是直接出售还是卖给员工。我们的董事会认为应该优先让员工获得股权。”² 244 • 规模虽小，新闻价值巨大 尽管买卖双方都不是上市公司，但这项收购的价值仍被公开披露。不过，交易文件并未说明哪些员工将成为最大股东。

<!--en-->
"We talked about whether to sell it outright or to sell it to employees,"Collens said. “Our trustees thought we should give first crack to the employees,” he said.²
244 • Small in Size, Large for News
The value of this acquisition is disclosed, even though neither the seller nor the buyer is a public company. Still, the transaction does not say who among the employees will be the largest shareholder.

所有权结构的变动，比如从非营利企业转变为营利企业，值得更仔细地审视。有些企业在长期按某种方式运营后，难以实现这种转变。近年来，许多企业从由客户持有所有权转变为由股东持有所有权。这种变化在保险和银行业最为常见，那些原本由储户和保单持有人拥有的储蓄贷款机构和保险公司已转为股份制结构。

<!--en-->
Changes in ownership structure, such as a shift from a nonprofit company to a for-profit business, merit closer scrutiny. Some businesses have trouble making the change after running themselves a certain way for so long. Many businesses made the switch in recent years from being owned by customers to being owned by stockholders. This change has occurred most commonly in the insurance and banking industries, where savings and loans and insurance companies that were owned by their depositors and their policyholders have converted to a stock ownership structure.

这些储蓄贷款机构和保险公司以前被称为互助公司。互助公司是指客户拥有股权且为公司利益而运营的公司。但如果客户终止保险合约或从银行提取资金，其股权就会消失。全美一些最大的公司就是互助公司，例如State Farm和Northwestern Mutual。21世纪的最初几年，许多储蓄贷款机构从互助公司结构转变为上市公司结构。在这种转变中，储户会获得该上市公司的股票。

<!--en-->
These thrifts and insurers were previously known as mutual companies. A mutual company is one in which the customers have an ownership interest and which is operated for the benefit of the customers. But their ownership ends if they should terminate their insurance policy or withdraw their money from the bank. Some of the largest companies in the country are mutuals, including State Farm and Northwestern Mutual. In the first few years of the twenty-first century, many thrifts converted from a mutual company structure to a public company structure. In such a conversion, the depositors are offered stock in the public company.

包括MetLife、John Hancock和Prudential在内的许多大型保险公司也经历了从互助结构向股份结构的转变。作为转变的一部分，它们向保单持有人分发了新公司的数百万股股票。这类转变需要得到州监管机构的批准，流程可能相当漫长。

<!--en-->
Many of the largest insurance companies, including MetLife, John Hancock, and Prudential, have also converted from a mutual structure. As part of the conversion, they distributed millions of shares of the new company to their policyholders. These conversions are approved by state regulators, and the process can be lengthy.

许多小型私营企业拥有独特的结构，其运营状况与一家规模更大的公司紧密相连。这些较小的企业被称为特许经营商。特许经营商是通过与已有产品或服务可销售的特许经营企业签订合同关系而成立的。随后，特许经营商在特许品牌的名下开展业务，通常会在该品牌的指导下运作，并为此支付费用。

<!--en-->
A number of small and private businesses have a unique structure in which their performance is tied to a much larger company. These smaller businesses are called franchisees. A franchisee is formed by entering into a contractual relationship with a franchise business that already has a product or a service to sell. The franchisee then operates under the trade name of the franchise, often with its guidance, in exchange for a fee.

特许经营商可以有多种形式。它们主要出现在麦当劳和汉堡王等快餐行业，不过需要注意的是，这些公司有时也会经营自己拥有的门店。特许经营商大多为私营企业，但也有一些是上市公司。位于阿拉巴马州伯明翰的帕帕约翰披萨店经营者就是一个例子：它曾是一家上市公司，如今已转为私营企业。

<!--en-->
Franchisees can take different shapes and forms. They are predominantly used in industries such as fast food for companies such as McDonald’s and Burger King, although it should be noted that these companies sometimes also operate locations that they own themselves. Franchisees are predominantly privately held businesses, although there are some franchise operations that are publicly traded. A Papa John’s pizza store operator, based in Birmingham, Alabama, is an example of a franchisee that was at one time publicly traded but is now a private company.

运营特许经营业务需要业主预先投入一笔资金。麦当劳估计，开设一家新餐厅的成本在461,000美元到788,500美元之间，且所有新餐厅都需要向麦当劳支付45,000美元的初始费用。开设麦当劳特许店的最低现金投资额为175,000美元，其余费用可通过贷款支付。[^2676]：² 摘自R. Merle于2003年1月8日发表在《华盛顿邮报》E5版的文章《员工以1.3亿美元收购科技公司；总部位于弗吉尼亚州的Alion公司由伊利诺伊理工学院在经济大萧条时期创立》，版权归《华盛顿邮报》所有，经许可转载。Small in Size, Large for News • 245 麦当劳会购买该地块并建造建筑，之后由特许经营商负责为建筑配备厨房设备、座椅、标识以及进行景观美化。

<!--en-->
Running a franchise operation requires an up-front amount of money to bepaid by the owner. McDonald's has estimated that the cost of a new restaurant ranges between $461,000 and $788,500, and an initial fee of $45,000 is paid to McDonald's for all new restaurants. The initial cash investment for a McDonald's franchise is a minimum of $175,000. The rest of the expense can be paid with a loan.
[^2676]: ² From “Employees buy tech firm for $130 million; Va.-based Alion was Depression-era creation of Illinois Institute of Technology,” by R. Merle, January 8, 2003, *Washington Post*, p. E5. Copyright 2003 by *Washington Post*. Reprinted with permission.
Small in Size, Large for News • 245
McDonald's acquires the property for the location and builds the building. The franchisee is then responsible for equipping the building with the kitchen equipment, the seating, signs, and landscaping.

为什么特许经营业主会从事这类业务？首先，有关产品和运营的所有决策都已为他们做出，他们只需按照计划运营企业来盈利即可。

<!--en-->
Why do franchise owners go into such business operations? For one, all of the decisions about products and operation have been made for them. All they have to do is run the business, executing the plan, to make money.

对于报道大型企业的记者而言，特许经营商可以是重要的信息来源。总公司将做出的某些决定可能会影响到特许经营商，令其不满。有时，特许经营商也会反抗大公司，迫使对方做出改变。

<!--en-->
Franchisees can be important sources for reporters covering the larger company. The parent may make decisions that affect the franchisees, upsetting the franchise owners. Sometimes, the franchisees may revolt against the bigger company and force it to make changes.

根据国际特许经营协会的数据，该国拥有超过909,000家特许经营门店，为经济创造了1100万个就业岗位。特许经营业务受联邦贸易委员会监管，部分州也出台了相关的特许经营法律。这些法律大多旨在保护特许经营商，要求特许权授予方披露与业务相关的成本，并对业务的盈利潜力进行公正评估。

<!--en-->
According to the International Franchise Association, there are more than 909,000 franchise locations in the country, and they provide 11 million jobs to the economy. Franchising is regulated by the Federal Trade Commission, and some states have also passed franchising laws. Many of them are designed to protect the franchisee, requiring the franchisor to disclose the costs associated with the business and make fair assessments of the earnings potential of the business.

一旦记者了解了所报道的中小型或私营企业的结构，就会产生一些问题。例如，如果这是一家为推动发展而向投资者出售部分股权的私营企业，它打算如何在不亏损的情况下管理这种增长？如果增长顺利，该公司计划发展到多大规模？如果是特许经营商，它是否有计划增加更多门店？如果是互助型企业，它是否考虑调整其结构？在某些情况下，这类中小型或私营企业的结构本身就可以成为报道的主题。

<!--en-->
Once a reporter knows the structure of the small or private business he or she is reporting about, some questions should emerge. For example, if it is a private company that has sold a stake to an investor to help fuel growth, how does it plan to manage that growth without losing money? If the growth is successful, how big does the company plan to get? If the business is a franchisee, does it have plans to add more locations to the business? If the business is a mutual company, is it considering changing its structure? In some of these cases, the structure of the small or private business may be the story.

#### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《新奥尔良时代-皮卡尤恩报》商业版编辑Kim Quillen关于报道中小型及私营企业的建议：

<!--en-->
New Orleans Times-Picayune business editor Kim Quillen on covering small and private companies:

**请求安排一次面对面的背景介绍会：** 如果你知道自己将会定期报道某家私营或小型企业，可以请求安排时间去见该企业的最高管理层，了解企业情况，甚至参观其设施。在没有突发新闻的时候，企业会更愿意接待你，而你也能将收集到的背景信息用于后续的报道。

<!--en-->
**Ask for a sit-down backgrounding session:** If there's a private or small company that you know you'll be covering regularly, ask for a time to go in and meet the top executive, get briefed on the company, and maybe even tour the facility. The firm will be much more receptive to having you over when news isn't breaking, and you'll be able to use the background you gather for future stories.

#### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《新奥尔良时代-皮卡尤恩报》商业版编辑Kim Quillen关于报道中小型及私营企业的建议：

<!--en-->
New Orleans Times-Picayune business editor Kim Quillen on covering small and private companies:

**让企业简介具有独特性：** 在撰写关于某家企业的专题报道时，试着从该企业克服的障碍或正在应对的问题出发进行描述。通常找到某个新闻点作为专题报道的切入点，能写出更好的文章。

<!--en-->
**Keep business profiles unique:** When doing a feature on a business, try to write about it in the context of an obstacle the firm has overcome or an issue it is grappling with. Finding some sort of news to peg the feature story to usually makes for a better article.

### 对私营或小型企业的报道

<!--en-->
*Profiling a Private or Small Business*

媒体机构经常会针对小型或私营企业进行报道。这类报道看似无害，往往被写成赞美的正面文章，讲述企业如何凭借产品或服务实现繁荣。很多时候，这类文章读起来就像广告软文，其实是企业本应付费让报纸刊登的内容。

<!--en-->
Many times a media outlet will profile a small or private business. These stories may seem innocuous, and they are often written as flattering, positive stories that tell the story of how a business is thriving because of its products or its services. Many times, these stories can read like advertorials, copy that the business should have probably paid the newspaper to run.

不过，关于中小型及私营企业的报道并不一定非得如此。就像20世纪90年代那些争相报道最新上市并让员工成为百万富翁的互联网公司的商业记者一样，许多报道中小型及私营企业的记者也没有做到应有的批判性。

<!--en-->
Profiles of small and private businesses, however, do not always have to be this way. Like the business reporters who fell over themselves in the 1990s writing about the latest Internet company to go public and make millionaires of its workers, many reporters writing stories about small and private businesses are not as critical as they can and should be.

报道小型私营企业时应反映当地经济状况。如果某镇因一家工厂关闭导致400名工人失业，从而使当地经济恶化，那么那些依赖这些工人消费其商品和服务的周边小型企业也会受到影响。情况不佳时，记者不应粉饰事实。246 • 规模虽小，新闻价值却大

<!--en-->
Writing about small and private businesses should reflect the local economy. If the economy is going bad in a town because a plant has closed, putting 400 workers out of jobs, then that is going to affect the surrounding small businesses that depend on these workers to spend part of their income buying their goods and services. If things are not going well, the reporter should not sugarcoat it. If a
246 • Small in Size, Large for News

#### 专家建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《新奥尔良时报-皮卡尤恩报》商业版编辑Kim Quillen关于报道小型私营企业的观点：

<!--en-->
New Orleans Times-Picayune business editor Kim Quillen on covering small and private companies:

影响类报道：州级及国家层面的立法与经济变化会对小型企业产生重大影响。最低工资上涨、汽油价格攀升以及税法变动只是其中的几个例子。需密切关注这些重大问题，或许能从中挖掘出有关小型企业受影响的报道。如果某个特定行业正面临困境，记者不应轻信该行业某位企业主所说的“我们这季的生意从未这么好过”之类的话，因为他很可能在撒谎。

<!--en-->
Impact stories: State and national legislative and economic changes can have a significant impact on smaller businesses. Increases in the minimum wage, climbing gasoline prices, and tax law changes are just a few examples. Keep an eye on these larger issues. You may be able to mine small business impact stories from them.
particular industry is suffering, reporters should not buy the story that one small business owner in that industry is telling them when he or she remarks, “We’ve never had a better season.” He or she is probably lying.

《彼得斯堡先驱报》（阿拉斯加）在2002年6月20日的报道中，直截了当地描述了当地鲑鱼渔业的困境：

<!--en-->
The following lead from the *Petersburg* (Alaska) *Pilot*, which focused on the struggles of local salmon fisheries in its June 20, 2002, paper, did not mince words:

一波又一波的不利预测正在冲击阿拉斯加的鲑鱼渔业，渔民和加工商们正在拼命寻找那片能带来奇迹的捕鱼区域。并非是返捕的鱼类数量不足导致了这一问题，而是不断上涨的价格让独立渔民们无力继续从事渔业。

<!--en-->
Wave after wave of bad forecasts are rocking Alaska’s salmon fishery as fishermen and processors scramble for that miracle seasick curing patch. The amount of fish not returning is not enough to cause this nausea; the price heaved at the independent fisherman, however, leaves them weak-kneed with sea legs.

Icicle Seafood公司的John Baird评论道：“所有品种的价格都在下降。罐装鲑鱼的供应量过多，养殖鲑鱼也在挤压我们的冷冻产品市场，而且最近欧洲国家还禁止中国产鱼类进入欧洲市场。红鲑鱼籽的市场行情也很糟糕，预计价格将低于去年，而且不太可能有太大变化。”

<!--en-->
“Price on all species is down,” commented Icicle Seafood’s John Baird. “There’s oversupplies of canned salmon. Farmed salmon are cutting into our frozen stuff, and recently the European countries have put a ban on Chinese-bought fish into the European market. The Ikura market for chum roe is off and is expected to start at less than last year, there’s no reason to think that will change much.”

州议会代表Peggy Wilson在最近访问彼得斯堡时表示：“我从渔民那里听到的最大担忧就是价格问题。许可证当初是以极高的价格卖出的，但现在其价值甚至不到当初的一半。传统上，各个渔具群体都有自己的问题，现在他们正试图团结起来共同解决这些问题。鲑鱼专项工作组可能是最好的解决办法，但目前仍处于待定状态。”

<!--en-->
“Prices are the biggest concern I have heard from fishermen,” commented State House Representative Peggy Wilson on a recent stop in Petersburg. “Permits were bought at an outlandish price and they are not worth even half that now. Traditionally, all gear groups have had their own problems. Now they are trying to come together and solve one. The salmon task force is probably going to be our best bet, but it’s in limbo right now.”

今年夏天，东南部的渔民可能会捕获2500万到3600万条粉鲑。全州的捕获量预计为8700万条，低于五年平均水平的1.04亿条。

<!--en-->
Southeast crews could harvest 25 to 36 million pink salmon this summer. The statewide harvest is believed to be 87 million, down from a five-year average of 104 million.

NorQuest工厂的经理Dave Ohmer说道：“今年鲑鱼洄游的基数并不大。去年是个丰收年，但今年可能不会出现那样的情况。当前的价格反映了去年遗留的大量供应以及去年的市场状况。”

<!--en-->
Said NorQuest plant manager Dave Ohmer, “The parent year for the run coming in this year is not very large. Last year was a huge year, that may not present itself this season. The price is reflective of the huge supply left from last year and the results of the market place from last year.”

红鲑的捕获量可能是24年来最少的。黑鲑的预计捕获量比2001年减少了15%，而银鲑的预计捕获量则与去年持平。帝王鲑的配额实际上还有所上调。³报道小型私营企业的原因有很多。也许这家企业是该城镇的新企业且独具特色，也许它与其他企业存在矛盾，也许它发展迅速并雇佣了大量当地员工，又或者它正处于困境之中，可能六个月后就会倒闭。

<!--en-->
The sockeye harvest might be the smallest in 24 years. Chum projection catches are down 15 percent from 2001 and coho catch predictions are consistent with last year. The King salmon quota has actually been revised upward.³
Stories about small and private businesses are reported for a number of reasons. Maybe the business is new to the town or city and is unique. Maybe the company is in conflict with another company. Maybe the business is fast-growing and adding many local employees. Or maybe the business is struggling and may not be around in six months.

无论出于何种原因，记者在报道大型企业时都应采用同样的方式来关注小型私营企业。这些企业对读者和观众而言同样重要，而且由于报道的对象可能是鲜为人知的企业，因此文章很可能会吸引那些此前从未听说过该企业的读者前来了解。此外，记者在文章写完后也不应忽视这些企业——它们或许正走向更大的知名度或负面声誉，而记者自然希望能在第一时间进行报道。试想，如果你是一名驻在人口约15,000人的小镇的记者：几年前，镇中心开了一家制作松露及其他特色甜点的巧克力店。记者写了一篇简短的文章后便将其抛诸脑后。直到某天早上，这位记者走进新闻编辑室，发现那家巧克力店登上了《华尔街日报》的头版。如今，这家店因其美味的甜点而闻名全球，由于需求旺盛，甚至无法满足情人节期间的订单量。店主希望扩大规模，但却无能为力，因为一天中的时间根本不够用来生产所需数量的松露。[^2707]：³摘自K. Stolpe所著《鲑鱼渔业面临危机》，2002年6月20日，《彼得斯堡导报》，第1–2页。版权所有2002年Pilot Publishing，经许可转载。规模虽小，新闻价值巨大 • 247 也许是因为当地记者没有与店主保持联系，也没有定期去店里与员工交谈，所以当地报纸才会在全国性大媒体之前错过这篇精彩的报道。

<!--en-->
Whatever the reason, reporters should think about small and private businessesthe same way they think about larger and public businesses. These companies are just as important to the reader and viewer, and because the stories are being written about a business that probably has not had much exposure, the piece will probably have readers wanting to learn about a company they have not heard about before. In addition, reporters should not forget about these businesses after the story has been written. They could just be headed for bigger fame or notoriety, and journalists will want to be there to report it. Imagine being a reporter in a small town of about 15,000 people. A few years ago, a chocolate shop opened downtown making truffles and other exotic desserts. The reporter wrote a short story about the shop, and afterward forgot about it. Then, one morning, that same reporter walks into the newsroom to discover that the chocolate shop is on the front page of *The Wall Street Journal*. It is now famous around the world because of its delicious sweets and cannot keep up with its orders for Valentine's Day because of the demand. The owner would like to expand, but he cannot because there are not enough hours in the day to make as many truffles as he needs.
[^2707]: ³ From “Storm on the horizon for salmon fisheries,” by K. Stolpe, June 20, 2002, *Petersburg Pilot*, pp. 1–2. Copyright 2002 by Pilot Publishing. Reprinted with permission.
Small in Size, Large for News • 247
Perhaps the local newspaper did not have that story before the large, national media because the local reporter did not keep in touch with the storeowner or check in regularly just by walking into the store and chatting with the employees. As a result, a great story was missed.

以下导语来自北卡罗来纳州达勒姆市的《先驱太阳报》，该报曾在美国商业编辑与作家协会的比赛中获得第一名。这篇报道虽然讲述的是一家私营企业，但其细节描写使得文章读起来仿佛这是一家上市公司。在得知该公司拖欠债券评级机构贷款的消息后，记者进一步调查，发现其问题比最初披露的更为严重。凭借从债券评级机构获得的消息，他成功获得了多方采访，从而展现了问题的严重程度。

<!--en-->
The following lead is from the *Herald-Sun* in Durham, North Carolina, which won first place in a Society of American Business Editors and Writers contest. It is about a private company, but the detail makes the story read as if the business was publicly traded. The reporter followed up on the disclosure that the company was delinquent in paying its loans from a bond-rating agency to discover there were even more troubles than had been disclosed. Armed with the bond-rating agency information, he was able to garner interviews that showed just how serious the problems were.

曾迅速发展成全美第二大私营便利店连锁店的总部位于达勒姆的Swifty Serve Corp.如今正在为生存而挣扎。

<!--en-->
After rapidly growing into the nation's second-largest privately owned convenience store chain, Durham-based Swifty Serve Corp. is fighting for its life.

这家连锁店曾在美国东南部拥有超过600家门店，但在努力应对亏损门店带来的资金压力之际，已关闭了70到100家分店，并裁掉了约1,000名员工。

<!--en-->
The chain, which at one time had more than 600 stores throughout the Southeast, has closed between 70 and 100 locations and cut about 1,000 jobs as it fights the red ink flowing from money-losing stores.

和整个便利店行业一样，Swifty Serve也因汽油销售利润空间缩小以及作为便利店核心业务之一的香烟销量下降而遭受重创。

<!--en-->
Swifty Serve, like the rest of the convenience store industry, has been hit hard by a shrinking profit margin on gas sales and dropping cigarette sales—two of the core businesses of convenience stores.

这家成立仅5年的公司正在与贷款方商谈，以筹集资金实施重组计划，但该公司4月上任的总裁兼首席执行官、前7-Eleven高管杰夫·哈米尔表示，相关问题“必须在几周内解决，而非几个月”。

<!--en-->
The 5-year-old company is talking with lenders to help finance a plan for remaking Swifty Serve, but something has to be resolved “in weeks, not months,” said Jeff Hamill, a former 7-Eleven executive who became the company's president and CEO in April.

哈米尔在位于希兰代尔路的公司总部表示：“如果问题无法解决，我不知道最终会是破产还是需要做出更多调整。”

<!--en-->
If something can't be worked out, “I don't know if it's bankruptcy or additional changes we'll have to make,” Hamill said from the company's headquarters on Hillandale Road.

达勒姆的开发商W. Clay Hamner于1997年与其长期商业伙伴韦恩·罗杰斯一起创立了Swifty Serve连锁店。Hamner最为人熟知的是他在Treyburn住宅开发项目中所扮演的主角角色。

<!--en-->
Durham developer W. Clay Hamner started building the Swifty Serve chain in 1997 with his longtime business partner, Wayne Rogers. Hamner is best known for playing a lead role in the Treyburn residential development

#### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《新奥尔良时代-皮卡尤恩报》的商业编辑Kim Quillen关于报道小型私营企业的建议：

<!--en-->
New Orleans Times-Picayune business editor Kim Quillen on covering small and private companies:

**明确报道对象：**小型私营企业是一个涵盖范围极广的类别，其中可能包括各种不同类型的企业——从拥有数十艘船只的家族式海运公司，到高科技初创企业，再到仅有两名员工的美发沙龙。务必了解你所报道的中小企业群体究竟由哪些类型的企业组成，这样才能确保报道的准确性与全面性。248 • 规模虽小，新闻价值巨大

<!--en-->
**Know who you're covering:** Small, private business is a broad category that can include many different types of firms, from family-run maritime firms with dozens of vessels to high-tech startups and hair salons with two employees. Make sure you understand what type of firms your small business community is comprised so that your coverage is accurate and inclusive.
248 • Small in Size, Large for News

#### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《新奥尔良时代-皮卡尤恩报》的商业编辑Kim Quillen关于报道小型私营企业的建议：

<!--en-->
New Orleans Times-Picayune business editor Kim Quillen on covering small and private companies:

寻找您所在社区中的小型企业专家：各地的中小企业管理局办公室及小型企业发展中心都配有专门负责日常为小型企业提供服务的人员。这些专家能够帮助识别小型企业的趋势与问题，其中一些问题或许可以转化为新闻素材。而罗杰斯则是电视剧《M*A*S*H》中饰演“捕兽人约翰”的演员。⁴ 在故事的后半部分，这家公司的首席执行官称其为“绝佳的机会”，企业主也对管理团队“充满信心”。然而，通过这个故事，读者仍能清晰地感受到，由于行业变化影响了其经营状况，这家便利店连锁店正面临困境。该故事并未使用任何具体的营收、利润（或亏损）数据来详细描述这些问题，而是通过有力的叙述说明了竞争对手如何在价格上压低其成本，并建造规模更大的店铺。即便没有具体数字，作者也能凭借所引用的言论以及评级机构提供的那一个关于逾期贷款的数字，论证该公司确实处于困境之中。

<!--en-->
Find the small business experts in your community: Local Small Business Administration offices and small business development centers are staffed with people who work with small firms on a daily basis. These experts can help pinpoint small business trends and issues, some of which you may be able to develop into stories.
and the retail center Brightleaf Square while Rogers is the actor who played Trapper John in the television series M*A*S*H.⁴
Later in the story, the CEO of this company calls the company a “tremendous opportunity” and the owner of the business is “confident” of the management team. Yet, the reader of this story gets a vivid picture that this convenience store chain is in trouble because of changes in the industry that have affected its performance. This story does not use any specific figures for revenues and profits (or losses) to detail the trouble but cogently explains how competitors are undercutting it in pricing and building bigger stores. Even without the numbers, the writer is able to make a case that the business is in trouble on the basis of the quotes he uses—and the one single number he does have about the delinquent loans from the bond-rating agency.

其他媒体也能以同样的方式有效地报道小型企业和私营企业。科罗拉多州的《洛夫兰每日记者先驱报》聚焦于航空公司宣布取消佣金后当地旅行社所面临的问题。加利福尼亚州的《羚羊谷新闻报》则将当地的职业棒球小联盟球队视为一家企业而非单纯的体育项目，报道了兰开斯特喷鹰队如何努力提升上座率。尽管该球队没有给出任何数据，但记者还是能够引用球队内部人士的话，表明球队在前一年出现了亏损。

<!--en-->
Other media are able to effectively report about small and private businesses the same way. The *Loveland Daily Reporter-Herald* in Colorado focused on the problems its local travel agencies were having after airlines announced they were eliminating commissions. The *Antelope Valley Press* in California focused on the local minor league baseball team not as a sport but as a business and wrote about how the Lancaster JetHawks were trying to boost attendance. Although the team did not cite any numbers, the reporter was able to quote a source within the organization saying that the team had lost money the previous year.

在撰写小型企业和私营企业的报道时，记者应将其视为未来可能被出售、倒闭或上市的公司，因为上市后它们将进入公众视野。由于已有相关报道，记者所在的媒体机构便能拥有背景资料，从而更全面地报道该公司的后续动态。

<!--en-->
When writing profiles of small and private businesses, reporters should think of them as companies that might be sold, go out of business, or go public in the future, which would put them in the public eye. Because stories have already been written about the company, the reporter’s media outlet will have the background to cover future stories about the company more thoroughly.

像小型企业和私营企业这样的机构，希望在初创阶段吸引顾客时能有媒体报道。但当它们即将倒闭时，却很少希望受到关注。不过，这类报道依然重要，因为它们可能反映出整个城镇或地区的经济状况。如果一家商店无法在某个城镇生存下去，那对该地区其他类似商店的未来又意味着什么？

<!--en-->
Small and private businesses like the media to write stories about them when they are new and trying to attract customers. But rarely do they want the attention when they are going out of business. Still, these stories can also be important because they might reflect on the broader town or county economy. If a store could not make it in the town, what does that say about the future of similar stores in the area?

报道小型企业和私营企业时，记者往往需要重点关注企业的创始人或所有者。他们通常是掌控公司的人。如果没有这次采访，记者该转向何处呢？如果可能的话，他或她应该查明创始人的前工作单位。也许那里有人能够讲述他的工作习惯或商业理念。也有可能他是因被解雇或主动离职，才去创办竞争性企业。

<!--en-->
Reporting about small and private businesses often requires the journalist to focus on the founder or owner of the business. They are often the ones that control the company. Without that interview, though, where would a reporter turn? If possible, he or she should find out where the founder used to work. Maybe someone there can talk about his or her work habits or business ideas. Maybe he or she was fired or dismissed from the previous job or left the previous employer to start a competing business.

小型企业和私营企业的所有者通常为自己能从一个简单想法起步并建立起公司而感到自豪。他们中的许多人极为保护自己的企业，希望记者能够认识到他们为让企业成功或至少存活下来所付出的长时间努力与艰辛。如果企业主不愿接受采访，记者就必须理解他们为何犹豫。记者克服这种犹豫的一种方法，是让企业主看到他们理解建立企业过程中所经历的痛苦。这并不意味着报道内容必须是积极的。但在大多数关于小型企业和私营企业的报道中，阐述它们的创立过程以及能够持续运营至今的原因，始终是一个重要的切入点。[^2731]：⁴ 摘自J. Zimmer于2002年9月27日发表在《达勒姆先驱太阳报》A1版的文章《Swifty Serve Corp. is in fight for its life; Durham-based convenience store chain has closed stores, cut jobs》，版权归2002年达勒姆先驱公司所有，经许可转载。Small in Size, Large for News • 249 记者应毫不犹豫地请求获取信息。企业主或总裁只能回答“是”或“否”。记者必须向与所报道企业有业务往来的公司索要信件或其他文件。也许竞争对手手中就有能构成精彩报道的信件或文件。不妨参考《罗切斯特商业杂志》上以下这篇报道的开头：

<!--en-->
Small and private business owners are often proud of what they have accomplished in building a company from a simple idea. Many of them are extremely protective of their business and want a reporter to recognize the long hours and the tough times they put in to make the business successful, or at least survive. If a business owner is reluctant to give an interview, the reporter must understandwhy they are leery. One way for reporters to get past the hesitation is to let the business owner see that they recognize the pain that went into building the operation. That does not mean the story should be positive. But a good point to make in most profiles of small and private businesses is how they were started and how they have lasted as long as they have.
[^2731]: ⁴ From “Swifty Serve Corp. is in fight for its life; Durham-based convenience store chain has closed stores, cut jobs,” by J. Zimmer, September 27, 2002, *Durham Herald-Sun*, p. A1. Copyright 2002 by Durham Herald Company Inc. Reprinted with permission.
Small in Size, Large for News • 249
Reporters should not hesitate to ask for information. All the owner or president can say is “yes” or “no.” Reporters must ask for letters or other documents from companies that do business with the company they are reporting about. Maybe a competitor has a letter or document that would make a good story about the business. Consider the lead of the following story from the *Rochester Business Journal*:

一位Strong Health的高层管理人员声称，Excellus Inc.故意破坏重要的Strong Health计划，且仍在试图颠覆罗切斯特大学的医疗系统。

<!--en-->
Excellus Inc. deliberately has sabotaged important Strong Health initiatives and continues trying to subvert the University of Rochester’s health system, a top Strong Health executive claims.

据《罗切斯特商业杂志》获得的、日期为1月4日、寄给Excellus首席执行官霍华德·伯曼的信件，以及三周后伯曼的回信，反映出斯特朗与罗切斯特地区Blue Cross Blue Shield的母公司Excellus之间存在严重分歧。二者是该地区最强大的两家医疗保健机构。

<!--en-->
In a Jan. 4 letter to Excellus CEO Howard Berman, obtained by the Rochester Business Journal, and Berman’s reply three weeks later, reflect a massive rift between Strong and Excellus, the parent of Blue Cross Blue Shield of the Rochester area. They are the area’s two most powerful health care organizations.

伯曼的回信逐条反驳了斯特朗纪念医院及海兰德医院首席执行官史蒂文·戈尔茨坦在先前信件中提出的指控。他还提出与斯特朗方面的官员会面，以进一步讨论这些问题。⁵ 这篇报道涉及两家公司，但由于记者获得了第一封邮件，因此在被问及此事后CEO才提供了回信。由此可见，获取一份文件往往能引出另一份文件。

<!--en-->
Berman’s response letter contains a point-by-point refutation of the charges in the earlier missive from Steven Goldstein, Strong Memorial and Highland hospitals CEO. Berman also offered to meet with Strong officials to further discuss the issues.⁵
The story is about two private companies. But because the reporter was able to obtain the first letter, the CEO supplied the response letter after being questioned about it. That is how obtaining one document can lead to another.

撰写关于小型或私营企业的报道时，不应仅限于采访企业主或总裁。这样无法为读者或观众提供报道所需的平衡性与客观性。应考虑采访其他了解该企业情况的人，并寻找其他相关资料来源。将所有信息整合起来，才能写出呈现完整图景的报道。

<!--en-->
Writing a story about a small or private business should not just consist of interviewing the owner or the president of the company. That is not going to give the reader or the viewer the balance and objectivity that the story demands. Think of other people to interview that know the business and where other information about the company can be obtained. Putting all of the pieces together will make for a story that tells the complete picture.

## 建议练习

<!--en-->
*Suggested Exercises*

1. 在您所在的城市找一位小型企业主并进行访谈。询问他为何创业以及创业的初衷。看看他愿意透露多少关于企业的财务信息。如果他不愿公开营收和利润，那就询问是否有其他财务信息愿意透露，比如销售额或利润的增长情况。规模虽小，新闻价值却大 • 251
2. 记下您采访过的企业主所经营的小企业名称，然后到州务卿办公室及县法院的公共记录中查找该企业的相关信息。别忘了查看诉讼记录、UCC备案文件以及联邦档案。收集完信息后，把它们展示给企业主看。这样他是否会更愿意提供更多关于该企业的信息？
3. 许多小型企业依赖大学生。在您校园附近找几家这样的企业——餐厅、书店、酒吧、复印店——询问他们有多少业务来自大学生群体。这能告诉您您所在城镇的经济状况如何？
4. 询问班上的其他学生是否在小型企业有兼职工作。如果有，问问他们是否认识企业主以及企业主多久在工作一次。如果他们不认识企业主，那么经理或主管每天在店里工作多少小时？![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/28ea43c75649b559f3d457664e5f2bf5.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T071651Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=dad81d05341e7c3dc2ac5ee5c8d19c2cba01bb2024fde22f0455cd314ab6dee1)

<!--en-->
1. Find a small business owner in your city and conduct an interview. Ask him how he started his business and why. See how much financial information the owner is willing to disclose about the business. If he's not willing to disclose revenues and profits, then ask if there's any financial information that he will disclose, such as an increase in sales or profits.
Small in Size, Large for News • 251
2. Take the name of the small business whose owner you interviewed and search for information about the business in public records with the Secretary of State's office and at the county courthouse. Don't forget to check lawsuits, UCC filings, and federal records. After you've collected the information, go show the business owner the information. Is the owner now more forthcoming about providing additional information on the company?
3. Many small companies rely on college students. Find a handful of these businesses—restaurants, bookstores, bars, copy centers—near your campus and ask them what percentage of their business comes from college-age students. What does this tell you about the economy of the town or city in which you're living?
4. Ask other students in the class if they have part-time jobs at small businesses. If they do, ask them if they know the owner of the company and how often the owner works at the business. If they don't know the owner, how many hours does the manager or supervisor spend at the business?
