## 12

没有利润，但资金充裕

<!--en-->
No Profits, but Lots of Money

### 像营利企业一样运营

<!--en-->
*Operating Like a For-Profit Business*

迄今为止，本书一直忽略了商业世界中一个重要的群体——由于其独特的结构，这一群体往往很少被提及。但实际上，有成千上万的机构和其他组织以企业的模式运作，为公众提供商品或服务，它们既不属于上市公司，也不属于营利性私营企业。

<!--en-->
So far, this book has ignored an important segment of the business world, one that is often underreported because of its unique structure. But there are thousands of businesses and other organizations operating like businesses that offer goods or services to the public that are neither public companies nor for-profit private enterprises.

根据美国国税局（IRS）的分类，该国共有超过150万家机构被归为非营利组织。据国家慈善统计中心的数据，其中近50万家机构会向IRS提交财务披露报告，显示它们的总资产高达2.6万亿美元。加利福尼亚州的非营利组织数量最多，而纽约州的非营利组织拥有的资产规模则最大。

<!--en-->
There are more than 1.5 million entities in this country that are classified as nonprofit organizations by the Internal Revenue Service (IRS). Collectively, nearly a half million of them file financial disclosures with the IRS that show they have a total of $2.6 trillion in assets, according to the National Center for Charitable Statistics. California has the most nonprofit organizations, whereas New York's nonprofit organizations have the most reported assets.

这些非营利组织涵盖的范围极广，从全国基督教青年会联合会、美国红十字会、国际善意工业协会，到当地的托儿中心、无家可归者收容所、健康保险计划、社区医疗诊所、博物馆、医院、教堂、学校、表演艺术中心以及交流小组等。它们往往是某个城镇或社区中规模最大的组织，通常也拥有极大的影响力。在很多情况下，这些组织会与公共企业和私营企业展开竞争。例如，当地的基督教青年会就会与营利性的健身中心竞争，以吸引健身爱好者；像凯撒医疗集团这样的非营利管理式医疗计划，则会与西格纳和安泰等营利性公司竞争。由天主教团体运营的医院也会与那些价值数十亿美元的医院企业竞争。很多时候，营利性企业会抱怨称，这些非营利竞争对手利用其特殊地位压低价格、抢走业务。

<!--en-->
These nonprofit organizations include everything from the National Council of YMCAs, the American Red Cross, and Goodwill Industries International to local child care centers, homeless shelters, health insurance plans, community health care clinics, museums, hospitals, churches, schools, performing arts centers, and conversation groups. They are some of the largest organizations in a town or a community, and often they are some of the most powerful as well. In many cases, these organizations compete against public and private companies. The local YMCA, for example, competes with for-profit workout centers to attract fitness nuts. Nonprofit managed care plans such as Kaiser compete with for-profit companies such as CIGNA and Aetna. Hospitals run by Catholic groups compete against hospitals managed by multibillion-dollar hospital corporations. Many times, the for-profit companies will complain that their non-profit competitors are taking advantage of their status to undercut them and steal business.

非营利组织是为了实现特定目标而成立的法人实体，这些目标可能涉及教育、宗教、科学或社区服务等领域。由于**专业人士的建议**，这类法人实体无需向州政府或联邦政府缴纳任何税款。

<!--en-->
A nonprofit organization is a corporation formed to carry out a specific purpose, whether it is educational, religious, scientific, or community-related. The corporation does not pay any taxes to the state or federal government because of
**Tips from the Pros**

*伊利诺伊大学新闻学教授、前《调查记者与编辑》执行主任布兰特·休斯顿关于报道非营利组织的建议：*

<!--en-->
*University of Illinois journalism professor and former Investigative Reporters and Editors executive director Brant Houston on covering nonprofits:*

你可以通过从IRS获取免税组织数据库，或从《调查记者与编辑》的数据库库中获取信息，来尽可能完整地列出你所在地区的非营利组织列表，www.ire.org.该数据库列出了所有获得IRS免税资格的机构，并包含一些基本的财务信息。具体而言，数据包括机构的名称、地址、联系人、年度总收入、总资产，以及用于概括描述其活动类型的代码。此外，你还可以在www.guidestar.org,进行搜索，那里收集了有关非营利组织的各类信息。请记住，几乎在任何领域或你能想到的主题中都存在非营利组织。254 • 无利润，却有大量资金

<!--en-->
Get as complete a list of nonprofits in your area as possible by getting the database of tax-exempt organizations from the IRS or from the database library at Investigative Reporters and Editors, www.ire.org. The database lists all organizations granted tax exemption by the IRS and includes some overall financial information. Specifically, the data includes the organization's name, address, contact person, total annual income, total assets, and codes describing their activities generically. Also, you can do searches at www.guidestar.org, which collects information on nonprofits. Remember that nonprofits exist on nearly every beat and any topic you can think of.
254 • No Profits, but Lots of Money

#### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

伊利诺伊大学新闻学教授、前《调查记者与编辑》执行主任布兰特·休斯顿关于报道非营利组织的建议：

<!--en-->
University of Illinois journalism professor and former Investigative Reporters and Editors executive director Brant Houston on covering nonprofits:

仔细查看董事会及其所有活动。获取董事会历任成员及现任成员的名单，如果可能的话获取董事会会议记录，阅读规范董事会成员行为准则的章程，并尽量参加董事会会议。尤其要注意该非营利组织是否与董事会成员拥有的公司有业务往来。前任董事会成员更有可能坦诚地谈论该组织及其现状。IRS和各州监管机构认为，这些组织为公众带来的利益使其有权享受特殊的税收待遇。

<!--en-->
Check out the board of directors and all of its activities. Get lists of both former and current members of the board of directors, get board minutes if you can, read the bylaws governing the code of conduct of board members, and try to attend board meetings. You should especially watch for the nonprofit doing business with companies owned by board members. Former board members are more likely to speak candidly about the organization. its status. The IRS and state regulatory agencies have determined that the public's benefit from these organizations entitles them to special tax status.

然而，成立非营利组织并不能保证一定能获得免税资格。该机构必须向IRS提出申请，由IRS来判断该机构是否符合免税条件。如果IRS同意，该机构将获得依据税法第501(c)(3)条提交财务文件的资格。正因如此，这类企业常被称为501(c)(3)类企业。

<!--en-->
However, forming a nonprofit organization does not guarantee tax-exempt status. The corporation must make a request with the IRS, which will then determine whether the organization merits tax-exempt status. If the IRS agrees, the organization receives the designation of filing financial documents under section 501(c)(3) of the tax code. That is why these companies are often referred to as 501(c)(3) businesses.

与公立和私营营利性企业一样，非营利组织也必须向所在州的州务卿办公室注册成立。每个州都有针对非营利组织的法律和行政规章，这些组织必须遵守。通常，各州的司法部门也会对慈善活动进行监管。大多数非营利组织还会设立主席或首席执行官来负责日常运营，并招聘和解雇员工，其员工人数有时可达数千人。它们会从营利性企业中招募高管，还经常借鉴营利行业的策略和方法以应用于自身组织。此外，非营利组织也被要求以与许多营利性企业相同的方式运作，必须召开董事会会议，并将这些会议的记录作为机构档案保存。

<!--en-->
Just like public and private for-profit corporations, nonprofit businesses must incorporate with their state's secretary of state's office. And every state has laws and administrative rules governing nonprofit organizations that they must follow. Typically, a state department of justice regulates charitable activities as well. Most nonprofit organizations also have a president or CEO who oversees the day-to-day operations, and they hire and fire staffs that sometimes can total in the thousands. They recruit executives from the for-profit world and often look at the for-profit sector for strategies and tactics that they can adapt to their organizations. In addition, nonprofits are required to conduct themselves in the same manner as many for-profit businesses. They must hold board meetings and keep records of those meetings for their corporate records.

但它们也存在差异。非营利组织被允许从公众、私营企业和政府机构处筹集资金。与营利性企业不同，它们不得将政治游说作为业务的核心部分，也不能以损害董事或高管的利益的方式来开展业务。同时，非营利组织也不得将利润分配给成员。

<!--en-->
But they are different as well. Nonprofits are allowed to raise funds from the public and from private business and government agencies. Unlike for-profit businesses, they are not allowed to make political lobbying a significant part of their operations, and they cannot conduct their business in a way that would benefit their directors or officers. And nonprofits are not allowed to distribute their profits to members.

实际上，非营利组织不属于任何人，也无法被出售。如果董事决定解散该组织，它必须先还清所有债务，再将剩余资产转交给另一家非营利组织。这类组织的核心在于其非营利属性。许多人出于这样的想法向非营利组织捐款捐物：这些组织是为了造福社区而存在的，而非为了赚取尽可能多的利润。非营利组织所获得的收入必须用于进一步发展其项目和服务。

<!--en-->
Nonprofits are not actually owned by anyone and cannot be sold. If the directors decide to dissolve the organization, it must pay off all of its debts and distribute the remaining assets to another nonprofit organization. The focus is on the nonprofit aspect of the business. Many people donate their time and money to nonprofits with the idea that these organizations are performing functions for the benefit of the community and are not in existence to make as much money as possible. The money that is made by a nonprofit organization must be used to further develop its programs and services.

尽管非营利组织的职能和结构各有不同，但其中许多其实都是盈利性的企业。有些甚至比其公立和私营竞争对手的盈利能力更强。美国癌症协会在2007年的收入为10.6亿美元，支出为9.66亿美元，支付完所有费用后仍有近9500万美元的盈余。

<!--en-->
Despite the function and structure of nonprofit organizations, many are profitable ventures. Some of them are more profitable than their public and private competitors. The American Cancer Society reported $1.06 billion in revenue and $966 million in expenses in 2007, resulting in nearly $95 million left over once it paid all of its bills.

这并非个例。救世军在2007年的收入为33亿美元，支出接近30亿美元，全年利润达3亿美元。事实上，2007年大多数大型非营利组织的收入都高于支出。公共广播服务局在2006年的收入为18亿美元，支出为15亿美元。其收入中有近三分之二，即约12亿美元，来自拨款和捐赠，而其项目成本则超过了6亿美元。

<!--en-->
It's not the only one. The Salvation Army had $3.3 billion in revenue in 2007 and nearly $3 billion in expenses, leaving it with $300 million in profits for the year. Indeed, most of the large nonprofit organizations reported more in revenue than they did in expenses in 2007. The Public Broadcasting Service reported $1.8 billion in revenue and $1.5 billion in expenses for 2006. Nearly two-thirds, or almost $1.2 billion, of its revenue came from grants and contributions, although its programs cost more than $600 million.

这些利润用到了哪里？和大多数营利性公司一样，它们会被用于通过增加服务项目、建设新设施或以更高薪酬奖励优秀员工来增强组织的实力。从这些例子可以看出，非营利组织往往可以像许多营利性企业一样规模庞大且盈利丰厚。然而媒体却常常将这些组织视为完全不同的实体。无利润，却有大量资金 • 255 这其实是个错误。这些组织是医疗保健和保险等特定行业中的重要参与者，在许多城镇，它们可能占据着市场的主导地位。而且有时，非营利组织可能会因滥用资金或未遵守监管标准而违反与公众签订的协议。

<!--en-->
Where do these profits go? The same place they go to for most for-profit companies, that is, into making the organization stronger by adding additional services or building new facilities or rewarding excellent employees with higherpay. The point to take away from these examples is that nonprofit organizations can often be as huge—and as profitable—as many for-profit enterprises. Yet the media often looks at these ventures as completely different entities.
No Profits, but Lots of Money • 255
This is a mistake. These organizations are major players in specific industries such as health care and insurance. In many towns and cities, they may have the dominant market share for their business. And sometimes, a nonprofit organization can violate its agreement with the public by misusing its money or by not adhering to regulatory standards.

《西雅图时报》报道称，当地公共电视台KCTS正面临财务困境。在该报道发表前不久，该台的台长便辞职了。报道指出：“员工、前高管以及该台聘请的顾问们都认为[这位台长]将这家公共机构当作私人领地来管理”（Phillips和McFadden，2003年，A1页）。报道还提到，尽管台长年薪高达268,000美元，但该台在2001年的亏损额仍达340万美元；同时由于未能提交财务报表，公共广播公司也暂停了对该台的资助。另一个例子是伊利诺伊州皮奥里亚市的《Journal Star》报，该报揭露了当地犯罪制止组织将55%的开支用于筹款，这一比例远高于其他非营利组织。当明尼苏达公共广播公司的管理层因出售一家盈利性的邮购子公司而个人获利超过700万美元的消息被曝光后，他们遭到了广泛批评。2003年4月，美国食品药品监督管理局针对美国红十字会颁布了一项同意令，要求该组织改进血液处理信息的报告方式，否则将面临高额罚款。在这项双方长期争执后出台的命令中，美国红十字会既未承认也未否认有任何违规行为。

<!--en-->
*The Seattle Times* reported that local public television station KCTS was suffering from financial woes. Shortly before their report ran, the station's president resigned. The story noted, "Employees, former executives and the station's own paid consultants say [the president] runs the public entity like a private fiefdom" (Phillips and McFadden, 2003, p. A1). Their reporting noted that the station's losses totaled $3.4 million in 2001 even though the president was receiving a $268,000 salary and that the Corporation for Public Broadcasting was withholding funding because it had not turned in financial statements. In another example, the *Journal Star*, in Peoria, Ill., documented how the local Crime-Stoppers organization was spending 55 percent of its expenses on fundraising, which is a high percentage compared with other nonprofit organizations. Executives at Minnesota Public Radio were widely criticized when it was disclosed that they had personally earned more than $7 million when they sold a for-profit mail-order subsidiary. And in April 2003, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration issued a consent decree against the American Red Cross requiring the organization to improve its method of reporting information about the handling of blood or face severe fines. The decree, in which the American Red Cross neither admitted nor denied any wrongdoing, followed a lengthy battle between regulators and the group.

从这些例子可以看出，非营利组织也无法免于那些困扰营利企业的相同问题和挑战。仍然存在滥用资金及违反业务管理规则的指控。无论此类事件发生在何处，都具有新闻价值。

<!--en-->
From these examples, we see that nonprofit corporations are not exempt from some of the same problems and issues that plague the for-profit world. There are still allegations of misuse of money and of disobeying rules governing the business. Such events are newsworthy no matter where they happen.

的确，非营利组织为所在社区提供了诸多服务。它们秉持“不应从他人身上牟利”的原则，帮助数百万人过上更好的生活。但它们同样具有新闻价值，媒体应当积极进行报道。然而，大多数媒体并没有专职的非营利领域记者，许多大众传播机构甚至没有专门负责报道这一经济领域的商业记者。

<!--en-->
To be sure, nonprofit organizations offer great services to their communities. They help millions of people live better lives under the principle that their organization should not be making a profit from others. But they are also newsworthy organizations, and they should be covered aggressively by media outlets. However, most media outlets do not have a full-time nonprofits reporter, and many mass communication organizations do not even have a business reporter cover this sector of the economy.

报道非营利组织的写作策略与报道营利企业的策略并无不同。在很多情况下，财务状况最能清晰地反映一个组织的运营状况是好是坏。正如下面这篇《达拉斯晨报》的报道所示，两种商业形态之间的竞争日益加剧，这也使得有人主张应由商业领域的记者来报道非营利组织。

<!--en-->
The reporting and writing tactics for covering the nonprofit world are the same as they are for writing about for-profit businesses. In many cases, the financial performance tells the clearest picture of how well—or how poorly—the organization is performing. And the competition between the two business structures is increasing, as the following *Dallas Morning News* story suggests, leading to the argument that nonprofits should be covered by the business staff:

> 这个口号或许没能拯救奥兹莫比尔，但慈善机构Goodwill Industries推出的全新高端理念让这家历史悠久的慈善机构能够自豪地宣称：“这已经不是你祖母时代的那家Goodwill商店了。”

<!--en-->
> The slogan might not have saved the Oldsmobile, but a new upscale concept among Goodwill Industries has left the venerable charity boasting that "this is not your grandmother's Goodwill store."

### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

伊利诺伊大学新闻学教授、曾任《调查记者与编辑》执行主任的布兰特·休斯顿关于报道非营利组织的建议：>如果该非营利组织获得了州政府用于项目的资金，那就查看该州是否对这些资金的支出进行了审计，并是否存在任何异常情况。多年前，我查阅过一家为智力障碍者提供服务的私营承包商的审计报告，发现州政府多次以该承包商将资金用于购买汽车、游泳池及其他个人开支为由对其提出指责，但却从未采取任何行动。256 • 无利润，却有大量资金事实上，赫斯特市议会周二晚间批准新建的一家超级商店将拥有22,000平方英尺的零售空间、一家咖啡店、一家高端二手书店以及一家时尚精品店。

<!--en-->
*University of Illinois journalism professor and former Investigative Reporters and Editors executive director Brant Houston on covering nonprofits:*> If the nonprofit gets state money for programs, then see if the state has audited the expenditure of that money and taken any exceptions. Years ago, I looked through audits of a private contractor providing services for the mentally disabled and saw the state had frequently cited the contractor for misuse of funds—cars, swimming pools and other personal expenses—but taken no action.
256 • No Profits, but Lots of Money
Indeed, a new superstore approved by the Hurst City Council on Tuesday night will feature 22,000 square feet of retail space, a coffee shop, a high-end used bookstore and a fashion boutique.

沃思堡Goodwill Industries公司的社区关系与营销总监大卫·考克斯表示：“我们希望人们早上能在尼曼马库斯购物，下午则去Goodwill购物。我们的停车场里随时都能看到梅赛德斯、雷克萨斯和宝马等豪华汽车。”

<!--en-->
"We envision people shopping at Neiman Marcus in the morning and at Goodwill in the afternoon," said David Cox, director of community relations and marketing for Goodwill Industries of Fort Worth Inc. "You will find Mercedes, Lexus and Beamers in our parking lot any day."

市议会的决定为位于Pipeline路西825号的新型超级商店的建成铺平了道路。作为Goodwill全国扩张趋势的一部分，这家新商店的规模将是传统Goodwill零售中心的近三倍，预计将在占地33,000平方英尺的前Food Lion店铺内于7月开业。

<!--en-->
The council action cleared the way for a new so-called superstore at 825 W. Pipeline Road. The new store, part of a growing national trend for Goodwill, will be nearly three times as big as traditional Goodwill retail centers and should open in the 33,000-square-foot former Food Lion by July.

考克斯先生表示，该慈善机构并未放弃其百年来的传统——通过销售二手衣物以及旧家具和电器来筹集资金，帮助残疾人就业。只是他们借鉴了俄勒冈州波特兰市那些高端二手店的成功经验，为业务增添了一些新变化。

<!--en-->
The charity isn't forsaking its century-old tradition of selling second-hand clothes and used furniture and appliances to raise money to put the disabled to work. It's just adding a little twist picked up by watching the agency's upscale thrift stores in Portland, Ore., thrive, Mr. Cox said.

他说：“我们的使命依然如故。我们是一家提供帮助而非直接施舍的组织。我们会利用商店的销售利润来培训残疾人工作，给他们一份工作，而不是仅仅送一件新衬衫。”

<!--en-->
"Our mission is still the same," he said. "We're a hand-up rather than a handout organization. We take the money [the stores' profits from the sales] and train handicapped people to work. We give them a job rather than a new shirt."

零售销售部门负责人埃琳·奎利安表示，事实上，沃思堡的这家机构去年获得了1000万美元的收入，其中600万美元来自零售销售和二手物品回收业务。

<!--en-->
Indeed, the Fort Worth agency took in $10 million last year, with $6 million coming from its retail sales and salvage operation, said Erin Quillian, director of retail sales.

国际善意工业组织的发言人戴夫·巴林格称，塔兰特县东北部的这家超级商店在德克萨斯州尚属首例，但它遵循着该慈善机构在全国范围内约1800家门店的发展模式。

<!--en-->
Dave Barringer, a spokesman for Goodwill Industries International, said the northeast Tarrant County superstore is a first for Texas, but it is following in footsteps of a growing number of the charity's approximately 1,800 stores across the nation.

他说：“我们越能与其他折扣商——从沃尔玛到凯马特——竞争，并提供更多附加服务，就越能更好地为民众服务。这些商店有两个主要用途：通常作为我们其他项目的资金来源，同时也经常为我们的服务对象提供就业机会。”

<!--en-->
"The better we compete with the other discounters—from Wal-Mart to Kmart—and add all the bells and whistles the better we will be able to serve our people," he said. "The stores have two main purposes: They are usually funding mechanisms for our other programs, and they often provide work opportunities for our clients as well."

达拉斯善意工业组织的主席罗德·金瑟表示，这类超级商店是推动善意工业组织零售业务不断发展的最新阶段。他说，达拉斯的门店已有10年的历史，规模更大，还配备了书店及其他设施。¹ 看过这篇报道后，还有谁会怀疑非营利组织是一个亟待讲述的重要商业故事呢？它们正在不断扩大规模，并与公共及私营企业展开更直接的竞争。看看文中提到的其他零售商——尼曼马库斯、沃尔玛和凯马特，这些都是当今最庞大的企业。然而，善意工业组织认为自己处于其他企业尚未涉足的零售细分市场之中。[^2793]：¹ 摘自M. 林登贝格2001年2月15日发表于《达拉斯晨报》的文章《善意工业将开设巨型超市：该零售中心将成为该地区最大的商店》，版权归《达拉斯晨报》所有，经许可转载。无利润，却有大量资金 • 257页

<!--en-->
Rod Ginther, president of the Dallas Goodwill, said such superstores were the newest stage of an evolution that has been changing Goodwill's retail operations. Dallas stores have been on a larger scale, with bookstores and other amenities, for 10 years, he said.¹
After reading this story, can anybody question that nonprofit organizations are an important business story waiting to be told? They are expanding, and they're competing more directly with public and private companies. Look at the names of the other retailers mentioned in this story—Neiman Marcus, Wal-Mart, and Kmart. These are some of the biggest companies operating today. Yet Goodwill Industries sees itself as fitting in a retailing niche that these others aren't fulfilling.

No Profits, but Lots of Money • 257

## 基金会

<!--en-->
*Foundations*

基金会与非营利组织类似，都属于不以盈利为目的的实体。实际上，基金会的存在目的仅仅是捐出资金，而非赚取利润。但这并不意味着它们不属于商业领域。

<!--en-->
Foundations are similar to nonprofit organizations in that they are entities that are not interested in making a profit. Foundations, in fact, simply exist to give money away, not to make it. But that does not mean they fall outside of the business world.

许多基金会是由营利性企业及其前任高管或通过企业股票致富的人士所创立的。美国规模最大的基金会是比尔及梅琳达·盖茨基金会，其名称源自微软的创始人及其妻子。根据最新的统计数据，截至2009年9月底，该基金会的资产已超过340亿美元。其他大型基金会的名称则堪称商业界的名人录，诸如礼来、福特、强生、凯洛格、帕卡德、惠普尔特、杜克、盖蒂和梅隆等。

<!--en-->
Many foundations are the result of the profits made by for-profit corporations and the executives that previously ran them or made their fortunes from the company's stock. The largest foundation in the country is the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation, named after the founder of Microsoft and his wife. The foundation had more than $34 billion in assets at the end September 2009, the latest statistics available. Other large foundations read like a Who's Who of the business world, with names such as Lilly, Ford, Johnson & Johnson, Kellogg, Packard, Hewlett, Duke, Getty, and Mellon attached to them.

根据基金会中心的数据，美国现有超过75,000家基金会，资产总额超过6820亿美元。2007年，这些基金会向非营利组织以及其他个人和团体捐赠了超过440亿美元的款项。

<!--en-->
According to The Foundation Center, there are more than 75,000 foundations in the country with more than $682 billion in assets. In 2007, they handed out more than $44 billion in gifts to nonprofit organizations and other individuals and groups.

基金会是以非营利组织或慈善信托的形式设立的，但其首要义务与之前讨论过的医院、善意工业组织等非营利组织不同。基金会的主要目的是通过拨款的方式，将资金甚至电脑等设备送给需要帮助的组织或个人。根据法律规定，基金会必须每年拿出其资产的5%用于捐赠，以维持免税地位。（基金会还会向美国国税局申请501(c)(3)资格。）

<!--en-->
A foundation is established as a nonprofit organization or a charitable trust, but its primary obligation is different from that of nonprofit organizations such as hospitals and Goodwill Industries discussed earlier. A foundation's primary purpose is to give away money and sometimes equipment such as computers by way of grants to organizations or individuals who request help. By law, a foundation must give away 5 percent of its assets every year to maintain its tax-free status. (Foundations also apply for 501(c)(3) status with the IRS.)

基金会有多种类型。最常见的就是独立基金会，这类基金会不隶属于任何公司或家族。企业基金会则与特定企业相关，通常是营利性企业，它们会向所在社区提供资助。家族基金会则由某个家族及其成员提供资金，其资助项目可能与该家族的利益相关。著名的运动员和名人也会创建基金会，根据这些基金会如何使用资金，有时也能为商业记者提供写作素材。当橄榄球明星马歇尔·福克被评为NFL年度最佳球员时，他的基金会获得了3万美元，用于向各类组织进行捐赠。

<!--en-->
There are different types of foundations. Independent foundations are the most common. These foundations are not associated with a company or a family. Corporate foundations are those connected to a business, quite often a for-profit company that makes grants to the communities in which it operates. Family foundations receive their money from an individual family and its members, and its grants may be tied to family interests. Famous athletes and celebrities also create foundations, and sometimes these organizations can result in stories for the business writer as well, depending on what the foundation is doing with its money. When football star Marshall Faulk was voted the NFL Player of the Year, his foundation received $30,000 to give to organizations.

基金会可被视为大型投资企业。尽管它们每年会向值得支持的事业捐赠数十亿美元，但其设计初衷却是永久存在。尤其是那些由私人投资资助的基金会，极有可能永远无法耗尽其拥有的所有资金和资产。这些基金会会将资产投资于股票、债券、房地产或其他旨在增值的投资项目。以拨款形式发放的资金通常来自这些投资带来的收益。因此，基金会的管理者，尤其是投资主管，会密切关注股市和经济形势。他们的工作与共同基金经理或华尔街投资专家类似。

<!--en-->
Foundations can be considered huge investment businesses. Although they give away billions of dollars each year to worthy causes, they are designed to exist forever. Foundations, particularly those funded by private investments, most likely will never give away all of the money and assets that they have. Foundations invest their assets in stocks, bonds, real estate, or other investments designed to build the assets. The money that is given away in the form of grants typically comes from the income and gains on these investments. Therefore, foundation managers, particularly investment officers, watch the stock market and the economy closely. Their jobs are similar to those of mutual fund managers or Wall Street investment pros.

2008年的股市暴跌影响了许多基金会，因为股市及其他投资的波动会直接影响基金会资产的价值。位于乔治亚州的罗伯特·W·伍德拉夫基金会就获得了可口可乐的资助

<!--en-->
The 2008 stock market drop affected many foundations, as the ups and downs in the stock market and other investments can affect the worth of a foundation's assets. The Robert W. Woodruff Foundation in Georgia, endowed with Coca-Cola

### 专家建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

伊利诺伊大学新闻学教授、前《调查记者与编辑》执行总监布兰特·休斯顿关于报道非营利组织的观点：

<!--en-->
University of Illinois journalism professor and former Investigative Reporters and Editors executive director Brant Houston on covering nonprofits:

切勿仅凭990表格就妄下结论。如果某名员工同时从非营利组织及其关联机构或其他团体领取报酬，其薪资数据可能会具有误导性。例如，如果一家非营利组织设在大学内，而该员工也在为大学工作，那么其部分薪资可能来自非营利组织，另一部分则来自大学。990表格仅会显示来自非营利组织的那部分薪资。又或者，某非营利组织的净资产可能逐年稳步增长，但这可能是由于捐赠给其捐赠基金的资金增加，而非运营收入增加。问题在于捐赠基金的主额本身不可动用，只能使用投资所得。这意味着如果投资表现不佳，该组织即便拥有500万美元的捐赠基金，也可能一分钱都花不了，进而因投资损失而不得不裁员。

<!--en-->
Beware of assuming too much from reading the Form 990. The salaries can be misleading if a staff member is receiving pay from the nonprofit and from an affiliated organization or another group. For example, if a nonprofit is based at a university, part of the salary for a staff member can come from the nonprofit and part from the university if the employee also does work for the university. The 990 would show only the nonprofit part of the salary. Or a nonprofit can show a steady increase in net assets year after year, but that may be due to more donations to its endowment rather than to its operating revenue. The problem is that the principal in an endowment cannot be spent, only investment income. That means that if investments go badly, the organization could have a $5 million endowment, but not be able to spend a penny of it, which could result in staff layoffs because of the investment losses.

由创始人兼前可口可乐总裁罗伯特·伍德拉夫所著的《258 • 无利润，却有巨额资金》一书的资产价值会随着可口可乐股价的波动而变化。其他一些基金会则将资金交由总部位于纽约的投资者伯纳德·麦道夫管理，当麦道夫的庞氏骗局被揭露后，这些基金会损失了大部分甚至全部资金。至少有147家基金会曾向麦道夫投资。

<!--en-->
258 • No Profits, but Lots of Money stock by founder and former Coca-Cola president Robert Woodruff, saw its asset value fluctuate with the value of Coca-Cola stock. Other foundations gave their money to New York-based investor Bernard Madoff to manage and then lost most or all of their money when it was discovered that Madoff was operating a Ponzi scheme. At least 147 foundations invested with Madoff.

基金会在对盈利性企业的持股比例上存在限制。《税改法案》规定，基金会持有的上市公司或私营公司的有表决权股份不得超过20%。有些基金会通过向监管机构证明自己已真诚努力出售相关股份，从而绕过了这一限制，并获得了五年的撤资期限。

<!--en-->
Foundations have limits on how much ownership they can have in for-profit businesses. The Tax Reform Act states that a foundation cannot own more than 20 percent of the voting shares in a public or private corporation. Some foundations have gotten around this limitation and received a five-year extension to divest by showing regulators that they have made a good-faith effort to sell the stake.

了解基金会的运作方式及其资金来源至关重要。基金会能够对当地经济和商业界产生重大影响，尤其是当小型企业依靠基金会的拨款或资助维持运营时。很多时候，基金会会向有需求的商业团体提供拨款，以帮助少数族裔经营的企业发展。此外，基金会还会向致力于研发治疗重大疾病药物的科研机构提供资金，他们的成功有望推动制药产业的发展。

<!--en-->
Understanding how foundations work and where their money comes from is important. Foundations can have a major impact on a local economy and business community, particularly if small businesses are receiving grants or funding from foundations to survive. Many times, foundations will give grants to needy business groups that will help minority-owned ventures. Foundations also give money to scientific and research organizations that may be seeking to develop drugs to treat major diseases or illnesses. Their success could spur the drug industry.

以下摘自《堪萨斯城星报》的内容展示了当地一家基金会如何影响堪萨斯城的经济：

<!--en-->
The following excerpt from the *Kansas City Star* shows how a local foundation might be affecting the Kansas City economy:

> 在去年决定逐步取消用于满足当地社会服务需求的小额资助后，尤因·马里恩·考夫曼基金会今年又决定增加这类小额资助的金额。作为该地区规模最大的慈善机构，该基金会宣布在未来几年内每年向专门用于资助非营利组织的基金投入250万美元。这些资金可用于延续考夫曼基金会长期以来对城市青少年的支持，涵盖领导力训练营和艺术课程等各类活动。根据《堪萨斯城星报》对考夫曼基金会资助情况的分析，2001年该基金会每年会向当地非营利组织提供约180万美元的小额资助。因此，该基金会的新承诺意味着用于25,000美元及以下金额的小额资助总额至少增长了36%。考夫曼基金会改变对这类资助的态度，是因为它找到了在精简机构的同时仍能发放资助的方法，同时也出于应对经济恶化形势的考虑。考夫曼基金会的新任首席执行官卡尔·施拉姆表示，基金会对弱势群体负有传统责任，而在经济不景气时期这一责任更为重要。“我们将经济衰退视为扩大社会福利的机会，”施拉姆说道。在非营利组织界，考夫曼基金会的这一宣布正值社会服务领域的领导者们屏息以待之际——他们正在观察自去年春天接替长期担任公益领袖的路易斯·史密斯的施拉姆领导下，这家堪萨斯城的慈善巨头将会发生怎样的变化。施拉姆表示希望基金会能以更高效的方式使用资金，即把更多资金投入到更少的项目中。他还承诺，当该基金会的新“业务计划”在今年晚些时候获得批准后，流入堪萨斯城的资金只会增加而不会减少。考夫曼基金会对小额资助的新承诺正是这一承诺的首个具体体现。无利润，但资金充裕 • 259 虽然一些非营利组织领导人对考夫曼基金会的举措表示赞赏，但他们也在担心大额资助将会面临什么变化。“向（小额资助）基金捐款以扩大其规模是个好主意，”获得考夫曼基金会资助的马蒂·罗兹艺术中心的执行主任玛丽·卢·贾拉米洛说，“我们所有非营利组织界的成员都在等待考夫曼基金会未来的发展方向。”多年来，考夫曼基金会一直扮演着某种社会看护者的角色，承担着原本主要由地方政府负责的各项职责，这些职责包括培训公立学校校长以及为社会服务机构提供补贴等。在履行这些职责的过程中，考夫曼基金会通过两种方式发放用于满足社区小型需求的小额资助：一种是通过由大堪萨斯城社区基金会管理、并由社区咨询委员会负责的考夫曼基金；另一种则是通过基金会自身的创业与发展部门。该基金会每年为考夫曼基金提供100万美元的资金支持。至于通过基金会运营渠道发放的小额资助，根据考夫曼基金会向美国国税局提交的990表格显示，2001财年共有838,000美元被用于资助当地各类事业和非营利组织，这一数字还不包括作为更大规模考夫曼项目一部分而拨给公立学校的资助款。考夫曼基金会官员表示无法对此838,000美元的数额发表评论，因为该基金会并未单独统计用于当地事业的小额资助金额。如今，施拉姆正在对考夫曼基金会的整个机构进行改革，同时将员工人数削减近一半。在此过程中，他此前曾宣布打算逐步取消由基金会直接管理的小额资助，即便有了每年250万美元的新投入，他仍打算通过社区基金会的考夫曼基金来发放这些资金，从而实现这一目标。 因此，至少在接下来的三年里，考夫曼基金会将增加资金投入，同时提升效率。“这或许是这件事带来的积极结果。这是一种将资助金有效分配到社区中的高效方式，”施拉姆说道。目前尚不确定的是，那些负责发放小额资助的考夫曼基金会项目将会如何发展。例如，有一个项目是青少年咨询委员会，该委员会由高中生组成，他们负责讨论并筛选各类青少年志愿服务活动的资助申请。大多数资助金额在1,000美元以下。如果青少年委员会及其他小额资助项目在施拉姆的领导下继续运作，那么考夫曼基金会在小额资助上的总投入将超过250万美元。² [^2830]：² 摘自J. 斯皮瓦克所写的《考夫曼基金会将增加对非营利组织的小额资助》，发表于2003年1月24日的《堪萨斯城星报》，A1版。版权所有2003年《堪萨斯城星报》，经许可转载。260 • 无利润，但资金充裕

<!--en-->
> After deciding last year to phase out small grants for local social service needs, the Ewing Marion Kauffman Foundation has decided this year to boost such small grants.
> The foundation, the region's largest philanthropy, has announced a $2.5 million annual commitment in coming years to a special fund dedicated to nonprofit agencies. This money could end up extending Kauffman's traditional support for urban youth, in activities ranging from leadership camps to art classes.
> In 2001, Kauffman dedicated about $1.8 million a year in small grants to local nonprofits, according to a *Kansas City Star* analysis of Kauffman's grant-making. So the foundation's new commitment represents at least a 36 percent increase in the total amount dedicated to small grants, those of $25,000 or less.
> Kauffman's turnaround on such grants evolved because the foundation figured out how to dispense them while still downsizing, and because the foundation wanted to respond to the worsening economy. Carl Schramm, Kauffman's new chief executive, said foundations have a traditional obligation toward the less-fortunate, and that duty is heightened in bad economic times.
> "We see the recession as an opportunity to expand social welfare," Schramm said.
> In the nonprofit community, Kauffman's announcement comes at a time when social service leaders are collectively holding their breath. They are waiting to see how Kansas City's philanthropic behemoth will change under Schramm, who took over from longtime civic leader Louis Smith last spring.
> Schramm has indicated he wants the foundation to get more bang for its bucks, to basically put more money into fewer programs.
> He also has promised that when the foundation's new "business plans"get approved later this year, more money will end up going into Kansas City, not less. Kauffman's new commitment to small grants is the first tangible follow-through of that promise.
No Profits, but Lots of Money • 259
So while some nonprofit leaders hailed Kauffman's action, they wondered what will happen with larger grants.
"It's a good move to make a gift to the (small-grant) fund so that pool grows," said Mary Lou Jaramillo, executive director of the Mattie Rhodes Art Center, which gets Kauffman funding. "We're all waiting in the nonprofit community for the direction Kauffman is going."
For years now, Kauffman has fulfilled a role as sort of a societal caretaker. The foundation assumed responsibilities that used to be primarily the province of local governments. These duties ranged from training public school principals to helping to subsidize social service agencies.
In doing this, Kauffman handed out small grants for smaller community needs in two ways. One way was through its Kauffman Fund, held at the Greater Kansas City Community Foundation and administered by a community advisory board. The other way was through the foundation's own entrepreneurship and youth development operating divisions.
The foundation has bankrolled the Kauffman Fund with $1 million a year. As for small grants funneled through foundation operations, a total of $838,000 was disbursed to local causes and local nonprofits in the 2001 fiscal year, according to the Form 990 that Kauffman filed with the Internal Revenue Service. That amount does not include small grants to public schools as part of a larger Kauffman program.
Kauffman officials said they could not comment on the $838,000 amount, because the foundation did not keep its own tally of small grants for local causes.
Now Schramm is revamping Kauffman's entire organization while cutting the staff nearly in half. In doing so, he previously announced a desire to phase out the small grants administered at the foundation. He still intends to do this even with the new $2.5 million annual commitment, by channeling that money through the Kauffman Fund at the community foundation.
So Kauffman will be increasing its monetary commitment—for at least the next three years—while also increasing its efficiency. "That may be a happy outcome of this. This is a very efficient way to get these grants into the community," Schramm said.
What remains uncertain is what will happen to some of the Kauffman operating programs that gave out small grants. One program, for instance, is a youth advisory board. It is made up of high school students who discuss and select grant applications for many youth volunteer activities. Most grants are less than $1,000.
If the youth board or other small-grant programs continue under Schramm, then Kauffman's small-grant commitment would end up exceeding $2.5 million.²
[^2830]: ² From "Kauffman Foundation will increase small grants to nonprofits," by J. Spivak, January 24, 2003, *Kansas City Star*, p. A1. Copyright 2003 by *Kansas City Star*. Reprinted with permission.
260 • No Profits, but Lots of Money

#### 专家建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

伊利诺伊大学新闻学教授、前《调查记者与编辑》执行主任布兰特·休斯顿关于报道非营利组织的建议：

<!--en-->
University of Illinois journalism professor and former Investigative Reporters and Editors executive director Brant Houston on covering nonprofits:

详细了解990表格中应填写的内容（本章会介绍很多相关内容），同时注意那些未提及的信息。例如，如果某非营利组织发放助学金或奖学金，所有受益人名单都应列出。在报道2002年盐湖城奥运会筹备情况时，有记者得知一家与奥运会相关的非营利组织曾发放奖学金，但990表格上并未列出这些信息。经过进一步调查，记者们获得了名单，发现这些奖学金实际上发放给了选定盐湖城为奥运主办城市的国际奥委会成员的家属。

<!--en-->
Know in detail what should be filed in a Form 990 (this chapter tells you much of it) and watch for what is not there. For example, if the nonprofit gives out fellowships or scholarships, all those receiving them should be listed. Reporters covering preparations for the 2002 Olympics in Salt Lake City heard that a Salt Lake Olympics-related nonprofit had given out scholarships, but none were listed on the Form 990. With deeper digging, the reporters got the list and saw scholarships had gone to family members of the International Olympic committee, which had selected Salt Lake City as the Olympic host city.

此外，还要留意缺乏重大的筹款支出情况。有些非营利组织可能会试图低估筹款开支，以为这样能显得更好，或者将所有费用都计入与自身相关的“教育”项目。

<!--en-->
Also, pay careful attention to the lack of significant fundraising expenses. Some nonprofits may try to underestimate how much they spend on fundraising, thinking it makes them look better, or they may allocate all the expenses into an “educational” program about the nonprofit.

这篇报道介绍了考夫曼基金会——其资金来源于创始人持有的制药公司股票——在资助方向上的变化如何影响当地机构。基金会也是大学和学校的重要捐助方。高校通常会开展大规模筹款活动，并以基金会为目标寻求捐赠。这些捐赠可能推动当地大学快速发展，进而用于建造新建筑和招聘新员工。在报道基金会提供的重大资助或礼物时，记者应评估其对当地经济的影响。

<!--en-->
This story explains how the shift in grant giving by the Kauffman Foundation, which received its funding from its founder’s pharmaceutical company stock, is affecting local organizations. Foundations are also major donors to universities and schools. Colleges and universities often undergo major fundraising initiatives and target foundations to make donations. These donations could spur major growth at a local university, leading to the construction of new buildings and the hiring of new employees. When writing about major grants or gifts given by foundations, reporters should assess the local economic impact.

对于那些希望在自己离任后仍留下影响力的企业高管而言，基金会及其资金同样重要。CEO等人士有时会创建基金会，并将自己持有的公司股票捐赠给这些基金会。通过查看美国证券交易委员会的文件，可以追踪这些股票的所有权转移情况。此外，企业高管即便离开公司后，仍可能继续在公司总部为自己的基金会租赁办公空间。这类协议也常常会在SEC的文件中披露。

<!--en-->
Foundations and their money can also be important to current business executives looking to leave their mark long after they are gone. CEOs and others sometimes create foundations and donate their stock holdings in their companies to these foundations. The ownership transfer of the stock can be traced by checking SEC filings. In addition, a company executive may continue to lease office space for his or her foundation in the company’s headquarters even after he or she has left the business. These agreements are also often disclosed in SEC filings.

然而，基金会也会面临与非营利组织类似的诸多问题，比如管理不善或滥用资金。

<!--en-->
Foundations, however, are also prone to some of the same issues that nonprofit organizations encounter. They can be mismanaged or misuse their money.

2003年4月，《圣何塞水星报》报道称，某当地基金会的负责人导致该基金会资产损失25%，还解雇了员工，而他本人获得的薪酬若经联邦当局审计可能会面临处罚。

<!--en-->
The *San Jose Mercury News* noted in April 2003 that the president of a local foundation lost 25 percent of its assets and fired staff members, while receiving a compensation package that could have faced sanctions if it had been audited by the federal authorities.

2003年5月，《巴尔的摩太阳报》则报道，当地基金会的税务记录显示，许多基金会支付给受托人的报酬其实是其他基金会认为属于志愿工作的内容，这一行为引起了美国国税局的关注。

<!--en-->
And *The Baltimore Sun* reported in May 2003 that the tax records of local foundations showed that many paid their trustees to do work that many other foundations consider volunteer work. The move attracted IRS attention.

基金会像企业一样运作，注重成本控制并关注资金去向。虽然它们并不销售产品或服务，但在某些情况下，它们管理的资金规模可达数十亿美元。

<!--en-->
Foundations are run like businesses, with an eye toward expenses and a focus on where the money goes. They’re not actually selling a product or a service, but they are important operations that control billions of dollars in some cases.

除少数例外，媒体往往忽视基金会，或仅聚焦于其获得的巨额资助或礼物进行报道。尽管这些新闻也值得报道，但这些机构内部还有更多值得关注的内容。

<!--en-->
The media, with a few notable exceptions, ignores foundations or downplays their coverage to focus on large grants or gifts handed out. While those stories are news, there’s more going on within these organizations that merits coverage.

在下一节中，我们将了解如何查找基金会和非营利组织的具体财务信息。

<!--en-->
In the next section, we’ll see how to find specific financial information for foundations and nonprofit organizations.

### 获取信息：990表格

<!--en-->
*Finding Information: The Form 990*

许多记者认为，基金会和非营利组织与私营企业一样具有保密性，根本无法真正评估其财务状况。

<!--en-->
The perception among many journalists is that foundations and nonprofit organizations are secretive entities, just like private businesses, and there is no real way to assess their financial performance.

然而，这种看法是错误的，就像对小型私营企业的看法一样。记者完全可以收集到大量关于基金会和非营利组织的信息。与企业一样，这些组织也被要求向其所在州的州务卿办公室提交文件，有时还需向负责监管慈善机构的州部门提交信息。这些文件有助于记者查明非营利组织的董事会成员和律师信息，但可能无法提供更多内容。

<!--en-->
That belief, however, is wrong, just as it is regarding small and private companies. There is plenty of information available for a reporter to gather about foundations and nonprofits. Just like businesses, these groups are required to file documents with the secretary of state’s office in the state in which they are located. They may also have to file information with the state office that tracks charities. These documents will help a reporter identify a nonprofit organization’s board members and attorney but may not provide much else.

许多非营利组织还会获得州政府、市政府或联邦政府的资助，或与它们签订合同。与这些安排相关的文件都属于公开记录。有时，向该非营利组织提供资金或签订合同的政府机构也会对其开展审计，以确保资金的使用符合协议规定。无利润，却有大量资金 • 261 其他一些机构也会追踪特定的非营利组织信息。例如，商业改进局就设有慈善咨询服务，用于评估非营利组织的运营状况。它会从管理方式、筹款行为、资金使用情况等方面对这类组织进行考核，并规定捐赠款项的60%必须用于提供服务，而组织的预算中用于筹款的金额不得超过35%。关于非营利组织的许多相关报告都可以在http://www.bbb.org/us/charity找到。不过，任何真正希望获取某基金会或非营利组织详细财务信息的记者，都必须查看一份能满足其大部分需求的文件。自1942年起，美国国税局就要求基金会和非营利组织提交990表格，而这些表格属于公开记录。

<!--en-->
Many nonprofit organizations also receive funding or have contracts with state, city, or federal governments. The documents related to these arrangements are public record. Sometimes, the government agency that has the contract orprovided funding to the nonprofit organization will also perform an audit on the group to make sure that the money is being spent in accordance with the agreement.
No Profits, but Lots of Money • 261
Other groups also keep track of specific nonprofit information. The Better Business Bureau, for example, has a philanthropic advisory service that evaluates the performance of nonprofit organizations. It measures groups on the basis of their management, their fundraising practices, how money is spent, and other items. It stipulates that 60 percent of donations must be used in providing services, and no more than 35 percent of a group's budget should be spent on fundraising. Many of its reports on nonprofits can be obtained by going to http://www.bbb.org/us/charity
However, any reporter truly interested in finding detailed financial information about a foundation or a nonprofit organization must examine one document that will provide most of what they need. The IRS has required foundations and nonprofit organizations to file a Form 990 since 1942, and it is a public record.

990表格会显示该非营利组织在上一年度筹集了多少资金、资金来源以及资金的使用情况。这些支出被分为项目支出、管理支出和筹款支出三类。990表格还会详细说明该组织正在开展哪些项目以及在这些项目上的支出金额。此外，这份文件还会提供有关该组织董事会成员的信息以及管理层的薪酬情况。其中还包含有关该组织在过去一年是否有任何交易以及是否从事游说活动的披露内容。

<!--en-->
A Form 990 shows how much money the nonprofit organization collected within the previous year, from which sources, and how it was spent. These expenses are divided among program expenses, management expenses, and fundraising expenses. The Form 990 also details what kind of programs the organization is running and how much it spends on them. In addition, this document provides information about the group's board members and how much its management is paid. There are also disclosures that show if the organization had any transactions in the last year and whether it lobbies.

990表格可被视为公共公司的10-Q或10-K表格的对应版本，同时还整合了其他美国证券交易委员会文件——如委托书——的部分功能。对于记者而言，990表格是最全面的财务文件之一。

<!--en-->
The Form 990 should be thought of as the equivalent of a Form 10-Q or 10-K for a public company, with some of the functions of other SEC filings—such as proxy statements—rolled in for good measure. The Form 990 is one of the most all-encompassing financial documents available for a reporter.

2000年通过的法规大大提升了获取990表格的便利性。非营利组织有义务向任何提出请求的人提供其最近三份990表格以及申请免税资格时的原始申请文件。这些文件必须在收到请求的当天，或通过邮件在30天内提供给对方。也可以通过填写4506A表格或写信的方式直接从美国国税局获取这些文件。不过，美国国税局可能需要长达六周的时间才会回复。许多州也会为本州的基金会存档990表格。现在也有许多基金会每年会在互联网上公布自己的990表格，方便任何人查阅。未能向公众公开990表格的组织可能会面临罚款。

<!--en-->
Regulations passed in 2000 greatly expanded access to Form 990 documents. Nonprofit organizations are required to provide their three most recent Form 990 filings and their original filing for tax-exempt status to anyone who requests them. They must be made available the same day of the request from the foundation's office or within 30 days by mail. The documents can also be obtained directly from the IRS by using Form 4506A or by writing a letter. The IRS may take up to six weeks to reply, however. Many states also keep Form 990s on file for foundations in their state. Many foundations are also now posting their Form 990 each year on the Internet, making them accessible to anyone. Organizations can be fined for not making their Form 990 filings available to the public.

大多数非营利组织必须在财政年度结束后的六个月内向美国国税局提交990表格。不过，这份文件可能不会立即可供获取，因为联邦政府机构需要数月时间来扫描它。非营利组织也可以申请延期，这可能会推迟文件的提交时间。

<!--en-->
Most nonprofit organizations must file their Form 990 with the IRS within six months after the end of their fiscal year. However, the document may not be immediately available, as it can take the federal government agency several months to scan it. Nonprofit organizations can also file for extensions, which may delay when the document is filed.

大多数宗教组织无需提交990表格，年度收入低于25,000美元的组织也可免于提交。但年度收入超过100,000美元或总资产超过250,000美元的非营利组织必须提交990表格，而年度收入在100,000美元以下但至少为25,000美元、总资产低于250,000美元的非营利组织则需提交990-EZ表格。

<!--en-->
Most religious organizations are not required to file Form 990 documents, and organizations with less than $25,000 in receipts in a year are also exempt. But nonprofit organizations with more than $100,000 in receipts or more than $250,000 in total assets must file a Form 990, whereas nonprofit organizations with receipts less than $100,000 but at least $25,000 and assets of less than $250,000 must file a Form 990-EZ.

### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

伊利诺伊大学新闻学教授、前《调查记者与编辑》执行主任布兰特·休斯顿关于报道非营利组织的建议：

<!--en-->
University of Illinois journalism professor and former Investigative Reporters and Editors executive director Brant Houston on covering nonprofits:

先从该非营利组织当前的990纳税申报表入手，但不要止步于此。至少获取三年的表格（通常可在www.guidestar.org免费获取）。如果该组织的网站上没有，可以要求查看其最近三年的年度审计报告及预算文件。如果网站上也没有且该组织不愿提供，就要询问原因。毕竟，非营利组织依靠免税资格寻求公众的资助，也呼吁公众捐款以支持其运作，为何不能尽可能做到透明呢？

<!--en-->
Start with the nonprofit's current 990 tax filing, but never stop there. Get at least three years of forms (usually available and free at www.guidestar.org). Ask for its last three annual audits and its budgets if they aren't on the organization's website. If they aren't on the website and the nonprofit won't give them to you, ask why not? After all, a nonprofit asks the public to subsidize it with tax-exempt status and asks the public to donate to support its operations. Why would a nonprofit not want to be as transparent as possible?

#### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

伊利诺伊大学新闻学教授、前《调查记者与编辑》执行主任布兰特·休斯顿关于报道非营利组织的建议：

<!--en-->
University of Illinois journalism professor and former Investigative Reporters and Editors executive director Brant Houston on covering nonprofits:

如果您认为或知道某家非营利组织获得了联邦拨款，可访问http://harvester.census.gov/sac/.上的Federal Audit Clearinghouse网站查看相关信息。如果一家非营利组织每年使用的联邦拨款金额超过50万美元（2004年1月1日之前为30万美元），则必须向联邦管理与预算局提交所谓的“单一审计”报告，对其财务状况进行审计。该独立审计报告会发布在上述网站上并可供查询。审计报告中包含大量细节，包括拨款的来源以及该组织是否存在会计漏洞。结合其他公开记录，这些信息可以成为了解该非营利组织如何使用政府资金的宝贵资料。262 • 无利润，却有大量资金

<!--en-->
If you think or know the nonprofit gets federal grants, check out the Federal Audit Clearinghouse website at http://harvester.census.gov/sac/. If a nonprofit spends more than $500,000 in federal grant money a year ($300,000 before Jan. 1, 2004), then it must submit what is known as a “single audit” of its finances to the federal Office of Management and Budget. The independent audit is then posted and searchable at the above listed website. The audit contains lots of details, including where the grant money came from and if the organization has accounting weaknesses. Cross-referenced with other public records, it can be a rich source of information on how the nonprofit is spending government funds.
262 • No Profits, but Lots of Money

#### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

伊利诺伊大学新闻学教授、前《调查记者与编辑》执行主任布兰特·休斯顿关于报道非营利组织的建议：

<!--en-->
University of Illinois journalism professor and former Investigative Reporters and Editors executive director Brant Houston on covering nonprofits:

建立自己的非营利组织信息来源库。非营利组织存在诸多特殊的会计和法律问题，因此您需要聘请熟悉非营利组织审计的会计师以及能为其提供法律支持的律师，帮助您解读文件并分析相关人员的陈述。让您的信息来源人员先审阅相关文件，然后给出指导或意见。

<!--en-->
Build up your nonprofit source base. Nonprofits have enough special accounting and legal twists that you want to get an accountant who audits nonprofits and lawyer who represents them to help you interpret documents and dissect what people tell you. Get your sources to look at documents on background and give you directions or opinions.

但最重要的是，在完成报道之前，要准备好与非营利组织坐下来讨论您的调查结果，以便发现任何错误或误解。如果有人行为不当，您必须确保自己的判断绝对正确。同时，请记住，规模较小的非营利组织往往是由那些深怀使命感但缺乏管理经验或商业头脑的人创建和运营的。有时问题并非腐败行为，而是他们技能不足所致。

<!--en-->
But most important, be ready to sit down with a nonprofit and go over your findings before you finish writing the story so you can catch any errors or misconceptions. If someone is doing wrong, you want to be absolutely right. At the same time, remember that the smaller nonprofits are often created and run by people who care deeply about the mission, but have no management experience or business acumen. Sometimes the story is not malfeasance, but their lack of skills.

与公司财务报表不同，非营利组织的990表格并不提供与前一年财务数据的对比。要想对非营利组织的财务状况进行有效比较，记者需要查看数年的财务信息，分析其随时间的变化趋势。一份990表格仅能反映组织在年末的财务状况，类似于上市公司的资产负债表或现金流量表。北卡罗来纳大学附近的Chapel Hill-Carrboro YMCA的990表格显示，截至2008财年的收入超过520万美元，支出超过430万美元，负债为167,000美元，资产则超过490万美元。

<!--en-->
Unlike financial statements from companies, Form 990 filings for nonprofit organizations do not offer a comparison with financial figures from the previous year. To make a valid comparison about a nonprofit group's finances, a reporter needs to look at the financial information for several years to analyze the changes through time. A single Form 990 only provides a snapshot of an organization's finances at the end of the year, much like a balance sheet or cash-flow statement for a public company. The Form 990 for the Chapel Hill-Carrboro YMCA near the University of North Carolina shows that the facility had more than $5.2 million in revenue in the fiscal year ended 2008, more than $4.3 million in expenses, liabilities of $167,000, and assets of more than $4.9 million.

990表格的顶部看起来与您每年提交的纳税申报表类似。非营利组织会在其中列出其名称、地址、电话号码以及网址。文件的第一部分会显示该组织的收入、支出以及净资产的变动情况。例如，负责监督其他非营利组织的非营利组织Better Business Bureau Wise Giving Alliance在2007年的990表格中显示，其总收入为173万美元（见图12.1）。该年度的总支出为171万美元，意味着其支出几乎与收入相当。其支出中，110万美元用于各项项目，182,000美元用于管理薪资及一般开支，258,000美元用于筹款活动。

<!--en-->
The top of a Form 990 looks just like the tax return you file each year. The nonprofit lists its name, address and phone number, and Web address. The first part of the document shows the group's revenue and expenses and changes in its net assets. For example, the Form 990 from 2007 for the Better Business Bureau Wise Giving Alliance, the nonprofit group that tracks other nonprofit organizations, listed total revenue of $1.73 million (see Figure 12.1). Its expenses for the year totaled $1.71 million, meaning that it spent almost as much as it took in. Its expenses included $1.1 million for its programs, $182,000 for management salaries and general expenses, and $258,000 on fundraising.

商业记者应当将这些数字与前一年的表格数据进行对比。如果支出大幅上升而组织的收入却没有相应增长，记者应查明哪些支出增加了，并向该非营利组织的相关人员询问原因。或者，如果该组织在一年中的收入较上一年大幅增加，记者也应弄清楚原因——是政府拨款增加了，还是私人捐赠增多？这类大幅增长或波动往往都能成为报道的主题。

<!--en-->
A business journalist should look at these numbers in comparison with the previous year's filings. If expenses rose dramatically and the money being brought into the organization did not, the reporter should examine which expenses rose and ask someone at the nonprofit why this happened. Or if the amount of money that the group took in during the year increased dramatically from the previous year, the reporter should find out why. Was there an increase in government funding? Or did the nonprofit receive more in private donations? These large increases or fluctuations can often be a story.

990表格第一页的底部会列出组织在年初和年末的净资产。这些数据对于评估该组织未来的生存能力非常重要。如果其净资产在上升，说明这是一个实力较强的组织；但如果资产在下降或变为负值，则可能预示着未来会出现财务问题。根据Better Business Bureau Wise Giving Alliance的990表格，该组织在2007年末的净资产为负302,051美元，而年初的净资产则为负319,604美元（见图12.1）。

<!--en-->
The bottom of the first page of the Form 990 lists the organizations net assets at both the beginning and end of the year. These can be important numbers to assess the future viability of the group. If its net assets are rising, then it is a strong organization. But if the assets are falling or have become negative, this may be an indication of future financial problems. The Better Business Bureau Wise Giving Alliance reported net assets of minus $302,051 at the end of 2007, compared to net assets of minus $319,604 at the beginning of the year, according to its Form 990 (see Figure 12.1).

文件的第二页将组织的各项开支进一步细分，包括法律费用、办公用品费、邮资与电话费、租金、印刷与出版费以及差旅费。这些开支还会按项目、管理及筹款活动进行分类。根据网站www.guidestar.org,的说明，许多组织会将大部分开支归入“其他开支”类别，并在附件中详细列出这些开支，尽管很多开支其实可以归入某个特定类别。因此，查看附件是明智之举。事实上，Better Business Bureau Wise Giving Alliance的最大开支——超过903,400美元——属于“其他开支”项下的“人事服务”类（见图12.1）。

<!--en-->
The second page of the document breaks the expenses for the organization down into further categories, including legal expenses, supplies, postage and telephone, rent, printing and publications, and travel. These expenses are broken down for programs, management, and fundraising. According to the website www.guidestar.org, many organizations will lump most of their expenses into the “Other Expenses” category and detail those expenses in an attachment, even though most of the expenses could be included in a category. Therefore, it would be wise to look at the attachment. Indeed, the largest expense for the Better Business Bureau Wise Giving Alliance—more than $903,400—is something called “personnel services” that is listed under “Other Expenses” (see Figure 12.1).

还需注意年度总开支中用于筹款的金额占比。有人认为，筹款开支应占非营利组织总开支的一小部分。然而，对于某些组织而言，尤其是新成立的机构或那些推广不受欢迎事业的机构，筹款开支可能占据其总开支的大部分。如果一个非营利组织在筹款上投入大量资金，但收入却没有增加，那就说明其筹款工作并未取得成效。《无利润，却有大量资金》•263 表格990的下一部分用于非营利组织列举上一年的成就，但该部分仅占一页的约三分之一，空间不足以让众多机构详细说明自己的工作内容。表格的第四部分是资产负债表，显示非营利组织的资产与负债情况。这可能是些基础信息，难以用来撰写报道。但第五部分则值得关注，因为其中列出了高管、董事及核心员工的薪酬与费用报销额度。

<!--en-->
Also pay attention to the amount of money spent on fundraising in relation tothe total expenses for the year. Some believe that fundraising expenses should be a small percentage of the total expenses of a nonprofit group. However, fundraising may represent a majority of the expenses for some organizations, particularly new groups or those that are promoting an unpopular cause. If a nonprofit is spending a lot of money on fundraising but its revenue is not increasing, the fundraising has not been effective.
No Profits, but Lots of Money • 263
The next section of the Form 990 is where nonprofit organizations can list their accomplishments for the previous year, but it is only about a third of a page and does not provide enough room for many groups to detail what they have done. Part IV of the form is a balance sheet, showing the nonprofit groups assets and liabilities. This can be basic information that may not lend itself to a story. But Part V does draw attention. Part V is where the compensation and expense account allowances of officers, directors, and key employees are

*图12.1* 续：在申报文件中也有相关内容。近年来，非营利组织为吸引来自营利行业的管理者，提供了更丰厚的薪酬待遇，这为许多媒体提供了报道素材。例如，Better Business Bureau Wise Giving Alliance的表格990显示，首席执行官Herman Taylor在2007年的薪资为196,875美元，还有21,211美元的员工福利；首席运营官Bennett Weiner的薪资为125,000美元，不过他们的薪资是由Council of Better Business Bureaus Incorporated支付的，而非Wise Giving Alliance。董事会成员均未领取薪资。264 •《无利润，却有大量资金》记者应将非营利组织的薪资与上一年的数据进行比较。如果薪资没有上涨或仅略有上升，很可能没什么可写的；但如果薪资大幅上升，或者新任首席执行官的薪资远高于前任，那就有可能成为新闻话题。

<!--en-->
*Figure 12.1*
Continued overleaflisted in the filing. In recent years, nonprofit organizations have been offering larger compensation packages to attract managers from the for-profit world. This can provide stories for many media outlets. For example, the Form 990 for the Better Business Bureau Wise Giving Alliance showed that CEO Herman Taylor was paid a 2007 salary of $196,875 as well as $21,211 in employee benefits, and COO Bennett Weiner was paid a salary of $125,000, but that their salaries were paid by the Council of Better Business Bureaus Incorporated, not by the Wise Giving Alliance. None of the board members were paid a salary.
264 • No Profits, but Lots of Money
Reporters should compare the salaries at nonprofit organizations with those from the previous year. If the salaries have not increased or have gone up only slightly, there is likely nothing to write about. But if the salaries have increased dramatically or a new CEO is making much more than the previous CEO, there may be a story.
