### 专家建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《华尔街日报》法律版块负责人詹妮弗·S·福赛斯关于报道法庭案件的看法：要关注那些有趣的公司之间相互起诉的案件——例如，生产广为人知的芭比娃娃的美泰公司成功起诉了生产风骚的布拉茨娃娃的MGA娱乐公司，理由是布拉茨娃娃的设计师是在为美泰工作期间构思出这些设计的。布拉茨公司被迫停止生产该娃娃，而MGA公司则被责令向美泰支付巨额罚款。这类纠纷在试图保护自身盈利产品的竞争对手之间十分常见。沃尔玛大多选择通过诉讼而非和解来应对针对它的诉讼。原告范围很广，从在沃尔玛门店内受伤的顾客到妻子在沃尔玛停车场被绑架后遇害的丈夫都有。

<!--en-->
Wall Street Journal *law bureau chief Jennifer S. Forsyth on covering courts:*Look for interesting companies suing other interesting companies: Mattel, the maker of the ubiquitous Barbie, successfully sued MGA Entertainment Inc., which made the saucy Bratz dolls, saying that the Bratz designer came up with the plans while working for Mattel. Bratz was forced to cease making the doll and MGA was ordered to pay Mattel a sizable fine. These kinds of disputes are common between rival companies looking to protect their lucrative products.
of fighting most of the lawsuits against it instead of settling. The plaintiffs run the gamut from shoppers injured while inside one of Wal-Mart's stores to a husband whose wife was abducted in a Wal-Mart parking lot and later killed.

企业高管每天做出的决策都可能引发诉讼。事实上，有些企业目前正因已去世100多年的高管所做出的决策而面临诉讼。2002年，保险公司安泰公司、铁路运营商CSX公司以及银行FleetBoston金融公司遭到奴隶后代的起诉，这些后代要求这些企业为利用奴隶制获利而赔偿。如今，一些制造商也因半个多世纪前决定建造含有石棉的建筑物而面临数百万美元的诉讼，因为后来发现吸入石棉会导致严重疾病甚至死亡。

<!--en-->
Business executives make decisions every day that can end up in a lawsuit. In fact, some businesses are currently facing lawsuits for decisions made by company executives who have been dead for more than 100 years. In 2002, insurer Aetna Incorporated, railroad operator CSX Corporation, and bank FleetBoston Financial Corporation were sued by descendants of slaves seeking compensation from these businesses for profiting from slavery. Manufacturers are now facing multimillion-dollar lawsuits for decisions made more than a half century ago to construct buildings with asbestos, later discovered to cause serious illness and death after inhalation.

其他诉讼也可能源于一些虽不那么戏剧化但同样违法的决策。一家公司可能未经另一家公司的许可，就决定使用其拥有专利或知识产权的技术来开发新产品。某经理可能会将前雇员的人事档案信息透露给潜在的新雇主。或者，经理可能会询问女性求职者的年龄以及她是否计划在接下来的12个月内生育。所有这些行为都可能引发诉讼。

<!--en-->
Other lawsuits may result from less dramatic but nonetheless illegal decisions. A company may decide to build a new product using technology patented or owned by another company without seeking its approval. A manager may share information from a former worker's personnel file with a potential new employer. Or a manager may ask a female job candidate her age and whether she plans to have a baby in the next 12 months. All of these incidents may lead to lawsuits.

企业之间也会互相起诉。一家企业可能与另一家企业签订合同，以固定价格向其供应某种产品。但如果生产该产品的成本上升，第一家企业可能会因在该协议下亏损而试图解除合同。而接收产品的企业则可以提起诉讼，要求签约企业履行义务。

<!--en-->
Businesses also sue other businesses. One business may enter into a contract with another business to supply it with widgets for a set price. But if the cost of producing widgets goes up, the first company may seek to break the contract because it is losing money under the arrangement. The business receiving the widgets may file a lawsuit seeking to force the company that signed the contract to honor its obligation.

如果一家企业有款项应收却遭到另一家企业的拒付，它也可以起诉对方。例如，某公司为一家房地产开发商在新建住宅区的房屋背面搭建露台，但开发商认为露台搭建质量很差，因此拒绝付款。那么搭建露台的公司就可以起诉开发商以追回欠款。

<!--en-->
A business may also sue another business if it is owed money and the other company refuses to pay. For example, maybe a company built decks on the backs of houses in a new subdivision for a homebuilder, but the homebuilder believes the decks were sloppily built so it refuses to pay. The deck builder may sue the homebuilder to attempt to collect the money.

或者，当一家企业认为自己的专有产品信息遭到侵犯时，也会起诉对方。企业拥有发明的专利和品牌名称的商标权，以此防止其他企业将其用于谋取利益。当一家企业认为另一家企业侵犯了其产品权益时，就会提起诉讼，正如以下彭博新闻报道中所描述的那样，两家软件公司之间就发生过此类情况：

<!--en-->
Or a business may sue another business if it believes that its proprietary product information is being violated. Companies own patents on inventions and trademarks on brand names so that other businesses cannot use them for their gain. When a company believes another company has infringed on its products, it will file a lawsuit, as happened between two software companies, according to the following Bloomberg News report:

用于管理计算机网络的软件供应商Novell公司，对SCO集团声称Linux操作系统侵犯了其知识产权的说法提出了质疑。总部位于犹他州普罗沃的Novell公司在一份声明中表示，该公司仍拥有Unix操作系统的专利和版权。SCO方面则称Linux系统包含部分Unix代码，使用或推广Linux的公司可能需要向SCO支付Unix使用费。Unix是由AT&T公司于20世纪60年代末开发的。Novell公司在1992年购得了Unix的专利，并在1995年将部分Unix授权权利卖给了SCO。

<!--en-->
Novell Inc., whose software is used to manage computer networks, challenged claims made by SCO Group Inc. that the Linux computer operating system violates SCO's intellectual-property rights. Novell retains patents and copyrights to the Unix operating system, Provo, Utah-based Novell said in a statement. SCO has said the Linux system contains some Unix code and companies that use or promote Linux may owe SCO Unix royalties. Unix was created by AT&T Corp. in the late 1960s. Novell bought Unix patents in 1992, and in 1995 sold some Unix-licensing rights to SCO.

“1995年SCO从Novell公司购买Unix的协议并未将相关的版权转让给SCO，”Novell公司首席执行官杰克·梅斯曼在写给SCO首席执行官达尔·麦克布赖德的信中说道。

<!--en-->
"The 1995 agreement governing SCO's purchase of Unix from Novell does not convey to SCO the associated copyrights," Novell Chief Executive Jack Messman said in a letter to SCO Chief Executive Darl McBride.

上周将名称从Caldera International Inc.改为SCO的该公司正在起诉国际商业机器公司，指控IBM销售和推广的Linux软件中包含了部分Unix代码，因此IBM应向SCO支付版税。SCO已警告另外1,500家企业，它们也可能面临诉讼。分析人士表示，SCO的法律威胁可能会阻碍IBM和甲骨文公司推动企业采用Linux的努力。法庭即将开庭 • 279 SCO在一份声明中表示：“SCO对IBM的诉讼不涉及专利或版权问题”，并补充称IBM的投诉“明确指出了合同违约行为。”

<!--en-->
SCO, which last week changed its name from Caldera International Inc.,is suing International Business Machines Corp., charging that the Linux software sold and promoted by IBM contains some of the Unix code and that IBM owes SCO royalties. SCO has warned 1,500 other companies that they may face lawsuits. IBM and Oracle Corp.'s campaigns to get companies to embrace Linux may be crimped by SCO's legal threats, analysts have said.
Headed to Court • 279
"SCO's lawsuit against IBM does not involve patents or copyrights," SCO said in a statement, adding that the IBM complaint "specifically alleges breach of contract."

SCO称其“拥有合同权利，可以阻止任何Unix供应商将Unix代码、方法或概念不当地引入Linux”。¹ 如果一家企业认为另一家企业通过窃取其客户等方式干扰了其正常运营，它也会提起诉讼。例如，银行或其他贷款机构如果发现某家公司未能偿还贷款，也可以对其提起诉讼；或者，一家企业如果觉得自己投资的公司表现未达预期，也可以对该公司提起诉讼。

<!--en-->
SCO said it "has the contractual right to prevent improper donations of Unix code, methods or concepts into Linux by any Unix vendor."¹
A business will also file a lawsuit if it believes that another business is interfering with its ability to operate by, for example, stealing its customers. A business such as a bank or another lender may file a lawsuit against another business if that company is not repaying its loan. Or, a business may sue a business in which it is an investor if it feels as if the company in which it has invested in is not performing the way it wants.

许多与企业相关的诉讼甚至可能不值得用一段文字来报道。是否报道这些诉讼中的指控，由记者和编辑决定。*《华盛顿邮报》*不太可能报道马里兰州贝塞斯达的一家小型便利店因薯片供应商一个月未供货导致其损失销售额而提起的诉讼。但在那个小镇上，这家店可能是为数不多的薯片销售点之一，这样的诉讼或许就具有新闻价值。

<!--en-->
Many business-related lawsuits may not merit even a one-paragraph brief. It is up to the reporter and the editor to decide if the allegations in the lawsuit warrant coverage. *The Washington Post* is not likely to write a story about a small convenience store in Bethesda, Maryland, filing a lawsuit against its potato chip supplier for failing to provide a shipment one month, causing it to lose sales. But that lawsuit may be news in a small town where the store could be one of the few places selling potato chips.

在涉及企业的任何诉讼案件中，记者都应阅读完整的诉讼文件，评估指控的严重性以及所要求的赔偿金额。原始文件中可能会提及多项指控。原告和被告——双方都可能不止一方——也会被明确列出。在许多企业诉讼中，还会注明他们的总部所在地及具体地址。这有助于记者联系到该公司的相关人员以获取回应。

<!--en-->
With any litigation involving a business, a reporter should read the entire filing, assessing the seriousness of the allegations and what damages are being sought. Multiple allegations may be mentioned in the original filing. The plaintiffs and the defendants—there can be more than one on both sides—are also specifically identified. In many business lawsuits, their headquarters location is named and an address is given. This can help a reporter find someone to talk to at the company to get a response.

在一些企业诉讼中，企业可能会请求法官下达临时禁令，阻止另一家公司采取可能对其造成损害的行动。许多诉讼仅要求赔偿损失。有些文件会提及作为赔偿金额的具体数额。在报道任何与企业相关的案件时，都应包含这一数额。

<!--en-->
In some corporate lawsuits, a business may ask for a judge to issue a temporary restraining order preventing another company from taking some action that may hurt the business. Many lawsuits simply ask for damages. Some filings may mention a monetary amount as a remedy for damages. This amount should be included in any story about a business-related case.

关于企业诉讼的报道应包含的重要信息包括：

<!--en-->
Important information to be included in any story about business litigation includes:

1. 原告和被告的姓名及其业务关系；
2. 这些企业的背景信息，这类信息通常会在诉讼文件中找到；
3. 案件中所声称的损害类型。例如，当两家香烟制造商Liggett Group和Brooke Group起诉二十多家公司时[^3043]：¹ 来自2003年5月28日Bloomberg News发布的J. Kelly撰写的文章《Novell称其拥有Unix权利，质疑SCO的主张》，版权归Bloomberg L.P.所有，经许可转载。280 • 法庭即将开庭

<!--en-->
1. The names of the plaintiffs and the defendants and their business relationship;
2. Background on these businesses, which is often contained in the lawsuit;
3. The type of damage alleged in the case. For example, when Liggett Group and Brooke Group, two cigarette makers, sued two-dozen
[^3043]: ¹ From "Novell says it owns Unix rights, challenges SCO claim," by J. Kelly, May 28, 2003, Bloomberg News. Copyright 2003 by Bloomberg L.P. All rights reserved. Reprinted with permission.
280 • Headed to Court

### 报道企业法庭案件时的信息来源

<!--en-->
*Sources When Covering Business Court Cases*

1. **法院书记员**：他或她会知道诉讼、取证和证据提交的时间。
2. **律师**：可与代表原告和被告的律师交谈。
3. **法官的行政助理**：他们可以告知法官的日程安排，从而帮助了解即将作出的裁决。
4. **原告和被告**：双方都希望自己的观点能被听取。

<!--en-->
1. **The clerk of the court:** He or she will know when lawsuits, depositions, and exhibits are filed.
2. **Lawyers:** Talk to the attorneys representing the plaintiffs and the defendants.
3. **Administrative assistants for judges:** They can tell you who is on the judge's calendar, giving you an indication of upcoming rulings.
4. **The plaintiffs and defendants:** Both will want to have their side of the story heard.

#### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《华尔街日报》法律部主管Jennifer S. Forsyth关于报道法庭案件的建议：

<!--en-->
Wall Street Journal *law bureau chief Jennifer S. Forsyth on covering courts:*

**诉讼能够揭示企业是否善待其员工**：员工——尤其是那些被解雇的员工——常常会以种族、性别或年龄为由提起歧视诉讼。这类歧视案件通常在联邦法院提起，这对记者来说是好消息，因为联邦法院的记录比州法院的记录更易于在线获取，尽管越来越多的州法院也在逐步实现网络化。同时也要留意在法院提交的举报人投诉，这些是由那些因揭露上司的违规行为而遭受恶劣对待的员工提出的。由于联邦法律限制企业惩罚举报人，这类诉讼的数量正在上升。他们还指控保险公司拒绝赔付本应在其保险范围内得到赔偿的吸烟者；

<!--en-->
**Lawsuits can show whether companies are doing right by the people who work for them:** Employees—particularly those who have been fired—often file suits claiming they have been discriminated against on the basis of their race, gender, or age. Discrimination cases often are filed in federal court, which is good news for reporters as federal-court records are easier to access online than state-court filings, though more and more state courts are now going online. Also keep a look out for whistleblower complaints filed at the courthouse. These are brought by employees who claim they were treated poorly because they exposed wrongdoing by their bosses. These suits are on the rise due to federal laws that restrict companies from penalizing whistleblowers.
insurance companies, they alleged the insurers were refusing to pay claims to smokers who should have been covered under their policies;

4. 诉讼的提起时间以及所在法院；
5. 诉讼双方的历史背景，有时也会在最初的起诉状中详细说明；
6. 在起诉文件中提出的任何特殊要求，例如永久性或临时性的禁令或限制令。报道与商业相关的诉讼时，记者还需要联系原告和被告以获取他们的回应。公司高管往往不会发表评论，最好联系公司的公关人员或代表公司的律师。为使报道客观公正，记者应尽力从双方获取意见。在最初的起诉状提交后，被告将有机会通过自己的诉状对指控作出回应。大多数情况下，他们会否认有任何不当行为。如果案件规模足够大，也应报道他们的回应。很多时候，案件在进入法庭审理之前就会达成和解。和解与判决通常是在双方就案件观点进行辩论的听证会之后做出的。听证会以及判决都可能具有新闻价值，记者应随时关注这些进展。法庭案件中有很多可能具有新闻价值的听证会。记者不应只报道诉讼的最初提交情况，然后就等待审判开始，其间还有很多新闻可报。

<!--en-->
4. When the lawsuit was filed and in which court;
5. History between the two parties of the lawsuit, again sometimes detailed in the initial complaint;
6. Any special considerations, such as permanent or temporary injunctions or restraining orders, sought in the filing.
Writing stories about business-related lawsuits also requires the reporter to call both the plaintiff and the defendant to obtain a reaction. Company executives often will not comment. It is best to go to the public relations staff or the lawyers representing the company. The reporter should try hard to get a comment from both sides to make the story fair. After the original complaint has been filed, the defendant will have a chance to respond to the charges with their own filing. Most of the time, they will deny any wrongdoing. If the case is large enough, their response should also be reported.
Many times, the case will be settled before it goes to court. Settlements and rulings usually come after hearings related to the case in which both sides of the lawsuit argue their point of view. The hearing, as well as the ruling, might be newsworthy, and the reporter should keep up to date on such developments.
There are many hearings involved in court cases that might be newsworthy. Journalists should not just report on the initial filing of the lawsuit and then wait until the trial begins. There is plenty of news occurring between the two.

## 员工相关诉讼

<!--en-->
*Employee-Related Litigation*

一名女员工走进休息室，发现男同事们正在杂志上观看其他女性的裸照。一名男性求职者想进入一家餐厅工作，但餐厅以该职位只招女性为由拒绝了他。一名男性主管对已婚女下属发表暧昧言论，并邀请她下班后一起喝酒。另一名员工请求接受培训以便未来获得晋升机会，但被拒绝。一名工厂工人某周工作了60小时，却只获得了40小时的工资。还有一名工人因工作中吸入灰尘而病重，不得不在医院休养三周。

<!--en-->
A female worker walks into a break room and finds male workers reviewing nude pictures of other women in a magazine. A male worker wants a job at a restaurant, but the restaurant declines to hire him, saying that they only hire females for the job that he wants. A male supervisor makes suggestive comments to a married female subordinate and asks her out for a drink after work. Another worker asks for training so that she can be considered for future promotions but is denied the opportunity. A factory worker spends 60 hours on the job one week, but is only paid for 40 of those hours. Another worker becomes seriously ill because of the dust inhaled while on the job and has to spend three weeks in the hospital recuperating.

以上都是可能导致员工起诉雇主以追偿工作中遭受损失的案例。根据美国司法部的研究，1990年至1998年间，联邦法院受理的员工诉讼数量增加了两倍。全国各地的州法院中的此类诉讼数量很可能也有所上升。

<!--en-->
All of the above are examples of incidents that may lead employees to sue their employer to recoup damages suffered while on the job. The number of employee lawsuits filed in federal courts tripled between 1990 and 1998, according to a U.S. Department of Justice study. They likely increased in state courts around the country as well.

员工对企业提起的诉讼是很好的报道素材，这又是“大卫对抗歌利亚”的场景。例如，一名普通员工起诉一家价值数十亿美元的公司，而该公司将这名员工视为用来提升利润和效率的工具。倘若员工诉讼真有那么非黑即白就好了。实际上，在员工诉讼中往往存在许多灰色地带。的确，员工可能受到了不公平对待，但公司真的要为此负责吗？

<!--en-->
Employee lawsuits against businesses make for good stories. They are David versus Goliath all over again. For example, an average employee sues a multibillion-dollar corporation that views him as an ant to be used to increase its profits and improve its productivity. If only employee lawsuits were that black and white. Too often, there are many shades of gray when it comes to employee litigation. Yes, an employee might have been mistreated. But is the company responsible?

可以肯定的是，在数千起案件中，工人们已经击败了现任或前任雇主并获得了赔偿。他们因未获得加班费而提起诉讼并胜诉，比如下文摘录中描述的沃尔玛事件：

<!--en-->
To be sure, in thousands of cases workers have defeated their current or formeremployer and won damages. They sue and win for not receiving overtime pay, such as what happened to Wal-Mart as described in the following excerpt:

即将开庭 • 281 据周四的一个联邦陪审团裁定，全球最大的零售商沃尔玛在1994年至1999年间强迫俄勒冈州的员工无偿加班，这是全国范围内数十起此类诉讼中首例进入庭审的案件。

<!--en-->
Headed to Court • 281
Wal-Mart, the world's largest retailer, forced employees in Oregon to work unpaid overtime between 1994 and 1999, a federal jury found Thursday in the first of dozens of such lawsuits across the country to come to trial.

还将另举行一场庭审，以确定沃尔玛商店应支付多少赔偿金。沃尔玛在俄勒冈州的27家门店中有24家的400多名员工起诉了这家零售商。

<!--en-->
A separate trial will be held to decide how much Wal-Mart Stores should pay in damages. More than 400 employees from 24 of Wal-Mart's 27 Oregon stores sued the retailer.

“基本上，我们对这一裁决感到失望。沃尔玛有一项明确的政策，即为所有工作时间支付报酬，”发言人比尔·沃茨说道。“我们想强调，这一裁决仅影响俄勒冈州15,000名员工中的大约350人。”

<!--en-->
"I guess, basically, we are disappointed with the verdict. Wal-Mart has a strong policy of paying its associates for all the time they work," said spokesman Bill Wertz. "We would emphasize that this ruling affects only approximately 350 workers out of 15,000 in Oregon."

提起这场诉讼的是曾在塞勒姆地区沃尔玛门店担任管理职务的卡罗琳·蒂布斯和贝蒂·奥尔德森。

<!--en-->
The lawsuit was filed by Carolyn Thiebes and Betty Alderson, who worked in managerial positions at Wal-Mart stores in the Salem area.

诉讼称，管理人员通过要求员工在下班后清理店铺以及从考勤记录中删除工作时间的方式，迫使员工继续工作。

<!--en-->
The lawsuit alleged that managers got employees to work off the clock by asking them to clean up the store after they had clocked out and by deleting hours from time records.

诉讼还指出，沃尔玛会斥责那些申请加班费的员工。原告表示，由于管理人员分配的工作量超出了正常班次所能完成的范围，员工们感到被迫在下班后继续工作。

<!--en-->
It also said Wal-Mart reprimanded employees who claimed overtime. Workers felt forced to work after clocking out because managers assigned them more work than they could complete in a regular shift, the plaintiffs said.

沃尔玛在周二的开庭陈述中承认确实存在一些下班后工作的情况，但声称公司政策明确禁止此类行为。

<!--en-->
Wal-Mart conceded during opening arguments Tuesday that some off-the-clock work occurred but said company policy expressly prohibited it.

沃尔玛是一家价值2180亿美元的公司，在美国拥有3250家门店，雇佣了100万名员工。在判决宣布后，沃尔玛的律师鲁迪·恩格伦德未作任何评论，而是将问题转交给了沃尔玛总部。沃茨表示公司正在考虑是否提出上诉。该判决是在股市收盘后作出的。在纽约证券交易所，沃尔玛当天的股价下跌22美分，收于50.16美元。

<!--en-->
Wal-Mart, a $218 billion company, employs 1 million workers in 3,250 stores in the United States. Rudy Englund, Wal-Mart's attorney, had no comment after the verdict was read, but referred questions to Wal-Mart headquarters. Wertz said the company is considering whether to appeal. The verdict came after the close of the stock market. Wal-Mart finished the day down 22 cents at $50.16 on the New York Stock Exchange.

目前还有39起集体诉讼正在30个州针对该公司展开。这些来自加利福尼亚州到纽约州的诉讼涉及数十万名员工，他们要求获得数千万美元的欠薪赔偿。

<!--en-->
Thirty-nine other class-action lawsuits are pending against the company in 30 states. Those suits, from California to New York, involve hundreds of thousands of workers seeking tens of millions in back pay.

此前，沃尔玛已在科罗拉多州和新墨西哥州解决了两起类似的加班费纠纷案件。

<!--en-->
Previously, Wal-Mart settled two similar overtime cases in Colorado and New Mexico.

据报道，两年前沃尔玛为解决一起涉及科罗拉多州69,000名员工的非工作时间工作纠纷案，支付了5000万美元；另一位原告律师称，沃尔玛最近还以50万美元的价格解决了一起涉及新墨西哥州加勒普市120名员工的类似案件。

<!--en-->
The company reportedly paid $50 million two years ago to settle an off-the-clock lawsuit covering 69,000 workers in Colorado, and it recently settled for $500,000 a case involving 120 workers in Gallup, N.M., said one of the plaintiffs' attorneys.

审判持续了大约四周，陪审团用了四天时间才作出裁决。

<!--en-->
The trial lasted about four weeks, and jurors took four days to arrive at their decision.

俄勒冈大学伦德奎斯特商学院院长菲利普·罗梅罗表示：“大概每过一两年，沃尔玛就会因劳动关系问题遭遇一些小麻烦。但它们依然不断扩张。因此我认为这不会对其形象和销售业绩造成实质性影响。”² [^3074]：² 摘自美联社2002年12月20日W.麦克卡尔撰写的《沃尔玛在加班费案中被判有罪》，版权归2002年美联社所有，经许可转载。282 • 前往法庭 注意这篇报道中的细节，比如案件审理所需的时间以及陪审团商议的时间。同时注意商学院院长的评论。引入法律专家或商业专家的分析总能增强文章的可信度，并有助于阐明更宏观的情况。

<!--en-->
"About once every one or two years, Wal-Mart suffers a minor black eye about something relating to labor relations," said Philip Romero, dean of the Lundquist College of Business at the University of Oregon. "Yet they keep growing and growing. So I don't believe this will materially affect their image and their sales."²
[^3074]: ² From "Wal-Mart guilty in overtime case," by W. McCall, December 20, 2002, Associated Press. Copyright 2002 by Associated Press. Reprinted with permission.
282 • Headed to Court
Note the details in this story, such as how long the case took to hear and how long the jury deliberated. Also note the comment from the business school dean. Getting analysis from a law expert or a business expert always lends credence to the writing and helps explain the bigger picture.

这篇报道还提供了沃尔玛在其他地区类似案件中的情况作为参考。如果记者在追踪一家在全国范围内运营的大型企业的案件，了解其在其他州类似案件中的表现或许是个明智之举。关于那些诉讼的报道可能会为读者提供看待该案件的新的视角。

<!--en-->
The story also provides the perspective of what is happening to Wal-Mart in similar cases in other parts of the country. If a reporter is tracking a case of a large company that operates throughout the country, it might be smart to see how the business has fared in similar cases in other states. A story about those lawsuits might give readers a fresh viewpoint on the case.

有时，员工对公司提起的诉讼最初是由一名员工单独发起的，随后其他认为自己遭遇类似待遇的员工也会加入成为原告。这类诉讼通常被归类为集体诉讼，以代表全体前员工。此类案件可能涉及歧视、骚扰或其他招聘行为。

<!--en-->
Sometimes suits filed by employees against companies begin as one lawsuit by one employee, and then other employees who believe they have been treated in a similar manner join as plaintiffs. Sometimes these suits are classified as class action lawsuits to represent a body of former workers. Cases like this can involve discrimination, harassment, or other hiring practices.

与员工相关的案件往往要求记者深入调查工作环境。如果记者希望向读者或观众展现在公司工作的真实状况，他可以查阅其他文件，如平等就业机会委员会的备案资料、针对该公司的其他诉讼文件以及职业安全与健康管理局的记录。

<!--en-->
Employee-related cases often require the reporter to dig deeper into the workplace environment. If a reporter is interested in giving readers or viewers a broader picture of what it is like to work at a company, he can review other documents, such as Equal Employment Opportunity Commission filings, other lawsuits filed against the company, and Occupational Safety and Health Administration records.

与员工相关的诉讼并不总是由陪审团来裁决。2002年12月，一个仲裁小组裁定证券经纪商所罗门史密森巴尼公司需向一名女证券经纪人支付320万美元，作为对该公司性歧视集体诉讼案的和解款项。这个由三名成员组成的小组的裁决，是针对那些无法与公司达成协议的原告所采取的争议解决程序中首次出现的裁决。

<!--en-->
Employee-related lawsuits may not always be decided by a trial jury. In December 2002, an arbitration panel ordered stockbroker Salomon Smith Barney to pay $3.2 million to a female stockbroker as part of a settlement of a sex discrimination class-action lawsuit against the firm. The three-member panel's decision was the first to come out of a dispute resolution process for plaintiffs who could not come to terms with the company.

有时案件会被提交给调解人或仲裁员来解决纠纷。调解和仲裁也常用于国际商业诉讼中。很多时候，一方或另一方会建议采用这种程序来结案，以此降低成本。

<!--en-->
Cases sometimes will be referred to a mediator or an arbitrator to resolve the dispute. Mediation and arbitration are also often used in international business litigation. Many times, one side or the other will suggest this procedure to settle a case as a way of lowering the costs.

此外，与员工相关的诉讼通常还包括与公司相关的其他文件，如员工合同和内部备忘录，这些文件可能更能反映工作条件。应当仔细阅读这些合同和文件，它们能为报道增添生动的细节和趣闻。

<!--en-->
In addition, employee-related lawsuits often include other documents related to a company, such as employee contracts and internal memos that may give a better indication of working conditions. These contracts and documents should be read carefully. They might add good color and anecdotes to a story.

这些员工合同还可能导致企业起诉现任及前任员工。如果企业认为某名前员工窃取了信息或文件并将其带到了新工作单位，尤其是当该员工为竞争对手工作时，企业就会对其提起诉讼。许多公司会使用竞业禁止协议或合同条款，要求员工在一定时间内不得为直接竞争对手工作。

<!--en-->
Those employee contracts can also lead to a business suing current and former workers. Businesses will sue a former employee if they believe that the ex-worker has stolen information or documents and taken them to a new job, particularly if the person is working for a competitor. Many companies use noncompete agreements or clauses in contracts requiring their workers to abstain from working for a direct competitor for a certain amount of time.

竞业限制协议用于保护商业秘密。商业秘密是指那些能为企业带来竞争优势的信息，因为它们并不为公众所知，其他可能从中获益的企业也无法轻易获取。它可以是企业为保密而付出合理努力的配方、图案、汇编资料、程序、设备、方法、技术或流程。

<!--en-->
Noncompete agreements protect trade secrets. A trade secret can be information that gives a company a competitive advantage because it is not generally known and cannot be readily learned by other businesses that could benefit from it. It can be a formula, pattern, compilation, program, device, method, technique, or process that a company has made reasonable efforts to keep secret.

例如，可口可乐会限制公司内部知晓其著名软饮料秘方的人员范围。如果这些员工中的某人离开公司，竞业限制协议很可能会禁止他们使用该秘方。（加利福尼亚州法律仅在极少数情况下允许竞业限制协议。）走向法庭 • 283 下文摘录讲述了一起案件，其中一项竞业限制协议因一家电信公司从另一家公司挖走高管而成为重大新闻。

<!--en-->
For example, Coca-Cola limits who at the company knows the secret formula to make its famous soft drink. If one of those employees were to leave the company, they would likely have a noncompete agreement preventing them fromusing the formula. (California law excludes noncompete agreements except in narrow instances.)
Headed to Court • 283
The following excerpt details a case in which a noncompete agreement became a major story regarding the hiring of an executive by one telecommunications company away from another.

斯普林特公司周日宣布，威廉·T·埃斯雷计划辞去首席执行官职务，该公司已将该职位提供给贝尔南方公司的副主席加里·福尔西。

<!--en-->
Sprint Corp. on Sunday said William T. Esrey plans to step down as chief executive and the company has offered the job to Gary Forsee, vice chairman of BellSouth Corp.

然而，贝尔南方正试图通过法律手段阻止福尔西的转岗。斯普林特在周日晚发布的一份简短声明中，实际上证实了数日来的猜测。

<!--en-->
BellSouth, however, is trying to block Forsee's move in court. In a brief statement released Sunday evening, Sprint effectively confirmed days of speculation.

声明称，“我们的独立董事一直在评估管理层的继任方案。”但并未说明董事会是否要求埃斯雷离职，或是该首席执行官因其他原因辞职。

<!--en-->
The statement said its “independent directors have been evaluating management succession alternatives.” It did not say whether the board asked Esrey to leave, or if the chief executive is resigning for other reasons.

声明表示，埃斯雷将在“过渡期内”担任斯普林特的董事长。声明还称，目前埃斯雷以及总裁兼首席运营官罗纳德·T·勒梅仍“将继续在斯普林特担任现有职务”。

<!--en-->
The statement said Esrey will be chairman of Sprint “for a transition period.” For now, Esrey and president and chief operating officer Ronald T. LeMay will “remain in their current positions with Sprint,” the statement said.

长期以来被视为埃斯雷接班人的勒梅也预计会离开该公司。

<!--en-->
LeMay, long considered Esrey's successor, also is expected to leave the company.

斯普林特公司官员周日拒绝进一步解释日益复杂的管理层状况。

<!--en-->
Sprint officials declined Sunday to shed further light on an increasingly murky management situation.

董事会成员小欧文·O·霍卡迪说：“我只想说，声明本身已经说得很清楚了。随着事态发展，如果需要或适当的话，即便不是必须，我们也会提供更多信息。”³ 其他公司会要求员工，尤其是高管，在离职时签署规定离职后行为的协议。这些协议可能会在满足某些条件（如不公开向媒体谈论自己在公司的任职经历）的前提下，为高管提供经济补偿。有些公司曾起诉违反这些离职协议的前员工。

<!--en-->
“I'm just going to tell you the statement speaks for itself,” said board member Irvine O. Hockaday, Jr. “As events progress and it becomes either required or appropriate, even if not required, to offer additional information, that will be done.”³
Other companies require employees, particularly executives, to sign agreements when they leave the company that set out post-employment guidelines. These agreements may provide the executives a monetary settlement in return for certain conditions, such as not publicly talking to the media about their tenure at the company. Some companies have sued former employees who have broken these severance package deals.

另一方面，如果公司未能履行协议义务，离职后的高管也可以起诉该公司。如果公司的高管对前同事进行诋毁，损害其找到新工作的能力，该公司就可能被起诉。或者，如果公司未按照离职协议的规定支付款项或其他约定内容，前高管也可以起诉该公司。

<!--en-->
On the other side, executives can also sue businesses after they have left the job if the company has not lived up to its side of the agreement. A business can be sued if its executives talk disparagingly about the former coworker, hurting his or her ability to get another job. Or a former executive can sue a company if the business does not uphold the terms of the severance agreement by providing payments or other terms agreed upon in the contract.

联邦百货公司前首席执行官艾伦·奎斯特罗姆因挽救梅西百货和里奇百货的运营免于破产而广受赞誉。但他退休后却起诉了该公司，称该公司欠他[^3098]：³ 摘自D. 海耶斯和S. 金2003年2月3日发表于《堪萨斯城星报》A1版的文章《斯普林特称首席执行官即将更替：埃斯雷将卸任，福尔西获聘，但贝尔南方获得法院命令留住他》，版权所有2003年《堪萨斯城星报》，经许可转载。284 • 走向法庭

<!--en-->
Allen Questrom, the former CEO of Federated Department Stores, was widely celebrated for saving the operator of Macy's and Rich's department stores from bankruptcy. But he sued the company after retiring, saying the company owed
[^3098]: ³ From “CEO change near, Sprint says: Esrey stepping down; Forsee offered job, but BellSouth gets court order to keep him,” by D. Hayes and S. King, February 3, 2003, *Kansas City Star*, p. A1. Copyright 2003 by *Kansas City Star*. Reprinted with permission.
284 • Headed to Court

### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《华尔街日报》法律部主管詹妮弗·S·福赛思谈法庭报道：

<!--en-->
Wall Street Journal *law bureau chief Jennifer S. Forsyth on covering courts:*

**不要低估白领犯罪的重要性：**法庭报道通常让人联想到满身是血的受害者和持刀的被告，但实际上，诈骗犯伯纳德·麦道夫通过其价值数十亿美元的庞氏骗局摧毁的生命数量，远超世界上任何连环杀手。窃取他人钱财的人也是值得关注的新闻人物，他们的受害者令人同情，而且当麦道夫不得不在法庭上面对受害者时，场面极具戏剧性。不过要记住，尽管麦道夫被判150年监禁，许多白领罪犯却只被判处较轻的刑期。

<!--en-->
**Don't diminish the importance of white-collar crime:** Courts coverage usually connotes bloody victims and knife-wielding defendants, but the swindler Bernard Madoff ruined many more lives with his multi-billion dollar Ponzi scheme than any serial killer the world has known. People who steal other people's money are big stories with sympathetic victims and there was great drama when he had to face his victims in court. Keep in mind, though, despite Madoff's 150-year prison sentence, many white-collar criminals get light prison sentences.

#### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《华尔街日报》法律部主管詹妮弗·S·福赛思谈法庭报道：

<!--en-->
Wall Street Journal *law bureau chief Jennifer S. Forsyth on covering courts:*

**诉讼能够揭露企业未妥善对待投资者的行为：**这类纠纷通常表现为证券欺诈诉讼，指控企业未向投资者披露所有应公开的信息。这些诉讼可以以集体诉讼的形式提起，即众多投资者联合行动。集体诉讼的透明度极高：各方必须公开披露和解条款，而提起集体诉讼的律师甚至需要公开其期望获得的费用数额。他被要求支付超过4500万美元的欠薪。法官驳回了他的诉讼，此后Questrom成为了竞争对手J.C. Penney的首席执行官。

<!--en-->
**Lawsuits can reveal when companies aren't doing right by their investors:** These disputes often come in the form of securities fraud litigation, which allege that the company didn't disclose to investors everything it was required to. These suits can be brought as class actions, in which many investors band together. Class actions are unusually transparent: parties must publicly disclose the terms of their settlements, and the lawyers filing the class actions suits are even required to divulge the amount of fees they hope to earn.
him more than $45 million in back pay. A judge ruled against his case, and Questrom later became the CEO of rival J.C. Penney.

雇主若披露员工个人生活信息，可能会自食恶果。在许多情况下，除非有正当的商业理由，企业不得讨论前员工的财务状况、婚姻状况或其他个人问题。在某些州，如果前员工的前雇主向潜在新雇主提供虚假信息以干扰其就业机会，前员工可对其提起诉讼。

<!--en-->
Employers can get themselves into trouble by disclosing information about a worker's personal life. In many cases, businesses are not allowed to discuss a former worker's financial status, marital status, or other personal issues unless there is a legitimate business reason for disclosing them. And in some states, an ex-worker can sue his or her former place of employment if they give false information to a potential new employer in a bid to interfere with his or her job prospects.

在大多数州，雇主因员工参与工会活动而将其“列入黑名单”是违法的。这一法律也适用于推荐信，要求推荐信不得包含虚假或诽谤性内容。

<!--en-->
In a majority of states, it is illegal for an employer to “blacklist” a former worker for participating in union activities. This law can apply to letters of recommendation, requiring them to be written without false and defamatory statements.

## 企业与刑事指控

<!--en-->
*Businesses and Criminal Charges*

现已声名狼藉的纽约投资者伯纳德·麦道夫承认诈骗客户，很可能将在狱中度过余生。前ImClone Systems首席执行官萨姆·瓦克斯尔因内幕交易罪被判七年监禁。康复医院连锁企业HealthSouth的近十几名前高管承认犯有刑事欺诈和共谋罪，该公司前首席执行官理查德·斯克鲁希目前也在得克萨斯州的监狱中。

<!--en-->
Bernard Madoff, the now infamous New York investor who pled guilty to defrauding his clients, will likely spend the rest of his life in jail. Former ImClone Systems CEO Sam Waksal was sentenced to seven years in prison after pleading guilty to insider trading charges. Nearly a dozen former executives at rehabilitation hospital chain HealthSouth pleaded guilty to criminal fraud and conspiracy charges, and former company CEO Richard Scrushy currently sits in a Texas prison.

所有这些案件都涉及针对大型企业及其高管的刑事犯罪指控。越来越多的州政府和联邦政府机构因企业高管诈骗投资者、会计师、商业伙伴等而对其提起刑事指控。商业领域的犯罪报道以往并不常见，但有时会成为新闻的重点。

<!--en-->
All of these cases involve charges of criminal wrongdoing against major companies and their executives. Increasingly, state and federal government agencies are bringing criminal charges against company executives for defrauding investors, accountants, business partners, and others. Crime reporting has never been common in the business world, but sometimes it becomes a major part of the story.

这些故事常常成为头版新闻。它们往往对一家企业来说是重大事件，也预示着该企业可能面临财务困境。

<!--en-->
These stories often become front-page news. They are often a major development for a company and signal that the business may be in financial trouble.

美国证券交易委员会和司法部可对涉嫌违规的上市公司展开刑事调查，正如2003年6月他们对抵押贷款公司Freddie Mac所做的那样，该公司的三名高层因此被免职。司法部的刑事部门负责调查各类商业犯罪，如企业欺诈计划、金融机构欺诈、证券欺诈、保险欺诈、涉及医疗保险等政府项目的欺诈行为，以及违反《反海外腐败法》的贿赂外国政府官员等国际犯罪活动。

<!--en-->
The SEC and the Justice Department can launch criminal investigations into public companies suspected of wrongdoing, as they did in June 2003 with Freddie Mac, the mortgage company that ousted three top executives as a result. The Criminal Division of the Justice Department investigates business crimes, such as corporate fraud schemes; financial institution fraud; securities fraud; insurance fraud; fraud involving government programs like Medicare; and international criminal activities, including bribery of foreign government officials in violation of the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act.

此外，美国证券交易委员会的执法部门负责调查违反联邦证券法的行为，并在联邦法院通过民事诉讼处理相关案件。该部门经常申请禁令，违反禁令的人可能会被处以罚款或监禁。其处理的许多案件涉及欺诈行为，如虚假股票发行、市场操纵、非法内幕交易，或是经纪人违反证券法的行为。

<!--en-->
In addition, the SEC's Division of Enforcement investigates violations of the federal securities laws andprosecutes cases using civil lawsuits in federal courts. It often seeks injunctions, and a person who violates an injunction can be subject to fines or a prison term. Many of its cases involve fraud, such as fraudulent stock offerings, manipulations, illegal insider trading, or conduct by brokers in violation of securities laws.

近年来，司法部还针对电话营销欺诈、身份盗窃和网络欺诈等手段展开了调查。司法部律师也可能与其他联邦机构合作起诉企业。2003年6月，一家心脏手术设备制造商承认隐瞒产品故障，而这些故障可能导致数十人死亡。Guidant Corporation的子公司Endovascular Technologies同意支付超过9200万美元的民事和刑事罚款。该案件的调查由美国食品药品监督管理局和司法部共同负责。

<!--en-->
In recent years, the Justice Department has also developed cases directed at schemes such as telemarketing fraud, identity theft, and Internet fraud. Justice Department attorneys may also work with other federal agencies to prosecute companies. In June 2003, a manufacturer of heart surgery devices pleaded guiltyto hiding malfunctions in its products that may have caused a dozen deaths. Endovascular Technologies, a subsidiary of Guidant Corporation, agreed to pay more than $92 million in civil and criminal penalties. The Food and Drug Administration and the Justice Department handled the investigation of the case.

In addition, the IRS can investigate and prosecute companies for attempting to evade taxes, willfully failing to file returns, submitting false tax forms, or otherwise attempting to defraud taxpayers.

所谓的白领犯罪案件可能源自多个不同领域，不一定涉及企业高管。商业犯罪案件也可能涉及消费者诈骗企业的情况。

<!--en-->
So-called white-collar crime cases can result from a number of different areas and do not always have to involve a business executive. Criminal business cases can also involve consumers defrauding companies.

即便是小城镇的报纸和广播电台，也能报道引人注目的商业犯罪故事，以下来自弗吉尼亚州西部乡村地区的《列克星敦新闻报》的报道标题便说明了这一点：

<!--en-->
Even small-town newspapers and radio stations can produce compelling stories about business crime, as the top of the following story from the *Lexington News-Gazette* in rural western Virginia illustrates:

白领犯罪可能像被拒付的支票一样令人烦恼，也可能像冒充急救人员的人那样危险。

<!--en-->
White-collar crime can be as annoying as a bounced check, or as dangerous as a person posing as a paramedic.

9月，卡罗琳·凯特·斯梅德利在洛克布里奇县因32项伪造支票的罪名被判处8年监禁，其中5年4个月的刑期暂缓执行。她还被责令赔偿4,148.64美元。

<!--en-->
In September, Carolyn Kate Smedley was sentenced in Rockbridge County to eight years in prison on 32 counts of forging checks, with five years and four months of that sentence suspended. She was also ordered to make restitution of $4,148.64.

通过伪造文件，一名北卡罗来纳州的男子不仅得以加入列克星敦救生与急救队，还进入了石墙杰克逊医院工作。34岁的大卫·哈罗德·苏伊特利用这些假文件在2001年5月至7月间接听了约60通电话。其中一通电话是打往81号州际公路的，当时VDOT的工作人员丹尼·凯格利遭卡车撞击。由于苏伊特自称拥有急救员资格，他便负责指挥现场救援人员。几天后，凯格利在卡尔顿罗阿诺克纪念医院去世。

<!--en-->
Forged documents allowed a North Carolina man to join not only the Lexington Lifesaving and First Aid Crew, but the staff of Stonewall Jackson Hospital. David Harold Suit, 34, answered about 60 calls between May and July 2001 on the bogus documents. One of those calls was to Interstate 81 when VDOT worker Denny Kegley was struck by a truck. Because Suit said he was certified as a paramedic, he was in charge of rescue squad members on the call. Kegley died at Carlton Roanoke Memorial Hospital a few days later.

苏伊特因伪造公共文件被判处5年监禁，又因以虚假手段获取财产这一轻罪被判处12个月监禁。

<!--en-->
Suit received a five-year prison sentence for forging public documents and 12 months for a misdemeanor charge of obtaining property by false pretenses.

本月早些时候，西南地区犯罪预防协会在弗吉尼亚马术中心举办了一整天研讨会，探讨当地商家如何降低此类犯罪的风险。来自该地区的60多名执法机构及零售业代表参加了会议。⁴正如这篇报道中的实例所示，白领犯罪并不总是由企业高管实施的。这些案例均可从法院和警方记录中轻松找到。

<!--en-->
Earlier this month the Southwest Regional Crime Prevention Association presented ways local merchants may reduce the risks of these crimes at a day-long seminar at the Virginia Horse Center. More than 60 law enforcement and retail representatives from across the region attended.⁴
As this story notes with excellent examples, white-collar crime is not always committed by business executives. The examples in this story were easily obtainable from court and police records.

还有许多其他涉及商业领域的刑事案件。根据美国刑法典的定义，洗钱行为包括隐瞒资金来源或去向，或是隐瞒通过非法活动获得的资金。20世纪90年代初，一些银行被指控协助毒贩洗钱。

<!--en-->
There are many other types of criminal cases that involve business. Money laundering, as defined by the U.S. Criminal Code, involves the concealment of the source of money or its destination or the concealment of money gained through illegal activities. In the early 1990s, some banks were accused of helping drug dealers launder money.

记者还应核实许多消息来源的犯罪记录，尤其是当其犯罪背景可能为报道增添内容或有助于了解某人的品格时。例如，假设一名记者正在报道橙汁制造商Tropicana工人代表的工会新主席选举情况，他在法院查看了两名候选人的犯罪记录，发现其中一人曾因持有可卡因而被捕并定罪。这一信息以及该候选人的回应都应被写入报道中。

<!--en-->

## 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《华尔街日报》法律版块负责人詹妮弗·S·福赛思谈法庭报道：***企业也可能被起诉犯罪：**大多数人认为只有个人才会被起诉，但实际上许多企业也遭遇过同样的命运。大型会计公司安达信合伙公司在因恩隆公司丑闻而面临起诉后几乎倒闭。（尽管最高法院最终撤销了对该公司的定罪，但损害已经造成。）虽然针对大公司的起诉较为罕见，但在经法官批准的诉讼中，许多公司会选择与政府和解。即便如此，这些公司的不当行为仍可能对其声誉造成严重损害。[^3130]：⁴摘自M.L.迪比亚塞2002年10月31日发表于《列克星敦新闻公报》D1–D2版的文章“本次区域研讨会聚焦降低风险的方法”，版权归The NewsGazette Corporation所有，经许可转载。286 • 前往法庭

<!--en-->
Wall Street Journal *law bureau chief Jennifer S. Forsyth on covering courts:***Companies can be charged with crimes:** Most people tend to think of individuals as being indicted, but many companies have faced the same fate. The big accounting firm, Arthur Andersen LLP, effectively went out of business after being indicted for its role in the Enron Corp. scandal. (The firm's conviction was eventually overturned by the Supreme Court but the damage was done.) Indictments against major companies are rare, though many settle with the government in court cases that are approved by a judge. When that happens, the company avoids being charged but their wrongdoing still can cause major reputational harm.

### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《华尔街日报》法律版块负责人詹妮弗·S·福赛思谈法庭报道：***法庭上的活动并非只有审判：**实际上，诸如请求法官冻结被告银行账户或命令其不得出境之类的看似常规的听证会，也能让人对针对该被告的指控有初步了解。此外，这还是结识案件相关人员的绝佳机会，包括那些平时可能不愿接电话的政府律师，以及被告的家人、同伙或其他与该案有间接关联、可能成为重要消息来源的律师。

<!--en-->
Wall Street Journal *law bureau chief Jennifer S. Forsyth on covering courts:***Trials aren't the only activities at a courthouse:** In fact, seemingly routine hearings, such as a request for a judge to freeze a defendant's bank account or to order that person not to leave the country, can be a good glimpse into the allegations against him or her. Plus, it's a great chance to meet the players in the case, including government lawyers who otherwise might be reluctant to pick up the phone, as well as family members or associates of the accused or other lawyers tangentially tied to the case who could be valuable sources.
person's character. For example, say a reporter is covering the election of the new president for the union that represents the workers at Tropicana, the orange juice manufacturer. The reporter checks the criminal records of the two candidates at the courthouse and discovers that one of them was once arrested and convicted of cocaine possession. That should likely be in the story, as well as a response from the candidate.

有时，核查包括CEO在内的高管的犯罪记录也是值得的。如果记者正在撰写一篇关于某CEO管理不善的文章，他可以通过提及该CEO曾在限速35英里/小时的区域以110英里/小时的速度行驶而被捕的事实，来描述其性格。某家总部位于新泽西州的公司的一名CEO因在其住宅阁楼种植大麻而被起诉。该公司在其被捕后将这名高管停职，而他再也没有回到原岗位。

<!--en-->
It sometimes even pays to check the criminal records of executives, including CEOs. If a reporter is writing a story about how a CEO is mismanaging a company, one of the ways in which he can help describe the CEO's personality is by including his arrest for speeding at 110 miles per hour in a 35 mile per hour zone. A CEO of a New Jersey-based company was charged with growing marijuana in the attic of his house. The company placed the executive on a leave of absence after his arrest, and he did not return to his position.

记者不应忽视州法院和联邦法院的刑事审判方面。正是在这些地方，常常能发现最有趣的商业新闻。例如，一起针对某保险经纪人的刑事案件——该经纪人被指控向坦帕地区的企业出售虚假保险单——促使当地企业更加仔细地核查自身的保险覆盖情况。

<!--en-->
Reporters should not forget about the criminal side of the state and federal courthouses. They are often where the most interesting business stories are found. For example, a criminal case against an insurance agent accused of selling fictitious insurance policies to businesses throughout Tampa caused local businesses to check their coverage more carefully.

### 宣誓作证与证据文件

<!--en-->
*Depositions and Exhibits*

在诉讼提起且被告对指控作出回应后，双方都可能开始准备自己的案卷。尽管许多与商业相关的诉讼并不会进入庭审阶段，但各方及其律师仍必须为这种可能性做好准备。届时会出现要求提供信息或阻止某些信息被使用的申请。此外，律师们会开始对案件中的关键人物进行宣誓作证，并向被告索要相关文件。原告方也会向案件中提交文件。

<!--en-->
After the lawsuit is filed and the defendant has issued a reply to the charges, both sides may begin to prepare their cases. Although many business-related lawsuits do not go to trial, the parties and their attorneys must prepare for that likelihood. There will be motions for information or to suppress information from the case. In addition, lawyers will begin taking depositions of key people involved in the case and asking for documents from the defendant. The plaintiff's side will also file documents in the case.

这些宣誓作证，即法庭审理前的证人宣誓作证程序，能够提供有价值的信息，让公众提前了解案件进入庭审后可能的发展态势。那些被称为证据文件的资料，其内容不同，会对案件的胜负产生有利或不利的影响。

<!--en-->
These depositions, or pretrial proceedings in which witnesses are questioned under oath, can yield valuable information and provide the public a glimpse of what might happen once the case goes to trial. The documents, known as exhibits, can help or hurt a case, depending on what they contain.

记者应当花时间仔细阅读这些宣誓作证记录和证据文件，尤其是那些对企业高管的采访内容或管理层撰写的备忘录等文件。单独来看，它们可能并无特别意义；但结合起来，却能拼凑出一个此前未向外界披露的公司或企业的真实面貌。

<!--en-->
A reporter should take the time to read through these depositions and exhibits, particularly if they are interviews with corporate executives or documents such as memos written by management. Taken separately, they may not say anything. But together, they could connect a story that paints a picture of a company or business previously unrevealed to the rest of the world.

在复杂的商业案件中，宣誓作证往往会持续数天，双方律师都会提出问题。现场会有速记员负责记录证词。宣誓作证的目的是收集有关案件的信息和事实。有时，如果案件进入庭审，这些证词也会被用来质疑证人的可信度。

<!--en-->
Depositions can often last several days in complicated business cases, and attorneys for both sides ask questions. A stenographer is present to record the statements. Depositions are used to collect information and facts about the case. Sometimes they are taken to discredit the testimony of the witness if the case goes to trial.

律师们经常会指导企业高管或其他人在宣誓作证前如何回答问题。对于许多公司而言，其高管所做的宣誓作证内容，会根据高管的回答方式，要么有助于维护公司的利益，要么对其不利。在庭审期间，律师们会寻找证人的陈述与宣誓作证内容之间的矛盾之处。这类矛盾可能会对案件的结果产生重大影响。前往法庭 • 287 PBS节目《前线》曾深入分析了20世纪90年代末各州总检察长为追回州政府为患病吸烟者支付的医疗补助费用而提起的诉讼中，香烟公司高管们的宣誓作证内容。《前线》发现，全球最大的香烟公司菲利普莫里斯的首席执行官杰弗里·比布尔：(a)否认听说过那个存在了30多年的律师团体——法律顾问委员会，该团体专门讨论烟草行业的战略；(b)声称自己不知道有多少青少年吸食菲利普莫里斯的香烟；(c)声称从未询问过自己的员工相关情况。洛瑞拉德烟草公司的董事长亚历山大·斯皮尔斯三世在宣誓作证时表示，他不认为吸烟会导致肺气肿或肺癌，吸烟也没有成瘾性，而且他的公司也从未做过关于青少年是否吸食其品牌香烟的研究。

<!--en-->
Lawyers often coach a business executive or another person on how to answer questions before a deposition. For many companies, the depositions taken by their executives can help frame the case in their favor or can harm their case, depending on the executive's answers. During the trial, lawyers will look for inconsistencies between the witness's statements and deposition. These incidents can have a significant impact on the outcome of the case.
Headed to Court • 287
The PBS show *Frontline* went through the depositions given by cigarette company executives in lawsuits filed by state attorneys general in the late 1990s in an attempt to recoup sick smokers' Medicaid expenses paid by the state. *Frontline* found that Geoffrey Bible, the CEO of Philip Morris, the largest cigarette company in the world, (a) denied ever hearing of the committee of counsel, a lawyers group that met for more than 30 years to discuss tobacco industry strategy; (b) claimed not to have any knowledge of how many teens smoke Philip Morris cigarettes; and (c) claimed not to have ever asked his employees about it. Alexander Spears III, the chairman of Lorillard Tobacco Company, said in his deposition that he did not believe that smoking caused emphysema or lung cancer, that smoking was not addictive, and that his company had never done a study to determine if teens smoked its brands.

通过使用宣誓作证，记者可以引用那些内容及说话人身份均无可置疑的言论和声明。《孟菲斯商业杂志》报道了一起员工离开当地一家投资银行转投另一家公司的案件，据称这些员工带走了可能为其新雇主带来业务机会的文件。这些文件包括联系人名单以及尚未完成的债券承销交易细节。根据其中一名员工的行政助理的宣誓作证内容，她的上司命令她销毁那些复制的文件。

<!--en-->
By using a deposition, a reporter can use quotes and statements made without any doubt as to what was said or who said it. The *Memphis Business Journal* covered the case of some employees who left a local investment bank to go work for another, allegedly taking documents with them that would help obtain business for their new employer. The documents included contact lists and details of bond underwriting transactions not yet completed. According to the deposition of the administrative assistant of one of the employees, her boss ordered her to destroy copied documents.

“麦克就像被砍了头的鸡一样乱跑，不停地喊‘把电脑里的所有东西都删掉’，”凯莉·费瑟斯在《孟菲斯商业杂志》的报道中引用的其宣誓作证内容说道，“‘我不管那是什么，哪怕是标签也行，必须删掉，因为我不想给任何人留下我们偷了东西的把柄，因为他们可能会拿走某些东西并加以歪曲，我可不想有任何操纵行为发生。’”

<!--en-->
"Mac was running around like a chicken with his head cut off, going, 'Get everything off the computer,'" said Kelli Feathers in a deposition used in the *Memphis Business Journal* report. "'I don't care what it is. I don't care if it's labels, but get it off because I don't want to give anybody any reason to think that we stole anything, because they can take something and turn it into something else, and I don't want any manipulation going on.'"

在针对超市连锁店Supervalu的年龄歧视诉讼中取得的宣誓作证显示，该公司的高管们曾讨论过将包含员工出生日期的员工信息表提供给主管。据《明尼阿波利斯星报论坛报》（Forster, 2003, p. 1D）报道的兰迪·维甘德的宣誓作证内容，Supervalu的副总裁莱兰·戴克对另一位副总裁兰迪·维甘德说：“咱们要把事情做好，这样就能剔除无用信息并节省一些开支。”

<!--en-->
Depositions taken in a lawsuit against grocery store chain Supervalu alleging age discrimination show that company executives had discussed making employee information sheets including birthdates available to supervisors. Leland Dake, a Supervalu senior vice president, told another vice president, Randy Wiegand, "Let's do it right so we can get rid of the garbage and save some money," according to Wiegand's deposition, which was reported in the *Minneapolis Star Tribune* (Forster, 2003, p. 1D).

在后续的证词中，维甘德表示他还有另一次会议，在会上他对相关流程提出了质疑。“我向他表达了对当前流程的不满、反感以及担忧，”维甘德说道。“显然，他很快便转移了话题，会议也随后很快就结束了”（福斯特，2003年，第1D页）。

<!--en-->
Later in his deposition, Wiegand said that he had another meeting in which he questioned the process. "I told him about my dissatisfaction, dislike, concern for the process that was taking place," said Wiegand. "He quickly got off that subject, obviously, and the meeting wound up very shortly thereafter" (Forster, 2003, p. 1D).

为商业诉讼中的指控提供支持而提交的其他文件，也能帮助记者更深入地了解问题，并向读者展现美国企业的内部情况。许多商业报道正是基于这些文件撰写的。

<!--en-->
Other documents filed in support of allegations made in business lawsuits can also be helpful to a reporter looking to better understand an issue and disclose to readers an inside look at corporate America. Many business stories have been reported and written solely on the basis of these documents.

当泰科公司起诉其前首席执行官丹尼斯·科兹洛夫斯基时，它在指控中附上了超过100页的证据材料。这些文件显示，这位前高管为自己及其他高管批准了许多由公司支付的福利，从曼哈顿价值250万美元的特朗普大厦公寓，到花费近1400万美元为十几名员工购买房产。

<!--en-->
When Tyco sued its former CEO Dennis Kozlowski, it added more than 100 pages of exhibits to its allegations. Those documents showed that the former executive had approved a number of perks for himself and other executives paid for by the company, from a $2.5 million Trump Tower apartment in Manhattan to spending nearly $14 million to buy homes for a dozen employees.

证词和证据材料并不总是具有新闻价值，且脱离上下文时可能难以理解。但它们可以让人了解诉讼前的发展状况，让读者和观众大致知晓如果案件进入审判阶段可能会听到哪些内容。288 • 进入法庭 全面的司法体系可被视为另一种商业监管形式。诉讼及相关文件作为公开记录被存档，旨在帮助企业证明自身清白或抵御可能损害其运营的指控。

<!--en-->
Depositions and exhibits may not always be newsworthy. And some of themmay be hard to understand out of context. But they can also provide an inside look at developments leading up to a lawsuit, and they can give readers and viewers an idea of what may be said if a case goes to trial.
288 • Headed to Court
The entire court system can be viewed as another layer of business regulation. Lawsuits and their related documents are filed as public records to help a company prove itself or defend itself against allegations that may hurt its operations.

### 企业衰败

<!--en-->
*Business Gone Bad*

并非所有公司和企业都能成功运营。许多拥有最精巧的商业计划和最佳管理团队的企业也难以盈利，有些甚至会亏损。这种情况既发生在上市公司，也发生在私营企业。

<!--en-->
Not all companies and corporations are successful. Many of them, including those with the smartest business plans and the best managers, struggle to make money, and some of them actually lose money. This happens to public and private companies.

导致企业亏损的原因多种多样。企业可能错过了行业内的重大变革，从而让竞争对手抢走了业务；也可能决定进军新业务领域，结果造成巨大损失；又或者收购了其他企业，背负了无法承受的债务和其他财务负担。

<!--en-->
What causes the problems leading to a company losing money can be wide and varied. A company could have missed a paradigm shift in its industry that caused competitors to take business away from it. A corporation could have decided to enter a new line of business that led to huge losses. Or a business could have acquired another company, taking on debt and other financial obligations that it is no longer able to meet.

以上只是企业衰败的一些例子。当一家企业陷入严重财务困境，无法按时支付账单和贷款时，它通常会向法院申请许可，以便继续运营的同时重组债务，使其还款压力更小。这被称为申请破产。

<!--en-->
These are just a few examples of why a business can go bad. When a company in dire financial straits can no longer pay its bills and loans in a timely manner, it often files papers with the court allowing it to continue operations but reorganize the money it owes, making those payments more manageable. This is called entering bankruptcy court.

破产法院属于联邦司法体系，不仅服务于企业，个人也可以向其申请破产。不过通过破产程序，企业可以免除部分或全部债务，或大幅减少债务数额。

<!--en-->
Bankruptcy court is a federal court system, and it is not just for businesses. Individuals can also file with the bankruptcy court. But a bankruptcy court filing allows a company to have some or all of its debts eliminated or reduced dramatically.

乍看之下，这样的安排对那些欠钱的人或其他企业似乎不公平，许多人会强烈抱怨自己应得的款项无法收回。但从申请破产的企业角度来看，通过法律程序减免部分债务，仍能让它偿还一部分欠款。如果没有这一程序，如果企业直接倒闭，那些欠钱的人和企业可能根本拿不到任何赔偿。此外，破产程序还试图找到一种公平的补偿债权人的方法，某些人或企业会比其他人更早获得赔偿。

<!--en-->
At first glance, such a proposition does not seem fair to the people or other businesses owed money. And many complain bitterly that they will not be repaid what they should receive. But from the perspective of the business in bankruptcy court, going into the court process to eliminate some of its debt allows it to repay some of the money it owes. Without such a process, the people and companies owed money may not have received anything if the company simply went out of business. In addition, the bankruptcy court process attempts to find a fair method for compensating creditors. Some people and businesses owed money by a company in bankruptcy court receive compensation before others.

如今，破产申请越来越成为商业记者的重要报道题材。按企业资产规模计算，2008年或2009年共发生了八起最大的破产案中的五起，这些大型企业包括雷曼兄弟、华盛顿互惠银行、通用汽车和克莱斯勒。即便是一家规模较小的企业寻求破产保护，对该地区而言也可能是个重要新闻。当企业进入破产程序时，通常会通过关闭门店和裁员来削减开支，这会对整个经济产生影响。

<!--en-->
Increasingly, bankruptcy filings have become a major story for business reporters. Five of the eight largest bankruptcies in terms of company assets were filed in 2008 or 2009. Those major companies include Lehman Brothers, Washington Mutual, General Motors, and Chrysler. And even when it is a smaller company seeking bankruptcy court protection, the story can be important to a local town or city. When companies go into bankruptcy court, they typically try to cut expenses by closing locations and firing workers. That can have an effect on any economy.

了解破产法院的运作机制以及企业为何申请破产保护，对所有记者都很重要，而不仅仅是负责商业报道的记者。当企业向债权人寻求保护时，那些欠钱的对象可能包括政府机构等。Headed to Court • 289

<!--en-->
Understanding how bankruptcy court works and why businesses file for bankruptcy court protection is important for any reporter, not just those working on the business desk. When businesses file for protection from their creditors, those that are owed money could range from government entities, such as the local

**需关注的破产法院申请文件：**

<!--en-->
**Bankruptcy Court Filings to Look For:**

1. 首次申请文件。其中会注明申请破产保护的公司或个人的名称，以及其资产和负债的数额。
2. 债权人名单。列出了所有有债权人的姓名及联系方式。可将其视为信息来源清单。
3. 重组计划。该文件详细说明了将向债权人偿还多少款项，以及公司是否计划关闭业务或出售部分业务以削减开支。
4. 法官的裁决。几乎所有事项都需要提交此类裁决，从向公司高管支付薪酬到批准重组计划，再到学校董事会，或是与该公司有服务或货物供应合同的联邦机构。也有可能是那些计划振兴市中心衰败区域的商家。每个州的多数主要城市都设有破产法院。通常情况下，企业会在距离其总部最近的破产法院申请保护，但并非总是如此。有时，企业会在其注册地所在的州申请破产保护。破产法院的运作方式与其他联邦法院及州法院类似，都会有一名书记员负责处理所有新提交的文件以及现有案件中的相关文件。对于商业记者而言，重要的是要了解这些破产法院的文件属于公开记录，应当可以获取。根据《美国破产法》，如果这些文件包含商业机密或有关公司运营的保密信息，或者涉及对个人的诽谤性内容，法院可禁止公众查阅。初始申请文件非常重要，因为它列出了公司的总资产和债务情况。这份债权人名单往往很有价值，因为它能帮助找到愿意透露该公司为何拖欠账款或违背商业协议的人士。当一家企业申请破产保护时，其资产就会被冻结。提交申请后，还会举行听证会来决定该公司是否可以支取大额资金。《匹兹堡商业时报》的一篇报道开头就展示了典型的破产法院首日流程，详细列出公司信息并公布其债务和资产总额供公众查看。报道指出，RedZone Robotics Incorporated这家负责设计用于核电站等危险环境清洁机器人的公司已申请第11章破产保护，第二段说明了该案件是在哪个破产法院提交的，第四段则列出了公司的资产和债务情况。文章其余部分引用了该公司总裁的话，并提到公司的就业人数正在减少。

<!--en-->
1. The initial filing. It will tell you the name of the company or individual filing for bankruptcy court protection and the amount of assets and liabilities.
2. Creditors list. It lists the name and contact information of everyone who is owed money. Consider this a source list.
3. Reorganization plan. A document that details how much creditors will be repaid and whether the company plans to close or sell any operations to cut its expenses.
4. Judge's rulings. They are filed for nearly everything, from paying company executives to approval of the reorganization plan.
school board, to a federal agency that contracted with the business to perform services or provide goods. Or it could be a business that was planning to revitalize a depressed part of downtown.
Bankruptcy courts are located in most major cities in every state. Typically, companies file for bankruptcy-court protection at the bankruptcy courthouse located closest to their headquarters. But that does not always happen. Sometimes, companies file for bankruptcy-court protection in the state where they are incorporated.
Bankruptcy courts operate similarly to other federal courts and to state courts. There is a clerk who handles all of the incoming filings as well as the documents filed in existing cases. It is important for a business reporter to know that these bankruptcy court filings are considered public record and should be accessible. The U.S. Bankruptcy Code allows a court to prevent public access to filings if they include trade secrets or confidential information about a company's operations, or if scandalous or defamatory information about a person is filed.
The initial filing is an important document because it lists the company's total assets and debts. This list of creditors can be valuable because it often leads to sources willing to talk about how the company has not been paying its bills or is reneging on some sort of business arrangement.
When a company files for bankruptcy-court protection, its assets are frozen. After the filing, there are hearings to decide whether a company can spend large amounts of money. The beginning of a *Pittsburgh Business Times* story illustrates the typical first day bankruptcy-court structure that details the company and totals its debts and assets for the world to see.

#### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《华尔街日报》法律版块负责人Jennifer S. Forsyth关于报道法院案件的看法：让破产法院揭示你们所在地区大型企业的真实状况——如果一家企业不得不寻求破产保护，那说明经济、该行业或该企业的管理方式出现了严重问题，甚至可能是三者皆有。法院的存在就是为了厘清责任归属，并帮助企业制定出更好的复苏计划。所有这些过程都必须公开进行，通常以法院提供的书面文件或现在的在线文档形式呈现。

<!--en-->
Wall Street Journal *law bureau chief Jennifer S. Forsyth on covering courts:*Let the bankruptcy courts reveal a whole new world about the local big employer in your town: If a company has to seek bankruptcy protection, something went very wrong with the economy, with that industry or with the way that company was managed—or possibly all three. The courts are there to help sort out who's to blame and to help the company come up with a plan to emerge in better shape. All of it must be done in public, usually in written documents available at the court or now online.
and manufactures robots to clean hazardous environments such as nuclear plants, filed for Chapter 11, and the second paragraph states in which bankruptcy court the case was filed. The fourth paragraph lists the company's assets and debts. The rest of the story quotes the company's president and mentions that its employment is down.

记者确实查看了法院的文件，以便让读者了解该公司资产的价值及债务的数额。记者还联系了该公司以获取关于申请原因的评论，不过总裁并未给出明确答复。然而，这篇报道并未解释这家机器人公司为何会进入破产程序。

<!--en-->
The reporter actually looked at the court filing to give the reader a sense of the value of the company's assets and the worth of its debt. The reporter also contacted the company to get a comment on the cause of the filing, although the president was not forthcoming. The story, however, does not explain what caused this robotics company to go into bankruptcy court.

以下摘自《波士顿先驱报》的内容很好地解释了企业走向衰落的原因。在任何报道企业破产申请的文章中，都应突出说明问题产生的原因。

<!--en-->
The following excerpt from the *Boston Herald* does a good job of explaining what led to a company's downfall. In any story reporting a company's bankruptcy court filing, the reasons for the problems should be explained prominently.

昨日，Kmart Corp.成为美国首家申请第11章破产保护的大型零售商，有消息称这一举措可能导致多达600家门店关闭。

<!--en-->
Kmart Corp. yesterday became the largest U.S. retailer to seek Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection, a move sources say could trigger the closing of up to 600 stores.

这家总部位于密歇根州特洛伊市的零售商是美国第二大折扣连锁店，去年营收为370亿美元。它因销售疲软、亏损加剧、糟糕的节日购物季以及供应商信心的下降而陷入困境，同时还受到了竞争对手沃尔玛公司的冲击。

<!--en-->
The Troy, Mich., retailer, the second-largest U.S. discount chain, with $37 billion in revenue last year, was battered by weak sales, mounting losses, a disastrous holiday shopping season and the erosion of supplier confidence. It has also suffered at the hand of giant rival Wal-Mart Stores Inc.

Kmart昨日表示，在寻求法院保护下进行重组期间，所有2,114家门店都将继续营业，直至另行通知。不过，该公司今年将关闭一些亏损且业绩不佳的门店。Kmart在马萨诸塞州拥有29家门店，约有3,000名当地员工。

<!--en-->
Kmart yesterday said all 2,114 Kmart stores will remain open until further notice as it seeks to reorganize under court protection. But it will close a number of unprofitable and underperforming stores this year. Kmart operates 29 stores in Massachusetts, with an estimated 3,000 local employees.

零售业消息人士称，他们预计Kmart将会关闭数百家门店——可能多达600家。

<!--en-->
Retail sources said they expect Kmart will close several hundred stores —perhaps as many as 600.

昨日，Kmart表示将终止290家已关闭门店或租给其他租户的门店的租赁协议，这将立即为该公司节省2.5亿美元。

<!--en-->
Yesterday, Kmart said it will terminate 350 leases for already-closed stores or for locations that are leased to other tenants, resulting in an immediate savings of $250 million.

该公司在新英格兰地区拥有69家门店，每家门店平均有100名员工。

<!--en-->
The company has 69 stores in New England, with an average of 100 employees each.

近期，一些观察家批评该连锁店在拥挤的货架上摆放不受欢迎的商品，且其库存管理技术陈旧，无法满足当今消费者的需求。⁵波士顿报纸的记者撰写了关于Kmart的报道，旨在反映这一地区将受到的影响。在报道任何破产申请时，记者注明该公司的本地业务状况以及雇佣的员工人数是明智的。

<!--en-->
Some observers have criticized the chain lately for carrying unpopular merchandise in cluttered aisles, for having outdated inventory technology and not keeping pace with today's consumer demands.⁵
The Boston newspaper reporter wrote the Kmart story to reflect how the region would be affected. With any bankruptcy-court filing, it is smart for the writer to note what the company's local operations are and how many workers it employs.

最初的申请对企业有着重要意义。处于破产程序中的公司，其供应商仍需继续向其提供产品或其他材料。这类公司会经历大量的法庭听证会。有些听证会用于决定是否应关闭某些门店或工厂，还有些听证会则用于确定应向高管支付多少赔偿金，以及应向代表公司的破产律师支付多少费用。[^3186]：⁵摘自G. Gatlin于2002年1月23日发表在《波士顿先驱报》第27页的文章《Kmart进入破产程序；零售巨头Kmart破产；其位于马萨诸塞州的29家门店暂无损失》，版权归2002年《波士顿先驱报》所有，经许可转载。此外，报道企业破产案的记者还需要了解这个看似复杂的司法体系中的其他关键要素。例如，有时申请破产保护的决定并非由公司自身做出，而是由其部分债权人提出，这被称为非自愿破产。三个或更多债权人可以联合起来迫使一家公司进入破产程序，而该公司也可以对这种非自愿申请提出异议。

<!--en-->
The initial filing helps businesses in an important way. A company's supplier must continue to provide products or other materials to the business in bankruptcy court. Companies in bankruptcy court go through a lot of court hearingsas part of the process. There are hearings to determine whether a company should be closing locations or factories. There are hearings to decide how much compensation should be paid to executives and how much in fees should be paid to the bankruptcy lawyers representing the company.
[^3186]: ⁵ From “Kmart enters bankruptcy; Retail giant Kmart is bankrupt; No immediate loss seen of any of its 29 Mass. stores,” by G. Gatlin, January 23, 2002, *Boston Herald*, p. 27. Copyright 2002 by Boston Herald. Reprinted with permission.
Headed to Court • 291
In addition, it is important for a reporter covering a business bankruptcy case to know some other vital parts of what can appear to be a complicated court system. For example, sometimes the decision to file for bankruptcy-court protection is not made by the company but by some of its creditors. This is called an involuntary bankruptcy. Three or more creditors can join together and force a company into bankruptcy court. The company can contest the involuntary filing.

记者还必须了解公司在申请破产保护后的实际掌控者是谁。在某些情况下，法院会指派一名受托人来监督公司的运营。

<!--en-->
And it is vital that a reporter understands who is running the company after it has filed for bankruptcy-court protection. In some cases, the court will appoint a trustee to oversee a company's operations.

对企业而言，评估其资产非常重要，资产可定义为企业所拥有的、有望为其运营带来益处的资源或物品。许多处于破产程序中的公司会试图出售部分资产，以筹集资金来扭转经营困境。

<!--en-->
It is important for a company to assess its assets, which can be defined as a resource or item owned by a business that can be expected to benefit its operations. Many times a company in bankruptcy court will look to sell some of its assets to help raise cash to turn its operations around.

当Conseco Incorporated决定出售部分业务时，彭博社、道琼斯社、路透社和美联社的记者都报道了该公司以超过7亿美元的价格将Conseco Finance业务单元出售给CFN Investment Holdings LLC，以及以3.1亿美元的价格将其Mill Creek Bank资产出售给GE Consumer Finance的消息。这些交易是在破产程序中的拍卖过程中达成的，但仍需得到负责审理该案的破产法官的批准。

<!--en-->
When Conseco Incorporated decided to sell part of its operations, reporters from Bloomberg, Dow Jones, Reuters, and the Associated Press reported its deal to sell its Conseco Finance unit for more than $700 million to CFN Investment Holdings LLC and its Mill Creek Bank assets to GE Consumer Finance for $310 million. The agreements were reached as part of its bankruptcy-court proceedings in an auction process. They still had to be approved by the bankruptcy-court judge overseeing the case.

申请破产保护的公司应被视为重大新闻，尤其是大型企业。然而，申请破产保护往往并不意味着该公司就要倒闭——这是许多读者甚至一些记者的常见误解。如果公司仍在运营，记者应确保报道中明确说明这一点。

<!--en-->
A company filing for bankruptcy-court protection should be considered major news, particularly if it is a large company. However, a company filing for bankruptcy-court protection often does not mean that the company is going out of business—a common misperception of many readers and even some journalists. Reporters should make sure that their copy clearly states that the company remains in business, if that is the case.

## 第11章与第7章

<!--en-->
*Chapter 11 versus Chapter 7*

美国破产法包含多个不同部分。其中一部分允许企业寻求重组债务，另一部分则允许企业尽可能偿还债务后关闭业务。

<!--en-->
The U.S. bankruptcy code has many different parts. One section allows companies to seek to reorganize their debt. Another allows companies to simply pay off as much of its debt as it can and close shop.

第11章的破产申请属于前者。这种破产申请允许企业或个人在不清算全部资产的情况下进行重组。除非法院指派受托人，否则债务人仍能掌控企业。公司通常会进入破产法庭，制定一份债务偿还计划提交给债权人。如果债权人同意该计划，且法院认为该计划公平合理，那么该公司就可以重组债务并摆脱破产状态。

<!--en-->
Chapter 11 court filings are of the former category. This bankruptcy filing allows a corporation, or an individual, to reorganize without having to liquidate all of its assets. The debtor maintains control of the business, unless the court appoints a trustee. The company typically goes into bankruptcy court to come up with a debt payment plan to submit to its creditors. If the creditors approve the plan, and if the court agrees that the plan is fair, then the company is allowed to reorganize its debts and emerge from bankruptcy court.

而第7章的破产申请则更为彻底。当公司根据破产法的这一部分提出申请时，意味着其所有资产都将被出售用于偿还债务，公司也将随之倒闭。

<!--en-->
Chapter 7 court filings, however, are more drastic. When a company files under this part of the bankruptcy law, it means that all of the company's assets will be sold to pay its debts and that the company is going out of business.

与商业记者相关的第三种破产申请类型是

<!--en-->
A third type of bankruptcy filing that is relevant to business reporters is a

### 专业人士的经验建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《华尔街日报》法律版块负责人詹妮弗·S·福赛思谈新闻报道中的法庭相关内容：***了解一家公司是否有望在破产中存活下来非常重要：**因此，掌握第11章破产申请与第7章破产申请之间的区别很有帮助。第11章允许公司在制定出让自己变得更优秀、更具盈利能力的计划之前，暂时免除部分债务。一家公司可以在第11章程序下运营很长时间，甚至数月之久。第7章则被称为清算程序，意味着该公司只需变卖所有资产后就停止营业。对于公司的长期发展而言，第11章有时是更好的选择；而第7章则绝非如此。292 • 前往法庭 第13章程序下，申请公司需在三到五年时间内偿还债务。

<!--en-->
Wall Street Journal *law bureau chief Jennifer S. Forsyth on covering courts:***It's important to know if a company is expected to survive bankruptcy:** So understanding the difference between a Chapter 11 bankruptcy filing and Chapter 7 filing is helpful. Chapter 11 allows a company to shield itself from its debts, and shed some of them, until it can come up with a plan to be a better, more profitable company. A company can operate in Chapter 11 for a very long time, even months. Chapter 7 is called a liquidation, which means the company is simply selling off everything it has and is going out of business. Chapter 11 is sometimes a good option for a company's long-term health; Chapter 7 never is.
292 • Headed to Court
Chapter 13, where the company filing repays its debts during a three- to five-year time period.

当记者查看一家公司在破产法院提交的初始申请时，首先需要确定的因素之一就是该公司是提交第11章申请还是第7章申请。两者之间存在重要差异，若弄错这一关键信息，不仅会损害该公司，还会严重影响记者与消息来源的关系。

<!--en-->
When a reporter is examining the initial filing of a company at bankruptcy court, one of the first facts he or she should determine is whether the business is filing under Chapter 11 or Chapter 7. The differences between the two are important, and getting this vital piece of information wrong could hurt a company, not to mention severely hamper a reporter's relationship with sources.

第11章是中型及大型企业最常选择的申请方式，但并非所有企业都首选此途径。2009年上半年，企业提交的破产保护申请共有30,333份，同比增长64%。而在2009年上半年的所有破产法院申请中，只有不到5%属于第11章的破产保护申请。这一比例看似较低，但若仔细研究近期通过第11章程序重组债务的公司，就会发现这些仍在运营的公司拥有数十亿美元的资产。例如，雷曼兄弟在2008年9月提交申请时拥有6910亿美元资产，而华盛顿互惠银行则拥有3279亿美元资产。即便有数千家小型企业提交破产保护申请，也难以达到这些数字。

<!--en-->
Chapter 11 is the most common filing for medium and large businesses, although it is not the most common filing for all businesses. In the first half of 2009, there were 30,333 filings of bankruptcy protection by businesses, up 64 percent. Less than 5 percent of all bankruptcy-court filings in the first half of 2009 were for Chapter 11 protection. That seems like a small amount, but upon examination of the recent cases under Chapter 11, a reporter will discover that there are billions of dollars in assets owned by companies in the process of seeking to reorganize debt while continuing to exist as viable companies. For example, at the time of its filing in September 2008, Lehman Brothers had $691 billion in assets, whereas Washington Mutual had $327.9 billion in assets. It would take thousands of small companies filing for bankruptcy-court protection to equal those amounts.

要查明某家公司是否已提交破产保护申请，并不像每天去法院查阅申请文件那么简单，不过这确实是个不错的起点。如果记者听到有传言称某家公司可能在寻求破产保护，就应该先做一些背景调查。

<!--en-->
Finding out that a company has filed for bankruptcy-court protection may not be as easy as just going to the courthouse and looking through the filings each day, though that is a good place to start. If a reporter is hearing rumors that a company may be seeking bankruptcy-court protection, he or she should do some background work.

首先，记者应查明该公司在所在州注册时的名称。有时该公司的注册名称可能与其实际经营使用的名称不同，这种情况在餐厅等行业尤为常见。

<!--en-->
First, the journalist should find out the name of the company as it is incorporated with the state. Sometimes the company's incorporated name may not be the same name under which it is doing business. This is typical for businesses such as restaurants.

其次，记者需要知道该公司在何处注册。这将有助于确定该申请应提交到哪个破产法院。如果记者在一个法院寻找初始申请却找不到，结果却被另一个在另一家法院找到该申请的记者抢先报道，那会非常令人沮丧。在这种情况下，法院的工作人员通常可以提供该公司提交申请的位置，从而提供帮助。最后，一些企业——尤其是那些在当地社区颇具影响力的企业——往往会在一天结束时或周五深夜提交破产保护申请，希望避免被人注意到。如果记者无法每天等到法院下班时间再查看申请文件，就应该要求获取前一天所有的申请文件。不过有时候，公司也会直接发布新闻稿宣布已提交破产保护申请。人寿保险公司Conseco Incorporated就曾发布过关于其第11章申请的新闻稿。对于关注该公司的许多人来说，这次破产保护申请并不意外。一些华尔街分析师在书面研究报告中甚至预测该公司会采取此类行动，而该公司在向美国证券交易委员会提交的文件中也暗示正在考虑申请破产保护。尽管如此，该公司仍选择在东部时间凌晨3点发布这份新闻稿。由于该公司的股票是公开交易的，它还提交了8-K表格来披露这一情况。以下内容展示了美联社是如何报道该申请以及当天晚些时候的听证会的：

<!--en-->
Second, the reporter needs to know where the company is incorporated. That will help determine in which bankruptcy court the filing can be found. It is frustrating for a reporter to go looking for an initial filing at one court and not find the document, only to be scooped by another reporter who found the filing at another court. Clerks at the court can often be helpful in cases like this by providing the location where a company has filed. And last, businesses—particularly those prominent in a local community—will file for bankruptcy-court protection at the end of the day or late on a Friday, hoping that the filing will escape notice. Reporters should ask for all of the previous day's filings if they cannot wait around the clerk's office every day until closing time. Other times, however, a company will simply issue a news release announcing that it has filed for bankruptcy-court protection. Life insurer Conseco Incorporated issued a news release about its Chapter 11 filing. This bankruptcy-court protection filing was not considered a surprise by many who followed the company. Some Wall Street analysts, in written research reports, even predicted the company would take such action, and the company also hinted in its SEC filings that it was considering bankruptcy-court protection. Still, the company chose to issue this release at 3 a.m. Eastern time. Because the company's stock was publicly traded, it also filed a form 8-K disclosing the filing. The following excerpt shows how the Associated Press covered the filing and subsequent hearing later that day:

前往法庭 • 293 Conseco周三表示，计划尽快结束破产保护程序，尽管有一群后来才介入的债权人威胁要拖延并可能使这家保险和金融公司的重组工作陷入混乱。

<!--en-->
Headed to Court • 293
Conseco said Wednesday it plans to make a quick exit from bankruptcy court protection, even though a group of creditors who were late to the table threaten to delay and potentially tangle the insurance and finance company's reorganization.

由于20世纪90年代的一些收购项目反噬导致负债累累，Conseco在周二晚些时候成为美国第三大申请破产保护的公司。

<!--en-->
Conseco, mired in debt from 1990s acquisitions that backfired, late Tuesday became the third-largest U.S. company to file for bankruptcy protection.

这家总部位于印第安纳州卡梅尔的公司拥有约14,000名员工，去年的营收为81亿美元。其首席律师在芝加哥的破产法庭上表示，该公司预计最迟将在明年第二季度摆脱第11章破产保护程序。

<!--en-->
The Carmel, Ind.-based company, which employs about 14,000 people and had $8.1 billion in revenues last year, expects to emerge from Chapter 11 protection during the second quarter of next year, if not earlier, the company's lead attorney told a bankruptcy court in Chicago.

银行与债券持有人就Conseco所欠的40亿美元债务，就破产条款达成了初步协议。

<!--en-->
Banks and bondholders reached a tentative agreement on bankruptcy terms with Conseco over the $4 billion those groups are owed.

不过，一部分优先股股东一直拒绝参与谈判——他们最初被排除在8月开始的Conseco债务重组谈判之外，但最终通过抗议获得了谈判资格——他们仍在继续与Conseco进行协商。

<!--en-->
But a group of preferred shareholders—who initially were left out of talks begun in August to restructure Conseco's debt, but eventually won a seat under protest—have held out. They continue negotiations with Conseco.

在从倒闭企业中收回投资方面，优先证券持有人的权利优于普通股股东，但其地位仍低于银行和债券持有人。普通股的Conseco投资者很可能几乎无法收回任何投资。

<!--en-->
Preferred securities holders carry privileges over owners of common stock in recovering their investments from failed companies, but rank below banks and bondholders. Common stockholders are expected to recover little if any of their investments in Conseco.

Conseco的第11章破产计划细节尚未提交，必须先获得各投资者团体的批准，才能将重组方案提交法院审批。Conseco发言人马克·卢伯斯称，相关详细文件可能在四到六周内提交。⁶ 如上述报道所指，Conseco在寻求法院保护之前先与其最大贷款方进行谈判，这一做法在第11章破产案件中较为罕见。在某些情况下，企业会采取这种策略，即所谓的“预包装破产申请”，这意味着在破产法庭监督下的大部分谈判早已完成，此类案件的破产审理时间通常更短。要实施此类计划，企业必须获得代表其总债务三分之二的多数债权人的同意。

<!--en-->
Details of Conseco's Chapter 11 plan, which have yet to be filed, must be approved by members of investor groups before a reorganization plan can be submitted for the court's approval. A filing outlining specifics could be submitted within four to six weeks, Conseco spokesman Mark Lubbers said.⁶
Conseco's bankruptcy-court filing, as the above story points out, is unusual for Chapter 11 cases in that the company negotiated with its largest lenders before it actually sought court protection from its debtors. In some cases, a company will take such a strategy, commonly called a prepackaged bankruptcy filing, which means that much of the negotiation that takes place during bankruptcy court supervision has already occurred. In many of these cases, the time a company spends in bankruptcy court is shorter. To do such a plan, the company must get the approval of a majority of creditors representing two-thirds of its total debt.

然而，通常情况下，企业在进入破产法庭之前并不会与债权人进行谈判。谈判通常在法庭内通过听证会等形式进行，还会任命债权人委员会。这些委员会由律师代表，他们往往能提供重要信息，让记者了解债权人是否赞同企业提出的重组方案。

<!--en-->
Often, however, a company does not negotiate with its creditors before entering bankruptcy court. The negotiations typically occur in the court, often through hearings. Committees of creditors are appointed. These committees are represented by attorneys, who can often be valuable sources, letting a reporter know if the creditors like or disapprove of a reorganization plan floated by the company.

<!--en-->
