The reporter for the *Louisville Courier-Journal* wrote the story the same way it would be written for a private or public company. The reporter lists the assets and debts and the cause of the problems leading to the filing toward the beginning of the story:

### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《华尔街日报》法律版块负责人詹妮弗·S·福赛思谈报道法庭新闻：***破产审查员和受托人可成为记者的得力助手：**这些人是由法院聘请的，负责接管正在清算的企业，或调查是否有任何人应为企业倒闭承担责任。审查员常常与可能正在调查违规行为的政府机构密切合作。他们的报告包含了关于企业为何倒闭的诸多宝贵信息，而且有时也愿意向媒体透露他们的调查结果。[^3220]：⁶ “Conseco承诺快速破产”，2002年12月18日，美联社。版权所有2002年美联社，经许可转载。294 • 提出破产申请1990年开业时，位于杰斐逊县东部的奥克斯穆尔高尔夫及障碍赛场地项目是HFH公司众多成功项目之一。这家路易斯维尔的房地产开发商在20世纪80年代末和90年代初的高尔夫球场及住宅建筑热潮中发展迅猛。

<!--en-->
Wall Street Journal *law bureau chief Jennifer S. Forsyth on covering courts:***Bankruptcy examiners and trustees can be a reporter's aide:** These people are hired by the court to take over a business that is liquidating or to investigate whether anyone should be held liable for a company's demise. Examiners often work closely with government agencies that might be looking into wrongdoing. The examiners' reports are a treasure trove of information about how a company failed. And examiners are sometimes willing to talk to the media about their findings.
[^3220]: ⁶ “Conseco promises swift bankruptcy,” December 18, 2002, Associated Press. Copyright 2002 by Associated Press. Reprinted with permission
294 • Headed to Court
When it opened in 1990, the Oxmoor golf and steeplechase development in eastern Jefferson County was another success among the vast holdings of HFH Inc., the Louisville real-estate developer that soared during the golf course and residential building boom in the late 1980s and early 1990s.

如今，运营着位于莱姆豪斯巷9000号的奥克斯穆尔乡村俱乐部的奥克斯穆尔高尔夫&障碍赛公司，因欠下近200家债权人的债务，并面临供应商为追回款项而提起的四起诉讼，正在走破产程序。

<!--en-->
Today Oxmoor Golf & Steeplechase Inc., which operates Oxmoor Country Club at 9000 Limehouse Lane, is proceeding through bankruptcy after running up debts to nearly 200 creditors and facing four lawsuits by suppliers seeking to recoup their money.

这家非营利公司在7月5日向肯塔基州西部地区的美国破产法庭申请债权人的保护，此举旨在在尝试重组的同时保护其资产。在提交给法庭的申请书中，奥克斯穆尔高尔夫&障碍赛公司声称自己有500万美元的债务和100万美元的资产。代表该俱乐部的律师大卫·坎托表示，这些债务是由于奥克斯穆尔高尔夫&障碍赛公司需向布利特家族设立的信托机构支付日益增长的土地租金所致。当HFH公司在20世纪90年代中期出现财务问题时，奥克斯穆尔的会员们便接手了俱乐部的运营。

<!--en-->
The not-for-profit corporation filed for protection from its creditors in U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Western District of Kentucky on July 5, a move that shields its assets while it attempts to reorganize. In a petition entered with the court, Oxmoor Golf & Steeplechase claimed debts of $5 million and assets of $1 million. The debts are the result of escalating rent payments on the land Oxmoor Golf & Steeplechase leases from trusts established by the Bullitt family, said attorney David Cantor, who is representing the club. When HFH experienced financial problems in the mid-1990s, Oxmoor members took over the club's operations.

他们继承了一座现代化的俱乐部会所以及一座颇具挑战性的18洞高尔夫球场，同时还背负着一份为期37年的租约，每月的租金高达约30,000美元，此外还需支付17,500美元的月度抵押贷款。⁷ 接下来文章列出了Oxmoor的一些最大债权人。破产案件中存在两种不同类型的债权人：有担保债权人拥有以抵押物为支撑的对公司的债权要求，这类似于汽车贷款或房屋贷款；也就是说，如果无法偿还汽车或房屋贷款，贷款就会以该汽车或房屋作为担保。

<!--en-->
They inherited a modern clubhouse and a challenging 18-hole golf course—and a 37-year lease with ballooning payments of about $30,000 a month, coupled with $17,500 in monthly mortgage payments.⁷
The story then lists some of the largest creditors for Oxmoor. There are two different types of creditors in bankruptcy-court cases. The secured creditors have claims against the company backed by collateral. This is similar to a car loan or a home loan; that is, if one does not make the payments on one's car or home loan, the loan is backed by the car or home.

另一种则是无担保债权人，这类债权人的债权没有抵押物作为支撑。通过股票经纪商购买上市公司股票的投资者就属于这一类。在破产案件中，有担保债权人会在无担保债权人之前获得偿付。

<!--en-->
The other type of creditors is unsecured creditors. These are creditors with no collateral against their claim. Investors who purchased stock in a public company via a stockbroker fall into this category. Secured creditors are paid before unsecured creditors in bankruptcy cases.

公司留在破产法庭的时间长短取决于其与债权人的谈判结果。有些破产诉讼会持续数年，而有些则只需几个月。作为记者，及时掌握公司的案件进展或停滞情况非常重要。目前一些破产法庭会在互联网上公布庭审时间和相关文件，但另一些法庭则要求记者亲自前往法院查看日程安排。

<!--en-->
The length of a company's stay in bankruptcy court can vary depending on the negotiations with its creditors. Some bankruptcy-court proceedings last for years, whereas others take months. As a reporter, it is important to stay on top of a company's case and its progress, or lack thereof. Some bankruptcy courts now post court hearing times and filings on the Internet. For others, however, reporters need to go to the courthouse to check the docket.

了解相关各方，尤其是公司方和债权人的律师，也至关重要。记者还应熟悉法官的情况。还记得之前提到的那些公司为了避免曝光而在最后时刻申请破产保护的事吗？有些法官甚至允许在法庭关门、灯光熄灭后的深夜将申请材料送到家中。尽管法官很少公开表态，但他们及其书记员通常会告知记者案件的进展情况。[^3230]：⁷ 摘自M. Green于2002年7月30日发表在《The Courier-Journal》上的文章《Oxmoor club hopes to survive bankruptcy》，第1D页。版权所有2002年《The Courier-Journal》，经许可转载。走向法庭 • 295家公司常常申请第11章破产保护，希望从中吸取教训后以更强大的姿态重新崛起。诸如Kmart等许多公司则希望在破产之后能够东山再起。

<!--en-->
It is also vitally important to know the players, particularly the company's and the creditors' attorneys. Reporters should know the judges as well. Remember the warning about companies filing for bankruptcy-court protection at the end of the day to avoid publicity? Some judges have even allowed filings to be sent to their homes late at night, long after the court has been locked and the lights turned off. Although judges will rarely talk on the record, they and their clerks will often let a reporter know what is happening with a case.
[^3230]: ⁷ From “Oxmoor club hopes to survive bankruptcy,” by M. Green, July 30, 2002, *The Courier-Journal*, p. 1D. Copyright 2002 by *The Courier-Journal*. Reprinted with permission.
Headed to Court • 295
Companies often file for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection hoping to emerge from the proceedings as a better company that has learned from its mistakes. A number of companies, such as Kmart, seek to become successful after bankruptcy court.

但情况并非总是如此。一些试图通过第11章重组债务的公司，一旦发现无法与债权人达成协议，或者业务状况恶化到债权人认为其最佳选择是让其倒闭，就会将案件转为第7章处理。这种清算决定往往是由债权人或法院强加给该公司及其管理层的。与所有破产案件报道一样，记者必须联系该公司以获取其对法庭程序的回应，这一点至关重要。

<!--en-->
But that is not always the case. A number of companies that look to Chapter 11 to reorganize their debt end up converting their case to Chapter 7 when it becomes apparent that they cannot reach an agreement with creditors or their business deteriorates so much that it becomes obvious that the best course of action for the creditors is to go out of business. The decision to liquidate is often forced upon the company and its management by creditors or by the court. As with all bankruptcy-court stories, it is critical that the reporter get in touch with the company to get its response to the court proceedings.

不过在另一些情况下，公司会申请第11章保护，并警告债权人可能会将其案件转为第7章清算。2002年12月，联合航空的首席执行官在接受《纽约时报》采访时警告称，该公司可能会将其第11章破产案件转为第7章处理。

<!--en-->
In other cases, however, a company will file for Chapter 11 protection and warn creditors that it could convert its case to Chapter 7 liquidation. In a December 2002 interview with the *New York Times*, the CEO of United Airlines warned that the company might switch its Chapter 11 bankruptcy-court case to a Chapter 7.

许多破产法庭专家认为，公司提及清算的可能性往往是试图从债权人或员工那里争取让步，以降低成本。在联合航空的案例中，首席执行官这么做可能是为了让工会同意降低工资。2003年3月的电讯报道指出，该公司在法庭文件中写道：“如果联合航空无法实现其拟定的劳动力成本削减目标，清算是完全有可能的”（美联社，2003年）。联合航空最终走出了破产程序，至今仍在运营。

<!--en-->
Many bankruptcy-court experts believe that a company often mentions the possibility of liquidation in an attempt to win concessions from creditors or from employees to lower its costs. In the case of United Airlines, the CEO could have been making that assertion to get labor unions to agree to lower wages. Wire reports in March 2003 noted that the company filed in court records that “liquidation is a distinct possibility if United does not achieve its proposed labor cost reductions” (Associated Press, 2003). United Airlines emerged from bankruptcy court and continues to operate today.

当一家公司虽已提交第11章申请，却开始谈论第7章时，记者需要探究其背后的动机。第7章案件意味着公司的终结。通过查阅法庭文件并采访相关人士，记者可以撰写出关于大小企业兴衰的引人入胜的文章。

<!--en-->
When a company begins talking about Chapter 7 even though it has filed a Chapter 11 case, a reporter needs to look at the company’s motives. Chapter 7 cases mean the end of the line for a company. By reviewing the court documents and talking to sources, a reporter can write a compelling story about the rise and fall of a company, large or small.

### 重组

<!--en-->
*The Reorganization*

那些打算重组债务并结束法院保护的公司，依赖于与债权人建立良好的关系，共同致力于一个目标：制定出一项重组计划，让企业能够在偿还部分债务的同时减少负债。

<!--en-->
Companies that enter bankruptcy court with the idea that they will reorganize their debt and terminate court protection rely on building relationships with their creditors to work toward a common goal: coming up with a reorganization plan that allows the business to lower its debt while repaying some of the money owed.

重组计划对公司的未来发展至关重要。一份不完善的重组计划可能导致公司再次申请破产。如果重组计划几乎不能或完全不能让债权人得到任何回报，往往会导致投资者不愿参与新公司的组建。

<!--en-->
The reorganization plan is vital to the future success of a company. A weak reorganization plan can lead to yet another bankruptcy-court filing. A reorganization plan that gives little or nothing back to creditors often results in investors not wanting to be involved in the new company.

企业进入破产法庭后采取的重要初步步骤之一，就是从贷款机构获得融资，以便在重组债务的同时继续运营。是否向该企业提供融资的决定需经法庭批准，且通常会在听证会上进行讨论。

<!--en-->
One of the important initial steps taken by a company after it enters bankruptcy court is to find financing from a lender that will allow it to continue to operate while it reorganizes its debt. This decision to provide financing to a company is approved by the court and is often discussed at a hearing.

获得融资只是制定重组计划的第一步而已。该计划是由债权人委员会共同制定的。部分债权人可能希望尽可能多地收回欠款，因此会试图迫使企业296 • 前往法庭

<!--en-->
Securing financing is just one of the first steps in creating a reorganization plan. The plan is developed with a committee of creditors. Some of the creditors may want to be repaid as much as possible and may try to force the company to
296 • Headed to Court

#### 专家建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《华尔街日报》法律版块负责人詹妮弗·S·福赛斯关于报道法庭案件的看法：

<!--en-->
Wall Street Journal *law bureau chief Jennifer S. Forsyth on covering courts:*

### 注意每个破产案件背后的激烈竞争：

<!--en-->
*Look for the free-for-all at the center of every bankruptcy:*

这家被称为债务人的企业很可能有一长串需要还钱的对象，即债权人。企业会努力削减开支和债务，而债权人则争相尽可能多地收回欠款。这意味着所有参与破产程序的各方都在争夺有限的资源。有时，他们还会为保住工作而斗争，因为企业可能会解除工会合同或关闭工厂。同样，债权人有时也会迫使企业高管离职，或要求企业出售部分资产。还有些债权人则希望用自己应得的款项换取企业在破产程序结束后的一部分股权。

<!--en-->
The company, called the debtor, will likely have a long list of people or companies it owes money to, called creditors. The company will be looking to reduce its expenses and its debt while the creditors will be jockeying to get as much of what they are owed as possible. That means that everyone involved in a bankruptcy is fighting over a limited pot of money. Sometimes, they are also fighting for their jobs, as companies can tear up union contracts or close plants. Likewise, creditors can sometimes force out the company's executives.
sell some assets. Other creditors may look to exchange the money they are owed for an ownership stake in the company once it exits bankruptcy court.

企业会向法庭提交重组计划。记者应查明该计划的提交截止日期，并在计划提交后立即获取副本。该计划很可能是值得报道的内容，因为它首次披露了企业打算向债权人偿还多少款项。重组计划通常还会说明企业是否会关闭分店、解雇员工、削减高管薪资，或是采取其他措施来降低开支。

<!--en-->
A company files a reorganization plan with the court. Reporters should determine the deadline for the plan and make sure to get a copy as soon as it is filed. The plan is likely a story because it discloses for the first time how much money the company is proposing to repay its creditors. A reorganization plan often also discloses whether a company will close locations, fire workers, cut salaries for executives, or take other steps to reduce expenses.

债权人、债券持有者和股东必须接受重组计划。需了解，在大多数破产案件中，股东通常在重组计划中得不到任何补偿。随后，该计划还需得到法官的批准。

<!--en-->
Creditors, bondholders, and stockholders must accept the reorganization plan. Understand that in most bankruptcy cases, the stockholders typically get nothing as part of a reorganization plan. Then, the judge must approve it.

关于重组的报道应指出该计划使企业的债务减少了多少。企业进入破产法庭的主要原因是无力偿债。如果债务没有得到足够削减，企业未来可能会面临更多问题。

<!--en-->
Reorganization stories should point out how much the company's debt is reduced by the plan. The primary reason a company enters bankruptcy court is an inability to pay. If the debt has not been reduced enough, the company could face trouble down the road.

## 相关方

<!--en-->
*Interested Parties*

当一家上市公司申请破产保护时，其股东通常不会得到任何回报。债券持有者通常能获得偿付，但所得金额通常低于其全部投资额。

<!--en-->
When a public company files for bankruptcy-court protection, its stockholders usually get nothing in return. Bondholders often get paid but typically receive less than their full investment.

在企业破产申请过程中，还有其他一些群体与诉讼进程有着直接利益关系。律师、会计师、投资银行家、企业转型顾问，甚至企业高管，往往因帮助企业走出法律困境而获得数百万美元的报酬。这些相关方在破产法庭审理期间常常会彼此冲突，也会与企业发生矛盾。因此，了解他们在整个流程中的角色非常重要；通常，这些相关方之间的关系能为报道提供最佳素材。

<!--en-->
There are other groups involved with the bankruptcy filing of a company that have a vested interest in the proceedings. Lawyers, accountants, investment bankers, turnaround consultants, and even company executives often receive millions of dollars in return for their services in helping steer the company through the legal maze. These interested parties often clash with each other and the company during bankruptcy-court proceedings. Therefore, it is important to understand their roles in the process; often, the relationships between interested parties result in the best stories.

企业之所以陷入破产法庭，是因为无法支付开支。但破产法庭本身的运作成本也非常高昂。批评者认为破产法庭制度存在缺陷，而这些缺陷在涉及企业的诸多听证会和申请中就会显现出来。

<!--en-->
A company lands in bankruptcy court because it is unable to pay its expenses. But bankruptcy court itself can be very expensive. Critics argue that the bankruptcy-court system is flawed, and some of these flaws become apparent during the numerous hearings and motions filed in cases involving companies.

例如，在破产法庭中为企业提供服务的律师、顾问等，其费用必须经过审理该案件的法官批准。这些费用有时会引发法官以及读者的不满。

<!--en-->
For example, attorneys, consultants, and others performing work for companies in bankruptcy court are required to have their fees approved by the judge presiding over the case. These fees can sometimes raise the ire of judges —and readers.

《丹佛商业杂志》在一篇关于科罗拉多州“海洋之旅”水族馆破产案的报道中，详细介绍了当地律师、房产估值专家及其他顾问的收费情况。截至9月和10月底，这些费用总计超过241,000美元，其中包括支付给破产案律师四个月工作的费用135,581美元。

<!--en-->
The *Denver Business Journal* noted how much local attorneys, property valuation experts, and other consultants were being paid in a story about the bankruptcy case of Colorado's Ocean Journey aquarium. The fees and expenses totaled more than $241,000 for late October and September, including $135,581 paid to its bankruptcy attorney for four months' work.

彭博新闻在探讨律师费用的问题上走得更进一步。通过深入调查，彭博透露，截至2003年1月31日，2001年和2002年发生的25起最大规模破产案件中，相关企业的核心律师事务所共收取了2.35亿美元的律师费。

<!--en-->
Bloomberg News went a step further in discussing fees for attorneys. In its exhaustive research, Bloomberg disclosed that the 25 largest bankruptcies in 2001 and 2002 resulted in a total of $235 million in legal fees from the companies' primary law firms as of January 31, 2003.

在Global Crossing破产案中，牵头律所Weil, Gotshal & Manges LLP收取的部分费用包括：21,694美元用于餐饮，73,182美元用于计算机化研究，还有超过24,000美元用于撰写费用申请以获得破产法院法官的批准等事宜。Headed to Court • 297。彭博社关于这些高额费用的报道引发了得克萨斯州总检察长的批评，他认为这些费用“几乎没有带来任何实际成果”，而且“本应获得这笔钱的债权人及其他人正在看着资金被耗尽”（St. Onge, 2003）。

<!--en-->
Some of the fees charged by the lead law firm, Weil, Gotshal & Manges LLP, in the Global Crossing bankruptcy case included $21,694 for meals, $73,182 forcomputerized research, and more than $24,000 for activities that included composing its fee applications for the bankruptcy-court judge to approve.
Headed to Court • 297
The Bloomberg report of the large fees drew criticism from the Texas attorney general, who said he saw “little accomplished” for the fees and that the “creditors and other people who deserve this money are seeing it depleted” (St. Onge, 2003).

跟踪破产案的记者应始终查看该公司员工及律师提交的文件和动议，以此了解他们的薪酬水平以及所提供的服务是否确实必要。通常，这些文件和动议能构成有趣的报道素材。

<!--en-->
Reporters following a bankruptcy case should always look for the filings and motions by attorneys and others working for the company to examine how much they are being paid and whether the services they provide are needed. Often, these filings and motions make interesting stories.

但引发不满的并不仅仅是律师费。有时，破产案中由法院指定的监督人员也会反对某些开支，尤其是当他们认为这些钱可以更高效地用于其他方面时。Conseco破产案中就出现了这种情况，那些仔细获取法院文件的记者据此撰写了相关报道。处于破产程序中的公司高管同样会受到审视——处理该案的法官必须批准高管的薪酬。有时法官会认定支付给高管的薪资和福利过高；而有时公司则可能向法院起诉要求从高管处追回款项。2003年1月，当时已陷入破产的零售商Kmart要求五名高管偿还董事会未批准的贷款，并解雇了一些获得了这些贷款的高管。这一来自破产法院文件的消息成为了报道该案的各类媒体的重要新闻。

<!--en-->
But it is not just attorney fees that draw the ire of those involved. Sometimes, the court-appointed overseers of bankruptcy cases object to money being spent, particularly if they believe that the money could be spent more efficiently elsewhere. This happened in the Conseco bankruptcy and led to stories outlining those concerns by reporters who were vigilant in obtaining the court documents. The executives of a company in bankruptcy court also come under scrutiny. The judge handling their case must approve executives' compensation. Sometimes, a judge will decide that the salary and benefits paid to executives are too much. Other times, the company may go to the court and seek money from its executives. In January, 2003, then bankrupt retailer Kmart demanded that five executives repay loans not approved by the board and fired some of the executives who had received the loans. The story, which came from bankruptcy-court documents, was major news for the mass communication outlets covering the case.

一些破产法院专家认为，在任何相关文件中真正受益的是那些受雇来改善公司状况的人，由于他们往往能获得数百万美元的报酬，因此债权人会受损。另一些人则认为，如果没有这些专家长时间努力从处于破产保护下的公司中挽回尽可能多的价值，债权人、债券持有者和股东可能根本无法得到任何回报。记者的任务就是谨慎地在这两种观点之间找到平衡点。那些密切关注破产案进展并记录资金使用情况的记者，能够在很大程度上向读者解释这一复杂的重组过程。这并非易事，但只要对各种关系及法院运作方式有基本了解，记者就能帮助读者理解自己可能会受到怎样的影响。

<!--en-->
Some bankruptcy-court experts argue that the real winners in any filing are the people hired by the company to turn around its performance, and because they are often paid millions, creditors are hurt. Others argue that without these experts working long hours to salvage what they can from a company in bankruptcy-court protection, creditors, bondholders, and shareholders might not receive anything in return. The job of the journalist is to carefully toe the line between these two viewpoints. Reporters who carefully watch a bankruptcy case unfold and document how money is spent go a long way in explaining to their readers this complicated process of reorganization. It is not an easy job, but with some basic understanding of relationships and how the court works, reporters can help readers understand how they might be affected.

## 个人破产

<!--en-->
*Personal Bankruptcies*

正如本章前文所述，并非所有公私企业都会向破产法院提交相关文件。事实上，超过95%的破产法院案件涉及个人。

<!--en-->
As noted earlier in this chapter, public and private companies do not make all bankruptcy-court filings. In fact, more than 95 percent of all proceedings in bankruptcy court involve individuals.

对于商业记者而言，这类案件也极具价值，尤其是那些希望为所在地区的经济状况增添人性化视角的记者。通过追踪某一地区个人破产申请的增减情况，报纸可以更好地记录当地的经济状况。如果某三个月内寻求破产法院保护的人数比去年同期更多，那就表明当地人们正面临财务困境——他们可能已被解雇，无力偿还信用卡账单；或者虽然找到了工作，但薪水的水平远低于之前的工作。298 • Headed to Court。大多数破产法院都会统计每季度和每年提交的案件数量。通过向书记员询问这些数据，记者就能为写作打下良好基础。随后，记者可以查阅部分文件，记下近期申请破产保护的人的名字。在与这些债务人或其律师交谈后，记者很可能会写出类似《印第安纳波利斯星报》上的那篇报道。

<!--en-->
These cases can also be valuable for a business reporter, especially one who is interested in putting a human face on economic conditions in his region. Tracking the ups and downs of personal bankruptcy filings in a region can help a newspaper document its local economy. If more people are seeking bankruptcy court protection in a three-month time period than they were the same time a year ago, that is a good indication that people are struggling with their finances. They may have been laid off from jobs and are now unable to pay their credit card bills. Or they may have found a job, but one that pays much less than their previous job.
298 • Headed to Court
Most bankruptcy courts keep tallies of how many cases have been filed during quarterly and annual time periods. By asking the clerk for these numbers, a reporter has a good start on a story. The reporter can then look through a few filings and write down names of people who have recently filed for protection. After talking to a few of these debtors or their attorneys, the reporter could likely write a story similar to the following one from the *Indianapolis Star*.

2002年，裁员、过度支出以及抵押贷款债务导致印第安纳州南部三分之二的地区个人破产申请增加了13%，不过这一增幅还不到2001年28%增幅的一半。

<!--en-->
Layoffs, overspending and mortgage debt helped drive a 13 percent increase in personal bankruptcy filings in the southern two-thirds of Indiana in 2002, although the size of the jump was less than half of the 28 percent rise in 2001.

截至12月31日的那一年，破产申请数量为32,158件，高于2001年的28,551件，“这仍然是一个巨大的增长幅度”，负责印第安纳州及伊利诺伊州部分地区破产事务的美国破产管理人凯文·P·邓普西说道。

<!--en-->
The 32,158 filings in the year ending Dec. 31, up from 28,551 in 2001, “is still a huge increase,” said Kevin P. Dempsey, U.S. bankruptcy trustee for Indiana and part of Illinois.

“我们正处于历史最高水平。绝对是无与伦比的最高水平。”

<!--en-->
“We’re at record levels. It is, by far and away, a record level.”

根据美国法院行政办公室的数据，在截至9月30日的联邦财政年度里，印第安纳州南部的个人破产申请率是全国平均水平的两倍：相比7.8%的全国比率，该地区的上升幅度为15.9%。

<!--en-->
Personal bankruptcy filings in the southern district of Indiana were at twice the national rate during the federal fiscal year that ended Sept. 30: up 15.9 percent versus the U.S. rate of 7.8 percent, according to the Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts.

在75个联邦破产管辖区中，包括印第安纳波利斯在内的南部地区在该财政年度的破产申请数量位居第八。印第安纳州北部的破产申请数量则增长了17.5%，排名第四。

<!--en-->
The southern district, which includes Indianapolis, ranked eighth highest in bankruptcy filings during the fiscal year among 75 federal bankruptcy districts. Northern Indiana filings rose 17.5 percent in the fiscal year, or fourth highest.

邓普西表示：“2002年，印第安纳州的申请增长率处于最高水平或接近最高。”破产专家称，去年的增长源于与2001年相同的种种问题，包括经济疲软导致的裁员增加。

<!--en-->
“Indiana was at or near the top in percentage increases in 2002,” Dempsey said. Bankruptcy experts said last year’s increase was fueled by the same problems they saw in 2001, including a rise in layoffs during the sluggish economy.

印第安纳波利斯的破产律师马克·扎克伯格说：“印第安纳州一直是个重要的制造业州，但过去几年我们失去了太多工作机会。我认为人们已经尽力坚持下来了。”

<!--en-->
“Indiana has always been a major manufacturing state, and we have lost so many jobs in the past few years,” said Indianapolis bankruptcy attorney Mark Zuckerberg. “I think people have held on as long as they can.”

他说：“通常情况下，人们会用尽所有资源，因为没人愿意申请破产。等到我见到客户时，他们已经没有钱支付账单了。”⁸ 和企业一样，个人也可以选择根据第11章或第7章申请破产，有时个人的第11章案件会转为第7章案件。个人破产案件要经历与企业破产案件类似的许多步骤，包括与债权人的协商。而且个人破产案件的提交地点也与企业案件相同。不过，某些州的个人破产案件数量更多。

<!--en-->
“Usually they have used all the resources they have because nobody wants to file for bankruptcy. By the time I see clients, they have no more money to pay their bills,” he said.⁸
Like companies, consumers file either under Chapter 11 or Chapter 7, and sometimes, personal Chapter 11 cases convert to Chapter 7 cases. Personal cases go through many of the same steps that business filings encounter, including negotiations with creditors. And personal cases are filed at the same place as company filings. Some states have more filings, however.

一个主要区别在于，与企业案件不同，很少有贷款机构愿意为个人提供融资以帮助他们度过破产法庭的程序。破产记录可能会在个人的信用报告中保留长达10年。

<!--en-->
One major difference is that unlike corporate cases, there are few lenders willing to give consumers financing to help them make it through bankruptcy court. Bankruptcies can stay on an individual’s credit report for up to 10 years.

个人破产案例也能为其他报道提供重要信息，尤其是关于企业的报道。那些持有由曾申请个人破产的高管管理的公司股票的投资者，会希望了解这些信息。当《亚特兰大宪报》让其零售行业记者调查当地杂货连锁店Harry's Farmers Market Incorporated存在的问题时，该记者将该公司高层管理人员的名字输入了当地破产法庭的电脑系统。结果发现，该公司的临时首席财务官和一名商品采购副总裁曾有过个人破产记录。[^3280]：⁸ 摘自C. O’Malley于2003年1月10日发表在《印第安纳波利斯星报》第1C版的文章《州级破产案件激增；当地地区破产申请数量创纪录，是全国平均水平的两倍》，版权归《印第安纳波利斯星报》所有，经许可转载。通过报道这些事实，记者利用破产法庭的案例质疑这些高管管理价值数百万美元的上市公司的能力。如果他们连自己的个人财务都管理不好以至于不得不申请破产，又怎能负责监督Harry's每周数百万美元的商品和服务支出呢？

<!--en-->
Personal bankruptcies can also be important sources of information for other stories, particularly stories about companies. Investors who own stock in acompany run by an executive who filed for personal bankruptcy in the past would want to know that information. When the *Atlanta Journal-Constitution* asked its retail reporter to investigate the problems at local grocery store chain Harry's Farmers Market Incorporated, the reporter ran the names of its top executives through the computers at the local bankruptcy court. The reporter found that the acting CFO and a vice president of merchandising had been involved in personal bankruptcies.
[^3280]: ⁸ From “State bankruptcies go through the roof; area district filings set record and are twice national rate,” by C. O’Malley, January 10, 2003, *Indianapolis Star*, p. 1C. Copyright 2003 by *Indianapolis Star*. Reprinted with permission.
Headed to Court • 299
By reporting these facts, the reporter used the bankruptcy-court cases to call into question the ability of these executives to run a multimillion-dollar public company. If they could not manage their personal finances well enough to avoid bankruptcy court, how would they be able to oversee the spending of millions of dollars on goods and services each week for Harry's?

在某些情况下，个人破产会成为高管所在公司出现问题的前兆，尤其是私营公司。许多小型私营企业的所有者会将个人财务与企业运营混为一谈。一旦其中一方或双方——在某些情况下甚至是双方同时——出现状况，就可能面临破产法庭的诉讼。

<!--en-->
In some cases, a personal bankruptcy is the precursor to problems at an executive's company, particularly if it is a private company. Many owners of small and private businesses intermingle their personal finances with their corporate operations. When one or the other—or even both, in some cases—start to falter, a bankruptcy-court filing could be looming.

个人破产案的听证会往往占据法官在法庭上的大部分时间。虽然许多个人破产案件并不具备新闻价值，但它们确实常常反映出许多人面临的严重财务困境。在破产法庭待上一天，能让记者看到他们可能未曾经历的生活面貌，从而更深入地理解信用卡、贷款及其他金融工具若使用不当会造成的破坏。

<!--en-->
Personal bankruptcy hearings often take up the bulk of a judge's time in court. And although many personal bankruptcy cases are not newsworthy, they do often show the dire financial straits that many people encounter. Sitting in a bankruptcy courtroom for a day will show reporters a side of life they may not have experienced, giving them a broader understanding of how credit cards, loans, and other financial instruments can wreak havoc if not used properly.

## 建议练习

<!--en-->
*Suggested Exercises*

1. 在课堂上讨论消费习惯。你的同学是否认为他们的消费习惯可能会在未来导致债务问题？大多数学生拥有多少张信用卡？他们中有谁有汽车贷款？
2. 如果你学校附近的破产法庭有开庭，就去旁听。在下次课上，分享你的所见所闻，并探讨法官、债权人和律师之间的关系。
3. 假设某个周末你在当地的沃尔玛购物时，因过道里的玩具滑倒而摔断了腿。你会起诉这家零售商，要求其赔偿你所受的痛苦以及失去的工资吗？为什么或为什么不？
4. 你是当地一家报纸的记者，某天你去法院查看可能成为新闻素材的诉讼案件。你发现一家便利店连锁店正在起诉当地的一家甜甜圈制造商，要求解除要求该店铺只能销售其产品的合同，因为销售额下降了。这家便利店连锁店希望也能开始销售Krispy Kreme品牌的甜甜圈。文件中包含由便利店连锁店作为证据提交的、被标记为“机密”和“私人”的甜甜圈制造商文件。你会将这些文件用于你的报道吗？
5. 州保险监管部门已对一家当地保险公司提出指控，称其资产不足以覆盖保单责任，需接受监管监督。你致电该公司并与首席执行官交谈，他告诉你，如果你报道这些指控，该公司很可能会倒闭，因为保单持有人会恐慌并提取资金。他甚至通过视频通话让公司的律师参与对话，律师也表达了类似的观点。你会撰写这篇报道并在明天的报纸上发表吗？![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/28ea43c75649b559f3d457664e5f2bf5.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T071651Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=dad81d05341e7c3dc2ac5ee5c8d19c2cba01bb2024fde22f0455cd314ab6dee1)

<!--en-->
1. Discuss spending habits in class. Do your fellow students believe that their spending might cause them problems paying debt in the future? How many credit cards do most students have? Do any of them have car loans?
2. If a bankruptcy court district is located near your school, attend a hearing. During the next class session, discuss what you saw and comment on the relationship between judges, creditors, and attorneys.
3. Pretend that you're shopping in the local Wal-Mart one weekend when you slip on a toy left in an aisle and break your leg. Do you sue the retailer for the pain and suffering caused by your injury and for lost wages? Why or why not?
4. You're a reporter for a local newspaper, and you're checking the courthouse one day for lawsuits that may be potential stories. You find that a convenience store chain is suing a local doughnut manufacturer to terminate a contract requiring that only its doughnuts be sold at the store's locations because sales have dropped. The convenience store chain wants to start selling Krispy Kreme doughnuts as well. The file includes documents from the doughnut manufacturer that are marked "confidential" and "private" submitted as evidence by the convenience store chain. Do you use them as part of your story?
5. The state insurance department has filed charges against a local insurance company alleging that it doesn't have enough assets to cover its policies and needs to be placed into regulatory supervision. You call the insurance company and talk to the CEO, who tells you that if you write a story about the allegations, the insurer will likely go under because policyholders will get scared and take their money out of the company. He even gets the company's attorney on the phone via conference call, and the attorney makes similar claims. Do you write the story and run it in tomorrow's newspaper?

### 14

气泡啊气泡，房地产真麻烦

<!--en-->
Bubble, Bubble, Real Estate is Trouble

### 为什么土地会被买卖

<!--en-->
*Why Land is Bought and Sold*

无论是在国内还是全球，每家企业都从一个中心地点开展业务，这个地点通常被称为总部。企业要么购买这块土地并在上面建造建筑，要么从房地产公司租用土地。如果其业务规模超出当前场所的承载能力，它就会购买或租赁更大的空间。

<!--en-->
Every business in the country—and in the world—operates from a central location, often called a headquarters. The business has either purchased that land and constructed a building on the property or leased the property from a real estate company. If its operations become too big for its current location, it purchases or leases a building that gives it more space.

个人和家庭的情况也是如此。他们要么租房，要么买房，居住在公寓或住宅中。如果从这种角度看待房地产——即它是全国所有企业和消费者都不可或缺的东西——那么撰写相关文章就不会像乍看之下那样枯燥。关于房地产的报道并不仅限于房屋买卖或为吸引制造商和其他企业而建设新的工业园区。房地产在商业领域及国家经济中发挥着至关重要的作用。

<!--en-->
Individuals and families are in the same situation. They live in an apartment or in a house, either renting or buying. If one thinks about real estate this way—that it is the one necessity for every business and every consumer across the country—then writing about the topic does not seem as boring as it might at first glance. Writing about real estate does not involve covering just the buying and selling of homes or the construction of a new industrial park to attract manufacturers and other businesses to an area. Real estate plays a vitally important role in the business world and in the country's economy.

21世纪头十年的后半段表明，房地产市场对于商业和经济报道而言有多重要。从股市到信贷，再到个人理财，几乎所有商业报道都与房地产市场息息相关。

<!--en-->
The latter part of the first decade in the twenty-first century showed how important the real estate market is to business and economics coverage. The real estate market has impacted virtually every story in business reporting, from the stock market to lending to personal finance.

房地产交易可以是面积不足一英亩的小额交易，尤其是用于新建住宅。其他房地产交易则可能规模巨大，数百英亩的土地会被转让给计划将土地改造成大型购物中心或住宅区的开发商。简而言之，房地产是商业新闻及各类报道中一个涉及范围极广的主题。

<!--en-->
Real estate transactions can be small deals for less than an acre of land, particularly for the residential construction of a new home. Other real estate deals can be extremely large, with the ownership of hundreds of acres being transferred to a developer who plans to turn the land into a giant mall or subdivision. Simply put, real estate is a broad-reaching story in business journalism and throughout all reporting.

零售商需要房地产来建造店铺，制造商需要房地产来建设工厂，农民需要房地产来种植作物和放牧牲畜，垃圾收集员需要房地产来停放卡车并倾倒收集的垃圾。就连互联网公司也需要办公空间来运营业务。专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
Retailers need real estate to build their stores. Manufacturers need real estate to build their plants. Farmers need real estate to plant their crops and allow their cattle to graze. Trash collectors need real estate to park their trucks and to dump the garbage they collect. Even Internet companies need office space to run their businesses.
Tips from the Pros

加利福尼亚州《橙县纪事报》的Jon Lansner分享的关于跟进房地产新闻的经验：

<!--en-->
Jon Lansner of the Orange County Register in California on following the real estate beat:

**重视其重要性：**对您的受众中的许多人而言，住房是他们最大的开支——无论是否为房屋所有者。报道房地产领域的记者往往容易陷入名利之争，关注那些土地拥有者及开发商，却忘记了房地产的本质是为普通人提供遮风避雨的居所，无论是住宅、公寓、酒店还是办公室。别误会我的意思：知名企业及其庞大的房地产项目确实是极好的报道素材。但在制定房地产内容策略时，务必始终将普通房主和租客——更不用说建筑工人了——放在心上。

<!--en-->
**Respect the importance:** For many in your audience, housing is their largest expense—homeowner or not. Journalists covering real estate can often get caught up in the name game—watching the landowning powers, the developer players—and forgetting that this property game is really about roofs over little people's heads, whether that shelter be a house or apartment, a hotel or an office. Don't get me wrong: Big names and their big real estate prey are fabulous content. But always keep the average homeowner and renter—not to mention the construction workers—in mind when crafting your real estate content strategies.

304 • 泡泡泡，房地产真麻烦

<!--en-->
304 • Bubble, Bubble, Real Estate is Trouble

#### 专家建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

加利福尼亚州《橙县纪事报》的乔恩·兰斯纳关于跟进房地产新闻的建议：

<!--en-->
Jon Lansner of the Orange County Register in California on following the real estate beat:

经常提及负面因素：大多数房地产交易都是通过杠杆实现的，这提升了包括普通人和百万富翁在内的购房者的购买力。你认为止赎危机是如何发生的？杠杆具有双刃剑效应：既能放大收益，也能放大损失。在正当的交易中，它是一种具有挑战性的金融工具；在不正当的房地产操作中，它则是核心问题。从最近这一轮房地产的繁荣与萧条中，媒体应吸取的教训是：很少有人——无论是小人物还是大亨——能够妥善应对极高的杠杆效应。在报道繁荣时期的交易时，别忘了提出风险问题；而在追踪危机余波时，也别怕再次强调掌握杠杆的难度。

<!--en-->
Frequently note the dark side: Most real estate is bought using leverage, boosting the buying power of shoppers with both modest and millionaire means. How do you think the foreclosure crisis happened? Leverage works two ways: amplifying both gains and losses. It's a challenging financial tool in legitimate deals. It's also the lynchpin of crooked real estate moves, too. If there's one lesson for the media from this most recent real estate boom and bust cycle, it's this: Few people—small fish or big-time—can adequately manage extreme leverage. When covering the deal making in the good days, don't forget to raise the risk question. And when tracking the ashes of a debacle, don't be afraid to re-teach the lesson of how difficult leverage is to master.

其他人也需要房地产。城镇需要房地产来建设公园和学校；州政府需要房地产来安置数千名员工、设立办公场所，以及在现有校园无法容纳更多学生时扩建公立大学和学院；联邦政府则因军队基地及诸多其他原因需要房地产。

<!--en-->
Others need real estate as well. Towns and cities need real estate to build parks and schools. State governments need real estate to house thousands of employees and offices and to expand public universities and colleges when they outgrow their campuses. The federal government needs real estate for armed forces bases and hundreds of other reasons.

即便房地产并非企业的核心业务，企业也可能对其投资。例如，银行和保险公司将房地产视为可能提升盈利的投资项目。20世纪80年代末和90年代初，一些银行和保险公司过度投资于房地产，当房地产价值尤其是办公楼价格暴跌时，它们便遭受了巨大损失。

<!--en-->
Businesses may also invest in real estate even though real estate is not their primary operation. For example, banks and insurance companies see real estate as an investment that may boost their earnings. Some banks and insurers invested too much in real estate in the late 1980s and early 1990s and suffered when real estate values, particularly the price for office buildings, plummeted.

甚至还有一些公司——无论是上市公司还是私营企业——其唯一业务就是买卖房地产。它们的利润来自公寓楼和办公楼收取的租金。当房地产需求旺盛、出租率较高时，这些上市公司的股价会上涨；而当房地产供应过剩时，股价则会下跌。

<!--en-->
There are even companies—public and private—the sole business of which is to buy and sell real estate. Their profits come from the rent they collect from apartment complexes and office buildings. The public companies see their stock prices rise when real estate is in demand and occupancy rates are high and fall when there is a glut of real estate available.

房地产投资信托基金，通常称为REIT，是指拥有并运营各类房地产资产的公司，如办公大楼、购物中心、商业广场和公寓。这类公司必须将其90%的应税收入以股息形式分配给股东。目前有超过170家公开交易的REIT，总市值超过1600亿美元。此外还有私营REIT，它们在各大都市市场都拥有房地产资产。

<!--en-->
A real estate investment trust, commonly known as a REIT, is a company that owns and operates real estate properties, such as office complexes, malls, shopping centers, and apartments. These companies must provide 90 percent of their taxable income to their shareholders in the form of dividends. There are more than 170 publicly traded REITs with a market capitalization totaling more than $160 billion. There are also private REITs. These companies operate real estate properties in every major metropolitan market.

除此之外，还有成千上万的其他房地产公司从事商业地产的买卖业务。它们可能只拥有一处房地产，也可能拥有数百处；有的甚至可能是其他公司的一部分。

<!--en-->
In addition, there are thousands of other real estate companies that buy and sell commercial real estate. They may only own one piece of real estate, or they may own hundreds. They may even be part of another company.

撰写商业地产交易报道的记者通常会明确指出所购买的建筑、该交易的重要性以及新的业主和卖家。《芝加哥论坛报》曾报道过芝加哥市中心的所谓“标志性摩天楼”——Aon Center的出售情况，称这是该市历史上规模最大的交易之一。第二段提到了买卖双方，并指出该建筑共有80层；第三段则说明了成交价格，并将其与卖家最初的要价进行了对比。

<!--en-->
Reporters writing about commercial real estate transactions typically identify the building being purchased, the significance of the sale, and the new owner and the seller. A *Chicago Tribune* article on the sale of Aon Center, a so-called “trophy tower” in downtown Chicago, noted that the deal was one of the largest transactions in the city's history. The second paragraph named the buyer and seller and noted that the building had 80 stories. And the third paragraph mentioned the price and compared that figure with the original asking price from the seller.

记者在文章后半部分通过计算告诉读者该建筑的每平方英尺价格。他还努力查明该房产的实际成交价格。在很多情况下，这一价格可以在本章后面提到的公开记录中找到。但在这个案例中，记者不得不依靠行业消息人士来披露这一价格。对于任何重大收购而言，房地产交易的价格可能是最重要的信息，记者应当竭力获取这一数据。

<!--en-->
The reporter did some math and told readers the price per square foot of the building later in the story. The reporter also tried hard to pinpoint the actual purchase price for the property. In many cases, that price is available in public records discussed later in this chapter. But in this instance, the reporter had to rely on industry sources to disclose the price. The price of a real estate transaction is probably the most important fact for any major acquisition and should be aggressively pursued by the reporter.

商业房地产可分为几类。其中办公市场主要包括企业用于办公的写字楼。全美房地产经纪人协会预计，2009年第三季度的办公空间空置率将升至16.7%，而2008年第三季度的空置率为13.4%。在2008年租金下降0.4%之后，2009年的平均租金预计还将下降4.2%。空置率和平均租金是衡量当地商业房地产经济状况的重要指标，许多大型房产中介都掌握这些数据。

<!--en-->
Commercial real estate can be divided into several categories. There is the office market, which primarily includes office buildings in which businesses operate. The National Association of Realtors projected that the vacancy rate for office spaces would rise to 16.7 percent in the third quarter of 2009, up from a 13.4 percent vacancy rate in the third quarter of 2008. The average rent was expected to fall 4.2 percent in 2009, after a 0.4 percent decline in 2008. Vacancy rates and average rents can be important barometers for a local commercial real estate economy. Many large brokers have this information.

仓库市场也是商业房地产业务中的重要组成部分。企业会将成品甚至半成品存放在仓库中，等待出售或运往门店。全美房地产经纪人协会预计，2009年仓库的空置率将升至12.2%，略高于2008年的10.7%。根据该协会的预测，仓库租金则预计平均下降4.1%。

<!--en-->
The warehouse market is another important part of the commercial real estatebusiness. Businesses store their finished goods or even unfinished materials in warehouses, waiting to sell them or ship them to their stores. The vacancy rate among warehouses was expected to rise to 12.2 percent in 2009, up slightly from 10.7 percent in 2008. And warehouse rents were expected to decline by an average of 4.1 percent, according to the National Association of Realtors.

泡沫啊泡沫，房地产有麻烦了 • 305 零售市场同样属于商业房地产范畴。其空置率预计将在2009年第三季度升至13.4%，高于2008年第三季度的9.8%；而租金率在2008年下降2%之后，2009年预计还将下降9%。

<!--en-->
Bubble, Bubble, Real Estate is Trouble • 305
The retail market is also part of commercial real estate. Its vacancy rate was expected to rise to 13.4 percent in the third quarter of 2009, up from a vacancy rate of 9.8 percent in the third quarter of 2008, whereas rental rates were expected to drop 9 percent in 2009 after a 2 percent drop in 2008.

在住宅房地产市场中，21世纪初创下纪录后，近几年的房屋销售量有所下滑。根据全美房地产经纪人协会的数据，2008年售出的现有住宅超过490万套，较2007年的560万套下降了13.1%。2008年的现有住宅总销量为十多年来最低水平。2008年全美现有住宅的中位价格为198,600美元，较2007年的219,000美元下降了9.3%。

<!--en-->
In the residential real estate market, home sales have fallen in the past few years after setting records in the early part of the twenty-first century. There were more than 4.9 million existing homes sold in 2008, down 13.1 percent from the 5.6 million homes sold in 2007, according to the National Association of Realtors. The total existing home sales in 2008 was the lowest in more than a decade. The national median price for an existing home was $198,600 in 2008, down 9.3 percent from the median of $219,000 in 2007.

事实上，房地产交易可被视为经济状况的关键指标。如果房地产总收购量增加，说明该地区或国家的经济增长势头强劲；但若房地产销售放缓，则经济也可能正在走弱。（有关房地产，尤其是新屋销售和现有住宅销售以及经济状况的更多信息，请参阅第3章。）不过需要注意的是，住宅房地产市场的活跃程度会随利率波动，而利率又与联邦公开市场委员会对经济走向的决策密切相关。记者应咨询当地的抵押贷款机构，了解所在地区的利率变动情况。

<!--en-->
Indeed, real estate transactions can be viewed as a key barometer of the economy. If total real estate acquisitions increase, the economic growth of a region or the country is also likely strong. But if real estate sales slow, the economy is likely slowing as well. (For more on real estate, particularly new home sales and existing sales, and the economy, see Chapter 3.) However, note that residential real estate activity rises and falls with interest rates, which are tied to the Federal Open Market Committee's decisions on where the economy is headed. Reporters should check with a local mortgage lender to find out how rates are moving in their area.

还需了解的是，住宅房地产交易涉及不同类型的贷款。固定利率抵押贷款是指在整个贷款期限内——通常为15年或30年——利率保持不变的贷款类型。而浮动利率抵押贷款则是利率会根据美联储的政策调整以及其他因素而变动。由于2001年和2002年的利率处于历史低位，许多房主重新办理了抵押贷款以获得更低的利率，从而减少贷款利息支出。

<!--en-->
Also understand that residential real estate transactions involve different types of loans. A fixed-rate mortgage is one in which the interest rate remains the same throughout the term of the loan, usually 15 or 30 years. An adjustable-rate mortgage is one in which the interest rate fluctuates on the basis of the Fed's moves and sometimes other factors. With interest rates near all-time lows in 2001 and 2002, many homeowners refinanced their mortgages to receive better interest rates, thereby paying less interest on their mortgages.

那些关注并报道所在城镇、城市、县、州或地区的房地产市场动态的记者，能够帮助读者和观众了解经济运行状况。如果某个特定市场出现了大规模的商业房地产交易，企业高管们往往会认为该市场有望发展。但如果大量商业房地产项目长期滞销，可能意味着大型房地产买家预计价格会下跌，同时经济增速也在放缓。

<!--en-->
Reporters who follow and report about the activity of real estate in their town, city, county, state, or region of the country can help tell readers and viewers how the economy is performing. If there are large commercial real estate transactions occurring in a specific market, business executives believe the market can grow. But if there are large commercial real estate properties for sale for an extended period of time, it could mean buyers of large real estate are betting that the prices will come down and that economic growth could be slowing.

一个社区正在建设或新增的商业房地产类型也很重要。新的商业建筑是为企业总部提供办公空间，还是用于工业园区，届时可能会建造仓库和制造工厂？办公空间的租金往往高于仓库建筑的租金。

<!--en-->
The type of commercial real estate being built or added to a community is also important. Will the new commercial buildings provide office space for corporate headquarters, or will they be for industrial parks where warehouses and manufacturing plants will likely be constructed? The rent paid for office spaces is quite often more than that for warehouse buildings.

记者还应留意地方政府或州政府可能为新的商业房地产建设提供的任何优惠政策。通常，政府机构会通过税收减免来吸引企业迁入其辖区并开展建设，因为新企业的出现能创造更多就业机会，从而整体推动当地经济发展。

<!--en-->
Reporters should also watch for any incentives that a local or state government might be providing for new commercial real estate construction. Often, a government entity will offer tax breaks to entice a business to move to its area and build. This is because the new business means more jobs, which will provide an overall boost to the local economy.

## 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

加利福尼亚州《橙县纪事报》的乔恩·兰斯纳关于跟踪房地产行业动态的经验分享：

<!--en-->
Jon Lansner of the Orange County Register in California on following the real estate beat:

将商业地产视为经济指标：任何一个城镇中那些成功的开发商的兴衰都能成为很好的参考。那些在办公或工业地产租赁业务中获胜或失败的中介，其表现同样值得关注。但看待商业地产时，不应将其视为这些参与者的成绩单。相反，从出租空置率到新建筑许可数量等商业地产相关数据，才是反映一个地区经济状况的重要晴雨表。当然，这一行业偶尔也会出现偏差。但例如当地办公租金的趋势，可能就与任何实时的本地经济基准一样具有参考价值。

<!--en-->
Track commercial real estate as economic marker: the ups and downs of any town's rich dealmaker developers can be good copy. The office or factory brokers winning or losing leases are a game worth watching, too. But keep a keen eye on commercial real estate not as a scorecard of these players. Rather, trends in commercial real estate rates—from rental vacancies to new building permits—are a valuable economic barometer for a region. Sure, this industry misses the mark now and then. But the direction of local office rents, for example, may be as good as any real-time local economic benchmark.

306 • 泡沫，泡沫，房地产正面临危机

<!--en-->
306 • Bubble, Bubble, Real Estate is Trouble

### 专家建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

加利福尼亚州《橙县纪事报》的乔恩·兰斯纳关于跟进房地产动态的建议：

<!--en-->
Jon Lansner of the Orange County Register in California on following the real estate beat:

将抵押贷款利率视为反直觉现象：媒体常常将低息贷款视为对房地产行业的利好，而将利率上升视为利空。但经济历史表明事实并非如此。通常情况下，经济压力较大、需要刺激时，才会出现更便宜的抵押贷款——这类时期往往伴随着失业率上升，而失业者很难成为房地产的购买者。即便有稳定工作的人，也可能会因为担心被裁员或等待更优惠的贷款条件而推迟购房。相反，利率上升往往是经济繁荣、商业环境创造就业机会的体现——而这正是房地产行业所青睐的。更不用说这还会促使消费者在贷款成本过高之前赶紧购房。因此，在思考房地产的未来时，应客观看待抵押贷款利率的市场影响力，重点关注真正推动房地产发展的因素——即高薪且稳定的就业机会。

<!--en-->
See mortgage rates as counter-intuitive: Too frequently, the media portrays cheap loans as good news for real estate—and rising rates as bad. Economic history suggests otherwise. Traditionally, cheaper mortgages became available in times of economic stress—when the business climate needed a spark. Such periods often saw growing unemployment, and the jobless are poor purchasers of real estate. Even those with steady jobs may put off home purchases during these times—either through fear of layoffs or just waiting for a better mortgage deal. Conversely, rising interest rates are often the product of a growing economy, a business climate creating job opportunities—the kind of lift real estate loves. Not to mention nudging shoppers to buy before mortgages get too expensive. So when pondering housing's fate—keep mortgage's market clout in perspective and tend to focus on what really drives housing—the outlook for well-paying, secure employment.

此类税收减免通常需要由市议会或县委员会等地方政府机构批准。政府记者可能无法完全理解税收减免带来的影响，因而需要了解房地产行业的商业记者提供帮助。以下这篇报道展示了《堪萨斯城星报》是如何报道某项针对新房地产项目及其租户的税收减免政策的：

<!--en-->
A local government body, such as a city council or county commission, must often approve these tax breaks. A government reporter may not fully understand the ramifications of the tax break and may need help from a business reporter who understands real estate. The following story shows how the *Kansas City Star* covered one of these tax breaks for a new real estate development and its tenant:

周五，一家城市机构批准了一项开创性的税收减免政策，推动将HOK体育场馆活动项目引入河市场区域。

<!--en-->
A plan to bring HOK Sport Venue Event to the River Market advanced Friday when a city agency approved a trailblazing tax break for the development.

这个耗资4000万美元的混合用途项目的开发商Opus Northwest，从计划工业扩张管理局那里获得了其要求的全部25年的财产税减免。

<!--en-->
Opus Northwest, the developer of the proposed $40 million mixed-use project, got the full 25-year property tax abatement it wanted from the Planned Industrial Expansion Authority.

Opus的房地产开发总监戴夫·哈里森表示：“这是一个独特的项目，我们的合作租户也非常出色。我们希望明年这个时候，该地块上就能有大量的建设活动。”

<!--en-->
"It's a unique project and a great tenant we're working with," said Dave Harrison, Opus' director of real estate development. "We're hopeful this time next year there will be a lot of activity on the site."

这是该扩张管理局首次批准对某个项目给予100%的税收减免。此前该局已制定政策，用于处理其所称的特别税收减免情况。

<!--en-->
It was the first time the expansion authority had approved a 100 percent tax break for a project. It followed the authority's adoption of a policy to cover what it called extraordinary tax abatements.

Opus计划在怀安多特街与第四街交汇处建造一座六层高的建筑，底层将用作300个车位的公共车库，上层两层则容纳HOK的250名员工以及二十多套公寓。

<!--en-->
Opus wants to erect a six-story building at Fourth and Wyandotte streets that would house the 250 employees of HOK and two dozen condominiums on the upper two floors. A public 300-space garage would occupy the lower levels.

虽然目前仍未能与位于西第八街323号的HOK公司达成最终协议，但这家建筑设计公司已经签署了意向书，同意使用80,000平方英尺的场地。

<!--en-->
Though a final deal has not been reached with HOK, which currently is at 323 W. Eighth St., the architectural firm has signed a letter of intent to occupy 80,000 square feet.

哈里森称：“一切都在顺利推进中”，并补充说施工可能会在今年晚些时候或2004年初开始。HOK公司的官员表示希望尽快与Opus签订租赁协议。“我们很高兴，因为这意味着进展正在取得，”高级主管兼首席行政官理查德·A·马丁说道，“我们希望尽快解决这个问题并开始动工。”

<!--en-->
"All is continuing to move forward well," Harrison said, adding that construction could begin late this year or early in 2004. HOK officials said they hoped to sign a lease soon with Opus. "We're happy because it means progress," said Richard A. Martin, senior principal and chief administrative officer. "We want to get this resolved and get moving."

在上次扩张管理局会议上，由于这项前所未有的税收减免申请，该提案的审议被推迟。此前该局规定的最高税收减免为100%，期限为10年，50%的减免期限为15年。

<!--en-->
Consideration of the proposal had been delayed at the last meeting of the expansion authority because of the unprecedented tax abatement request. The authority previously has limited abatements to 100 percent for 10 years and 50 percent for 15 years.

理事会成员决定制定政策指南，用于审查Opus的请求以及未来所有要求全额税收减免的申请。在就Opus项目进行投票之前，该政策已获得一致通过。

<!--en-->
Board members decided they wanted to adopt policy guidelines to review the Opus request, as well as future requests for full tax abatements. That policy was approved unanimously before the vote on the Opus development.

这项新政策是基于城市规划与发展部门去年冬天提出的一份经济发展政策草案制定的。

<!--en-->
The new policy is based on a draft economic development policy proposed last winter by the City Planning and Development Department.

堪萨斯城议会推迟了对这项政策的审议。城市规划与发展主任维基·诺泰斯参与了新政策的讨论，并对其给予了总体肯定。“这是朝着正确方向迈出的一步，”她说，“它并不完美，但我们的草案也不尽如人意。”

<!--en-->
The Kansas City Council has delayed consideration of the policy. Vicki Noteis, city director of planning and development, was on hand for the discussion of the new policy and generally praised it. "This is a step in the right direction," she said. "It's not perfect, but neither was our draft."

该管理局的新政策与城市规划者所倡导的政策之间的一个区别在于，新政策并未要求将100%的税收减免仅限于市中心高速公路环线内的项目。

<!--en-->
One difference between the authority's new policy and the one advocated by city planners is that the new policy doesn't call for limiting 100 percent tax abatements to projects within the downtown freeway loop.

诺蒂斯表示，她的部门依然认为，与城市其他地区相比，市中心区域更需要额外的支持。“我们认为有必要为这些区域预留一两种应对手段，”她说道。

<!--en-->
Noteis said her department continues to believe the downtown loopdeserves help beyond that given other areas of the city. “We feel the need to reserve one or two tools in our arsenal for them,” she said.

《泡沫、泡沫，房地产真麻烦》• 307 诺蒂斯指出，如果将全面的税收减免以及所谓的“超级TIF”城市激励政策也提供给包括河市场、十字路口和西底部在内的非市中心区域，将会削弱这些政策的效力。

<!--en-->
Bubble, Bubble, Real Estate is Trouble • 307
Noteis said it would dilute the effectiveness of full tax abatements and so-called Super TIF city incentives if they were to be available to nonloop areas, including the River Market, Crossroads and West Bottoms.

在相关事宜上，董事会成员敦促Opus Northwest与附近另一个河市场项目“河景中心”的开发商合作，以便互相满足各自的停车需求。

<!--en-->
In a related matter, board members urged Opus Northwest to cooperate with the developer of another nearby River Market project, River View Central, to help each other meet their parking needs.

“河景中心”项目计划将位于西第四街228号的旧亚当斯转运公司大楼改造成办公及零售空间。不过，该项目的推进需要大量由公共资金支持的停车位。

<!--en-->
The River View proposal calls for the old Adams Transfer Co. building at 228 W. Fourth St. to be converted into office and retail space. The project, however, needs substantial publicly financed parking to proceed.

负责扩张事务的委员会主席埃德·德雷克表示，他的机构希望这两个项目能够协同合作，共同提供充足的停车位。

<!--en-->
Ed Drake, the expansion authority chairman, said his agency wants both projects to work together to provide adequate parking.

“河景中心”项目的开发协调人吉姆·德塔尔称，他的公司与Opus合作得很好。他表示，如果Opus的开发项目中能容纳更多车辆，那么“河景中心”项目就可以使用更简单、成本更低的停车场。¹ 这篇报道展示了已获批税收优惠的先例。每当有此类税收优惠获得批准时，记者们就应该查看是否有其他开发项目也获得了类似的待遇；如果没有，其他房地产开发商及其租户可能会要求类似的优惠。

<!--en-->
Jim DeTar, development coordinator for River View, said his firm was working well with Opus. The River View project would need a simpler, less expensive garage if more cars could be accommodated in the Opus development, he said.¹
This story shows the precedent for the approved tax break. Anytime one of these tax breaks has been approved, reporters should see if other developments have received similar deals. If they have not, other real estate developers and their tenants might go asking for a similar break.

住宅房地产对商业领域也很重要，尤其是那些开发住宅小区的开发商，比如D.R. Horton Incorporated。不过其他行业也对住宅房地产市场感兴趣。20世纪90年代，由于加利福尼亚州硅谷地区的房价过高，一些科技公司难以吸引员工。企业希望员工能够搬到他们感到舒适的社区或地区居住，同时也希望有价格符合其招聘员工经济能力的住房。

<!--en-->
Residential real estate can also be important for business, particularly developers, such as D.R. Horton Incorporated, that build subdivisions. But other businesses are interested in the residential real estate market as well. Some technology companies in the Silicon Valley of California had trouble attracting employees during the 1990s because of the high cost of homes in the area. Businesses want their employees to be able to move into a neighborhood or region with which they are comfortable. They also want housing that fits the price range of workers they are hiring.

住宅房地产还能以其他方式为企业带来好处。市中心的零售商希望看到公寓、联排别墅、共管公寓等住宅建筑建在市中心附近，这样他们的店铺才能有人光顾。如果没有居民住在他们店铺附近，这些零售商就会倒闭。

<!--en-->
Residential real estate can also be important to business in other ways. Downtown retailers like to see apartments, townhouses, condos, and other residential housing built near downtown so that their shops will be visited. Without residents living near their locations, retailers would close.

但房地产远不止是房产的买卖而已。正如本章其余部分所详述的，实际的交易只是始于数月之前的一系列漫长流程的终点。尤其是商业用地的收购过程中，会进行多次谈判，买家或租户会考察多个地点。与此同时，公共记录也会记载下房地产交易的许多环节。

<!--en-->
But real estate is much more than just the buying and selling of property. As the rest of this chapter details, the actual transaction is just the end of a long process that starts months earlier. Negotiations occur, particularly for commercial space. The buyer or the renter views multiple sites. And, along the way, public records record much of the process of a real estate transaction.

## 住宅房地产

<!--en-->
*Residential Real Estate*

虽然大多数房地产记者把大部分时间都用于报道商业市场，撰写关于在市中心建造新摩天大楼的交易新闻，或是关于[^3361]的内容：¹ 摘自K. Collison于2003年6月21日发表在《堪萨斯城星报》上的文章《HOK公司搬迁获税收优惠；这家建筑公司计划将总部迁至河市场》，第C1版。版权所有2003年《堪萨斯城星报》，经许可转载。

<!--en-->
While most real estate reporters spend the bulk of their time covering the commercial market, writing about deals to build new skyscrapers downtown or about
