## 建议练习

<!--en-->
*Suggested Exercises*

1. 查找你某位教授或学校院长的房产记录。在某些县，这些记录可能可在互联网上查询，先从那里开始。记下该房产的购买价格及年份，同时查找其评估价值。该房产的评估价值与购买价格之间存在什么差异？
2. 查阅当地的房地产记录，了解你的大学近期是否有任何资产收购行为。如果找到了，大学是否公开了对其拟如何处置这些资产的计划？是谁将这些资产出售给大学的？此人之前与大学有何关联？324 • 泡泡，房地产就是麻烦
3. 了解当地市或县政府何时会为未缴税的房产举行下一次止赎拍卖。参加这次拍卖，看看出售的是什么类型的房产——主要是商业房产还是住宅房产？尝试与部分买家交谈，了解他们是谁以及他们对这些房产的兴趣所在。
4. 参加当地分区委员会或规划委员会的会议，并撰写一篇500字的报告，说明当晚提交给委员会的各种房产类型，注明是否有任何反对这些开发项目的声音，以及这些项目最终是否获得批准。如果有些申请被否决，反对这些项目的理由是什么？

<!--en-->
1. Find the real estate records of the home of one of your professors or the dean of your school. In some counties, these records may be available on the Internet, so look there first. Write down how much the home was purchased for and in which year. Also look for the appraised value of the home. What is the difference between the appraised value of the home and the purchase price?
2. Check local real estate records to see if your university has made anyacquisitions recently. If you find some, has the university disclosed what it plans to do with the property? Who sold the property to the university? Did this person have any prior connection to the university?
324 • Bubble, Bubble, Real Estate is Trouble
3. Find out when the local city or county government will hold its next foreclosure auction for properties for which taxes have not been paid. Attend the auction. What types of property were sold? Was it primarily commercial property or residential property? See if you can talk to some of the buyers. Who are they, and what was their interest in the property?
4. Attend a meeting of the local zoning commission or planning board and write a 500-word report on the types of properties that went before the council that evening, noting whether there was any opposition to the developments and whether they were approved or not. If some requests were voted down, what were the reasons against the project?

## 15

政府监管

<!--en-->
Government Issue

## 监管机构

<!--en-->
*Agencies That Regulate*

在前面的许多章节中，都探讨了美国证券交易委员会及其在监管企业和股票方面的权力，尤其是这些监管措施如何帮助商业记者更好地向公众传递信息。

<!--en-->
Throughout many of the earlier chapters, the SEC and its powers in regulating businesses and stocks are discussed, particularly how those regulations can help business journalists do their job in informing the public.

但还有许多其他联邦监管机构也负责监督企业和公司。州级和地方政府机构同样致力于确保美国企业不会违规行事。

<!--en-->
But there are plenty of other federal regulatory agencies that also have a hand in overseeing businesses and corporations. State and local government bodies are also involved in ensuring that Corporate America does not run afoul.

商业监管是指制定规则、程序和法律来管理商业和工业领域。尽管许多企业高管可能会认为监管限制了他们的盈利能力，但这些法律和规则确实有其作用。大多数针对企业的法律和法规都是为了保护其他企业、消费者、员工以及竞争对手而制定的。

<!--en-->
Business regulation is the passing of rules, procedures and laws to govern business and industry. Although many business executives might argue that regulation limits their ability to produce a profit, the laws and rules do serve a purpose. Most laws and regulations governing businesses are enacted to protect other businesses, consumers, employees, and competitors.

美国的商业监管历史并不悠久。大多数规范商业领域的法律直到19世纪才得以颁布，这比第一批商人开设店铺并向消费者销售商品和服务已经过去了数百年。事实上，正是某些大型企业的不良行为促使立法者制定了针对企业的严格规则和限制。如今，全球性的政府组织也在参与监管企业的运营方式。

<!--en-->
Business regulation has not been around that long in the United States. Most laws governing the business world were not enacted until the nineteenth century, hundreds of years after the first proprietors set up shop and began selling their goods and services to consumers. In fact, it took the misdeeds of some major businesses to lead lawmakers into creating major rules and restrictions on companies. Even world-wide government organizations now play a part in overseeing how businesses operate.

美国政府对商业的监管是在19世纪末工业革命期间逐步形成的。随着一些企业规模不断扩大，其他企业也希望得到保护，以确保自身的权益得到保障。此外，由于一些公司滥用权力——忽视员工的工作条件、试图破坏工会，甚至对工人实施身体伤害甚至致其死亡——监管也应运而生。

<!--en-->
U.S. government regulation of business developed with the Industrial Revolution in the late nineteenth century. As some businesses became bigger and bigger, other businesses wanted protection so that their rights would be covered. In addition, regulation also came about because some companies misused their power. They neglected the working conditions of their employees and attempted to break unions. Some businesses physically harmed and killed their workers.

各州的政治家试图对企业进行监管，但他们的行动力十分有限。各州只能针对在其境内运营的企业制定相关法规。

<!--en-->
State politicians tried to regulate businesses, but they were limited in what could be done. States could only pass laws regulating businesses that operated within their borders.

### 专家建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

道琼斯通讯社华盛顿分社社长罗布·威尔斯关于将华盛顿相关新闻作为商业题材报道的经验：

<!--en-->
Dow Jones Newswires
Washington bureau chief Rob
Wells on covering Washington as a business story:

**竞选捐款：**请在日历上标注联邦选举委员会的季度及月度申报截止日期，以便追踪贵公司向政治人物捐赠的资金情况。同时查看各州的竞选信息披露记录也很有用，不过这些记录在质量和详细程度上差异很大。

<!--en-->
**Campaign contributions:**
Note on your calendar the quarterly and monthly filing deadlines at the Federal Election Commission to track the money one of your companies sprinkles on politicians. It's also useful to check the state campaign disclosure records, which vary greatly in quality and detail.

### 专家建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《克雷恩纽约商业报》前编辑总监格雷格·大卫关于报道商界与政府关系的经验：

<!--en-->
Former Crain's New York
Business editorial director Greg
David on covering the intersection between business and government:

**不要以为政治家了解商业运作方式：**他们通常并不了解。而你应该了解。326 • 政府干预在1880年代之前，联邦政府在美国商业领域的作用微乎其微。第一部重要的商业监管立法是1877年成立的州际商务委员会，该委员会最初负责监管当时全国主要的货物运输方式——铁路行业。1890年《谢尔曼反托拉斯法》的通过，使得联邦当局在商业监管方面迈出了重要一步，该法律禁止大型企业联盟的存在。由于最高法院阻止监管机构执行该法律，该法起初几乎没有任何效果。但到了世纪之交，政府最终取得了胜利：1904年政府获准拆分北方证券公司，1911年最高法院又支持政府拆分标准石油公司和美国烟草公司。

<!--en-->
**Don't assume politicians understand how business works:** They generally don't. You should.
326 • Government Issue
Before the 1880s, the federal government played a minor role in American business. The first major legislation regulating business was the creation of the Interstate Commerce Commission in 1877. The commission regulated the railroad industry, then the major transportation mode for goods across the country. With the passage of the Sherman Antitrust Act in 1890, federal authorities took a major step in regulating business. The law prohibited large trusts of businesses. The law initially had little effect, as the Supreme Court prevented its usage by regulators. But by the turn of the century, the government won out. In 1904, it was allowed to break up Northern Securities Company, and in 1911 the Supreme Court sided with the federal government in its breakup of Standard Oil Company and American Tobacco Company.

小型企业希望得到保护，免受大型竞争对手通过压低价格将其挤出市场的侵害；消费者则希望避免因垄断行为导致的价格上涨。不出所料，大型企业反对这些立法。

<!--en-->
Small businesses wanted protection against larger competitors squeezing them out of business by lowering prices. Consumers wanted protection from monopolistic operations raising prices. Not surprisingly, large business opposed this legislation.

从那以后，联邦层面通过了更多立法，赋予政府更多权力。1914年，国会通过《克莱顿反托拉斯法》，从而设立了联邦贸易委员会，该法对《谢尔曼反托拉斯法》进行了修订，禁止掠夺性定价，并将其他一些商业手段定为非法行为。

<!--en-->
Since then, more legislation has been passed at the federal level giving the government more powers. In 1914, Congress created the Federal Trade Commission when it passed the Clayton Antitrust Act, which amended the Sherman legislation by outlawing predatory pricing and making illegal other business tactics.

其他监管机构也相继出现。虽然食品药品监督管理局的历史可以追溯到1862年农业部的一名化学家，但1906年的《联邦食品和药品法》才赋予其监管权力。这部法律的出台源于厄普顿·辛克莱所著的《丛林》，书中描述了一家卫生条件极差的肉类加工厂里的工人状况。

<!--en-->
Other regulators also sprung up. Although the Food and Drug Administration traces its roots back to a single chemist in the Department of Agriculture in 1862, the Federal Foods and Drug Act in 1906 gave it regulatory authority. This act was spurred by Upton Sinclair's *The Jungle*, an account of workers in an unsanitary meat packing plant.

富兰克林·D·罗斯福执政期间，又有大量旨在规范商业行为的立法出台。1929年10月的经济危机引发了大萧条，为此国会成立了证券交易委员会来监管股市和上市公司。1934年的《通信法》设立了联邦通信委员会，负责监管广播和电视行业。与此同时，国会还成立了联邦存款保险公司，以稳定美国的银行业。

<!--en-->
Franklin D. Roosevelt's presidency saw another flurry of legislation creating laws governing business. Sparked by the October 1929 crash that led to the Great Depression, Congress created the SEC to oversee the stock markets and public companies. The Communications Act of 1934 established the Federal Communications Commission to regulate radio and television industries. And Congress created the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation at the same time to stabilize the country's banking industry.

1935年的《瓦格纳法案》设立了国家劳工关系委员会，该委员会负责防止企业干涉工人组建工会的权利，以及调查有关不公平劳动行为的投诉。该法律还允许委员会向违规企业发出停止违规行为的命令。

<!--en-->
The Wagner Act of 1935 created the National Labor Relations Board, which prevented companies from interfering with the rights of workers to organize into unions and to investigate complaints of unfair labor practices. The law also allowed the board to issue cease and desist orders against companies.

此后几十年里又陆续出现了其他监管机构。交通部直到20世纪60年代才成立，不过其部分下属机构的历史更为悠久。1970年通过的《职业安全与健康法》赋予联邦政府制定和执行工作场所安全与健康标准的权力。

<!--en-->
Other regulatory bodies have been added throughout the decades. The Department of Transportation was not created until the 1960s, although some of its units have longer histories. The Occupational Safety and Health Act passed in 1970, giving the federal government the authority to set and enforce workplace safety and health standards.

然而，20世纪70年代联邦政府开始出现放松监管的趋势。1978年，国会通过了《航空业放松管制法》，这意味着机票价格将由市场而非政府决定。尽管遭到航空业的反对，这项立法仍催生了许多新航空公司，同时也导致了一些航空公司倒闭。

<!--en-->
The 1970s, however, saw the beginning of a period of deregulation by the federal government. In 1978, Congress passed the Airline Deregulation Act, which meant that the market would set prices for airline tickets, not the government. Opposed by the industry, the legislation led to a number of new airlines, and a number of airline company failures.

然而，联邦监管依然有效。1984年，反垄断法被成功用于迫使AT&T分拆，这与70年前用于标准石油公司和美国烟草公司的做法如出一辙。20世纪70年代末，联邦贸易委员会开始负责审查所有的并购交易。一个多世纪以来，州政府和地方政府机构也一直在参与商业监管。例如，各州在20世纪初就开始对公用事业进行监管。俄勒冈州公共事业委员会最初成立于1887年，名为州铁路委员委员会，后于1907年被废除并重组为俄勒冈州铁路委员会。四年后，其管辖范围扩大到了包括公用事业在内。

<!--en-->
Federal regulation, however, is still alive and well. In 1984, the antitrust laws were successfully used to force the breakup of AT&T just as they had beenused 70 years earlier in Standard Oil and American Tobacco. And the Federal Trade Commission took on reviewing all mergers and acquisitions in the late 1970s.
Government Issue • 327
State and local government agencies have also had a hand in regulating business for more than a century. States, for example, began regulating utilities near the beginning of the twentieth century. The Oregon Public Utility Commission began as the State Board of Railroad Commissioners in 1887, but was abolished and then recreated as the Railroad Commission of Oregon in 1907. Four years later, its jurisdiction was expanded to include utilities.

全国各地的公共服务委员会和公共事业委员会负责监督电力公司、水务公司及其他公用事业向客户收取的费用。它们还常常设定这些公司可获得的利润上限。有时，这些公司会因违规行为而受到监管机构的处罚。几年前，北卡罗来纳州的一家公用事业公司因盈利过高而遭到查处，《夏洛特观察家报》为此刊登了一篇头版报道，开篇如下：

<!--en-->
Public service commissions and public utility commissions across the country oversee how much electrical companies, water companies, and other utilities charge their customers. They also often set limits on how much of a profit these companies can make. Sometimes, these companies can get in trouble with the regulatory agencies that oversee their business. A few years ago a North Carolina utility was found to have made too much money, causing the *Charlotte Observer* to write one front-page story that began the following way:

> 据知情人士透露，联邦调查人员将在比卡罗来纳州监管机构去年进行的调查更深入的基础上，进一步审查杜克能源公司的数千份文件。据消息人士称，联邦检察官和FBI特工将仔细查看超过4万份文件，其中包括在该州调查期间发现的那份存在争议的电子表格，以判断杜克能源公司是否故意且不当地篡改了账目并犯下了罪行。在去年为期10个月的调查之后，独立审计机构格兰特·桑顿有限责任合伙公司称，杜克能源公司在三年间少报了1.24亿美元的受监管利润。该机构表示，杜克能源公司改变了会计方法，以便符合监管机构规定的利润率标准。当杜克能源公司的利润超出规定限额时，公用事业委员会可以降低该公司在北卡罗来纳州210万客户的电费。杜克能源公司称自己只是犯了无意的一次性错误，并未犯罪。作为北卡罗来纳州最大的公用事业公司，杜克能源公司是总部位于夏洛特的杜克能源公司的子公司，后者在《财富》500强榜单中排名第118位，去年的营收为152亿美元。《观察家报》在10月刊文报道格兰特·桑顿公司关于杜克能源公司违规行为的指控后，联邦调查人员开始了调查。2月份，杜克能源公司宣布已收到大陪审团的传票，要求提供与格兰特·桑顿公司审计相关的文件。在收到传票前几天，杜克能源公司聘请了前美国检察官马克·加洛韦为公司代理。该公司还为十几名员工找来了顶尖的刑事辩护律师。通常，企业和员工在得知自己正在接受调查时就会聘请律师。¹ [^3606]：¹ 摘自S. Choe和G.L. Wright所写的《联邦政府进一步深入调查杜克能源公司》，2003年5月11日，《夏洛特观察家报》，第1A页。版权所有2003年《夏洛特观察家报》，经许可转载。328 • 政府资讯

<!--en-->
> Federal investigators will review thousands of additional documents in a deeper probe of Duke Power's accounting than the one Carolinas regulators conducted last year, sources close to the investigation say.
> Federal prosecutors and FBI agents will scour more than 40,000 documents, including a controversial spreadsheet unearthed during the states' investigation, as they evaluate whether Duke intentionally and inappropriately altered its accounting and committed any crimes, according to sources.
> After a 10-month investigation last year, independent auditing firm Grant Thornton LLP said Duke underreported $124 million in regulated profits over three years. Duke changed its accounting methods to fall under the profit margin mandated by regulators, the firm said.
> When Duke goes over its allowed limit, utility commissioners can lower the power bills for Duke's 2.1 million Carolinas customers.
> Duke says it made unintentional, one-time errors but committed no crime. Duke Power, the Carolinas' largest utility, is a subsidiary of Charlotte-based Duke Energy Corp., which is No. 118 on the Fortune 500 with $15.2 billion in revenue last year.
> Federal investigators began their probe after *The Observer* published stories in October about Grant Thornton's allegations of Duke wrongdoing. In February, Duke announced it had received a grand jury subpoena requesting documents related to the Grant Thornton audit.
> Days before receiving the subpoena, Duke hired former U.S. Attorney Mark Galloway to represent the corporation. The company also helped assemble A-list criminal defense lawyers for more than a dozen employees. Companies and their employees typically hire lawyers when they learn they're under investigation.¹
[^3606]: ¹ From “Fed deepens Duke probe,” by S. Choe and G.L. Wright, May 11, 2003, *The Charlotte Observer*, p. 1A. Copyright 2003 by *The Charlotte Observer*. Reprinted with permission.
328 • Government Issue

### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《克雷恩纽约商业报》前编辑总监格雷格·大卫谈如何报道商业与政府的交叉领域：

<!--en-->
Former Crain's New York Business editorial director Greg David on covering the intersection between business and government:

追踪资金流向：受监管行业的企业高管们会向政治候选人捐款数百万美元，以此确保能获得政策支持或有利决策。例如，纽约州参议员查尔斯·舒默就瞄准大型银行和华尔街机构，为民主党掌控国会提供资金支持。那么，为什么这些企业及其高管要向民主党人捐款呢？

<!--en-->
Follow the money: Regulated industries and their executives give millions to political candidates to ensure access and maybe favorable decisions. For example, New York Sen. Charles Schumer targeted big banks and Wall Street firms to help finance the Democratic takeover of Congress. Why did the companies and their executives give to Democrats?

该报道后来引用了南卡罗来纳州公共服务委员会的执行主任的话，称他查阅过的文件让他确信，这些公司显然存在少报利润的意图。

<!--en-->
The story later quotes the executive director of the South Carolina Public Service Commission saying that documents he reviewed convinced him there was an obvious effort to underreport profits.

各州在监管其他行业，如银行业和保险业方面也发挥着重要作用。与大多数由联邦政府监管的行业不同，保险业的监管是按州来进行的。每个州都设有保险专员，负责监管在该州开展业务的保险公司。一些州，如纽约州，针对保险公司的法律比其他州更为严格，这迫使一些保险公司不得不在当地设立独立的子公司，或者干脆放弃在该州开展业务。各州还要求在其境内经营的每一家企业都必须向州政府注册。这些信息可能具有很高的价值，本章后面将会讨论。

<!--en-->
States also play a major role in regulating other industries, such as banking and insurance. Unlike most industries that are regulated by the federal government, regulation of the insurance industry is done on a state-by-state basis. Each state has an insurance commissioner who regulates the insurers doing business in that state. Some states, such as New York, have laws governing insurance companies that are more strict than other states, forcing some insurers to create separate subsidiaries to do business there or to eschew the state altogether. States also require each and every business that operates in its territory to register with the state. This information can be valuable, and is discussed later in this chapter.

最后，一些县、市和镇还制定了企业必须遵守的法律法规。例如，开发商在动工推平土地之前，必须先获得镇议会或市委员会的批准，才能建造新的住宅区。若要扩大建筑规模以适应业务发展，同样需要许可证。

<!--en-->
Last, some counties, cities, and towns also have laws and rules that businesses must follow. Developers, for example, must get plans to build a new subdivision approved by a town council or a city commission before they can start bulldozing. Expanding a building to handle the growth of a business also takes a permit.

政府机构对企业提出的所有规则、法律、法规及其他要求，都是为了在公众利益与企业发展、扩张以及持续成为社区重要组成部分的需求之间取得平衡。有时，政府机构甚至会试图推动立法，以吸引新企业入驻该地区，或提升现有企业的经营水平。

<!--en-->
All of the rules, laws, regulations, and other requirements that government agencies require of businesses attempt to balance the interest of the public with the need of a business to grow, expand, and continue to be a thriving part of the community. Sometimes, a government entity will even try to get legislation passed that will bring new business into the area, or improve the quality of existing businesses.

以下摘录是一则关于企业故事的开头示例，源自某州立法机构为改变企业运营方式而提出的法案：

<!--en-->
The following excerpt is an example of the beginning of a business story that comes from following bills introduced in a state Legislature to change how businesses would operate:

如果劳工专员切丽·贝里能如愿以偿，北卡罗来纳州那些改善工作场所安全的企业或许可以获得税收减免作为奖励。

<!--en-->
North Carolina businesses that improve workplace safety could be rewarded with a tax break if Labor Commissioner Cherie Berry has her way.

贝里正在推动众议院和参议院已提交的法案，这些法案旨在为那些主动改善工厂、办公室、商店及建筑工地安全措施的企业提供税收抵免，而这些地方正是数百万北卡罗来纳州民众的工作场所。

<!--en-->
Berry is pushing for bills that have been introduced in the House and Senate that would give tax credits to companies that voluntarily improve safety in factories, offices, stores and construction sites where several million North Carolinians spend their working hours.

贝里在周二表示，其目的是帮助那些尚未设立安全主管，或是担心向劳动部门求助后会被迫进行无力承担的改进措施的中小雇主。

<!--en-->
The idea, Berry said Tuesday, is to reach smaller employers that don't have a safety director on board or fear that by asking the labor department for help they might be forced to make improvements they can't afford.

“在当前的商业环境下，我们正竭尽所能促进安全与健康，并对采取此类措施的企业给予奖励，”她说。“这表明我们是在努力与各方沟通，而非像过去那样仅用强硬手段进行监管。”

<!--en-->
"We're trying in this business climate to do as much as we can to promote safety and health and reward businesses that take that step," she said. "It shows that we're trying to reach out, rather than, as in the past, just go out and enforce with that big hammer and club."

自两年前上任以来，自愿合规一直是贝里的工作重点。她的首批举措之一就是撤销前任哈里·佩恩试图实施的那些要求企业更加重视重复性劳损问题的人体工程学规定。她的机构一直与雇主合作，帮助他们减少此类伤害，在某些案例中取得了显著成效。

<!--en-->
Voluntary compliance has been a mission of Berry's since she took office two years ago. One of her first moves was to roll back ergonomics rules that her predecessor, Harry Payne, had sought to make businesses pay closer attention to repetitive stress injuries. Her agency has worked with employers to help them reduce such injuries, reporting strong results in certain cases.

但有人质疑这些税收抵免法案的公平性，以及在经济危机时期出台此类立法的时机。

<!--en-->
But some question the fairness of the tax credit bills, as well as the timing of such legislation during a budget crisis.

位于罗利市的保守派智库约翰·洛克基金会主席约翰·胡德表示：“你可不希望出现一种制度，让那些已经投资于安全措施的企业得不到任何回报。现在这些企业在法律通过后才来申请补贴。这种出发点固然值得赞赏，但我对于通过修改税法来推行除增加收入之外的其他政策还是持谨慎态度。”² 政府动态 • 329 此外，近年来许多州都开始积极起诉违规企业，前纽约州总检察长埃利奥特·斯皮策就是监管机构因企业涉嫌犯罪而提出指控的典型例子。了解政府如何监管企业，往往能催生出精彩的企业故事。政府与企业之间常常发生冲突，而这种冲突正是优质新闻素材的来源。

<!--en-->
"You don't want to create a system where companies that have already invested in safety get nothing," said John Hood, president of the John LockeFoundation, a conservative think tank in Raleigh. “And now that they’re coming in after the law is passed, they get money. The impulse here is commendable, but I would be hesitant to go into the tax code to find a tool to pursue policies other than raising revenue.”²
Government Issue • 329
In addition, many states have recently become aggressive in prosecuting companies for wrongdoing, with former New York Attorney General Eliot Spitzer being a prime example of a regulator filing charges for alleged crimes by business. Following how government regulates business can turn into exciting business stories. Government and business often clash, and that conflict results in good copy.

本章其余部分将探讨政府监管为何是撰写涉及商业和经济领域报道的重要要素。

<!--en-->
The rest of this chapter explores how government regulation is an important part of writing stories that explain the ins and outs of covering business and the economy.

## 私营企业监管

<!--en-->
*Private Company Regulation*

对于负责撰写商业版面新闻的记者而言，跟进政府的监管动向至关重要，尤其是那些主要负责报道私营企业的记者。

<!--en-->
Following the government trail of regulation is important to a reporter who writes stories for the business section, particularly for a writer who spends most of his or her time covering private companies.

大多数私营企业无需像上市公司那样向美国证券交易委员会报告其财务表现及其他重大变动。但了解私营企业向政府监管机构披露的信息，有助于记者挖掘私营企业的新闻线索。尽管私营企业似乎不愿提供信息，但实际上只要知道去哪里查找，就能找到大量相关信息。

<!--en-->
Most private companies do not have to report on their financial performance and other major moves like public companies do to the SEC. But knowing and understanding what private companies disclose to government regulators can help a reporter uncover the news at private businesses. Even though it may seem that private companies are reticent in providing information, the truth is that there is plenty of information available if you know where to look.

所有企业，无论是上市公司还是私营企业，都必须向所在州的州务卿办公室登记相关资料。为撰写文章而调查某家企业的记者应查询该企业在州政府的注册记录，其中会包含邮寄地址、电话号码以及高管信息。例如，当记者正在报道一家被起诉但无法联系到企业相关人员发表意见的公司时，这些信息就非常重要。非营利组织以及律师事务所等有限责任公司也需要提交注册记录。

<!--en-->
All companies, public and private, are required to register certain information with their Secretary of State’s office. Reporters researching any company for an article should look up the company’s incorporation records with the state, which will provide the mailing address, phone number, and officers. This can be important information, for example, if a reporter is writing about a company that has been sued but has been unable to contact anyone at the business for comment. Incorporation records are also required of nonprofit organizations and limited liability corporations such as law firms.

各州还保存着大量关于私营公司的公共记录。每个州都有职业许可机构，要求从理发店到助听器供应商等众多企业在开业前取得许可证。这些机构可能还保存着记者正在调查的该公司的相关额外记录。

<!--en-->
There are plenty of other public records available on private companies at the state level. In every state there are occupational licensing boards that require many businesses, from barbershops to hearing aid providers, to obtain a license before opening shop. These boards may have additional records on the company a reporter may be writing about.

如果私营公司的名称与公司法人名称不同，还必须注册该商业名称。在很多地方，这项工作由县级的土地登记处或类似的法院办公室负责办理。这是查明一家公司实际所有人的好途径。[^3632]：² 来自K. Rives于2003年5月7日发表在《The News & Observer》杂志D1版的文章《劳工部试图用激励措施：建议为主动提升安全标准的企业提供税收优惠》，版权归《The News & Observer》所有，经许可转载。330 • 政府动态

<!--en-->
Private companies must also register their business name if that name is not the same name as the corporation. In many places, this is done with the Register of Deeds office, or a similar courthouse office, at the county level. This is a good place to find out who is the actual owner of a company.
[^3632]: ² From “Labor Department tries carrot: It recommends tax breaks for companies that willingly improve safety,” by K. Rives, May 7, 2003, *The News & Observer*, D1. Copyright 2003 by *The News & Observer*. Reprinted with permission.
330 • Government Issue

### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《Crain's New York Business》前编辑总监Greg David谈如何报道企业与政府的交集：***追踪说客：** 查明哪些人既作为企业和行业协会的员工，又作为知名游说公司的雇员，代表关键行业和企业。了解这些说客的过往经历，他们通常曾是立法者、监管人员或立法者的工作人员。为什么大型制药公司会聘请一名前国会议员来为全国医疗保健政策游说，而他为何又敦促这些公司与奥巴马政府达成协议？

<!--en-->
Former Crain's New York Business *editorial director Greg David on covering the intersection between business and government:***Track the lobbyists:** Find out who represents key industries and companies both as employees of companies and trade associations and as hired guns for well-known lobbying firms. Check the lobbyists' prior lives, usually as legislators, regulators or staff members to legislators. Why did the big drug companies hire a former congressman to lobby on national health care and why did he urge them to reach a deal with the Obama administration?

房地产记录也是获取私营公司信息的另一重要渠道。记者应核查这些交易记录，看该公司是否拥有任何土地或建筑物。以公司总裁或首席执行官的姓名查询这些记录也很有效。这项工作可在县法院或该公司买卖房产所在的县进行。

<!--en-->
Real estate records are another good place to look for information about private companies. Reporters should check these transactions to see if a company owns any land or buildings. It is also good to check these records under the name of the company president or CEO. This can be done at the county courthouse, or the county in which the business is buying or selling property.

私营公司还需披露有关裁员及工作条件的信息。这些记录可通过当地的劳工部门或职业安全与健康管理局（OSHA）获取。例如，大规模裁员情况通常会向劳工监管机构报告，而OSHA则会对工厂和生产企业进行检查，尤其是在发生事故或人员死亡之后。只需一个电话就能获取这些记录。

<!--en-->
Private companies are also required to disclose information about layoffs and working conditions. These records can be obtained through your local Department of Labor or Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) office. For example, mass layoffs and firings of workers are typically disclosed to labor regulators, and OSHA conducts inspections on factories and plants, particularly after an accident or death. Obtaining those records can be as easy as one phone call.

特定行业的州级监管机构也要求许多企业提交其财务绩效信息。这类监管机构包括负责监督银行、保险公司以及水电公用事业的机构。私营公司需向这些监管机构提交利润和收入数据。找到这些记录存放处的记者很可能会获得企业原本不愿公开的信息。

<!--en-->
State regulators of specific industries also require many companies to file information about their financial performance. Some of these regulatory agencies include those that oversee banks and insurance companies, as well as water and electrical utilities. Private companies document their profits and revenues to these regulatory agencies. Reporters who find out where these records are kept will likely get information that the company otherwise would not be willing to disclose.

私营公司还受多层级联邦监管机构的管辖。即便是最小的企业，如非营利机构和信用合作社，也必须提交其运营相关的财务信息。有关非营利组织的更多信息，请参见第12章。

<!--en-->
Private companies come under the jurisdiction of federal regulators at numerous levels. Even the smallest companies, such as nonprofit institutions and credit unions, are required to file financial information about their operations. For more information about nonprofits, see Chapter 12.

全美所有的信用合作社都受国家信用合作社管理局的监管。信用合作社必须每季度向该联邦机构提交信息，内容包括总资产、总贷款额、总股本以及贷款收入的明细。

<!--en-->
All credit unions across the country are governed by the National Credit Union Administration. Credit unions are required to file information to this federal agency on a quarterly basis. The information includes total assets, total loans, total equity, and a breakdown of the loan income.

北卡罗来纳州东部《Goldsboro News-Argus》报的财经记者会定期查看其所在地区的信用合作社——北卡罗来纳社区信用合作社的这些信息。通过这些数据，他发现该信用合作社在该年度第三季度报告的净收入为124,586美元，但在同年最后三个月却亏损了242,469美元，降幅极为显著。

<!--en-->
The business reporter for the *Goldsboro News-Argus* in eastern North Carolina regularly reviews this information for the credit union in his town, North Carolina Community Credit Union. By receiving this information, he discovered that the credit union had reported net income of $124,586 in the third quarter of a year, but lost $242,469 in the last three months of that year, a dramatic drop.

私人拥有的银行和储蓄机构也需向联邦监管机构，如联邦存款保险公司（FDIC）、储蓄机构监管局以及货币监理局，提交财务信息。

<!--en-->
Privately owned banks and thrifts are also required to provide financial information to federal regulators such as the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC), the Office of Thrift Supervision, and the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency.

联邦政府还有其他一些经常与企业打交道的机构。例如，环境保护局掌握着处理环境敏感化学品和产品的企业的相关资料；食品药品监督管理局则存有数千家企业销售的食品和药品的相关信息；美国专利商标局则保存着企业用于生产产品的专利和商标申请文件。记者应定期查看这些申请文件，以了解所报道的企业是否获得了可能有助于其业务发展的新专利或商标。

<!--en-->
The federal government has other agencies that come in contact regularly with businesses. The Environmental Protection Agency, for example, has information on companies that handle environmentally sensitive chemicals and products. The Food and Drug Administration has information on food products and drugs sold by thousands of companies. The U.S. Patent and Trademark Office maintains filings of patents and trademarks that a company uses to make its products. Reporters should check these filings regularly to see if businesses they write about have received new patents or trademarks that may help their operations.

有时，私营企业会与这些政府机构产生矛盾。除了核查企业的基本财务信息和背景资料外，记者还应留意相关的罚款及监管措施。与受SEC监管的上市公司不同，私营企业若想拓展新业务领域无需向政府披露——当然，除非新业务涉及需要审批的新产品，比如药品。但“私营”企业并不像看上去那么隐秘。通过恰当的调查，记者只需查看监管该企业的政府机构并追踪相关文件，就能让私营企业的运营透明度堪比上市公司。（有关私营企业的更多信息，请参见第11章。）政府专题 • 331

<!--en-->
Sometimes, private companies run into trouble with these government agencies. In addition to checking for simple financial information and background information about private businesses, a reporter should also look for fines and regulatory actions. Unlike public companies regulated by the SEC, private companies do not have to disclose to the government if they want to branch into different business lines—unless, of course, the new business line requiresapproval of a new product, such as a drug. But “private” companies are not as private as they may seem. With the right research, a reporter can make the operations of a private company as transparent as that of a public business simply by looking at the government agencies that oversee it and following a paper trail. (For more information about private companies, see Chapter 11.)
Government Issue • 331

## 保险与银行监管机构

<!--en-->
*Insurance and Banking Regulators*

对于任何记者而言，金融服务行业的各个领域都可能是极具挑战性的报道领域。银行和保险公司几乎影响着所有大众传媒用户的生活：大多数人都有支票账户、储蓄账户以及自动取款机卡，人人都有汽车保险，还有很多人购买了人寿保险。然而，银行和保险公司往往是最难理解的机构。它们是如何盈利的？又如何使用消费者支付的资金？

<!--en-->
Sectors of the financial services industry can be daunting beats for any reporter. Banks and insurance companies touch the lives of virtually every user of mass communication. Most people have checking and savings accounts, and automated teller machine cards, everyone has auto insurance, and many people have life insurance policies. Yet banks and insurance companies can be some of the hardest to understand. How do they make money? What do they do with the money that consumers pay them?

与大多数行业不同，保险业由各州的保险专员负责监管，而这些专员在监管标准上往往存在分歧，并非总是达成一致。此外，每个州都制定了管理保险公司的法律，而这些法律在全国范围内并不统一。因此，一家全国性保险公司在加利福尼亚州必须遵守的法律可能与佛罗里达州的法律不同。

<!--en-->
Unlike most industries, the insurance business is regulated by state insurance commissioners who often, but not always, agree on regulation. In addition, each state has passed laws to govern insurance companies, and these laws are not the same across the country. So the laws that a national insurance company must adhere to in California might not be the same as the laws in Florida.

保险专员都是政治人物。他们中的许多人是民选官员，必须获得所在州的多数选票才能任职。因此，担任这些职务的人可能并不具备丰富的保险行业背景。有些人可能会将这一职位视为通往更高职位的跳板，比如州长或参议员。

<!--en-->
Insurance commissioners are politicians. Many of them are elected officials who must win a majority of the votes in their state to hold the position. As such, the people holding these positions may not have had much background in the insurance industry. Some of them may view the office as a stepping stone to something greater, such as governor or senator.

在许多州，保险专员负责监管价值数十亿美元的保险行业。保险公司提供的保险产品涵盖从汽车、房屋到用于股票市场投资的变额年金等各类产品。当一家保险公司希望提高在某州的保险费率时，需向保险专员的办公室提交申请。

<!--en-->
Insurance commissioners oversee a multibillion dollar industry in many states. Insurance companies sell coverage for everything from cars and homes to variable annuities used to invest in the stock market. When an insurance company wants to raise the rate it is charging for coverage in a state, it files a request with the insurance commissioner's office.

这些费率调整申请属于公开记录，如果相关公司在该州占据较大市场份额，很可能会成为重要的新闻素材。如果全美规模最大的两家汽车和房屋保险公司——State Farm和Allstate——打算在某州提高费率，这将影响到数以万计的读者或观众。

<!--en-->
These rate requests are public records, and could be major stories, particularly if the company holds a large market share in the state. If State Farm or Allstate, the two largest auto and home insurers in the country, want to raise rates in a state, that will affect tens of thousands of readers or viewers.

*Tips from the Pros*

《Crain’s New York Business》杂志前编辑总监Greg David谈如何报道企业与政府的互动关系：

<!--en-->
Former Crain's New York Business editorial director Greg David on covering the intersection between business and government:

**不要轻信消费者权益保护者的说法：**先问问他们代表的是哪类消费者，以及其他消费者是否有不同的利益诉求。限制信用卡费用或许能帮助那些欠款较多且无法按时还款的消费者，但可能会对那些每月都能按时还款的消费者造成不利影响。

<!--en-->
**Don't take consumer advocates at face value:** Ask yourself which sorts of consumers they represent and whether other consumers might have different interests. Limiting credit card fees could help consumers with high balances who don't pay their bills on time. It could hurt consumers who pay their bills on time every month.

这些费率申请可通过各州保险监管部门随时查询。由于大多数州都有数百家保险公司运营，几乎每周都会有某家保险公司为其某个保险产品申请费率上调。在某些情况下，整个行业会共同提出费率申请，例如工伤赔偿保险或汽车保险产品。该行业有一个游说团体，负责向监管专员办公室提交申请，随后这些申请通常会由精算师及其他专家进行审核。有时还会举行公开听证会，邀请公司高管和公众就相关提案发表支持或反对意见。监管专员通常会主持此类听证会，并在听证会结束数天或数周后对费率申请作出裁决。

<!--en-->
These rate requests can be checked regularly with any state insurance department. With hundreds of insurance companies operating in most states, it is likely that one of them is filing for a rate hike in one of its insurance lines on almost a weekly basis. In some cases, the entire industry files a rate request. This can happen for workers' compensation coverage or auto insurance policies, for example. The industry has a lobbying group that files requests with the commissioner's office, which then typically gets reviewed by actuaries and other experts. Sometimes, there are public hearings at which company executives and the general public are invited to speak for and against the proposal. The commissioner typically presides over such cases and issues a ruling on the rate request days or weeks after the hearing occurred.

保险监管专员还负责确保保险公司有足够的资金用于支付理赔费用。这笔资金通常被称为盈余，监管机构有法律规定要求保险公司的银行账户中必须保持一定水平的盈余。如果某家公司的盈余低于规定水平，保险监管专员可能会诉诸法院，请求法官允许监管机构接管该公司以改善其财务状况。这可被称为监管监督或监管控制。

<!--en-->
Insurance commissioners are also charged with ensuring that insurers have enough money set aside to pay for claims. This money is often called surplus, and regulators have laws requiring a certain level of surplus to be in an insurance company's bank account. If a company falls below that level, then the insurance commissioner may go to court and ask a judge to allow regulators to take over that company to improve its financial position. This can be called regulatory oversight, or regulatory control.

保险公司会将消费者和企业缴纳的保费用于投资。其中许多公司的保费收入不足以覆盖其运营成本，因此它们希望依靠投资收益来实现盈利。但如果发生重大风暴或自然灾害，它们可能面临超出预期的理赔压力。1994年加州北岭地震发生后，汽车、房屋和企业保险商不得不支付数十亿美元的理赔款；2001年9月11日恐怖袭击导致世贸中心及五角大楼近3,000人遇难后，人寿保险商也遭遇了同样的情况。

<!--en-->
Insurance companies take the premiums paid to them by consumers and businesses and invest that money. Many of them do not charge enough in premiums to cover their expenses, so they are hoping that their investment income will allow them to report a profit. But if a major storm or natural disaster hits, they could be hit with more claims than they anticipated. Insurers of autos, homes, and businesses paid billions in claims after the Northridge earthquake hit California in 1994, and life insurers did the same after the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks killed nearly 3,000 at the World Trade Center and the Pentagon.

保险监管专员也会与保险行业合作。他们希望各公司能为尽可能多的消费者和企业提供保险服务。如果由于监管专员不允许其提高费率，某些公司开始取消保单或决定退出某个州，那么该专员在下次选举中可能会遇到麻烦。消费者和企业则希望保险市场能有更多选择和竞争。

<!--en-->
Insurance commissioners also work with the industry. Insurance commissioners want companies to offer coverage to as many consumers and businesses as possible. If companies begin to drop policies or decide to withdraw from a state because an insurance commissioner will not allow them to raise rates, then the commissioner may have a problem during the next election. Consumers and businesses want a variety of choices and competition in the insurance market.

Although banks are not filing requests to raise or lower the rates they charge consumers, they do file information with state and federal regulators that can give an insight into their performance.

For a reporter in a small or medium-sized town, following this branch data can show who is winning the banking battle in the community. ### 专业人士的建议

*Tips from the Pros*

<!--en-->
Former Crain's New York Business editorial director Greg David on covering the intersection between business and government:

**始终要问谁是赢家，谁是输家：**网络中立性争议被描绘成一场阻止互联网服务提供商强迫用户为所接收的内容付费的斗争，但实际上这是谷歌与服务提供商之间关于谁应为互联网付费的较量。

<!--en-->
**Always ask who wins and who loses:** The controversy over net neutrality is portrayed as a fight to keep Internet providers from forcing consumers to pay for the amount of content they receive. But it is really a struggle between Google and the providers over who pays for the Internet.

<!--en-->
There remains plenty of room for growth. No. 8 Downey now holds a mere 1.8 percent of California deposits.

他说道：“我们预计今年还将再开设20家分行。”纽约大都会区是美国最大的银行业市场，也有人认为它是竞争最激烈的地区。对于几家在纽约大都会统计区内运营的大型储蓄银行——其中包括国内规模最大的几家互助储蓄银行而言，情况确实如此。

<!--en-->
"We anticipate this year that we will open an additional 20 branches," he said. Metropolitan New York is the biggest banking market in the United States, and some would say it is the most competitive. That's certainly the case for several large thrifts—including a handful of the nation's largest mutual thrifts—that operate in the New York Metropolitan Statistical Area.

由于在1月4日完成了对Dime Bancorp Inc.的收购，华盛顿互惠银行如今在纽约大都会区的存款规模位居首位。有传言称，该银行最终可能会收购GreenPoint Financial Corp.，后者在纽约大都会区的储蓄银行中拥有第二大的存款规模。

<!--en-->
Washington Mutual now has the largest deposit position in metro New York, thanks to its acquisition of Dime Bancorp Inc., which it completed on Jan. 4. The thrift has been rumored to be an eventual acquirer of GreenPoint Financial Corp., which holds the second-largest deposit franchise among thrifts in the metro New York market.

然而，近年来该市场中规模最大的两家储蓄银行在留住存款方面遇到了困难。诸如Astoria Financial Corp.、New York Community Bancorp以及Staten Island Bancorp Inc.等规模较小的储蓄银行一直在蚕食它们的市场份额。截至6月30日，Staten Island Bancorp在该市场的存款同比增长了7.9%；Astoria Financial Corp.和New York Community Bancorp的增长率分别为4.9%和3.4%（后一数据已经过并购调整）。

<!--en-->
However, the two largest thrift operations have had trouble holding on to deposits in that market in recent years. Picking away at the top have been a host of somewhat smaller thrifts like Astoria Financial Corp., New York Community Bancorp and Staten Island Bancorp Inc. The latter grew deposits in the market by 7.9 percent year-over-year through June 30; Astoria and New York Community saw gains of 4.9 percent and 3.4 percent, respectively (the latter figure being adjusted for acquisitions).

Dime Community Bancshares Inc.的存款在该市场从一年前的9.471亿美元增长至6月30日的11亿美元，增幅达16.0%。该公司首席财务官肯·马洪将这一增长归因于该银行在1999年战略上的重大调整。

<!--en-->
Dime Community Bancshares Inc. grew its deposits in the market by 16.0 percent to $1.1 billion at June 30 from $947.1 million at the same time a year earlier Dime Community CFO Ken Mahon attributed the growth to a fundamental change in the thrift's strategy in 1999.

马洪说：“大约两年前，我们在存款业务方面开始实施新的策略。我们是一家面向多户家庭的贷款机构，这也是我们的主要业务。1996年上市后的几年里，我们的重点一直是发放贷款，而且都是通过批发借款来为贷款提供资金。”

<!--en-->
"About two years ago, we embarked on a new strategy here as far as raising deposits," Mahon said. "Our company's a multifamily lender, and that was really our major line of business. For a few years after we went public in 1996, our focus was on originating loans, originating loans, originating loans. And what we were doing was funding with wholesale borrowings."

不过，这种策略也带来了代价，因为该银行的资产负债表逐渐失衡。因此，Dime Community决定在吸收存款方面也采取更积极的策略。⁴虽然这篇文章是关于加州和纽约顶级银行的市场份额及其变化，但对于国内任何存在竞争性银行的城镇或城市，同样可以写出类似的分析。[^3706]：⁴摘自M. Saunders所著《研究与分析：最新分行数据披露》，2002年1月28日，SNL Interactive发布。版权所有2002年SNL Financial，经许可转载。336 • 政府发行版

<!--en-->
That strategy came with a price, however, as the thrift's balance sheet began to become unbalanced. So Dime Community decided to become more aggressive on the deposit-taking end as well.⁴
Although this story was written about state market share and how that has changed among the top banks in California and New York, a similar story can easily be written for any town or city in the country with competing banks just

#### 专家建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

《Crain's New York Business》前编辑总监格雷格·大卫谈如何报道商业与政府之间的关系：

<!--en-->
Former Crain's New York Business editorial director Greg David on covering the intersection between business and government:

**警惕意外后果：**试图对新药物实施更严格的监管或许能保护一些患者免受有害药物的伤害，但同时也会延缓那些可能挽救生命的药物的审批速度。

<!--en-->
**Beware the unintended consequences:** Efforts to impose stricter rules on new drugs might save some patients from harmful drugs, but it will also slow the approval of drugs that may save lives.

#### 专家建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

道琼斯新闻社华盛顿分社社长罗布·威尔斯谈如何将华盛顿地区的新闻作为商业话题进行报道：

<!--en-->
Dow Jones Newswires Washington bureau chief Rob Wells on covering Washington as a business story:

**学会阅读与理解财报：**政府资助的抵押贷款巨头房利美是商业与政府相互交织的典型例子。它由政府创建，旨在扩展并简化抵押贷款融资流程，同时由股东持有。在2008年金融危机前被政府接管之前，房利美拥有世界级的游说团队，用以影响国会。许多关于房利美的重要报道都源自其季度财报发布和管理层电话会议。这些文件中往往蕴含着有关监管事务或在政治上重要的州内扩大贷款项目的关键信息。许多金融通讯社会安排债券市场记者和华盛顿政策记者共同审阅这些财报和电话会议内容，并通过分析相同的数据来协作挖掘线索。虽然可能需要稍作加工与跟踪数据，但最终写出的报道能够让读者或观众了解这个所有消费者都依赖的重要行业的发展状况。

<!--en-->
**Learn to read and understand an earnings report:** Fannie Mae, the government sponsored mortgage giant, is a classic example of the intersection of business and government. It was created by the government to expand and smooth the mortgage finance process while being owned by shareholders. Before the government seized it in the 2008 financial crisis, Fannie Mae employed a world-class lobbying operation to influence Congress. Some of the best Fannie Mae stories originated from the quarterly earnings releases and management conference calls. Deep into these documents were gems about regulatory matters or expansion of loan programs in politically important states. Many financial wire services would have both a bond markets reporter and a Washington policy reporter review these earnings statements and conference calls, and collaborate on any resulting tips.
by reviewing the same data. It may take some addition and subtraction, and following the numbers for a while, but the story will likely be well read and show readers or viewers what is happening in an important industry used by all consumers.

与保险行业类似，银行和储蓄机构的监管机构也负责确保这些机构有足够的资金用于偿还贷款及支付储户存款。监管机构会设定资本充足率的相关要求，若某银行的资本充足率低于标准，就可能面临被接管的风险。

<!--en-->
Bank and thrift regulators, like their insurance brethren, are also charged with making sure that banks have enough money set aside to pay off loans and their depositors. Regulators set certain requirements on capital adequacy levels. If a bank falls below these levels, it could be taken over.

记者在分析银行向监管机构提交的文件时，应重点关注两个指标：贷款损失额和贷款损失准备金。当一家银行开始拨出大量资金用于弥补逾期贷款时，这可能表明该银行过去的放贷行为并不稳健。

<!--en-->
Two barometers a reporter should follow in a bank's filings with regulators are its loan losses and loan loss reserves. When a bank starts setting aside large amounts of money to cover loans that have become past due, that could be an indication that the bank's past lending practices were not sound.

与保险公司一样，银行也会将储户存入的资金及其他资金用于投资。其投资组合可以反映出银行是否正在从事高风险的业务操作。如果银行将资金投入于经济不稳定、货币波动较大的国外地区的房地产项目等高风险投资领域，这可能意味着它正在试图弥补其他不良投资带来的损失。记者应当始终审查银行的投資组合，以了解其资金的具体投向。

<!--en-->
Like insurance companies, banks also invest deposits and other money paid to them by consumers. The investment portfolio can be an indication that a bank is engaging in risky business practices. If it is investing in high-risk investments such as real estate ventures in shaky foreign economies or volatile currencies, that can be a sign that the bank is trying to make up for other bad investments. A reporter should always review an investment portfolio to see where a bank—or an insurance company—is putting its money.

保险公司和银行的州级监管机构也负责审批企业之间的并购交易。一旦有并购公告，相关州级监管机构可能会举行听证会，要求记者参加，或者征求公众意见。

<!--en-->
State regulators of insurance and banking companies are also involved in approving mergers and acquisitions between businesses. If a merger or acquisition is announced, there might be a hearing by the state regulatory agency that should be attended, or the regulators might ask for public comment.

通过深入调查以及了解必须向监管机构提交的文件，记者能够收集到关于那些否则可能不为人知的私人银行或保险公司的足够信息。这类报道往往能比其他任何内容更准确地反映当地经济的状况。

<!--en-->
With a little digging and some knowledge of the documents that must be filed with regulators, a reporter can piece together enough information about a private bank or insurance company that might otherwise go uncovered. These stories can often tell more about a local economy than anything else.

## 医疗保健监管

<!--en-->
*Health Care Regulation*

另一个主要由州级机构监管的行业是医疗保健业。医院、医生以及管理式医疗公司都属于这一快速发展且对众多经济体至关重要的行业。在许多城镇，当地医院往往是最大的雇主，这本身就为撰写相关报道提供了充分理由。

<!--en-->
Another industry primarily regulated by state agencies is the health care business. Hospitals, doctors, and managed care companies are part of a fast-growing industry that is a vital part of many economies. In many towns and cities, the local hospital is the largest employer. That should be a good reason as to why stories should be written about them.

医院、医生和管理式医疗公司之间存在着互利共生的关系。医生和医院依赖管理式医疗公司为他们带来大量患者，而管理式医疗公司则依靠医生和医院以尽可能低的成本为患者提供医疗服务。不过，由于双方都需要依靠对方来维持自身的盈利水平，这种关系有时也会出现紧张状况。

<!--en-->
Hospitals, doctors, and managed care companies have a symbiotic relationship. Doctors and hospitals rely on managed care companies to bring them large amounts of patients. Conversely, managed care companies rely on doctors and hospitals to treat patients as cost efficiently as possible. Sometimes, these relationships can become strained, as each is out to maintain a level of profitability that is dependent on others.

寻找关于医院，尤其是私立或非营利医院的报道的一个途径，就是查阅州级监管机构的备案文件。许多医院必须向州级监管机构提交财务信息，而且部分医院提供的手术及其他服务的收费标准也需获得州级机构的批准。（在马萨诸塞州，州立医院行业在20世纪80年代被取消管制，结果导致多家医院关闭。）

<!--en-->
One of the ways to find stories about hospitals, particularly private or non-profit hospitals, is through state regulatory filings. Many hospitals are required to file financial information with state regulators, and the rates that some hospitals charge for operations and other services must be approved by a state agency. (In Massachusetts, the state hospital industry was deregulated in the 1980s. The result caused a number of hospitals to close.)

记者应先查明所在州负责监管医院的机构，随后致电或前往该机构，了解有关当地医院的各类信息。记者可能会发现当地医院正在亏损，不得不提高收费才能生存；或者发现那些所谓的非营利医院近年来却获得了数百万美元的利润。政府议题 • 337 在许多州，医院在扩大规模或提供新服务之前还必须获得州监管机构的许可。例如在密歇根州，一个名为“需求证明委员会”的政府机构会审批全州各医院提出的新建床位或心脏科等医疗服务的申请。这类法规的目的是防止某个社区内的医疗服务供给过剩。在佛罗里达州，“需求证明”程序涵盖新增医院床位、开展心脏直视手术、器官移植、新生儿重症监护、烧伤治疗、住院精神科或药物滥用治疗服务、住院综合医学康复、独立式临终关怀床位以及专业护理服务。

<!--en-->
Reporters should check to see what agency oversees hospitals in their state,then call or visit that agency to find out what information is available about local hospitals. A reporter may find out that the local hospital is losing money and needs to raise its rates to survive, or that the so-called nonprofit hospital has had profits of millions of dollars in recent years.
Government Issue • 337
In many states, hospitals must also receive permission from state regulators before they are allowed to expand and offer new services. In Michigan, for example, a government body called the Certificate of Need Commission approves filings by hospitals across the state asking to build new additions that add beds or services such as cardiac units. The idea behind such regulations is to prevent a glut of hospital services in a certain community. In Florida, the certificate of need process covers new hospital beds as well as the beginning of open heart surgery, organ transplantation, neonatal intensive care, burn services, inpatient psychiatric or substance abuse services, inpatient comprehensive medical rehabilitation, hospice freestanding inpatient beds, and skilled nursing.

正如《克利夫兰平原商报》的以下报道所示，许多州的“需求证明”程序还允许消费者、竞争对手及其他方对竞争对手的扩建计划提出反对意见：

<!--en-->
The certificate of need process in many states also allows consumers, competitors and others to argue against an expansion plan by a competitor, as the following story from the *Cleveland Plain Dealer* shows:

昨晚，帕尔马规划委员会未经投票便将那个有争议的、计划建造260张床位的老年人综合设施的方案退回给了市议会。

<!--en-->
Without taking a vote, the Parma Planning Commission bounced a controversial proposed 260-bed senior citizen complex back to City Council last night.

在70人出席的近三小时的听证会之后，该委员会表示仍支持其3月9日对帕尔马社区综合医院以及由长期经营养老院的库里家族成员成立的Generations Healthcare公司所提出的项目的认可决定。

<!--en-->
After a nearly three-hour hearing attended by 70 persons, the commission said it stands behind its March 9 endorsement of the project proposed by Parma Community General Hospital and Generations Health care, a company formed by members of the Coury family, longtime nursing home operators.

7月10日，居民们至少取得了暂时性的胜利，因为市议会将经过三次修改的项目重新送回了规划委员会。

<!--en-->
On July 10, residents won at least a temporary victory as council sent the thrice-revised project back to the Planning Commission.

市议会这么做是因为居民们的律师罗杰·佩拉加利威胁要申请禁令，他主张根据城市法律，任何在规划委员会通过后经过重大修改的项目都应再次由该委员会进行审查。

<!--en-->
Council did so under the threat of an injunction made by the residents' lawyer, Rodger Pelagalli, who had argued that city laws required any project that has been radically changed since its adoption by the Planning Commission be reviewed again by the panel.

市议员约翰·斯托弗表示：“居民们觉得规划委员会只是在推卸责任。”他认为自己和其他人认为自3月以来提出的各种方案修改都应该由该委员会进行投票表决。

<!--en-->
"Residents feel the Planning Commission was just washing its hands of the deal," said Councilman John Stover who said he and others felt the panel should have voted on an array of plan changes since March.

该综合设施计划建在旧费伊初中周围的空地上，将提供包括阿尔茨海默病专科在内的多种护理服务。

<!--en-->
The complex, proposed for vacant land ringing the old Fay Junior High School, would offer a wide range of care, including an Alzheimer's unit.

开发商们称，那栋旧建筑已被改造成健康教育中心，这将为拟建的老年人综合设施增添更多功能。他们表示已经考察过其他选址，但因成本原因予以放弃。

<!--en-->
The old building has been converted to a health education center that would give the proposed senior complex an added dimension, developers have argued. They said they have reviewed alternate sites but ruled them out because of cost.

这一做法引发了第5选区市议员米歇尔·斯泰斯的强烈反对，她说道：“我不在乎他们的资金状况，我在意的是现有的邻居们。”

<!--en-->
That drew fire from Ward 5 Councilwoman Michelle Stys, who said: "I'm not concerned about their purse strings. I am concerned about the existing neighbors."

居民们发誓下个月将继续抗争，要求俄亥俄州卫生部不要为该项目颁发“需求证明”。338 • 政府议题

<!--en-->
Residents have vowed to continue the fight next month by asking the Ohio Department of Health to not award a certificate of need for the project.
338 • Government Issue

### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

道琼斯新闻专线华盛顿分社社长罗布·威尔斯关于将华盛顿的新闻作为商业话题进行报道的经验分享：

<!--en-->
Dow Jones Newswires
Washington bureau chief Rob
Wells on covering Washington as a business story:

**学习并使用Excel：**这款软件能比电脑上的其他任何工具都更有效地帮助你整理和分析数据。掌握简单的排序功能以及百分比变化等基础数学函数，就能让你找出哪些公司部门在亏损，或是政治献金多年来是如何增长的。调查记者与编辑协会在其网站上提供了关于Excel及众多其他主题的各类培训课程和资料。加入并支持这个团体吧，它为记者提供了极佳的人脉交流和持续学习机会，能助力你的整个职业生涯。

<!--en-->
**Learn and use Excel:** This program will help you organize and analyze numbers better than anything else on your computer. Mastering the simple sort and basic math functions, such as percentage change, can allow you to learn which company division is losing money or how political contributions have increased over several years. The IRE (Investigative Reporters and Editors) has various training sessions and materials on its website on Excel and many other topics. Join and support this group, a wonderful networking and continuing education opportunity for journalists that will sustain you throughout your career.

其他反对者主要是周边房产所有者，他们认为该提案缺乏紧急车辆的通行通道，可能使雨水管道和污水管道超负荷运转，还会导致房产价值下降。

<!--en-->
Other opponents, composed mainly of abutting property owners, said the proposal lacks access for emergency vehicles, threatens to overload storm and sanitary sewers, and could erode property values.

萨萨弗拉斯路的玛丽·安·尼斯表示，帕尔马医院任由费伊那块地逐渐恶化。那里到处都是涂鸦，有刺鼻的污水气味，还有碎玻璃和杂草丛生，尼斯说道。

<!--en-->
Mary Ann Nice, of Sassafras Dr., said Parma Hospital has allowed the Fay property to deteriorate. It is marked with graffiti, smells of raw sewage, is covered in places by broken glass and high grass, Nice said.

居民们还得到了该市工程部的支持，该部门批评该计划不够完善，指出其中缺少关于停车、绿化缓冲带、防侵蚀措施以及公用设施的详细内容。

<!--en-->
The residents picked up support from the city's Engineering Department, which criticized the plan as incomplete. The department reported the plan lacks details on parking, landscaping buffers, erosion and utilities.

布鲁克帕克的莉兹·瓦尔加作证称，她所在城市中另一家由库里家族经营的养老院——东公园护理中心也并非理想的邻舍。

<!--en-->
Liz Varga, of Brook Park, testified that another Coury-operated nursing home, the EastPark Care Center in her city, has been less than an ideal neighbor.

“我邀请帕尔马市的居民们全天都来拍摄所有进出的卡车，”瓦尔加说道。

<!--en-->
"I invite the people of Parma to come and take videos of all the trucks going in and out all day," said Varga.

帕尔马海茨市长保罗·卡西迪以及该医院的法律顾问坚称，帕尔马医院-世代医疗保健项目的设计在最近几个月已经做出调整，以回应城市及居民的关切。他表示，现在的建筑数量从五栋减少到了四栋，每栋建筑也由单层变成了两层，同时老年人居住区与普通住宅之间的缓冲区也得到了扩大。⁵ 商业领域中冲突频发，记者从政府文件中发现的冲突并不一定总是企业与监管机构之间的矛盾，正如前面的案例所示，往往还有其他企业牵涉其中。

<!--en-->
Parma Heights Mayor Paul Cassidy, the hospital's legal counsel, insisted that the Parma Hospital-Generations Health Care design has been changed in recent months to reflect city and resident concerns. He said there are now four buildings instead of five, they have two floors instead of one, and the buffer between senior complex and homes has been widened.⁵
Conflict occurs often in the business world, and the conflict a reporter finds in state documents may not always be between business and regulators. Often, another business is also involved, as the preceding story illustrates.

与保险公司费率申请及银行分行数据的情况类似，很少有媒体会主动关注医疗需求证明的提交情况。但在许多情况下，这些文件却可能成为重大新闻，因为它们表明某家医疗机构计划投入数百万美元。这笔钱从何而来？又是否被合理使用？这些问题往往得不到解答。

<!--en-->
As in the case with insurance company rate requests and bank branch data, few media outlets actively watch certificate of need filings. But in many cases, these documents can be major news, indicating that a health care facility plans to spend millions of dollars. Where is that money coming from? And is that money being spent wisely? Too often, those questions are not answered.

州医疗委员会也是商业报道的来源之一。这些机构负责监管某一地区的医生和外科医师，如果医生进行了不必要的手术或为某种疾病开了错误的药物，他们可以吊销或暂扣该医生的执照。这些都是公开记录，能够为了解一个城镇内的企业状况提供重要信息。这些委员会还负责监督其他医疗工作者，如护士和养老院管理人员。

<!--en-->
State medical boards can also be a source of business stories. These organizations regulate doctors and surgeons in an area. They can revoke or suspend the license of a doctor if he or she performed an unnecessary surgery or prescribed the wrong medication for an illness. These are public records, and can be important information about a business in a town. These boards can also oversee other medical workers, such as nurses and nursing home administrators.

医疗保健行业中最具影响力的参与者之一可能是管理式医疗服务运营商。在很多情况下，这类企业由保险公司运营，通常也受州保险部门的监管。

<!--en-->
One of the biggest players in the health care business can be the managed care operators. In many instances, these are businesses operated by insurance companies, and often they also come under the regulation of the state insurance department.

管理式医疗公司一般会向消费者提供两种类型的保险计划：健康维护组织（HMO）和优选医疗服务提供者组织（PPO）。HMO会以固定费用为其计划成员安排医生和医院的医疗服务。HMO必须事先确定一系列基本及补充的健康维护和治疗服务内容。而PPO则会与医生和医院签订合同，通过这些合同，如果客户选择签约的医疗服务提供者，管理式医疗公司就会降低患者的自付费用。管理式医疗公司也会像保险公司一样收取保费，且那些营利性的管理式医疗公司期望通过所收取的保费获得利润；非营利性的管理式医疗公司通常也能从业务运营中盈利。通常可以通过咨询州监管机构，尤其是保险部门，获取管理式医疗公司的财务业绩数据。[^3752]：⁵ 摘自J. Wagner于2000年7月21日发表在《克利夫兰平原商报》第3B版的文章《规划者将养老院计划退回议会；帕尔马居民誓言继续反对该提案》，版权归《克利夫兰平原商报》所有，经许可转载。Government Issue • 339 以下是一篇评估堪萨斯城地区管理式医疗公司财务表现的文章：

<!--en-->
Managed care companies generally offer two types of plans to consumers: a health maintenance organization (HMO) and a preferred provider organization (PPO). An HMO provides and arranges for coverage with doctors and hospitals for its plan members for a set rate. The HMO must agree on a set of basic and supplemental health maintenance and treatment services. A PPO establishes contracts with doctors and hospitals, and with those contracts the managed carecompany provides lower co-payments if its subscribers use one of those preferred providers. Managed care companies charge premiums, just like insurance companies. And the for-profit managed care companies expect to make a profit on the basis of the premiums they have collected. Nonprofit managed care companies often also make a profit on their operations. The financial results of managed care companies can usually be found by asking state regulators, probably with the insurance department.
[^3752]: ⁵ From "Planners bounce nursing home plans to council; Parma residents vow to continue fighting proposal," by J. Wagner, July 21, 2000, *Cleveland Plain Dealer*, p. 3B. Copyright 2000 by *Cleveland Plain Dealer*. Reprinted with permission.
Government Issue • 339
The following is a story that assessed the financial performance of managed care companies operating in Kansas City:

在保费不断上涨的情况下，去年在堪萨斯城开展业务的各大管理式医疗公司整体上实现了惊人的财务好转。

<!--en-->
Amid rising premiums, the principal managed care companies doing business in Kansas City on the whole enjoyed a spectacular financial turnaround last year.

去年，在这里运营的八家管理式医疗公司总共获得了7190万美元的净收入，而2001年的净亏损总额则为1270万美元。

<!--en-->
Eight managed care companies that operate here earned an aggregate net income of $71.9 million last year, compared with an aggregate net loss of $12.7 million in 2001.

并非所有公司都能享受到这种好运。八家大公司中有四家实现了盈利，但其余四家在2002年则出现了亏损。

<!--en-->
The good fortune was not shared by all. Four of the eight big companies were profitable, but the four others reported losses for 2002.

这些数据还包括了在此运营的全国性管理式医疗公司在堪萨斯城以外地区的经营业绩。

<!--en-->
The numbers include results outside the Kansas City area for national managed care companies operating here.

密苏里州保险局发言人兰迪·麦康奈尔表示：“自1998年以来，HMO行业一直致力于提升盈利能力，2002年对它们来说正是在这方面取得突破的一年。”

<!--en-->
"The HMO industry since 1998 has been focusing on profitability," said Randy McConnell, a spokesman for the Missouri Department of Insurance. "2002 turned out to be a breakthrough year for them on that score."

麦康奈尔称，这种财务好转主要得益于HMO们在选择服务对象时更加谨慎，以及“大幅上涨的保费”。

<!--en-->
McConnell said the financial turnaround was largely brought about by HMOs being more selective in choosing the groups they cover, along with "substantial premium increases."

其他数据也显示出了类似的趋势。根据密苏里州保险局的数据，去年在密苏里州运营的HMO公司实现了1.677亿美元的创纪录的合并净收入，而2001年的合并净亏损则为598,287美元。这些数据中也包含了一些全国性管理式医疗公司的经营业绩。

<!--en-->
Other numbers pointed to a similar trend. HMOs operating in Missouri earned a record consolidated net income of $167.7 million last year, compared with a $598,287 consolidated net loss in 2001, according to the Missouri Department of Insurance. The numbers include national operating results of some managed care companies.

根据堪萨斯州保险局公布的数据，去年在堪萨斯州运营的HMO公司实现了9380万美元的合并净收入，而2001年的合并净亏损则为2590万美元。这些数据同样也包括了一些全国性公司的经营业绩。

<!--en-->
HMOs operating in Kansas earned a consolidated net income of $93.8 million last year, compared with a $25.9 million consolidated net loss in 2001, based on numbers reported by the Kansas Insurance Department. Those numbers also include the national operating results of some companies.

受益于此转机的是堪萨斯城的蓝十字蓝盾组织。去年，蓝十字的净收入为3110万美元，而2001年的净亏损则为630万美元。这些数据包括了蓝十字HMO和PPO网络的业务业绩。

<!--en-->
Beneficiaries of the turnaround included Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Kansas City. Blue Cross earned $31.1 million in net income last year, compared with a 2001 net loss of $6.3 million. The numbers include results from Blue Cross HMOs and PPO networks.

蓝十字的执行副总裁约翰·W·肯尼迪表示，该公司得益于更高的保费以及整体业务增长。

<!--en-->
John W. Kennedy, Blue Cross's executive vice president, said the company had benefited from higher premiums and overall growth.

“我们签下了很多业务合同，”肯尼迪说道。

<!--en-->
"We sold a lot of business," Kennedy said.

肯尼迪称，蓝十字还因退出了那些亏损的Medicare HMO业务以及降低了管理成本而受益。此外，他还提到，由于蓝十字买下了TriSource管理护理集团中的合作伙伴，2001年的财务状况因此受到了1400万美元的负面影响。340 • 政府发行版

<!--en-->
Kennedy said Blue Cross also benefited from dropping its money-losing Medicare HMOs and from lower administrative costs. In addition, he said the 2001 bottom line had suffered a $14 million hit as a result of Blue Cross buying out its partners in the TriSource managed care group.
340 • Government Issue

### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

道琼斯新闻专线华盛顿分社社长罗布·威尔斯关于如何将华盛顿的新闻报道成商业题材的经验：

<!--en-->
Dow Jones Newswires
Washington bureau chief Rob
Wells on covering Washington as a business story:

**为华尔街寻找翻译人员：**你需要一名会说英语的会计，还需要一名其偏见和利益冲突都为人所知的华尔街投资分析师。会计会帮你梳理复杂的财务数据。例如，有一位优秀的会计让我得以报道前众议院议长纽特·金里奇正在考虑扣除与众议院道德委员会调查相关的30万美元费用的消息。金里奇承认违反了众议院规则，并因就其政治组织与免税活动的关联提供虚假陈述而在1997年受到谴责。投资分析师则会提供有关资产负债表的有用评论和分析，为报道时需要考虑的问题指明方向。他们通常会向客户持续发送报告，并会将你加入他们的邮件列表。要了解各大经纪公司研究分析师的各种偏见和利益冲突，需要花费一定的时间和精力进行研究。

<!--en-->
**Find translators for Wall Street:** You need an accountant who speaks English. You need a Wall Street investment analyst whose biases and conflicts are known. The accountant will guide you through a major numbers story. For example, a good accountant allowed me to break the story that former House Speaker Newt Gingrich was considering deducting $300,000 in costs related to a House Ethics Committee investigation. Gingrich admitted violating House rules and received a reprimand in 1997 for providing misleading statements about his political organization's connection to tax-exempt activities. The investment analyst will provide useful commentary and analysis of the balance sheet, a sort of road map to issues worth considering in reporting. They churn out a stream of reports to clients and usually will put you on their email lists. It requires some amount of study and time to learn the various biases and conflicts of research analysts at the major brokerage houses.

其他管理护理公司的表现则没那么好。堪萨斯州的Coventry Health Care去年出现了860万美元的净亏损，而前一年的净亏损为300万美元。

<!--en-->
Other managed care companies did not fare so well. Coventry Health Care of Kansas suffered an $8.6 million net loss last year, compared with a $3 million net loss the previous year.

Coventry 2002年的财务数据还包括了它去年以3800万美元收购的Mid America Health Partners Inc.的业绩。

<!--en-->
Coventry's 2002 financial results include those of Mid America Health Partners Inc., which Coventry bought for $38 million last year.

堪萨斯州Coventry Health Care的总裁兼首席执行官珍妮特·M·斯塔尔迈耶拒绝对该公司的最新财务数据发表评论，仅表示这些数据是Coventry与Mid America Health合并后的结果。

<!--en-->
Janet M. Stallmeyer, president and chief executive officer of Coventry Health Care of Kansas, declined to comment on the company's latest figures, except to acknowledge that they represent the consolidated results of Coventry and Mid America Health.

“我无法讨论这些报表背后的细节，”斯塔尔迈耶说。她补充道：“我相信我们已经为未来的发展打下了坚实的基础，2003年的法定报表将会体现这一点。”

<!--en-->
"I'm not in a position to discuss the details behind those filings," Stallmeyer said. She added: "I believe that we've built a strong platform for moving forward, and our statutory filings will reflect that in 2003."

堪萨斯州的Coventry Health Care隶属于总部位于马里兰州贝塞斯达的Coventry Health Care Inc.。

<!--en-->
Coventry Health Care of Kansas is part of Bethesda, Maryland-based Coventry Health Care Inc.

在其他公司中，Aetna Health Inc.、FirstGuard Health Plan Inc.以及United Healthcare of the Midwest Inc.均报出了盈利成绩。在堪萨斯州和密苏里州开展业务的俄亥俄州Cigna Healthcare Inc.、Family Health Partners以及Humana Health Plan Inc.则出现了亏损。⁶本文中提到的许多公司都是私营企业，或是那些在SEC备案中不单独披露子公司财务表现的上市公司子公司。这也解释了为何在很多情况下，从州级监管机构那里获取这些记录能更准确地反映当地业务的表现。

<!--en-->
Among the others, Aetna Health Inc., FirstGuard Health Plan Inc. and United Healthcare of the Midwest Inc. reported positive earnings. Cigna Healthcare of Ohio Inc., which does business in Kansas and Missouri, Family Health Partners and Humana Health Plan Inc. reported losses.⁶
Many of the companies mentioned in this story are private companies, or subsidiaries of public companies that do not break out the financial performance of subsidiaries in their SEC filings. That shows why getting these records from state regulators can provide a better indication of how a local operation is performing in many instances.

全美范围内的蓝十字蓝盾体系是主要的医疗管理护理服务提供商之一，CIGNA和Aetna等全国性运营商也是如此。在蓝十字蓝盾计划体系中，各家公司各自独立运营，不过这些计划一直在走向整合。当此类并购交易被宣布时，监管机构通常会介入，尤其是当一家营利性的蓝方运营商想要收购一家非营利性的蓝方计划时。2003年，马里兰州的监管机构拒绝了在加利福尼亚州、密苏里州和乔治亚州经营的营利性蓝方公司WellPoint收购该州非营利性蓝方运营商的请求。

<!--en-->
The Blue Cross-Blue Shield system across the country is one of the dominant managed care players, as are national operators such as CIGNA and Aetna. With Blue Cross-Blue Shield plans, each company operates separately, although the plans have been undergoing a consolidation move. When such deals are announced, regulators are typically involved, especially if a for-profit Blue operator wants to acquire a not-for-profit Blue plan. In 2003, Maryland regulators turned down the request by WellPoint, the for-profit Blue company operating in California, Missouri, and Georgia, to acquire the nonprofit Blue operator in that state.

医疗管理护理公司会密切关注医疗成本上涨的情况。如果医疗产品及服务的成本上升过快，它们就无法通过提高保费来跟上这一趋势。一旦医疗成本开始上升，许多公司可能会向监管机构申请提高费率。

<!--en-->
Managed care companies watch medical inflation carefully. If the cost of medical goods and services rises too fast, they are unable to keep pace by raising premiums. Many may ask for rate increases from regulators if medical costs start rising.

### 水电公用事业

<!--en-->
*Water and Power Utilities*

每家企业和房主都需要支付电费、水费和电话费，其中一些还需缴纳燃气费。令他们许多人惊讶的是，这些费用的标准是由州公用事业委员会来规定的。这些监管机构负责确保这些公司为其服务收取合理的费用，从而保护消费者权益。此外，公共服务委员会还会与这些公司合作，努力提高公用事业的效率，从而降低未来费用上涨的可能性。[^3782]：⁶ 摘自J. Karash所著《运营利润》，2003年4月11日，《堪萨斯城星报》C1版。版权所有2003年《堪萨斯城星报》，经许可转载。Government Issue • 341 此外，还有一个联邦机构也负责监管部分公用事业。联邦能源管理委员会（FERC）负责监管跨州销售的电力价格、条款及条件，是各州公用事业监管委员会的联邦对应机构。

<!--en-->
Every business and homeowner pays electricity, water, and telephone bills. Some of them also pay a gas bill. What is surprising to many of them is that the rates are regulated by state utility commissions. These regulatory agencies are charged with protecting the consumer by making sure these companies arecharging fair rates for their services. In addition, public service commissions also work with the companies to try to make utilities more efficient, thereby lowering the potential for rate increases in the future.
[^3782]: ⁶ From "Operating profits" by J. Karash, April 11, 2003, *Kansas City Star*, p. C1. Copyright 2003 by *Kansas City Star*. Reprinted with permission.
Government Issue • 341
In addition, there is a federal agency that also regulates some utilities. The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) regulates the price, terms, and conditions of power sold across state lines and is the federal counterpart to state utility regulatory commissions.

与保险行业的监管机构类似，州公共服务委员也必须批准任何上调费率的申请。这类费率申请通常会附带相关文件，说明电力公司为何需要提高费率。在委员会做出决定之前，往往还会举行听证会，听取该公司及消费者的意见。

<!--en-->
Like their insurance brethren, state public service commissioners must approve any request to raise rates. These rate requests are sometimes accompanied by documents justifying why the electrical company, for example, needs to raise rates. And there is often a hearing to take testimony from the company and consumers before the commission makes its decision.

这类申请的提交及其审批过程都应该是值得报道的内容，尤其是那些涉及大量消费者利益的费用上调事件。《密尔沃基商业杂志》曾简短报道过一起此类申请：威斯康星电力照明公司向威斯康星州公共服务委员会提交了总计1.131亿美元的费率上调申请。如果该申请获批，普通用户的电费将增加7.58美元，燃气费则将上升10.91美元。这篇报道向读者说明了如果申请通过，他们的月均账单会增加多少。这类信息对于任何关于费率申请的报道来说都至关重要，因为它能让消费者了解自己将受到多大的影响。

<!--en-->
The filing of these requests, as well as their approval, should be stories, particularly those about rate hikes that affect a large number of consumers. One of these rate requests was covered by a brief item in the *Milwaukee Business Journal*, which notes that Wisconsin Power & Light filed a rate increase with the Public Service Commission of Wisconsin totaling $113.1 million. If the rate increase was passed, the average customer would see a $7.58 increase in their electric bill and a $10.91 hike in their gas bill. Note how this story told the reader how much his or her average monthly bill would increase if the rate request passed. This is information that is vital to any story about a rate request because it tells the consumer how much he or she will be affected.

在许多费率听证会上，消费者权益倡导者会代表民众发声。这类倡导者通常在政府机构任职，职责就是维护公民的利益。这些倡导者办公室经常会针对公用事业为何需要上调费率展开研究。这些研究内容很重要，可以用来撰写相关报道。它们属于公开文件，往往能呈现出与该公司提交的费率申请不同的情况。

<!--en-->
At many rate hearings, the people are represented by a consumer advocate. Often, the consumer advocate is in a government position with the sole job of protecting the interest of citizens. These consumer advocate offices may often conduct studies on why a utility needs a rate hike. These studies can be important to read and even write stories about. They are public documents that often paint a different picture than the company's rate filing.

公共事业委员会还会就其他事项举行听证会。如果他们认为某家公用事业公司没有公平对待客户或未为公众利益着想，就会开展调查。当一场冰暴袭击北卡罗来纳州时，数千名居民停电长达一周之久。许多人抱怨称，该州的电力公司本应更好地做好应对灾害及恢复供电工作的准备。在大量投诉的压力下，州公用事业委员会仍在许多居民的草坪上还有树枝和树木的情况下，对此事展开了听证。

<!--en-->
Public utility commissions also hold hearings on other matters. They may feel as if the utility has not treated its customers fairly or acted in the public's best interests. When an ice storm hit North Carolina, thousands of residents went without power for as long as a week. Many of them complained that the power companies in the state should have been better prepared to handle the damage and repairs needed to get power restored. Besieged with complaints, the state utilities commission conducted a hearing into the matter while many residents still had branches and trees throughout their lawn.

以下是一份报纸对相关事件的报道方式：

<!--en-->
The following shows how one newspaper covered the proceeding:

周四，在州公用事业委员会的听证会上，杜克电力公司的用户有机会与该大型企业对质，他们指责该公司在12月4日的冰暴之后规划不周、物资短缺且沟通不畅。

<!--en-->
Duke Power customers, given the opportunity to confront the utility giant at a state Utilities Commission hearing Thursday, lashed out at the company for poor planning, material shortages and unreliable communications after the Dec. 4 ice storm.

在报名在由六人组成的评审小组前发言的33人中，有前查珀尔希尔市议会成员、电气工程师乔·卡波斯基，他批评杜克电力公司在1996年9月的弗兰飓风过后，未能采取更多措施重建查珀尔希尔的电力分配系统。

<!--en-->
Among the 33 people who signed up to speak before the six-member panel was Joe Capowski, a former Chapel Hill Town Council member and an electrical engineer who criticized Duke Power for not doing more to rebuild Chapel Hill's power distribution system after Hurricane Fran in September 1996.

他在达勒姆市政厅面向150多名听众表示：“杜克电力公司并非诞生于2002年12月4日。虽然他们的努力确实很英勇，但那是由于公司管理层缺乏远见和经验所致。”342 • Government Issue 达勒姆市长比尔·贝尔回忆说，那场冰暴让该州第四大城市“突然陷入严寒的停滞状态”，他建议委员会分析杜克电力公司员工在风暴后的工作报告，查看他们灾后被分配到了何处。贝尔指责该公司没有在达勒姆投入足够资源——在风暴高峰期，该公司93%的顾客，即107,000户家庭，都处于停电状态。

<!--en-->
"Duke Power was not born on December 4, 2002," he said before anaudience of more than 150 people in Durham's City Hall. "Their efforts, while indeed heroic, were made so by their own management's lack of foresight and learning."
342 • Government Issue
The ice storm brought the state's fourth largest city to "an abrupt and frigid halt," recalled Durham Mayor Bill Bell, who suggested that the commission analyze work reports of Duke Power personnel to see where they were assigned immediately after the storm. Bell has accused the company of not concentrating enough resources in Durham—where 93 percent, or 107,000 of the company's customers, were without power at the peak.

贝尔称，风暴过后，杜克电力公司提供的信息“往往过于笼统，无法为应急管理工作提供任何参考价值”。

<!--en-->
In the storm's aftermath, the information Duke Power supplied "was often too general to give any value to emergency management operations," Bell said.

杜克电力公司高级副总裁E.O. Ferrell表示，尽管该公司“与民选官员及应急中心的沟通并未如我们所愿地顺利进行”，但西部三角地区的巨大破坏程度仍阻碍了其救援工作的开展。

<!--en-->
E.O. Ferrell, a Duke Power senior vice president, said that although the company's "communication with the elected officials and with the emergency centers did not function the way we would have liked," the utility's efforts were hampered by the magnitude of the damage in the western Triangle.

在达勒姆官员的要求下召开的这次听证会，是该委员会为评估杜克电力公司与Progress Energy公司在冰暴后应对表现而安排的系列公开会议中的第一次。本周早些时候，杜克电力公司与CP&L公司的代表一同在罗利州监管机构面前出席听证会，双方均为自己的应急预案进行了辩护。

<!--en-->
The hearing, requested by Durham officials, was the first in a series of public meetings the commission has scheduled around the state to evaluate Duke Power's and Progress Energy's emergency preparedness in response to hundreds of complaints about utilities' performance after the ice storm. Earlier this week, Duke Power joined CP&L officials at a hearing before state regulators in Raleigh where both companies defended their emergency protocol.

来自西部三角地区的投诉不断，那里有147,000名用户受到影响，且电力恢复速度在卡罗来纳州各地区中最为缓慢。

<!--en-->
Complaints have poured in from the western Triangle, where 147,000 customers were affected and power-restoration efforts were the slowest in the Carolinas.

风暴过后一周，达勒姆仍有20,000户家庭断电，查珀尔希尔则有8,100户家庭断电。⁷ 没有哪家公司愿意成为公众关注的焦点；当它们被带到州监管委员会面前并被迫回应消费者投诉时，会感到极为不安。记者应当在场记录这一切。

<!--en-->
One week after the storm, 20,000 remained without power in Durham and 8,100 in Chapel Hill.⁷
No company likes to be in the public spotlight. They dread it when they are dragged before a state regulatory board and asked to answer consumer complaints. A reporter should be there to document it all.

虽然关于公用事业委员会的报道大多集中在电力公司上，但在大多数州，这些委员会还负责监管水务公司和电话公司，对相关行业的费率申请及纠纷作出裁决。与其他州级监管文件一样，公用事业委员会的文件往往蕴含丰富的新闻素材，但由于记者认为其中内容枯燥，往往无人报道。

<!--en-->
Although most of the reporting on utility commissions focuses on electrical companies, the commissions also regulate water utilities and phone companies in most states, making decisions on rate requests and disputes in those industries. Like other state regulatory filings, utility commission documents are often a goldmine for stories and are frequently unreported because journalists think they contain boring information.

不过，追踪那些影响数千消费者的公用事业公司的运作情况，正是大众媒体能够为读者或观众提供的最佳服务之一。可以说，没有哪种行业比公共事业更能影响到如此众多的消费者。[^3803]：⁷ 摘自M. Fishman于2002年12月20日发表在《The News & Observer》上的文章《Duke Power assailed at hearing: Customers complain about the utility's planning and actions after recent ice storm》，第B1页。版权所有2002年《The News & Observer》。经许可转载。Government Issue • 343 记者不应忘记，许多能源和电力公司同时也是拥有股东的上市公司，应利用它们向美国证券交易委员会提交的文件来补充州级监管文件中的信息。此外，记者还应务必向联邦机构核实相关信息，尤其是针对能源公司。以安然公司倒闭为首的诸多能源公司兴衰起伏，促使联邦能源监管委员会开始介入众多能源公司的业务监管。

<!--en-->
But tracking the dealings of utilities that affect thousands of consumers can be one of the best services a mass communication outlet can provide to its readers or viewers. It can be argued that no other business beat affects as many consumers as the public utilities beat.
[^3803]: ⁷ From "Duke Power assailed at hearing: Customers complain about the utility's planning and actions after recent ice storm," by M. Fishman, December 20, 2002, *The News & Observer*, p. B1. Copyright 2002 by *The News & Observer*. Reprinted with permission.
Government Issue • 343
Reporters should not forget that many utilities such as energy and electrical companies are also public companies with shareholders. Information from their SEC filings should be used to supplement information contained in state regulatory filings. Also, reporters should be sure to check with the federal agency as well, particularly for energy companies. The recent rise and fall of many energy companies, led by the collapse of Enron, caused the FERC to become involved in many energy company dealings.

这些公司中的许多还与各州及其他大型客户签订长期供电合同。如果电价上升或下降，这些公司可能会获得巨额利润，也可能面临困境。

<!--en-->
Many of these companies also sign long-term contracts to provide power with states and other major customers. If the cost of power should rise or fall, these companies could reap a financial windfall, or face difficulty.

#### 消费品安全

<!--en-->
*Consumer Product Safety*

政府的职能之一就是保护消费者。监管机构履行这一职责的方式之一，就是确保企业生产出对消费者而言安全的商品、产品和服务。一旦监管机构发现某些产品或商品可能危害消费者，他们可能会要求企业改变生产方式；如果该产品或商品导致人员死亡或严重受伤，他们甚至可能要求将其从市场上撤下。

<!--en-->
One of the functions of the government is to protect the consumer. And one of the ways regulators go about this job is to make sure that businesses are producing goods, products and services that are safe for consumers to use. When regulators find out that some product or good could harm a consumer, they may ask the business to change the way it is made. If the product or good is causing people to die or become seriously injured, they may even ask that it be withdrawn from the market.

过去几十年来最重大的商业新闻中，就有不少涉及此类事件。关于固特异轮胎是否会导致驾驶福特探险者汽车的人发生事故甚至死亡的问题，最初是由休斯顿的KHOU-TV报道的，随后才演变成全国性的新闻事件。数百万条轮胎最终被召回，福特公司遭遇了史上最大亏损，并终止了与长期轮胎供应商的合作关系。这一事件促使全国各地的越野车驾驶员检查自己的轮胎，质疑自己驾驶的车辆是否安全。

<!--en-->
Some of the biggest business stories in the last few decades have involved such stories. The question of whether Firestone tires were causing people to crash and die in their Ford Explorers was first reported by KHOU-TV in Houston before it became a national story. Millions of tires ended up being recalled. Ford posted its largest loss ever and ended its relationship with its longtime tire supplier. The story made drivers of sports utility vehicles across the country check their tires and question whether they were driving a safe vehicle.

20世纪80年代最重大的商业新闻之一，发生在制药公司强生因芝加哥地区有七人因服用含有氰化物的药片身亡而被迫召回数百万瓶泰诺之后。此次事件引发的恐慌促使全球各地的制药公司在产品包装上安装防篡改封条。

<!--en-->
One of the biggest business stories of the 1980s occurred after drug maker Johnson & Johnson was forced to recall millions of Tylenol containers after seven people in the Chicago area died as a result of ingesting cyanide-laced pills. The ensuing scare caused drug makers around the world to install tamper-proof seals to their packages.

世界各地都经常出现对产品安全性的担忧。在美国，有多个监管机构负责确保销售给消费者的产品和商品是安全的。这些担忧的范围从快餐店汉堡的健康程度到儿童是否会因玩具部件而窒息不等。

<!--en-->
Concerns about the safety of products occur on a regular basis around the world. In the United States, a number of regulatory agencies are charged with making sure the products and goods sold to consumers are safe. The concerns can range from the healthiness of the hamburger at a fast-food restaurant to whether a child can choke on a toy part.

消费者产品安全委员会（CPSC）成立于1972年，是负责监管大多数产品的政府机构。其监管范围涵盖从粘合剂到木炉等各类产品。而弹药、汽车、化妆品、药品、食品、轮胎和烟草等属于其他监管机构的管辖范畴，不在其监管范围内。

<!--en-->
The Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) was created in 1972 and is the government agency that oversees most products. The products it covers range from adhesives to wood-burning stoves. It does not regulate products such as ammunition, automobiles, cosmetics, drugs, foods, tires, and tobacco, which are under the realm of other regulatory agencies.

CPSC会与企业及行业合作，制定产品制造的安全标准。它负责执行这些标准，若产品未达到标准则可予以禁止销售。该机构还会研究产品可能存在的隐患，并可针对有缺陷的产品发出召回命令或要求进行维修。该机构由总统任命并经参议院确认的三名委员负责管理，其中一名委员是……

<!--en-->
The CPSC works with companies and industries to set guidelines as to how products should be manufactured so that they are safe. It enforces those standards and can ban products if those standards are not met. The agency also conducts research on potential product hazards, and can issue a recall or order repairs on a defective product. The agency is run by three commissioners appointed by the president and confirmed by the Senate. One of the commissioners is a

#### 专家建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

道琼斯通讯社华盛顿分社社长罗布·威尔斯关于将华盛顿相关新闻作为商业题材报道的经验：

<!--en-->
Dow Jones Newswires
Washington bureau chief Rob
Wells on covering Washington as a business story:

**让不同故事相互补充：**一篇关于国会某个委员会正在考虑对投资银行家的薪酬设定新限制的文章，若能加入一段介绍那些获得高额奖金和薪水的银行家们的内容，会更有说服力。而对CEO或企业高层管理人员的采访，若能补充一段关于他们参与竞选捐款或游说活动的信息，也会更加充实。试着将外部信息作为对新闻内容的“现实检验”。

<!--en-->
**Cross-pollinate your stories:**
An article about a Congressional committee considering new restrictions on investment bankers' pay would always benefit from a paragraph identifying the bankers with the fat bonuses and paychecks. An interview with a CEO or a top company executive will benefit with a paragraph about their campaign contributions or lobbying activities. Try to bring in the outside information as a "reality check" to a story.

作为该机构的主席以及420名员工，他负责监督15,000多种产品的安全性。

<!--en-->
344 • Government Issue chairman, and the agency's 420 employees oversee the safety of more than 15,000 products.

显然，有些产品及其制造商无法达到CPSC的标准。一旦出现这种情况，该机构就会运用权力保护消费者。这时，商业记者很可能会在这个机构找到新闻素材，尤其是当相关产品是在当地工厂生产的，或是由位于其媒体机构所在地区的公司销售的。

<!--en-->
Naturally, some products and the companies that manufacture them fail to meet the CPSC standards. And when that happens, the agency will use its power to protect the consumer.
