That is when a business reporter is likely to find a story at this agency, particularly if the product is manufactured at a local plant or sold by a company with headquarters located in his or her media outlet's area.

CPSC始终忙碌不已。例如在2009年8月，该委员会就与企业合作宣布召回41,000台Baby Jogger City迷你婴儿车、约200,000台Frigidaire和Kenmore Elite Smoothtop电灶、15,400副横百叶窗、16,400副竖百叶窗、800个蜂窝状遮阳帘、85,000个罗马式遮阳帘、46,000台Maytag、Magic Chef、Maytag的Performa系列以及Crosley品牌的冰箱、15,000本eebee’s“Have a Ball” Adventures系列布书、150万台Durabrand DVD播放机、3,000台Ridgid 10英寸台锯、9,800台Black & Decker热咖啡机，以及160万套Little Tikes手工套装和玩具车。而这还仅仅是该月所有的召回产品数量。CPSC的总法律顾问办公室还会就那些无需通过召回即可解决缺陷的问题出具咨询意见。

<!--en-->
The CPSC remains busy. In August 2009, for example, the commission worked with businesses to announce the recall of 41,000 Baby Jogger City mini strollers, about 200,000 Frigidaire and Kenmore Elite Smoothtop electric ranges, 15,400 horizontal blinds, 16,400 vertical blinds, 800 cellular shades, 85,000 Roman shades, 46,000 Maytag, Magic Chef, Performa by Maytag and Crosley brand refrigerators, 15,000 eebee's "Have a Ball" Adventures cloth books, 1.5 million Durabrand DVD players, 3,000 Ridgid 10-inch table saws, 9,800 Black & Decker thermal coffeemakers and 1.6 million Little Tikes workshops sets and trucks. And these were not even all of the product recalls for the month. The CPSC's Office of the General Counsel also issues advisory opinions about products that may not need a recall to correct a defect.

由于这些产品往往遍布全国，因此几乎任何报纸、网站、电视台或广播电台都可以将产品召回事件作为新闻报道，因为该媒体的受众中很可能有人拥有被召回的产品。

<!--en-->
Product recalls can be stories for almost any newspaper, Internet site, TV station, or radio station because the products are often distributed throughout the country. It is likely that someone in the outlet's audience has a product that has been recalled.

通过观察趋势，了解哪些类型的商品或产品被召回，也能挖掘出产品召回相关的新闻。*洛杉矶时报*的一名记者就发现了这样的趋势——快餐连锁店随儿童餐免费赠送的玩具因存在安全隐患而被大量召回。这些快餐店赠送的玩具占所有被召回玩具的77%。

<!--en-->
Product recall stories can also be developed by watching trends to see what type of goods or products have been recalled. A reporter from the *Los Angeles Times* spotted such a trend—the toys that fast-food restaurant chains were giving away with kids' meals were being recalled by the millions because of safety concerns. Fast food toys accounted for 77 percent of all of the toys recalled.

并非只有CPSC在努力保护消费者免受不安全产品的侵害。化妆品、药品、食品和医疗设备由食品药品监督管理局负责监管，而汽车座椅、轮胎和汽车则由国家公路交通安全管理局（NHTSA）进行审查。

<!--en-->
The CPSC is not the only agency that is trying to protect consumers from unsafe products. Cosmetics, drugs, foods, and medical devices come under the watch of the Food and Drug Administration, whereas car seats, tires, and vehicles are reviewed by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA).

NHTSA在宣布产品召回方面与CPSC一样忙碌。2009年8月，它宣布了从现代汽车到校车以及捷豹等品牌的车辆召回计划。2010年，丰田汽车公司在其汽车中存在导致车辆无故加速的问题后被迫召回数百万辆汽车。涉及全国各地数千辆汽车或卡车的重大召回事件很可能会影响到每个州的消费者。尽管许多大众媒体可能不需要将这些新闻作为完整报道，但至少也应简要提及。

<!--en-->
The NHTSA is as busy as the CPSC in announcing recalls. In August 2009, it announced recalls involving vehicles ranging from Hyundais to school buses and Jaguars. In 2010, Toyota Motor Corp. recalled millions of vehicles after it was determined that something in its cars was causing them to accelerate without warning. Major recalls involving thousands of cars or trucks across the country are likely to affect consumers in every state. Although such news may not need to be covered as full stories in many mass communication outlets, they should merit at least a brief mention.

各州也参与保护消费者。例如，每个州都制定了所谓的“柠檬法”，允许消费者退回购买后多次出现故障的汽车及其他车辆。大多数州规定，故障必须在购车后的12至24个月内，或行驶12,000至24,000英里内发生。如果缺陷涉及刹车或转向等严重问题，制造商只需有一次修复机会；若是其他与安全相关的缺陷，则有两次修复机会；对于其他类型的缺陷，制造商最多可有四次修复机会。政府机构 • 345 许多其他联邦及州级监管机构也在致力于保护消费者。例如，联邦贸易委员会（FTC）积极打击网络欺诈行为；州保险专员则起诉那些销售虚假保单的保险代理人；联邦通信委员会（FCC）则处理消费者关于电话公司无故中断服务以及广播电台播放低俗内容的投诉。商业界中甚至还有私人组织也参与消费者保护工作。商业改进局也会受理针对企业的投诉，并统计企业收到的投诉数量。

<!--en-->
States are also involved in protecting consumers. For example, every state has passed what is known as a lemon law, which allows consumers to return cars and other vehicles that have broken down repeatedly after purchase. Most states have a period where the breakdowns must occur within the first 12 to 24 months of purchase, or within 12,000 to 24,000 miles. If the defect is related to something serious such as brakes or steering, the manufacturer is given one chance at repairing it. If it is another safety-related defect, the manufacturer has two chances to repair the vehicle. The manufacturer is allowed as many as four chances for repair on other defects.
Government Issue • 345
Many other federal and state regulators also act to protect consumers. The Federal Trade Commission (FTC), for example, is active in pursuing Internet fraud. State insurance commissioners prosecute insurance agents who sell fake policies. The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) addresses consumer complaints about telephone companies cutting service without reason and radio stations broadcasting vulgar words. There are even private organizations within the business community that also are involved with consumer protection. The Better Business Bureau also handles complaints against businesses, and tracks the number of complaints that a business receives.

每当记者撰写有关某家公司的报道，尤其是那些向消费者销售产品的企业时，最好先查看是否有相关投诉。

<!--en-->
Anytime a reporter is writing about a company, particularly a business which sells products to consumers, it is wise to check to see if there are complaints.

并非所有消费者都会一直满意。如果像沃尔玛或微软这样的大型公司所售产品只有少数几起投诉，可能就没什么可写的新闻价值。但如果针对同一家公司的同类产品或同一缺陷存在大量投诉，那就有可能成为新闻素材。

<!--en-->
Not every consumer is going to be happy all of the time. If there are a handful of complaints about the products being sold by a huge company, such as Wal-Mart or Microsoft, then there may not be a story. But if there are a number of complaints against any company that are all about the same product or the same defect, then there may be a story.

### 环保局与食品药品监督管理局

<!--en-->
*The EPA and FDA*

另外两个在商业监管中起着关键作用的联邦机构——环境保护局（EPA）和食品药品监督管理局（FDA）——常被认为主要负责非商业领域的事务。但实际上，食品和药品销售都是价值数十亿美元的产业。而且，日益受到关注的那些影响环境的商业行为也正被更严格地审查。

<!--en-->
Two other federal agencies that play a vital business regulation role—the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and the Food and Drug Administration (FDA)—are often thought of as focusing on nonbusiness topics. But selling foods and drugs are multibillion dollar businesses. And increasingly, business practices that affect the environment are coming under closer scrutiny.

食品药品监督管理局成立于一个多世纪前，而环境保护局则直到1970年7月才设立。这两个机构都有数千名工作人员，负责监管众多企业——其中许多企业同时也受其他州级和联邦机构的监管。

<!--en-->
The FDA was formed more than a century ago, while the EPA was not established until July 1970. Both of them have thousands of staff members charged with regulating numerous companies—many companies that also fall under regulations from other state and federal agencies.

雷切尔·卡森于1962年在《纽约客》上首次发表、后来结集成书的《寂静的春天》引发了人们对农药使用及其对环境影响的强烈抗议。这篇经过深入研究的报道可被视为促使联邦政府成立专门环保机构的契机。

<!--en-->
Rachel Carson's *Silent Spring*, published first in the *New Yorker* in 1962 and later as a book, led to an outcry about the use of pesticides and their effects on the environment. This exhaustively researched reporting can be considered to be what led the federal government to create an agency to protect the environment.

环境保护局的职责是保护人类健康并维护环境。它通过执行现有的环境法规并制定标准来履行职责，同时还会对不达标且造成污染的企业进行处罚。该机构在全国设有10个区域分部，每个分部负责执行相关法规。

<!--en-->
The EPA's job is to protect human health and to safeguard the environment. It carries out its job by enforcing existing environmental laws and setting standards. The agency also sanctions companies that do not meet its requirements and pollute. The EPA is divided into 10 regional divisions across the country, and each region is charged with enforcing the laws.

环境保护局已采取措施禁止某些企业销售的产品。1972年，它禁止了杀虫剂DDT的使用；两年后开始实施《安全饮用水法》。1975年，该机构禁止在大多数家庭和农业用途中使用七氯和氯丹这两种杀虫剂，称其会对人体造成癌症威胁。三年后，环境保护局又禁止了联合化学、杜邦、凯泽铝业与化学公司、彭沃尔特公司以及雷肯公司等大型企业生产的多数气雾剂产品（如发胶和除臭剂）中所含的破坏臭氧层的氟碳气体。

<!--en-->
The EPA has taken measures to ban products sold by companies. In 1972, it banned the use of the pesticide DDT, and two years later it began enforcing the Safe Drinking Water Act. In 1975, the agency banned the use of pesticides heptachlor and chlordane for most household and agricultural uses, calling them a cancer threat to humans. Three years later, the EPA banned ozone-destroying fluorocarbon gases in most aerosol products—such as hair spray and deodorant—produced by large companies such as Allied Chemical, DuPont, Kaiser Aluminum and Chemical, Pennwalt, and Racon.

环境保护局还在“超级基金计划”以及老旧建筑中石棉的清理工作中发挥了重要作用。“超级基金计划”已在全国范围内确定了多个存在化学物质及其他污染物的地点。

<!--en-->
The EPA has also played a major role in the Superfund program and in the cleanup and removal of asbestos from older buildings. The Superfund program has identified sites across the country in which chemicals and other products are

#### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

道琼斯通讯社华盛顿分社社长罗布·威尔斯谈如何将华盛顿的新闻作为商业题材进行报道：

<!--en-->
Dow Jones Newswires
Washington bureau chief Rob
Wells on covering Washington as a business story:

**网络与日历：**深入了解这两个领域的实际运作：参加涉及电话公司监管的冗长委员会听证会，同时出席年度股东大会。与国会委员会中的工作人员以及负责管理日益发展的手机或信用卡业务的中层管理者会面。在报道委员会听证会时，留意走廊里的动态——往往最精彩的新闻就发生在会议室之外。说到实地采访，不妨将日历当作报道工具。当某个机构提出新规则时，记下公众意见征询期的结束时间。那些资金雄厚的企业和行业协会通常会在意见征询期结束前一两天寄来高质量的评论信。提前一周就开始打电话，以便抢先获取独家消息。Outlook等日历软件有提前一周的提醒功能——充分利用它们。

<!--en-->
**Networking and calendars:**
Get into the dirty work of both worlds: attend the long committee hearings involving regulation of a telephone company, and attend the annual shareholder meetings. Meet the staff directors on the Congressional committees and the middle managers who oversee the growing cell phone or credit card businesses. When covering a committee hearing, check the action in the hallways—often the best stories are happening outside the room. And speaking of shoe-leather reporting, use the calendar as a reporting weapon. When an agency proposes new rules, note when the public comment period expires. The good comment letters from the big money companies and trade groups typically come a day or two before the comment period ends. Start making calls a week ahead and get the scoop. Outlook and other calendars have week ahead reminders—use them.

346 • 政府机构造成的污染问题已下令进行清理，而这可能耗资数百万美元。超级基金清理项目在保险公司等行业引发了争议，因为根据旧政策，这些企业必须承担清理费用。美国环保局维护着全国各超级基金污染点的清单。如果其中某个点位于记者所在地区，那或许就能成为一篇新闻稿的主题。

<!--en-->
346 • Government Issue polluting the area and has ordered their cleanup, which can cost millions of dollars. Superfund cleanups have caused controversy in industries such as insurance companies, who have to foot the bill to clean up on the basis of old policies. The EPA maintains a list of Superfund sites across the country. If one of them is in a reporter's area, it might be a story.

自美国环保局成立以来最严重的环境事件，是2010年夏季墨西哥湾发生的近500万桶石油泄漏事故。英国石油公司同意向受该泄漏影响的周边企业和个人支付200亿美元的赔偿金。

<!--en-->
The biggest environmental issue since the EPA's creation was the spill of nearly 5 million barrels of oil in the Gulf of Mexico in the Summer of 2010. British Petroleum agreed to pay $20 billion in claims for companies and people who were affected by the spill in the surrounding area.

1996年，美国环保局推动了含铅汽油的逐步淘汰，因为这种汽油曾导致儿童患病。2000年，该机构几乎全面禁止了国内最常用的家用杀虫剂Dursban在家庭和园艺领域的使用，这款产品由陶氏化学公司生产。

<!--en-->
In 1996, the EPA led the phasing out of leaded gasoline, which had been causing illnesses in children. And in 2000, it eliminated virtually all home and garden uses of Dursban—the most widely used household pesticide in the country and a product of Dow Chemical.

尽管这些新闻大多属于全国性议题，但美国环保局也监管着全国各地的众多企业。该机构每年会对数千家企业的空气、水和危险废物处理情况进行检查，若发现企业违反法规，就会对其处以罚款。此外，美国环保局还会为那些被允许使用特定产品并通过规定方式处置这些产品的设施颁发许可证。

<!--en-->
Although most of these stories are national issues, the EPA also regulates many businesses in every town and city in the country. The agency conducts thousands of air, water, and hazardous waste compliance inspections every year, and can fine a business if it is found to be violating the laws. The EPA also grants permits to facilities that are allowed to use certain products and get rid of them by approved methods.

如果某个城镇或城市发生环境泄漏事故，负责报道的记者应查阅相关记录，确认涉事企业是否拥有合法许可证，以及其过去是否因违反美国环保局规定而被处罚。有时候，更重要的新闻线索就在过去发生过或没有发生过的事情中。

<!--en-->
If there is an environmental spill in a town or a city, a reporter covering the story should check these records to see if the business had the proper permits and to see if the business had been fined in the past for violating EPA rules. Sometimes, the bigger story can be found in what happened, or did not happen, in the past.

几乎所有涉及化学品、液体或其他可能污染环境的产品的企业都会与美国环保局产生联系。如果记者怀疑某家企业可能在造成污染，应首先向监管机构咨询，了解他们已发现的实际情况。

<!--en-->
Virtually every company or business dealing with chemicals, liquids, or other products that can pollute the environment comes into contact with the EPA. If a reporter suspects a company may be polluting, he or she should check with regulators first to see what those agencies have uncovered.

食品药品监督管理局在监管化妆品、食品、药品和医疗设备生产企业方面扮演着类似的角色。它的职责也是通过多种方式保护消费者权益。对于我们每天在杂货店购买的食品，食品药品监督管理局会确保冷冻食品、包装肉制品等产品的安全性、卫生性、营养价值以及标签的准确性。对于药品，该机构会审查有关其功效的医学研究，并批准其向公众销售。

<!--en-->
The FDA plays a similar role with companies that manufacture and produce cosmetics, foods, drugs, and medical devices. Its job is also to protect the consumer in many ways. With food products that each of us buy in the grocery store on a daily basis, the FDA ensures that these frozen dinners and packaged meat trays, among other things, are safe, sanitary, wholesome, and properly labeled. With drugs, the FDA reviews medical research on the effectiveness of the drugs and approves them for sale to the general public.

食品药品监督管理局的监管范围还包括化妆品的安全性与标签规范、医疗设备的制造与性能、微波炉、X光机及太阳灯等辐射产品的安全性，以及宠物食品、兽药和医疗器械的安全性。所有这些产品和商品都是由营利性企业生产的，这意味着它们在投放市场前必须获得食品药品监督管理局的批准，且标签内容必须真实，不得具有误导性。

<!--en-->
The FDA's oversight also includes the safety and labeling of cosmetics; the manufacturing and performance of medical devices; the safety of radiation-emitting products such as microwaves, x-ray machines, and sun lamps; and the safety of pet foods, veterinary drugs, and devices. All of these products and goods are manufactured by for-profit companies, which means these companies have to receive FDA approval for their products and goods before they can be sold to the public. The labeling must be truthful and not misleading.

近年来，由于在为制药公司审批新药方面的作用，尤其是随着国内艾滋病患者数量增加，他们急需能够对抗该疾病的药物，食品药品监督管理局频频成为媒体关注的焦点。其药品审批流程也在其他方面引发过关注，比如2001年它未能对ImClone公司的抗癌药Erbitux进行审核，导致该公司首席执行官萨姆·瓦克斯尔在信息公开前抛售股票，最终他被逮捕并入狱服刑。政府机构 • 347 食品药品监督管理局的审批流程决定着一款药品的命运。制药公司会向监管机构提交包含该药品疗效研究资料和背景信息的申请。该机构可以审查申请并要求制药公司提供更多信息，或者直接接受申请，随后将该药品纳入审批流程。

<!--en-->
The FDA has garnered media coverage in recent years for its role in approving new drugs for pharmaceutical companies, particularly with the increase in the number of AIDS patients in the country wanting medications that can help them combat the illness. Its drug approval process has also garnered attention in other ways, such as when it failed to review ImClone's cancer drug Erbitux in 2001, leading CEO Sam Waksal to sell shares in the company beforethe information was publicly disclosed, resulting in his eventual arrest and prison term.
Government Issue • 347
The FDA's review process can make or break a drug. A pharmaceutical company submits an application to the regulators with research and background on the drug's effectiveness. The agency can review the filing and ask for more information from the drug company, or it can accept the filing, which then places the drug into its review pipeline.

一种药物能否获批用于公众使用，可能决定一家小型制药公司的兴衰。许多初创制药公司都会向投资者出售股票，承诺在资金耗尽之前让他们的药物获得美国食品药品监督管理局的批准。因此，对于小型公司而言，药物的获批，或是针对重大疾病的药物获批，都可能成为重要的商业新闻，正如以下《圣何塞水星报》的报道所示：

<!--en-->
Approval of a drug for public consumption can make or break a small pharmaceutical company. Many start-up drug companies sell stock to investors on the promise that their drugs will be approved by the FDA before their money runs out. Therefore, drug approval for a small company, or drug approval for a major illness, can be an important business story, as the following *San Jose Mercury News* story illustrates:

吉利德科学公司周五获得了美国食品药品监督管理局对其治疗慢性乙型肝炎新药Hepsera的批准。慢性乙型肝炎是一种严重的疾病，可能导致肝癌、肝衰竭甚至死亡。

<!--en-->
Gilead Sciences won Food and Drug Administration approval Friday for Hepsera, its new pill for treating chronic hepatitis B, a devastating illness that can lead to liver cancer, liver failure and death.

这是这家位于福斯特城的生物技术公司在不到一年时间内获得的第二项药物批准，预计将提升吉利德的盈利能力。Hepsera的首批货物应在周二前送达批发商手中。该药需每日服用一次，每位患者的年度费用为5,353美元。

<!--en-->
The agency action is the Foster City biotechnology company's second drug approval in less than a year and is expected to boost Gilead's newfound profitability. The first shipments of Hepsera should reach wholesalers by Tuesday. The annual cost of the once-a-day pill will be $5,353 per patient.

在估计的125万感染乙型肝炎的美国人群中，目前只有约5万人正在接受治疗，因此吉利德计划开展大规模宣传，让医生了解Hepsera的益处。

<!--en-->
Only about 50,000 of the estimated 1.25 million Americans infected with hepatitis B are currently being treated, so Gilead is planning an extensive campaign to convince physicians of Hepsera's benefits.

吉利德首席财务官约翰·F·米利根表示：“华尔街预计该药第一年的销售额可达3000万美元。我们需要通过与医生合作，逐步让他们习惯这种治疗方法，从而拓展市场。”

<!--en-->
"Wall Street is estimating $30 million in sales the first year," said Gilead Chief Financial Officer John F. Milligan. "We will have to grow the market over time working with physicians, getting doctors used to the treatment."

美国食品药品监督管理局的一份简报指出，Hepsera通过干扰乙型肝炎病毒的复制来减缓疾病进展，且对已经对另一种抗病毒药物拉米夫定或Epivir产生耐药性的病毒也有效。

<!--en-->
An FDA briefing paper points out that Hepsera slows the progress of the disease by interfering with the duplication of the hepatitis B virus and that it is effective against viruses that have grown resistant to another anti-viral drug, lamivudine or Epivir.

迈阿密大学肝脏病专家、参与该药物患者试验的研究人员之一尤金·希夫博士说：“今天美国食品药品监督管理局批准Hepsera，为医生及其患者提供了对抗慢性乙型肝炎的新武器。”

<!--en-->
"Today's FDA approval of Hepsera gives physicians and their patients a new weapon in the fight against chronic hepatitis B," said Dr. Eugene Schiff, a liver specialist at the University of Miami and one of the investigators who tested the drug in patients.

乙型肝炎是多种病毒性肝炎之一。与艾滋病类似，它也是通过体液传播的——主要途径是无保护性行为和脏针头。

<!--en-->
Hepatitis B is one of several forms of viral hepatitis. Like AIDS, it is spread through bodily fluids—primarily through unprotected sex and dirty needles.

吉利德将在美国和欧洲推销这款药物，这些地区的乙型肝炎发病率是这里的两倍多。其合作伙伴葛兰素史克则将在包括亚洲在内的其他地区销售该药，那里有超过3亿名患者。

<!--en-->
Gilead will market the drug in the United States and Europe, where the incidence of hepatitis B is more than twice what it is here. Its partner, GlaxoSmithKline, will sell it elsewhere, including Asia, where there are more than 300 million patients.

Hepsera其实是阿德福韦二吡呋酯的商品名，最初是为治疗艾滋病而研发的。但在杀死艾滋病病毒所需的剂量下，它的毒性过大。研究人员发现，在低得多的剂量下，该药物可以逆转慢性乙型肝炎患者的肝脏损伤。

<!--en-->
Hepsera—the brand name for adefovir dipivoxil—was first developed for treating AIDS. But in the doses required to kill the AIDS virus, it proved too toxic. Researchers showed that in much lower doses, the drug can reverse liver damage in patients with chronic hepatitis B.

#### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

道琼斯通讯社华盛顿分社社长罗布·威尔斯关于如何将华盛顿的新闻报道成商业题材的建议：

<!--en-->
Dow Jones Newswires
Washington bureau chief Rob
Wells on covering Washington as a business story:

**数字化存在感：**建立电子邮件分发列表或推特账号，将已发布的新闻发送给消息来源。有些媒体公司不赞成免费分发内容。向编辑说明这是一种提升与消息来源联系频率的社交工具。务必对列表中的收件人进行“盲发”，否则消息来源看到自己的姓名和邮箱被广泛传播会感到不满。

<!--en-->
**Digital presence:** Create an e-mail distribution list or Twitter feed to distribute your published stories to sources. Some media companies frown on giving away content. Explain to your editor that this is a networking tool to increase your visibility to your sources. Make sure to "blind copy" people on the list. Your sources would be annoyed to see their names and emails distributed widely.

#### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

道琼斯通讯社华盛顿分社社长罗布·威尔斯关于如何将华盛顿的新闻报道成商业题材的建议：

<!--en-->
Dow Jones Newswires
Washington bureau chief Rob
Wells on covering Washington as a business story:

**游说披露报告：**花时间阅读你所报道的公司提交的游说披露报告（别忘了他们所聘请的咨询公司的报告）。这些报告通常会包含游说者的电话号码和电子邮箱地址，还会提供有关游说活动范围的详细信息，而这些信息通过诸如“响应政治中心”这类实用数据库查看时可能并不明显。348 • 政府相关内容

<!--en-->
**Lobby disclosure reports:** Take the time to read the lobby disclosure reports for the companies you cover (and don't forget the reports for the consultants they use). The actual reports often contain phone numbers and e-mail addresses for the lobbyists. They also provide some detail about the scope of lobbying activities, material that might not be obvious when reviewing lobby information through the very useful databases such as Center for Responsive Politics.
348 • Government Issue

#### 专业人士的建议

<!--en-->
*Tips from the Pros*

道琼斯通讯社华盛顿分社社长罗布·威尔斯关于如何将华盛顿的新闻报道成商业题材的建议：前高管与顾问：寻找那些曾在你所报道的公司或行业担任高级职务的人士，让他们为你介绍你所报道机构的特色与历史。各类行业行业协会都有这样的人，从美国商会到银行控股公司协会都有。要记住，那些员工人数有限的小型行业协会里也可能有善于表达的聪明人。

<!--en-->
Dow Jones Newswires
Washington bureau chief Rob
Wells on covering Washington as a business story:
Former executives,
consultants: Find people who once held senior positions in the companies or industries you cover. Get them to explain the personalities and history of the organizations you are covering. The various industry trade associations have these people, ranging from the U.S.
Chamber of Commerce to the
Association of Bank Holding
Companies. Remember that small trade associations, with limited staff, can have smart people who like to talk a lot.

一个建议：查阅针对某项有争议的监管提案提交给监管机构（如美国证券交易委员会）的评论信，弄清楚是谁写了这些信，又是谁负责处理相关事务。与这些人建立良好关系。

<!--en-->
One tip: Examine the comment letters filed to a regulatory agency, such as the SEC, on a controversial regulatory proposal. Find out who wrote the letters and who did the staff legwork to make the letter happen. Cultivate these people.

去年，吉利德公司的抗HIV药物Viread获得了批准，该药物很快便成为最畅销的艾滋病治疗药物之一，也是该公司盈利能力的核心。⁸与所有关于药品的报道一样，本报告将评估这款新药能为该公司带来多少营收，并分析其对该公司利润的影响。

<!--en-->
Last year, Gilead won approval for Viread, an anti-HIV drug that rapidly became one of the bestselling AIDS treatments and is the cornerstone of the company's profitability.⁸
As any story about a pharmaceutical drug should, this report assesses how much in revenue the new drug will add to the company's financial picture, and also evaluates what it will mean to its profits.

美国食品药品监督管理局还可以对其监管范围内的企业提起诉讼，要求其停止生产或销售某种产品。它还经常与其他监管机构，如联邦贸易委员会，联手制止食品、药品或美容产品中的虚假广告行为。

<!--en-->
The FDA can also file litigation against companies involved in the businesses it regulates, asking them to halt production or dispensing of a product. And it often joins with other regulatory agencies, such as the FTC, to halt misleading advertising of food, drug, or beauty products.

相关行动会通过类似2009年7月的以下新闻稿形式公布：

<!--en-->
An action would be announced in a news release similar to the following one from July 2009:

美国食品药品监督管理局今日宣布了一项永久性禁令的同意令，禁止Teva Animal Health Inc.、其总裁以及母公司的两名高管生产及销售掺假兽药。一旦法院正式下达此禁令，被告在遵守现行良好生产规范（cGMP）并获得FDA批准之前，将被禁止生产及销售兽药。

<!--en-->
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration announced a consent decree of permanent injunction filed today that prohibits Teva Animal Health Inc., its president, and two principals from its parent company, from manufacturing and distributing adulterated veterinary drugs. The injunction, once entered by the court, will prevent the defendants from manufacturing and distributing veterinary drugs until they achieve compliance with current Good Manufacturing Practice (cGMP) and obtain FDA approval.

FDA兽医医学中心主任Bernadette Dunham博士表示：“良好生产规范标准是产品质量的基石，也是FDA确保兽药产品安全有效的最重要依据。”

<!--en-->
"Good manufacturing practice standards are the backbone of product quality and the instrument on which the FDA relies most heavily for assurance that veterinary drug products are safe and effective," said Bernadette Dunham, D.V.M., Ph.D., director of the FDA's Center for Veterinary Medicine.

在2007年至2009年的检查中，FDA在位于密苏里州圣约瑟夫的Teva Animal Health工厂发现了严重的cGMP违规行为。

<!--en-->
During inspections between 2007 and 2009, the FDA found significant cGMP violations at Teva Animal Health's facilities, located in St. Joseph, Mo.

根据该同意令的规定，除非建立起适当的流程、设施和管控措施，并有独立专家对相关设施和流程进行检查并确认其符合cGMP标准，否则Teva Animal Health不得恢复兽药的生产和销售。FDA还会在批准该公司恢复运营前视需要对其设施进行检查。如果该公司在恢复运营后仍未能遵守同意令的任何条款、cGMP标准或《联邦食品、药品和化妆品法》，FDA可命令其停止生产及销售兽药、召回产品或采取其他纠正措施。

<!--en-->
Under the terms of the consent decree, Teva Animal Health cannot resume manufacturing and distributing veterinary drugs until adequate methods, facilities, and controls are established and an independent expert inspects the facilities and procedures and certifies that they comply with cGMP. The FDA also will inspect Teva Animal Health's facilities as needed before authorizing the company to resume operations. If, after resuming operations, the defendants fail to comply with any provision of the consent decree, cGMP, or the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, the FDA may order the company to stop manufacturing and distributing veterinary drugs, recall the products, or take other corrective actions.

FDA监管事务代理副局长Michael Chappell表示：“FDA绝不容忍掺假兽药的制造和销售。兽医和宠物主人可以放心，FDA会调查那些在无法保障产品安全和质量的情况下生产兽药的企业，并对其采取监管措施。”[^3881]：⁸摘自P. Jacobs于2002年9月21日发表在《圣何塞水星报》上的文章《吉利德公司的乙肝药获批准；FDA称Hepsera能减缓疾病进展》，第1页。版权归《圣何塞水星报》所有，保留所有权利。经许可转载。政府专刊 • 349。如果未来再次出现违规行为，该同意令还将规定，每有一天被告未遵守同意令的任何条款，Teva Animal Health需支付20,000美元；每有一批违反规定的兽药被运出，还需额外支付25,000美元，每年最高罚款额可达750万美元。⁹与CPSC和NHTSA一样，FDA也会对其监管的产品发布召回通知和安全警示。这些产品可能是被沙门氏菌等细菌或其他致病微生物污染的食品，也可能是包装标识不当、含有可能因过敏而引发严重疾病甚至死亡的成分的产品。

<!--en-->
"The FDA will not tolerate the manufacture and distribution of adulterated animal drugs," said Michael Chappell, the FDA's acting associate commissioner for regulatory affairs. "Veterinarians and pet owners can be assured that the FDA will investigate and take regulatory actions againstcompanies that produce animal drugs under conditions and controls that are inadequate to assure their safety and quality.”
[^3881]: ⁸ From "Gilead pill wins approval to treat hepatitis B; FDA says Hepsera slows disease's progress," by P. Jacobs, September 21, 2002, *San Jose Mercury News*, p. 1. Copyright 2002 by *San Jose Mercury News*. All rights reserved. Reprinted with permission.
Government Issue • 349
In the event of future violations, the consent decree also subjects Teva Animal Health to payments of $20,000 for each day the defendants fail to comply with any provision of the decree and an additional $25,000 for each shipment of veterinary drugs in violation of the decree, up to $7.5 million per year.⁹
Just like the CPSC and the NHTSA, the FDA will also issue product recalls and safety alerts for products it regulates. These can be food products contaminated with bacteria or other illness-causing organisms such as salmonella, or they may be products with improperly marked packaging that contain ingredients that can cause serious illness or death as a result of allergies.

在每种情况下，记者都应核实是否有适合读者阅读的报道素材。如果该产品是在当地生产或销售的，或者生产该产品的公司位于当地，通常就有报道价值。如果当地有人因该产品而患病或死亡，那很可能会成为头版新闻。2001年，《底特律自由报》曾刊登了一系列报道，讲述Sara Lee肉类加工厂运送了受污染的肉类，导致15人死亡、100多人患病。

<!--en-->
In each case, reporters should check to see if there is a story for their readership. This is often the case if the product or good has been distributed or manufactured locally, or the company that made the product is located in the area. If local people have become sick or died as a result of the product, it is likely front-page news. *The Detroit Free Press* ran a series of stories in 2001 about how a Sara Lee meat plant shipped tainted meat, killing 15 and making more than 100 sick.

食品或药品的召回或禁售可能会对生产企业造成损害。有些企业无法妥善处理此类情况，反而将问题归咎于他人。如果记者所关注的某家企业存在这种情况，他或她应采访行业专家和科学家，以查明问题所在。监管机构也会发表意见，企业很可能也会如此。但各方可能都有自己的目的，而独立第三方或许更为客观。

<!--en-->
The recall or banning of a food or drug product can be damaging to the manufacturing company. Some fail to handle the situation properly and blame others for their problem. If this is the case with a business on a reporter's beat, he or she should interview industry experts and scientists to find out what went wrong. The regulators will also talk, as likely will the company. But each side will probably have an agenda, and the independent parties may be more objective.

### FCC和FTC

<!--en-->
*The FCC and FTC*

FCC和FTC在监管企业方面也发挥着重要作用。近年来，两机构都在执法及法规解读方面采取了引人注目的举措。

<!--en-->
The FCC and the FTC also play important roles in regulating businesses. And both of them have taken high-profile positions in recent years in enforcing and interpreting their laws and regulations.

FCC的职责是监管通过无线电、有线、卫星、电视和有线电视进行的州际通信。换句话说，在拥有广播电台、电视台或有线电视公司的城镇中，FCC都会对这些企业进行监管。该委员会由总统任命并经参议院批准产生的五名委员组成，任期为五年。

<!--en-->
The FCC's role is to regulate interstate communication by radio, wire, satellite, television, and cable. In other words, in a town with a radio station, television station, or a cable company, the FCC is involved in overseeing those businesses. The commission is run by five commissioners appointed by the president and approved by the Senate to five-year terms.

所有受FCC监管的企业都必须获得该机构的许可。此外，该机构还负责处理消费者的投诉并调查潜在的违规行为。它会就针对这些企业的新法规召开听证会，并可对违反其监管法规的企业处以罚款。FCC还会举办拍卖，中标者将获得在其竞标频段内进行广播的权利。对于企业而言，赢得此类拍卖可能是一个重要契机。除非获得FCC的许可，允许其在特定频段内运营，否则广播电台无法正常工作。[^3891]：⁹ 联邦贸易委员会新闻稿，2009年7月31日。350 • 政府动态 2003年中，FCC放宽了媒体资产所有权的限制。此前，电视台、报纸和广播电台的所有权都受到诸多限制。但新规定允许更多的跨行业所有权形式。当然，FCC希望维持其所监管行业间的竞争。如果没有竞争，企业可能会提高价格。如果FCC要改变其监管行业的规则，记者应咨询当地企业，了解这是否会对其产生影响。如果这些规则导致当地企业做出调整，那便可能成为新闻素材。

<!--en-->
Each business that the FCC oversees must have a license from the agency. In addition, the agency handles complaints from consumers and investigates potential wrongdoing. It holds hearings about new regulations for these companies, and can fine companies that violate the laws it oversees. The FCC holds auctions, and the winners of these auctions receive the right to broadcast over the bandwidths on which they bid. Winning these auctions can be an important step for a business. A radio station cannot operate unless it has received approval from the FCC to operate on a certain bandwidth.
[^3891]: ⁹ Federal Trade Commission news release, July 31, 2009.
350 • Government Issue
In mid-2003, the FCC took the step of loosening rules on ownership of media properties. Previously, ownership of television stations, newspapers, and radio stations had been limited. But the new rules allow for more cross ownership. To be sure, the FCC wants to maintain competition among the industries that it regulates. Without competition, companies might raise rates. If the FCC is changing the rules for one of the industries it regulates, reporters should check with their local companies to see if it is going to affect them. If the rules cause local companies to make changes, then that could be a story.

对于撰写有关电话费或手机费以及各项收费项目的消费者相关报道的记者来说，FCC也是一个很好的信息来源。

<!--en-->
The FCC can also be a good resource for reporters writing consumer-related stories about phone bills or wireless phone bills, explaining the different charges.

FCC还参与其他事务，比如推动农村地区电信服务的普及，以及促使农村地区的医疗服务提供者能获得与城市地区相同的收费标准。这些都是全国各社区的重要发展趋势，应当作为当地商界的重要事件进行报道。

<!--en-->
The FCC also is involved in other issues, such as pushing for more rural telecommunication services and promoting rural health care providers to receive the same rates as those paid to health care providers in urban areas. These are important trends in communities across the country that should be covered as major events for the local business community.

FCC还监管那些拨打烦人电话试图说服人们办理新信用卡或向当地警察协会捐款的电话推销员。根据FCC的规定，这类电话不得在早上8点之前或晚上9点之后拨打，且来电者必须说明自己的身份以及代表哪个机构致电。

<!--en-->
The FCC also regulates telemarketers who make those pesky phone calls trying to get people to accept a new credit card or donate to the local police league. According to the FCC, these calls cannot be made before 8 a.m. or after 9 p.m., and the callers must identify themselves and what organization they are calling for.

在关于并购的第七章中，已经讨论了FTC在审查企业间交易中的作用。但实际上，FTC参与企业监管的方式还有很多。服装背面的护理标签以及家用电器上显示能效等级的贴纸，都是FTC法规的成果。FTC负责制定各种针对企业的规章制度，旨在保护消费者免受不公平和欺诈行为的侵害。该机构会审查从减肥广告到网络儿童保护等各种内容。如果某家网上零售商承诺在节假日前发货却未能交付，FTC会介入并进行调查。如果小型企业被收取了并未订购的墨粉或打印机墨盒费用，该机构也会对相关指控进行审查。

<!--en-->
In Chapter 7 on mergers and acquisitions, the FTC's role in reviewing deals between companies was discussed. But there are plenty more ways that the FTC becomes involved with regulating business. The care labels on the backs of clothing are the result of FTC regulations, as are the stickers on home appliances showing their energy efficiency. The FTC oversees a wide variety of rules and regulations for businesses that are designed to protect the consumer from unfair and deceptive practices. The agency reviews everything from weight loss advertising to the protection of children online. If an online retailer promises to ship a gift before a holiday but doesn't deliver, the FTC steps in and investigates. If a small business is billed for unordered toner or printer cartridges, the agency will review the claim.

该机构还监管信贷相关法律，例如《贷款真实法案》，该法案要求债权人在消费者进行信贷交易之前以书面形式披露某些成本信息，如年化利率（APR）；还有《消费者租赁法案》，该法案要求出租方向消费者提供有关租赁成本和条款的信息。FTC实施的另一项信贷法律是《公平债务催收行为法案》，该法案禁止债务催收机构使用不公平、欺诈性或虐待性的手段，包括过度收费、骚扰以及向第三方透露消费者的债务信息。

<!--en-->
The agency also regulates credit laws, such as the Truth in Lending Act, which requires creditors to disclose in writing certain cost information, such as the annual percentage rate (APR), before consumers enter into credit transactions, and the Consumer Leasing Act, which requires lessors to give consumers information on lease costs and terms. Another credit law that the FTC enforces is the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, which prohibits debt collectors from using unfair, deceptive, or abusive practices, including overcharging, harassing, and disclosing consumers' debt to third parties.

竞争与抵制也是美国联邦贸易委员会面临的重要问题。该机构曾对那些试图阻止竞争对手医疗机构成立的医生发起的抵制行为提出质疑，同时也不赞成有线电视公司之间达成的不进入对方业务领域的协议。价格操纵同样被美国联邦贸易委员会禁止，它鼓励竞争对手独立制定收费标准与条款。美国联邦贸易委员会有权对企业提起诉讼，以阻止其使用被视为不公平或非法的商业手段；或者它会试图出台新规则，禁止那些其认为会损害竞争或欺骗消费者的商业策略。政府议题 • 351 本文开头介绍了美国联邦贸易委员会是如何打击那些通过谎称资金将用于慈善事业，从而从不知情的消费者手中骗取钱财的非法筹款者的：

<!--en-->
Competition and boycotts are also big issues with the FTC. The agency has challenged boycotts by physicians seeking to prevent the establishment of a competing health care facility. And it frowns upon agreements between cable TV companies not to enter a competitor's territory. Price fixing is also banned by the FTC. It encourages competitors to set rates and terms independently. The FTC has the power to charge businesses with lawsuits to prevent them from using what has been interpreted to be unfair or illegal business practices, or it may seek to introduce new rules to outlaw a business tactic that it believes is hurting competition or deceiving consumers.
Government Issue • 351
The top of this story shows how the FTC was going after illegal fundraisers trying to get money from unsuspecting consumers by telling them they were donating to needy causes:

联邦监管机构正在通过法律诉讼并开展公众教育活动，来打击那些欺诈性筹款者，这些筹款者从那些以为自己是在为贫困退伍军人、残疾儿童、警察及消防员捐款的捐赠者那里骗走了数百万美元。

<!--en-->
Federal regulators are going to court—and launching a public education campaign—against fraudulent fundraisers charged with bilking millions of dollars out of donors who thought they were giving to needy veterans, disabled children, police officers and firefighters.

美国联邦贸易委员会周二宣布已对五家机构提起欺诈指控。其中一家位于佛罗里达州的电话推销公司被指让推销人员冒充消防员或警察来接触捐赠者；另一家位于圣地亚哥的公司则被指谎称所筹资金将用于帮助退伍军人；还有一家位于阿纳海姆的电话推销公司则被指为虚假的非营利组织筹集资金。

<!--en-->
The Federal Trade Commission on Tuesday announced it had charged five operations with fraud. One Florida telemarketer is accused of donors by having its solicitors claim to be firefighters or police officers. One in San Diego falsely said that money raised would benefit veterans, the FTC contends. Another telephone solicitor in Anaheim is accused of raising money for sham non-profits.

除了美国联邦贸易委员会的执法行动外，16个州的执法官员也在周二宣布了对他们所称的虚假慈善机构的欺诈指控。

<!--en-->
In addition to the FTC enforcement actions, law-enforcement officials in 16 states also announced fraud charges Tuesday against what they called sham charities.

美国联邦贸易委员会消费者保护局局长霍华德·比尔斯表示：“这些诈骗分子通过挪用慈善资金，破坏了公众对合法慈善筹款活动的信任，同时也损害了合法的非营利组织。”

<!--en-->
"By diverting charitable dollars, these scam artists undermine the public's confidence in legitimate charitable fundraising and injure legitimate non-profit organizations," said Howard Beales, director of the FTC's Bureau of Consumer Protection.

本月早些时候，美国最高法院裁定，那些虚报实际用于慈善事业的捐款比例的电话推销者可因消费者欺诈罪被起诉。¹⁰ 本文中提到的美国联邦贸易委员会等监管措施针对的是小型企业，而非那些通常占据商业报道头条的大型企业。许多记者误以为大型联邦监管机构只关注规模最大的企业，但实际上它们很大一部分工作都是针对那些过去可能从未被商业媒体报道过的小型企业来执行相关法规的。

<!--en-->
Earlier this month, the U.S. Supreme Court ruled that telemarketers who misrepresent the percentage of a donation that actually goes to charity can be prosecuted for consumer fraud.¹⁰
The FTC and other regulations went after small companies in this story, not the huge corporations that dominate most business coverage. Many reporters mistakenly think that huge federal regulatory agencies concern themselves only with the biggest businesses. But a large portion of their work is in enforcing the rules against small companies that may have never been covered by the business media in the past.

## 工作场所法规

<!--en-->
*Workplace Regulations*

除了监管企业向消费者销售产品的方式以及产品的生产过程外，政府机构还会确保工作场所对工人来说是安全的，并防止员工遭到雇主的骚扰。

<!--en-->
In addition to regulating how companies sell products to consumers and how they manufacture these products, government agencies ensure that the workplace is safe for workers and that employees will not be harassed by employers.

负责监督工作场所相关问题的政府机构包括职业安全与健康管理局（OSHA）、平等就业机会委员会（EEOC）以及国家劳工关系委员会（NLRB）。尽管它们属于联邦机构，但在全国几乎每个城镇都积极开展工作。

<!--en-->
The government agencies that oversee workplace-related issues include the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC), and the National Labor Relations Board (NLRB). Although federal agencies, they are active in virtually every town and city across the country.

职业安全与健康管理局会调查发生工伤事故的企业，也会调查与工作相关的死亡事件。如果企业的违规行为导致了工伤或死亡，该公司就会被处以罚款。自1971年该机构成立以来，工作场所的死亡人数下降了62%，与工作相关的伤害和疾病发生率则下降了42%。[^3912]：¹⁰ 摘自J. Boudreau所写的《美国联邦贸易委员会指控慈善机构欺诈；该机构称某公司欺骗了捐赠者》，发表于2003年5月21日的《圣何塞水星报》，第1页。版权所有2003年《圣何塞水星报》，经许可转载。352 • 政府议题 根据最新的2005年统计数据，美国有420万员工遭受了工作相关的伤害或疾病。大约每100名员工中就有4.6人经历过与工作相关的伤害或疾病，而在2006年，有5,703名员工在工作中丧生。

<!--en-->
The OSHA investigates businesses where there have been accidents or injuries on the job. It also investigates job-related deaths. If the business has violatedOSHA regulations that led to the injury or death, then the company can be fined. Since its creation in 1971, the number of workplace deaths has declined by 62 percent and work-related injuries and illnesses have declined by 42 percent.
[^3912]: ¹⁰ From "Charity fraud alleged by FTC; Agency: firm scammed donors," by J. Boudreau, May 21, 2003, *San Jose Mercury News*, p. 1. Copyright 2003 by *San Jose Mercury News*. All rights reserved. Reprinted with permission.
352 • Government Issue
In 2005, the latest statistics available, there were 4.2 million occupational injuries and illnesses among U.S. employees. Approximately 4.6 of every 100 employees experienced a job-related injury or illness, and in 2006, 5,703 employees lost their lives on the job.

2006年，职业安全与健康管理局共进行了38,500多次工作场所调查，其中大部分发生在建筑业等高风险行业。各州的职业安全与健康机构则又进行了58,000次调查。这些工作场所调查以及可能随之而来的罚款都属于公开记录，可通过申请获取。对于那些报道工作中受伤或死亡的工人的记者来说，这些文件尤为重要。以下摘录展示了如何通过查阅职业安全与健康管理局关于某工作场所的记录来更好地撰写报道：

<!--en-->
In 2006, OSHA conducted more than 38,500 workplace investigations, with the bulk of those occurring in high-hazard worksites such as construction. State job safety and health plans conducted another 58,000 investigations. These workplace investigations, and the fines that may occur, are public record, and can be obtained by asking for them. They are important documents, particularly for journalists reporting about workers who were injured or killed on the job. The following excerpt shows how reviewing OSHA records about a workplace can help tell a better story:

一名在凯斯纽荷兰工厂操作设备的意大利男子，在落入装有有毒氢氧化钾的容器并严重烧伤两天后，仍留在林肯医院接受治疗。

<!--en-->
An Italian man working on equipment at the Case New Holland plant remained in a Lincoln hospital Tuesday, two days after he fell into a tank of poisonous potassium hydroxide and suffered severe burns.

联邦官员称，这起发生在周日的事故是他们在五个月内所知的该格兰德岛农业机械工厂发生的第三起事故。此前，一名来自墨西哥的外包工人已于10月25日在此坠落身亡。

<!--en-->
Federal officials said the Sunday accident was the third they were aware of in five months at the Grand Island farm-machinery plant, where a subcontracted worker from Mexico fell to his death Oct. 25.

林肯医院的女发言人乔·米勒表示，38岁的赫拉尔多·皮亚扎目前仍在圣伊丽莎白地区医疗中心接受治疗，情况危急。他身体80%以上的面积遭受了二度及三度烧伤。

<!--en-->
Gerardo Piazza, 38, was in critical condition at St. Elizabeth Regional Medical Center. He suffered second- and third-degree burns over 80 percent of his body, said Jo Miller, a spokeswoman with the Lincoln hospital.

皮亚扎的家人居住在意大利米兰，周日他通过医疗直升机从格兰德岛的圣弗朗西斯医疗中心被送往林肯医院。

<!--en-->
Piazza, whose family lives in Milan, Italy, was flown to Lincoln Sunday by medical helicopter from Grand Island's St. Francis Medical Center.

格兰德岛警察局长威廉·霍洛韦周二表示，皮亚扎似乎是在当天下午2点30分左右掉进氢氧化钾储罐中，但他成功爬出并呼救。

<!--en-->
He apparently fell into the potassium hydroxide tank about 2:30 p.m. that day but managed to get out and yell for help, Grand Island Police Capt. William Holloway said Tuesday.

霍洛韦称，在格兰德岛的急救人员赶到之前，其他工人们立刻冲向皮亚扎，帮其脱掉衣服并用水冲洗。只有他的头部和臀部没有受到烧伤。

<!--en-->
He said other workers rushed to Piazza, removed his clothing and rinsed him off with water before Grand Island paramedics arrived to treat him. Only Piazza's head and buttocks were not burned, Holloway said.

氢氧化钾，有时也被称为苛性钾或烧碱，是一种具有腐蚀性的物质，常用于清洁。吞食后可能致命，接触活体组织则会导致严重烧伤。

<!--en-->
Potassium hydroxide, sometimes called lye or caustic potash, is a corrosive acid sometimes used for cleaning. It can be fatal if swallowed and can cause severe burns if it comes into contact with living tissue.

凯斯纽荷兰工厂的经理史蒂夫·李周二未回复电话留言。他周一表示，皮亚扎的家人已接到通知，正计划前往林肯。李称，皮亚扎坠入储罐时是独自一人，而那个储罐位于需要授权才能穿越的安全屏障后面。工厂方面不清楚皮亚扎为何会出现在那个用于给联合收割机部件上漆前的储罐附近。李指出，皮亚扎是总部位于米兰的涂料供应商Comau Geico的项目工程师。这家公司以及在格兰德岛拥有700名员工的凯斯纽荷兰都属于总部位于意大利的菲亚特集团。

<!--en-->
Steve Lee, manager of the Case New Holland plant, did not return telephone messages Tuesday. He said Monday that Piazza's family had been notified and planned to travel to Lincoln. Lee said Piazza was alone when he fell into the tank, which is behind a safety barrier that requires authorization to cross. Plant officials didn't know why Piazza was near the tank, in which parts of combines are dipped before painting. Lee identified Piazza as a project engineer with Comau Geico, a paint-supply firm based in Milan. That firm and Case New Holland, which employs 700 people in Grand Island, are part of the Italy-based Fiat Group.

根据菲亚特网站上的资料，纽荷兰NV在1999年与凯斯公司合并之前就属于该集团。这两家公司都在美国农业机械生产领域有着深厚的根基。此次合并形成了CNH Global，该公司在2000年7月宣布将把凯斯IH和纽荷兰的联合收割机生产业务整合到格兰德岛的工厂中。

<!--en-->
New Holland NV belonged to that group before merging with Case Corp. in 1999, according to material on Fiat's Internet site. Both firms had deep roots in U.S. farm-machinery production.
Government Issue • 353
The merger formed CNH Global, which announced in July 2000 that it would consolidate its Case IH and New Holland combine production at the Grand Island plant.

美国职业安全与健康管理局奥马哈地区助理局长博妮塔·威宁厄姆表示，另一家菲亚特旗下公司Comau Pico以及一家外包商，因与该起死亡事故相关或早于该事故的工厂安全问题而被处以罚款。

<!--en-->
Another Fiat company, Comau Pico, and a subcontractor have been fined for safety problems at the plant related to or predating the Oct. 25 fatality, said Bonita Winingham, assistant Omaha-area director for the U.S. Occupational Safety and Health Administration.

霍洛韦称，36岁的胡安·希门尼斯·莱穆斯从12英尺高的脚手架上坠落到混凝土地面上，头部受伤身亡。警方表示，他当时正在处理绝缘材料，并佩戴了安全带，但安全带并未系好。莱穆斯来自墨西哥瓜纳华托州的塞拉亚，受雇于一家名为One de Mexico的公司。

<!--en-->
Holloway said Juan Jimenez Lemus, 36, died of head injuries after he fell 12 feet from a scaffolding onto a concrete floor. He had been working with a piece of sheathed insulation and wore a safety harness, but the harness was unattached, police said. Lemus, who came from Celaya in the Mexican state of Guanajuato, was employed by a firm called One de Mexico.

威宁厄姆称，这家注册地址在格兰德岛的公司已同意为莱穆斯死亡后发现的4项OSHA违规行为，以及8月7日至9月11日期间检查中发现的6项违规行为，共计支付24,479美元的罚款。

<!--en-->
Winingham said that firm, which lists a Grand Island address, has agreed to pay fines totaling $24,479 for four OSHA violations found after Lemus' death and six found in inspections between Aug. 7 and Sept. 11.

她表示，之前的检查是由于7月31日有人举报称该工厂在建造输送系统时有一名工人受伤而启动的。

<!--en-->
The earlier inspections were triggered by a July 31 allegation that a worker was hurt during construction of a conveyor system at the plant, she said.

她称，Comau Pico已同意为8月7日至9月17日的检查中发现的4项违规行为支付7,425美元的罚款。

<!--en-->
Comau Pico has agreed to pay $7,425 in fines for four violations found in inspections from Aug. 7 to Sept. 17, she said.

她表示，该公司有时间在1月13日前对OSHA在12月16日因10月23日至12月16日期间发现的8项违规行为而处以的70,000美元罚款提出异议。

<!--en-->
The firm has until Jan. 13 to contest $70,000 in fines that OSHA assessed Dec. 16 for eight violations found from Oct. 23 to Dec. 16, she said.

威宁厄姆称，凯斯纽荷兰工厂本身也已加入OSHA的自愿保护计划。该计划仅面向那些具备良好健康与安全记录的雇主，可使其免于接受OSHA的例行检查。¹¹ 如果没有关于诸多罚款和违规行为的背景信息，读者可能会认为最近这起事故只是一起孤立事件。但通过OSHA的资料可以看出，这个工作场所对工人而言可能存在安全隐患，而且该公司在改善工作条件方面做得不够好。

<!--en-->
The Case New Holland plant itself has been admitted to OSHA's Voluntary Protection Program, Winingham said. The program, limited to employers with a strong health and safety record, exempts a worksite from programmed inspections by OSHA.¹¹
Without the background information about the numerous fines and violations, a reader might believe that the most recent accident was an isolated incident. But the story indicates, by using OSHA information, that this workplace may be unsafe for workers and that the company has not done a good job in improving conditions.

OSHA会根据违规行为的严重程度以及是否为重复违规来决定罚款金额。雇主故意或明知故犯的违规行为，罚款金额在5,000美元至70,000美元之间。如果违规行为有可能导致死亡或严重身体伤害，且雇主知晓或应当知晓该危险，那么每项违规行为的罚款最高可达7,000美元。

<!--en-->
OSHA can levy fines on the basis of the seriousness of the violation and whether it is a repeat offense. A violation that the employer willingly or knowingly commits carries a fine between $5,000 and $70,000. A violation in which there is a probability that death or serious physical harm could occur and the employer knows, or should know, of the hazard, can result in a penalty of up to $7,000 per violation.

如果一家公司在一次检查中被发现违反某项规定，而在再次检查时又被发现违反类似规定，可能面临最高70,000美元的罚款。若未能纠正违规行为，则每天可能被处以最高7,000美元的罚款，直至问题得到解决。而对于那些虽会影响安全与健康但 unlikely导致死亡或严重伤害的违规行为，罚款金额同样可达最高7,000美元。[^3937]：¹¹ 来自T. von Kampen于2003年1月1日发表在《奥马哈世界先驱报》第1B版的文章《工人掉入毒液池；意大利工程师在格兰德岛的Case New Holland工厂事故中严重烧伤》，版权归《奥马哈世界先驱报》所有，经许可转载。354 • 政府资讯 记者通常需要等到有受伤工人对公司提起诉讼或工会提出投诉后，才能得知当地企业存在工作场所安全问题。对于负责报道大型企业的记者而言，与员工建立联系以了解OSHA的投诉情况很有帮助。此外，也可以在OSHA网站（http://www.osha.gov）上通过公司名称搜索相关投诉。

<!--en-->
If a company was found in violation of a regulation on one inspection and then found in violation of a similar rule on a re-inspection, it could be fined up to $70,000. Failure to correct a violation can result in a fine of up to $7,000 per day until it is corrected. And violations that have an effect on safety and health, but probably would not cause death or serious injury, can result in a fine of up to $7,000.
[^3937]: ¹¹ From “Worker falls into tank of poison; An Italian engineer sustained severe burns in an accident at Grand Island’s Case New Holland plant,” by T. von Kampen, January 1, 2003, *Omaha World Herald*, p. 1B. Copyright 2003 by *Omaha World Herald*. Reprinted with permission.
354 • Government Issue
A reporter may not get an indication that there is a workplace safety problem at a local company until tipped off by a lawsuit filed against the company by an injured worker or by a union complaint. It is helpful for any reporter covering a large employer to develop relationships with employees to learn about OSHA complaints. In addition, the OSHA website (http://www.osha.gov) can also be searched for complaints by company name.

平等就业机会委员会成立于1964年，旨在防止企业基于种族、肤色、性别、年龄、宗教或国籍进行就业歧视。1990年，《美国残疾人法案》将平等就业机会委员会的监管范围扩展到残疾工人。该委员会由五名由美国总统任命、任期为五年的委员以及一名任期为四年的总法律顾问组成。

<!--en-->
The EEOC was created in 1964 and prevents businesses from employment discrimination on the basis of race, color, sex, age, religion, or national origin. In 1990, the Americans with Disabilities Act extended the EEOC's regulations to include workers with disabilities. The commission has five commissioners, all appointed by the U.S. president, who serve five-year terms, as well as a general counsel who serves a four-year term.

平等就业机会委员会每年会收到大约80,000起来自私营企业员工的歧视投诉。该机构会对此展开调查，若发现有合理理由相信确实存在歧视行为，可能会尝试与公司达成和解。如果无法达成和解，平等就业机会委员会便可在联邦法院对该公司提起诉讼。

<!--en-->
The EEOC receives approximately 80,000 charges of discrimination annually from employees of private businesses. The agency will then investigate, and if it discovers that there is reasonable cause to believe that discrimination has occurred, the EEOC may attempt to reach a settlement with the company. If a settlement cannot be reached, the EEOC may file charges against the business in federal court.

2008年，平等就业机会委员会对多家企业提起了325起诉讼，并解决了366起诉讼，为工人争取到了超过1.022亿美元的赔偿款。这类和解案往往具有新闻价值，应当予以报道，南佛罗里达州的以下案例便是如此：

<!--en-->
In 2008, the EEOC filed 325 lawsuits against businesses and settled 366 lawsuits, obtaining more than $102.2 million in damages for workers. These settlements are often newsworthy, and should be reported, as were the following cases in South Florida:

一名商店经理称自己因举报女员工遭受男经理性骚扰而遭解雇，在监管机构起诉其雇主后，她获得了250,000美元的欠薪及经济补偿。

<!--en-->
A store manager who alleged she was fired after complaining about sexual harassment that female employees endured from a male manager was awarded $250,000 in back pay and monetary relief after regulators sued her employer.

这是美国平等就业机会委员会迈阿密办事处近期解决的针对佛罗里达州雇主的三起报复性诉讼案件之一。

<!--en-->
It was one of three retaliation lawsuits against Florida employers recently settled by the Miami office of the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission.

迈阿密地区的平等就业机会委员会律师Delner Franklin-Thomas表示：“因员工合理认为存在就业歧视而对其实施报复，违反了联邦法律。”

<!--en-->
"Retaliating against employees for complaining about what they reasonably believed to be employment discrimination is contrary to federal law," said Delner Franklin-Thomas, EEOC regional attorney in Miami.

2002年，佛罗里达州共有1,725起报复性投诉案件，占该州所有歧视投诉案件的29%。全美范围内向平等就业机会委员会提交的报复性投诉案件数量从1995年的17,070起增至2002年的22,768起，增长了33%。

<!--en-->
In Florida, there were 1,725 retaliation filings in 2002, accounting for 29 percent of all discrimination charge filings in the state. Retaliation charge filings with the EEOC nationwide have increased by 33 percent from 17,070 filings in 1995 to 22,768 filings in 2002.

周二宣布的和解对象包括：

<!--en-->
The settlements announced Tuesday were with:

总部位于纽约的女装连锁店Fashion Cents旗下的Norstan Apparel Shops Inc.。该机构为一位坦帕店的经理赢得了250,000美元的经济补偿，其中包括欠薪和惩罚性赔偿金。这名经理称自己因向区域经理举报有经理骚扰女员工而被解雇。

<!--en-->
Norstan Apparel Shops Inc., a New York-based chain of women's clothing stores called Fashion Cents. The agency won $250,000 in monetary relief, including back pay and compensatory damages, for a store manager in Tampa. She alleged that she was fired for complaining to district managers about a manager who harassed female workers.

试图联系该公司总裁以获取评论未果。

<!--en-->
Attempts to reach the company president for comment were unsuccessful.

佛罗里达群岛海洋银行。平等就业机会委员会指控该银行对一名副总裁的性骚扰行为视而不见，还因一名女员工举报该行为而解雇了她。政府资讯 • 355 最终该银行同意向两名员工支付220,000美元，并在所有分支机构开展年度培训，同时遵守平等就业机会委员会的监督要求，从而解决了这场诉讼。

<!--en-->
Marine Bank of the Florida Keys. The EEOC charged the bank with allowing a vice president's sexually offensive conduct to go unchecked and with firing a female employee for complaining about the conduct.
Government Issue • 355
The suit was resolved with the bank agreeing to pay two employees $220,000 as well as do annual training at all facilities and comply with EEOC monitoring.

该银行行长Hunter Padgett表示：“我们非常重视这个问题。很高兴这场诉讼已经了结。4月4日我们将开始培训，而且我们已经明确表示绝不容忍此类行为。”

<!--en-->
"We take this very seriously," said the bank's president, Hunter Padgett. "We're glad to have the lawsuit behind us. On April 4, we begin the training, and we've made it clear that we will not tolerate those behaviors."

总部位于加利福尼亚州圣安娜的物流货运公司GeoLogistics Americas被联邦法官责令向一名员工支付100,000美元，该员工称杰克逊维尔的门店经理在她投诉遭受歧视后解雇了她。

<!--en-->
GeoLogistics Americas, a Santa Ana, Calif.-based logistics and freight forwarder, was ordered by a federal judge to pay $100,000 to an employee who alleged that a branch manager in Jacksonville fired her after she complained of discrimination.

她抱怨称GeoLogistics只为男性员工提供叉车操作培训及认证，却一直以她是女性为由拒绝为她提供培训。法院还要求GeoLogistics为管理人员开展年度培训，并向平等就业机会委员会提交报告。

<!--en-->
She complained that GeoLogistics provided forklift training and certification to male workers, but consistently denied her requests for the training because she is a woman. The court also required GeoLogistics to do annual training for managers and complete reports to the EEOC.

试图联系该公司的人力资源总监未果。¹²需要再次强调的是，这些案件针对的都是小型企业，而非那些常出现在新闻报道中的大型企业。的确，EEOC也曾对Home Depot和Hooters等知名雇主提起过诉讼，但其大部分监管工作仍集中在构成经济主体的小型企业上。

<!--en-->
Attempts to reach the company's director of human resources were unsuccessful.¹²
Again, these cases were against small companies, not the big businesses that dominate coverage. To be sure, the EEOC has filed charges against high-profile employers such as Home Depot and Hooters. But again, a large amount of its regulatory work is with small businesses that make up the bulk of the economy.

记者应查明所在州当地的EEOC办公室位置。当地工人会在那里提交投诉，调查也从那里开始。如果EEOC决定对某家企业采取行动，它会在联邦法院提起诉讼。如果记者怀疑某起案件即将发生，应定期前往该办公室了解情况。

<!--en-->
Reporters should find out where the local EEOC office is in their state. That is where complaints are filed by local workers, and where the investigations begin. If the EEOC is going to take action against a business, it will file its lawsuit in federal court. If a reporter suspects a case is about to happen, he or she should check the clerk's office regularly.

NLRB同样负责保护在职工人。它监督规范代表工人的工会与企业之间关系的法律。NLRB有两个主要职能：其一是通过秘密投票选举来确定特定企业的工人是否希望由某个工会代表，以及希望由哪个工会代表；其二是对企业或工会的不公平劳动行为进行调查。

<!--en-->
The NLRB also protects workers on the job. It oversees the laws governing relationships between labor unions representing workers and corporations. The NLRB has two basic functions: One is to conduct secret-ballot elections to determine whether the workers at a specific employer want to be represented by a union and which one; the other is to investigate unfair labor practices by employers or unions.

NLRB官员会监督选举过程。有时，与这些选举相关的故事实际上正是促使工人考虑成立工会的起因。采访一些工人，询问他们的工作环境以及他们认为加入工会能获得什么好处，可能会很有帮助。在雇主处可能存在支持工会和反对工会的工人，而雇主也可能积极活动以阻止工会成立。大多数企业都不希望自己的工人有工会代表，因为他们认为这会增加运营成本。

<!--en-->
An NLRB official oversees an election. Sometimes the story with one of these elections is actually the events that caused the workers to consider union representation. It might be beneficial to interview some of these workers to ask them about their working conditions and what they believe they will get out of joining a union. There may be pro-union and anti-union workers at the employer. And the employer may also be campaigning actively to defeat the union. Most businesses do not want their workers represented by a union. They believe it brings additional costs to running their operations.

不公平劳动行为可能包含多种表现形式。可能是主管威胁工人，称如果他们加入工会就会失去工作，或者威胁说如果工人投票支持成立工会就会关闭工厂或仓库。向工人承诺如果他们投票反对工会就会给予某些好处，这也属于违规行为。[^3962]：¹²摘自J. Fleischer Tamen所著《3起雇主诉讼达成和解；监管机构着手调查报复行为》，2003年3月19日，《The Sun-Sentinel》报，第3D页。版权所有2003年《The South Florida Sun-Sentinel》报，经许可转载。356 • 政府支持的工会也可能存在可能导致调查的不公平劳动行为。它们可能会威胁工人，称如果不支持工会就会失去工作，或者如果工人曾批评过工会官员，就拒绝为其处理投诉。

<!--en-->
An unfair labor practice can mean a number of different things. It could be a supervisor threatening workers with the loss of their jobs if they join a union, orthreatening to close the plant or warehouse if the workers vote to join the union. Promising benefits to workers if they vote against the union can also be a violation.
[^3962]: ¹² From "3 employer lawsuits settled; regulators take aim at retaliation," by J. Fleischer Tamen, March 19, 2003, *The Sun-Sentinel*, p. 3D. Copyright 2003 by *The South Florida Sun-Sentinel*. Reprinted with permission.
356 • Government Issue
Unions can also engage in unfair labor practices that could lead to an investigation. They may threaten workers with the loss of their job if they do not support the union, or they could refuse to file a grievance against a supervisor if the worker has criticized union officials in the past.

在提出指控后，会展开调查。如果区域主管认为存在违规行为，NLRB会尝试调解达成和解。如果无法达成和解，案件将交由NLRB的行政法法官处理，由其出具书面裁决。这些裁决可向上级由五名成员组成的NLRB管理委员会提出上诉。每年约有3万起不公平劳动行为指控被提出，其中约三分之一被认定有事实依据。这些案件中超过90%最终得以和解。

<!--en-->
After a charge is filed, an investigation is conducted. If a regional director believes a violation has occurred, the NLRB will attempt to mediate a settlement. If no settlement can be reached, then the case will go to an NLRB administrative law judge who will issue a written decision. Those decisions can be appealed to the five-member board that oversees the NLRB. About 30,000 unfair labor practice charges are filed each year. And of those, about one-third are found to have merit. More than 90 percent of those cases are settled.

企业与监管机构之间的关系往往是对立的，这对于那些懂得如何获取相关细节以撰写相关报道的记者来说，是很好的素材来源。尽管监管机构乍看之下可能显得乏味，但它们在商业世界中起着重要作用，为美国企业的发展制定各种规则和法规。正因如此，它们是值得定期关注的重要信息来源。

<!--en-->
The relationship between businesses and regulatory agencies can often be adversarial, which makes for good stories by reporters who know how to obtain the details leading to the confrontation. Although regulatory agencies may seem boring at first glance, they play an important role in the business world, setting rules and regulations for how Corporate America should operate. Because of that role, they are vital sources of information that should be regularly checked.

## 建议练习题

<!--en-->
*Suggested Exercises*

1. 询问你认识的五个人，如果他们觉得在工作中受到骚扰或歧视，是否会向EEOC投诉。哪些情况会迫使他们提出投诉？如果有人回答不会投诉，原因是什么？
2. 你的电话公司或有线电视公司需要提供多糟糕的服务，才会让你向监管机构投诉？
3. 如何判断你的电力公司或自来水公司是否多收了费用？你可以去哪里核对账单？
4. 如果你购买的产品无法使用，可以采取哪三个步骤尝试从零售商或制造商那里拿回钱款？
5. 为什么政府要在企业监管中扮演如此重要的角色？如果政府不监管企业的产品销售和制造方式，会发生什么？![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/28ea43c75649b559f3d457664e5f2bf5.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T071651Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=dad81d05341e7c3dc2ac5ee5c8d19c2cba01bb2024fde22f0455cd314ab6dee1)

<!--en-->
1. Ask five people you know if they would file a complaint with the EEOC if they felt they were being harassed or discriminated against on the job. What circumstances would force them to file a complaint? If some answered that they wouldn't file a complaint, why wouldn't they?
2. What type of bad service would it take from your phone company or cable company to lead you to file a complaint with regulators?
3. How would you know if your electrical company or water company was overcharging you? Where could you go to have your bill checked?
4. If you purchased a product that didn't work, what three steps could you take to try to get your money back from the retailer or the manufacturer?
5. Why does the government play such a large role in regulating business? What would happen if the government didn't regulate how companies sold their products or manufactured them?
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/28ea43c75649b559f3d457664e5f2bf5.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T071651Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=dad81d05341e7c3dc2ac5ee5c8d19c2cba01bb2024fde22f0455cd314ab6dee1)

### 16

网络让工作更轻松

<!--en-->
The Web Makes it Easier

#### 网站的可靠性

<!--en-->
*The Reliability of Sites*

记者们越来越多地从互联网上获取新闻报道所需的资讯与事实。但网上的一切信息都可信吗？并非如此，正因如此，在线进行调研的商业记者应当对所找到的内容保持警惕。

<!--en-->
Reporters are getting more and more of their information and the facts they use in stories from the Internet. But is everything on the World Wide Web credible? No, and that is why business journalists conducting research online should be wary of what they are finding.

互联网彻底改变了新闻业各个领域的记者与编辑的工作方式。过去，记者或编辑必须亲自前往法院查询诉讼记录或犯罪记录，或者寄支票给外地的联邦机构，然后等待两周才能收到邮件中的文件。

<!--en-->
The Internet has drastically changed how reporters and editors do their jobs in every area of journalism. It used to be that reporters or editors would have to go to the courthouse to find a lawsuit or criminal record, or they would have to send a check to some out-of-town federal agency and wait two weeks for a document to show up in the mail.

互联网让记者只需点击桌面上收藏的几个网站，就能在不出新闻编辑室的情况下获得报道所需的大部分信息。不过根据公共记录研究系统的数据，只有约20%的公共记录可在互联网上找到，其余的仍保存在数以百万计的文件柜和抽屉中的纸质资料里，无法通过简单点击键盘查阅。

<!--en-->
The Internet has made it possible for journalists to get much of the information they need to report a story just by clicking on a few favorites on their desktop—without leaving their desk in the newsroom. But, according to the Public Record Research System, only about 20 percent of public records are available on the Internet. The others are still maintained on paper stored in millions of file cabinets and drawers, unable to be perused with some keyboard clicks.

即便是在互联网上可找到的公共记录，也往往难以寻觅。许多记者不知道该从何处入手。北卡罗来纳州东部《格林维尔每日反射报》的记者金杰·利文斯顿在需要了解当地一家大型企业荷兰母公司的相关信息时不知该去哪找，而公关人员也未能提供太多帮助。事实上，利文斯顿所需的信息就在多个网站上。

<!--en-->
And even the public records available on the Internet can be hard to find. Many reporters do not know where to begin. Ginger Livingston, a reporter for the *Greenville Daily Reflector* in eastern North Carolina, did not know where to turn when she needed to find information about the Dutch parent company of a large employer in her town, and the public relations people were not much help. As it turns out, the information Livingston needed was available on several websites.

在线调研主题的另一个问题是，相关信息可能来自那些运营者身份不明的网站。许多年轻记者发现网上有相关资料后，就认为只要能上网就能证明其真实性，但事实并非如此。互联网上的信息可能反映出现有网站运营者的观点或偏见，而且还有大量多年未更新的信息。360 • 网络让工作更轻松 虽然可以合理地认为由政府机构和为传播自身运营信息而设立的公私公司运营的网站是获取新闻素材的可靠来源，但仍有数以百万计的其他网站并不那么值得信赖。

<!--en-->
Another problem with researching topics online is that the information may come from a site where it is not clear who is operating the URL. Many young reporters find information on the Internet and believe it must be true if it is available online. That is simply not the case. Information on the World Wide Web may reflect the opinion or biases of whoever is operating the site. And there is plenty of information online that has not been updated in years.
360 • The Web Makes it Easier
Though it can be reasonably assumed that websites operated by state and federal government agencies and Internet domains run by public and private companies for the purpose of disseminating information about their operations are reliable places to obtain information for a story, millions of other sites are not as trustworthy.

实际上有一些网站允许人们查询其他网站的所有权。这一实用工具对于判断网站是否可靠大有帮助。其中一个网站位于**www.whois.net**,**，用户可以查看当前域名所有者的信息，以及已关闭的网站的曾有所有者。其他类似网站则位于**www.allwhois.com****和**www.networksolutions.com**.**，将某公司的网址输入这些网站即可查看相关信息。

<!--en-->
There are actually some websites that allow a person to check the ownership of other websites. This handy tool can go a long way in determining whether the website is reliable. One of these sites is located at **www.whois.net**, which allows people to look at the ownership of current domain names as well as who owned an Internet site that is now defunct. Other similar sites are located at **www.allwhois.com** and **www.networksolutions.com**. Insert a company's Web address into one of these and see what you find.

大多数情况下，行政联系人会是该公司的律师，但通常也会包含技术联系人。这个人很可能就是实际运营网站、根据需要更新内容的人。通过这类查询得到的信息还能告知你该网站最后一次更新的时间。

<!--en-->
Most of the time, the administrative contact person will be an attorney for the company, but often they will also include a technical contact. This is the person who probably actually runs the website, updating it with information as needed. And the information that comes back from one of these searches could also tell you when the site was last updated.

关于在线查找信息最后一点建议：避免使用谷歌或Lycos等常用搜索引擎进行基础搜索。尽管这些服务很棒，但它们也会提供大量与搜索主题无关的人或话题信息。

<!--en-->
One last word about searching for information online: Beware of doing basic searches using a common search engine such as Google or Lycos. Although these are great services, they will also give an abundance of information about people or topics that may not be germane to the search.

以下为面向商业记者的网站列表，并非面面俱到，但尽力列出了记者们在收集商业和经济领域信息时最常使用的一些知名网站。所有这些网站都经过审核，属于可靠的信息来源。如有疑问，可利用上述资源中的工具对该网站进行核查。

<!--en-->
The following list of websites for business journalists is by no means comprehensive. But it does attempt to offer some of the most widely known and used sites by reporters in gathering information about business and economics topics and issues. All of these sites have been reviewed and are credible sources of information. When in doubt, check the site with one of the resources above.
